The maker's launch release called it medium-full; Neptune lists medium and halfwheel's review found it a little above medium. Halfwheel spells the smallest size Festive; retailers list Festivo.

cigars.about: A Dominican puro from Rafael Nodal's core Aging Room line, made at Jochy Blanco's Tabacalera Palma. It came out of the 2018 overhaul of the Aging Room portfolio alongside Connecticut and Maduro versions.
cigars.researchNote: Launched as Aging Room by Rafael Nodal Habano; retailers call it Core Habano. No published strength rating was found. Neptune has no sizes in stock and it is not on Altadis USA's Aging Room page, so it may be discontinued.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro in the New World series, blended by Ismael Fernandez using only tobacco from his son's Estelí farms, aged three to five years.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's site calls the wrapper Nicaragua Habano; AJ Fernandez said at launch it is Criollo '98 seed, and Neptune and Famous Smoke list it as Criollo. Neptune lists it as medium; Famous Smoke's spec says full but its description says medium-bodied.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The Connecticut Shade version of AJ Fernandez's New World, released in 2015. Unlike the box-pressed original it is rolled round, with a Mexican San Andrés binder under a U.S.-grown shade wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Fuller than most Connecticut Shade cigars. Neptune lists it as medium and Holt's as mild-medium; halfwheel's reviewer found medium strength with medium-full body.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: AJ Fernandez's first Cameroon-wrapped cigar, a box-pressed New World extension over Nicaraguan binder and filler from his Estelí farms.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune and Famous Smoke list it as medium; Holt's lists it as full.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The original New World from 2014, the first cigar AJ Fernandez blended with his father Ismael. It is a box-pressed Nicaraguan puro with a dark wrapper, built to sell at a value price.
cigars.researchNote: This is the original New World, and many shops list it simply as New World. Sizes were first sold as Navegante (robusto), Almirante (belicoso), Virrey (gordo) and Gobernador (toro). Holt's lists it as medium-full, Famous Smoke as full, Neptune as medium.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The Habano blend of San Lotano, the brand AJ Fernandez revived from his grandfather's Cuban label. It launched in 2010 as his first nationally distributed line.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2010 as San Lotano Habano; Requiem was added to the name a few years later. Blend is as the maker lists it. Neptune also lists Dominican filler, and halfwheel's 2011 review listed a Honduran binder.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The maduro blend of San Lotano, the brand AJ Fernandez revived from his grandfather's Cuban label in 2010. It wears a dark Mexican San Andrés wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2010 as San Lotano Maduro; Requiem was added to the name a few years later. Retailers disagree on strength: Holt's says medium-full, Neptune full, Famous Smoke medium.

cigars.about: A box-pressed San Lotano that comes in a cedar sleeve, with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco from AJ Fernandez's farms. It is positioned as the fuller blend in the brand.
cigars.researchNote: First sold in 2013 as a Meier & Dutch distributor exclusive, then released nationwide in February 2014. AJ Fernandez described it as medium to full; Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A line of short, quick-smoking cigars that began as the blend AJ Fernandez handed to guests at his Estelí compound. It went on sale to brick and mortar shops in 2016.
cigars.researchNote: The maker now lists this original blend as Last Call Habano. It launched in one size, the 4 1/2 x 48 Geniales. Holt's lists it as medium-full, Neptune as medium, and Famous Smoke's spec as full.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The maduro version of AJ Fernandez's Last Call line of short cigars, introduced in 2016 a few months after the original.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is Pennsylvania Broadleaf seed that AJ Fernandez grows in Nicaragua, so the company calls this a Nicaraguan puro. Some retailers list it as U.S. Pennsylvania leaf. Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The Connecticut Broadleaf version of Enclave, launched in 2017 as a darker and fuller take on the original. Like the first Enclave it was blended by AJ Fernandez and his father Ismael.
cigars.researchNote: Formally launched at the July 2017 trade show after a small pre-release to select shops in 2016. Neptune and Famous Smoke list it as full; Holt's lists it as medium-full.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The first extension of Días de Gloria, released in 2024. It puts a Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper over AJ Fernandez's Nicaraguan binder and filler, and all five sizes are box-pressed.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's lists it as medium-full; Neptune's spec says medium, though its description says medium to full.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The maduro follow-up to Bellas Artes, released in 2018. It pairs a Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper with a Mexican San Andrés binder, an uncommon combination, and the Robusto placed 10th on halfwheel's Top 25 of 2018.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune and Famous Smoke list it as full; Holt's lists it as medium-full. The 7 x 40 Lancero began in 2019 as a limited run of 2,000 boxes.

cigars.about: A bundle cigar from AJ Fernandez, a Nicaraguan puro made with long filler and sold 15 to a paper bundle. It was announced in 2020 for markets outside the United States.
cigars.researchNote: Full name is Blend 15 by AJ Fernandez. It was announced in September 2020 for a November launch in markets outside the U.S. only, so a U.S. shop is unlikely to stock it. Only that announcement could be confirmed: no wrapper type, strength, factory or tasting notes are published, and it is not on the maker's site.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Honduran cigar built around a dark Corojo wrapper grown in Trojes, rolled at Raíces Cubanas in Danlí. The Churchill was Cigar Aficionado's No. 1 Cigar of the Year for 2011.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists body as medium to full. Cigar Aficionado and Neptune rate strength full, Holts medium-full. Halfwheel reported the Corona Gorda discontinued in June 2026.

cigars.about: The first line to carry the Alec Bradley name, built on estate tobacco from Trojes, Honduras and rolled at Raíces Cubanas. Tempus is Latin for time, a nod to how long the tobacco is aged.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists medium strength, Famous calls it full-bodied, and the maker says medium to full. Halfwheel reported the Figurado, Corona, Robusto and Torpedo discontinued in 2025 and the Churchill in 2026.

cigars.about: One of Alec Bradley's best sellers, a multi-country blend with a dark Nicaraguan wrapper over a Sumatra binder and Panamanian and Honduran filler. It is made by the Plasencia family in Danlí, Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: The maker, halfwheel and Neptune list the binder only as Sumatra; Holts says it is from Ecuador. Famous describes the wrapper as Jalapa grown. The maker says medium to full body, while Holts and Neptune list medium strength. Halfwheel reported the Punk size discontinued in March 2025.

cigars.about: A stronger, mostly Nicaraguan take on Black Market, rolled at Plasencia's factory in Estelí. It uses a Nicaraguan wrapper and filler with a double binder.
cigars.researchNote: Not a Nicaraguan puro: one of the two binder leaves is Honduran. The maker says medium to full body, while Holts, Neptune and Famous list full strength.

cigars.about: A dark Honduran-wrapped blend made at Raíces Cubanas in Danlí. The name comes from a late-night toast founder Alan Rubin made in a Honduran tobacco field, and some of the tobacco comes from that field.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper variety is not published. Holts and Neptune list medium strength, Famous lists full, and the maker says medium to full body.

cigars.about: A value-priced Nicaraguan puro with a sun-grown Habano wrapper from Jalapa. It is the fuller, spicier sibling of the American Classic.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers disagree on strength: Neptune lists medium, Holts medium-full and Famous full, while the maker calls the body medium. Halfwheel reported the Corona and Torpedo discontinued in August 2025.

cigars.about: A value-priced everyday cigar with a Honduran-grown Connecticut seed wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, rolled by Plasencia in Nicaragua. It was blended to recall the smooth, simple American cigars of an earlier era.
cigars.researchNote: Often sold as American Classic Blend. The maker says mellow to medium body, while Holts, Neptune and Famous list medium strength. Halfwheel reported the Corona and Torpedo discontinued in 2025 and the Robusto in 2026.

cigars.about: Alec Bradley's Connecticut Shade cigar, with a Honduran binder and Honduran and Nicaraguan filler, made in Honduras. The maker describes it as mellow to medium bodied.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the wrapper only as Connecticut; Holts, Neptune and Famous say it is Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade. Retailers range from mild to medium on strength. Halfwheel reported the Nano, Torpedo and Churchill discontinued in August 2025.

cigars.factory: J. Fuego Cigar Co. de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A budget-priced Nicaraguan cigar made at Jesus Fuego's factory in Estelí and the first release in Alec Bradley's Experimental Series. The name refers to the idea that 40 percent of a person's happiness comes from how they think.
cigars.researchNote: Sizes are named for their dimensions. The maker's site lists the Churchill as 07.52 (7 x 52), while halfwheel reported it as 07.50 (7 x 50). The wrapper variety is not published.

cigars.factory: J. Fuego Cigar Co. de Nicaragua
cigars.about: The maduro version of Project 40, keeping the Brazilian Habano binder and Nicaraguan filler but swapping in a Mexican San Andrés wrapper. It is made at the J. Fuego factory in Estelí and priced as an everyday smoke.
cigars.researchNote: The maker says medium to full body, while Neptune lists medium strength. Sizes are named for their dimensions.

cigars.about: The third cigar from Alec and Bradley Rubin, the founder's sons, made at Raíces Cubanas with a Honduran Habano wrapper from Trojes. It is named for the Japanese art of repairing broken pottery with gold.
cigars.researchNote: Sold under the Alec & Bradley name. Halfwheel reported the Corona Gorda discontinued in June 2026.

cigars.about: The second cigar from Alec and Bradley Rubin, blended with Ernesto Perez-Carrillo. It pairs an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper with Nicaraguan and Dominican tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Sold under the Alec & Bradley name. It was first made at Perez-Carrillo's Tabacalera La Alianza in the Dominican Republic; production moved to Plasencia's Tabacos de Oriente in Honduras starting in 2021, so older boxes are Dominican.

cigars.about: Alec Bradley's first all-Nicaraguan cigar, made by Plasencia in Estelí. The line was discontinued in 2021.
cigars.researchNote: Discontinued in March 2021 and now listed in the maker's Vault of retired lines. The maker lists the wrapper only as Nicaraguan; Holts and Neptune call it Habano. Holts lists medium strength and Neptune full.

cigars.filler: Honduras (Jamastran), Nicaragua (Jalapa, Estelí), Mexico (San Andrés), Dominican Republic (Criollo)
cigars.about: Alec Bradley's limited series, started in 2011 and released most years since, in which every release blends ten different tobaccos: one wrapper, two binders and seven fillers. Each edition has its own code name and is rolled at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Blend and size change with each release. The blend, body and flavors here are for the 2025 edition, ANB-228 (1,500 boxes of 10), which comes in one size: the maker lists 7 1/4 x 50, halfwheel lists 7 x 50. The maker writes the wrapper as Trojes C-98, shorthand usually read as Criollo 98.

cigars.about: A medium-bodied Honduran blend in large ring gauges, made at Raíces Cubanas with a Trojes wrapper. It launched in 2014 as an extension of the Family Blend to mark founder Alan Rubin's sons turning 18.
cigars.researchNote: Originally called Family Blend The Lineage; the maker's site now lists it simply as Lineage. The wrapper variety is not published. Halfwheel reported the Robusto and 665 discontinued in August 2025.

cigars.about: The third release in Alec Bradley's Experimental Series, using broadleaf tobacco for both the wrapper and the binders. It is a dark, full-bodied cigar made at Tabacos de Oriente in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: The broadleaf wrapper is Connecticut seed grown in Honduras, not grown in Connecticut. Holts and Famous list full strength, Neptune medium. Halfwheel reported the Gran Corona discontinued in March 2025.

cigars.about: The first cigar blended by Alec and Bradley Rubin, the founder's sons the company is named for, made at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras. The line has been discontinued.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Blind Faith by Alec & Bradley. STG discontinued the whole line in March 2025 and the maker now lists it in its Vault. The maker and Holts say medium, while Neptune lists full strength. The wrapper variety is not published; the maker's tasting notes call it Honduran Broadleaf but its blend table and halfwheel say only Honduran from Trojes.

cigars.about: The first regular production line from All Saints Cigars, the company co-founded by former CAO sales head Micky Pegg. It is made at Rocky Patel's TAVICUSA factory with a San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium bodied; halfwheel's review found the strength below medium. Sizes are the four listed since September 2025. It launched with Berkey (5 1/2 x 50), Commandant (6 1/2 x 52), Huge and Coach (7 x 48, now discontinued). A Dedicación Habano version is a separate blend.

cigars.about: The second All Saints line, named for Francis of Assisi and made at Rocky Patel's TAVICUSA factory with a dark Ecuadorian oscuro wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco. The Cigar Authority named it its 2021 Cigar of the Year.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium-full bodied; Neptune calls it full. Sizes are the four listed since September 2025. It launched with Robusto (5 1/2 x 50), Toro (6 1/2 x 52), Huge and Churchill (7 x 48). St. Francis Colorado is a sister blend with an Ecuadorian Habano Colorado wrapper.

cigars.about: The limited edition that launched All Saints Cigars in December 2019, sold in a single 5 x 58 size. It returned in October 2023 in a run of 500 boxes of 23.
cigars.researchNote: Filler is as listed for the 2023 release; the 2019 original was described as all Nicaraguan under the wrapper. Neptune calls it medium strength, while halfwheel's 2023 review found mild to medium strength with a full body.

cigars.about: A series made entirely of perfecto shapes, which Carlos Fuente Jr. revived in 1983 when very few factories still rolled them. The standard version uses a Cameroon wrapper over Dominican binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Every size is a perfecto. Fuente's site and Cigar Aficionado list Signature and Classic at 46 ring; Holt's lists them at 47 and 48. Maduro versions use Connecticut Broadleaf, and Between the Lines is a two-wrapper barber pole.

cigars.about: The 6 inch perfecto in Fuente's Hemingway series, long and slim with a tapered nipple foot. It has a Cameroon wrapper over Dominican binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: One size of the Hemingway line. Fuente's site and Cigar Aficionado list it at 6 x 46; Holt's lists 6 x 47. Fuente also makes it in Maduro and Sun Grown wrappers.

cigars.about: The 7 inch double-tapered perfecto in Fuente's Hemingway series. It has a Cameroon wrapper over Dominican binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: One size of the Hemingway line. Fuente's site and Cigar Aficionado list it at 7 x 46; Holt's lists 7 x 48. Fuente also makes it in Maduro and Sun Grown wrappers.

cigars.about: A short, heavily tapered perfecto in Fuente's Hemingway series that swells from a narrow foot to a 60 ring. Cigar Aficionado ranked it No. 6 on its Top 25 of 2018.
cigars.researchNote: One size of the Hemingway line and a later addition to it. Fuente lists the ring gauge as 46/60, the larger number being the widest point. A Maduro version is also made.

cigars.about: The Hemingway perfectos dressed in a dark Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper instead of Cameroon. The Untold Story size is made only in this maduro version.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's and Neptune rate it medium; Cigar Aficionado rates the Short Story Maduro medium-full. Neptune describes the Short Story Maduro as a rare, limited release. Holt's lists Untold Story at 7 5/8 and Signature and Classic at 47 and 48 ring.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro, aged in Cognac barrels
cigars.about: An OpusX-style Dominican blend finished with a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper aged in Cognac barrels. Fuente created it after Hurricane Georges destroyed OpusX wrapper leaf in 1998, and ships it in small batches around Father's Day and Christmas.
cigars.researchNote: Often called Añejo Reserva. Cigar Aficionado, Holt's and Mike's Cigars all rate it full. The No. 77 Shark starts round at the head and ends in a square press; Fuente lists it as a 48/64 ring, and it joined the line in 2001. Fuente's site gives No. 55 as 5 7/8 inches; halfwheel and Holt's say 6.

cigars.about: The last blend created by Carlos Fuente Sr., made to recall the Cuban-leaf cigars the family rolled decades ago. It pairs an Ecuadorian Havana wrapper with Cuban-seed Dominican binder and filler, and the sizes are named after domino tiles.
cigars.researchNote: Cigar Aficionado and halfwheel list it as its own brand, Casa Cuba, made by Fuente. Fuente's site prints Doble Dos as 6.75 inches but 165 mm; halfwheel measured 6 1/2 x 42. Divine Inspiration (2016) and Doble Dos (2018) were added after the original four sizes.

cigars.about: A Fuente line built around a long-aged Ecuadorian rosado sun grown wrapper taken from the lower primings, over Dominican binder and filler. Carlos Fuente Jr. pitched it as a balanced, smoother blend, and most sizes are named for their ring gauge.
cigars.researchNote: Fuente's site calls it Magnum R Rosado Sungrown. Cigar Aficionado rates it medium-full; Neptune lists medium. Sizes are named for ring gauge except Vitola 44, which Fuente lists at 47 ring.

cigars.about: The Chateau Fuente series in a darker Ecuadorian sun grown wrapper, still wrapped in cedar. It has the same Dominican filler blend as the natural version and adds several belicoso and pyramid shapes.
cigars.researchNote: The sun grown wrapper version of the Chateau Fuente line. Queen B, Cuban Belicoso and King B are made only in Sun Grown. Holt's lists the Cuban Belicoso and Queen B at 52 and 50 ring; Fuente's site says 51 and 52.

cigars.about: The Chateau Fuente series in a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper, still wrapped in cedar. It has the same Dominican filler blend as the natural version.
cigars.researchNote: The maduro wrapper version of the Chateau Fuente line, made in three sizes.

cigars.about: The core Arturo Fuente series, made with aged Dominican tobaccos in classic parejo sizes such as the 8-5-8 and Rothschild. The natural version has a Cameroon wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Specs are for the natural. Most sizes also come in Maduro (Connecticut Broadleaf), and some in Sun Grown (Ecuador), Candela or D'Oro wrappers. Holt's rates the line medium; Neptune lists the naturals as mild.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (mixed long and short filler)
cigars.about: The maduro version of Fuente's budget Curly Head Deluxe lonsdale, with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over a mixed-filler Dominican blend. It is sold in boxes of 25.
cigars.researchNote: This is the maduro wrapper option of the Curly Head Deluxe. It is a mixed-filler (Cuban sandwich) cigar, not long filler.

cigars.about: An affordable Fuente corona made with medium-length Dominican filler. It is also the cigar Fuente packs as It's a Boy and It's a Girl for birth announcements.
cigars.researchNote: Fuente's site spells it Brevas Royales and does not name the wrapper; Neptune and Famous Smoke list Cameroon. Specs are for the natural; a Maduro is also sold. Medium-length filler, not long filler. Neptune rates it mild; Famous Smoke and Holt's list medium.

cigars.line: Don Carlos Eye of the Shark
cigars.about: A Don Carlos in a shortened version of Fuente's Shark shape, with a rounded belicoso head and a box-pressed foot. It came out in 2015 for Carlos Fuente Sr.'s 80th birthday and was Cigar Aficionado's 2017 Cigar of the Year.
cigars.researchNote: One shape in the Don Carlos line, released in batches. Size is disputed: Fuente's site and Holt's say 5 1/4 x 52; halfwheel, Neptune and Cigar Aficionado's 2017 list say 5 3/4 x 52. Cigar Aficionado rated it medium-full in 2017 and medium in 2020; Neptune says full. Fuente has not confirmed the blend.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican Chateau de la Fuente Sun Grown (middle priming)
cigars.about: A milder take on OpusX that uses wrapper from the middle of the plant instead of the top primings. Fuente says the name was inspired by aged tobacco the family lost in a warehouse fire.
cigars.researchNote: Same wrapper plant as regular OpusX but a lower, milder priming. Cigar Aficionado has rated it both medium and medium-full; halfwheel called it medium to medium-full. Cigar Aficionado ranked the Reserva D'Chateau No. 9 of 2025.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Barber pole of Connecticut Broadleaf and Connecticut Shade
cigars.about: A short Hemingway perfecto rolled with two wrappers twisted together in a barber pole stripe, one light and one maduro. It is made in limited quantities.
cigars.researchNote: One size of the Hemingway line. Cigar Aficionado names the two wrappers as Connecticut Broadleaf and Connecticut Shade; Fuente's site only says natural and maduro, and Holt's lists Cameroon. No single wrapper category fits a two-wrapper cigar.

cigars.about: The house cigar of the Casa Fuente shop in the Forum Shops at Caesars Palace, Las Vegas, made by Fuente and sold only there. It was introduced when the store opened in 2005.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only at Casa Fuente in Las Vegas. Fuente has not published the blend: halfwheel reports a Cameroon wrapper grown by the Meerapfel family over a modified OpusX blend. No source gives a strength rating. Sizes are from halfwheel's 2012 list.

cigars.about: A medium-bodied Ashton made by the Fuente family with a reddish Cuban-seed wrapper grown in Ecuador over Dominican binder and filler. Puro Sol refers to the tobaccos all being grown in full sun.
Released in 2014 as the first new Ashton line in close to a decade, blended by Carlito Fuente. It was the first Ashton to use Nicaraguan tobacco, set under an Ecuador Habano Rosado wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Ashton's site and Holt's now list strength as Full. At launch Ashton described it as medium to full.

cigars.about: The flagship Asylum blend from Tom Lazuka and Christian Eiroa, distributed by CLE Cigar Co. It is a Nicaraguan puro with a dark habano wrapper, best known for very large ring gauges such as 7 x 70 and 8 x 80.
cigars.researchNote: Strength varies by source: Neptune's spec says medium, Holt's medium-full, and a halfwheel reviewer found the 7 x 70 mild to medium. Halfwheel and Neptune place production in Nicaragua, while Holt's says Honduras. Asylum writes sizes ring gauge first.

cigars.about: The lighter member of the Asylum 13 family, released in 2016 by Asylum and CLE Cigar Co. It puts an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Honduran binder and filler and is made at Christian Eiroa's El Aladino factory in Danli.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is listed as mild by Neptune, mild-medium by Holt's and medium by Famous, so mild to medium is the safe description.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro from Asylum that debuted at the 2013 IPCPR show, blended by Christian Eiroa and Tom Lazuka as the strongest cigar in the Asylum range. It has a dark wrapper and was sold in ten-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker never named the Nicaraguan factory or the wrapper variety. Neptune lists a maduro-colored Nicaraguan wrapper and marks the line discontinued. Holt's lists the country as Honduras, while Cigar Aficionado and Neptune say Nicaragua.

cigars.about: An all-maduro Asylum line with a Mexican San Andres wrapper, made at Christian Eiroa's El Aladino factory in Honduras. It was announced in 2014 and first shipped in 2015 to TAA retailers before going national.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel reports Nicaraguan fillers while Famous lists Honduran filler. Halfwheel does not name the binder, though Neptune describes a Nicaraguan binder. The name means love of darkness. Famous currently shows only the 7 x 70.

cigars.about: An all-Nicaraguan Asylum blend with a dark Habano Maduro wrapper, released in 2016 as an exclusive for Famous Smoke Shop.
cigars.researchNote: A Famous Smoke Shop exclusive, so most lounges will not stock it. Famous calls it full while Neptune lists it as medium. Neptune says it is rolled in Nicaragua, but the launch report listed the country and factory as not disclosed. Famous also sells a separate Lobotomy Corojo.

cigars.about: A smooth, medium-bodied AVO made at Davidoff's Dominican factory with tobaccos aged about six years under an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. The sizes carry musical names such as Intermezzo and Legato.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's says the Connecticut-seed wrapper is grown in direct sunlight, while Famous and Neptune call it Connecticut Shade.

cigars.about: AVO's maduro, with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over Dominican binder and fillers that include 25-year-old tobacco. It is the first blend Avo Uvezian developed with Hendrik Kelner in the 1980s.
cigars.researchNote: Now sold as AVO Classic Maduro. The original AVO Maduro was discontinued in 2015, came back as a limited release in 2018, and returned to regular production in 2020 with the same blend.

cigars.about: The first AVO Syncro release, launched in 2015 as the brand's first regular line built around Nicaraguan tobacco. It is box-pressed, with a dark Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper and filler that includes leaf from Nicaragua's Ometepe island.
cigars.researchNote: Despite the name it is rolled in the Dominican Republic. Halfwheel lists a Dominican binder, while Neptune lists a Nicaraguan binder and medium strength. Halfwheel describes the Connecticut-seed wrapper as dark.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Yamasa viso, Piloto, San Vicente ligero), Nicaragua (Esteli ligero, Condega viso)
cigars.about: The second AVO Syncro line, shipped in 2016, with an Ecuadorian Habano 2000 wrapper, a Mexican San Andres binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers. Unlike the box-pressed Syncro Nicaragua it is round, and Fogata is Spanish for campfire.
cigars.researchNote: Famous lists it medium-full and Neptune lists it full. It shares a name with Syncro Nicaragua but is a different blend. Rolled in the Dominican Republic.

cigars.filler: Brazil, Dominican Republic, Honduras, Nicaragua, Peru
cigars.about: The third AVO Syncro line, widely released in May 2017 after a small 2016 run. It is box-pressed and blends tobaccos from seven countries, and Ritmo is Spanish for rhythm.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper variety is not published, only that it is Ecuadorian and dark. Famous lists it medium-full and Neptune full. Rolled in the Dominican Republic, and at launch Davidoff said it was a U.S.-only release.

cigars.about: The maduro-wrapped version of the core Baccarat cigar, made in Honduras by Davidoff's Camacho operation. It keeps the line's mild blend and sweetened cap under a darker wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Usually sold simply as Baccarat Maduro. Famous Smoke and Holt's list a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper; Neptune lists a Honduran maduro wrapper. The cap is sweetened.

cigars.about: A green candela-wrapped version of the mild Baccarat cigar, made in Honduras by Davidoff's Camacho operation. It keeps the sweetened cap and has only been sold in small limited runs.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Baccarat Candela or Baccarat The Game Candela in limited runs; Neptune now lists it as discontinued. A Churchill was also made. The cap is sweetened. Binder and filler are not confirmed by a major source; Cigars Direct lists a Mexican binder and Honduran filler, the same as the regular Baccarat.

cigars.factory: Agio Caribbean Tobacco Company (Royal Agio, San Pedro de Macoris)
cigars.about: The flagship Balmoral blend from the Dutch company Royal Agio, built on aged tobaccos under a Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper. It was rolled at Agio's own factory in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: No longer sold in the U.S.: pulled in 2020 after Scandinavian Tobacco Group bought Royal Agio. Strength is unclear: Neptune lists it as full, but halfwheel's review found it smooth and mellow.

cigars.factory: Agio Caribbean Tobacco Company (Royal Agio, San Pedro de Macoris)
cigars.about: A darker version of Balmoral's Añejo XO from Royal Agio, using a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over the line's Dominican, Nicaraguan and Brazilian tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: No longer sold in the U.S.: pulled in 2020 after Scandinavian Tobacco Group bought Royal Agio. Strength is unclear: Neptune lists it as full, while halfwheel's review had it building from light to medium-full with no pepper.

cigars.factory: Agio Caribbean Tobacco Company (Royal Agio, San Pedro de Macoris)
cigars.about: The Connecticut shade version of Balmoral's Añejo XO from Royal Agio, with a U.S.-grown shade wrapper over an Ecuadorian Sumatra binder. It was rolled at Agio's factory in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: No longer sold in the U.S.: pulled in 2020 after Scandinavian Tobacco Group bought Royal Agio. Halfwheel's review put strength between mild and medium; Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.about: The first Balmoral Serie Signaturas release, a collaboration between Royal Agio's Boris Wintermans and Ernesto Perez-Carrillo Jr. It was made at Perez-Carrillo's Tabacalera La Alianza in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: No longer sold in the U.S.: pulled in 2020 after Scandinavian Tobacco Group bought Royal Agio. The wrapper's seed variety is not published. Neptune lists the Gran Toro as 6 x 52.

cigars.about: One of the original Black Label Trading Co. core blends from James Brown, a Nicaraguan cigar under an Ecuadorian Habano Rosado wrapper. It is made at the company's own Oveja Negra factory in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium-plus; some retailers list it as medium. The maker also lists a 7 x 48 size.

cigars.about: One of the original Black Label Trading Co. core blends from James Brown, with an Ecuadorian sun grown wrapper over a Honduran binder and Nicaraguan filler. It is made at the company's Oveja Negra factory in Estelí.

One of the original Black Label Trading Co. core blends from James Brown, with an Ecuadorian Corojo wrapper over a Honduran binder and Nicaraguan filler. It is made at the company's Oveja Negra factory in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium; Neptune lists it as mild.

cigars.about: The strongest of the original Black Label Trading Co. core blends from James Brown, with an Ecuadorian maduro wrapper over Honduran and Nicaraguan tobaccos. It is made at the company's Oveja Negra factory in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: The maker also lists a 6.5 x 42 size. Neptune lists the wrapper as Ecuadorian Habano; the maker and halfwheel say Ecuadorian Maduro.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua, United States (Connecticut Broadleaf, Pennsylvania Broadleaf)
cigars.about: A limited Black Label Trading Co. blend that returns in a new vintage most years, built around broadleaf fillers under an Ecuadorian maduro wrapper. It is made at the Oveja Negra factory in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: Released in dated yearly batches. The 2026 edition is a barber pole that adds a Connecticut broadleaf wrapper to the usual Ecuadorian maduro. Neptune lists it as full; halfwheel's review of the 2026 Lancero put strength at medium to medium-full.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Maduro with Connecticut shade accents
cigars.about: One of the three debut blends from Black Works Studio, James Brown's small-batch brand at the Oveja Negra factory. It is a Nicaraguan cigar in an Ecuadorian maduro wrapper, known for its closed foot and a striped cap made with a lighter leaf.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium-plus and at launch said it sits between medium-full and full; some retailers list medium. Killer Bee Connecticut is a separate blend.

cigars.about: One of the three debut blends from Black Works Studio, James Brown's small-batch brand at the Oveja Negra factory. It is a box-pressed Nicaraguan cigar in an Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro wrapper with a closed foot.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's site lists it as medium, but at launch James Brown described it as between medium-full and full.

cigars.about: One of the three debut blends from Black Works Studio, James Brown's small-batch brand at the Oveja Negra factory. It is a Nicaraguan cigar in an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper that started as a small, inexpensive petite panatela.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium-plus; some retailers list it as medium. Rorschach Sumatra is a separate version with a Sumatra wrapper.

cigars.about: A core line from Jonas Santana's Blackbird Cigar Co., made at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic. It has a dark Mexican San Andrés wrapper and is one of the stronger cigars in the range.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium to full; some retailers list medium. A limited 6 x 52 box-pressed toro also exists.

cigars.about: A core line from Jonas Santana's Blackbird Cigar Co., made at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic. It is a creamy, aromatic cigar with a Sumatra wrapper and blue bands.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not say where the Sumatra wrapper is grown. The maker calls it mild to medium; some retailers list mild.

cigars.about: A core line from Jonas Santana's Blackbird Cigar Co., made at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic. It pairs a Brazilian wrapper with an Indonesian binder and Dominican filler, and is one of the fuller cigars in the range.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not name the Brazilian wrapper variety. The maker calls it medium to full; some retailers list medium.

cigars.about: A mild core line from Jonas Santana's Blackbird Cigar Co., made at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic. It has a Sumatra wrapper and some U.S. tobacco in the filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not say where the Sumatra wrapper is grown. The maker now lists only the Robusto; it launched with a 6 x 54 Gran Toro too, and some retailers carry a 6 x 52 Toro.

cigars.about: The non-Cuban Bolivar line sold in the U.S. by Scandinavian Tobacco Group's Forged Cigar Co., made in Honduras. It is a value-priced cigar with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over a Connecticut broadleaf binder.
cigars.researchNote: This is the non-Cuban Bolivar. Halfwheel lists the Churchill at 7 1/2 inches; Famous Smoke and Neptune list 7 1/4. Bolivar Cofradia Oscuro is a separate blend with a Connecticut broadleaf wrapper.

cigars.about: Christian Eiroa's Connecticut-wrapped core line, launched in 2012. An Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper sits over Honduran binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Blend sources disagree: Cigar Coop, Neptune and halfwheel (2024) give Honduran binder and filler, but halfwheel in 2018 listed Honduran, Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler, and Mike's describes a Corojo binder with Peruvian Pelo de Oro in the filler. Strength: Mike's and Cigar Coop say mild to medium, Neptune says Medium.

cigars.about: A Honduran puro with a Honduran Corojo wrapper from Christian Eiroa, formerly of Camacho. It has been part of the C.L.E. core line since the brand launched in 2012.
cigars.researchNote: Cigar Aficionado and Cigar Coop list it as a Honduran puro; halfwheel in 2018 listed fillers from Honduras, Nicaragua and Peru, but in 2024 said Honduran binder and filler. Strength: Cigar Aficionado, Cigar Coop and Mike's say Medium-Full, Neptune lists Medium. No source checked names the current factory.

cigars.about: The Habano-wrapped member of Christian Eiroa's C.L.E. core line, made in Honduras. It uses a Honduran Habano wrapper over Honduran binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is disputed: Neptune's spec lists Medium (used here) though its description says medium to full-bodied, and Cigar Aficionado lists Medium-Full. Filler is disputed: Neptune, Cigar Coop and halfwheel (2024) describe an all-Honduran blend, but Cigar Aficionado and halfwheel in 2018 listed Honduras, Peru and Nicaragua.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Connecticut Broadleaf maduro from Christian Eiroa, launched in 2016 alongside Chele as the first C.L.E. cigars rolled in Nicaragua. It contains no Honduran tobacco, and the 50x5 scored 92 points in Cigar Aficionado.
cigars.researchNote: Hard to find: off the C.L.E. price list since March 5, 2025. Per halfwheel it is not discontinued but made only when a retailer orders five boxes of a size, with about a two month wait. The factory is reported, not official: halfwheel says NACSA, but Christian Eiroa told Cigar Aficionado the company was not disclosing it.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Ecuadorian Connecticut cigar from Christian Eiroa, launched in 2016 alongside Prieto as the first C.L.E. cigars rolled in Nicaragua. The name is Spanish slang for a light-skinned person, a nod to the pale wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is disputed, so quote it with care: the company and Mike's say medium to full (used here), Neptune says Medium and The Cigar Authority Mild-Medium. Off the price list since March 5, 2025 but not discontinued; made only when a retailer orders five boxes of a size. The factory is reported by halfwheel, not official.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Honduran puro released in late 2020 to mark Christian Eiroa's 25 years in the cigar business, not the company's age. The blend includes Authentic Corojo tobacco and is the same across all sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is listed only as Honduran: sources say the blend uses Authentic Corojo but not which leaf is the wrapper. Factory name differs: halfwheel lists The CLE Factory, Cigar Coop calls it El Aladino. The 11/18 began as a 2020 TAA exclusive and is now sold alongside the other sizes.

cigars.about: A box-pressed San Andrés maduro from Christian Eiroa that began as a 2016 TAA exclusive and joined the regular C.L.E. lineup in 2017. Unlike most C.L.E. blends, it adds Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler to the Honduran tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is disputed and the company published none: halfwheel and Cigar Coop say Medium (used here), The Cigar Authority and GoBourbon medium-plus to full. The Cigar Authority lists Nicaragua as origin, which the other sources show is an error. Not discontinued, but made only when a retailer orders five boxes of a size.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (ligero from Estelí, Condega and Jalapa)
cigars.about: The strongest regular Cain blend, made by Oliva in Nicaragua and blended by Sam Leccia. It is about 82 percent ligero, with a heavier share of Estelí ligero than the original Cain.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper is disputed: Oliva, halfwheel and retailers say Nicaraguan (Habano), but Cigar Aficionado's rating page lists Ecuador. Strength: Neptune and Mike's list Full, Cigar Aficionado lists Medium-Full. Oliva's current website does not list Cain, but retailers still stock it.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (ligero from Estelí, Condega and Jalapa)
cigars.about: The original Cain, introduced by Oliva in 2009 with Sam Leccia, who also fronted Oliva's Nub brand. It is a Nicaraguan puro billed as a straight ligero cigar, with about 82 percent ligero in the filler.
cigars.researchNote: Strength: Neptune and Mike's list Full; Cigar Aficionado's tasting note calls it medium to full bodied. The blend is about 82 percent ligero rather than 100 percent so that it burns properly. Oliva's current website does not list Cain, but retailers still stock it.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Oliva's ligero-heavy Cain, released with the Habano in 2009 and blended by Sam Leccia. A near-black Mexican maduro wrapper covers Nicaraguan ligero binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper: Cigar Aficionado and Mike's list Mexico and Neptune specifies Mexican San Andrés, but a 2009 Stogie Review write-up listed a Brazilian maduro. Strength is disputed: Neptune and Mike's list Full (used here), while Cigar Aficionado lists Medium. Oliva's current website does not list Cain, but retailers still stock it.

cigars.about: The milder Cain blend, introduced by Oliva in spring 2011 as the fourth Cain line. Its ligero comes only from Nicaragua's Jalapa Valley, which makes it smoother than the other Cain cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper unsettled: do not quote one without checking the box or the Oliva rep. Cigar Coop, Neptune and halfwheel reviews say Nicaraguan (Habano); Cigar Aficionado says Ecuador and a 2011 halfwheel piece Ecuadorian Sumatra. Strength: the maker says medium (used here), Cigar Aficionado and Cigar Coop medium to full, Neptune Full.

cigars.about: Introduced in 2015 and made in Honduras at the factory that rolls Camacho, unlike Caldwell's Dominican core lines. The original blend puts an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Honduran and Dominican tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: The original blend is now sold as Blind Man's Bluff Habano to tell it apart from the Connecticut, Maduro and Nicaragua versions. halfwheel and Neptune say it is made in Honduras at the factory that rolls Camacho; Smokingpipes lists the country as Dominican Republic.

cigars.about: The Connecticut Shade version of Blind Man's Bluff, shown in 2016 and shipped in 2017. It keeps the original binder and filler under an Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Caldwell rates it 3 of 5 for strength; Neptune lists it as Mild. halfwheel and Neptune say it is made in Honduras. It launched in five sizes; Caldwell now lists three.

cigars.about: The maduro extension of Blind Man's Bluff, released in 2019. It is a different blend from the other two, with a Pennsylvania Broadleaf wrapper over a Sumatran binder and Dominican filler.
cigars.researchNote: Caldwell rates it 4 of 5 for strength; Neptune calls it medium. Most sources say it is rolled at Tabacalera William Ventura in the Dominican Republic, but a 2024 halfwheel piece placed it at the Diadema factory in Honduras with the other Blind Man's Bluff blends.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Corojo Ligero, Negrito Viso, HVA 20/20)
cigars.about: A Dominican puro and one of Caldwell's three original 2014 lines. It is built around an aged Dominican Negrito wrapper over a Corojo binder.
cigars.researchNote: Caldwell rates it 3 of 5 for strength, but Neptune lists it as Full and Atlantic as Medium-Full. Caldwell's own spec sheet tags the Negrito wrapper as Maduro, while Neptune lists the wrapper color as Natural.

cigars.about: A 2016 offshoot of Long Live the King with a habano wrapper and band artwork by the Italian artist PixelPancho. The original line ended after the 2022 factory fire and the name has since returned only as small limited editions.
cigars.researchNote: Caldwell only disclosed the habano wrapper; Neptune lists a Dominican binder with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. The limited Crafted & Curated editions Savages Mal Caída (2025) and Savages Malpensante (2026) are based on it but are not the same blend.

cigars.about: A limited Caldwell line that debuted in 2016 as a collaboration with Ernesto Perez-Carrillo and the follow-up to The Last Tsar. It has come back in several small runs, each told apart by the color of its second band.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is secret; Caldwell says only that it is always a Habano. The 2016 original (green band) was rolled at E.P. Carrillo's Tabacalera La Alianza in different sizes. The 2022 Yellow Label, whose sizes are listed here, is a different blend from an undisclosed Dominican factory.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Eastern Standard, released in 2016. It used the Eastern Standard filler under the dark hybrid Connecticut and Arapiraca wrapper from The Last Tsar.
cigars.researchNote: Caldwell discontinued it after the September 2022 fire at Tabacalera William Ventura. halfwheel and Atlantic call it Medium-Full; Neptune calls it Medium. The country where the wrapper is grown is not published.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Habano (origin undisclosed); also sold in a Maduro version
cigars.about: A short Caldwell cigar that began in 2014 as an event-only release made with tobacco left over from the main lines. It returned in 2025 as a regular release sold in paper five-packs, in Habano and Maduro wrappers.
cigars.researchNote: The current blend and factory are undisclosed. The 2014 original was a 4 x 44 with a Dominican Corojo wrapper, rolled at Tabacalera William Ventura. Caldwell's site rates it 3 of 5 and calls it medium bodied; Smokingpipes rates the Habano 2 of 5 and Atlantic lists Medium.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A box-pressed cigar made as a three-way collaboration between Robert Caldwell, Matt Booth of Room101 and A.J. Fernandez, released in 2017 and rolled at Fernandez's factory in Nicaragua. It was first shown as The Truth and renamed over a trademark conflict.
cigars.researchNote: Caldwell's own site lists a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper, but halfwheel and Neptune described the 2017 release as a Nicaraguan puro, so check before quoting the wrapper. Neptune says the line is discontinued. Connecticut (2018) and Habano (2019) versions followed.

cigars.filler: United States (Connecticut Broadleaf Ligero), Dominican Republic (Corojo 97), Nicaragua (Estelí, Jalapa)
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut-grown Habano (stalk cut and sun cured)
cigars.about: A collaboration between Caldwell and Drew Estate, made at Drew Estate in Nicaragua under master blender Willy Herrera. It was shown in 2016 and shipped in March 2017, and uses the same wrapper varietal as Liga Privada T52.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune reports the line has been discontinued, and Caldwell no longer lists it on its site.

cigars.about: Camacho's flagship line, a Honduran puro made entirely from Corojo tobacco grown in the Jamastran Valley. It launched in 2000 under the Eiroa family and is now made by Davidoff's Camacho factory in Danli.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke and Holt's list it Full; Neptune lists it Medium. The blend was tweaked in the 2013 rebrand but stayed an all-Corojo Honduran puro.

cigars.about: Camacho's milder offering, introduced in mid-2009 with an Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper over a Honduran Corojo binder. It was built for smokers who want something lighter than the brand's usual full-strength cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's and Neptune list it Medium; Famous Smoke lists it Mild-Medium. Camacho itself called it a medium-bodied smoke.

cigars.about: A medium-strength Camacho with a Honduran-grown Criollo wrapper over a Corojo binder. It was sold as Camacho Havana before the 2013 rebrand and was cut from the portfolio in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Called Camacho Havana until the 2013 rebrand, when it was renamed Criollo and reblended. Davidoff discontinued it in October 2022. Holt's lists the filler as Nicaraguan and Honduran; Neptune lists Honduran and Dominican.

cigars.filler: Honduras, Dominican Republic (Pelo de Oro ligero)
cigars.about: A 2014 addition to Camacho's core range built around an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper and a Brazilian Mata Fina binder. The filler pairs high-priming Honduran leaf with Dominican Pelo de Oro ligero.
cigars.researchNote: Camacho's launch release called it medium-to-full; Neptune lists it Full.

cigars.about: A Camacho made with maduro leaf in every part of the cigar: wrapper, binder and filler. It is rolled in Honduras and is one of the brand's darkest and heaviest core lines.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's and Neptune list it Full; Famous Smoke lists it Medium-Full.

cigars.about: Released in September 2023, this is the first Camacho to use a Honduran-grown broadleaf wrapper. The binder is Honduran and the filler is Honduran and Dominican.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium intensity; Famous Smoke and Holt's list it Medium-Full. The wrapper is broadleaf grown in Honduras, not Connecticut. Binder and filler varietals are not disclosed.

cigars.filler: United States (Broadleaf, Pennsylvania maduro), Honduras (barrel-aged Corojo)
cigars.about: Launched in 2015 as the first Camacho made in the Dominican Republic, with mostly American tobacco. One Honduran Corojo filler leaf is aged for five months in used bourbon barrels.
cigars.researchNote: Davidoff discontinued the line in October 2022. Only one filler leaf is barrel-aged, not the whole blend. Neptune lists it Full; Holt's lists it Medium-Full.

cigars.about: A 2020 core line meant to show Nicaraguan flavor, though it is rolled in Honduras and only part of the filler is Nicaraguan. The wrapper is from Ecuador and the binder from Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Despite the name it is made in Honduras with an Ecuadorian wrapper; the wrapper varietal is not published. Famous Smoke and Holt's list it Medium-Full; Neptune lists it Full. halfwheel's review found it just under medium.

cigars.about: A Honduran puro from Camacho made only from high-priming Corojo leaves. The regular line ended in 2015 and it returned in 2017 as the limited Diploma Special Selection, sold in individual coffins.
cigars.researchNote: Today it is sold as the limited Diploma Special Selection. The 2013 to 2015 version used an Ecuadorian Habana 2000 wrapper instead of Corojo. halfwheel found it medium-full; Neptune lists it Full.

cigars.about: A Honduran puro made with tobacco from a single 15-acre plot on the Coyolar farm. First released in 2005, it was dropped in 2013, brought back in 2018 with Criollo leaf, and discontinued again in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: The 2018 version uses Criollo tobacco rather than Camacho's usual Corojo. Davidoff discontinued it in October 2022.

cigars.about: Part of the CAO World series, built around Habano-seed tobacco grown in the Benevento region of southern Italy. A Honduran wrapper and binder cover fillers from Italy, Nicaragua and Peru.
cigars.researchNote: Cigar Aficionado's 2024 rating lists it as made in Nicaragua; Holt's and Famous Smoke still list Honduras, where it was originally rolled. The maker's spec sheet says medium, though its own description calls it full-bodied.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut Broadleaf with a Connecticut Shade pinstripe
cigars.about: A barber-pole cigar that pairs two American-grown wrappers, dark Connecticut Broadleaf with a stripe of Connecticut Shade. The filler is all ligero from four countries.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrappers, not one: mostly Broadleaf with a Shade pinstripe. Cigar Aficionado's 2022 rating lists Nicaragua as the country; Holt's lists Honduras. The maker's spec sheet says medium while its description says full-bodied.

cigars.about: A World series blend built around Ica Mazinga, a Cuban-seed tobacco grown in the mountains of Colombia. CAO presents it as the first cigar to feature Colombian leaf prominently.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is Honduran, not Colombian; the Colombian leaf is in the filler. An earlier, different CAO Colombia from 2008 was made in Honduras. The Vallenato size was discontinued in March 2025. Retailers tend to call it medium.

cigars.about: The name means maduro times two: a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper over a Brazilian maduro binder. The filler draws on four countries.
cigars.researchNote: Country left blank because sources split: Cigar Aficionado (2009) and Neptune say Honduras, Holt's and Famous Smoke say Nicaragua. Check the box before quoting it.

cigars.about: CAO's original cigar blend, later renamed Black. It has an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper and has long been sold through only a few retailers rather than in general distribution.
cigars.researchNote: Despite the name it is a light Connecticut-wrapped cigar, not a maduro. It is not on CAO's own site and is sold only by select retailers. Honduras and 1995 come from Cigar Aficionado's account of the original C.A.O. line it descends from, so check the box before quoting the country.

cigars.about: A sweet African Cameroon wrapper over an all-Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is one of the oldest CAO lines and is known for its balance.
cigars.researchNote: Originally sold as CAO L'Anniversaire Cameroon, and some shops still use that name. The Churchill size was discontinued in November 2024. Neptune rates it medium; the maker says mellow to medium.

cigars.about: A Connecticut Broadleaf maduro introduced in 1998 as L'Anniversaire Maduro for CAO's 30th anniversary. The wrapper is heat-fermented for about three months to darken it.
cigars.researchNote: Discontinued by STG in July 2024, though it still appears on CAO's site and remaining stock may be on shelves. Originally named CAO L'Anniversaire Maduro. Neptune rates it medium; the maker says medium to full.

cigars.about: A value-priced line released in 2009 that revived the name of an early 1900s Cuban brand. An Ecuadorian Habano wrapper sits over a Cameroon binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: No longer on CAO's site. Neptune says the maker discontinued it (2020) and Holt's shows every size sold out. STG's Cigar World rates it medium; Cigar Aficionado and Holt's say medium-full.

cigars.about: The maduro version of La Traviata, added in 2010. It keeps the Cameroon binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler and swaps the Habano wrapper for Connecticut Broadleaf.
cigars.researchNote: No longer on CAO's site and sold out at Neptune and Holt's. The Animado and Favorito maduro sizes were discontinued in January 2014 and the Luminoso in 2017, leaving Intrepido, Radiante and Divino. STG's Cigar World rates it medium; Cigar Aficionado and Holt's say medium-full.

cigars.about: A medium-bodied everyday cigar with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. Unusually for a non-flavored CAO, it was rolled in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Discontinued by STG in November 2024. It still appears on CAO's site and leftover stock may be around.

cigars.about: CAO's tribute to the country where most of its cigars are made, with filler from three Nicaraguan growing regions. The wrapper and binder are Honduran, from the Jamastran valley.
cigars.researchNote: Not a Nicaraguan puro: the wrapper and binder are Honduran. Discontinued by STG in July 2024, though it still appears on CAO's site. Neptune calls it medium; the maker says medium to full.

cigars.filler: Honduras (Jamastran, La Entrada), Nicaragua (Estelí), Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano)
cigars.about: A Connecticut Broadleaf cigar themed on dominoes and dice, with sizes named after domino games. It was made in Nicaragua with filler from three countries.
cigars.researchNote: STG discontinued the Matador in August 2025 and the other three sizes in June 2026, so the whole line is now being sold off.

cigars.about: The name stands for Brazil times three: Brazilian leaf is used in the wrapper, the binder and the filler. It followed the success of Brazilia and Amazon Basin.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the Toro as 6 x 52; halfwheel listed it as 6 x 54 at launch.

cigars.filler: Brazil (Bragança and rope-fermented Arapiraca), Honduras, Nicaragua
cigars.about: The second cigar in the CAO Amazon trilogy, after Amazon Basin. Its name means smoke on a rope, after Brazilian Arapiraca tobacco that is twisted into ropes to ferment.
cigars.researchNote: Also written Amazon Fuma Em Corda. Halfwheel calls the wrapper Honduran Corojo; STG's Cigar World calls it Honduran Colorado Oscuro. The 2017 run was limited. A 6 x 52 Toro came back in late 2025 only inside the CAO Outpost Sampler Vol. 2.

cigars.about: CAO's first cigar with a Mexican wrapper, named for the main square of a Mexican city. It began as a limited 6 x 60 in 2018 and became a regular line in 2021.
cigars.researchNote: Binder sources disagree: halfwheel and the maker's own description say Cameroon (African), but the maker's spec table says Nicaraguan. Halfwheel reported the Robusto discontinued in March 2025, yet it is still on CAO's site.

cigars.about: An infused cigar from the CAO Flavours range: a mild Dominican blend under a Cameroon wrapper, flavored with bourbon vanilla and peach.
cigars.researchNote: Part of CAO Flavours, the brand's infused range, so it is a flavored cigar. Shops usually list it as CAO Flavours Moontrance. The flavor words describe the infusion, not the tobacco.

cigars.about: An infused cigar from the CAO Flavours range: a mild Dominican blend under a Cameroon wrapper, flavored with Madagascar vanilla.
cigars.researchNote: Part of CAO Flavours, the brand's infused range, so it is a flavored cigar. Shops usually list it as CAO Flavours Bella Vanilla.

cigars.about: An infused cigar from the CAO Flavours range: a mild Dominican blend under a Cameroon wrapper, flavored with Irish whiskey, coconut milk, cream and white chocolate.
cigars.researchNote: Part of CAO Flavours, the brand's infused range, so it is a flavored cigar. Shops usually list it as CAO Flavours Eileen's Dream. The flavor words describe the infusion, not the tobacco.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro created by Manuel Quesada with Nestor Plasencia and released in 2008. Its Robusto was named Cigar Aficionado's Cigar of the Year for 2008.
cigars.researchNote: Owned by Quesada Cigars and rolled by Plasencia in Esteli, Nicaragua. Famous Smoke lists the wrapper leaf as Habano; the line is named for the wrapper's colorado shade.

cigars.about: The darker, fuller follow-up to Casa Magna Colorado, made by Manuel Quesada with Nestor Plasencia. It uses a dark Honduran wrapper and binder over Nicaraguan and Honduran filler.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on where it is rolled: Famous Smoke and Mike's Cigars list Honduras, while Neptune's product pages and halfwheel put Casa Magna production at Plasencia in Nicaragua. Check the box before quoting the country. Neptune's product pages also list a Nicaraguan binder.

cigars.about: A 2021 Casa Magna whose name is short for liga fuerte, or strong blend. Unlike the original Casa Magna it is rolled at Quesada's own factory in the Dominican Republic, with an Ecuadorian sun grown Corojo wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Made in the Dominican Republic by Quesada, not in Nicaragua by Plasencia like the original Casa Magna. The 6 x 54 box press began as a 2023 TAA exclusive and became a regular size in 2024.

cigars.factory: Nueva Matacapan de Tabacos S.A. de C.V.
cigars.about: Named for the year the Turrent family began growing tobacco in Mexico, and built almost entirely from the family's own San Andrés leaf. It debuted in late 2017 as a single 6 1/2 x 54 toro.
cigars.researchNote: Blend shown is the original 2017 cigar, renamed 1880 Edición Limitada in 2020. Since then 1880 is a series (Claro, Colorado, Oscuro, Maduro, later Doble Claro, Rosado, Doble Maduro), each with its own Mexican wrapper. In 2023 the maker cut its lines to one 5 1/4 x 55 robusto.

cigars.filler: Mexico (San Andrés Criollo, San Andrés Negro), Nicaragua
cigars.factory: Nueva Matacapan de Tabacos S.A. de C.V.
cigars.about: Named for the birth year of Alejandro Turrent's father and released in 2016. It pairs the family's Mexican San Andrés wrapper and binder with Mexican and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium to full bodied and spicy, with more complexity than Serie 1901. halfwheel's trade show report lists the wrapper as San Andrés Maduro. In 2023 Casa Turrent said it had cut its lines to a single 5 1/4 x 55 robusto and turned its focus to Europe, so U.S. stock may be scarce.

cigars.filler: Mexico (San Andrés Criollo and Negro), Nicaragua
cigars.factory: Nueva Matacapan de Tabacos S.A. de C.V.
cigars.about: The first Casa Turrent line, named for the birth year of Alejandro Turrent's grandfather. It is a box-pressed Mexican cigar with a San Andrés maduro wrapper and some Nicaraguan leaf in the binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: It reached the U.S. in 2015 after about two years on sale abroad. Not a Mexican puro: it has a double binder with Nicaraguan leaf. In 2023 Casa Turrent said it had cut its lines back to a single 5 1/4 x 55 robusto and turned its focus to Europe, so U.S. stock may be scarce.

cigars.filler: Varies by blend: Mexico, Nicaragua, Dominican Republic
cigars.factory: Nueva Matacapan de Tabacos S.A. de C.V.
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican-grown, different on each of the four blends
cigars.about: A set of four blends named for places in the Turrent family's history: Cuba, Miami, Nicaragua and Mexico. Each comes in one 5 1/2 x 54 size and shows off a different Mexican-grown wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Four separate blends, so ask which one. Wrappers: Miami is Mexican sun grown Connecticut, Cuba is Mexican Criollo, Nicaragua and Mexico use San Andrés leaf. Shown in Europe in 2018, U.S. in 2019. In 2023 Casa Turrent said it had cut its lines back to a single 5 1/4 x 55 robusto and turned its focus to Europe, so U.S. stock may be scarce.

cigars.about: The first line from Swiss-owned Cavalier Genève, made in Danli, Honduras. Like the brand's other cigars it carries a diamond of edible 24-karat gold leaf on the wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: It reached U.S. stores in 2016. The gold diamond on the wrapper is meant to be smoked through. A Salomones and a Lancero are released in limited runs.

cigars.about: Introduced in 2017 as a tribute to Tabak Rhein, a Geneva tobacconist the company had bought. It has a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler and carries the brand's edible gold diamond.
cigars.researchNote: Different blend from the earlier event-only Black Series, which used a Brazilian binder. Most sizes are box pressed; the Corona and Petit N2 are round. A Salomones and a Lancero are limited sizes. halfwheel's review found it milder than medium.

cigars.about: A 2021 line made entirely of Nicaraguan tobacco but rolled at Cavalier's factory in Honduras. It is named for its wrapper, a viso-priming leaf from Jalapa that is normally used as filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it 4 out of 5 for strength, but halfwheel found it below medium and Neptune lists it Medium. All Nicaraguan tobacco, rolled in Honduras. The wrapper's seed variety is not published.

cigars.about: The lower-priced, everyday line in General Cigar's Cohiba range, introduced in 2017. It leans on Honduran tobacco for both wrapper and binder and is rolled in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers list it as medium. The maker's own description calls it medium to full bodied, while its rating scale shows medium. Famous Smoke describes the wrapper and binder as Honduran Olancho San Agustin.

cigars.about: The first Cohiba from General Cigar to be blended and rolled in Nicaragua, released in 2014. It uses Nicaraguan binder and filler from Estelí and Jalapa under a Colorado Oscuro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Not a Nicaraguan puro: halfwheel says the wrapper is Honduran, from Jamastran, and Famous Smoke lists it as Honduran Corojo. Famous and Neptune call it full, Holt's medium-full, and the maker rates the body medium. Sizes have changed since the 2014 launch.

cigars.about: Released in 2020 as the fullest-bodied Cohiba from General Cigar and the first one made in Honduras. Its tobaccos are aged five to six years under a Nicaraguan Jalapa wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it strong and full-bodied and Neptune lists it as full, but Famous Smoke lists medium. Halfwheel's filler list has only Honduras and Nicaragua, while the maker also names Dominican leaf. The 5 1/2 x 54 was first sold under the name Royale.

cigars.about: An all-Dominican Cohiba from General Cigar, made only from the company's own Dominican tobaccos aged in tercios and charred wooden barrels. It has been retired from the lineup.
cigars.researchNote: General Cigar's Cigar World site marks this line as retired, and it is no longer on cohiba.com. The maker does not name the wrapper variety beyond Dominican.

cigars.about: Launched in 2023 as the only box-pressed line in General Cigar's Cohiba range and the first with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper. It is made in Nicaragua with Honduran and Nicaraguan tobaccos and no Dominican leaf.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on strength: the maker's launch release said medium to full bodied and cohiba.com now says medium-bodied, while Famous Smoke and Neptune list it as full.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98, Vuelta Abajo seed), Mexico (San Andrés)
cigars.about: The highest-priced limited series in General Cigar's Cohiba range, first released in 2018. Each edition is a different blend in a single size, sold in elaborate boxes of 10 at around 90 to 150 dollars a cigar.
cigars.researchNote: The blend and size change with every edition (2018, 2019, 2021, 2022 and the latest). Details here are for the latest, shipped June 2025: halfwheel calls it Spectre 2024, the maker's sites label it 2025. Earlier editions used Ecuadorian Sumatra, Nicaraguan Jalapa, Ecuadorian Habano and Brazilian wrappers.

cigars.binder: USA (Broadleaf, aged in Weller Antique 107 bourbon barrels)
cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano), Honduras (Jamastran, La Entrada, Olancho San Agustin), Nicaragua (Estelí)
cigars.about: An annual limited collaboration between General Cigar's Cohiba and Weller bourbon, started in 2021. Since 2022 the broadleaf binder has been aged in used Weller bourbon barrels, and the cigars come in tubes in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: The blend changes each year; details here are the 2025 edition. The 2021 original was a 5 1/2 x 50 robusto with a Honduran wrapper, and 2023 used a Nicaraguan Jalapa wrapper. Retailers list it as full, but the maker rates the body medium-full and halfwheel's reviewer found the strength about medium.

cigars.about: The Miami-made line from Cornelius & Anthony, the Bailey family's Virginia cigar company, rolled at El Titan de Bronze. It is named for Cornelius Bailey, who started the family tobacco business in 1866.
cigars.researchNote: The brand appears to be defunct: halfwheel wrote in 2026 that it effectively ended around 2019 after the owners' cigarette company was sold, so any stock is old. The launch announcement listed only Nicaraguan filler; later sources add Dominican.

cigars.about: A Brazilian-wrapped blend from Cornelius & Anthony, made at Erik Espinosa's La Zona factory in Estelí. It is a tribute to Mac Bailey, father of company owner Steven Bailey.
cigars.researchNote: The maker called it medium to full bodied; Neptune lists it as medium. The type of Brazilian wrapper leaf was not published. The brand appears to be defunct since about 2019, per halfwheel.

cigars.about: A full-strength Cornelius & Anthony line made at La Zona in Estelí with Nicaraguan binder and filler under an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. Its box art shows the patent drawing for the Bailey machine gun.
cigars.researchNote: The maker billed it as a rich and flavorful powerhouse, and Cigar Coop rated both strength and body full. The brand appears to be defunct since about 2019, per halfwheel.

cigars.about: The first cigar Cornelius & Anthony showed, in 2015, then relaunched in 2016 with a new blend made at La Zona in Estelí. The relaunched version has an Ecuadorian Rosado wrapper over Nicaraguan and Dominican tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: Details are for the 2016 relaunch; the 2015 original was a different blend made by PDR Cigars in the Dominican Republic. Cigar Aficionado lists it as medium, while halfwheel and Cigar Coop found it medium to medium-full. Cigar Coop lists the Robusto as 5 x 50. The brand appears to be defunct since about 2019.

cigars.about: The first Crowned Heads line, launched in late 2011 by former CAO staff and named after a Kings of Leon song. It is made for them by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo Jr. in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Corona Gorda, Robusto and Sublime are the sizes retailers stock today; Piramide and Seleccion No.5 are older regular sizes that are harder to find. Separate Four Kicks Maduro and Capa Especial lines use different wrappers.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Four Kicks, released in 2017. It keeps the Nicaraguan binder and filler of the original and swaps the Ecuadorian wrapper for a dark Connecticut-grown Habano leaf.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is Connecticut Habano, not Connecticut Broadleaf. A separate Famous Smoke Shop exclusive, Four Kicks Black Belt Buckle, is the one that uses broadleaf.

cigars.about: A San Andres wrapped Nicaraguan cigar made for Crowned Heads by the Garcia family at My Father Cigars. The name and the size names come from Johnny Cash's version of Cocaine Blues on At Folsom Prison.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers disagree on strength: Holt's says medium-full, Neptune says full. New packaging arrived in late 2025 with boxes of 21, and the .44S (5 1/8 x 44) and LBV (6 1/2 x 46) sizes were discontinued, though some stores still have LBV.

cigars.about: An annual limited edition made at My Father Cigars since 2014, released as a tribute to people close to the company who have died. Every year is a different blend in three or four sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The blend and sizes change every year, so check the year on the band. The wrapper, sizes and flavors here are the 2025 release. The related Las Calaveras Decimo (2024, back in 2026) uses an Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco.

cigars.about: A box-pressed broadleaf cigar from 2016, made by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo Jr. and named after the French chef Marie-Antoine Careme. Crowned Heads built the blend around the idea of a chocolate souffle.
cigars.researchNote: The Belicosos Finos (5 1/2 x 52, not box-pressed) and Pastelitos (4 x 54) are limited editions, not regular sizes. Halfwheel lists the Cosacos as both 5 3/8 and 5 1/2 inches.

cigars.about: Released in 2020 and made at Eradio Pichardo's factory in Esteli. The name means a thousand days, roughly the three years Crowned Heads spent working on the blend.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers disagree on strength: Neptune says medium, Holt's says medium-full. Mil Dias Maduro is a separate line with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. New packaging and boxes of 21 arrived in 2025 with no blend change.

cigars.about: The second Crowned Heads line, from 2012, made by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo Jr. It is named after the English house where Led Zeppelin recorded When the Levee Breaks.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's rates it medium; halfwheel found it starting mild-medium and building past medium. Black Dog (Connecticut Habano maduro) and Chamuco (San Andres) are darker spin-offs, not this blend. Holt's and Neptune both showed it sold out in October 2026, and whether it is still made is not confirmed.

cigars.about: A 2015 regular production line made at My Father Cigars, created as the follow-up to the sold-out Las Calaveras 2014. It pairs a dark Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro wrapper with Nicaraguan tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's says medium-full, Neptune says full. Retailers often call it the Las Calaveras 2014 blend; halfwheel says it is based on that cigar but is not the exact same blend. New packaging was shown in 2025.

cigars.about: A lower-priced San Andres cigar made at Tabacalera Pichardo in Esteli, built as a value alternative to Jericho Hill. It began in late 2018 as a Thompson Cigar exclusive and went to all retailers in 2019.
cigars.researchNote: Strength varies by source: Neptune says medium, Holt's medium-full, and halfwheel found it medium-full to full. The Bulldozer and Mini-Dozer limited editions add Mexican filler to the blend.

cigars.about: A 2018 release made by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo Jr. and the first cigar Crowned Heads put its own company name on. It was a thank-you to the company's supporters, which it calls its Court.
cigars.researchNote: Total production was 150,000 cigars across the three sizes, so it is hard to find now.

cigars.about: The first regular production Connecticut cigar from Crowned Heads, previewed in late 2016 and shipped nationally in 2017. It is made by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo Jr. in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel says the binder and filler were not disclosed; Neptune lists both as Nicaraguan. Crowned Heads billed it as mild to medium, but halfwheel's reviewer found it medium or a little above. Whether it is still in production is not confirmed.

cigars.about: The third Crowned Heads line, from 2013, made by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo Jr. with a dark Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper. J.D. Howard was the alias Jesse James used while living in Nashville.
cigars.researchNote: Brazilian Arapiraca is a dark natural leaf that does not fit the usual wrapper categories. Strength is not settled: Neptune calls it full-bodied, while halfwheel's review put it at medium to medium-plus. Whether it is still in production is not confirmed.

cigars.about: An Ohio-only release from 2018 and the first Crowned Heads cigar made at Drew Estate, blended with Willy Herrera. The name refers to Ohio and to the maiden name of co-founder Jon Huber's wife.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only through Ohio retailers, in one 6 x 48 size. Halfwheel found the strength just under medium for most of the cigar, building to medium-full at the end.

cigars.about: Curivari's value-priced Nicaraguan puro, launched in 2012 and one of the company's best-known regular lines. It is sold under the Buenaventura name, usually without Curivari on the band.
cigars.researchNote: Curivari does not say much about its tobacco or factory. Halfwheel has listed Tabacalera de Nicaragua S.A. for some Curivari cigars and Plasencia for others; Neptune lists Plasencia. Buenaventura Maduro, Cremas and Favoritos are separate blends.

cigars.about: One of the three Reserva Limitada blends from Curivari, a Nicaraguan puro made in Esteli with Cuban-seed Criollo and Corojo tobacco. The maker pitches it as a cigar to pair with coffee.
cigars.researchNote: Curivari names Cuban-seed Criollo and Corojo for the blend but does not say which leaf is the wrapper. It was already on sale in 2011; the exact release year is not published. Cafe Noir is a separate, darker maduro version. Halfwheel's reviewer found it milder than the maker's medium to full.

cigars.about: A full-bodied Nicaraguan puro from Curivari, made with Cuban-seed Criollo and Corojo tobacco. It is one of the core lines listed on the maker's site.
cigars.researchNote: Curivari names Cuban-seed Criollo and Corojo for the blend but does not say which leaf is the wrapper, and it does not publish a release year or factory for this line.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro introduced by Curivari in 2013 and named after the Greek hero, a nod to owner Andreas Throuvalas's heritage. At launch halfwheel found it stronger than other Curivari cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Specs are for the original 2013 Achilles. Halfwheel lists Tabacalera de Nicaragua as the factory and found it medium-full; Neptune says medium and names Plasencia. Two later versions share the name: Mirmidones (2015, San Andres wrapper, made at Plasencia) and La Iliada (2017, Nicaraguan puro in 12 sizes).

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Esteli, Jalapa), Dominican Republic (Habano 92), USA (Pennsylvania Broadleaf)
cigars.about: A strong five-country blend from Dapper Cigar Co. of Fresno, California, made at NACSA in Esteli under Raul Disla. The name means godmother in Spanish.
cigars.researchNote: This is the original Habano blend, also sold as La Madrina Natural. La Madrina Shade and La Madrina Maduro are separate blends. The maker rates it full to extra full. Earlier 5 1/4 x 54 and 5 5/8 x 50 sizes are retired.

cigars.about: The third Cubo blend from Dapper Cigar Co., shown at the 2018 trade show and shipped at the end of that year. It revisits the company's first cigar with a Sumatra wrapper and some Connecticut Broadleaf in the filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium to medium plus. Sizes have changed since launch: the 2018 lineup was Corona 5 5/8 x 45, Robusto 4 1/2 x 50, Toro 6 1/8 x 50 and Gordo 6 x 54. A 4 1/2 x 50 Short Robusto is now sold only in the United Kingdom.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped version of Cubo, the first brand from Dapper Cigar Co. Owner Ian Reith made it as a nod to the Connecticut cigars his father smoked.
cigars.researchNote: Dapper's own site marks Cubo Claro as discontinued. The original Cubo dates to around 2013; an exact year is not published. Three thinner sizes (5 3/4 x 40, 6 x 44, 6 1/2 x 42) were made in small batches. Unlike Dapper's other lines it was made at Tabacaleras Carreras, not NACSA.

cigars.about: A box-pressed San Andres cigar from Dapper Cigar Co., released in 2017 and made at NACSA in Esteli. The name is Spanish for the drunk.
cigars.researchNote: Renamed El Borracho San Andres in 2022; older boxes say El Borracho or El Borracho Natural. El Borracho Broadleaf (formerly Maduro) is a separate blend. The maker and Neptune call it full, but halfwheel's reviewer found the strength closer to medium. All four sizes are box-pressed.

cigars.about: A 2018 release from Dapper Cigar Co. with a dark sun grown Sumatra wrapper over a Connecticut Broadleaf binder, made at NACSA in Esteli. Siempre is Spanish for always.
cigars.researchNote: The full name is Siempre Sun Grown; Siempre Rosado is a separate blend. The maker rates it medium to medium plus in strength and full in flavor. Sizes have changed since the 2018 launch, which included a 6 x 60 Gordo.

cigars.about: Davidoff's classic mild white band line, rolled in the Dominican Republic with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. The 2000 corona is the company's best-selling cigar worldwide.
cigars.researchNote: The Signature name arrived in 2016 and took in older Classic cigars (the Signature No. 1 is the former Classic No. 1). Binder is listed as Ecuadorian by halfwheel (2023) and Neptune, Dominican by older listings. halfwheel's 2016 launch report called the wrapper Ecuadorian Sun Grown. Neptune's spec table says medium strength.

cigars.about: A mild white band Davidoff line made in the Dominican Republic with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Dominican tobaccos. Davidoff ties it to Zino Davidoff's 1946 idea of blending cigars the way fine Bordeaux wines are blended.
cigars.researchNote: The Robusto and Toro were added in 2016; the numbered sizes are older.

cigars.about: A white band Davidoff line first created in 1986 for Zino Davidoff's 80th birthday and made in the Dominican Republic since the early 1990s. It uses an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper and is offered in larger formats than the Signature line.
