cigars.researchNote: The 1986 original was Cuban-made; Dominican production began in 1990. Davidoff calls it medium intensity; Holt's rates it mild, Famous mild to medium, Neptune medium. halfwheel listed an Ecuadorian binder for the 2023 No. 1 Limited Edition, while retailers list a Dominican binder for the regular line.

cigars.about: The strongest of the four lines in Davidoff's White Band Collection, built around an Ecuadorian hybrid wrapper the company calls 151. It was introduced in 2001 as a regular production follow-up to the Millennium Collection released for the year 2000.
cigars.researchNote: Long sold as the Millennium Blend Series. Sources disagree on the binder: halfwheel's 2023 Lancero story and Neptune say Mexican, an earlier halfwheel review says Dominican seco. Davidoff calls it medium intensity. Holt's lists the wrapper as Ecuador Connecticut.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto, Olor/Piloto hybrid), Nicaragua (Condega, Estelí)
cigars.about: Davidoff's tribute line to Sir Winston Churchill, rolled in the Dominican Republic with an Ecuadorian wrapper, Mexican binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers. The current blend was relaunched in 2015 and became one of the company's most successful releases.
cigars.researchNote: Davidoff now labels it The Original Series. An earlier Winston Churchill line with a different blend came out in 2007; this version dates to 2015. Davidoff and halfwheel list the Robusto at 5 1/4 inches; Neptune and Holt's say 5 1/2.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Olor, Piloto, San Vicente), Nicaragua (Condega, Estelí)
cigars.about: A darker, bolder companion to the Davidoff Winston Churchill line, introduced in 2017. Part of the filler is Nicaraguan Condega tobacco aged for six months in Scotch whisky casks.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's calls it medium to full; Neptune lists it as full. The Petit Panetela and Belicoso use mixed (partly short) filler and are sold in tins.

cigars.about: Davidoff's first Nicaraguan puro and its first black band cigar, released in 2013. All of the tobacco is Nicaraguan, but the cigars are rolled at Davidoff's factory in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers rate the strength anywhere from medium (Holt's) to full (Neptune); halfwheel's reviewer found it medium. The Box Pressed sizes, added in 2016, use a Nicaraguan Habano Oscuro wrapper and extra ligero rather than the original Rosado blend.

cigars.filler: Brazil (Cubra, Mata Fina), Dominican Republic (Olor, San Vicente)
cigars.about: The second Davidoff black band line, introduced in 2015 and inspired by Brazil. It pairs Brazilian Mata Fina and Cubra tobaccos with Dominican filler under an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Davidoff describes it as medium intensity; Holt's lists it as medium to full. The Mata Fina is in the filler, not the wrapper; the binder is Brazilian Cubra.

cigars.about: The third Davidoff black band line, released in 2016. Its wrapper and binder come from Yamasá, a Dominican region where Davidoff spent about 20 years learning to grow tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Strength listings vary: Holt's says medium, Famous medium to full, Neptune full. halfwheel's reviewer called strength medium-plus and body medium-full.

cigars.about: A darker, stronger take on the Davidoff Aniversario shapes, using a reddish-brown Ecuadorian sun-grown Connecticut wrapper over Dominican tobaccos. Davidoff makes it in small quantities because the wrapper is scarce.
cigars.researchNote: Not a one-time edition: it is an ongoing line with limited availability, and Davidoff files it under limited editions. Retailers disagree on the ring gauge of the Special R and Special T (50 or 52).

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Corojo 99 Seco, Piloto Viso, San Vicente Mejorado Seco, San Vicente Seco, Yamasá Viso)
cigars.about: A limited Davidoff release from May 2021 honoring the Dominican Republic, made almost entirely of Dominican tobacco from the 2014 crop. Only the Ecuadorian binder comes from elsewhere, and each cigar has a pigtail cap.
cigars.researchNote: Limited edition with undisclosed numbers. Holt's lists it as medium to full and Neptune as full, but halfwheel's reviewer found the strength closer to medium.

cigars.about: A high-priced Davidoff line launched in 2016, built around a Dominican Aromatica wrapper kept for this cigar and aged at least eight years. Only eight senior rollers make it, and it comes in royal blue lacquered boxes of ten.
cigars.researchNote: Launch was limited to 500 boxes of 10 per size for the U.S., at $80 and $100 a cigar. halfwheel did not get the binder or filler from Davidoff; those details come from Neptune. Neptune lists the Salomones at 54 ring; Davidoff and halfwheel say 57.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A stronger blend inspired by the original Diesel, made by AJ Fernandez with a dark Ecuadorian Habano ligero wrapper. Its sizes carry d. names such as d.5 and d.6.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's spec sheet says medium-full, while its own description and Famous Smoke call it full. A separate Unlimited Maduro uses a Pennsylvania Broadleaf wrapper.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A box-pressed limited edition toro from Diesel and AJ Fernandez, released in 2019. It was the first of the three cigars later called the Elixir trilogy.
cigars.researchNote: One size only, limited to 5,000 boxes of 10. The maker's spec sheet and Neptune say medium, though the maker's description calls it medium to full-bodied.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A full-bodied limited edition toro made by AJ Fernandez, released in 2021 as the last of Diesel's Elixir trilogy after Hair of the Dog and Delirium. It reuses the name of a 2012 Diesel limited edition.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 3,000 boxes of 10. The maker's spec sheet calls the wrapper Nicaraguan, but its own description, halfwheel and Neptune say Ecuadorian Habano. Halfwheel lists 6 x 52 with some Honduran filler; the maker and Neptune say 6 x 50. A different Diesel Crucible came out in 2012.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A series of six seasonal limited releases from Diesel and AJ Fernandez, each a different blend and size priced at about five dollars. It ran from August 2021 to October 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Each of the six releases is its own blend; the blend shown is San Marzano, the first. Pecorino used a San Andrés wrapper and Gabagool an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. The maker's spec sheet calls the San Marzano wrapper Nicaraguan, while halfwheel says Ecuadorian Habano.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made only with tobacco grown on AJ Fernandez's farms in Estelí and rolled at his factory there. It joined the Diesel lineup in 2020.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium-full; Neptune lists it as full. The maker's page now shows only the Robusto and Toro.

cigars.binder: Brazil (Arapiraca, aged in Rabbit Hole Pedro Ximénez sherry casks)
cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The second Diesel and Rabbit Hole collaboration, made by AJ Fernandez. Its Brazilian Arapiraca binder is aged in Pedro Ximénez sherry casks that Rabbit Hole used to finish bourbon, under a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium-full; Famous Smoke lists it as medium.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A San Andrés wrapped Diesel made by AJ Fernandez that began in 2021 as a lancero exclusive to Tobacconists' Association of America shops. It became a regular line in 2022 and gained a toro and torpedo in 2023.
cigars.researchNote: Scandinavian Tobacco Group told retailers in July 2024 that it was discontinuing the line. The maker's spec sheet and Neptune rate it full, while the maker's description places it in the medium-full range.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A maduro Diesel line made by AJ Fernandez around aged Nicaraguan filler, which the company says is five to eight years old. It launched in 2023 as a regular production line.
cigars.researchNote: This is the original San Andrés maduro blend. A separate Vintage Series Natural with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper followed in 2024 and is rated medium-full by the maker. The 4.5 x 60 and 6 x 46 Rabito sizes have since been dropped. The maker rates this blend full; Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.about: The core line of Altadis USA's Don Diego brand, rolled in the Dominican Republic with a Connecticut Shade wrapper. The brand started in the Canary Islands after the Cuban embargo and is known as a mild, creamy smoke.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls this line simply Don Diego, not Original. Holt's describes the inside as Dominican and Brazilian tobaccos and rates it mild-medium; the maker lists Dominican binder with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler.

cigars.about: The Blue Label, a Nicaraguan puro with a Habano Rosado wrapper from Jose "Pepin" Garcia, sold by My Father Cigars. The maker says it is handcrafted in the USA.
cigars.researchNote: Commonly called the Blue Label. The maker says it is handcrafted in the USA, where it began at the El Rey de los Habanos factory in Miami; Neptune lists Nicaragua as the origin. The maker calls it full-bodied, Neptune medium.

cigars.about: The Black Label, a Nicaraguan puro introduced in 2006 and the first Don Pepin Garcia blend rolled at the family's factory in Estelí. Its sizes are named for Garcia family birth years.
cigars.researchNote: Commonly called the Black Label. The maker rates it medium to full; retailers such as Famous Smoke list it as full. It was first rolled at Tabacalera Cubana S.A., the Garcias' original Estelí factory.

cigars.about: A white-banded Nicaraguan puro with a Corojo Rosado wrapper that Pepin Garcia introduced in 2005. The maker says the name comes from the initials of his children, Jaime and Janny.
cigars.researchNote: The maker says it is handcrafted in the USA (it began at El Rey de los Habanos in Miami), but Famous Smoke lists it as made at My Father in Estelí, Nicaragua. The maker rates it three-quarters to full; Famous lists full. Halfwheel says JJ stands for Jose and Jaime.

cigars.about: One of the first cigars Pepin Garcia made under his own name, around 2003 in Miami. It is a milder Nicaraguan puro with a Corojo Rosado wrapper, now rolled at My Father's factory in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: Largely phased out after its early years, it returned in 2017 with production moved to Estelí and was reblended and repackaged in 2023. Strength follows Holt's, which lists medium; the text on the maker's page describes the My Father line by mistake.

cigars.about: A 2018 limited edition marking 15 years since Pepin Garcia opened his first factory in Miami. It is a Nicaraguan puro from the family's Estelí farms with some Pelo de Oro in the blend.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,000 boxes of 14 in each of the two sizes. The full-bodied rating comes from Neptune only; the maker's site no longer lists the cigar.

cigars.about: The natural wrapper version of Don Tomás Clasico, a long-running value cigar from Danlí, Honduras, sold by General Cigar under Scandinavian Tobacco Group. The Don Tomás brand dates to 1971.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers disagree on strength: Famous and Neptune say medium, Holt's medium-full. Famous calls the wrapper Honduran Habano; Neptune and Holt's just say Honduran. No maker spec sheet was found.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Don Tomás Clasico, a Honduran value cigar from General Cigar under Scandinavian Tobacco Group. It pairs a dark wrapper with Honduran and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the wrapper: Famous Smoke lists Connecticut Broadleaf, Mike's Cigars lists Cameroon. Famous rates it medium, Mike's full. The binder is not published.

cigars.about: An all-Honduran Don Tomás blend with a sun grown wrapper, built on tobacco from the Jamastran Valley. It has been part of the brand since 2007.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke lists the wrapper variety as undisclosed. Its spec sheet says medium while its description calls the smoke medium to full-bodied.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut River Valley Broadleaf No. 1 Dark
cigars.about: Drew Estate's flagship full-bodied cigar, built around a dark Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. It started as a private blend for the company's own people, and the name comes from the ninth test blend.
cigars.researchNote: First sold in 2007 as a single 6 x 52 size. A 3 15/16 x 60 Flying Pig is also made as a seasonal release.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut River Valley stalk-cut and stalk-cured Habano
cigars.about: The second Liga Privada blend, wrapped in a Habano-seed leaf grown in Connecticut that is cut and cured on the whole stalk. It is full-bodied like the No. 9 but with a different wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Stalk-cut means the whole plant is cut and hung in the barn instead of picking the leaves one at a time. A 3 15/16 x 60 Flying Pig is also made as a seasonal release.

cigars.binder: Mexico (San Andres Otapan Negro Ultimo Corte)
cigars.filler: Nicaragua, Honduras, USA (Pennsylvania Green River One Sucker)
cigars.wrapperLeaf: H99 hybrid of Connecticut Corojo and stalk-cut Habano, grown in the Connecticut River Valley
cigars.about: A Liga Privada blend built on a hybrid Corojo-seed wrapper grown in Connecticut by a single farmer for Drew Estate. It came out in tiny quantities in 2018 and became a regular release in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel lists the Robusto as 5 1/2 x 54; the maker and Neptune list 5 x 54. Halfwheel says the Super Ancho is sold only at retailer events. Wrapper supply is small, so it can be hard to find.

cigars.binder: Mexico (San Andres Otapan Negro Ultimo Corte)
cigars.filler: Nicaragua, USA (Pennsylvania Green River One Sucker)
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut Criollo (hybrid, criollo-seed grown in Connecticut)
cigars.about: Made to mark ten years of Liga Privada, with a heavy Criollo-seed wrapper grown in Connecticut. It is a dense, full-strength cigar finished with a fishtail cap and a covered foot.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in December 2018 in very small numbers sold to stores by raffle; regular production since June 2022. Sold in boxes of 10.

cigars.line: Liga Privada Único Serie Feral Flying Pig
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut Broadleaf (the Liga Privada No. 9 wrapper)
cigars.about: A larger version of Drew Estate's Flying Pig perfecto, sold in the Liga Privada Único Serie. It has its own blend under the No. 9 Broadleaf wrapper and is very full-bodied.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the Único Serie, where each vitola has its own blend. The maker only confirms the No. 9 Broadleaf wrapper; binder and filler are from halfwheel's 2011 review. Made in small batches, so supply comes and goes.

cigars.line: Liga Privada Único Serie Dirty Rat
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut River Valley stalk-cut and cured sun grown Habano (the Liga Privada T52 wrapper)
cigars.about: A small pigtail-capped corona that was the first release in the Liga Privada Único Serie. It packs five filler tobaccos into a 44 ring gauge under the T52 Habano wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the Único Serie, where each vitola has its own blend. The maker only confirms the T52 Habano wrapper; binder and filler are from halfwheel. Made in small batches, so supply comes and goes.

cigars.binder: USA (Connecticut River Valley stalk-cut and stalk-cured Habano)
cigars.about: The original Undercrown, created by Drew Estate's rollers as their own smoke when Liga Privada tobacco ran short. It uses many of the same tobaccos from different primings under a dark Mexican wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2011 simply as Undercrown; Maduro was added to the name after other versions arrived. A 3 15/16 x 60 Flying Pig is also made as a seasonal release.

cigars.about: The Connecticut Shade version of Undercrown, blended by Willy Herrera with the factory's rollers. It is a completely different blend from the original, not just a wrapper swap.
cigars.researchNote: A 3 15/16 x 60 Flying Pig is also made as a seasonal release.

cigars.binder: USA (Connecticut River Valley stalk-cut and cured sun grown Habano)
cigars.filler: Nicaragua (including aged ligero from Nueva Segovia)
cigars.about: The third Undercrown blend, in red and gold bands, with a sun grown Sumatra-seed wrapper from Ecuador. Drew Estate dropped the whole line in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Discontinued in September 2022 and no longer on Drew Estate's site, so any stock is leftover. No official strength rating confirmed; halfwheel's reviewer found it medium-full by the end.

cigars.about: Released for the tenth anniversary of Undercrown. It keeps a Mexican San Andres wrapper like the original but uses a Connecticut Broadleaf binder and a bolder, full-bodied blend.
cigars.researchNote: The maker and Neptune call it Full; Holt's lists it as Medium-Full.

cigars.about: The first blend by Willy Herrera after he joined Drew Estate, made in a Cuban style with entubado bunching and a triple cap. It is a smooth, medium-bodied cigar and a change from the company's darker lines.
cigars.researchNote: Originally sold simply as Herrera Estelí; the maker now labels it Herrera Estelí Habano.

cigars.about: Willy Herrera's second line for Drew Estate, a soft box-pressed cigar with a Mexican San Andres wrapper. The name refers to people from northern Nicaragua, where Estelí is.
cigars.researchNote: Drew Estate discontinued the line in December 2024, so stock is leftover. By then only the Lonsdale, Robusto Grande and Toro Especial were still listed. Strength is from Neptune and Holt's, which both say Full.

cigars.about: A Herrera Estelí blend built to show off dark Brazilian Mata Fina leaf as a wrapper instead of its usual role as binder or filler. Willy Herrera blended it to be smooth and floral with a medium to full body.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists Nicaraguan and Dominican filler; halfwheel's 2018 report lists Nicaragua only.

cigars.about: A Herrera Estelí blend rolled in Miami's Little Havana at El Titan de Bronze, the small factory where Willy Herrera learned to blend. The factory is owned by his mother-in-law, Sandra Cobas.
cigars.researchNote: First released in 2016 as a single limited size, then as a full line in late 2018. Drew Estate discontinued it in December 2024, so stock is leftover. Strength is from Neptune and halfwheel's review, not the maker.

cigars.about: A low-priced bundle cigar from Drew Estate's Factory Smokes line, made at the company's own factory in Estelí. This version has a sun grown Habano wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper's country of origin is not published. The maker lists Central American filler; halfwheel's 2018 launch coverage listed mixed Indonesian filler. Sold in bundles of 20.

cigars.about: A low-priced bundle cigar from Drew Estate's Factory Smokes line, made at the company's own factory in Estelí. This version has a dark, oily maduro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not say what the maduro leaf is or where it is grown. The maker lists Central American filler; halfwheel's 2018 launch coverage listed mixed Indonesian filler. Sold in bundles of 20.

cigars.about: A low-priced bundle cigar from Drew Estate's Factory Smokes line, made at the company's own factory in Estelí. This is the mild one, with a Connecticut Shade wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not say where the shade wrapper is grown. The maker calls it Mellow. It lists Central American filler; halfwheel's 2018 launch coverage listed mixed Indonesian filler. Sold in bundles of 20.

cigars.about: The lighter of Drew Estate's two coffee-infused Tabak Especial cigars, with a Connecticut Shade wrapper. It is mild, creamy and sweet, in the style of a cafe con leche.
cigars.researchNote: This is a coffee-infused cigar, not a traditional one. The maker calls it Mellow. Neptune lists the wrapper as U.S. Connecticut Shade; the maker, halfwheel and Holt's say Ecuadorian. Year of introduction not confirmed.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andres Maduro, aged two years
cigars.about: The darker of Drew Estate's two coffee-infused Tabak Especial cigars, with a Mexican maduro wrapper. It leans toward dark-roast espresso and chocolate where the Dulce is creamy and sweet.
cigars.researchNote: This is a coffee-infused cigar, not a traditional one. Halfwheel in 2019, Holt's and Neptune call the wrapper Connecticut Broadleaf; the maker and halfwheel's 2022 coverage say Mexican maduro. Year of introduction not confirmed.

cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A cigar built around Kentucky tobacco that is cured with fire and smoke in the barn, which gives it a smoky, hickory character. It began as an extension of Drew Estate's My Uzi Weighs a Ton brand.
cigars.researchNote: Drew Estate has not officially disclosed the wrapper or binder; the wrapper here is Neptune's listing. Launched as MUWAT Kentucky Fire Cured. Halfwheel reported most sizes are made at the Joya de Nicaragua factory, not Drew Estate's own; the maker names no factory.

cigars.about: A deliberately rustic, value-priced cigar made as a tribute to Estelí, Nicaragua. Its artwork shows El Brujito, a shaman figure from a pre-Columbian rock carving found in the region.
cigars.researchNote: This is the original Nica Rustica. It was renamed Nica Rustica Broadleaf after the Adobe and Shade versions were added. The Belly size was discontinued in 2024. The maker says Medium-Full; Neptune rates it Full.

cigars.about: A mild, value-priced cigar infused with Sumatra Mandheling coffee and finished with a sweetened tip. Drew Estate describes it as one of the mildest cigars it makes.
cigars.researchNote: Coffee-infused with a sweet tip. The original is now called Sun Grown; a Maduro version was added in 2018. The maker lists Indonesian and Nicaraguan filler and names no binder; halfwheel and Neptune list Nicaraguan binder and filler. Year of introduction not confirmed.

cigars.about: The first Deadwood cigar, a sweet, aromatic maduro corona that Drew Estate first made as a house cigar for Deadwood Tobacco Co. in Deadwood, South Dakota. It went on sale nationally in 2016.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is secret: Drew Estate says only a maduro wrapper and aromatic tobaccos. Holt's and Neptune call the wrapper Connecticut Broadleaf and rate it Medium; the maker calls Sweet Jane Mellow. Store exclusive from 2009, national since 2016.

cigars.about: A thicker, fuller member of Drew Estate's sweet, aromatic Deadwood family, which started as house cigars for Deadwood Tobacco Co. in South Dakota. It has a maduro wrapper and an undisclosed blend.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is secret: Drew Estate says only a maduro wrapper and aromatic tobaccos. Holt's and Neptune call the wrapper Connecticut Broadleaf and rate it Medium; the maker says Medium-Full. Store exclusive from about 2014, national since 2016.

cigars.about: A short tapered cigar in Drew Estate's sweet, aromatic Deadwood family, which started as house cigars for Deadwood Tobacco Co. in South Dakota. It has a maduro wrapper and a mostly undisclosed blend.
cigars.researchNote: Maker lists the size as 4 x 38-52 (it tapers); Holt's and Neptune list 4 1/2 x 52. Halfwheel names an Indonesian binder; Neptune lists Nicaraguan binder and filler. Holt's and Neptune call the wrapper Connecticut Broadleaf and rate it Medium. Store exclusive from about 2014, national since 2016.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua, USA (Pennsylvania Green River One Sucker)
cigars.about: An all-maduro cigar Drew Estate made with Metallica's James Hetfield and Blackened Whiskey distiller Rob Dietrich. The M stands for Metallica and 81 for 1981, the year the band formed.
cigars.researchNote: Drew Estate lists the body as medium to full. Famous Smoke and Neptune rate the strength full, while halfwheel's review found it medium-plus. A Flying Pig, 4 x 32 tins and a 2025 Lancero also exist outside the four core sizes.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua, USA (Pennsylvania Green River One Sucker)
cigars.about: The second Blackened cigar from Drew Estate and Metallica's James Hetfield, putting a Connecticut Shade wrapper over the same maduro binder and filler as the M81. The name plays on the song Fade to Black from the band's 1984 album.
cigars.researchNote: Drew Estate's site calls it simply Blackened S84. A 7 x 40 Lancero was added in September 2025.

cigars.about: A Connecticut Shade cigar from Drew Estate that uses Florida Sun Grown filler from Jeff Borysiewicz's 20 acre farm in Clermont, Florida. It is the company's second line built around that tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the binder: Drew Estate's site says Connecticut River Valley Habano, while halfwheel and Corona Cigar say Honduran Habano. halfwheel lists the Robusto at 5 1/2 inches; Drew Estate says 5 1/4.

cigars.about: Known as FSG, this is Drew Estate's first cigar to use tobacco grown on Jeff Borysiewicz's farm in Clermont, Florida. It began in 2016 as a Corona Cigar Co. exclusive and went national in 2017.
cigars.researchNote: Since January 2022 it has been sold only through Corona Cigar Co. Sources disagree on the wrapper: halfwheel says Brazilian Mata Fina, Corona says Brazilian Arapiraca maduro. Corona rates it medium to full; halfwheel's review found medium to medium-full. The Limited Edition Toro is a different, broadleaf-wrapped blend.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Three versions: Brazilian Maduro, Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade, or Cuban-seed Corojo
cigars.about: Drew Estate's first brand, started in New York City in 1996 and later moved to Nicaragua. It was a budget, mixed-filler cigar sold in three wrapper versions until Drew Estate dropped the whole line in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Discontinued in September 2022. It came in three wrappers, so there is no single wrapper type: Neptune rates the Connecticut Shade mild and the Brazilian Maduro and Corojo medium. Blend details come from a retailer, not the maker.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Kentucky fire-cured, barrel-fermented tapa negra over an Indonesian base wrapper
cigars.about: A Drew Estate collaboration with Pappy & Company, the Van Winkle family's merchandise business. It is built around Kentucky fire-cured tobacco that is fermented in bourbon barrels, which gives it a smoky, charred oak character.
cigars.researchNote: Blend here is from Drew Estate's site. halfwheel lists a Mexican San Andres base wrapper and a Nicaraguan binder, and the Toro as 6 x 52. Drew Estate says the tobacco ferments in retired Pappy Van Winkle bourbon barrels; halfwheel reported in 2019 that the barrels had not held Pappy, so do not promise it. Made in small batches.

cigars.about: The original Java, a coffee and cocoa infused cigar that Drew Estate makes for Rocky Patel. Most sizes are box-pressed.
cigars.researchNote: Banded Java by Drew Estate; Drew Estate makes it for Rocky Patel, which distributes it. It is an infused (flavored) cigar. Blend comes from retailers, not the maker. Not every size is still stocked by retailers.

cigars.about: The Connecticut Shade version of Java, a coffee and cocoa infused cigar that Drew Estate makes for Rocky Patel. Retailers rate it mild, lighter than the other Java lines.
cigars.researchNote: Banded Java by Drew Estate; Drew Estate makes it for Rocky Patel, which distributes it. It is an infused (flavored) cigar. Blend comes from retailers. Not every size is still stocked by retailers.

cigars.about: A mint and chocolate take on Java, the infused cigar that Drew Estate makes for Rocky Patel. It keeps the dark Brazilian wrapper of the original Java Maduro.
cigars.researchNote: Banded Java by Drew Estate; Drew Estate makes it for Rocky Patel, which distributes it. It is an infused (flavored) cigar. Blend comes from retailers; Famous Smoke calls the wrapper Brazilian Mata Fina. Not every size is still stocked by retailers.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: Dunbarton's top-tier regular line, a soft-pressed cigar with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over an Ecuadorian Habano binder, made at Joya de Nicaragua. Steve Saka calls it his best blend, and it comes cedar-sleeved in boxes of 13.
cigars.researchNote: Maker rates strength 6 out of 10; Neptune lists medium but describes it as medium to full bodied. Paladin de Saka (7 x 52) is a stronger, year-aged limited version. Halfwheel reported production of the 7 x 44 Varita Mágica was halted in 2023.

cigars.about: Dunbarton's value-priced broadleaf cigar, sold in paper bundles of 10 and named for Steve Saka's favorite fishing lake on the New Hampshire and Maine border. It uses Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper judged too rough looking for Mi Querida.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's site lists a San Andrés Negro binder, while halfwheel and Neptune list a Nicaraguan binder. Maker rates strength 7 out of 10; Neptune lists it as full. Bronzeback (5 x 48) is a more peppery version with a 2LS Broadleaf wrapper.

cigars.about: A stronger take on Mi Querida that swaps in darker No. 1 Dark broadleaf wrapper and adds Dominican ligero to the filler. Dunbarton calls it arguably its boldest cigar, and the sizes are named for their length and ring gauge.
cigars.researchNote: Maker rates strength 9 out of 10. It grew out of the 2018 Mi Querida Firecracker made for United Cigars. The maker's blend chart lists Nicaraguan and USA filler while its description and halfwheel name Dominican ligero.

cigars.binder: Mexico (San Andrés Negro, Matacapan Negro de Temporal)
cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A milder version of the Sobremesa blend with an Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper and the Pennsylvania ligero removed. Steve Saka made it to recall the creamy, sweet Connecticut cigars of decades past.
cigars.researchNote: Maker rates strength 3 out of 10; Neptune's spec says medium but its description says mild to medium. Brûlée Blue and Brûlée Wagashi are limited variants of this blend.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A limited single-size version of Sobremesa Brûlée, blended a touch stronger and aged a full year after rolling. It comes as a 6 1/4 x 46 grand corona with a pigtail cap and placed fourth on halfwheel's Top 25 of 2020.
cigars.researchNote: This is one limited size within the Sobremesa Brûlée line, not a separate line. No source gives it its own strength rating: the maker only says it is a touch stronger than regular Brûlée (3 out of 10), and halfwheel's review found it just shy of medium. A 6 1/4 x 60 Unicorn was also made in very small numbers.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A strong Nicaraguan puro from Steve Saka, made at Joya de Nicaragua with a sun grown Cuban-seed wrapper. The name is his own Spanglish for "all the days", and the blend builds in strength to a powerful finish.
cigars.researchNote: Regular production has been on hiatus since mid-2021 over a filler tobacco quality issue; sizes have returned only as limited Archive Series releases, and the maker hopes to restart in late 2026. Maker rates strength 9 out of 10. Neptune calls the wrapper Nicaraguan Criollo.

cigars.about: A Connecticut Broadleaf maduro that Steve Saka blended to be smoked after a steak dinner, first made for the Red Meat Lovers Club charity dinners. Three sizes are trunk pressed, and the Beef Stick is a round, flat-capped, closed-foot parejo.
cigars.researchNote: It started in 2019 as a Smoke Inn store exclusive and became a national regular line in 2023. Maker rates strength 7 out of 10 and calls it full bodied; Neptune lists it as full. Fritanga (6 x 52) is a bolder limited version.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua, plus pipe tobaccos that differ by blend
cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A line of 6 x 52 toros that blend Nicaraguan cigar filler with pipe tobaccos made by Jeremy Reeves of Cornell & Diehl. Each blend uses a different pipe mixture, such as Latakia in English No. 27 and Perique in Bayou No. 32.
cigars.researchNote: Maker styles the name StillWell Star. Strength depends on the blend: the maker rates the Aromatics 4, Navy No. 1056 5, English No. 27 6 and Bayou No. 32 7 out of 10. Aromatic No. 1 has a sweetened cap. Limited Holiday editions use other wrappers.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (mixed filler: trimmings from the broadleaf lines plus two long-leaf tobaccos)
cigars.about: Dunbarton's least expensive cigar, a 4 x 48 mixed-filler smoke built from the table trimmings of its broadleaf lines such as Mi Querida, Umbagog and Red Meat Lovers. The name is Italian for meatball.
cigars.researchNote: It began in late 2019 as an event-only cigar and became regular production in January 2024. This is a sandwich-style mixed-filler cigar, not all long filler. Maker rates strength 9 out of 10.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Honduran puro from Christian Eiroa's CLE Cigar Company, released to mark his first 20 years in the cigar business. The tobaccos were grown by his father Julio in the Jamastran Valley, including an heirloom binder leaf.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel lists the wrapper only as Honduran; Neptune and Famous call it a Honduran maduro, and no source names the varietal. Neptune and Famous list it as medium, though Neptune's write-up calls it full bodied. The Diadema is 8 inches with a 48 to 60 ring taper. A separate Colorado-wrapper version also exists.

cigars.about: A maduro from Christian Eiroa's CLE Cigar Company in which the wrapper, binder and filler are all maduro leaf from the upper primings. CBT stands for capa, banda and tripa, the Spanish words for those three parts.
cigars.researchNote: The maker has not disclosed the blend, per halfwheel. Neptune lists a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper over Honduran binder and filler, which is unconfirmed. Eiroa calls it full bodied and Neptune lists full; halfwheel's reviewer found it medium-full.

cigars.about: The original Eiroa cigar from Christian Eiroa's CLE Cigar Company, a Honduran puro made at the Aladino factory in Danlí. Its band carries the old Spanish toast "Salud, Amor y Pesetas" in tribute to his family's century in tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2013 simply as Eiroa; now sold as Eiroa Classic. Halfwheel and Neptune describe it as a Honduran puro with a Corojo wrapper. Neptune rates it medium, while halfwheel's review found medium-plus to medium-full and the maker billed it as bold and full bodied.

cigars.about: The lighter-wrapped line of the Honduran-made El Rey del Mundo, introduced in 2022 with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over a Honduran binder. It is a mellow, value-priced cigar from the same company that makes Punch and Hoyo de Monterrey.
cigars.researchNote: This is the non-Cuban, Honduran El Rey del Mundo; the maker and Famous call the line Naturals. The maker describes it as mellow to medium bodied, while Neptune and Famous list medium strength. Famous lists Rectangulare at 45 ring and Reserva Salado at 64 ring, against 46 and 54 at halfwheel and Neptune. Famous also mentions Dominican filler.

cigars.about: The dark-wrapped core of the Honduran-made El Rey del Mundo, with an extra-dark Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over Honduran binder and filler. It is an old-school, value-priced maduro made alongside Punch and Hoyo de Monterrey.
cigars.researchNote: This is the non-Cuban, Honduran El Rey del Mundo. Retailers label the same cigars Oscuro (Holt's), Broadleaf (Famous) or Maduro (Neptune). Holt's lists medium-full; Famous and Neptune list full in their spec tables but describe it as medium to full.

cigars.about: The first cigar in the Perez-Carrillo Series, a dark San Andrés-wrapped blend introduced in 2014. Each size is named after a member of Ernesto Perez-Carrillo's family.
cigars.researchNote: Three sizes launched in 2014; the box-pressed Regalias D'Celia was added in 2015. La Historia Silk is a separate, newer line.

cigars.about: A Perez-Carrillo Series cigar with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco. It is rolled by Oliva in Esteli, Nicaragua, instead of at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Made by Oliva in Nicaragua, not at the Carrillo factory in the Dominican Republic. The first run was 7,500 boxes, with more to follow on demand; the maker still lists it.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Perez-Carrillo Series cigar that puts a Cameroon wrapper from the Meerapfel family over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It appeared in late 2024 and went nationwide in early 2025.
cigars.researchNote: A 6 x 46 Corona Gorda was added in August 2025, first through one retailer (Two Guys Smoke Shop). The maker's page still lists only the Robusto and Toro.

cigars.about: The natural-wrapper half of Core Plus, the reblended and repackaged line that replaced E.P. Carrillo's original Core Line in 2016. It sat in the company's Classic Series alongside a Maduro version.
cigars.researchNote: No longer in the maker's current lineup. Halfwheel's spec table lists an Ecuadorian binder, but its text and Cigar Coop both say Nicaraguan. Cigar Coop gives the wrapper only as Ecuadorian. No strength rating found.

cigars.about: A dark Connecticut Broadleaf maduro that E.P. Carrillo introduced in 2016 as the one all-new blend in its Classic Series. It was priced as an everyday cigar and sold in 20-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: No longer in the maker's current lineup. Shown at the 2016 trade show in small quantities, with the full rollout in early 2017.

cigars.about: A sun-grown Ecuadorian wrapper blend over Nicaraguan tobacco, added in 2016 to E.P. Carrillo's Elite Series. The name means wrapper of the sun.
cigars.researchNote: Put on hiatus in 2022; the maker said then it was not fully discontinued, but it is not in the current lineup. Halfwheel lists the wrapper as Ecuadorian Habano; Cigar Coop calls it Ecuadorian Sun Grown. Strength comes from a Cigar Coop review, not the maker.

cigars.about: Two short, thin cigars that E.P. Carrillo introduced in 2016, offered in Natural and Maduro blends. They were sold in five-count packs.
cigars.researchNote: Two blends share the name. Natural: Ecuadorian wrapper, Nicaraguan binder and filler. Maduro: Mexican San Andrés wrapper, Ecuadorian binder, Nicaraguan filler. No longer in the maker's current lineup. No strength rating found.

cigars.about: A follow-up to the New Wave Connecticut that keeps the Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper but uses a Connecticut Broadleaf binder. It debuted in Europe in 2014 and reached U.S. stores later that year.
cigars.researchNote: Put on hiatus in 2022; the maker said then it was not fully discontinued, but it is not in the current lineup. Three sizes added in 2015 (Corona Extra, Elegantes, Soberanos Real) were dropped in the 2016 repackaging.

cigars.about: A dark Brazilian-wrapped E.P. Carrillo line that began in 2011 using the blend of the company's Edicion Limitada 2010. It was phased out, then brought back in 2017 with a slightly changed blend.
cigars.researchNote: Specs are the 2017 relaunch, which swapped the original Dominican binder for Ecuadorian. The original wrapper was called Brazilian Habano; 2017 sources say only Brazilian. Halfwheel and Neptune put strength at medium; Cigar Coop says medium to full. Not in the maker's current lineup.

cigars.about: The Connecticut Broadleaf maduro version of E.P. Carrillo's INCH series of very thick cigars, with ring gauges from 60 to 70. It has been in production since the series launched in 2012.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's own page disagrees with itself on the binder: the spec table says Ecuador, the description says Nicaraguan. Cigar Coop also says Nicaraguan. An 8 x 58 size added in 2016 is no longer listed.

cigars.about: The natural-wrapper version of E.P. Carrillo's INCH series of very thick cigars, with ring gauges from 60 to 70. It uses an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper and has been made since the series launched in 2012.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the wrapper only as Ecuador; Cigar Coop identifies it as Ecuadorian Sumatra. The maker rates it medium, while Cigar Coop's review called it medium to full.

cigars.about: A dark Mexican San Andrés-wrapped cigar that E.P. Carrillo launched in 2015 and later placed in its Elite Series. The wrapper sits over an Ecuadorian binder and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: On hiatus since 2022 and not in the maker's current lineup. Launched in six sizes; Cigar Coop reported the Nacionales (5 1/2 x 44) and Dinamicos (6 7/8 x 49) dropped in 2016, though a 2017 review there still counted six. Strength is from a Cigar Coop review, not the maker.

cigars.about: The first cigar Erik Espinosa blended after starting his own company, rolled at his La Zona factory in Esteli. It pairs an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2012 as a Nicaraguan puro, then reblended in 2015 with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. The maker calls it medium bodied and Neptune lists it medium, but Famous Smoke lists it as full.

cigars.about: The first Connecticut-wrapped cigar under the Espinosa name, made at La Zona in Esteli. An Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper covers Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish a strength. Neptune lists it as mild and Famous Smoke as medium with a mild to medium body, so it sits between the two.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Brazilian (the maker's blend table says Brazilian Ballaño and its description says Brazilian Anaranjado)
cigars.about: Laranja is Portuguese for orange, a nod to the orange tint of its Brazilian wrapper. Espinosa rolls it at La Zona in Esteli over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: The exact Brazilian wrapper varietal is not published; Neptune says the leaf comes from the Reconcavo region. Strength is described differently: the maker says medium bodied and full flavored, Famous Smoke says medium to full bodied, and Neptune lists full.

cigars.about: A darker, box-pressed take on Laranja Reserva with a Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos. It is made for Espinosa at AJ Fernandez's San Lotano factory in Ocotal.
cigars.researchNote: All sizes are box pressed. The maker lists the robusto as 5 1/2 x 54, while halfwheel and Famous Smoke list it as 5 1/2 x 56. Halfwheel's review found the strength closer to medium-full than full.

cigars.about: Murcielago, Spanish for bat, is a mostly box-pressed cigar with a dark Mexican San Andres wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. The current version has been made at AJ Fernandez's San Lotano factory since 2017.
cigars.researchNote: It debuted in 2009 under EO Brands at My Father Cigars, was relaunched by Espinosa in 2015, and was reworked by AJ Fernandez in 2017. Retailers disagree on strength: Famous Smoke lists full (medium-full in its description) and Neptune lists medium.

cigars.about: One of the two original blends in celebrity chef Guy Fieri's Knuckle Sandwich line, created with Erik Espinosa. It uses an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler and is rolled at AJ Fernandez's San Lotano factory.
cigars.researchNote: Knuckle Sandwich is Guy Fieri's own brand, made in partnership with Espinosa, which distributes it. The letters after the size names honor people in Fieri's life.

cigars.about: The darker of the two original Knuckle Sandwich blends from Guy Fieri and Erik Espinosa. An Ecuadorian Sumatra maduro wrapper covers Nicaraguan binder and filler, rolled at AJ Fernandez's San Lotano factory.
cigars.researchNote: Knuckle Sandwich is Guy Fieri's own brand, made in partnership with Espinosa, which distributes it. The maduro wrapper is Ecuadorian Sumatra seed, not broadleaf.

cigars.about: The third regular blend in Guy Fieri's Knuckle Sandwich line with Espinosa, added in January 2023. It has an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler and is rolled at San Lotano.
cigars.researchNote: Knuckle Sandwich is Guy Fieri's own brand, made in partnership with Espinosa, which distributes it. It smokes fuller than most Connecticut cigars: retailers and halfwheel put the strength at medium.

cigars.about: A limited edition series honoring the six original provinces of Cuba, with a different blend and its own box artwork for each release. Espinosa has the cigars made at AJ Fernandez's San Lotano factory.
cigars.researchNote: Each release is its own blend and single size, so there is no one wrapper or strength for the line. Releases: LHB 2018, MTZ 2019, LV 2021, CMW 2022, ZDT 2023, ORT 2024 (Ecuadorian Habano over Nicaraguan). A seventh, MIA, was announced for 2026.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Broadleaf (Connecticut Broadleaf on the original, Nicaraguan broadleaf on recent releases)
cigars.about: A near-annual limited edition offshoot of Espinosa's 601 La Bomba, known for its painted bomb band and military theme. It puts a dark broadleaf wrapper on a strong, spicy Nicaraguan blend.
cigars.researchNote: Sold under Espinosa's 601 brand as 601 La Bomba Warhead. Each numbered release is one limited size and the wrapper has changed: Connecticut broadleaf on early ones, Nicaraguan broadleaf on Warhead 11 (2025) and 12 (2026). The maker's size list stops at No. 9 and differs from halfwheel on Nos. 2, 5 and 8.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Nicaraguan puro made by Plasencia, carried over from the old Nat Sherman portfolio by Ferio Tego. The size names are the length and ring gauge run together.
cigars.researchNote: Introduced in 2012 as Nat Sherman Timeless Nicaraguan, renamed Timeless Supreme in 2018, and brought back by Ferio Tego in 2021 with the same blend and factory. The wrapper varietal is not published; Neptune describes it as a dark maduro leaf.

cigars.about: A line of classic Cuban-style sizes with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over aged Dominican tobaccos, made by the Quesada family. It began as Nat Sherman Sterling and now belongs to Ferio Tego.
cigars.researchNote: Debuted in 2013 as Nat Sherman Sterling and returned under Ferio Tego in 2021. The maker lists Dominican filler, while halfwheel's 2021 report said Dominican and Nicaraguan. Strength comes from one retailer; the maker only says balanced.

cigars.about: One of the two cigars that launched the Ferio Tego name in 2021, made by Plasencia in Nicaragua in a single 6 x 50 toro. It is released in dated yearly vintages, each a fresh take on the blend.
cigars.researchNote: Released as yearly vintages (2021 to 2024 so far), so flavors shift from year to year. The maker calls the Honduran wrapper dark and sun grown, while halfwheel's 2021 coverage described it as shade grown.

cigars.about: The lighter partner to Generoso, launched with it in 2021 as the first cigars to carry the Ferio Tego name. Quesada makes it in the Dominican Republic in a single 6 x 50 toro, released in dated yearly vintages.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the wrapper only as light, shade-grown Ecuadorian leaf and does not name the seed; halfwheel says it looks and smokes like Connecticut shade. The maker rates the body full, but halfwheel found the nicotine strength mild, so strength is left blank.

cigars.about: A mellow Connecticut-wrapped cigar with a sweetened cap, long sold as Nat Sherman Host and now part of Ferio Tego's Metropolitan Selection. It is made in Honduras at Davidoff's Diadema Cigars de Honduras factory.
cigars.researchNote: The cap is sweetened. Sources disagree on where the Connecticut wrapper is grown: Famous Smoke says U.S. Connecticut and Neptune says Ecuador, and the maker just says Connecticut. Neptune lists it mild; Famous Smoke lists medium but describes it as a mild cigar.

cigars.about: The original Flor de Selva blend from Maya Selva, a Honduran puro with a Connecticut-seed wrapper grown in Honduras. It is known for a balanced, woody profile.
cigars.researchNote: Made by Maya Selva Cigars, which calls this line Coleccion Clasica. Halfwheel names the factory as Plasencia's Tabacos de Oriente, while Neptune lists San Judas Tadeo in Danli. Neptune gives the filler as Jamastran viso and Azacualpa ligero.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Maya Selva's Flor de Selva, with a naturally fermented Honduran Habano wrapper from the Jamastran valley over Honduran filler. The maker describes it as bold but not aggressive.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the binder: halfwheel's 2016 report and Neptune say Brazilian Mata Fina, while halfwheel's 2023 report says the binder is Honduran from Jamastran, so it is left blank. The company calls it medium to full bodied; Neptune lists medium strength.

cigars.about: The long-running Dominican Fonseca that the Quesada family made from 1974, with a Connecticut Shade wrapper over Dominican binder and filler. It is the older, lighter counterpart to the Nicaraguan Fonseca from My Father.
cigars.researchNote: This is the Quesada-made Dominican blend. My Father Cigars bought the U.S. Fonseca brand in December 2019 and its own Fonseca is a different, Nicaraguan cigar. Strength is disputed: Manuel Quesada called it a medium smoke in 2018, while Cigar Aficionado called it a mild blend. Sources do not agree on where the wrapper is grown.

cigars.about: The Garcia family's take on Fonseca, released in 2020 after My Father Cigars bought the U.S. rights to the brand from Quesada. It is a Nicaraguan puro made from the family's own tobacco, fuller than the old mild Dominican Fonseca.
cigars.researchNote: My Father only names the wrapper varietal; binder and filler are just listed as Nicaraguan. The Cedros comes in a cedar sleeve and the Cosacos in tissue paper.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA, Aganorsa)
cigars.about: The first cigar from Nicholas Melillo's Foundation Cigar Co., a Nicaraguan puro made entirely from Aganorsa tobacco. It is named for a Nicaraguan folk drama whose title means the wise man.
cigars.researchNote: Discontinued in 2024 when Foundation stopped working with Aganorsa. The Wise Man Corojo, made at My Father, took its place.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro with a Corojo 99 wrapper that Foundation introduced in 2024 as the successor to El Güegüense. It is made by the Garcia family at My Father Cigars in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: Replaced El Güegüense (which means the wise man) when Foundation moved from Aganorsa to My Father in 2024. Flavor words are the maker's description of the Lancero size.

cigars.line: The Tabernacle Havana Seed CT No. 142
cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A version of The Tabernacle that swaps the Broadleaf wrapper for Havana Seed CT No. 142, a Cuban-seed leaf grown in Connecticut that Foundation says needs three years of fermentation. Made at AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is Cuban-seed tobacco grown in Connecticut, not Broadleaf or Shade and not a Habano from Ecuador or Nicaragua. Same binder and filler regions as the Broadleaf Tabernacle.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The Connecticut Broadleaf version of Foundation's value-priced Charter Oak, made at AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua. Nicholas Melillo blended it as a nod to the broadleaf cigars his grandfather smoked in Connecticut.
cigars.researchNote: Foundation calls this one Charter Oak CT Broadleaf; shops often list it as Charter Oak Maduro.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The third Charter Oak blend, added in 2020 to sit between the Shade and the Broadleaf in strength. It has an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco and is made at AJ Fernandez.
cigars.researchNote: Foundation says it was named Cigar Aficionado's number one best value cigar.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The darker and stronger of Foundation's two Olmec blends, with a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is made at AJ Fernandez and named for the ancient civilization of the San Andrés region.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel lists the Double Corona as 7 x 52, the maker as 7 x 54.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Varies by size: Connecticut Shade, Connecticut Broadleaf, Sumatra or Candela
cigars.about: Foundation's Jamaican-themed infused line, built around Jamaican Cow Tongue filler tobacco blended with Nicaraguan leaf. It is named after Lee "Scratch" Perry's band and each size has its own wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: This is an infused, sweet cigar, not a traditional one. Wrapper depends on the size: Zola and Original Rude Boy are Broadleaf, Django is Sumatra, Para El Sapo is Candela, the rest Connecticut Shade. The Skipper and Para El Sapo are figurados tapering from 38 to 54 ring. Factory is not disclosed.

cigars.about: A box-pressed San Andrés-wrapped cigar with a pigtail cap that began in 2017 as an event-only smoke and went on sale in 2019 in small quarterly batches. It is named for Menelik I of Ethiopia, the son of King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba.
cigars.researchNote: Released at about 1,000 boxes of 12 per quarter. Made by Aganorsa, which Foundation stopped using for its main lines in 2024. Menelik is no longer on Foundation's site and Neptune lists it as sold out or discontinued, so it may be gone. A Corona Gorda (5 5/8 x 46) was a store exclusive.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A soft box-pressed Foundation line built around an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, sold in Claro and Maduro versions and made at AJ Fernandez. It launched in 2023 as Metapa, after the birthplace of Nicaraguan poet Rubén Darío.
cigars.researchNote: Renamed Aksum in February 2024 with new bands; the blend did not change. Comes in Claro and Maduro, both Ecuadorian Sumatra. Flavor words are from halfwheel's review of the Claro.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Jalapa, Ometepe; Criollo, Corojo and Nicadan)
cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A collaboration between Nicholas Melillo and the Earl of Carnarvon, owner of Highclere Castle, the house seen in Downton Abbey. It is a Connecticut Shade cigar meant to recall what was smoked at the castle around 1900, made at AJ Fernandez.
cigars.researchNote: First released in 2017 simply as Highclere Castle; the Edwardian name sets it apart from the darker Victorian. Foundation only says Connecticut Shade. Halfwheel describes the wrapper as Ecuadorian, while Neptune lists U.S. Connecticut Shade. Sold under the Highclere Castle Cigar Co. name and distributed by Foundation.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Estelí, Jalapa, Ometepe; Criollo and Corojo)
cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The darker follow-up to the original Highclere Castle cigar, added in 2019 with a higher-priming Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. It keeps the Brazilian Mata Fina binder and is made at AJ Fernandez in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: Often described as the maduro version of Highclere Castle, but the wrapper is a dark Habano, not Broadleaf. Sold under the Highclere Castle Cigar Co. name and distributed by Foundation.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The original Fratello blend, launched in 2013 by Omar de Frias while he was still working at NASA, and made at Joya de Nicaragua. It has a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper over an Ecuadorian binder with Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler.
cigars.researchNote: Originally just called Fratello; the Classico name was adopted in 2018. Strength and body are from Neptune, which lists Medium strength and calls it medium to full-bodied. Fratello does not give a rating. The Boxer is a box-pressed torpedo.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: Fratello's second line and its maduro, released in 2015 with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper. The name means white in Italian and refers to the white band, not the cigar, which is dark.
cigars.researchNote: Despite the name this is a maduro. The Bianco I lonsdale (6 1/4 x 44) was dropped in 2023. Strength is from Neptune and halfwheel's review; Fratello does not list one.

cigars.about: Fratello's Connecticut Shade cigar, introduced in 2016 and the first Fratello made in the Dominican Republic, at La Aurora. It pairs an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper with a Cameroon binder.
cigars.researchNote: Strength varies by source: Neptune lists Mild, while halfwheel's review put strength at medium to medium-plus with full flavor. Fratello gives no rating. Fratello adds Colombian filler that halfwheel does not list. Halfwheel and Neptune give the Corona a 47 ring; Fratello says 46.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: Omar de Frias's tribute to his 12 years at NASA; navetta is Italian for shuttle and each size is named after a space shuttle. It has a dark Ecuadorian oscuro wrapper and is made at Joya de Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is only described as Ecuadorian oscuro, a very dark leaf; the seed type is not published. Strength is Neptune's rating, Fratello does not list one. The 6 x 60 Enterprise was dropped in 2023. Navetta Inverso is a separate line with the blend components flipped.

cigars.about: A mellow, value-priced Honduran cigar from Altadis U.S.A., rolled at the Flor de Copan factory with an Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper. The Gispert name goes back to a 19th century Cuban brand.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis calls this Gispert Natural; shops usually list it simply as Gispert. Altadis describes it as mellow to medium, Neptune lists Mild and Holt's lists Medium. The stronger Gispert Intenso, made by AJ Fernandez, is a different cigar.

cigars.about: The God of Fire blend created by Carlos Fuente Sr., rolled by Arturo Fuente for Keith Park's Prometheus company. It is the medium-bodied counterpart to the Cameroon-wrapped by Carlito blend, and each band carries the year the cigars were made.
cigars.researchNote: Maker only says the wrapper is Ecuadorian. Halfwheel calls it Ecuadorian Sumatra; Corona Cigar lists Ecuadorian Habano. Maker calls it medium bodied, while retailers list medium-full to full. Made in small yearly batches; also sold as a Robusto Tubo.

cigars.about: The God of Fire blend created by Carlos "Carlito" Fuente Jr., rolled by Arturo Fuente for Keith Park's Prometheus company. The maker calls it the boldest God of Fire, with a Cameroon wrapper over Dominican binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Maker describes it as medium to heavy; Corona Cigar and Neptune call it full. Made in small yearly batches with the production year on the second band. Halfwheel lists the Diademas 56 at 5 3/4 x 56; the maker lists 6 1/4 x 56.

cigars.wrapperOrigin: USA or Ecuador, depending on size
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro (Double Robusto, Gran Toro, Diademas 56) or Ecuadorian Sun Grown (Robusto, Robusto Gordo 54)
cigars.about: A darker-wrapped God of Fire line rolled by Arturo Fuente for Prometheus, added in 2011. The wrapper depends on the size: Connecticut Broadleaf maduro on some, Ecuadorian sun grown on others, all over Dominican binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrappers in one line, so check the size: Robusto and Robusto Gordo 54 are Ecuadorian Sun Grown, the others Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro. Maker gives no strength rating; halfwheel found it medium to medium-full and Corona Cigar lists full. Made in small yearly batches.

cigars.about: The mildest of Gran Habano's three core blends from the Rico family, rolled at their factory in Danli, Honduras. A Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Maker only says Connecticut wrapper. Holt's lists it as Ecuador-grown Connecticut and Neptune as USA Connecticut Shade, so the origin is left blank. Maker rates it mild; Holt's says mild-medium and Neptune medium. Maker gives a single rating, labeled body, used here as strength.

cigars.about: The middle of Gran Habano's three core blends, which the Rico family calls its classic blend. A Nicaraguan Habano wrapper and binder over Nicaraguan, Mexican and Costa Rican filler, rolled in Danli, Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Maker's spec line and Holt's say medium to full, but the maker's own description and Neptune call it medium. Maker gives a single rating, labeled body, used here as strength.

cigars.about: The strongest of Gran Habano's three core blends, with a reddish Nicaraguan Corojo wrapper and a full, spicy profile. Rolled by the Rico family in Danli, Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Maker lists about 15 sizes, including a 7 x 70 Grandioso; 10 of them are listed here. Maker gives a single rating, labeled body, used here as strength.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Gran Habano's full-bodied Corojo #5, with a dark sun-grown Nicaraguan wrapper over the same Nicaraguan and Costa Rican filler. Rolled at the Rico family's factory in Danli, Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Maker lists a Nicaraguan Habano binder; halfwheel reported in 2015 that wrapper and binder are Nicaraguan Corojo, and Neptune lists a Costa Rican binder. Launch year not found; it got new bands and boxes in 2015. Maker gives a single rating, labeled body, used here as strength.

cigars.about: A Gran Habano line released in 2016 whose name means the conquest, with sizes named after Columbus's three ships. A Nicaraguan Corojo wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler from Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Colombia, sold in boxes of 24.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel lists the binder as Nicaraguan Corojo. Its reviewer found the cigar closer to medium than the maker's medium to full rating. Maker gives a single rating, labeled body, used here as strength.

cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped line from Gran Habano, shipped in late 2018 and sold in cedar sleeves. It was made to show a Connecticut cigar does not have to be mild.
cigars.researchNote: Maker lists Nicaraguan and Costa Rican filler; halfwheel and Neptune list Nicaraguan only. Maker now rates it medium, though it was announced as mild to medium. Maker gives a single rating, labeled body, used here as strength.

cigars.about: The original Graycliff blend and the company's first line, rolled at its factory in Nassau, Bahamas. Graycliff Cigar Company was started in 1997 by Enrico Garzaroli of the Graycliff hotel with Cuban blender Avelino Lara.
cigars.researchNote: Also called Graycliff Original. Maker publishes no blend. A 2011 Cigar Coop review and Cigars Direct both give an Indonesian wrapper but disagree on the filler. Graycliff reworked its blends and cut sizes in 2015, so the size list may be out of date. Sold as medium, though that review found it mild.

cigars.about: Graycliff's second line after the Red Label, properly called the Profesionale Series and commonly known as the Blue Label. It is rolled at the Graycliff factory in Nassau, Bahamas.
cigars.researchNote: Blue Label is the nickname for the Profesionale Series. Blend is from Neptune's listing; the maker publishes none. A 2007 review listed an Indonesian wrapper and binder with Brazilian, Nicaraguan and Honduran filler, so the blend has changed over time. Confirm against the box before quoting.

cigars.about: A separate brand from Graycliff Cigar Company, which lists it alongside its main Graycliff line. Retailers describe a mild to medium Connecticut-wrapped cigar with nutty, toasty flavors.
cigars.researchNote: Maker publishes no blend. Wrapper, strength and Nicaraguan origin come from Cigars Direct, whose product pages list Nicaraguan filler only while its line description adds Dominican. The 2026 Tasters size is rolled in Nassau.

cigars.about: Introduced in late 2003 as the fullest-bodied Graycliff blend, created by Avelino Lara with owner Enrico Garzaroli. It is rolled in Nassau, Bahamas, with a dark, rough Costa Rican wrapper, and is also known as the Black Label.
cigars.researchNote: Binder is disputed: halfwheel says Cameroon, Corona Cigar says undisclosed and Cigars Direct lists Costa Rican. Halfwheel's reviewer found it nearer medium in strength. Other sizes such as the Elegante lancero were store exclusives. Do not confuse it with the separate Double Espresso line.

cigars.about: A Dominican cigar from Gurkha built around tobacco the company says is aged 15 years, sold in boxes styled like wine barrels. It launched as a brick and mortar exclusive.
cigars.researchNote: Gurkha's 2011 launch release listed the filler as Nicaraguan criollo; its site now says Dominican. A separate limited 6 x 52 15-Year Cellar Reserve from 2017, made for the line's tenth year, used an Ecuadorian rosado wrapper.

cigars.about: The Nicaraguan entry in Gurkha's Cellar Reserve family, with binder and filler tobacco the company says is aged up to 12 years. It comes in three thick sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Gurkha calls the wrapper Ecuadorian oscuro and does not name the seed type. The factory is as reported at the 2015 launch.

cigars.about: A dark Brazilian maduro wrapped cigar from Gurkha, made in the Dominican Republic and first shipped around Halloween 2012.
cigars.researchNote: Gurkha's site currently lists three sizes: Shadow, Asura and Exorcist. Ghost Gold and Ghost Connecticut are separate blends.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA, Aganorsa Leaf)
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made for Gurkha at the Aganorsa factory using Aganorsa tobacco. It was the first Gurkha made there and the company billed it as its fullest cigar to date.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to select retailers at its 2019 launch and not on Gurkha's current site. Gurkha first described the strength as medium to three-quarters and later called it its fullest cigar; Cigar Aficionado says medium to full.

cigars.about: Gurkha's Connecticut shade cigar, introduced in 2011 as a brick and mortar exclusive at a modest price. It got new packaging in 2022 with the blend unchanged.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers disagree on where it is rolled: Mike's Cigars says Dominican Republic and Neptune says Nicaragua. Gurkha's current site does not list the line, though retailers still sell it. The Royal Challenge Maduro (2015) has been discontinued.

cigars.about: A mild Connecticut wrapped Dominican cigar from Gurkha. It is sold in frosted tubes in boxes of 25.
cigars.researchNote: Gurkha's site says only Connecticut for the wrapper; Neptune specifies Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade. Gurkha lists one size, the XO. The 25th Anniversary Beauty is a separate cigar.

cigars.about: A Gurkha cigar with a dark Costa Rican maduro wrapper, rolled in Costa Rica and sold in black lacquered boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Gurkha says only 1,000 boxes are made a year and lists one size, the XO.

cigars.about: Gurkha's flagship cognac infused cigar, a Dominican blend under a Connecticut Shade wrapper. Each cigar comes in a glass tube sealed with wax.
cigars.researchNote: Gurkha's site lists the strength as medium to full, but Neptune describes it as mild bodied. Neptune lists the wrapper as US-grown Connecticut Shade and the origin as Honduras; Gurkha says Dominican Republic.

cigars.about: A Gurkha blend with a dark Brazilian maduro wrapper over a Dominican binder and Nicaraguan filler. Cigar Aficionado scored the Torpedo 90 points in 2010.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on where it is rolled: Cigar Aficionado says Dominican Republic, Neptune says Honduras, and Mike's lists Nicaragua on one size and Dominican Republic on another. Cigar Coop names the wrapper as Brazilian Mata Fina. Not on Gurkha's current site. Pure Evil is a separate blend.

cigars.about: A limited Gurkha double perfecto made in the Dominican Republic. Neptune Cigar repeats the story that the blend was first made for the Sultan of Brunei.
cigars.researchNote: Blend details come from Neptune's listing only; Gurkha does not list it. Neptune describes the wrapper as Connecticut Shade but colorado maduro in color, so it is darker than a typical Connecticut.

cigars.about: The core non-Cuban H. Upmann from Altadis U.S.A., rolled in the Dominican Republic with an Ecuadorian wrapper. It was repackaged in 2020 with the blend unchanged.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis calls the wrapper Ecuadorian Cubano; Neptune lists it as Ecuadorian Habano. Altadis lists the Demitasse at 5 1/4 inches; halfwheel reported 5 1/2.

cigars.about: A Honduran made H. Upmann from Altadis U.S.A. in which every tobacco is aged at least five years. It joined the repackaged 1844 line in 2020.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis and Mike's Cigars call it medium to full; Neptune rates it full.

cigars.about: A Dominican made H. Upmann from Altadis U.S.A. wrapped in aged Cameroon leaf, a nod to the wrapper the non-Cuban brand used in its early days. It is part of the 1844 line.
cigars.researchNote: Also written as 1844 Vintage Cameroon since the 2020 repackaging. Mike's Cigars lists the strength as full, while Altadis and Neptune call it medium.

cigars.about: A Dominican made H. Upmann from Altadis U.S.A. released in 2014, sold on the story of the cigar the Upmann brothers kept in their bank vault for favored clients.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers rate it medium; Altadis describes it as robust and full flavored. The Banker Daytrader is a separate line.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: An H. Upmann blended and rolled by AJ Fernandez in Estelí for Altadis U.S.A., launched in 2017. Altadis credits it with strong growth for the brand.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as H. Upmann Nicaragua by AJ Fernandez; it is the same cigar. Neptune rates it medium. A 4 x 38 Papi in tins was added in 2019.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The Sumatra wrapped H. Upmann made by AJ Fernandez in Estelí for Altadis U.S.A., launched in 2017. It is the same cigar that is also labeled H. Upmann by AJ Fernandez.
cigars.researchNote: Same cigar as H. Upmann by AJ Fernandez; both names are used. Do not confuse it with H. Upmann Nicaragua AJ Fernandez Heritage, a different blend with a Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper.

cigars.about: A Connecticut wrapped H. Upmann blended by Altadis U.S.A.'s Grupo de Maestros and rolled in La Romana. It was pitched as bolder than a typical Connecticut and has a dark maduro cap.
cigars.researchNote: Full name is H. Upmann Connecticut by Grupo de Maestros. It is no longer listed on Altadis U.S.A.'s site, though some retailers still stock it.

cigars.about: An H. Upmann line extension from Altadis U.S.A. launched in 2013, made in Honduras with a dark Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. It was billed as a bolder take on the brand.
cigars.researchNote: No longer listed on Altadis U.S.A.'s site and out of stock at retailers checked, so it appears to be out of production. Neptune's product pages say medium, its line page says medium to full.

cigars.about: An H. Upmann from Altadis U.S.A. released in 2019 as a tribute to brand founder Hermann Upmann. It was blended by Rafael Nodal with the Grupo de Maestros and every size has a pigtail cap.
cigars.researchNote: No longer listed on Altadis U.S.A.'s site and Neptune marks it discontinued, though some retailers still have stock.

cigars.about: A box pressed Henry Clay from Altadis U.S.A.'s Grupo de Maestros, released in 2016 as the regular production follow up to the Henry Clay Tattoo. The name refers to the way broadleaf is harvested by cutting the whole plant.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers list it as full, but halfwheel's reviewer found it stayed around medium. It is no longer on Altadis U.S.A.'s site and Neptune marks it discontinued, though some retailers still have stock.

cigars.about: A Henry Clay from Altadis U.S.A. launched in 2019 that breaks with the brand's habit of broadleaf wrappers, putting the broadleaf on the binder under an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. It is rolled in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis and retailers list the Corona at 5 x 44; halfwheel reported 5 1/2 x 44 at launch. Neptune says it is made in the Dominican Republic, but the maker says Honduras. War Hawk Rebellious is a separate limited edition.

cigars.about: A slim, rough looking Henry Clay from Altadis U.S.A. with a pigtail cap and closed foot, sold in one size. Its filler uses second growth leaves the company calls capa dura.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis lists a broadleaf binder; halfwheel reported a Honduran binder at launch and Neptune says Dominican. Altadis gives no strength rating, only that it is a robust, stronger blend; Neptune says medium on one page and full bodied on another.

cigars.about: A mild to medium cigar in Hiram & Solomon's Masonic-themed core line, named for the first degree of Freemasonry. It pairs a Honduran-grown Connecticut Shade wrapper with a three-country filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it mild to medium; Neptune lists it as mild. It was first made at Plasencia in Nicaragua, and production moved to PDR Cigars in the Dominican Republic in 2022.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Habano Jalapa, Habano Ometepe, Habano Esteli ligero)
cigars.about: The middle cigar of Hiram & Solomon's three Masonic degree blends, named for the second degree of Freemasonry. It uses a dark Habano wrapper over an Indonesian binder and Nicaraguan fillers.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium to full; Neptune lists it as medium. The maker does not say where the wrapper is grown. Production moved from Plasencia in Nicaragua to PDR Cigars in the Dominican Republic in 2022.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Habano Jalapa, Habano Ometepe, Habano Esteli ligero)
cigars.about: The fullest of Hiram & Solomon's three Masonic degree blends, named for the third degree of Freemasonry. It wears a dark Habano maduro wrapper over an Indonesian binder and Nicaraguan fillers.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not say where the wrapper is grown. Production moved from Plasencia in Nicaragua to PDR Cigars in the Dominican Republic in 2022.

cigars.filler: Brazil (Arapiraca), Nicaragua (Habano Jalapa, Habano Ometepe), Dominican Republic
cigars.about: A medium-bodied Hiram & Solomon core blend named for a term used by Freemasons. It uses Indonesian wrapper and binder over fillers from Brazil, Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Production moved from Plasencia in Nicaragua to PDR Cigars in the Dominican Republic in 2022.

cigars.about: The long-running Honduran Excalibur line from the non-Cuban Hoyo de Monterrey brand, made by General Cigar. The natural version has a Connecticut Shade wrapper and comes mostly in large sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it mellow to medium, while Neptune says medium and Holt's says medium-full. Retailers date the line to the 1970s without giving a year. Also sold as cigarillos and miniatures.

cigars.about: The maduro version of the Honduran Excalibur line from the non-Cuban Hoyo de Monterrey brand. It swaps the Connecticut Shade wrapper for Connecticut Broadleaf over the same three-country filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium; Holt's lists Excalibur as medium-full. Also sold as cigarillos and miniatures.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A 2016 collaboration between General Cigar's Hoyo de Monterrey brand and AJ Fernandez, who blended it and rolls it at his factory in Esteli. La Amistad means friendship in Spanish.
cigars.researchNote: Now sold as La Amistad Gold. The maker's site lists an Ecuadorian Criollo wrapper, but General Cigar's own store description, halfwheel and Neptune say Ecuadorian Habano. The maker lists the Robusto at 5.25 x 54; halfwheel and Neptune say 5 x 54. Neptune rates it full.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A 2018 follow-up to Hoyo La Amistad, again blended and rolled by AJ Fernandez in Esteli for General Cigar. It has a dark Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over a Mexican San Andres binder and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium to full; Neptune lists it as full. halfwheel's launch story gave the Gigante as 6 x 60, while the maker lists 5 7/8 x 60.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A dark Ecuadorian Sumatra-wrapped Hoyo de Monterrey blend. Since 2019 it has been made by AJ Fernandez in Esteli and sold under the La Amistad name, replacing the Honduran-made original.
cigars.researchNote: The original Hoyo Dark Sumatra was made at STG Danli in Honduras. Since 2019 the same blend has been made by AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua and sold as La Amistad Dark Sumatra. The maker rates it medium to full; Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.about: The short robusto size of the core Honduran Hoyo de Monterrey line from General Cigar. It measures 4.5 x 50 and is sold in both Sumatra and maduro wrappers.
cigars.researchNote: Rothschild is one size (4.5 x 50) of the core Hoyo de Monterrey line, not a line of its own. Details here are for the Sumatra version; the Maduro version has a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper and Connecticut Shade binder. The La Amistad lines also have a Rothschild size. Holt's rates the line medium-full.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro from HVC made with Aganorsa tobaccos from Jalapa, named for the Havana street address where founder Reinier Lorenzo lived. It debuted in 2015 and every size has been a small limited run.
cigars.researchNote: Details are for the original 2015 blend. The 2022 Rare of Rare (made in Miami at El Titan de Bronze, Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper) and the 2025 10 Year Anniversary (Ecuadorian Habano 92 wrapper) are different blends. No maker strength rating; halfwheel's reviews found it medium, building toward full.

cigars.binder: Nicaragua (Corojo 99 from Jalapa, Corojo 98 from Esteli)
cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos HVC S.A. de Reinier Lorenzo
cigars.about: HVC's regular-production San Andres maduro, launched in 2020 as a follow-up to the limited Pan Caliente. It uses Aganorsa-grown Nicaraguan corojo under a Mexican wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Now also called Hot Cake Maduro, since a Golden Line (Ecuadorian Connecticut) and a Broadleaf version were added. It was first made by Aganorsa at the TABSA factory and is now made at HVC's own factory in Esteli. Neptune calls it fuller bodied but lists strength as medium.

cigars.about: HVC's first Connecticut Broadleaf cigar, made with Aganorsa-grown Nicaraguan binder and filler. It began in 2018 as a 500-box limited edition and became regular production in 2019.
cigars.researchNote: Full name is First Selection Limited Edition Broadleaf. It was the first broadleaf-wrapped cigar made at Aganorsa's TABSA factory. halfwheel's review rated the strength medium-full; Neptune lists it as medium. Not the same cigar as HVC Seleccion No. 1.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos HVC S.A. de Reinier Lorenzo
cigars.about: The first line made at HVC's own factory in Esteli, which founder Reinier Lorenzo opened in 2022. It is a San Andres-wrapped Nicaraguan blend done in an old Cuban style.
cigars.researchNote: Details are for the original San Andres blend, now sold as Seleccion No. 1 Maduro. A Natural (Ecuadorian Habano 92, 2023) and a Connecticut (Ecuadorian Connecticut, 2024) come in the same three sizes. Neptune lists it as medium, but halfwheel and Cigar Coop both found it full strength.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (Aganorsa Leaf)
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro from HVC named for the grade A Aganorsa tobacco it is made from, with a corojo 99 wrapper. It launched in 2019 as a regular-production line.
