cigars.researchNote: Also sold as Nub Double Maduro and not shown on Oliva's Nub site. Neptune and Cigars Direct rate it full, CigarPlace medium-full. CigarPlace says the second maduro leaf doubles as the binder, while Neptune and Cigars Direct list a Nicaraguan binder.

cigars.about: A full-bodied Oliva line built around fermented Jalapa Valley ligero under a high-priming sun grown wrapper. It debuted in 2007 and has been a regular on Cigar Aficionado's year-end lists.
cigars.researchNote: Oliva lists an Ecuadorian sun grown wrapper, which halfwheel and Holt's call Ecuadorian Habano; Neptune's spec table says Ecuadorian Sumatra seed. Holt's rates it full strength while Neptune lists medium.

cigars.about: A box-pressed step up from the Serie V, named for Melanio Oliva, who first grew tobacco in Cuba in 1886. The Figurado was Cigar Aficionado's Cigar of the Year for 2014 with a 96 rating.
cigars.researchNote: Strength varies by source: Holt's says medium-full, Neptune medium, and Famous and halfwheel's 2012 review full. Oliva and Neptune list the Figurado at 6.5 x 54; Holt's and Famous list 6.5 x 52.

cigars.about: The Serie V Melanio blend with the Ecuadorian wrapper swapped for a Mexican San Andrés maduro. It launched in 2013 as a single Torpedo and has since grown to match the Melanio size list.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's lists strength as medium-full; Neptune lists full.

cigars.about: The maduro version of the Serie V, with Nicaraguan ligero under a Mexican San Andrés wrapper. It ran as a once-a-year limited edition from 2008 and became a regular production line in 2019.
cigars.researchNote: Oliva now calls it Serie V Maduro; Maduro Especial was the name of the yearly limited edition that began in 2008. The 2008 release used Connecticut Broadleaf and 2009 a Nicaraguan Habano maduro; San Andrés has been the wrapper since 2010.

cigars.about: A medium-strength Oliva core line built on Habano-seed tobacco from Esteli, Condega and Jalapa. It dates to 2001, when it was sold as Serie O Bold, and took its current name in 2006.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper origin is disputed. Oliva's spec table and Holt's say Ecuador, but Oliva's own description still calls it a sun grown puro, and Neptune and Famous list a Nicaraguan wrapper. It was long sold as a Nicaraguan Habano puro.

cigars.about: The Serie O blend of Nicaraguan sun grown binder and filler finished with a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper. Oliva describes it as full-bodied but smooth.
cigars.researchNote: Oliva calls it full-bodied and Neptune lists full strength; Holt's lists medium-full.

cigars.about: A medium-bodied Oliva line with an African Cameroon wrapper over Nicaraguan sun grown tobacco, sold mostly box-pressed. It debuted in 2006 after the Oliva Grand Cameroon was discontinued.
cigars.researchNote: Oliva and Holt's call it medium; Neptune lists it as mild.

cigars.about: The maduro counterpart to the Cameroon-wrapped Serie G, box-pressed and medium-bodied. Oliva now lists a Mexican wrapper over Nicaraguan sun grown filler.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the wrapper: halfwheel's 2013 review listed Connecticut Broadleaf, while Oliva lists a Mexican wrapper that Holt's and Neptune call San Andrés. Oliva lists a Mexican binder; Neptune and halfwheel list Nicaraguan. Oliva lists the Torpedo at 6 x 52; retailers list 6.5 x 52.

cigars.about: Oliva's mellow Connecticut offering: an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan long filler and binder. It is pitched as an any-time-of-day smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Oliva calls it medium-bodied but mellow; Holt's lists mild-medium strength and Neptune lists mild.

cigars.about: The third release in Oliva's Master Blends series of small-batch blends, pairing Nicaraguan ligero with a sun grown Broadleaf wrapper. It came out in 2006, after Master Blends 1 in 2003 and Master Blends 2 in 2005.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's lists medium-full strength; Neptune lists full. Oliva lists the Torpedo at 6.5 x 52, but halfwheel, Holt's and Neptune list 6 x 52. halfwheel and Holt's also list a 5 x 54 Double Robusto.

cigars.about: A Cigars International exclusive made by Oliva, blended only from tobacco of a single crop year. It pairs an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper with Nicaraguan filler from Oliva's farms in Somoto, Esteli and Condega.
cigars.researchNote: A Cigars International exclusive made by Oliva. Only the 6 x 50 Toro could be confirmed. Strength and flavors come from a Blind Man's Puff panel review.

cigars.about: Oliva's long-filler value bundle, with a Sumatra wrapper over aged Nicaraguan tobacco. It is sold in bundles of 20 and has Gold, Corojo and Maduro siblings.
cigars.researchNote: This entry is the original Sumatra-wrapped blend. Flor de Oliva Gold, Corojo and Maduro are separate blends with Ecuadorian wrappers.

cigars.about: A value-priced Oliva line named for family patriarch Gilberto Oliva Sr., with a dark Sumatra wrapper over an Ecuadorian binder and Nicaraguan filler. It was Oliva's first new line since 2012 when it shipped in 2017.
cigars.researchNote: It was announced in 2016 as Facundo and renamed Gilberto before the 2017 release because of a trademark conflict with Bacardi.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped sibling of the Gilberto Oliva Reserva, sharing its Ecuadorian binder and Nicaraguan filler. It began shipping in August 2017 in the same five sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists it as mild; halfwheel's review put the strength between mild and medium.

cigars.about: A ligero-heavy, full-bodied Nicaraguan puro that Oliva makes for Famous Smoke Shop, sold as Inferno by Oliva. It was introduced in 2012 and has since spawned Flashpoint, Melt, Scorch and other offshoots.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Inferno by Oliva, a Famous Smoke Shop brand rather than part of Oliva's own catalog. Famous lists a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper and all-Nicaraguan tobacco but no separate binder. Flashpoint, Melt, Scorch, Singe and 3rd Degree are separate Inferno blends.

cigars.about: A budget-priced, full-bodied blend Oliva makes for Famous Smoke Shop, sold as Baptiste by Oliva. The original has an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan long filler and launched in 2016.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Baptiste by Oliva, a Famous Smoke Shop exclusive rather than part of Oliva's own catalog. This entry is the original Habano blend; Famous also sells Baptiste Connecticut and Baptiste Maduro. The binder is not published. The 6 x 60 was first called Grand Robusto.

cigars.about: A square-pressed maduro from Altadis USA, made in the Dominican Republic with a dark Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and Dominican, Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis calls it medium to full bodied, and Holt's and Mike's Cigars list it the same way. Altadis lists every size except the Churchill as square pressed.

cigars.about: The Corojo version of Leaf by Oscar, a Honduran puro that comes wrapped in a raw tobacco leaf instead of cellophane. It is made by Oscar Valladares in Danlí for "Island" Jim Robinson's brand.
cigars.researchNote: One of four wrapper versions of Leaf by Oscar. Older halfwheel articles list the toro as 6 x 50; the maker and retailers list 6 x 52.

cigars.about: The Maduro version of Leaf by Oscar, with a Nicaraguan Jalapa maduro wrapper over Honduran tobacco. Like the rest of the line it comes wrapped in a raw tobacco leaf instead of cellophane.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium to full. Famous Smoke lists Full and Neptune lists Medium. Older halfwheel articles list the toro as 6 x 50; the maker and retailers list 6 x 52. The 8 x 66 Big Johnny is based on this blend.

cigars.about: The Connecticut version of Leaf by Oscar, the mildest of the four wrappers, over Honduran binder and filler. It comes wrapped in a raw tobacco leaf instead of cellophane.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists a Honduran wrapper and mild to medium strength. Famous Smoke lists Medium. Neptune and an early Cigar Coop review call the wrapper Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade. Older halfwheel articles list the toro as 6 x 50; the maker and retailers list 6 x 52.

cigars.about: The Sumatra version of Leaf by Oscar, with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Honduran binder and filler. Like the rest of the line it comes wrapped in a raw tobacco leaf instead of cellophane.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on strength: the maker lists Medium, Famous Smoke and Neptune list Full, and Cigar Coop's review rated it medium to full with medium body. Older halfwheel articles list the toro as 6 x 50; the maker and retailers list 6 x 52.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Honduran cigar with a sun-grown Honduran Corojo wrapper, made by Oscar Valladares in Danlí. The name goes back to his first cigar line from 2012, which he brought back in 2017 for the company's fifth anniversary.
cigars.researchNote: The original 2012 by Oscar came out in 2012; this is the 2017 relaunch, briefly called the Rebirth Edition. The maker, Famous Smoke and Neptune all list Medium. The maker lists the short robusto as 4 x 50; halfwheel and retailers list 4 x 54.

cigars.about: The maduro version of the box-pressed 2012 by Oscar line, with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over a Honduran binder. Oscar Valladares makes it in Danlí, Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Some retailers sell it as 2012 by Oscar San Andres. The maker lists Nicaraguan filler and medium to full strength; halfwheel's 2017 launch coverage listed Honduran and Nicaraguan filler, and Famous Smoke lists Medium. The maker lists the short robusto as 4 x 50; halfwheel and retailers list 4 x 54.

cigars.about: The Connecticut version of the box-pressed 2012 by Oscar line, with a Honduran-grown Connecticut-seed wrapper over a Honduran binder and Honduran and Nicaraguan filler. Oscar Valladares makes it in Danlí, Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists a Honduran wrapper and Mild strength. Retailers disagree: Famous Smoke lists an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper and Medium, Neptune lists U.S. Connecticut Shade and Mild. The maker lists the short robusto as 4 x 50; halfwheel and retailers list 4 x 54.

cigars.about: A line from Oscar Valladares launched in 2019 and billed by the company as its strongest blend at the time. It was the first Valladares cigar to use Dominican tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it strong and full bodied. Famous Smoke lists Full, Neptune lists Medium, and halfwheel's review found it medium-full. A separate Super Fly Connecticut with a Honduran Connecticut wrapper also exists.

cigars.about: A Honduran toro named after Altar Q, a Mayan monument at Copán in western Honduras. Each box holds 16 cigars, and each one wears a different band showing one of the 16 rulers carved on the altar.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in one size only. The full name on the box is Altar Q by Oscar Valladares.

cigars.about: A follow-up to Super Fly from Oscar Valladares, themed on Back to the Future with a holographic 1980s-style box. It uses a Mexican wrapper over a Honduran binder and filler from three countries.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium to full; Famous Smoke and Neptune list Medium. Halfwheel lists the wrapper only as Mexican; the maker and Famous Smoke specify San Andrés.

cigars.about: A torpedo made to look like a No. 2 pencil, with a dark tip, a light stripe below it and a shaggy foot. It is "Island" Jim Robinson's own brand, made and sold by Oscar Valladares Tobacco & Co. in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: The blend was kept secret at launch. Halfwheel reports a Jalapa habano wrapper and in 2018 described the core as Honduran, but its 2025 review calls the binder and filler undisclosed. Neptune lists Honduran binder and filler and sells it as Island Jim Corojo #2. Strength is from Neptune only.

cigars.about: The first line from Tim Ozgener, son of CAO founder Cano Ozgener, named for the strait in Turkey. It is a box-pressed cigar with two binders, made at Ernesto Perez-Carrillo's factory in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: The company now goes by OZ Family Cigars. The first 2022 batches were made at Tabacalera Pichardo in Nicaragua with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper; production moved to La Alianza with a Habano 2000 wrapper in late 2022. Some retailers still describe the old blend or list it as Medium.

cigars.about: The second regular line from Tim Ozgener's company, made with Ernesto Perez-Carrillo in the Dominican Republic. The name blends Ararat and Masis, two names for the same mountain, as a nod to Cano Ozgener's Armenian roots.
cigars.researchNote: The company now goes by OZ Family Cigars. The maker lists it as medium-full; Neptune lists Medium.

cigars.about: A limited edition toro from Tim Ozgener's company, named after a series of paintings by his late father, CAO founder Cano Ozgener. The original 2022 release was limited to 2,500 boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Specs are for the original 2022 release, which has a yellow ribbon at the foot. Later Red (2023) and Brown (2024) editions are different blends; the Red is made in the Dominican Republic. Neptune lists the original as Medium, while Famous Smoke's description calls it mellow. The company now goes by OZ Family Cigars.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown natural (also sold in Nicaraguan maduro)
cigars.about: The 4000 is the 6 1/2 x 54 toro in the Padrón Series, the company's original core line of Nicaraguan puros. It comes in natural and maduro wrappers and is sold in boxes of 26.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the Padrón Series (Thousand Series), not a separate blend. The maker calls the series medium to full bodied, but Cigar Aficionado rated the natural 4000 Medium and Holt's lists the series as Medium.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown natural (also sold in Nicaraguan maduro)
cigars.about: The 5000 is the 5 1/2 x 56 size in the Padrón Series, the company's original core line of Nicaraguan puros. It comes in natural and maduro wrappers and is sold in boxes of 26.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the Padrón Series (Thousand Series), not a separate blend. The maker calls the series medium to full bodied, but Cigar Aficionado rated the natural 5000 Medium and Holt's lists the series as Medium. Cigar Aficionado files it as a toro while some retailers call it a robusto, so no shape name is given.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown natural (also sold in Nicaraguan maduro)
cigars.about: The 6000 is the 5 1/2 x 52 torpedo in the Padrón Series, the company's original core line of Nicaraguan puros, and the only tapered-head size among the numbered vitolas. It comes in natural and maduro wrappers and is sold in boxes of 26.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the Padrón Series (Thousand Series), not a separate blend. Same 5 1/2 x 52 dimensions as the 3000 but with a tapered head; Holt's calls it a torpedo and Cigar Aficionado a belicoso. Cigar Aficionado rated the natural 6000 Medium-Full, matching the maker's series description, while Holt's lists the series as Medium.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown natural (also sold in Nicaraguan maduro)
cigars.about: The 7000 is the 6 1/4 x 60 size in the Padrón Series, the thickest vitola in the company's original core line of Nicaraguan puros. It comes in natural and maduro wrappers and is sold in boxes of 26.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the Padrón Series (Thousand Series), not a separate blend. The maker calls the series medium to full bodied, but Cigar Aficionado rated the 7000 Maduro Medium and Holt's lists the series as Medium. Padron.com and Cigar Aficionado give 6 1/4 x 60; halfwheel gives 6 1/2 x 60.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown natural (also sold in Nicaraguan maduro)
cigars.about: The Londres is the 5 1/2 x 42 corona in the Padrón Series, the company's original core line of Nicaraguan puros. It comes in natural and maduro wrappers and is sold in boxes of 26.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the Padrón Series, not a separate blend. The maker calls the series medium to full bodied, but Cigar Aficionado rated the natural Londres Medium and Holt's lists the series as Medium.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown natural (also sold in Nicaraguan maduro)
cigars.about: The Delicias is the 4 7/8 x 46 corona extra in the Padrón Series, the company's original core line of Nicaraguan puros. It comes in natural and maduro wrappers and is sold in boxes of 26.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the Padrón Series, not a separate blend. The maker calls the series medium to full bodied, but Neptune lists the Delicias as Medium and Holt's lists the series as Medium.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown natural (also sold in Nicaraguan maduro)
cigars.about: The Ambassador is the 6 7/8 x 42 lonsdale in the Padrón Series, the company's original core line of Nicaraguan puros. It comes in natural and maduro wrappers and is sold in boxes of 26.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the Padrón Series, not a separate blend. Cigar Aficionado rated the natural Ambassador Medium-Full, matching the maker's series description, while Holt's lists the series as Medium.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown natural (also sold in Nicaraguan maduro)
cigars.about: The Executive is the 7 1/2 x 50 double corona in the Padrón Series, the company's original core line of Nicaraguan puros. It comes in natural and maduro wrappers and is sold in boxes of 26.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the Padrón Series, not a separate blend. The maker calls the series medium to full; an older Cigar Aficionado review said medium bodied and Holt's lists the series as Medium. That review gave the country as Nicaragua and Honduras, but Cigar Aficionado later reported Padrón makes all its cigars in Estelí, Nicaragua.

cigars.about: Padrón's milder line, a round cigar with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is named for Dámaso Padrón, the first of the family to arrive in Cuba from the Canary Islands.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it mild and also mild to medium; Cigar Aficionado rates the No. 15 Mild-Medium. The maker says the Red Label No. 32 and No. 34 are for those wanting a more robust profile. The maker calls it limited production, but halfwheel lists it as regular production.

cigars.about: The maduro-wrapped version of Padrón's 1964 Anniversary Series, a box-pressed Nicaraguan puro made with tobacco aged four years. It is offered in the same sizes as the natural.
cigars.researchNote: Same line as the 1964 Anniversary with the maduro wrapper, not a separate blend name on padron.com. Padron.com does not state strength, and Cigar Aficionado's maduro ratings disagree by size: Exclusivo Maduro Full, Diplomatico Maduro Medium. Holt's lists the line as Medium-Full, which is used here.

cigars.about: The maduro-wrapped version of Padrón's 1926 Serie, a box-pressed Nicaraguan puro made with tobacco aged five years. It is offered in the same sizes as the natural.
cigars.researchNote: Same line as the 1926 Serie with the maduro wrapper. 2002 is the year the series premiered; the maker does not give a separate date for the maduro.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown natural (also sold in Nicaraguan maduro)
cigars.about: A box-pressed perfecto in the 1926 Serie made to honor founder José Orlando Padrón's 80th birthday, sold in boxes of eight. The maduro was Cigar Aficionado's No. 2 cigar of 2008.
cigars.researchNote: Padron.com lists it as the 1926 Serie No. 80; Cigar Aficionado and retailers call it 80 Years. It remains in the line but output is small: Cigar Aficionado reports one buncher and one roller making about 300 a day. Strength Full is from the maker's series description and Neptune; Cigar Aficionado rated the natural Medium-Full.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown natural (also sold in Nicaraguan maduro)
cigars.about: A box-pressed torpedo in the 1926 Serie released in 2004 for Padrón's 40th anniversary, with every leaf aged at least five years. It was Cigar Aficionado's Cigar of the Year for 2004.
cigars.researchNote: The first release was 400 hand-painted boxes of 40; Cigar Aficionado said it would stay in the line as a rare regular size, and padron.com still lists it. No source rates this size alone: Full is the maker's description of the 1926 Serie, and Cigar Aficionado says only that it is slightly stronger than a 1964 Anniversary.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown natural (also sold in Nicaraguan maduro)
cigars.about: A heavily pressed 6 x 52 toro released in 2009 for Padrón's 45th anniversary, blended from tobacco up to ten years old. The maduro was Cigar Aficionado's Cigar of the Year for 2009.
cigars.researchNote: Padron.com calls it Family Reserve No. 45; 45 Years is the name on the band. The maker calls the series full-bodied; Cigar Aficionado rates the maduro Full and the natural Medium-Full, describing the natural as milder.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown natural (also sold in Nicaraguan maduro)
cigars.about: A box-pressed 5 x 54 robusto released in 2014 for Padrón's 50th anniversary as part of the Family Reserve line. It made Cigar Aficionado's Top 25 in both maduro (2014) and natural (2015).
cigars.researchNote: Padron.com calls it Family Reserve No. 50; Cigar Aficionado calls it 50 Years. Strength is disputed: the maker calls the series full-bodied (used here), but Cigar Aficionado rates the Maduro Medium-Full and the Natural Medium. Do not confuse it with the separate, larger Padrón 50th Anniversary limited edition sold in a humidor.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown natural (also sold in Nicaraguan maduro)
cigars.about: A box-pressed 5 1/4 x 50 robusto in the Family Reserve line, named for founder José Orlando Padrón's 85th birthday rather than a company anniversary. It shipped in October 2011 in boxes of ten.
cigars.researchNote: Padron.com calls it Family Reserve No. 85. Strength sources disagree: the maker calls the Family Reserve series full-bodied (used here), while Cigar Insider rated the No. 85 Maduro Medium-Full. Cigar Aficionado reported at launch that most were maduro.

cigars.about: The classic non-Cuban Partagas, known for its Cameroon wrapper and yellow boxes. It is made in the Dominican Republic and remains the brand's core line.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists this core line simply as Partagás, and it is often called the Yellow Box line. The maker rates it mellow to medium, while Famous and Holt's list it as medium. Famous lists the Naturales at 49 ring, the maker and Holt's at 50.

cigars.about: A box-pressed non-Cuban Partagas released in 2018 as a tribute to five men who shaped the brand, sold in white lacquered boxes. The maker now lists it as retired.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it full bodied, Cigar Aficionado medium to full, and Neptune medium. halfwheel lists the Corona Extra Leyenda at 5 1/2 inches, while the maker and Cigar Aficionado give 5 1/4.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano), Honduras (Jamastran), Mexico (San Andrés)
cigars.about: A 2017 non-Cuban Partagas with a reddish Honduran wrapper, made as a look back at the brand's earlier blends. The maker now lists it as retired.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel lists the Gigante as 6 x 50, while the maker and Cigar Aficionado give 6 x 60.

cigars.about: The stronger offshoot of the Partagas 1845 line, first sold in 2014 as a brick and mortar exclusive and reblended in 2017. The maker now lists it as retired.
cigars.researchNote: Blend shown is the 2017 reblend. The 2014 original used an Ecuadorian Habano ligero wrapper, and the maker's site still lists that older blend. The maker rates it medium to full, while Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.about: The darkest and fullest version of the Partagas 1845 line, first sold in 2014 through catalog and online retailers and reblended in 2017. The maker now lists it as retired.
cigars.researchNote: Blend shown is the 2017 reblend. The 2014 original used a Connecticut Habano Oscuro wrapper and Dominican La Vega Especial binder, and the maker's site still lists that older blend. Sources disagree on the Robusto and Rothschild dimensions.

cigars.about: Released in 2021 as the first non-Cuban Partagas with a Connecticut Shade wrapper and the first made in Nicaragua. It is the mildest cigar in the current lineup.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's launch release called it mellow to medium and its site rates it mellow. Neptune lists it as mild and Famous as medium.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Barber pole of 1998 Cameroon and 2013 Connecticut Shade
cigars.about: A 2022 non-Cuban Partagas and the brand's first barber pole, pairing a 1998 Cameroon wrapper with a strip of 2013 Connecticut Shade. It is sold in limited seasonal batches in two short sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrapper leaves are used: Cameroon is the main one, with Connecticut Shade as the contrasting stripe. The maker rates it mellow to medium, while Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.about: A limited non-Cuban Partagas built around a long-aged Cameroon wrapper and sold in glass tubes. General Cigar offered it from 2005 to 2009 and brought it back in 2019.
cigars.researchNote: Blend shown is the 2019 edition (2,500 boxes of 10). Each year is its own limited blend: the 2020 edition used a Mexican San Andrés binder with Dominican and Mexican filler.

cigars.about: A 2023 non-Cuban Partagas with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over a Cameroon binder, made in Honduras. It is a current regular production line.
cigars.researchNote: The maker and Neptune rate it medium, while Famous lists it as full. A box-pressed Belicoso (6 1/2 x 52) was a limited size at launch.

cigars.about: One of the two debut lines from Mo Maali's Patina Cigars, released in 2017. It pairs an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper with Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania filler.
cigars.researchNote: It launched at the Casa Favilli factory in Granada. halfwheel reported production at NACSA in Estelí by 2019, though some retailers still list Casa Favilli. The maker gives no strength rating: Neptune lists medium, and halfwheel's review had it building from medium to medium-full.

cigars.about: One of the two debut lines from Mo Maali's Patina Cigars, released in 2017. It uses an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania tobacco and is pitched as a Connecticut with some spice up front.
cigars.researchNote: It launched at the Casa Favilli factory in Granada and is now made at NACSA in Estelí. The mild rating comes from Neptune only. The Copper size was announced in 2025 and shipped in March 2026.

cigars.about: The third Patina line, added in April 2020 and made at NACSA in Estelí. Brand owner Mo Maali has not disclosed the blend.
cigars.researchNote: The maker keeps the blend secret: wrapper, binder and filler are all undisclosed. Strength and body come from reviews: halfwheel put strength a little over medium, and most Developing Palates reviewers called it medium.

cigars.about: The Connecticut Shade version of PDR's value-priced 1878 line from Abe Flores, made in Tamboril with Dominican Criollo 98 binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: The 1878 line was reblended and renamed 1878 Recordando a Santiago in late 2020. The maker describes it as medium bodied.

cigars.about: The dark oscuro-wrapped version of PDR's value-priced 1878 line from Abe Flores, made in Tamboril with Dominican Habano binder and Corojo filler.
cigars.researchNote: The 1878 line was reblended and renamed 1878 Recordando a Santiago in late 2020. The wrapper is a dark sun grown Ecuadorian leaf, not a broadleaf. The maker describes it as medium bodied.

cigars.about: The San Andrés maduro version of PDR's value-priced 1878 line from Abe Flores, made in Tamboril with Dominican Criollo 98 binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: The 1878 line was reblended and renamed 1878 Recordando a Santiago in late 2020. The maker describes it as medium bodied.

cigars.about: A PDR line named for founder Abe Flores, first released in 2013 with a Dominican-grown Corojo 2006 wrapper. The maker describes it as medium bodied.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel reported in 2025 that the Gran Reserva lines were being renamed Gran Reserva Premier Cru with the same blends. The maker's spec list calls the Habano filler Dominican, while its description and halfwheel say Nicaraguan.

cigars.about: A PDR line from Abe Flores introduced in 2016, whose name means troubadour. It comes in a Rosado version and a Maduro version, and the Rosado was a Robb Report Best of the Best pick in 2023.
cigars.researchNote: Two versions exist: Rosado (shown here) and Maduro, which uses a Mexican San Andrés wrapper. It launched with Nicaraguan binder and filler. The maker now lists Dominican binder and filler, while Neptune still shows Nicaraguan. Neptune lists it as medium strength, Famous as full.

cigars.about: The original Reserve 10th Anniversary cigar, introduced in 2004 and the first Perdomo to use a bourbon barrel-aged wrapper. It pairs an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler aged at least six years.
cigars.researchNote: Round, not box-pressed. A maduro-wrapped round version has been sold as Champagne Noir.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Nicaraguan puro added to the Reserve 10th Anniversary line in 2020. The six-year-old maduro wrapper spends another 14 months in bourbon barrels.
cigars.researchNote: Often listed as Reserve 10th Anniversary Box-Pressed Maduro. Different from the older round Champagne Noir maduro.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Nicaraguan puro added to the Reserve 10th Anniversary line in 2020. The six-year-old sun grown wrapper spends another 10 months in bourbon barrels.
cigars.researchNote: Often listed as Reserve 10th Anniversary Box-Pressed Sun Grown.

cigars.about: The Connecticut version of Perdomo's 20th Anniversary, added in 2016. It uses an eight-year-old Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper finished in bourbon barrels over Nicaraguan binder and filler, and unlike its siblings it is not box-pressed.
cigars.researchNote: Added four years after the Sun Grown and Maduro. Round rather than box-pressed.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Nicaraguan puro released for Perdomo's 20th anniversary. The eight-year-old maduro wrapper is aged a further 14 months in bourbon barrels.
A box-pressed Nicaraguan puro released for Perdomo's 20th anniversary. The eight-year-old sun grown wrapper is finished in bourbon barrels.
cigars.researchNote: Perdomo's site says the wrapper gets 10 months in bourbon barrels; the 2012 launch release said 14 months.

cigars.about: The Connecticut version of the line marking 30 years of Perdomo. It uses a bourbon barrel-aged Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler that Perdomo says are aged 15 years.
cigars.researchNote: Shown at the 2023 PCA show and shipped that November. Sold as 30th Anniversary Box-Pressed Connecticut.

cigars.about: The Maduro version of the line marking 30 years of Perdomo. A box-pressed Nicaraguan puro using bourbon barrel-aged wrapper and tobaccos Perdomo says are aged 15 years.
cigars.researchNote: Shown at the 2023 PCA show and shipped that November.

cigars.about: The Sun Grown version of the line marking 30 years of Perdomo. A box-pressed Nicaraguan puro using bourbon barrel-aged wrapper and tobaccos Perdomo says are aged 15 years.
cigars.researchNote: Shown at the 2023 PCA show and shipped that November.

cigars.about: The mildest of Perdomo's Habano Bourbon Barrel-Aged trio. A six-year-old Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper is finished in bourbon barrels and rolled over Cuban-seed Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Perdomo's site says the wrapper gets 8 months in bourbon barrels; the 2015 launch coverage said 6 months.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Perdomo's Habano Bourbon Barrel-Aged line, a Nicaraguan puro. The six-year-old wrapper spends 14 more months in bourbon barrels, the longest of the three versions.
The sun grown version of Perdomo's Habano Bourbon Barrel-Aged line, a Nicaraguan puro. The six-year-old wrapper spends 10 more months in bourbon barrels.
The mildest Lot 23, pairing a five-year-aged Ecuadorian Connecticut shade wrapper with binder and filler from Perdomo's single Lot 23 farm in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: The only Lot 23 that is not a Nicaraguan puro. Perdomo rates it mild to medium; Neptune Cigar calls it mild.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Perdomo's single-farm Lot 23, a Nicaraguan puro with tobacco aged five years. It was added to the line in 2007.
cigars.researchNote: Perdomo and Cigar Aficionado both say the wrapper is Nicaraguan maduro. Perdomo and Cigar Coop rate it medium to full; Neptune Cigar calls it medium.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Three versions: Ecuadorian Connecticut, Nicaraguan Sun Grown or Nicaraguan Maduro
cigars.about: Perdomo's value-priced line, usually sold in bundles, made in Esteli with Cuban-seed Nicaraguan binder and filler. It comes in Connecticut, Sun Grown and Maduro versions.
cigars.researchNote: Comes in three wrappers. Perdomo rates the Connecticut mild to medium and the Maduro medium to full; its page calls the Sun Grown both medium and medium to full. Neptune Cigar's listing mentions Dominican filler, but Perdomo says the binder and filler are all Nicaraguan.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Two versions: Nicaraguan Sun Grown or Nicaraguan Maduro
cigars.about: A Perdomo line where every size is a 70 ring gauge, made as a Nicaraguan puro with tobacco aged five years. It revives the Inmenso name Perdomo used in the early 2000s.
cigars.researchNote: Comes in two wrappers. Perdomo rates the Sun Grown medium (earth, cedar, spice) and the Maduro medium to full (oak, espresso). The original Inmenso from the early 2000s was discontinued; this version shipped in May 2021.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Three versions: Ecuadorian Connecticut, Nicaraguan Sun Grown or Nicaraguan Maduro
cigars.about: A 2015 Perdomo series made with Nicaraguan binder and filler aged ten years and bourbon barrel-aged wrappers, in small sizes at modest prices. Production was capped at 3,000 boxes a year per size for each of three wrappers.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as Small Batch 2005. Came in Connecticut, Sun Grown and Maduro versions. No longer in Perdomo's catalog and marked discontinued at Neptune Cigar.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped cigar in Perdomo's Special Craft Series, a 2015 line blended to pair with craft beer. This one was aimed at pilsners and other light beers.
cigars.researchNote: Also called Special Craft Series Connecticut. Unusual for Perdomo in using a U.S. grown Connecticut wrapper rather than Ecuadorian. Perdomo called it mild to medium; Neptune Cigar's spec table says medium. Marked discontinued at Neptune Cigar and absent from Perdomo's current catalog.

cigars.about: The sun grown cigar in Perdomo's Special Craft Series, a 2015 line blended to pair with craft beer. This one was aimed at ambers, pale ales and IPAs.
cigars.researchNote: Also called Special Craft Series Sun Grown. Perdomo called it medium to full; The Cigar Authority's review rated it medium. The series is no longer in Perdomo's catalog.

cigars.about: The maduro cigar in Perdomo's Special Craft Series, a 2015 line blended to pair with craft beer. This one was aimed at stouts, porters and other dark beers.
cigars.researchNote: Also called Special Craft Series Maduro. Perdomo called it medium to full; Neptune Cigar lists it as full. No longer available at Neptune Cigar and absent from Perdomo's current catalog.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan Sun Grown (also made with Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade and Nicaraguan Maduro wrappers)
cigars.about: ESV is a Perdomo line first released in 2005 as a tribute to Nick Perdomo Sr., then reworked in 2016 and again in 2019 as a box-pressed cigar using tobacco from the family's Finca Natalie farm. It came in three wrapper versions over Cuban-seed Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Usually called ESV. Three wrappers: Connecticut (mild to medium), Sun Grown (medium; Neptune's text and halfwheel put it a notch higher) and Maduro (medium-full). Wrapper, strength and flavors here are the Sun Grown. Neptune lists it as discontinued and Perdomo's site no longer shows it; Perdomo has not announced that.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan Shade-Grown, a Cuban-seed/Cameroon-seed hybrid (also made with Ecuadorian Connecticut and Nicaraguan Maduro wrappers)
cigars.about: Legacy is a 2025 line created by Nicholas Perdomo III as a tribute to his father, Nick Perdomo Jr. It is built around a new Cuban-seed and Cameroon-seed hybrid leaf grown on the family's Finca Natalie farm in Esteli, with wrappers aged 10 years and finished in bourbon barrels.
cigars.researchNote: Three wrappers. Details here are the Nicaraguan Shade-Grown, a hybrid leaf that fits no standard wrapper category. The Ecuadorian Connecticut is medium (cream, cedar, honey); the Nicaraguan Maduro is medium-full (chocolate, espresso). Both use the hybrid as binder. The Gran Belicoso is box-pressed. A limited Father & Son figurado came in 2026.

cigars.about: The second cigar in Plasencia's Alma series, a Nicaraguan puro that showcases tobacco from the Jalapa valley. It is the smooth, creamy, medium-strength member of the series.
cigars.researchNote: Brand is spelled Plasencia. The maker lists the wrapper only as Nicaragua; Famous Smoke calls it Habano. The Guajiro and Travesia are box-pressed.

cigars.binder: Nicaragua (double binder, one leaf from Ometepe)
cigars.about: The third cigar in Plasencia's Alma series, a box-pressed Nicaraguan puro built around tobacco grown in the volcanic soil of Ometepe island. It is the spicy, bolder blend of the series.
cigars.researchNote: Brand is spelled Plasencia. Maker rates strength 4 of 5. The 2024 Ometepe Edition, a torpedo with an Ometepe-grown wrapper, is a separate limited release.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro in Plasencia's Alma series made with tobacco grown above 3,500 feet at the family's San Julian farm in Condega. It is the sweeter, more delicate blend of the series.
cigars.researchNote: Brand is spelled Plasencia. Maker rates strength 2.5 of 5, so it sits between mild-medium and medium. The maker lists the wrapper only as Nicaragua; halfwheel says Condega and Neptune calls it Habano.

cigars.about: The first release in Plasencia's Cosecha (harvest) series, made with tobacco from the family's 146th crop, grown in 2011 and 2012. It was discontinued in 2023 when Cosecha 151 arrived.
cigars.researchNote: Brand is spelled Plasencia. Discontinued in September 2023. halfwheel called it a milder offering at launch and Neptune lists it as medium; the maker no longer lists it and gives no strength rating.

cigars.about: A Honduran puro in Plasencia's Cosecha (harvest) series, made with tobacco from the family's 149th crop, harvested in 2014. It is a full-bodied cigar rolled at the family's Tabacos de Oriente factory in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Brand is spelled Plasencia. Sizes follow the maker's site; halfwheel and retailers list La Vega as 5 x 52 and Santa Fe as 4 3/4 x 60. The Criollo wrapper seed comes from Famous Smoke.

cigars.about: A Honduran puro in Plasencia's Cosecha (harvest) series, made with tobacco from the family's 151st crop, grown in 2016 and 2017. It was named Cigar Journal's top new cigar of 2024.
cigars.researchNote: Brand is spelled Plasencia. Maker rates strength 4 of 5, though halfwheel's reviewer found the nicotine strength only mild to medium. The wrapper is similar to Cosecha 149's but from a later harvest and a lower priming. A 6 x 54 Salomon was a limited TAA exclusive.

cigars.about: One of Powstanie's two original core lines, from the brothers who own the Cigar Hustler shop in Florida. It is rolled at the NicaSueño factory in Estelí, the home of RoMa Craft, with a dark broadleaf maduro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not say where the broadleaf wrapper is grown. Famous Smoke lists the brand as medium to full and Neptune calls this blend full-bodied, but halfwheel's reviewer found the nicotine strength only about medium. First announced as Powstanie Maduro.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo), Nicaragua (Estelí ligero, Condega, Jalapa)
cigars.about: The first Powstanie cigar, released in May 2015 by the brothers who own the Cigar Hustler shop in Florida. It is rolled at the NicaSueño factory in Estelí, the home of RoMa Craft, with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over an Indonesian binder.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is Neptune's word; Famous Smoke describes the brand overall as medium to full. The Belicoso launched at 5 1/4 x 54 and is now listed at 5 1/2 x 54.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Barber pole of Ecuadorian Habano and Mexican San Andrés
cigars.about: A limited Powstanie release named for the bear adopted by Polish soldiers in World War II, rolled with two wrappers in a barber pole pattern. It returns in a different size most years in small runs.
cigars.researchNote: Each edition is one size: 500 boxes of 21 through 2023, then 1,000 boxes of 8 for 2025, when it was renamed War Bear. No published strength rating; halfwheel reviewers found it medium to medium-full. Flavors are from halfwheel's 2023 review.

cigars.about: The original Protocol cigar, launched in 2015 by Cubariqueño Cigar Co., a company founded by two police officers. It is a strong Nicaraguan blend with four ligero leaves in the filler under an Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: This is the original Protocol, also called Protocol Habano; Blue is the band color. Smoke Inn bought the brand in 2026 and is now its only seller. Launched at La Zona; halfwheel reports Protocol production now runs through AJ Fernandez's San Lotano factory in Ocotal.

cigars.about: Protocol's Connecticut-wrapped cigar, named after the Greek Titaness of law and order and blended by company partner William Agathis with Hector Alfonso Sr. It is a creamy, medium blend with more flavor than a traditional Connecticut.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as Protocol Gold Themis, after its gold band. The company called it a medium-strength cigar with full flavor. Launched at La Zona; halfwheel reports Protocol production now runs through AJ Fernandez's San Lotano factory in Ocotal.

cigars.about: Protocol's 2018 release, a second Ecuadorian Habano blend that is toned down from the original Protocol Blue. It is known by its silver band and packaging.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as Protocol Silver Official Misconduct. Smoke Inn, the brand owner, describes it as closer to medium in body, though halfwheel's reviewer found the strength built to just under full. Smoke Inn currently lists only the Toro. Launched at La Zona; production reportedly now with AJ Fernandez.

cigars.about: The lighter-wrapped version of Protocol's Sir Robert Peel, the first cigar in its Lawmen Series, named for the British statesman who founded London's Metropolitan Police. It pairs an Ecuadorian Rosado wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on strength: Smoke Inn, the brand owner, describes the line as medium-bodied, while halfwheel's reviewer found the Natural full strength. Flavor notes are Smoke Inn's for both wrappers together. Launched at La Zona; production reportedly now with AJ Fernandez.

cigars.about: The dark-wrapped version of Protocol's Sir Robert Peel, the first cigar in its Lawmen Series. It was the first Protocol to use a Pennsylvania Broadleaf wrapper, over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is from Smoke Inn, the brand owner, which describes the line as medium-bodied. Flavor notes are Smoke Inn's for both wrappers together, not the Maduro alone. Launched at La Zona; production reportedly now with AJ Fernandez.

cigars.about: The core Honduran Punch line from General Cigar, now sold under the Clásico name. It pairs an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper with a Connecticut Broadleaf binder and a three-country filler.
cigars.researchNote: Clásico is the current name for the original Honduran Punch, which dates to 1969. Holt's and Neptune rate it medium, Famous says medium to full. A Clásico Maduro with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper is sold alongside it.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: Billed by General Cigar as the strongest Punch, made for it by AJ Fernandez in Estelí, Nicaragua. It was the first General-owned Punch made outside the company's Honduran factory.
cigars.researchNote: Famous and Neptune list the Brute as 6 x 60; halfwheel and Holt's list 6 1/4 x 60.

cigars.about: A value-priced Punch from General Cigar, launched in 2020 as an everyday smoke. The original blend uses Nicaraguan Habano wrapper and binder over Nicaraguan and Honduran filler.
cigars.researchNote: This is the original Habano blend. Knuckle Buster Maduro (2022, Connecticut Broadleaf) and Shade (Ecuadorian Connecticut) are separate blends. Famous calls the Habano medium to full; Punch and Neptune say medium.

cigars.about: A fuller Punch introduced in 2015 as a tribute to the original non-Cuban Punch blend. It uses an Ecuadorian Corojo wrapper grown for the line over a Connecticut Habano binder.
cigars.researchNote: Famous lists the binder as Nicaraguan; Punch and halfwheel say Connecticut Habano. Punch and retailers call it full, though the brand manager described it as medium-plus in 2021.

cigars.about: A Honduran-made Punch that General Cigar produced as an exclusive for the retailer Cigars International. It has an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan and Honduran filler.
cigars.researchNote: Made as a Cigars International exclusive and reviewed as new in 2013, so most shops will not have it. It is not on the Punch website. Neptune calls it full strength with an undisclosed binder; Cigar Coop's review rated it medium to full. Neptune shows no sizes in stock.

cigars.about: A Honduran-made Punch from General Cigar sold in a few traditional sizes, mainly the 7 1/4 x 54 Chateau L. The natural version uses an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Punch calls it medium-bodied, while Holt's lists it as full. The Chateau L also comes in Maduro and Maduro Maduro (oscuro) versions with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper.

cigars.about: A limited 2022 Punch robusto that General Cigar developed over three years with feedback from its Punch Brotherhood fan club. It was sold in bundles through brick-and-mortar shops only.
cigars.researchNote: One size only, a 5 x 50 robusto sold in 5 and 10 count bundles. Some retailers list it as Punch Brotherhood The People's Champ.

cigars.about: Released in 2014 to mark Manuel "Manolo" Quesada Jr.'s 40 years in the cigar business. The regular sizes use a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Dominican binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: The Corona Clasica size is a different blend with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper, known as the Manolo blend. Toro Press and Salomon Press were limited editions. Full is Neptune's rating; halfwheel's review of the 4 x 50 size found it medium.

cigars.about: Introduced in 2015 as what was then Quesada's most premium line, built around Dominican San Vicente tobacco from the 1997 harvest. The cigars are aged for at least a year after rolling.
cigars.researchNote: Production is limited by the supply of 1997 vintage tobacco. Oscuro (Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper) and Barber Pole versions are separate releases. Strength is Famous Smoke's rating. Famous lists the Robusto as 4 3/4 x 52; halfwheel says 4 1/2 x 52.

cigars.about: An annual limited release from Quesada, first made in 2011 and blended to pair with the Märzen-style beer served at Oktoberfest. It ships each year in late summer.
cigars.researchNote: Recent releases (2021 on) use a San Andrés wrapper; Neptune still describes an older version with a Dominican wrapper. Sizes vary by year, with Bavarian, Das Boot and Über as the core three. Full is Neptune's rating; halfwheel's 2022 review put strength just over medium.

cigars.about: A Quesada line launched in January 2013 with the tagline "Embrace Uncertainty". Quesada deliberately keeps the blend secret so smokers judge it without preconceptions.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is secret by design: Quesada has never disclosed wrapper, binder, filler or strength. Medium-full and the reddish Corojo maduro wrapper are Neptune's description, not confirmed by Quesada. It also launched in Corona, Petite and Coronet Cuadrada sizes.

cigars.filler: Brazil, Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano, ligero), Iconic ligero (proprietary)
cigars.about: A 2013 release from Iconic Leaf Cigar Company's Recluse brand, rolled entubado style in the Dominican Republic. It introduced the company's box-pressed Sidewinder shape.
cigars.researchNote: The binder is proprietary and not disclosed. It launched in 2013 in three Sidewinder sizes; the maker now lists the five sizes shown. Draconian Corojo, Connecticut and Habano versions were added in 2016 as separate blends.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (ligero, viso, seco), USA (Pennsylvania Broadleaf)
cigars.about: A habano-wrapped follow-up to the Connecticut-wrapped Recluse Amadeus, introduced by Iconic Leaf at the 2015 trade show. It is rolled entubado style in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: The maker now lists an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper; at the 2015 launch it was undisclosed. The maker gives no strength. Neptune's page for this cigar describes a different blend (Ecuadorian Connecticut over Nicaraguan tobacco), so do not rely on it.

cigars.about: The original Recluse blend from Iconic Leaf Cigar Company, released in 2012 with a Brazilian maduro wrapper. OTG stands for Off The Grid, and the cigars are rolled entubado style in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: OTG is the original Recluse maduro. It launched in 2012 in ten sizes; the maker now lists the five shown. The 2012 launch material named a Cameroon binder; the maker now says only select binder and Neptune lists it as undisclosed.

cigars.about: The maduro version of The Edge, one of the two original wrappers the line launched with in 2004. It is made in Honduras and sold as a bold, low-priced smoke.
cigars.researchNote: The maker only says it has an exclusive maduro wrapper. Retailers identify it as Costa Rican. Famous Smoke and Holt's list Full, while Neptune describes it as medium to full.

cigars.about: The mild-to-medium member of The Edge family, with an Ecuadorian Connecticut shade wrapper. It was previously sold as The Edge Lite.
cigars.researchNote: Formerly called The Edge Lite. The maker only says Connecticut wrapper. Retailers specify Ecuadorian Connecticut shade. Neptune lists it as Mild and Famous Smoke as Medium.

cigars.about: The Edge blend with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, added in 2007 after the original Corojo and Maduro. It is rolled at El Paraiso in Danlí, Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are Cigar Aficionado's listing, not the maker's. Neptune instead lists a Nicaraguan binder with Honduran, Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler.

cigars.about: The only Edge blend rolled in Nicaragua, launched in 2012 with a Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and fillers from Estelí, Condega and Jalapa.
cigars.researchNote: The maker now says the Habano-seed wrapper is grown in Ecuador. The 2012 launch release, halfwheel, Cigar Aficionado and Neptune call it a Nicaraguan puro. Strength is listed anywhere from Medium (Neptune, halfwheel) to Full (Famous Smoke, Cigar Aficionado).

cigars.about: A box-pressed Honduran cigar with a 10-year-old Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers. It is the spicier sibling of the Vintage 1990.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it Vintage 1992 Sumatra. Neptune lists a Honduran binder, but the maker says Nicaraguan.

cigars.about: The Cameroon-wrapped member of the Vintage series, released in 2011 with a wrapper from the 2003 crop. It was Cigar Aficionado's No. 16 cigar of 2017.
cigars.researchNote: Unlike the 1990, 1992 and 1999, this Vintage is made by Plasencia at El Paraiso.

cigars.about: The newest Vintage blend, launched in 2017 with an 11-year-old Mexican San Andrés wrapper. It is the first Vintage made in Nicaragua instead of Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: The name really is spelled San Andreas, although the wrapper comes from San Andrés, Mexico. Neptune lists Medium and halfwheel's review found it just under medium, while Famous Smoke lists Full.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Nicaraguan cigar released in 2010 for Rocky Patel's fifteenth year in the business. It has made Cigar Aficionado's Top 25 several times with ratings up to 93.
cigars.researchNote: Often written 15th Anniversary. Cigar Aficionado calls it medium to full, while retailers list anything from Medium (Neptune) to Full (Famous Smoke). halfwheel gives the Robusto as 5 x 50 and the Torpedo as 6 1/8 x 52.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Honduran cigar released in 2015 to mark twenty years since Rocky Patel entered the business. It has a Honduran wrapper over Honduran and Nicaraguan tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: After a Maduro version arrived in 2017 the original was renamed 20th Anniversary Habano, and the maker also called it Natural. Rocky Patel called it medium-plus, and halfwheel's review found medium strength with medium-full body. It is no longer in the maker's online portfolio, so availability is unclear.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Nicaraguan cigar released in 2021 for Rocky Patel's 60th birthday, aged at least two years after rolling. The Sixty size was Cigar Aficionado's No. 2 cigar of 2022 with a 96 rating.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is disputed: the maker lists Medium, Cigar Aficionado says Medium-Full, and Neptune and Famous Smoke list Full. Sixty is also the name of the 6 x 60 size in many Rocky Patel lines, so confirm which one a guest means.

cigars.about: A Honduran-made cigar released in 2019 and named for the code the blend carried at the factory during development. It has an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Honduran and Nicaraguan tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium-bodied, while halfwheel's review found it medium-plus to medium-full and Famous Smoke lists Full. halfwheel lists a Nicaraguan binder and Neptune a Honduran one. A 7 x 48 Churchill Shaggy Foot also exists.

cigars.about: The second release in the A.L.R. (Aged, Limited and Rare) series, rolled in 2016, rested at least two years and released in 2019. It was Cigar Aficionado's No. 5 cigar of 2019.
cigars.researchNote: The maker names only the San Andrés wrapper and calls the rest a mystery. Binder and filler come from halfwheel and Cigar Aficionado, which disagree on the filler regions (Estelí and Jalapa versus Estelí and Condega). It is a different blend from the first A.L.R. halfwheel lists the Robusto as 5 1/2 x 52.

cigars.about: A medium-bodied Honduran cigar released in 2019 and named for the number of the test blend Rocky Patel liked best. The Corona was Cigar Aficionado's No. 9 cigar of 2020 with a 95 rating.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the filler as Honduran. halfwheel and Cigar Aficionado say it also includes Nicaraguan leaf from Jalapa.

cigars.about: A blend created in 2018 for markets outside the United States and brought to U.S. stores in 2020. Cigar Journal named it its top cigar of 2018.
cigars.researchNote: The maker keeps the blend secret and says only that it is rolled in Honduras. The blend shown is Cigar Aficionado's, which rates it Medium-Full. Famous Smoke calls the wrapper Habano. halfwheel files it under the TAVICUSA factory, and Neptune and Famous Smoke list Nicaragua as the country.

cigars.about: A round Nicaraguan cigar released in 2021 with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It shipped alongside the Sixty, which lists the same wrapper, binder and filler origins.
cigars.researchNote: The Bala is a perfecto that tapers from 58 to 50 ring gauge. Neptune lists the strength as Medium and Famous Smoke as Full, against the maker's Medium-Full.

cigars.about: DBS stands for Double Broadleaf Selection, after the two broadleaf tobaccos in the binder and filler. The wrapper is Mexican San Andrés, not broadleaf, and the line debuted in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: The maker gives no strength. Neptune describes it as medium to full, Famous Smoke lists Full, and halfwheel's reviewer found it only reached medium. The broadleaf is in the binder and filler, not the wrapper.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Rocky Patel line sold in two versions, Maduro and Corojo, that was brought back to wide release in 2018 after years as a retailer exclusive. The original Maduro Torpedo was Cigar Aficionado's No. 8 cigar of 2009.
cigars.researchNote: Two blends; the Maduro is shown here. The Corojo has a Honduran Corojo wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler and is made at El Paraiso in Honduras. Halfwheel lists the Maduro filler as Costa Rica and Nicaragua. Cigar Aficionado dates the line to 2005 and rated the older Honduran-made Maduro medium to full.

cigars.about: The second line blended by former Cuban roller Hamlet Paredes for Rocky Patel, marking his 25 years in the cigar trade. It was built to be milder than his first cigar, Tabaquero.
cigars.researchNote: A 7 5/8 x 55 Salomon was added in 2018. Launched as regular production, but it is no longer on the maker's site and Neptune shows none in stock, so current production is unconfirmed. The maker calls it medium bodied, and halfwheel's reviewer said it is not a mild cigar.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan line named after Rocky Patel's own factory in Estelí and released for the factory's tenth anniversary. The filler comes from three Nicaraguan regions under a San Andrés wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Strength ratings vary: Cigar Aficionado says medium, while Holt's and Mike's Cigars say medium to full. The maker calls it a rich and full cigar. Halfwheel scored the Toro 92.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut Shade (grown in the Connecticut River Valley, USA)
cigars.about: A premium-priced Connecticut Shade cigar from Rocky Patel's Estelí factory, made with tobaccos the company says were aged for ten years. The wrapper is grown in the Connecticut River Valley, not Ecuador.
cigars.researchNote: Part of the filler is undisclosed. Halfwheel found the body medium-full with medium strength; the maker calls it medium bodied.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Honduran Habano (the maker calls it St. Augustine habano)
cigars.about: A strong Honduran-made Rocky Patel built around ligero filler from a hybrid seed grown by the Plasencia family. The aim was ligero strength without the usual harshness.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it full bodied; Cigar Aficionado rated the Lancero medium to full (90 points). Halfwheel names a habano binder without an origin; Cigar Aficionado lists Nicaragua. It is no longer listed on the maker's site, so it may be out of production.

cigars.about: A Rocky Patel seasonal name that returned in 2020 as a new San Andrés blend made at the company's own Nicaraguan factory. Earlier limited versions came out around 2009 and in 2012.
cigars.researchNote: Details are for the 2020 blend, the third version. The original was a limited release made by A.J. Fernandez with a Pennsylvania broadleaf wrapper; the maker and Cigar Aficionado date it to 2009, halfwheel to 2008. The maker rates the 2020 blend medium plus, halfwheel found it medium, and Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.about: A full-strength, box-pressed Nicaraguan cigar with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper, made at Rocky Patel's Estelí factory. The Robusto was Cigar Aficionado's No. 2 cigar of 2016 with 95 points.
cigars.researchNote: A separate line from Rocky Patel Sun Grown. Some retailers list it as Special Reserve Sun Grown Maduro. Halfwheel's 2015 launch report gave the Toro as 6 x 52 and listed a 4 1/2 x 50 Rothschild; Famous and Neptune now list a 6 1/2 x 52 Toro and a 5 x 50 Robusto.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Nicaraguan cigar that began shipping in December 2024, dressed in a bright green sleeve. Rocky Patel describes it as his first box-pressed blend on the lighter side of medium.
cigars.researchNote: The filler is mostly Nicaraguan with a single Honduran Jamastran leaf. Not the same as the older Rocky Patel ITC Emerald, a candela cigar made for catalog retailers. Halfwheel's review lists the Toro at 52 ring; the maker and retailers say 54. Famous lists the strength as full.

cigars.about: Released in 2020 to mark Rocky Patel's 25 years in the cigar business. The company says the tobacco was aged ten years before rolling and the finished cigars rested two more years.
cigars.researchNote: Part of the filler is undisclosed. The maker rates it medium plus; Neptune lists it as medium. Rated 91 by Cigar Aficionado according to the maker.

cigars.about: A Honduran-made Rocky Patel line sold by Famous Smoke Shop, built on aged Honduran ligero filler. It comes in a Corojo wrapper and a Maduro version, plus a Fumas version of each.
cigars.researchNote: Contains no Cuban tobacco. A 2009 review called it a Famous Smoke Shop exclusive. Binder and factory are not published. Wrapper origins are disputed: Famous lists the Corojo as Nicaraguan and the Maduro as Honduran, while the 2009 review says Honduran Corojo and Costa Rican Maduro. Reviews put it nearer medium to full.

cigars.about: A value-priced Rocky Patel line launched in 2014 and sold mostly in boxes of 22. It is rolled in Honduras at General Cigar's factory in Danlí.
cigars.researchNote: Also written Catch Twenty-Two. The origin of the Corojo wrapper is not published. A Catch 22 Connecticut version is also sold.

cigars.about: The first blend in Noel Rojas's Street Tacos series, released in March 2021. It uses an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler from the Somoto region.
cigars.researchNote: First made at Tabacalera Flor de San Luis; halfwheel now reports all Street Tacos are made at the Rojas Cigar Factory in Estelí. Neptune lists the Toro as 6 x 52, halfwheel as 6 x 50. Famous rates it full; Neptune and halfwheel's review say medium.

cigars.about: The second Street Tacos blend from Noel Rojas, released in July 2022. It is the Connecticut-wrapped member of the series, with Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists the Toro as 6 x 52; halfwheel lists the box-pressed Toro as 6 x 50.

cigars.about: One of the first lines in Noel Rojas's relaunched Rojas Cigars portfolio, kept to ring gauges of 50 and under. The maduro uses a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers list it simply as Rojas Statement. Strength is left blank because the two retailers disagree: Neptune says medium, Famous says full.

cigars.about: A 2022 line from Noel Rojas and one of the first rolled at his own factory in Estelí. It keeps to ring gauges of 50 and under, with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists a Mexican binder with Nicaraguan filler and the Toro as 6 x 52; halfwheel lists a Nicaraguan binder with Nicaraguan and Mexican filler and the Toro as 6 x 50.

cigars.about: RoMa Craft's first blend, a dark, full-strength broadleaf cigar rolled at the company's own Nica Sueño factory in Estelí. It was reblended in 2024 around a Pennsylvania Broadleaf wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Blend changed in 2024. The original (made until mid-2022) used a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper, Cameroon binder and all-Nicaraguan filler. White band text marks the current Pennsylvania version (CroMagnon PA); dark gray text marks the original.

cigars.about: The darker of RoMa Craft's two original Intemperance blends, named for its Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper. It went on hiatus in 2022 over wrapper supply and returned to shelves in late 2025.
cigars.researchNote: Strength ratings vary: Atlantic lists Medium-Full, Neptune lists Full, and halfwheel's 2026 review found it closer to medium. halfwheel gives the filler as Nicaragua plus undisclosed; retailers say Nicaragua and Dominican Republic. Treachery (6 x 54) replaced the Ambition belicoso in 2025.

cigars.about: RoMa Craft's Ecuadorian Connecticut blend and the mildest cigar in its core range, introduced in 2012 alongside the BA XXI. It is rolled at the company's Nica Sueño factory in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel's spec sheets list Dominican and Nicaraguan filler; Neptune lists Nicaraguan filler only. Fidelity (6 x 54) replaced the Industry belicoso as a regular size in 2025.

cigars.about: RoMa Craft's most powerful line, introduced in 2015 and known for its flat caps. The filler includes Pennsylvania Green River One Sucker, a very strong ligero.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune's attribute table lists it as Medium, but its own description and Atlantic both call it a full-strength cigar. The HN figurado is listed as 52/56 or 52/58 ring depending on the source.

cigars.about: A sister blend to the original CroMagnon that swaps the broadleaf wrapper for Ecuadorian Habano ligero. It shares CroMagnon's size names and is made at RoMa Craft's Nica Sueño factory.
cigars.researchNote: Often sold as CroMagnon Aquitaine. Sources describe it with the original CroMagnon binder and filler; none say it changed with the 2024 CroMagnon reblend. Some later halfwheel reviews list the binder as not disclosed. Body is from a halfwheel review of one size.

cigars.about: RoMa Craft's Cameroon-wrapped line, shown at the 2019 trade show and named for the Baka people of Cameroon and neighboring countries. It is made at the company's Nica Sueño factory in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: The binder and part of the filler are undisclosed. Atlantic lists it as Medium-Full; Neptune's page says both medium and full.

cigars.about: A Brazilian Mata Fina-wrapped blend RoMa Craft launched in 2016 as a Europe-only line through its European distributor. Some sizes have since reached U.S. shops in limited quantities.
cigars.researchNote: The name is written Wunder|Lust. The filler is undisclosed. No maker or retailer strength rating was found: a Blind Man's Puff panel rated the Gran Toro medium-strong, and halfwheel's reviews ran from medium to nearly full depending on the size. U.S. availability is limited.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro version of the Romeo y Julieta 1875, made for Altadis U.S.A. by the Plasencia family in Nicaragua. It was introduced in 2018 and wears an orange band.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's and Neptune list Medium; Atlantic lists Medium-Full.

cigars.about: An all-Nicaraguan Romeo y Julieta made by Plasencia, wrapped in Connecticut-seed leaf grown in Nicaragua and aged over three years. It is the Connecticut companion to the 1875 Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The full name is Romeo y Julieta 1875 Connecticut Nicaragua. The wrapper is grown in Nicaragua, not Ecuador or the U.S. halfwheel reported it in 2019 as an October 2019 release under the name Nicaragua Connecticut; the launch year is not confirmed.

cigars.about: A Honduran-made Romeo y Julieta that Altadis U.S.A. created in 2013 as an exclusive for Famous Smoke Shop. It is the Connecticut-wrapped partner to the darker House of Montague.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke Shop exclusive, so most shops will not carry it. Strength, body, factory and flavors come from one Blind Man's Puff panel review of the Churchill. Current availability is not confirmed.

cigars.about: A Honduran-made Romeo y Julieta with a Brazilian Arapiraca maduro wrapper, created by Altadis U.S.A. in 2013 as an exclusive for Famous Smoke Shop. It is the darker partner to the House of Capulet.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke Shop exclusive, so most shops will not carry it. No strength rating was found; one Cigar Dojo review of the robusto called it very mild in body and strength. Tasting notes come from that same review. Current availability is not confirmed.

cigars.about: A bolder Romeo y Julieta introduced in 2012, with a dark Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Dominican Piloto and Olor tobaccos. It is made at Tabacalera de García and was built as a fuller alternative to the 1875.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis and Neptune call it full-bodied; Holt's lists Medium-Full. The Magnum size was added in 2020.

cigars.about: The first Romeo y Julieta made in Nicaragua from all-Nicaraguan tobacco, produced by Plasencia and launched in 2016. The 505 is Nicaragua's telephone country code, and the sizes are box-pressed.
cigars.researchNote: Full name is Romeo 505 Nicaragua by Romeo y Julieta. Altadis no longer lists it on its site and retailers show it sold out, so it may be out of production.

cigars.about: A San Andrés-wrapped Romeo y Julieta made for Altadis U.S.A. by AJ Fernandez in Estelí, released in 2018. It pairs the Mexican wrapper with a Nicaraguan binder and Nicaraguan and Dominican filler.
cigars.researchNote: Full name is Romeo San Andrés by Romeo y Julieta. Altadis described it as medium to full; Neptune calls it medium. Altadis no longer lists it on its site, so it may be out of production.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan-made Romeo y Julieta blended and rolled by AJ Fernandez, with a dark Habana 2000 maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers disagree on strength: Neptune lists Medium, Cigar Place lists Medium-Full. No source states where the wrapper is grown or the launch year. Not the same as the Thompson-exclusive RyJ Nicaragua by AJ Fernandez or the Reserva Real Nicaragua.

cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro made by Plasencia with Rafael Nodal to mark 145 years of Romeo y Julieta, released in 2021. It came in a single toro size in boxes of 11, with one cigar wearing a gold band.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis described it as medium to full-bodied; Neptune lists Medium. Sources describe the wrapper color differently (caramel-toned in the press release, maduro at Neptune), and no seed type is published.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto from Navarrete and La Canela)
cigars.about: A limited edition Romeo y Julieta released in 2023, a single toro built around Dominican Piloto tobacco under an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. It comes in red 10-count boxes made to look like books.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is the maker's own description (medium-to-full body). No published tasting notes were found.

cigars.about: The first new Room101 release after Matt Booth's brief retirement in 2017, launched in 2018, and the first Room101 made in the Dominican Republic. It is rolled at Tabacalera William Ventura with an Ecuadorian wrapper over an Indonesian binder.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel and Neptune list the wrapper only as Ecuadorian; Mike's Cigars calls it Ecuadorian Habano. The Toro is 6 1/4 x 54 in halfwheel's review but 6 x 54 at retail. STG, which now owns Room101, dropped Farce from its price lists in January 2026 and has not said what happens to it.

cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped companion to Room101 Farce, introduced at the 2018 trade show. It shares the name but is a different blend, and none of its sizes match the original Farce.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists it as medium, but halfwheel's and Cigar Dojo's reviews found it mild to just under medium. halfwheel and Neptune call the binder undisclosed; Cigar Dojo and Mike's Cigars list Indonesian. Retailers show the Short Corona with a 46 ring. STG dropped Farce from its price lists in January 2026.

cigars.about: The third version of Room101 Farce, shipped in 2019. It puts a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over an Ecuadorian Sumatra binder with broadleaf and Nicaraguan fillers.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists it as medium; Mike's Cigars and a Developing Palates review put it at medium to full. halfwheel's launch report gave the Robusto as 5 1/2 x 52, but retailers and Developing Palates list 50. A 6 1/2 x 42 Thicc Lancero was previewed in late 2021. STG dropped Farce from its price lists in January 2026.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A 2021 Nicaraguan puro marking twelve years of Room101 cigars, made by AJ Fernandez with tobacco he grew. It came in one 6 x 52 toro and was produced only to fill the orders received.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel's review put strength and body at medium, while Neptune lists it as full. A 6 x 56 Perfecto followed in 2022 as a small limited run.

cigars.about: A value-priced Room101 line introduced in 2019 and sold in 55-count boxes. It comes in one 6 x 55 toro in two wrappers over the same binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Two versions share one binder and filler: Passive has the Ecuadorian Habano wrapper and Aggressive has a maduro wrapper whose origin is not disclosed. The wrapper fields here describe the Habano version. The factory is as reported at the 2019 launch, before STG owned Room101.

cigars.about: A large ring gauge line from Altadis U.S.A.'s Honduran-made Saint Luis Rey brand; the G stands for gigante and every size is 56 ring or bigger. The natural version wears a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: These details are for the Natural. A separate Serie G Maduro uses a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. Holt's lists the strength as medium-full and Famous Smoke as full.

cigars.about: A 2021 line from Altadis U.S.A. named for Puerto de Carenas, the old name of the Port of Havana. It is made at La Flor de Copan in Honduras with a Nicaraguan wrapper over Honduran binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis calls it a solid medium-bodied cigar, while halfwheel's review put strength and body at medium-full. Carenas Ultramar is a separate, later blend.

cigars.about: The core Honduran-made Saint Luis Rey from Altadis U.S.A., with a dark Nicaraguan wrapper and binder over Honduran, Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler. It is known as a full-flavored cigar at a low price.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis now lists this line as Saint Luis Rey Original; Famous Smoke still sells it as Reserva Especial. Altadis and Famous call it full, Neptune medium. A Maduro version with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper is sold separately.

cigars.about: The first San Cristobal, created in 2007 by Jose 'Pepin' Garcia for Ashton and rolled at the Garcia family's My Father factory in Esteli. It is a dark, full-bodied cigar with Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: The core line is sold simply as San Cristobal. Sources split on the wrapper: Holt's, the retailer tied to Ashton, and Cigar Aficionado's 2023 rating say Ecuador, while halfwheel, Famous Smoke and Neptune describe a Nicaraguan puro. Neptune rates it medium; Holt's, Famous and Cigar Aficionado say full.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped San Cristobal, introduced in 2011. The Garcia family makes it in Nicaragua for Ashton with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke and Neptune list it as medium, while Holt's, the retailer tied to Ashton, calls it mild to medium.

cigars.about: The fifth San Cristobal blend, released in 2016 with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler from the Garcia family's farms. Cigar Aficionado named it its number 3 cigar of 2021.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's and halfwheel's review put it at medium-full; Neptune lists medium.

cigars.about: The fourth San Cristobal line, introduced in 2013 with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It launched with a mix of round and box-pressed sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke and Neptune list it as full, while Holt's, the retailer tied to Ashton, calls it medium. The Prophet is listed as 5 x 54 by some sources and 5 1/4 x 54 by others.

cigars.about: A limited San Cristobal that debuted in 2015 with a Mexican San Andrés oscuro wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco grown by the Garcia family. It is released in small batches of 22-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: The first run in 2015 was 3,000 boxes of the 6 1/2 x 52 only, later named Decadence. The other sizes were added in later batches.

cigars.about: The mildest of the three Sancho Panza lines General Cigar reblended in 2022 with Matt Booth of Room101. It is made in Honduras with a Honduran-grown Connecticut-seed wrapper and is now round instead of box-pressed.
cigars.researchNote: Details are for the 2022 blend; earlier box-pressed versions were a different blend. STG removed Sancho Panza from its price lists in January 2026 and has not said what happens to the brand.

cigars.about: The strongest of the three non-Cuban Sancho Panza lines General Cigar reblended in 2022 with Matt Booth of Room101. It is made in Honduras with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over a Connecticut broadleaf binder.
cigars.researchNote: Details are for the 2022 blend; older Extra Fuerte boxes were a different blend. STG removed Sancho Panza from its price lists in January 2026 and has not said what happens to the brand.

cigars.about: A 2024 addition to General Cigar's non-Cuban Sancho Panza, blended by Matt Booth and Justin Andrews. Unlike the Honduran-made lines it is rolled in the Dominican Republic, with Dominican piloto filler aged in palm-leaf tercios.
cigars.researchNote: Launched as a regular production line. STG removed Sancho Panza from its price lists in January 2026 and has not said what happens to the brand.

cigars.about: Kudzu is the oscuro blend that launched Southern Draw in 2014, rolled for the company by AJ Fernandez in Esteli. It is a box-pressed cigar with an Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro wrapper over an Ometepe binder.
cigars.researchNote: Filler: the maker lists Nicaragua and USA; Neptune and Cigar Coop list Nicaraguan only. Strength varies by source: Neptune says Full, Holt's Medium-Full, a Blind Man's Puff panel medium-strong, and a review quoted on the maker's page Medium+. Kudzu Lustrum is a separate limited blend.

cigars.about: Firethorn is Southern Draw's Habano Rosado blend and the company's second line after Kudzu. It pairs an Ecuadorian rosado wrapper with a Mexican San Andres binder and Nicaraguan filler, made at AJ Fernandez's factory.
cigars.researchNote: Strength: Neptune, Holt's and Cigar Coop call it medium; a Blind Man's Puff panel rated it medium-strong. Body is medium to full per a Smoke Magazine quote on the maker's page, but Cigar Coop rated it medium. The box-pressed Belicosos Fino (5.5 x 54) the maker lists is the Firethorn Augusta release.

cigars.about: Jacobs Ladder is Southern Draw's strongest core blend, a Pennsylvania Broadleaf cigar with a heavy dose of Nicaraguan ligero, made at AJ Fernandez's factory in Esteli. It is known as a bold, full-flavored smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Binder is disputed: the maker lists a USA Maduro binder, while Cigar Coop lists an Ecuadorian Maduro binder. A limited run came out just before August 2016 and the national launch was at the 2017 IPCPR show. Jacobs Ladder Brimstone is a separate, stronger release.

cigars.about: Rose of Sharon is Southern Draw's Ecuadorian Connecticut blend, a semi box-pressed cigar made at AJ Fernandez's factory. Dominican Piloto Cubano in the filler gives it more flavor than a typical Connecticut.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper: the maker and Cigar Coop say Ecuadorian Connecticut, but Neptune's spec table lists USA Connecticut Shade. Strength: Corona Cigar and Holt's list mild to medium, Neptune lists mild, and Cigar Coop rated the Lancero at the low end of medium. A very limited run came out in 2016, with the wide release in 2017.

cigars.about: Cedrus is Southern Draw's Indonesian-wrapped blend, first released in 2018 as a single box-pressed belicoso called The Hogan and expanded to more sizes in 2019. It is made at AJ Fernandez's factory in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Strength varies: Holt's lists Medium-Full (used here), Neptune lists Full, and Cigar Coop rated The Hogan Medium.
