Filler: the maker lists Nicaragua only; Cigar Coop and Neptune add Dominican Piloto Cubano. Cigar Coop labels the Besuki wrapper as Sumatra, Indonesia; the maker says only Besuki, Indonesia.

cigars.about: The Habano blend in Southern Draw's value-priced 300 Hands charity line, sold in ten-count bundles and made at AJ Fernandez's factory. The maker brands this version 300 Manos.
cigars.researchNote: Strength: Neptune lists medium; Cigar Coop rated both strength and body medium to full. The maker's page gives the wrapper only as Ecuador; Cigar Coop and Neptune say Ecuadorian Habano.

cigars.about: The Maduro blend in Southern Draw's value-priced 300 Hands charity line, sold in ten-count bundles and made at AJ Fernandez's factory. It uses a dark Nicaraguan wrapper from Esteli over an Indonesian binder.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Three wrapper versions: Connecticut, Ecuadorian Dark Habano, Pennsylvania Broadleaf
cigars.about: QuickDraw is Southern Draw's small-format line, built for a shorter smoke and offered in three wrappers: Connecticut, Dark Habano and Pennsylvania Broadleaf. It is made at AJ Fernandez's factory in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: A line of three blends, so there is no single wrapper category or strength, and the maker publishes no strength rating. Connecticut wrapper: the maker lists it as USA grown; Cigar Coop says Ecuadorian Connecticut. Filler: the maker lists Nicaraguan and Honduran; Cigar Coop and Blind Man's Puff list Nicaraguan only.

cigars.about: Crook of the Crown is the debut blend from Stolen Throne, the Virginia boutique brand founded by Lee Marsh and JR Cannon, released in 2019. It is a San Andrés maduro made with Noel Rojas in Esteli, Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Strength: Atlantic Cigar lists medium to full and Luxury Cigar Club medium plus; a Blind Man's Puff panel and other reviews rated it medium. Filler: the maker lists Nicaraguan; Blind Man's Puff and Luxury Cigar Club list Indonesian and Nicaraguan. Older reviews name other factories tied to blender Noel Rojas.

cigars.about: 3 Kingdoms is the third regular blend from Stolen Throne, released in late 2021 and made at the Rojas Cigar Factory in Nicaragua. It is the brand's full-strength cigar, with a Habano Oscuro wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: Some retailers write the name as III Kingdoms. Wrapper origin is disputed: the maker and Famous Smoke's description say Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro, while Famous Smoke's spec table and a Simply Stogies review say Nicaraguan. Atlantic lists binder and filler as undisclosed; the maker's site lists both as Nicaraguan.

cigars.about: Call to Arms is the second regular blend from Stolen Throne, a Sumatra-wrapped cigar over Nicaraguan binder and filler made at the Rojas Cigar Factory in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the wrapper only as Sumatran. Luxury Cigar Club says Ecuadorian Sumatra, but no maker or top-tier source confirms the growing country, so wrapper origin is left blank. No source gives a firm release year; it followed Crook of the Crown and was being reviewed by March 2021.

cigars.about: Skull Breaker is a Connecticut Broadleaf belicoso in the Surrogates line, blended by Pete Johnson of Tatuaje and rolled by the Garcia family at My Father Cigars in Nicaragua. It is one of the two original Surrogates cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Each Surrogates name is a single size. The line began as a New Havana Cigars house brand, moved to L'Atelier Imports in 2012, and is now sold under Tatuaje, whose own site does not list it. Body is disputed: Cigar Coop rated it medium while Cigar Dojo called it full bodied, so body is left blank.

cigars.about: Tramp Stamp is the Ecuadorian Habano robusto in the Surrogates line, blended by Pete Johnson of Tatuaje and made at My Father Cigars in Nicaragua. It was added when L'Atelier Imports took the line national in 2012.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper: Corona Cigar and Cigars Direct say Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro; Cigar Aficionado and Cigar Coop say Ecuadorian Habano. Strength: Corona Cigar, Cigars Direct and Cigar Coop say medium to full, while Cigar Aficionado called it very full-bodied. Each Surrogates name is a single size; the line is now sold under Tatuaje.

cigars.about: Crystal Baller is the box-pressed Ecuadorian Habano toro in the Surrogates line, blended by Pete Johnson of Tatuaje and made at My Father Cigars in Nicaragua. It was added when L'Atelier Imports took the line national in 2012.
cigars.researchNote: Ring gauge is unsettled: current retailers list 56 (used here), while Cigar Aficionado and Cigar Coop list 54, so check the box if a guest asks. Strength: Cigars Direct and Cigar Coop say medium to full; Tobacconist of Greenwich lists full. Each Surrogates name is a single size; the line is now sold under Tatuaje.

cigars.about: The original Tatuaje line, created by Pete Johnson in 2003 and known as the Brown Label for its band. It is a Cuban-style blend of Nicaraguan tobaccos under an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, rolled by the Garcia family.
cigars.researchNote: Tatuaje rates it 4 on its 1 to 5 strength scale. The six original sizes are rolled in Miami; the 7th, Petite and other later Brown Label sizes are made in Nicaragua at My Father Cigars.

cigars.about: Tatuaje's red band line, introduced in 2006 as a medium strength Nicaraguan-made counterpart to the Miami Brown Label. It uses an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over a double Nicaraguan binder and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: Tatuaje rates it 3 on its 1 to 5 strength scale. Series E and Series B are soft-pressed sizes added in 2026 with a 20th anniversary second band.

cigars.about: A regular production line launched in 2011 and built on the blend of the limited 2009 T110. It is one of Tatuaje's strongest cigars, made at My Father Cigars in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Tatuaje rates it 5+ on its 1 to 5 strength scale. Size names are the length in millimeters.

cigars.about: A stronger take on the Tatuaje Brown Label that uses more ligero in the filler. Most sizes are named for a year, following a three-year cycle that began in 2003.
cigars.researchNote: Cojonu 2003, 2006, 2009 and Gran Cojonu are rolled in Miami. Cojonu 2012, 2015, 2018 and 2021 are made in Nicaragua at My Father Cigars. Some years also come with broadleaf, Sumatra, corojo or San Andres wrappers.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro that began in 2007 as Pete Johnson's personal cigar, modeled on a farm-rolled cigar he was given in Cuba. It was sold mostly in limited batches, including the well known ceramic jars, until it became a full regular line in 2016.
cigars.researchNote: Formal name is Black Label Private Reserve. Tatuaje rates it 4 on its 1 to 5 strength scale. The box-pressed Robusto and Torpedo were added in 2026 with a 20th anniversary second band.

cigars.about: Tatuaje's value-priced line, launched in 2014 with a red band and box art drawn from Pete Johnson's own tattoos. It is made at the Garcia family's TACUBA factory in Esteli rather than the main My Father factory.
cigars.researchNote: Tatuaje rates it 3 on its 1 to 5 strength scale. The Tattoo name first appeared in 2011 on a limited box-pressed lancero; the current blend dates to 2014. The Favoritos size was retired in the U.S. in 2023.

cigars.about: A Tatuaje Limited Series cigar from 2012 that put a Mexican San Andres wrapper over Pete Johnson's usual Nicaraguan binder and filler. It returned in 2019 in four sizes with the red, white and green band.
cigars.researchNote: Sizes shown are the 2019 release, limited to 1,000 bundles of 15 per size. The 2012 originals were store and regional exclusives in other sizes. The regular production sibling, ME II, was retired from the U.S. price list in 2023.

cigars.about: Ten Tatuaje Brown Label sizes dressed in a Connecticut broadleaf wrapper, first sold together in 2017 as a 100-cigar chest. The sizes were later sold in their own boxes.
cigars.researchNote: In 2026 Tatuaje retired five of the ten sizes (Havana Cazadores, Tainos, Especiales, Reserva SW, Cojonu 2003) and moved the five listed here to 21-count boxes. It was shown at the 2016 trade show and shipped nationwide in February 2017.

cigars.about: The broadleaf-wrapped version of the 7th, a corona gorda that was the seventh size in the Tatuaje Brown Label line. It came out in 2010 as a regular production cigar made in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: This is one size of the Seleccion de Cazador (Brown Label) line, not a line of its own. The same 5 5/8 x 46 size also comes as 7th Natural (Ecuador Habano), Capa Especial (Ecuador Sumatra) and, since 2025, Tuxtla and Corojo. Tatuaje rates its Nicaraguan Brown Label sizes 5 of 5 for strength.

cigars.about: Tatuaje's annual Halloween release, begun in 2008 with The Frank. Each cigar is named for a horror character and sold as a limited edition, usually in boxes of 13.
cigars.researchNote: Every Monster has its own blend, wrapper and size, so there is no single spec. The 13 originals ran 2008 to 2019. Since 2021 a Redux series rereleases them one per year. Spin-offs include Skinny Monsters (6 x 38) and the Monster Mash and Monster Smash samplers.

cigars.about: An early Tatuaje brand meant to feel like a simple farm-rolled cigar, with the Jibaro sizes finished with a shaggy foot. It was dropped in 2007 and brought back in 2018, made by My Father Cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the wrapper: Tatuaje's site lists Ecuador, while halfwheel calls the 2018 version a Nicaraguan puro with a corojo 99 wrapper. All three sizes were retired from Tatuaje's price list in April 2026. The original run was made at Tabacalera Tropical and ended in 2007.

cigars.about: A stronger version of Tatuaje Havana VI that started in 2007 as a pair of limited regional releases. It became a full regular production line in 2015.
cigars.researchNote: Tatuaje rates it 4+ of 5; Famous Smoke says medium. Wrapper sources disagree: Tatuaje lists Ecuador and halfwheel said Ecuadorian Habano in 2015, but halfwheel in 2022 and Famous Smoke call it a Nicaraguan puro. Flavors are from a review of the 2007 original. A corojo-wrapped Verocu Blue was added in 2022.

cigars.about: A box-pressed perfecto offshoot of the Tatuaje Fausto blend. One size was released each year from 2011 to 2013, each named for its year.
cigars.researchNote: Avion 11 and 12 are perfectos that taper from 48 to 52 ring. Avion 13 wears a Connecticut broadleaf wrapper, not the Ecuadorian Habano. Tatuaje rates the line 5+ on its 1 to 5 strength scale.

cigars.about: A co-branded cigar from Tatuaje and its sister company L'Atelier Imports, named for the French wine merchants who blend wine from other growers. It uses an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper with Mexican and Nicaraguan binders.
cigars.researchNote: The line is called Negociant; Monopole is the name of the sizes. Tatuaje rates it 3 on its 1 to 5 strength scale. It debuted at the 2016 trade show and shipped nationally in March 2017. It does not use L'Atelier's signature Sancti Spiritus leaf.

cigars.about: A darker version of the L'Atelier LAT line that uses higher primings of its Ecuadorian Sancti Spiritus wrapper. It was introduced in 2013 by L'Atelier Imports, Pete Johnson's sister company to Tatuaje.
cigars.researchNote: Sold under the L'Atelier name, a Pete Johnson brand now part of Tatuaje, not with a Tatuaje band. LAT52, LAT54 and LAT56 were retired in April 2026; the 38 Special and Torpedo went on hiatus in 2020. The original LAT46 was on neither list, so its status is unclear. Strength is halfwheel's reviewer's call.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Sumatra grown in the San Andrés Valley
cigars.about: The long-running core Te-Amo line from the Turrent family, a Mexican puro of sun-grown San Andrés tobacco aged about two and a half years. It is the brand's mild to medium classic and comes in a wide range of sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's Clasico page says born in 1964, while its About page and halfwheel date the brand to 1966. Gran Reserva and Magnificos are sold in tubes.

cigars.filler: Mexico (San Andres Negro, San Andres Corojo), Nicaragua
cigars.about: A Te-Amo line introduced by Altadis U.S.A. at the 2012 trade show in an oval, box-press style shape. It was the first Te-Amo to add Nicaraguan tobacco to the Turrent family's San Andres leaf.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is a Habano-seed leaf grown in San Andres, Mexico. Altadis described it as fuller bodied but no source gives a strength rating. No current retailer listing was found, so it may be out of production. Te-Amo cigars are made in Mexico by the Turrent family.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (San Vicente seco, piloto, olor)
cigars.about: The core line of The Griffin's, a Davidoff-owned brand made in the Dominican Republic. It is a mild, creamy cigar with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Dominican tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: Davidoff's own release calls it mild to medium; Neptune lists it as mild and Famous Smoke as mild-medium. The same Davidoff release mentions a Peruvian binder, while halfwheel and retailers list a Dominican binder. Neptune lists the No. 300 at 43 ring.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (San Vicente seco, piloto mejorado seco), Honduras (Olancho seco), Nicaragua (Esteli ligero, Ometepe viso)
cigars.about: A fuller, spicier Griffin's built around Nicaraguan tobacco, including a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper. Davidoff launched it in Europe in late 2015 and in the U.S. in February 2016.
cigars.researchNote: Despite the name it is a multi-country blend rolled in the Dominican Republic, not a Nicaraguan-made cigar. Strength is not settled: Neptune lists it as full, while Cigar Coop's review found it medium. Current availability was not confirmed.

cigars.about: A Toraño blend released in 2009 to mark 50 years since the 1959 exodus of cigar makers from Cuba. It pairs a dark Brazilian wrapper with Nicaraguan filler and placed in Cigar Aficionado's Top 25 for 2010.
cigars.researchNote: Cigar Aficionado lists medium strength and halfwheel found medium strength with a full body; Holt's lists medium-full and Neptune full. Neptune lists Honduras as the origin, against Nicaragua everywhere else. Dormant after General Cigar bought Toraño in 2014, it returned in 2018.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Mexico
cigars.about: The original gold-label Exodus 1959 from 2001, named for the 1959 exodus of tobacco growers and cigar makers from Cuba. It is a box-pressed cigar known for its five-country filler blend.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers describe a Nicaraguan Habano or Habana 2000 wrapper, but Cigar Aficionado's 2007 rating and Neptune list a Honduran wrapper. Holt's says medium-full; Neptune lists full. Dormant after the 2014 sale to General Cigar, it returned in 2018.

cigars.about: A series of blends drawn from the Toraño family's blend book, which is kept in a bank vault. The first, Vault A-008, came out in 2011 and Toraño called it the strongest blend it had made.
cigars.researchNote: Vault is several different blends. Details here are the original A-008. D-042 followed in 2013, and General Cigar added P-044, TM-027, C-033 and L-075 in 2016 and E-021 and W-009 in 2017. Ask which code is on the band. Neptune lists A-008 as full strength; halfwheel found it medium-plus.

cigars.about: The Toraño house blend, a mild to medium cigar with an Ecuadorian Connecticut shade wrapper. It went dormant after General Cigar bought the brand in 2014 and came back in 2018.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the blend: Neptune lists a Nicaraguan binder with Honduran and Nicaraguan filler, Mike's Cigars lists Dominican and Nicaraguan, and Cigar Aficionado's 2004 rating gave an Indonesian binder. Neptune's spec and Cigar Aficionado call it mild; Mike's Cigars says mild to medium.

cigars.about: A 2010 release from the Toraño family, blended by Charlie Toraño with the company's master roller Felipe Sosa, whose image is on the box. It uses an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists it as medium while Mike's Cigars says medium to full, so no strength is given here. Master Maduro, with a Nicaraguan Habano Maduro wrapper, is a separate 2012 extension.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made for Altadis U.S.A. by AJ Fernandez, launched in 2019 for the Trinidad brand's 50th anniversary. Its bright packaging is inspired by Havana in the 1960s.
cigars.researchNote: This is Espiritu Series No. 1; Series No. 2 and No. 3 are later, different blends. Altadis lists the Robusto at 5 x 50 and Toro at 6 x 54, while halfwheel listed both at 52 ring. A 7 1/2 x 40 Fundador was sold only at events.

cigars.about: A Dominican puro made by Jochy Blanco at Tabacalera Palma, the first Altadis U.S.A. project developed with Rafael Nodal. It came out in October 2017.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is listed as medium-full by Holt's and full by Neptune; halfwheel found it medium-plus. Halfwheel lists the Belicoso at 6 x 52, Neptune at 6 1/8 x 52. Neptune and Holt's describe the wrapper as dark, and Neptune calls it Habano maduro.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro that is rolled in the Dominican Republic at Tabacalera de García. Altadis added it to the VegaFina brand in 2014.
cigars.researchNote: All Nicaraguan tobacco but made in the Dominican Republic. Cigar Coop reports Altadis no longer sells it in the U.S., though it continues in other markets with more sizes.

cigars.about: A VegaFina line made by Tabacalera de García with a Mexican San Andrés Criollo wrapper over Dominican binder and filler. It reached U.S. stores in 2012.
cigars.researchNote: Strength and flavor notes come from Neptune's listing only. It is not on Altadis U.S.A.'s current VegaFina page, but Fortaleza 2 releases continue in international markets.

cigars.about: Named for the year the VegaFina brand was founded. It is made at Tabacalera de García with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper and aged tobaccos, and came to the U.S. in 2020 after starting in Europe.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis describes it as medium-bodied, while Neptune lists it as full. Altadis's site and Neptune list the VF 52 at 5 inches; the 2020 press release gave 5 1/4. Sold in Europe before the September 2020 U.S. release.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, Mexico, Peru, Honduras, United States, Nicaragua
cigars.about: The original PSyKo SEVEN from Ventura Cigar Co., launched in 2013 and named for its seven tobaccos from six countries. It is made in the Dominican Republic and is now sold as the Natural.
cigars.researchNote: Ventura now calls this blend PSyKo SEVEN Natural, alongside Maduro, Connecticut and Nicaragua versions. Ventura rates it mild-medium; Neptune lists mild. The factory is as halfwheel reported in 2014.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua, Peru, Honduras, Dominican Republic, United States
cigars.about: The maduro version of Ventura's PSyKo SEVEN, with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over an Ecuadorian binder and a multi-country filler. It is made in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Ventura rates it medium; Neptune calls it medium to full. Ventura only says the filler is a multi-country blend; the country list is Neptune's. It was the second PSyKo SEVEN blend, out before the 2016 Connecticut.

cigars.about: A series of 26 numbered blends that Ventura Cigar Co. launched in 2016, commissioned from factories owned by Davidoff, Drew Estate, La Aurora, Plasencia and Rocky Patel. The name honors the Case Study houses of mid-century Southern California.
cigars.researchNote: Not one cigar: each Case Study number is its own blend, factory and size list, so there is no single wrapper or strength. White bands mark regular production and black bands mark limited editions. Ask which number is on the band.

cigars.about: One of two Archetype blends that Drew Estate made for Ventura Cigar Co., released in 2016. It has a dark Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: Ventura only described a Habano Maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos; the Ecuadorian origin and Indonesian Sumatra binder come from Neptune. Neptune rates it full strength, though its line description says medium to full-bodied, and marks it discontinued. Its sister blend is Archetype Initiation.

cigars.about: One of Viaje's two original lines from when Andre Farkas started the company in 2008, a Nicaraguan puro. Viaje brought it back in 2021 with a slightly updated blend made at the AGANORSA Leaf factory.
cigars.researchNote: Made at Joya de Nicaragua at first, then Raíces Cubanas in Honduras from 2009, then TABSA in Nicaragua from 2021. The Corojo 99 wrapper is as listed for the Honduran-made version; Viaje calls the 2021 version a Nicaraguan puro with slight blend changes. Strength is CigarsDirect's listing. Released in small batches.

cigars.about: The sister line to Viaje Oro and one of the company's original releases, a Nicaraguan puro. Viaje revived it in 2021 with a slightly updated blend made at the AGANORSA Leaf factory.
cigars.researchNote: Earlier Platino releases were made at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras; the 2021 return moved to TABSA in Nicaragua. The Corojo 99 wrapper is as listed for the Honduran-made version. Strength is CigarsDirect's listing; Atlantic calls it full bodied. Released in small batches rather than year-round.

cigars.about: Originally the personal blend of Viaje founder Andre Farkas, first sold in 2009. It is a Nicaraguan puro of AGANORSA tobacco rolled at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras, and is seen as one of Viaje's more balanced lines.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje made it regular production in 2015 in three sizes; a 2023 batch was announced as a return to shelves. Neptune calls it medium strength; halfwheel's Double R review found it building to full. Halfwheel's release lists give the Double R as 5 1/4 inches, its review 5 1/2. Exclusivo Nicaragua and Exclusivo Leaded are different blends.

cigars.about: Viaje's largest series, a run of small-batch releases that began with the Daisy Cutter in 2010 and is known as one of the company's strongest. The cigars are named after bombs and, more recently, comic book characters.
cigars.researchNote: A series, not one blend: Viaje usually does not disclose the wrapper, blend or factory, and they change from release to release. Recent ones are described only as Nicaraguan tobaccos. Strength is as retailers put it (CigarsDirect: usually full). Sizes are the releases that have returned more than once; the MOAB has also been 4 1/2 x 52.

cigars.about: A Dominican-made Villiger line named after an old Cuban brand, reblended by Heinrich Villiger and Jose Matias Maragoto of the ABAM factory. The Robusto placed tenth on Cigar Aficionado's Top 25 of 2017.
cigars.researchNote: This is the 2017 reblend of a line Villiger first sold from 2005 to 2007. Villiger rates it 3 out of 5 for strength and Neptune lists medium, but Cigar Aficionado rated the Robusto medium-full. The type of Ecuadorian wrapper leaf is not published. A 6 x 52 Toro added in 2019 is not on Villiger's current list.

cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made for Villiger at Joya de Nicaragua, launched in 2018 for the company's 130th anniversary. The name means the victor, and Villiger bills it as the fullest cigar in its range.
cigars.researchNote: Villiger rates it 4 out of 5 for strength. Neptune lists it as full, while halfwheel's reviewer found the strength closer to medium. Villiger's current page shows a Torpedo but not the Gordo.

cigars.about: The Ecuadorian Habano-wrapped member of Villiger's three-blend San'Doro family, with Nicaraguan binder and filler. Villiger says it placed in a top 25 list for the United States in 2018.
cigars.researchNote: Villiger rates it 4 out of 5 for strength, but Neptune lists it as medium. Launch coverage and Neptune name Oliva's TABOLISA factory, while a 2020 limited Diadema size was rolled at Joya de Nicaragua, so the current factory is uncertain.

cigars.about: A Brazilian puro in Villiger's San'Doro family, rolled at the company's own factory in Bahia. It comes in a single Toro size.
cigars.researchNote: Unlike the Nicaraguan-made San'Doro Claro and Colorado, this one is all Brazilian tobacco and made in Brazil. Villiger rates it 4 out of 5 for strength, though Developing Palates reviewers found it around medium. Villiger do Brasil opened in Bahia in 2018; the 2015 launch came from Villiger's earlier factory in the same city.

cigars.about: Named for the year Villiger was founded, this was the first handmade premium cigar to carry the Villiger name. It is a Dominican-made blend put together by Heinrich Villiger and was reblended and repackaged in 2016.
cigars.researchNote: Details are for the 2016 reblend of the original line, which Villiger now labels 1888 Dominican Republic. There are separate 1888 Nicaragua and 1888 San Andres cigars with different blends made in Nicaragua, so check the band. The type of Ecuadorian wrapper leaf is not published.

cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made for Villiger at Joya de Nicaragua, named after a 19th century Havana cigar factory once owned by Pedro Murias. The wrapper is said to be aged about four years.
cigars.researchNote: It was a European-market line first and reached the United States in March 2019. The year it first launched in Europe was not found. Villiger still lists it on its Swiss and German sites but not on its U.S. page, and the wrapper leaf type is not published. Sizes shown are the U.S. launch sizes.

cigars.about: Warped's flagship, rolled in Miami at El Titan de Bronze in the style of Cuban custom rolls, with entubado bunching, a triple cap and a covered foot. The name means the beehive, and output is capped at about 100 cigars a day.
cigars.researchNote: Warped rates the body mild to medium, while Neptune lists it as medium. Warped's site currently shows only the Amado No. 44 as the regular size. Black Honey and Unico Especial are limited 5 x 48 versions, and Black Honey uses a darker Habano Oscuro wrapper.

cigars.about: The first line Kyle Gellis released when he brought Warped back in 2014, rolled in Miami at El Titan de Bronze. The name means the bear.
cigars.researchNote: El Oso is no longer listed on Warped's website, and recent releases such as El Oso Blanco and the 10th anniversary Grand Papa have been limited runs with altered blends. The MaMa lancero used a Mexican San Andrés wrapper instead of the Habano Oscuro.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA, Aganorsa)
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro of Aganorsa tobacco and the first Warped cigar made outside Miami. The name means flower of the valley.
cigars.researchNote: Flor del Valle is no longer listed on Warped's website, so its current status is unclear. The Sky Flower size uses a tweaked, stronger blend with medio tiempo leaf in the filler.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA, Aganorsa)
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro built from Aganorsa tobaccos chosen from farms and lots Warped had not used before. The name means master of time.
cigars.researchNote: Warped told retailers in January 2025 that the line was being discontinued, though its website still shows it as regular production. The limited 6102R (5 1/4 x 48, with medio tiempo leaf) was announced to return in fall 2026. Kyle Gellis called the blend medium to full at launch, but Warped's site now rates it medium.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA, Aganorsa)
cigars.about: Warped's revival of an old Cuban brand name, made as a Nicaraguan puro with Aganorsa tobacco. The name means the estate.
cigars.researchNote: First Growth, added in 2021, uses higher priming leaves than the original two sizes for more body and spice.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA, Aganorsa)
cigars.about: A lower-priced Nicaraguan puro of Aganorsa tobacco from Kyle Gellis, named for his and his brother Devin's love of travel. It comes in two small sizes.
cigars.researchNote: It first shipped in August 2017 under a separate brand called Edition One, run by Kyle and Devin Gellis, and is now listed on Warped's own site. Warped's spec sheet says medium body while its tasting note says medium to full.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA, Aganorsa)
cigars.about: A short, box-pressed Nicaraguan puro whose name means short. It was the first full-bodied blend Warped made, built for a quick smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Warped calls it full bodied, though Neptune lists it as medium. It launched as a single 4 1/2 x 50 size called X50 with a plan to swap in a new size each year. Corto Maduro is a separate line with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA, Aganorsa)
cigars.about: A single-size Nicaraguan puro named for the birth year of Warped founder Kyle Gellis. Cigar Aficionado rated it 95 points and named it its number 3 cigar of 2019.
cigars.researchNote: Warped rates the body as medium plus. It was shown at the 2017 trade show but did not ship until August 2018. Often shortened to GR88.

cigars.about: One of the two debut lines from West Tampa Tobacco Co., the company Rick Rodriguez started in 2022 after leaving CAO. It is the darker, stronger partner to the White.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel's review calls it a medium-full blend that builds late, while Neptune lists it as full. The wrapper is the same leaf type as the White but from a higher priming, which makes it darker.

cigars.about: One of the two debut lines from West Tampa Tobacco Co., the company Rick Rodriguez started in 2022 after leaving CAO. It is the lighter, creamier partner to the Black.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree under the wrapper. Halfwheel lists an Ometepe binder with Condega and Estelí fillers. Developing Palates lists an Ometepe binder with Ometepe, Jalapa and Pueblo Nuevo fillers. Neptune lists an Ecuadorian Habano binder. The launch announcement said only Nicaraguan binder and filler.

cigars.about: The third regular line from Rick Rodriguez's West Tampa Tobacco Co., added in May 2023. Rodriguez described it as a full-bodied blend made to his own taste.
cigars.researchNote: The maker and Neptune call it full. Halfwheel's reviewer found the strength starting at medium and finishing just under full.

cigars.about: A limited edition series from West Tampa Tobacco Co. built around blends Rick Rodriguez says he kept locked away for nearly 30 years. The first release, simply called Attic, came in boxes of 14 with a QR code on the foot band linking to a video.
cigars.researchNote: Details are for Attic, the only Attic Series release found. It shipped in December 2022 (2,000 boxes of 14) and was made again in 2024 (2,500 boxes). No maker strength rating was found. Halfwheel's review ran medium-plus to medium-full, while Neptune and two of three Developing Palates reviewers call it medium.

cigars.about: One of three Wynwood Hills blends from Christian Eiroa's C.L.E. Cigar Co., sold alongside the Asylum brand. The line was first planned under the name Waverly Hills.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the wrapper. The 2018 launch report gave Deranged the Connecticut Broadleaf and Unhinged the Sumatra, with Dominican and Honduran fillers. Halfwheel's 2019 show report, Cigar Coop and Neptune all say Deranged is the Ecuadorian Sumatra. Strength is from Neptune alone. Check the box before quoting it.

cigars.about: One of three Wynwood Hills blends from Christian Eiroa's C.L.E. Cigar Co., sold alongside the Asylum brand. The line was first planned under the name Waverly Hills.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the wrapper. The 2018 launch announcements gave Unhinged the Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper and Deranged the Broadleaf. Halfwheel's 2019 show report, Cigar Coop and Neptune all say Unhinged is the Connecticut Broadleaf. Neptune lists it as discontinued and gives conflicting strength, so strength is left blank.

cigars.about: The Honduran puro among the three Wynwood Hills blends from Christian Eiroa's C.L.E. Cigar Co., with a Corojo wrapper from the Eiroa family's farm.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists it as discontinued. Its page calls the cigar full bodied but tags the strength as medium, so strength is left blank. The factory name comes from Cigar Coop only.

cigars.about: Zino Platinum is the high-end Zino brand Davidoff launched in 2002, rolled in the Dominican Republic. It is sold as two families, the Scepter Series and the Crown Series, with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over a Connecticut binder and Dominican and Peruvian filler.
cigars.researchNote: Platinum is a family (Scepter and Crown Series), not one cigar; specs are the core blend, and limited editions use other blends. Retailers list it as medium; a 2004 Cigar Aficionado note calls the Scepter mild to medium. The maker's Zino site now lists only Nicaragua and Honduras, so it may no longer be made.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (San Vicente and San Vicente Mejorado Seco), Honduras (Olancho and Jamastran Viso), Nicaragua (Ometepe Viso)
cigars.about: Zino Nicaragua is the value-priced relaunch of Davidoff's Zino brand from 2021. Despite the name it is rolled in Honduras at Davidoff's Diadema factory, with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and a three-country filler.
cigars.researchNote: Rolled in Honduras, not Nicaragua, and it is not a Nicaraguan puro. The maker's line page says medium strength (intensity 3 of 5), though its home page calls it bold and full-bodied; halfwheel found medium body and strength. The Half Corona comes pre-cut with a punch.

cigars.about: The green-banded, criollo-wrapped version of Viaje's Zombie, a small-batch release that usually comes as a 5 x 52 perfecto with a tapered foot. In 2026 it returned as a 6 x 56 figurado with alternate box art.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje does not disclose the factory. The 2014 release was made at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras; Atlantic Cigar lists the 2026 release as made in Nicaragua and full strength. The Zombie line began in 2011 and the Green and Red versions arrived in 2014.

cigars.about: The red-banded, maduro-wrapped version of Viaje's Zombie, released in small batches and usually sold as a 5 x 52 perfecto in 20-count boxes. In 2026 it returned as a 6 x 56 figurado with alternate box art.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje does not disclose the factory. The 2014 release was made at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras, while Atlantic Cigar lists the 2026 release as made in Nicaragua. Tasting notes are from Halfwheel's review of the 2016 release.

cigars.about: The black-banded version of Viaje's Zombie, released as a Collector's Edition in 2020 and brought back in 2026 as a 6 x 56 figurado with alternate box art.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel says the black band means a natural wrapper; Atlantic Cigar lists it as Habano over Nicaraguan binder and filler, full strength. Viaje has not disclosed the blend or factory. A 5 1/2 x 54 Collector's Edition came out in 2020.

cigars.about: A slim lonsdale follow-up to Viaje's Zombie line, sold in plastic jars of 24 styled like a jar of syringes. It is a Nicaraguan puro with a tapered foot.
cigars.researchNote: Factory was confirmed for the 2021 release and Viaje said the 2024 release was unchanged. The wrapper varietal is not published; one retailer lists it as criollo, medium-full and made in Nicaragua. A larger 6 1/4 x 50 Collector's Edition came out in 2017.

cigars.about: A box-pressed offshoot of Viaje's Zombie, based on the regular Zombie blend and sold in very small batches. It debuted in 2016 in Green and Red, and a Black version was added in 2025.
cigars.researchNote: Three blends: Green (criollo), Red (maduro) and Black (blend undisclosed). Binder, filler and factory are not published. Reviews found the Green medium in strength and the Red full. Tasting notes are for the Green.

cigars.about: A 2022 Viaje release that crosses the Zombie line with the perfecto shape of its Pepper Series. It came in Red, Green and Black versions in boxes of 25.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not disclosed the blends, only that they are similar to but not the same as the regular Zombie. The size (5 3/16 x 55) comes from a retailer listing; Halfwheel did not publish one.

cigars.about: A crossover of Viaje's Zombie and Super Shot lines: the Zombie blend in a short, fat 3 1/2 x 54 size called 10 Gauge, sold in boxes of 25.
cigars.researchNote: The 2013 and 2014 releases were made at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras; Viaje has not named the factory for later ones. Strength and tasting notes are from Halfwheel's reviews of those early releases.

cigars.about: A Thanksgiving-season Viaje release that merges the Zombie line with its Farmer Bill Hatchet cigar. It is a box-pressed robusto sold in boxes of 30.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not disclosed the factory. Strength, body and tasting notes come from Cigar Coop's review of a 2016 cigar with a year of age; it said the cigar was closer to medium-full when new.

cigars.about: A Zombie-themed version of Viaje's Thanksgiving cigar Farmhand Andre, a box-pressed robusto that debuted in May 2020 and returned in 2023.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not disclosed the blend or the factory. One retailer lists it as medium-full and made in Nicaragua; Halfwheel found the strength anywhere from medium to near full.

cigars.about: A Zombie-themed version of Viaje's Thanksgiving cigar Mrs. Hatchet, shipped in November 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje declined to give any details, so the blend, size and factory are unpublished. The regular Mrs. Hatchet from 2021 was a 6 x 50 box-pressed toro.

cigars.about: A special version of Viaje's former Oro line, a Nicaraguan puro with a corojo 99 wrapper and added aged ligero. The 2010 VOR No. 5 was Cigar Aficionado's number two cigar of that year.
cigars.researchNote: Also called V.O.R. Blend and factory are as published for the 2010 and 2011 releases; Viaje has not confirmed them for the 2024 Double Torpedo or 2026 Perfecto. Cigar Aficionado rated it medium-full, Atlantic Cigar lists it as full.

cigars.about: A special version of Viaje's former Platino line that uses more aged tobacco under a corojo 99 wrapper. It dates to 2010 and came back in 2024 as a double torpedo and in 2026 as a box-pressed perfecto.
cigars.researchNote: Also called V.P.R. Blend and factory are as published for the early releases; Viaje has not confirmed them for the 2024 and 2026 releases. Halfwheel found the 2026 Perfecto medium-full, Atlantic Cigar lists it as full.

cigars.about: A stronger version of Viaje's Exclusivo, founder Andre Farkas's personal blend, made fuller by adding medio tiempo leaf. It is a Nicaraguan puro rolled in Danlí, Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper varietal is not published. Exclusivo Nicaragua Leaded (2018) is a separate blend made at TABSA in Nicaragua.

cigars.about: A new Viaje line from June 2026: a Nicaraguan-made robusto extra with a gold foil cap, sold unbanded in jars of 30. The name refers to standout bales of tobacco noticed during sorting.
cigars.researchNote: Blend and factory are undisclosed. Sources disagree on strength: Halfwheel found the nicotine strength mild with medium to medium-full body, while Atlantic Cigar lists it as full.

cigars.about: A near-annual Viaje release marking founder Andre Farkas's birthday, usually a 6 x 52 torpedo. Recent boxes include one extra gold-foil cigar in a different blend for good luck.
cigars.researchNote: Blend shown is the criollo 98 version used from 2017 through 2022. Only the 2016 debut used a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper, and the 2026 blend is undisclosed. It was made at TABSA in Nicaragua in 2018 and 2019; the factory is not confirmed since.

cigars.about: A Viaje line introduced in spring 2026, named after the butcher's term for a hand-picked premium cut. It comes in two sizes in 25-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Blend and factory are undisclosed; the bands indicate it is made in Nicaragua. One retailer lists a rosado wrapper, which Viaje has not confirmed.

cigars.about: A Fourth of July release from Viaje: a box-pressed robusto gordo capped at both ends, packed in 75-count crates styled like explosives boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Binder, filler and factory are undisclosed for the 2023 and 2026 releases. The 2019 version was a Nicaraguan puro made at TABSA in Estelí; 2015 and 2016 came from PDR with a broadleaf wrapper. One retailer lists it as full strength.

cigars.about: Viaje's dynamite-themed Fourth of July cigar, a toro gordo with a covered foot and a long pigtail cap meant to look like a fuse. It ships in 75-count crates.
cigars.researchNote: Binder, filler and factory are undisclosed for recent releases; the 2019 version was a Nicaraguan puro made at TABSA in Estelí. Before 2021 the size was 6 1/4 x 54. Strength and tasting notes are from Halfwheel's review of the 2021 release.

cigars.about: A 9 x 50 Fourth of July release from Viaje, sold in 15-count boxes marked Fireworks. It debuted in 2012 and returned in 2014, 2017, 2019 and 2023.
cigars.researchNote: It debuted as a Nicaraguan puro based on the TNT blend, made at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras, but Viaje has not disclosed the blend or factory since. The 2023 release was aged about 18 months in the box. Tasting notes are from the 2012 release.

cigars.about: A Fourth of July cigar Viaje added in 2023, named after a loud type of roman candle firework. It is a toro extra sold in boxes of 60 and is not the same blend as the Viaje Roman Candle.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not named the factory. One retailer lists it as full strength and made in Nicaragua.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan Corojo 99 (Corojo version); Mexican San Andrés Maduro (Maduro version)
cigars.about: A Japan-themed perfecto from Viaje sold in two blends, one with a Nicaraguan corojo 99 wrapper and one with a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper. It debuted in 2022 in bento-style boxes and returned in 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Two blends share the name: Corojo and Maduro (San Andrés wrapper). Blend, factory, strength and tasting notes are from halfwheel's review of the 2022 Corojo, which built to full strength by the end. Viaje has not confirmed the 2026 blend, and the 2022 run was 400 boxes.

cigars.about: The first cigar in Viaje's Pepper Series, a small perfecto with green foil over its top half so it looks like a jalapeño. It comes back in occasional batches.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje keeps the blend secret. The 2015 debut was made at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras; a 2018 post hinted production moved to Nicaragua, and the current factory is not disclosed. The Phat Jalapeño (5 3/16 x 55) is the larger version.

cigars.about: A larger Pepper Series perfecto from Viaje, built on the Jalapeño blend but reworked to be less strong and a little sweeter. It is a Nicaraguan puro rolled in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper varietal and the factory are not disclosed. Length is listed as both 5 3/16 and 5 13/16 inches; Viaje gives 5 3/16 x 55 for its Phat peppers. halfwheel's review put strength at medium, rising to medium-plus.

cigars.about: A Pepper Series perfecto from Viaje named after one of the hottest peppers, dressed in red foil. It is a Nicaraguan puro made with Aganorsa tobacco and rolled in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper varietal is not disclosed. Strength and tasting notes come from halfwheel's review of the Phat Carolina Reaper (5 3/16 x 55), the larger version, which finished at full strength.

cigars.about: The larger Phat version of Viaje's Scotch Bonnet, a Pepper Series perfecto with gold foil over its top half. It shipped in 2023 as the first Scotch Bonnet release since the 2019 debut.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not disclosed the blend or the factory. halfwheel reviewed the regular Scotch Bonnet (4 7/8 x 50) as full strength. halfwheel lists the Phat at 5 13/16 x 55, but a retailer and Viaje's other Phat peppers give 5 3/16 x 55.

cigars.about: A 2024 addition to Viaje's Pepper Series, named for the mild Japanese pepper and sold in regular and Phat formats. Most cigars in a box are milder, with a few stronger ones mixed in.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not disclosed the blend, factory or exact size. Viaje says it is on the milder side with stronger cigars sprinkled in, and the stronger ones wear red foil. Earlier peppers measured 4 7/8 x 50 or 51, and Phat versions 5 3/16 x 55.

cigars.about: The sixth release in Viaje's Private Keep series of favorite blends that had no other home. The cigars come unbanded in 37-count boxes and are identified only by the ribbon color.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not disclosed the blend or the factory. Each Private Keep release is a different blend.

cigars.about: The fifth release in Viaje's Private Keep series, named for the lime-colored ribbon on the unbanded cigars. It shipped in March 2024 in 37-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not disclosed the blend or the factory. Each Private Keep release is a different blend.

cigars.about: The fourth release in Viaje's Private Keep series, named for the lemon-colored ribbon that identifies the unbanded cigars. It is a Nicaraguan puro with a criollo 98 wrapper that shipped in June 2022.
cigars.researchNote: The blend comes from Viaje's comments on Instagram as reported by halfwheel; Cigar Coop reported the blend as undisclosed. The factory and country of manufacture are not published.

cigars.about: A very short, unbanded Nicaraguan puro that Viaje's Andre Farkas created to smoke between rounds of clay shooting. It is packed in boxes made to look like shotgun shell cartons and returns most winters.
cigars.researchNote: The 2012 debut was made at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras, but Viaje no longer says where it is made. Some early batches used a corojo wrapper. Buckshot is the San Andrés maduro version, and there is also a Zombie Super Shot.

cigars.about: A spinoff of Viaje's Super Shot that swaps the Nicaraguan criollo wrapper for Mexican San Andrés maduro. It comes in the same two short sizes and shotgun shell style boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Part of Viaje's Shotgun Shells family with Super Shot. The factory and country of manufacture are not disclosed. Released in 2020 and 2023; Viaje said it would not return with the 2026 Super Shot batch.

cigars.about: A one-time Viaje release from December 2025 in three sizes, with fewer than 200 boxes of each. It has no set MSRP, and early retail prices were around 26 to 27 dollars a cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not disclosed the blend or the factory, and says the line will not be made again. Tailwind is listed as 6 3/4 x 52 x 56, so it tapers from 52 to 56 ring. Boxes hold 30 cigars.

cigars.about: A Viaje line introduced in January 2025 in two sizes with a vampire backstory. Reviewers found it milder than most Viaje cigars, topping out around medium.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not disclosed the blend, factory or country. When Vampire Dust Red came out, Viaje said this original line is called Vampire Dust Purple. Strength and tasting notes are from halfwheel's review.

cigars.about: The second Vampire Dust release from Viaje, shipped in November 2025 in a single 5 x 54 size. It is a different blend from the original Vampire Dust Purple.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not disclosed the blend, factory or country. halfwheel gives the size as 5 x 54 without a vitola name, so Robusto here is only a description of the shape.

cigars.line: Private Bale Bird on a Branch
cigars.about: The first release in Viaje's Private Bale series, which is built on aged tobacco picked leaf by leaf from selected bales. The finished cigars rest nine months before boxing, and Viaje calls it an eight-year project.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel's review lists it as regular production but files it under limited editions, so its status is unclear. The review found strength building to full by the end. Boxes hold 34 cigars.

cigars.line: Private Bale Sunlight On a Field
cigars.about: The second release in Viaje's Private Bale series of aged-tobacco blends, shipped in September 2025 in two sizes. Viaje says each size has its own expression of the blend.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not disclosed the blend, factory or country. Strength and tasting notes are from halfwheel's review of the Twilight size.

cigars.about: A Japan-inspired Viaje torpedo named with the Japanese word for cigar. It began in 2017 as a White Label Project release and came back in 2019 and 2025.
cigars.researchNote: The 2017 original was a full-bodied Dominican puro with a negrito wrapper made by Quesada. In 2019 production moved to TABSA in Nicaragua, and the blend since then has not been disclosed. Factory details for the 2025 batch were not published.

cigars.about: An offshoot of Viaje's Hamaki named for the Japanese dining term for leaving the choice to the chef. Viaje keeps the blend secret on purpose and asks smokers to trust it.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is secret by design. The 2017 and 2019 releases were 6 x 52 toros (2019 made at TABSA); the 2022 release was a tweaked 5 x 52 box-pressed robusto made by Aganorsa Leaf. Strength and tasting notes are from halfwheel's review of the 2019 toro.

cigars.about: Viaje's Halloween release, a thick 5 x 58 Nicaraguan puro with a corojo wrapper and jack-o-lantern packaging. It has returned most Octobers since 2013.
cigars.researchNote: Releases through 2017 were made at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras; 2019 and 2021 were made at TABSA in Nicaragua. Viaje said 2023 was made in Nicaragua without naming the factory, and gave no details for 2025. Strength is from halfwheel's review of the 2013 release.

cigars.about: A smaller-run version of Viaje's Halloween Full Moon that swaps the corojo wrapper for Mexican San Andrés maduro. It first appeared in 2015 and ships alongside the regular Full Moon.
cigars.researchNote: The 2015 and 2017 batches were made at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras; 2019 and 2021 were made at TABSA in Nicaragua. Viaje did not name the factory for 2023 or confirm the blend for 2025. Tasting notes are from halfwheel's 2017 review.

cigars.about: A Halloween-season release from Viaje, introduced in 2024 as a Nicaraguan puro with a corojo 99 wrapper. It is named for the small crow that appears on the packaging of Viaje's Full Moon.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje describes the blend as full-bodied; no separate strength rating is published. A The Crow Edición Limitada shipped with it in October 2025 in the same 5 1/2 x 50 size, and its blend has not been disclosed.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA / Aganorsa Leaf)
cigars.about: One of three Viaje Skull and Bones cigars named after characters from Marvel's Ghost Rider. It first shipped in December 2019 and returned in July 2026, sold in bundles of 25.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has never disclosed the blend. The factory listed is for the original 2019 run; Viaje has not said where the 2026 run was made.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA / Aganorsa Leaf)
cigars.about: One of three Viaje Skull and Bones cigars named after characters from Marvel's Ghost Rider. It first shipped in December 2019 and returned in July 2026, sold in bundles of 25.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has never disclosed the blend. Factory, strength and tasting notes are from the 2019 run; halfwheel's review found it milder than the name suggests, settling just past medium and well short of full. Viaje has not said where the 2026 run was made.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA / Aganorsa Leaf)
cigars.about: The longest of three Viaje Skull and Bones cigars named after characters from Marvel's Ghost Rider. It first shipped in December 2019 and returned in July 2026, sold in bundles of 25.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has never disclosed the blend. The factory listed is for the original 2019 run; Viaje has not said where the 2026 run was made.

cigars.about: The nuclear-themed branch of Viaje's Skull and Bones series: short, thick cigars named after atomic bombs. It returns every few years, most recently in February 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not disclosed the current blend or factory. The 2011 originals were Nicaraguan puros with a sun grown criollo wrapper, rolled in Honduras; the 2016 run used a Mexican San Andrés wrapper and was made at PDR in the Dominican Republic. Full strength comes from reviews of the early runs, not the current blend.

cigars.about: A Viaje Skull and Bones cigar named after the Marvel character, shipped in August 2025 alongside Logan and Weapon X. The three are different blends in the same size, sold in bundles of 25.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not disclosed the blend or where it is made.

cigars.about: A Viaje Skull and Bones cigar named after Wolverine's alter ego, shipped in August 2025 alongside Wolverine and Weapon X. The three are different blends in the same size, sold in bundles of 25.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not disclosed the blend or where it is made.

cigars.about: A Viaje Skull and Bones cigar named after the program that created Wolverine in the Marvel comics, shipped in August 2025 alongside Wolverine and Logan. The three are different blends in the same size, sold in bundles of 25.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not disclosed the blend or where it is made.

cigars.about: A trio of Viaje Skull and Bones cigars released in December 2024 as Camo Green, Camo Orange and Camo Yellow. The name comes from a British earthquake bomb used in World War II.
cigars.researchNote: Three separate blends in one size. The Nicaraguan puro blend and Aganorsa factory come from retailer listings reported by halfwheel; Viaje has not confirmed them or said how the three blends differ.

cigars.about: A trio of Viaje Skull and Bones cigars that arrived quietly at a few stores in December 2023 as Camo Red, Camo Blue and Camo Grey. It is named after the Soviet bomb regarded as the most powerful nuclear weapon ever tested.
cigars.researchNote: Three separate blends in one size. Viaje has not disclosed the blends or factory; one retailer says they are made at Aganorsa with all AGANORSA Leaf tobacco, which Viaje would not confirm. Strength and tasting notes are from halfwheel's review of the Camo Blue.

cigars.about: The cigar that started Viaje's Skull and Bones series in May 2010, a short, thick Nicaraguan puro named after a Vietnam-era bomb. It has come back only a few times, most recently in 2020 and 2024.
cigars.researchNote: The original 2010 run of 150 boxes was rolled at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras. Viaje has not said where the 2020 and 2024 runs were made. Strength and tasting notes are from halfwheel's review of the 2020 run.

cigars.about: Viaje's secretive Skull and Bones release, usually shipped around October in a different size each time. It began in 2010 as a cigar simply called "?" and took the M?stery name in 2012.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje does not disclose the blend or the factory, and the size changes with each release. Strength and tasting notes are from halfwheel's reviews of the 2020 and 2022 releases and may not hold for other years.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA / Aganorsa Leaf)
cigars.about: A short, thick Nicaraguan puro in Viaje's Skull and Bones series, named after the U.S. bomb nicknamed the Mother of All Bombs. It debuted in 2011 and returns every few years, usually with FOAB.
cigars.researchNote: Runs through 2014 were rolled at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras; the 2019 and 2022 runs were made at TABSA in Nicaragua. The size has varied: the 2012 and 2014 runs were about 4 1/2 inches long. Strength and tasting notes are from a review of the 2011 run.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA / Aganorsa Leaf)
cigars.about: A short, thick Nicaraguan puro in Viaje's Skull and Bones series, named after the Russian bomb nicknamed the Father of All Bombs. It debuted in 2012 and returns every few years, usually with MOAB.
cigars.researchNote: The 2012 and 2014 runs were rolled at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras; the 2019 and 2022 runs were made at TABSA in Nicaragua. Strength and tasting notes are from halfwheel's review of the 2014 run.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA / Aganorsa Leaf)
cigars.about: The big 5 x 60 member of Viaje's Skull and Bones series, named after the American T-12 Cloudmaker bomb of the 1940s. It debuted in 2014 and came back in 2019 and 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has never disclosed the blend. The 2014 debut was rolled at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras; the 2019 and 2022 runs were made at TABSA in Nicaragua. Strength and tasting notes are from the 2014 run.

cigars.about: A Viaje Skull and Bones cigar named after the Marvel vigilante, shipped in April 2021 with its sibling Frank Castle. Both are the same size and were sold in bundles of 25.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje calls it a proprietary blend of Nicaraguan tobaccos and has not named the factory. It appears to use a lighter wrapper than Frank Castle. halfwheel's review found it starts mild and builds to full by the end.

cigars.about: A Viaje Skull and Bones cigar named after the man behind Marvel's Punisher, shipped in April 2021 with its sibling The Punisher. Both are the same size and were sold in bundles of 25.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje calls it a proprietary blend of Nicaraguan tobaccos and has not named the factory. It appears to use a darker wrapper than The Punisher.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA / Aganorsa Leaf)
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Three blends: Nicaraguan corojo (Original), maduro of undisclosed origin (Bold), Nicaraguan criollo (Spicy)
cigars.about: A Viaje sampler-style release of three short robusto blends called Original, Bold and Spicy, packed 30 of each in a 90-count box. It debuted in 2015 and returned in 2018 and 2025.
cigars.researchNote: The wrappers, binder, filler and factory listed are from the 2015 and 2018 runs. The 2025 Edición Limitada run has three new blends Viaje has not detailed, and is box-pressed for the first time. The 2015 run was thinner at 4 1/2 x 48.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA / Aganorsa Leaf)
cigars.about: One of Viaje's oldest seasonal releases, shipped in select summers since 2010 and often in a different size. It is known for its brushed foot, where the wrapper stops short and leaves the binder and filler exposed.
cigars.researchNote: The corojo 99 puro blend is from earlier releases; Viaje has not confirmed it for recent years. The 2025 Collector's Edition came in three wrappers (Ecuadorian habano, Mexican maduro, and a barber pole) over Nicaraguan binder and filler. Factory, strength and tasting notes are from the 2020 release.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA / Aganorsa Leaf)
cigars.about: A Viaje line named for 1845, the year the Partagás factory was founded in Havana. It began in 2016 as a European exclusive, reached U.S. stores in 2020 and returned in 2025.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje calls it a Nicaraguan puro, but Cigar Aficionado lists the wrapper as Ecuadorian and has rated it both medium and medium-full. The 2016 European version was made at PDR in the Dominican Republic. The Maduro and Reserva versions are different blends.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA, Aganorsa Leaf)
cigars.about: A version of Viaje's Circa '45 that swaps the Nicaraguan wrapper for Mexican San Andrés over Aganorsa-grown Nicaraguan binder and filler. It shipped in February 2021 with 300 boxes of each of three sizes.
cigars.researchNote: A fourth size, the 7 x 50 Reserva Edición Limitada, shipped unannounced in bundles of 25. Reviewers found it medium or just under, with little of the pepper Viaje is known for.

cigars.about: A box-pressed toro in Viaje's White Label Project series with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It shipped in May 2025.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje declined to say which factory makes it. Production appears to be 200 boxes of 30. No published strength rating or tasting notes from a trusted source.

cigars.about: A 6 x 56 White Label Project release from Viaje with a corojo 99 wrapper. It shipped in August 2024, more than a year after the cigars were rolled.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje disclosed only the wrapper: binder, filler, wrapper origin and factory are not published. Box labels show the cigars were rolled in May 2023. Limited to 200 boxes of 25.

cigars.about: A 6 x 56 White Label Project release from Viaje with a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper. It shipped in August 2024 alongside Blunderbuss, after more than a year of rest.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje disclosed only the wrapper: binder, filler and factory are not published. Box labels show the cigars were rolled in May 2023. Limited to 200 boxes of 25.

cigars.about: A box-pressed robusto in Viaje's White Label Project series that went to select retailers in August 2024. The name appears to come from the Hungarian word for cigar.
cigars.researchNote: The blend and factory are not disclosed: even Viaje's own representative said he knew nothing about it. EL appears to stand for Edición Limitada. Sold in boxes of 25 to Viaje's preferred retailers.

cigars.about: A 6 x 52 toro in Viaje's White Label Project series, named for the Caribbean mashed plantain dish. It was one of the first Viaje cigars made at Tabacalera La Isla in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 300 boxes of 25 (7,500 cigars), shipped February 2023. A departure for Viaje, which usually works with Aganorsa in Nicaragua or Raíces Cubanas in Honduras.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA, Aganorsa Leaf)
cigars.about: A small 4 1/2 x 48 White Label Project cigar from Viaje, the follow-up to the 2020 Amuse-Bouche. It swaps the original's Nicaraguan habano wrapper for Mexican San Andrés.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 300 boxes of 25, shipped January 2022. The original Amuse-Bouche (2020) was an all-Nicaraguan blend in the same size.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Criollo and candela (barber pole double wrapper)
cigars.about: A barber pole cigar in Viaje's White Label Project series that pairs a criollo wrapper with green candela. The two leaves stand for Bruce Banner turning into the Hulk.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrappers, so no single wrapper category applies. Viaje told retailers the pair is criollo and candela but disclosed no binder, filler, factory or country. halfwheel found the strength building from medium-full to full.

cigars.line: Fifteen Plus Two and a Half Anniversary
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan Criollo (Silver and Gold), Nicaraguan Corojo (Red)
cigars.about: A set of box-pressed toros marking Viaje's 17 1/2 years in business, told apart by the color of the foot ribbon. Silver, Gold and Red are all-Nicaraguan blends made by Aganorsa Leaf.
cigars.researchNote: Silver and Gold wear criollo, Red wears corojo, and a pricier Black has an undisclosed blend. Viaje calls them full-bodied, but halfwheel found the Black only about medium in strength. Flavor notes are from that Black review.

cigars.factory: Aganorsa Leaf (Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A., Estelí)
cigars.about: Viaje's 15th anniversary cigars, made by Aganorsa Leaf as three Nicaraguan puro blends called Silver, Gold and Black. They came out as torpedoes in 2022 and returned in 2023 as perfectos packed in ceramic jars.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not said how Silver, Gold and Black differ. The criollo 98 wrapper is confirmed only for the 2023 remake, called 15th Anniversary Pt. II (315 jars of 24 per blend). halfwheel found the Gold Pt. II finishing full in strength.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro from Viaje in an unusual shape, with a rounded cap and a tapered perfecto foot wrapped in red foil. The sizes are named after blades and it comes back in occasional batches.
cigars.researchNote: The 2012 original was rolled at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras. Cigar Aficionado reported in 2023 that Aganorsa Leaf in Estelí now makes the line. Released in 2012, 2013, 2016, 2019 and 2025, with limited Katana (7 x 48) and Falchion (6 x 54) sizes.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Viaje's Honey & Hand Grenades, which trades the Nicaraguan criollo wrapper for Mexican San Andrés. It keeps the rounded cap, tapered foot and red foil of the original.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje declined to disclose the binder, filler, factory or country of origin. The three sizes come from retailer listings and match the original line.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The sixth release in Viaje's craft beer inspired Craft Series, a 6 x 52 toro made at Joya de Nicaragua. The name nods to Viaje's start, since Joya made the company's first cigars in 2007 and 2008.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in 10-count boxes with a silver foil sleeve over most of the cigar. halfwheel found the strength building from medium-full to very strong by the end.

cigars.about: The fifth release in Viaje's Craft Series, a 6 x 52 toro with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Dominican binder and filler. It was among the first Viaje cigars made at Tabacalera La Isla in Santiago.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in 10-count boxes, shipped February 2023. No published strength rating or tasting notes from a trusted source.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA, Aganorsa Leaf)
cigars.about: The fourth release in Viaje's Craft Series, a 6 x 54 Nicaraguan puro made by Aganorsa Leaf. It is creamier and lighter than a typical Viaje.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in 10-count boxes with a silver foil sleeve over most of the cigar. Shipped July 2021.

cigars.about: A 6 x 54 toro Viaje introduced in September 2024, apparently named after the Japanese name for Godzilla. It is packed two cigars to a coffin, 13 coffins to a box.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not disclosed the wrapper, binder, filler, factory or country. halfwheel found it about medium in strength for most of the smoke, then full at the finish.

cigars.about: Viaje's Thanksgiving cigar, a thick 5 x 58 robusto gordo with a Nicaraguan criollo wrapper. It began in 2011 as a White Label Project release and got its own bands and boxes in 2014.
cigars.researchNote: Seasonal: lately shipped in even-numbered years. Raíces Cubanas in Honduras was the stated factory through 2018; Viaje has not confirmed the factory for later batches. The White Meat name dates to 2012, when Dark Meat was added.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Viaje's Thanksgiving cigar, a 5 x 58 robusto gordo with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It was added in 2012 alongside the original, now called White Meat.
cigars.researchNote: Seasonal: lately shipped in even-numbered years. Raíces Cubanas in Honduras was the stated factory through 2018; Viaje has not confirmed the factory for later batches. Reviewers found it medium early, building to medium-full.

cigars.about: A box-pressed 6 x 50 toro in Viaje's Thanksgiving family of cigars, a companion to Farmer Bill Hatchet. It debuted in November 2021 and returned in 2024.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje declined to disclose the blend or factory, and no wrapper has been named. Cigar Coop reported that Viaje called it 100 percent Nicaraguan tobacco. Sold in boxes of 10; a separate Zombie Mrs. Hatchet came out in 2022.

cigars.about: A box-pressed 7 x 52 Nicaraguan puro from Viaje's Thanksgiving lineup, named for the farmer who gets the Stuffed Turkey to the table. It debuted in 2014 and returns in some Novembers.
cigars.researchNote: The cigar's full name is Farmer Bill Hatchet Handle. Viaje has not published the factory or country. Zombie Farmer Bill Hatchet and the Holiday Edition are separate cigars.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut Criollo (criollo seed, rosado color, grown in the Connecticut River Valley)
cigars.about: A version of the Liga Privada 10 Aniversario that Drew Estate blends for markets outside the United States. It is known for its reddish rosado wrapper and a smoother profile than the U.S. cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Not sold in the U.S. Drew Estate lists Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania filler; halfwheel reports Honduras and Nicaragua. The product page says medium to full, the launch release said medium-bodied, and halfwheel's reviewer found the strength below medium.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut River Valley stalk-cut and cured sun grown Habano
cigars.about: A longer, slightly thicker take on the Dirty Rat from Drew Estate's Único Serie, wrapped in the same Connecticut-grown habano leaf as the T52. Drew Estate describes it as a creamier, smoother version of the Dirty Rat blend.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the Único Serie, where each vitola has its own blend. Holt's lists it as full, and halfwheel's review ended at full.

cigars.line: Liga Privada Único Serie Velvet Rat
cigars.about: A broadleaf-wrapped lonsdale in Drew Estate's Único Serie, the same length and ring as the Ratzilla. It began in 2012 as a small release for a Chicago retailer and later became a regular offering.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the Único Serie, where each vitola has its own blend.

cigars.line: Liga Privada Único Serie Year of the Rat
cigars.about: A broadleaf-wrapped corona gorda first made in 2016 for the Drew Estate lounge at the Florida Panthers' arena, named for the team's 1996 Stanley Cup Finals season. It now comes back in gold foil in occasional batches.
cigars.researchNote: Drew Estate lists it among the Único sizes, but it ships in occasional batches (2016, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2024). Strength and body are from halfwheel's 2020 review; Drew Estate gives no rating for it.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut River Valley stalk-cut and cured sun grown Habano
cigars.about: The lancero of Drew Estate's Único Serie, built around the T52 habano wrapper. The name comes from its 40 ring gauge, two points thicker than a classic lancero.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the Único Serie. Halfwheel lists Nicaraguan filler only; Holt's describes the Único line in general as Nicaraguan and Honduran. Halfwheel rated the strength medium-full to full; Holt's lists full.

cigars.line: Liga Privada Único Serie UF-13 Dark
cigars.about: A broadleaf-wrapped robusto in Drew Estate's Único Serie with a small twisted fan cap. It started as a test blend made for a 2012 Cigar.com charity event and went on general sale in 2013.
cigars.researchNote: Drew Estate's site calls it UF13 and lists 5 1/4 x 52; halfwheel lists 5 1/2 x 52. Halfwheel's original 2013 review ended at full strength, while its 2018 review of an aged one stopped at medium.

cigars.about: A toro that grew out of a stronger Liga Privada test blend and is released once a year around Halloween at Casa de Montecristo in Countryside, Illinois. UF stands for Ultra Fuerte.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only at Casa de Montecristo near Chicago, once a year. First sold in 2011, though Drew Estate says the store has had it since 2010. No formal strength rating is published: Drew Estate calls it the Ultra Fuerte blend and halfwheel's reviewer called it strong. Older halfwheel pieces list Nicaraguan filler only.

cigars.line: Liga Privada 10 Year Aniversario A Savage Feast
cigars.binder: Mexico (San Andrés Otapan Negro Último Corte)
cigars.filler: Nicaragua, USA (Pennsylvania Green River One Sucker ligero)
cigars.about: The Liga Privada 10 Aniversario blend rolled in the Feral Flying Pig perfecto shape. It is not sold through normal channels and is offered at events that Jonathan Drew attends.
cigars.researchNote: Event-only cigar, packed in two-count coffins. It carries the 10 Aniversario blend, so strength and flavor words come from Drew Estate's 10 Aniversario page. In 2025 it was also offered to stores buying the S.T. Dupont humidor set.

cigars.line: Liga Privada Único Serie Papas Fritas
cigars.about: A short mixed-filler cigar made from the leaf trimmings left over from rolling Liga Privada No. 9 and T52, finished with a broadleaf wrapper. It is a lower-priced Liga Privada that smokes in about 30 minutes.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed filler, not long filler. Drew Estate lists 4 1/4 x 43; halfwheel and Holt's list 4 1/2 x 44. Drew Estate says medium to full, while Holt's lists the Único line as full.

cigars.line: Liga Privada Único Serie Nasty Fritas
cigars.about: The Papas Fritas idea in the cone-shaped Nasty vitola borrowed from Drew Estate's ACID line. It uses short-cut filler left over from Liga Privada No. 9 and T52 under a broadleaf wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed filler, not long filler. The whole cigar tapers from foot to head. Drew Estate says medium to full; Neptune lists full.

cigars.binder: Mexico (San Andrés Otapan Negro Último Corte)
cigars.filler: Honduras, Nicaragua, USA (Pennsylvania Green River One Sucker)
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut Corojo (H99 hybrid, corojo seed grown in the Connecticut River Valley)
cigars.about: The Papas Fritas format made with the Liga Privada H99 blend, using trimmings saved from rolling the larger H99 sizes. It pairs a Connecticut-grown corojo wrapper with a San Andrés binder.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed filler. Drew Estate lists 4 1/4 x 43; halfwheel lists 4 1/2 x 44. Drew Estate's Papas Fritas page says medium to full, but halfwheel's reviewer found the strength under medium.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut River Valley stalk-cut and cured sun grown Habano
cigars.about: A box-pressed belicoso in Drew Estate's Único Serie made only for the Casa de Montecristo chain of stores. It debuted in late 2023 and came back with new packaging in 2024.
cigars.researchNote: Casa de Montecristo exclusive. Announced in 2023 as an ongoing item, but it arrives in dated yearly batches (800 boxes of 20 in 2024). Halfwheel's 2023 story called the wrapper Brazilian mata fina; its 2024 story lists Connecticut habano over a mata fina binder. No strength rating is published.

cigars.about: A short belicoso in Drew Estate's Único Serie that uses the same Connecticut habano wrapper as the Liga Privada T52. It is released once a year to two Liga Privada lounge stores.
cigars.researchNote: Annual release sold only at Wooden Indian Tobacco Shop in Havertown, Pa., and Barrister Cigars in Union, N.J. Strength is from halfwheel's review, which had it building to just under full.

cigars.about: A short robusto in Drew Estate's Único Serie made for the European market and named after the Bauhaus school of design. It went on sale in Germany in February 2021.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only in Europe. Drew Estate has not said whether it is a limited item. Halfwheel's first review had the strength reaching full; a later one had it at medium-plus.

cigars.line: Liga Privada Único Serie Papas Bravas
cigars.about: A broadleaf-wrapped Único Serie blend that Drew Estate created for the European market in 2024, in two sizes that both have a pigtail cap. The name plays on Papas Fritas and refers to a Spanish fried potato dish.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only in Europe. Despite the name it comes in full robusto and toro sizes, not the small Papas Fritas format.

cigars.about: A Churchill in Drew Estate's Único Serie made for Hong Kong retailer CoH Cigars and tied to Lunar New Year. It is named after a Chinese dried pork dish eaten around the holiday.
cigars.researchNote: Exclusive to CoH Cigars of Hong Kong. Drew Estate disclosed only the wrapper; the binder and filler are not published. Strength and body are from halfwheel's review.

cigars.line: Liga Privada Único Serie Year of the Ox
cigars.about: The 2021 entry in Drew Estate's Chinese zodiac series of Liga Privada cigars, wrapped in gold foil and sold in boxes of eight. It was made for the Chinese market and smokes milder than most Liga Privada blends.
cigars.researchNote: Released for the Chinese market through Drew Estate's distributor there. Halfwheel's news story lists 6 1/4 x 54, while its review lists 6 x 54. Strength and body are from halfwheel's review.

cigars.line: Liga Privada Único Serie Year of the Tiger
cigars.about: The 2022 entry in Drew Estate's Chinese zodiac series of Liga Privada cigars, wrapped in gold foil and sold in boxes of eight. It was an exclusive for Hong Kong retailer CoH Cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Exclusive to CoH Cigars of Hong Kong. Drew Estate pitched it as powerful, but halfwheel's reviewer found it one of the mildest Liga Privadas, medium at most.

cigars.line: Liga Privada Único Serie Year of the Rabbit
cigars.about: The 2023 entry in Drew Estate's Chinese zodiac series of Liga Privada cigars, a short, thick parejo sold in boxes of eight. It was an exclusive for Hong Kong retailer CoH Cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Exclusive to CoH Cigars of Hong Kong. Drew Estate lists it as 4 1/2 x 54; halfwheel measured its samples at about 56 ring. Strength and body are from halfwheel's review.

cigars.line: Liga Privada Único Serie Year of the Dragon
cigars.about: The 2024 entry in Drew Estate's Chinese zodiac series of Liga Privada cigars, sold in boxes of ten by Hong Kong retailer CoH Cigars. Drew Estate never formally announced it.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is undisclosed: neither Drew Estate nor CoH Cigars has published the wrapper, binder or filler. It is listed as 6 x 52, but halfwheel measured its samples at 6 1/2 x 56. Strength is from halfwheel's review.

cigars.line: Liga Privada Único Serie Year of the Snake
cigars.about: A 7 x 44 lonsdale in Drew Estate's Lunar New Year series, released in January 2025 for the Year of the Snake. It was sold only through CoH Cigars in Hong Kong in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Exclusive to CoH Cigars in Hong Kong, so rarely seen in US shops. Drew Estate gives no strength rating; halfwheel's reviewer found strength mild to medium-minus with medium body, lighter than most Liga Privada.

cigars.line: Liga Privada Único Serie Year of the Horse
cigars.about: The 2026 entry in Drew Estate's Lunar New Year series, a 5 1/4 x 60 cigar sold in boxes of 10 outside the United States. Drew Estate never formally announced it.
cigars.researchNote: Blend is undisclosed and Drew Estate never announced the cigar; it is not sold by US retailers. halfwheel's reviewer noted a lighter wrapper than usual for Liga Privada and rated strength medium-plus. One retailer lists it as 6 1/4 x 60, which halfwheel says is wrong.

cigars.line: Liga Privada Único Serie Tres Serpientes
cigars.about: The first Liga Privada culebra: three 6 1/2 x 43 cigars twisted and tied together, made with the Liga Privada H99 blend. It is sold only at Drew Estate in-store events from September through December 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Event-only, $160 for a box of three culebras (nine cigars). halfwheel says it uses the Liga Privada H99 blend, so binder and filler are Drew Estate's H99 details. No strength is published for the culebra; Drew Estate rates the regular H99 line full.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Undercrown built around Dominican filler under an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. It shipped in late April 2026 in four sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Despite the name it is rolled in Nicaragua; Drew Estate says production will move to its new Dominican factory later. Drew Estate lists it as medium to full; halfwheel's reviewer found the strength mild at first and medium by the end. All four sizes are box-pressed.

cigars.about: A box-pressed 6 x 56 Undercrown Maduro made with the Cigar Dojo online community, using the slightly stronger Corona Viva version of the blend. It began in 2014 as a single-store release and went national in 2018 as a recurring limited edition.
cigars.researchNote: One box-pressed size of the Undercrown Maduro line, which Drew Estate rates medium to full; halfwheel's reviewer found this one medium. A separate 10th Anniversary version from 2022 is a 6 x 46 box-pressed belicoso, limited to 2,500 boxes of 10.
