cigars.about: A box-pressed 5 x 54 robusto in the Undercrown Sun Grown blend, made with the Cigar Dojo community as a companion to the original Dojo Dogma Maduro. It debuted in September 2020 and has returned in later batches.
cigars.researchNote: This is one box-pressed size of the Undercrown Sun Grown line, also written as Undercrown Dojo Dogma Sun Grown. The filler includes aged ligero from Nueva Segovia. Strength is halfwheel's review rating (medium-full, easing to medium-plus), as Drew Estate gives none for this size.

cigars.about: A 5 x 50 box-pressed belicoso made for the 20th anniversary of Shady Records, the label founded by Eminem and Paul Rosenberg. It debuted in 2019 and returned in 2020, sold in 10-count packs.
cigars.researchNote: Shares its blend with the Undercrown Dojo Dogma Maduro, an offshoot of Undercrown Maduro first made for the Corona Viva. It followed the 2015 Undercrown ShadyXV, which was sold only in Detroit. Strength and body are from a Blind Man's Puff panel review.

cigars.about: The second Nica Rustica blend, a value-priced habano-wrapped cigar added in 2022 alongside the original broadleaf version. It is named for adobe, a building material widely used in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Drew Estate rates it mellow to medium, but halfwheel's reviewer found it full in flavor with strength building to medium-full by the end.

cigars.about: The third Nica Rustica blend, a value-priced cigar with an Ecuadorian Connecticut shade wrapper. It reached stores in September 2025 in 25-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Drew Estate rates it mellow; halfwheel's reviewer found full flavor with strength reaching medium by the end.

cigars.about: A 7 x 38 lancero in Willy Herrera's Connecticut broadleaf blend, released nationally to Drew Diplomat retailers in September 2020. It returned as a limited batch in 2021, in boxes of 15.
cigars.researchNote: This is a single lancero size, first billed as a Tienda Exclusiva. The same blend was the 6 x 52 Herrera Estelí TAA Exclusive in 2016, and a 2016 Houston store exclusive called the H-Town Lancero used this size. No strength rating is published.

cigars.about: A 6 x 52 toro made for member shops of the Tobacconists' Association of America, and the first Herrera Estelí blend to use a Connecticut broadleaf wrapper. It was released in 2016 and again in 2020.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only through TAA member retailers. The 2020 run was the same cigar in new packaging, limited to 800 boxes of 12. Strength is from halfwheel's review, which called it medium to medium-plus.

cigars.about: A 6 x 46 box-pressed corona gorda made for Small Batch Cigar and its parent shop Maxamar Ultimate Cigars in Orange, California. It uses the original Herrera Estelí blend with a darker, higher-priming wrapper, and was released in 2016 and again in 2024.
cigars.researchNote: Exclusive to Small Batch Cigar and Maxamar. The 2016 run was only 1,000 cigars and placed sixth on halfwheel's Top 25 that year. No strength rating is published.

cigars.line: Herrera Estelí Tienda Exclusiva Vintage Cigar Lounge
cigars.about: A 6 x 52 toro blended by Willy Herrera as a store exclusive for Vintage Cigar Lounge in Rhode Island. It launched in April 2021 in boxes of 18.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only at Vintage Cigar Lounge in Charlestown and Westerly, Rhode Island. Tienda Exclusiva releases share packaging but each store gets its own blend. No strength rating is published.

cigars.about: A value-priced bundle cigar from Drew Estate with a sweetened cap on a habano wrapper. It is one of the original four Factory Smokes blends introduced in 2018.
cigars.researchNote: Often sold as Factory Smokes Sweets. Drew Estate rates it mellow with Central American filler; halfwheel says mixed Indonesian filler and Corona Cigar calls it medium. halfwheel's 2018 launch list had the Toro at 6 x 52 and Churchill at 7 x 50, unlike Drew Estate's site.

cigars.about: A green candela-wrapped version of Drew Estate's value-priced Factory Smokes bundle line, added in 2020. It is a web exclusive rather than a shop cigar.
cigars.researchNote: A web exclusive: it launched at Thompson Cigar and Drew Estate's site now points to Cigars International. The wrapper's origin is undisclosed and Drew Estate publishes no strength rating.

cigars.about: An infused ACID Subculture blend that Drew Estate makes only for Corona Cigar Company. It gets an extra year of aging and is described as mild to medium with a light sweetness.
cigars.researchNote: Corona Cigar exclusive. The blend details come only from Corona Cigar, the sole seller; Drew Estate confirms the cigar and its 5 x 54 size but not the blend.

cigars.about: An infused Sumatra-wrapped figurado that Drew Estate makes as an exclusive for Cigars International. Drew Estate lists it in one 6 x 52 size.
cigars.researchNote: Cigars International exclusive, per Drew Estate. Blend details come from one reseller, Cigars Direct, which lists it as a mild to medium torpedo.

cigars.about: An infused Connecticut-wrapped cigar that Drew Estate makes as an exclusive for Thompson Cigar. Drew Estate lists it in one 6 x 54 size.
cigars.researchNote: Thompson Cigar exclusive, per Drew Estate. Binder, filler and strength are not confirmed. The first Kindred Spirit, from 2015, was a 5 1/2 x 50 Cameroon robusto for the 100th anniversary of Thompson.

cigars.about: The maduro version of the infused Kindred Spirit cigar that Drew Estate makes as an exclusive for Thompson Cigar. Drew Estate lists it in one 6 x 54 size.
cigars.researchNote: Thompson Cigar exclusive, per Drew Estate. The type and origin of the maduro wrapper, the binder, the filler and the strength are not confirmed.

cigars.about: An infused Drew Estate blend with a San Andrés maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos, made as a web exclusive for Cigars International. The infusion is described as more subtle than on other ACID cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Drew Estate lists it as a Cigars International web exclusive in multiple sizes. Blend details come from other retailers, not Drew Estate. Mike's Cigars lists it as medium, while Cigar Place calls it medium to full bodied.

cigars.about: A Christmas-themed offshoot of Viaje's Farmer Bill Hatchet, the character from its Thanksgiving Stuffed Turkey story. It is its own blend and is sold in 25-count bundles wrapped in holiday paper.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje has not disclosed the blend, factory or country; it is a different blend from the regular Farmer Bill Hatchet. Halfwheel found it medium, while one retailer lists it as medium-full. Shipped in December 2021 and again in December 2023.

cigars.about: A Thanksgiving-season Viaje release named for founder Andre Farkas, who appears on the band as the helper to Farmer Bill Hatchet. It comes as a single box-pressed 7 x 52.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje keeps the blend, factory and country secret. Halfwheel rated it medium-plus in strength with full body; Cigar Coop called it medium in both. Released in 2019 and again in 2023 with the same blend.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA), the Aganorsa factory in Estelí
cigars.about: A San Andrés-wrapped Viaje made with Aganorsa tobacco in Estelí. It is known for its box: 20 round cigars on top and a hidden compartment of five box-pressed cigars underneath.
cigars.researchNote: Released in 2014 (5 x 52 only), 2018 (5 x 52 and 6 x 50) and 2024. Blend and factory are from 2014 and 2018; Viaje did not confirm the blend or sizes for 2024. Halfwheel found the 2014 medium-full and the 2018 toro closer to medium.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Raíces Cubanas S. de R.L.
cigars.about: A small-batch Viaje named for Imperator Furiosa from the Mad Max films. It debuted in 2016 as a Nicaraguan puro of corojo and criollo tobaccos and came back in 2024 in two new sizes, sold in 51-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Blend, factory and country are from the 2016 release; Viaje did not disclose them for the 2024 Fury and Imperator. The Corojo 99 wrapper detail comes from Cigar Coop; halfwheel says only that it uses corojo and criollo tobaccos.

cigars.about: Viaje's Christmas release, shipped most Decembers since 2009 in gift-wrapped cigars. It was a Nicaraguan criollo-wrapped blend for years and switched to a corojo 99 maduro wrapper in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Blend shown is the 2022 version; earlier years used a Nicaraguan criollo wrapper. Viaje has not said where the 2022 version is made. Halfwheel found it medium, while a retailer lists it as full, and sizes change from year to year.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Barber pole of two wrappers; Brazilian Arapiraca and Ecuadorian Habano on the 2015 edition
cigars.about: The barber pole version of Viaje's Holiday Blend, with two wrapper leaves striped like a candy cane. It first shipped in 2012 and returns some Decembers as a 6 x 54.
cigars.researchNote: The blend changes by year and Viaje has not disclosed recent ones. The 2012 was made at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras and the 2015 at PDR Cigars in the Dominican Republic. Strength varies: halfwheel found the 2015 medium-full to full and the 2018 mild to medium.

cigars.factory: Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A. (Aganorsa Leaf), Estelí
cigars.about: A limited Viaje that started in 2010 as an exclusive for retailers who attended the trade show. The name is a Japanese word for sudden enlightenment, and since 2011 it has worn a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: The 2010 debut was a Nicaraguan puro with an oscuro wrapper. Releases through 2014 were made at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras; the 2023 release was made by Aganorsa Leaf in Estelí. Strength is from a single retailer listing.

cigars.about: Originally founder Andre Farkas's private blend for handing to friends and family, which he compared to his own Cohiba. It reached stores in 2012 and comes in small batches in boxes of 15, soft-pressed with a covered foot.
cigars.researchNote: Viaje keeps the blend, factory and country secret. Each release is usually a single size; the most recent one covered was the Merci in 2022.

cigars.about: A Hawaiian-themed Viaje (piña is Spanish for pineapple) made at Ernesto Perez-Carrillo's factory in the Dominican Republic. It has a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over an Ecuadorian binder and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: First released in 2017 as part of Viaje's White Label Project, then brought back in 2022 with its own pineapple band, limited to 350 boxes of 24 per size. Strength and flavors are from a Cigar Coop review of the 2017 release; the maker says the 2022 run is a little sweeter.

cigars.about: Viaje's nod to late harvest wine: a Nicaraguan puro built mostly from the highest primings, the leaves that stay on the plant longest. It comes with a pigtail cap in crate-style boxes of 35.
cigars.researchNote: Blend is from the 2011 and 2012 releases, which were made at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras. Viaje did not disclose the blend or factory for the 2021 return. Viaje says the line is blended for seasoned smokers.

cigars.about: The stronger sibling of Viaje's Late Harvest, added in 2013. It uses a wrapper from a higher priming than the original, meaning leaf that hung on the stalk longer, for a more intense smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Blend is from the 2013 release, made at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras. Viaje did not disclose the blend or factory for the 2021 return; Cigar Coop lists TABSA in Nicaragua for that run. Strength rating is from Cigar Coop's review of the 2021 release.

cigars.about: The Connecticut shade member of Gurkha's Cellar Reserve family, introduced in 2016 and sold only in perfecto shapes. Gurkha says the blend includes some 21-year-old tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Gurkha lists Dominican and Nicaraguan binder and filler; halfwheel and Neptune list Dominican only. Gurkha calls it a limited edition, halfwheel lists it as regular production. Per halfwheel, a Gurkha rep said only a small part of the filler is 21-year-old tobacco.

cigars.about: The third Cellar Reserve release, a corojo-wrapped Dominican cigar from 2014 built around 18-year-old tobacco. All sizes are perfectos and it ships in a mahogany-finish box.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2014 limited to 1,000 boxes per size, but Gurkha still lists it as a core brand. Gurkha rates it medium; halfwheel's review found it full bodied and medium-full in strength, and Neptune lists it as full. The corojo wrapper's country is not disclosed.

cigars.about: The maduro take on Gurkha's Cellar Reserve, introduced in 2013 with a dark Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper over aged Dominican tobacco. It is sold in the line's perfecto shapes, and Gurkha describes it as sweeter and fuller than the original.
cigars.researchNote: Usually just called Cellar Reserve Limitada by retailers and halfwheel. Gurkha rates it medium to full; Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (T-13 hybrid), Nicaragua, Broadleaf (origin undisclosed)
cigars.about: One of two Revenant blends from 2021, the first cigars Tabacalera El Artista made for Gurkha. It pairs a San Andrés wrapper with a Cameroon binder and El Artista's own T-13 hybrid tobacco in the filler.
cigars.researchNote: Blended by Ram Rodriguez of El Artista. Gurkha lists the robusto as 5 x 52; halfwheel reported 5 x 50 at launch.

cigars.about: The corojo-wrapped half of Gurkha's 2021 Revenant line, made by Tabacalera El Artista in the Dominican Republic. Like the Maduro, it is built on a Cameroon binder.
cigars.researchNote: Blended by Ram Rodriguez of El Artista. Gurkha calls the Dominican filler Corojo 98; one halfwheel report says Criollo 98, and halfwheel adds a broadleaf of undisclosed origin. Gurkha lists the robusto as 5 x 52; halfwheel reported 5 x 50 at launch.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98 ligero and seco), Nicaragua
cigars.about: Gurkha's mild Connecticut-wrapped line, introduced in 2019 and made at Tabacalera Las Lavas in the Dominican Republic. The name is pronounced ray-al.
cigars.researchNote: Gurkha's spec table lists only Criollo 98 ligero and seco in the filler, while its description mentions Honduran fillers; halfwheel and Neptune list Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. Neptune rates it medium.

cigars.filler: USA (Connecticut Broadleaf), Habano seco and ligero (origin undisclosed)
cigars.about: A Connecticut hybrid wrapped Dominican cigar that Gurkha launched in 2022, first as an exclusive for Tobacconists' Association of America shops. It is sold through a limited group of retailers in 10-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Originally made at PDR Cigars; paused in 2024 over a wrapper shortage and returned in 2025 from Tabacalera Palma with the same blend. Gurkha says it is released in limited quantities to select retailers. The lonsdale was first listed as 6 1/2 x 48.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Varies by blend: Connecticut, Habano or Maduro (origins undisclosed)
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan-made collection launched in November 2024 with Volition America and Folds of Honor, offered as Connecticut, Habano and Maduro blends in one toro size. Boxes hold 13 cigars and 13 percent of each sale funds scholarships for families of fallen and disabled service members and first responders.
cigars.researchNote: This is three blends under one name, each a 6 x 54 toro. Gurkha has not disclosed the wrapper origins or the factory. Gurkha gives one strength for the whole collection, "Strong", with no rating per blend, so the Connecticut may smoke lighter.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro follow-up to Gurkha's Colección Especial, made at American Caribbean Cigars. It debuted in 2023 as a Tobacconists' Association of America exclusive and went to all retailers in 2024.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as Nicaraguan Colección Especial. The tobacco varietals are not disclosed. The 2023 TAA release was a single pirámide limited to 1,500 boxes of 10, which halfwheel listed at 6 1/8 x 54.

cigars.about: An Ecuadorian Habano wrapped cigar that Gurkha first sold in 1999 and brought back in 2017 with new packaging. It is made in Nicaragua and Gurkha describes it as an everyday smoke.
cigars.researchNote: In January 2025 Gurkha announced the U.S. line was being renamed Legend 1959, the name used overseas, so boxes may carry either name. The 2017 version was reported with a Dominican olor binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. Halfwheel lists the robusto as 5 x 54.

cigars.about: Made at Tabacalera El Artista to mark 35 years since Kaizad Hansotia bought the Gurkha brand in 1989. It debuted in a red commemorative humidor in late 2023 and moved into regular 10-count boxes in 2024.
cigars.researchNote: Gurkha lists the pointed size as a Pirámide at 6 1/4 x 52; halfwheel lists it as a Torpedo at 6 1/8 x 52. The humidor was limited but the cigars are regular production.

cigars.about: Gurkha's coffee-flavored cigar, one of a flavored trio alongside the cherry Red Head and vanilla White Rascal. It was brought back in 2018 after more than a decade off the market.
cigars.researchNote: This is a flavored (coffee) cigar. Reintroduced in 2018; the original release year is not published. Halfwheel listed the small size as 4 x 34 in tins of five and reported Dominican tobacco in the blend, which differs from Gurkha's current spec.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Nicaraguan cigar with a San Andrés wrapper, launched in 2014 under Gurkha's East India Trading Company label. Gurkha says the blend took twenty revisions to settle.
cigars.researchNote: Gurkha lists the binder and filler only as proprietary; halfwheel says Nicaraguan fillers and Neptune lists both as Nicaraguan. Gurkha rates it medium, Neptune lists it as full. It launched with a 6 x 60 XO that Gurkha no longer lists.

cigars.about: The original Gurkha Heritage from 2015, a rosado-wrapped Nicaraguan-made cigar blended with Gurkha's Juan Lopez at American Caribbean Cigars. It is the lighter partner to the Heritage Maduro.
cigars.researchNote: Most retailers just call this Gurkha Heritage. Gurkha rates it medium; the 2015 launch called it medium to full and Neptune lists it as full. Early reports gave the U.S. filler leaf as Pennsylvania rather than Connecticut broadleaf.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Gurkha Heritage, added in 2016 and made at American Caribbean Cigars in Nicaragua. Gurkha calls it a double maduro because both the San Andrés wrapper and the Brazilian binder are maduro leaf.
cigars.researchNote: Gurkha's strength rating is full, while its own description calls the cigar medium to full bodied. Now sold in 15-count boxes.

cigars.about: A value-priced Dominican cigar that Gurkha relaunched in 2020 under the name of an old Cuban brand. It wears an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper and sits at the mild end of the Gurkha range.
cigars.researchNote: Castle Hall was previously a private label Gurkha made for Thompson Cigar. The factory has not been disclosed. Neptune sells a Castle Hall Habano with a different blend, so check the band before quoting this one.

cigars.about: The Nicaraguan extension of Gurkha's value-priced Castle Hall line, added in 2020 and made at American Caribbean Cigars. It uses an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over all Nicaraguan tobacco and is the stronger of the two Castle Hall blends.
cigars.researchNote: Also written Castle Hall Nicaragua. It launched with a 6 x 60 Magnum as well, which Gurkha no longer lists.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro (Maduro version); Connecticut Shade (Natural version)
cigars.about: Gurkha's rum-infused cigar, made with tobacco infused with seven-year-aged Ron Abuelo rum and first shipped in 2014. It comes in Maduro and Natural versions.
cigars.researchNote: This is a rum-infused cigar. Gurkha's spec table says Dominican binder, filler and origin, but its own description, halfwheel and Neptune say Nicaraguan tobacco made in Nicaragua, so the country is in doubt. The maduro wrapper's country is not disclosed.

cigars.about: Gurkha's bourbon-infused cigar, launched in 2016 with Kentucky distillery Hartfield & Company. It sits alongside the rum-infused Private Select and cognac-infused Grand Reserve.
cigars.researchNote: This is a bourbon-infused cigar. Gurkha's specs list only Natural (Connecticut Shade) sizes, but it launched as a maduro Churchill (7 x 47) and a natural Toro (6 1/2 x 52). Halfwheel listed Nicaraguan binder and filler in 2017; Gurkha now says Dominican.

cigars.about: A military-themed Dominican cigar from 2016 that replaced Gurkha's Spec Ops No. 1. It comes in a single 7 1/2 x 52 size with a dark Dominican maduro wrapper over an Indonesian binder.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel lists the filler as Dominican and Nicaraguan; Gurkha lists Dominican only. It launched in a 20-count hard travel case with a combat knife and challenge coin. The factory is not published.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan-made Gurkha with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is a 2022 relaunch of an older limited release, with the blend reworked by Damian Tapanes of American Caribbean Cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Gurkha lists strength as Full but describes it as medium to full bodied. The original Pure Evil was a limited release around 2006; this regular-production version came back in 2022. Not the same cigar as Gurkha Evil, which has a Brazilian maduro wrapper.

cigars.about: The third blend in Gurkha's Ghost family, wrapped in Ecuadorian-grown Connecticut seed leaf and made for Gurkha by PDR Cigars in the Dominican Republic. It debuted at the TPE show in 2023.
cigars.researchNote: Strength varies by source: Gurkha says Medium, halfwheel's review found it mild in strength with medium body, and Neptune lists it as Full.

cigars.about: An extension of Gurkha's Ghost line that swaps the original Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper for Ecuadorian Habano. It launched in 2018 and is made in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Binder is unclear: Gurkha's spec list says Mexican, its own description says Criollo 98, and the 2018 launch announcement said Criollo 97. Gurkha's site shows all three sizes as 6x54, which looks like a typo; the sizes here are from halfwheel and Neptune.

cigars.about: A cognac-infused Gurkha first released in 1996 and long marketed as one of the most expensive cigars in the world. It has an aged Connecticut maduro wrapper over aged Dominican binder and filler and comes in one Churchill size.
cigars.researchNote: This is an infused cigar: Gurkha says the tobacco is aged with a bottle of cognac, which halfwheel identifies as Louis XIII. Gurkha says only 75 boxes are made a year. Gurkha rates it mild to medium, while Neptune calls it full-bodied.

cigars.about: An ultra-expensive limited Gurkha announced in late 2014, sold in mahogany humidors of 10 individually coffined cigars. Gurkha describes it only as a maduro wrapper over Dominican binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is secret beyond a maduro wrapper and Dominican binder and filler, and Gurkha would not name the factory. It was announced in November 2014 at $2,000 a cigar in 100 humidors of 10 and shown at the July 2015 trade show. Gurkha's site now quotes $6,000 a cigar.

cigars.about: A large Dominican-made Gurkha maduro with a Cameroon binder and Dominican filler, sold in frosted glass tubes in a velvet-covered box. It comes in one size.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the wrapper: Gurkha lists Ecuadorian maduro, while Neptune and Mike's Cigars describe an aged Connecticut Broadleaf. Gurkha rates it Medium; Neptune says Full and Mike's says medium to full. Mike's also lists it as 7 x 52 and made in Honduras.

cigars.about: The lighter-wrapped of Gurkha's two high-priced Triad cigars, built on aged tobaccos under an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. Gurkha says only 300 boxes were made.
cigars.researchNote: Gurkha lists the size as 7.25 x 52; a 2011 halfwheel review gave both Triad cigars as 7 x 52. Triad Platinum is a separate maduro blend.

cigars.about: The maduro member of Gurkha's Triad pair, with an aged Connecticut maduro wrapper, Cameroon binder and Dominican filler. It was priced around $100 a cigar and limited to 300 boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Factory and 2011 release date come from halfwheel's 2011 review, which listed the size as 7 x 52 rather than Gurkha's 7.25 x 52 and found the strength medium. Gurkha calls the wrapper Connecticut Maduro; halfwheel calls it Connecticut Broadleaf. Triad Natural is a separate blend.

cigars.about: A cognac-infused Gurkha made in the Dominican Republic. Gurkha describes it as a triple-infused step up from its Grand Reserve cognac cigar.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is secret: Gurkha lists wrapper, binder and filler as proprietary. This is an infused cigar. Neptune describes it as a Connecticut maduro wrapper over Dominican binder and filler, infused with Louis XIII cognac.

cigars.about: A 2023 release marking 25 years of the Gurkha Beauty, made at Tabacalera Las Lavas in the Dominican Republic. It trades the original Beauty's Connecticut wrapper for Ecuadorian Corojo and comes in frosted tubes, 25 to a box.
cigars.researchNote: A different blend from the regular Beauty, which has a Connecticut wrapper. Gurkha called it regular production, but the first run was 1,000 boxes. It comes in one size with no vitola name.

cigars.about: A glass-tubed Gurkha made at Tabacalera El Artista that was sold mainly outside the United States. It came to U.S. stores in a single toro size in April 2025, after a brief appearance in a late 2023 sampler.
cigars.researchNote: Blend is from Gurkha's 2025 announcement as reported by halfwheel; Gurkha's own web page shows the blend, sizes and strength of its Cellar Reserve 15 Year instead, which looks like a copying error. The first U.S. run was 2,000 boxes of 20. Neptune calls it medium strength.

cigars.about: Gurkha's limited Lunar New Year series for 2024. It began with a figurado from Tabacalera El Artista in December 2023, followed by four different blends made by AJ Fernandez, E.P. Carrillo, Oliva and Oscar Valladares.
cigars.researchNote: Five different cigars, not one blend. Wrappers: El Artista undisclosed (DR), AJ Fernandez Ecuador Habano (Nicaragua), E.P. Carrillo San Andrés (DR), Oliva San Andrés per halfwheel but Sumatra per Neptune (Nicaragua), Oscar Valladares Jamastran Corojo (Honduran puro). The four collaborations were 2,000 boxes of 10 each.

cigars.about: Gurkha's limited Lunar New Year release for 2025, made up of three different cigars from Casa Carrillo, Oliva and Oscar Valladares. Each version was limited to 750 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Three different cigars, not one blend. Casa Carrillo (DR): Ecuadorian Corojo wrapper, Ecuadorian Sumatra binder, Dominican, Mexican and Nicaraguan filler; Oliva (Nicaragua): San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco; Oscar Valladares (Honduras): Habano wrapper of undisclosed origin over Honduran tobacco.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro introduced in 2026 and made at Nicaragua American Cigars S.A. in Esteli. Some of the filler tobacco was aged in used bourbon barrels before rolling.
cigars.researchNote: Only some filler leaf was barrel aged; the finished cigars are not infused. Gurkha has not published a strength: Neptune lists it as medium and Mike's Cigars as medium to full. The wrapper variety is not named.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Condega viso, Esteli ligero, Ometepe seco)
cigars.about: A 2026 limited edition honoring Gurkha sales vice president Juan Lopez's 30 years in the cigar business. It is made in Nicaragua with an Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro wrapper over all-Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,000 boxes of 10 per size; the factory is undisclosed. Retailers disagree on strength: Neptune says medium, Mike's Cigars says full. Neptune also lists the wrapper as Nicaraguan, against halfwheel's Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro.

cigars.about: A big ring gauge line Gurkha began shipping in February 2025, made in Nicaragua with a Habano wrapper. It was created after customers asked for the return of the larger ring gauges Gurkha used to offer.
cigars.researchNote: Gurkha did not disclose the wrapper's origin, the binder, the filler or the factory. Neptune and Mike's Cigars list an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. The sizes have no names, only dimensions.

cigars.about: One of two blends in Gurkha's 2024 collaboration with boxer Mike Tyson's Tyson 2.0 brand, made at Tabacalera El Artista in the Dominican Republic. This one has an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper and comes in a gold box.
cigars.researchNote: The first run was limited to 2,000 boxes per size, with Gurkha saying it expected the line to become regular production. Gurkha describes it as medium body with full flavor.

cigars.about: The maduro half of Gurkha's 2024 collaboration with boxer Mike Tyson's Tyson 2.0 brand, made at Tabacalera El Artista in the Dominican Republic. It has a Mexican San Andrés wrapper and comes in a black box.
cigars.researchNote: The first run was limited to 2,000 boxes per size, with Gurkha saying it expected the line to become regular production. Gurkha did not say where the filler tobaccos come from; Neptune lists the broadleaf as USA grown.

cigars.about: A Honduran puro made for Gurkha by Oscar Valladares as an exclusive for Tobacconists' Association of America member shops. It is a single box-pressed torpedo limited to 1,000 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only through TAA member retailers. It was announced in October 2024 as a TAA 2024 exclusive and shipped in January 2025. The maduro wrapper description comes from Neptune; halfwheel says only that the blend is all Honduran.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Gurkha's Grand Reserve, its long-running cognac-infused cigar sold in wax-sealed glass tubes. It is made in the Dominican Republic with Dominican binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: This is an infused cigar and the maduro wrapper option of the Grand Reserve line. Corona Cigar and Mike's Cigars rate it mild to medium while Neptune says medium, and only Neptune names the wrapper as Connecticut Broadleaf. Mike's lists it as made in Honduras and the Churchill as 7.25 inches.

cigars.about: A stronger take on Drew Estate's coffee-infused Tabak Especial, built on the maduro blend with extra ligero in the filler. It comes in one short robusto size.
cigars.researchNote: Coffee infused. Famous lists a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper; Neptune's listing shows Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade but tags the cigar Maduro. Both rate it Medium. Drew Estate lists it as a web exclusive.

cigars.line: Tabak Especial Limited Café con Leche
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade with Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro foot and cap
cigars.about: A coffee-infused Tabak Especial belicoso with a two-tone wrapper: light Connecticut shade in the middle and dark broadleaf at the foot and cap. It is sold in one size.
cigars.researchNote: Coffee infused. Drew Estate and Neptune give the size as 5 1/2 x 54; Famous lists 5 1/4 x 54. The two-wrapper detail comes from Famous. Drew Estate lists it as a web exclusive.

cigars.about: A coffee-infused Tabak Especial cigar that Drew Estate makes as an exclusive for Thompson Cigar. Drew Estate lists it among its web exclusives in one size.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only through Thompson Cigar. Drew Estate lists the size as 5.7 x 52 and publishes no wrapper, blend or strength for it.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Drew Estate's value-priced, coffee-infused Isla del Sol line, with a sweetened tip. It was added in 2018 alongside the original Sumatra-wrapped cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Drew Estate's site calls the wrapper a Mexican maduro; halfwheel and Famous list it as Nicaraguan and Neptune as undisclosed. Drew Estate rates it Mellow, while Famous and Neptune say Medium. Coffee infused with a sweet tip.

cigars.about: The fourth cigar in Drew Estate's Deadwood family of sweet-tipped aromatic cigars, launched in 2020 as a torpedo. Drew Estate calls it the spiciest blend in the series.
cigars.researchNote: Blend is secret beyond a maduro wrapper and aromatic dark air-cured fillers. Drew Estate rates it Full; halfwheel's review found the strength medium to medium-full. Sweetened cap.

cigars.line: Deadwood The Girl With No Name
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andres (Lonsdale; other sizes differ)
cigars.about: A Deadwood sub-brand that Drew Estate began in 2022 and uses mostly for sizes made for individual large retailers. The 7 x 44 Lonsdale, added in 2024, is the one size offered to all stores.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are secret. The wrapper changes by size: San Andres on the Lonsdale, maduro on the Cigars International Toro, Sumatra on the Famous Robusto Extra and Connecticut Shade on JR's 5 x 50 Robusto. Drew Estate says body varies by size.

cigars.about: A Deadwood line from 2025 built around Dominican filler tobacco from Jose Mendez & Co., under a Connecticut shade wrapper with a sweetened cap. It was Drew Estate's first blend centered on Dominican tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Despite the name it is rolled in Nicaragua; the Dominican part is the filler. It has a sweetened cap. Drew Estate has said production will move to its new Dominican factory once that opens.

cigars.about: The darker, broadleaf-wrapped companion to Deadwood Dominicana, released in spring 2026. It keeps the Dominican-leaning filler and the sweetened cap.
cigars.researchNote: Rolled in Nicaragua despite the name. Drew Estate describes the filler only as a Dominican-forward blend. It has a sweetened cap.

cigars.line: Deadwood Sweet Jane Día de los Muertos
cigars.about: A limited box-pressed toro version of Deadwood Sweet Jane with Day of the Dead packaging. It first appeared in 2019 and returned in 2024 and 2025.
cigars.researchNote: Blend is secret beyond a maduro wrapper; it is infused with a very sweet cap. Strength and body are from halfwheel's 2024 review, which found strength mild rising to medium; Drew Estate's release calls it full-bodied. The 2025 cigar is the same as 2024 in new packaging.

cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A sweet-tipped version of Drew Estate's Kentucky Fire Cured, which blends fire-cured Kentucky tobacco with Nicaraguan filler for a smoky, campfire character. It launched in 2018.
cigars.researchNote: Drew Estate rates it Mellow; Neptune and Famous rate it Medium. The Joya de Nicaragua factory is as reported at the 2018 launch. It has a sweetened tip.

cigars.about: A non-infused cigar blended by Willy Herrera at Drew Estate and made with the Van Winkle bourbon family. It debuted in 2017 and, unlike the other Pappy cigars, uses no fire-cured tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Since 2020 it has been sold only through Pappy & Company, not regular cigar shops. Full is Drew Estate's body rating; halfwheel's review found the strength mild to mild-medium. The 2017 release had seven sizes; Drew Estate's site now lists four.

cigars.about: A novelty egg-shaped cigar from Drew Estate, tapered at both ends and swelling to more than a 100 ring gauge in the middle. This is the Connecticut-wrapped version, sold one to a box.
cigars.researchNote: Drew Estate publishes no length, binder, filler or strength rating for The Egg, only that it tops 100 ring gauge at the center. It calls this version mellow. The shape first appeared years ago under its Natural line.

cigars.about: A novelty egg-shaped cigar from Drew Estate, tapered at both ends and swelling to more than a 100 ring gauge in the middle. This is the maduro-wrapped version, sold one to a box.
cigars.researchNote: Drew Estate publishes no length, binder, filler or strength rating for The Egg, only that it tops 100 ring gauge at the center. It calls this version dark and bold. The shape first appeared years ago under its Natural line.

cigars.about: One of Drew Estate's first traditional, non-infused cigars, introduced in 2006 and later dropped. It came back in late 2023 as a budget-priced Connecticut shade blend sold through online retailers.
cigars.researchNote: Drew Estate calls it mellow with Nicaraguan binder and filler; Neptune and Famous list a Habano binder and rate it Medium. The current version is sold only through online retailers. Habano and Maduro versions are separate blends.

cigars.about: A Habano-wrapped version of Drew Estate's budget Chateau Real line, released in August 2024. It is made as an exclusive for Cigars International.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only through Cigars International. Drew Estate does not say where the Habano wrapper is grown and publishes no strength rating.

cigars.about: One of Drew Estate's early infused lines, first released in 2002 and made in Nicaragua. It uses spiced aromatic tobacco for a sweet, clove-like smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers disagree on the wrapper: Neptune lists Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade with a Nicaraguan binder, Famous lists it as undisclosed. Famous gives the Spice torpedo as 5 x 54, Neptune and Corona as 6 x 54. Still sold by retailers but no longer shown on Drew Estate's own site.

cigars.about: A cherry, cocoa and coffee infused cigar in the Java by Drew Estate line, added in 2017. Drew Estate makes it in Esteli for Rocky Patel, which owns and distributes the brand.
cigars.researchNote: Java is a Rocky Patel brand made by Drew Estate, so shops may shelve it under either name. The blend is not disclosed: Famous lists a Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper and Neptune lists Corojo maduro. Most sizes are box-pressed and the cap is sweetened.

cigars.about: The third version of Caldwell's Blind Man's Bluff, introduced in 2021. It is a Nicaraguan puro with a Habano wrapper and a different blend from the original and Connecticut versions.
cigars.researchNote: All Nicaraguan tobacco, but halfwheel and Neptune say it is rolled at STG's Danli factory in Honduras; Smokingpipes lists Nicaragua as the country. Caldwell rates it 5 of 5 for potency while Neptune calls it medium. Caldwell's site currently shows only the Magnum.

cigars.line: Long Live the King Mad MoFo
cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, Nicaragua, USA (Pennsylvania); includes Corojo 98, Habano and Pennsylvania double ligero
cigars.about: The maduro take on Caldwell's Long Live the King, with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over an Indonesian binder and fillers that include Corojo 98 and Pennsylvania double ligero. It first shipped in 2018 under the name LLTK MAD MF.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2018 as a 75,000-cigar limited run called LLTK MAD MF and is now in Caldwell's regular catalog. Caldwell rates it 4 of 5 for potency. A separate 5 x 50 Mad MoFo robusto with a Dominican binder and filler was made in 2021 for Cigars for Warriors.

cigars.line: Long Live the King Mad MoFo Habano
cigars.about: A Habano-wrapped version of the Mad MoFo that Caldwell introduced at the 2025 PCA show. The company describes it as its most pepper-forward blend and one of its strongest cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Caldwell calls it the boldest cigar in its lineup and one of its strongest, yet its potency meter and Smokingpipes both show only 3 of 5. Caldwell and halfwheel give no wrapper origin; Smokingpipes lists it as Dominican.

cigars.about: Caldwell's companion line to Long Live the King, built around a Cameroon wrapper over a Sumatran binder with Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers. It is rolled at the Ventura family's El Maestro factory in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Shown at the 2022 PCA trade show but did not reach stores until January 2023. The box-pressed Ace of Hearts began as a limited size and became regular production in late 2023.

cigars.about: A separate maduro blend in the Long Live the Queen family, with a Mexican San Andres wrapper, Indonesian binder and Dominican and American fillers. It shipped in July 2024 as the first new Caldwell release under Laudisi ownership.
cigars.researchNote: Not the original Queen with a darker wrapper: the whole blend is different. Caldwell calls it medium-to-full; Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.line: The King Is Dead Escape Plan
cigars.about: A box-pressed version of Caldwell's The King Is Dead, first released in 2022 and reworked in 2025. The current version uses the same Dominican tobaccos as the regular line with different primings and fermentation.
cigars.researchNote: Two versions exist. The 2022 original used fillers from the Dominican Republic, Nicaragua and Peru and was capped at 300 boxes per size; the 2025 version is all Dominican. Halfwheel and Smokingpipes call it a limited release, though Caldwell lists it with its regular lines.

cigars.about: A 2026 Crafted & Curated small-batch release that pays homage to Caldwell's discontinued Savages line. It comes in one 6 x 54 size and was limited to 400 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Malpensante loosely translates to cynic. It is not the original Savages blend, which stopped production after the 2022 fire at Tabacalera William Ventura. Limited to 400 boxes of 10.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Arapiraca and Connecticut hybrid Oscuro (called Aracon Oscuro)
cigars.about: A 2026 Crafted & Curated release made as a tribute to Caldwell's discontinued The Last Tsar. It is a single 6 x 54 size limited to 220 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: El Olvidado means the forgotten one. It is an homage to The Last Tsar, not the same blend, and the wrapper's country of origin is not disclosed. Limited to 220 boxes of 10.

cigars.line: Long Live the Queen Forbidden Fruit Claro
cigars.about: The lighter of two Long Live the Queen Forbidden Fruit cigars released in March 2026 in Caldwell's Crafted & Curated series. It pairs a San Andres Rosado wrapper with an all-Dominican binder and filler in a single 6 x 60 size.
cigars.researchNote: A new blend, not the regular Long Live the Queen. Limited to 400 boxes of 10. Smokingpipes rates it 3 of 5 and Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.line: Long Live the Queen Forbidden Fruit Oscuro
cigars.about: The darker of two Long Live the Queen Forbidden Fruit cigars released in March 2026 in Caldwell's Crafted & Curated series. It uses a San Andres Oscuro wrapper over a Sumatra binder with Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers in a single 6 x 60 size.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is disputed: Smokingpipes rates it 4 of 5 and Neptune lists full, but halfwheel's review found it mild in strength with a medium body. A new blend, not the regular Queen Maduro. Limited to 400 boxes of 10.

cigars.about: A 2025 Crafted & Curated release based on Caldwell's discontinued Savages line, made with specially aged Dominican and Sumatra tobaccos. It is a single box-pressed 6 x 54 toro limited to 200 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Mal caida roughly translates to misfit. It is based on the original Savages but is not the same blend, and Caldwell keeps most of it undisclosed. Limited to 200 boxes of 10 and sold out.

cigars.about: A Crafted & Curated lancero from late 2022 with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. It was limited to 750 boxes of 20 and was originally intended as a Lost & Found release.
cigars.researchNote: Caldwell's site now confirms only the Connecticut Desflorada wrapper and calls the rest undisclosed; the binder and filler here come from halfwheel's review. Strength and body are from that review. Limited to 750 boxes of 20 and sold out.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Hybrid Connecticut and Arapiraca Maduro (origin undisclosed)
cigars.about: A 2022 Crafted & Curated release that reworks The Last Tsar with a different priming and fermentation on the wrapper and binder. It was limited to 500 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are undisclosed. Caldwell describes it as creamier, sweeter and smoother than The Last Tsar. Limited to 500 boxes of 10 and sold out.

cigars.about: A 2022 Crafted & Curated culebra: three lanceros braided together, rolled at William Ventura's El Maestro factory. It is its own blend rather than a variation on an existing Caldwell line.
cigars.researchNote: Each culebra is three 7 x 38 lanceros twisted together, meant to be separated and smoked individually. Limited to 202 boxes of 10 culebras and sold out.

cigars.about: A 2022 Crafted & Curated release that takes the Long Live the King blend and swaps its Dominican Corojo wrapper for a Nicaraguan Habano leaf, with one filler change. It was limited to 300 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: A Long Live the King variant: Nicaraguan Habano wrapper, and one Corojo filler replaced by Dominican aromatico. Limited to 300 boxes of 10. It is not shown on Caldwell's current Crafted & Curated page.

cigars.about: A 2023 limited edition in the Long Live the King family, made entirely of Dominican tobacco at Chico Rivas' Manufactura Rivas factory. Caldwell turned to that factory after the 2022 fire at Tabacalera William Ventura.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is disputed: halfwheel's review found medium body with strength just under medium and Neptune lists it as medium, while Smokingpipes rates it 5 of 5 and full-bodied. Limited to 500 boxes of 20 per size.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Honduran Habano Maduro (Habano version) or Honduran Maduro Oscuro (Oscuro version)
cigars.about: A Honduran puro first released on November 7, 2022 for Robert Caldwell's 40th birthday and brought back in 2023 in Habano and Oscuro versions. It is rolled at Davidoff's Camacho factory in Honduras, unlike the Dominican Long Live the King.
cigars.researchNote: The 2023 release came in two blends: Habano (225 boxes of 10) and Oscuro with added ligero (325 boxes of 10), both aged about three years. The tasting notes are from halfwheel's Oscuro review. The 6 x 54 size has a tapered shape.

cigars.about: A third Long Live the Queen blend, made for Tinder Box International stores and released in November 2025. It uses a San Andres Rosado wrapper in a single 6 x 50 toro.
cigars.researchNote: Exclusive to Tinder Box stores; no production cap was announced. The binder and filler are largely undisclosed, though the filler includes broadleaf and Dominican San Vicente.

cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped spin-off of Caldwell's Yellow Cake, released in September 2026. It comes in one 5 x 50 size sold in five-packs and was limited to 12,000 cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Caldwell has not disclosed the binder, filler or factory. Smokingpipes lists it as made in the Dominican Republic, but the company declined to confirm the country to halfwheel. Strength is Smokingpipes' 2 of 5 rating.

cigars.about: The maduro-wrapped version of Caldwell's Yellow Cake, added in 2025 when the former event-only cigar returned to stores. It is a small cigar sold in paper five-packs in two sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The blend and factory are not disclosed. It ships in yearly batches (2025 and 2026); halfwheel has called it both regular production and a limited edition line. Smokingpipes rates strength 2 of 5, while halfwheel's review found it medium.

cigars.about: A limited cigar marking ten years of Caldwell Cigar Co., made at Tabacalera William Ventura with a San Andrés wrapper aged about three and a half years. Each cigar comes in its own coffin.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 200 boxes of 10 at $50 a cigar. Robert Caldwell said he chose a well-aged, fuller-bodied wrapper instead of his usual mild to medium style. No maker strength rating is published; Smokingpipes, which shares an owner with Caldwell, rates it 3 of 5.

cigars.line: Blind Man's Bluff This Is Trouble
cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (corojo, double ligero), Nicaragua (Estelí habano)
cigars.about: A limited edition Blind Man's Bluff robusto from Caldwell with a San Andrés wrapper and a blend unrelated to the regular Blind Man's Bluff. It is made in the Dominican Republic at Tabacalera William Ventura.
cigars.researchNote: 2021 run was 1,000 boxes of 20. Only 200 boxes shipped in 2022 because a factory fire destroyed the rest. Strength and body are from the halfwheel review, which had strength finishing just over medium.

cigars.about: A limited Blind Man's Bluff toro from Caldwell sold only in 100-count boxes. It was rolled in 2022 at Tabacalera William Ventura in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: First release was 160 boxes of 100 in 2023, with all-Dominican binder and filler unlike the regular Blind Man's Bluff. Later Chico Gold and Chico White versions were made at Manufactura Rivas after the Ventura factory fire. Strength is from the maker's 3 of 5 potency rating.

cigars.about: A limited Caldwell cigar rolled in 2016 and held until 2022. It shares the Anastasia name but is a different blend from the original Anastasia and was made at a different factory.
cigars.researchNote: Caldwell does not disclose the factory or country, only that it was not Tabacalera La Alianza, which made the original Anastasia. Limited to 6,000 boxes of 20. Strength and body are from the halfwheel review.

cigars.about: A Lost & Found lancero that reissues The Cookie, a blend first made for Privada Cigar Club. It was the first release after Lost & Found switched in 2022 from repackaging found cigars to commissioning and aging its own.
cigars.researchNote: The factory is an undisclosed Dominican one. Strength is from the maker's 3 of 5 potency rating. The first 2022 run was 750 bundles of 20, and it now comes in boxes of 20.

cigars.about: A short Lost & Found robusto that reissues The Half Cookie, a blend first sold through Privada Cigar Club. It uses the same tobaccos as 15 Minutes of Fame in a shorter, thicker size.
cigars.researchNote: The factory is not disclosed. Strength is from the maker's 3 of 5 potency rating.

cigars.about: One of the original Lost & Found blends, a Dominican puro built on aged Corojo tobacco. It is now a regular Lost & Found line sold in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it an all-Dominican puro built on aged Corojo but lists the wrapper as undisclosed; halfwheel's 2022 coverage listed a Dominican Negrito wrapper. An early found-cigar release that became a regular line in 2022. Strength is from the maker's 4 of 5 potency rating.

cigars.about: One of the original Lost & Found blends, remade since 2022 as a regular line with an Ecuadorian-grown Arapiraca wrapper over Dominican tobacco. It is known for a sweet, creamy start and a peppery finish.
cigars.researchNote: The blend first appeared in January 2014, when the project was called Impromptu, and became regular production in 2022. The factory is not disclosed. Strength is from the maker's 3 of 5 potency rating.

cigars.about: Lost & Found's annual charity robusto, sold in paper-wrapped bundles of 10. Part of each sale goes to Project Unleashed, a Miami program that gives free veterinary care to pets of families in need.
cigars.researchNote: Lost & Found's GAF charity program began in 2020; this robusto came out in 2025 (about 500 bundles) and again in 2026 (600 bundles). The factory and the wrapper and binder origins are undisclosed, though the maker's page lists the binder as Indonesia. Strength is from the maker's 3 of 5 potency rating.

cigars.about: A one-time Lost & Found release that revisits the earlier Backdoor Bambi with a Corojo wrapper. It was sold in packs of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Binder, filler, factory and country are undisclosed. The maker gives no strength rating; Smokingpipes, which shares an owner with the brand, rates it 3 of 5. The maker lists it as sold out.

cigars.about: A one-time Lost & Found release that revisits the earlier Backdoor Bambi with a San Andrés wrapper. It was sold in packs of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Binder, filler, factory and country are undisclosed. The maker gives no strength rating; Smokingpipes, which shares an owner with the brand, rates it 3 of 5. The maker lists it as sold out.

cigars.about: The last entry in Lost & Found's Bambi series, a one-time release with a Negrito wrapper made as a tribute to the original Backdoor Bambi. It was sold in packs of 10.
cigars.researchNote: The origin of the Negrito wrapper, the binder, filler, factory and country are all undisclosed. The maker gives no strength rating; Smokingpipes, which shares an owner with the brand, rates it 3 of 5. The maker lists it as sold out.

cigars.about: A limited Lost & Found robusto with an undisclosed blend, released around Halloween 2023 in bundles with artwork inspired by 1980s Italian cannibal horror films.
cigars.researchNote: The blend, factory and country are fully undisclosed. Strength is from the maker's 3 of 5 potency rating. The maker lists it as a sold-out past brand.

cigars.about: A Lost & Found blend commissioned from Oliva in Nicaragua, with a dark Pennsylvania Broadleaf wrapper over Estelí habano tobacco. It came out in 2023 in boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel calls this 2023 release Foreverfresh Dark Broadleaf; 350 boxes of 20 were made per size. The Forever Fresh name was first used in 2016 on a different found cigar. Strength is from the maker's 4 of 5 potency rating, and the maker calls the 4 x 48 a Shorty.

cigars.about: A limited Lost & Found robusto with an undisclosed blend, released around Halloween 2023 in five-count bundles with artwork inspired by 1980s horror films.
cigars.researchNote: The blend, factory and country are fully undisclosed. Strength is from the maker's 3 of 5 potency rating. The maker lists it as a sold-out past brand.

cigars.about: An aged Lost & Found blend made as a collaboration between Robert Caldwell and Room101 founder Matt Booth. It has a San Andrés maduro wrapper over Dominican and Nicaraguan tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: The factory is not disclosed. Strength is from the maker's 3 of 5 potency rating, and the maker calls it medium-bodied. The maker lists it as a sold-out past brand.

cigars.about: A short, thick box-pressed Lost & Found cigar that Robert Caldwell built for himself as a big-cigar smoke in a travel-friendly size. It is made at Tabacalera William Ventura in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: A box-pressed 4 1/4 x 54. Initial production was 150 boxes of 20. No maker strength rating is published; Smokingpipes, which shares an owner with the brand, rates it 3 of 5.

cigars.line: Lost & Found Late to the Party
cigars.about: A limited Lost & Found robusto extra blended by Robert Caldwell before Laudisi bought the company in 2024. It was sold in bundles of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 180 bundles of 10. The wrapper's country of origin is not published. No strength rating is published.

cigars.line: Lost & Found Don't Sit on the Furniture
cigars.about: A limited Lost & Found toro with a San Andrés wrapper, one of the first cigars the brand released after Laudisi bought it in 2024. It was sold in bundles of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 200 bundles of 10. The origins of the habano aromatico binder and the corojo and habano fillers are undisclosed. Strength and body are from the halfwheel review.

cigars.about: A limited Lost & Found robusto with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper, one of the first cigars the brand released after Laudisi bought it in 2024. It was sold in bundles of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 200 bundles of 10. No strength rating is published.

cigars.about: A full-bodied Connecticut Broadleaf maduro blended by Nish Patel, Rocky's brother, as the follow-up to his Xen line. It is rolled at Rocky Patel's TaviCusa factory in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's description and Neptune call it full-bodied, though the maker's site filter files it under medium. It uses a double binder, one Mexican San Andrés leaf and one Connecticut leaf.

cigars.about: The official cigar of the Cigar Smoking World Championship, a slow-smoking contest, made by Rocky Patel since 2020 when it took over from Macanudo. It is a San Andrés wrapped blend rolled in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: Often shortened to CSWC. The Mareva is the size actually smoked in competition. The maker's page gives no blend or strength; Medium comes from Neptune.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andrés, aged four years in tercios
cigars.about: Rocky Patel's $100 cigar, a box-pressed San Andrés toro sold in individual tubes, ten to a humidor-style box. Most of the filler comes from the 2014 crop and only two pairs of rollers made it.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's exact word for strength is medium-plus; Neptune lists Medium. Limited to 5,000 boxes of 10 (50,000 cigars). Halfwheel's review describes the Nicaraguan binder as a dual binder.

cigars.about: A medium-bodied Honduran cigar with a Honduran Corojo wrapper, made for Rocky Patel at Plasencia's El Paraiso factory. It is known for a Paraguayan tobacco in the filler, a first for the brand.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the filler as Honduras and Paraguay. Halfwheel reports the Paraguayan leaf is Paraguay seed grown in Honduras by the Plasencias, and that Nicaraguan Jalapa leaf is also in the filler.

cigars.about: A Honduran puro toro that Rocky Patel entered in the 2011 Humo Jaguar festival in Honduras, where the company says it took top honors. It is sold in small batches in chests of 100 cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Released in 2011 (500 chests) and again in 2013 (1,000 chests). Miami Cigar & Co. also claimed the festival-winning blend with its Humo Jaguar cigar. The wrapper seed type is not published; Neptune calls it a maduro.

cigars.about: A box-pressed cigar made for Rocky Patel's 50th birthday in 2011, using tobaccos aged more than eight years under an Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro wrapper. It was ranked number 8 on Cigar Aficionado's Top 25 of 2012.
cigars.researchNote: Originally three sizes (Robusto, Toro, Torpedo); brought back in 2017 as the Toro only, in small batches. The maker says medium to full while Neptune lists Medium. It uses two binders whose details the maker keeps secret.

cigars.about: Made to mark Rocky Patel's 55th birthday, this line comes only in 55 ring gauge with both ends tapered. It is rolled at the TaviCusa factory in Estelí and became a regular production cigar.
cigars.researchNote: The maker and Neptune list a Costa Rican binder; halfwheel's review listed Ecuadorian Habano. The maker says Medium while Neptune lists Full. The wrapper seed type is not published.

cigars.about: A box-pressed, gold-foil-wrapped line that was Rocky Patel's one new regular production release for 2024. It pairs an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper with a Connecticut Shade and Broadleaf double binder over aged Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's description says Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, but its own spec box says Sumatra; halfwheel and Neptune both list Ecuadorian Habano. The maker says Medium-Full while Neptune lists Medium.

cigars.line: It's a Boy / It's a Girl
cigars.about: Rocky Patel's birth announcement cigars, a mild Toro sold in separate It's a Boy and It's a Girl versions for handing out when a baby arrives.
cigars.researchNote: These are two separately banded cigars listed as two lines on the maker's site. The maker gives only the size, mild strength and Nicaraguan origin; the wrapper, binder and filler come from Neptune alone.

cigars.about: A single-size toro made with former Baltimore Ravens linebacker Ray Lewis, who wore number 52. Lewis met Rocky Patel at the Burn lounge in 2013 and the cigar reached stores in 2015.
cigars.researchNote: First shown in 2013, put on hold, then launched in fall 2015 with a changed blend. The maker's page gives only the size; the blend comes from halfwheel's launch report and Neptune.

cigars.about: Rocky Patel's 2026 box-pressed release, following Emerald in a gemstone theme. It is a medium San Andrés blend built around aged tobacco and a lingering sweetness modeled on older Cuban cigars.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the binder as a trade secret. Halfwheel reports two binders (Honduran Jamastran and Nicaraguan Estelí) and all-Nicaraguan filler, while the maker says Nicaraguan and Honduran filler. Neptune lists the origin as Honduras; the maker and halfwheel say Nicaragua.

cigars.about: A medium-bodied, box-pressed blend of small-batch tobaccos that Rocky Patel sells only through select brick-and-mortar tobacconists. Cigar & Spirits named it its number 1 cigar of 2018.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish the blend. Neptune lists a Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler but does not say where the wrapper is grown.

cigars.about: A 2022 blend marking twenty years since work began on The Edge, Rocky Patel's best-known value line. It is built around a ten-year-old Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, the original Edge wrapper type, and rolled in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: The maker gives no strength and retailers split: Neptune lists Medium, Holt's lists Medium-Full. Halfwheel reported a Honduran Habano binder with Honduran and Panamanian filler, unlike the maker's Nicaraguan and Honduran.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Honduran Corojo and Maduro, barber pole
cigars.about: A barber pole cigar that twists together the wrappers of The Edge Corojo and The Edge Maduro, made to mark ten years of The Edge. It began as a limited Toro in 2015 and was kept as a regular line.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrappers, so it is half Corojo and half Maduro. Halfwheel calls both leaves Honduran; Neptune calls the maduro Costa Rican. The maker's site and Neptune file it under Medium, while Holt's lists Full.

cigars.about: The green-wrapped version of The Edge, a single Toro with a Habano-seed Candela wrapper grown in Honduras. It is rolled at Plasencia's El Paraiso factory alongside the rest of The Edge.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's 2012 release called it medium bodied and Holt's lists Medium, while Neptune calls it mild to medium. The maker called the binder and filler a secret; the ones listed come from Neptune alone. The first run in 2012 was a limited edition of 1,000 boxes.

cigars.about: A box-pressed San Andrés blend released in 2025 for the company's thirty years in business. It uses two Nicaraguan binders aged over seven years and Honduran and Nicaraguan fillers aged over five.
cigars.researchNote: A separate Thirtieth Anniversary Limited Edition toro in tubes (1,000 boxes of 10) uses a different blend. The maker says Medium-Full; Neptune's spec lists Medium.

cigars.about: Rocky Patel's first Chinese zodiac cigar, a 2024 limited edition San Andrés toro using tobaccos aged since 2014. It started the brand's yearly Lunar New Year series.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium-plus, meaning medium to medium-full. The U.S. Toro was limited to 6,000 boxes of 10; other sizes went overseas and to duty-free. Halfwheel listed two Connecticut binders and some Honduran filler, unlike the maker's page.

cigars.about: The 2025 entry in Rocky Patel's Chinese zodiac series, a limited edition toro with a dark Nicaraguan Habano wrapper over a Nicaraguan broadleaf binder. It is made at the TaviCusa factory in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: These details are for the U.S. version, limited to 6,000 boxes of 10. The international version uses a Nicaraguan Habano 2000 Oscuro wrapper and is blended to Medium. Neptune lists the U.S. cigar as Medium.

cigars.about: The 2026 Chinese zodiac release from Rocky Patel, a box-pressed San Andrés Churchill sold in boxes of ten. It was blended by Nish Patel and is the third cigar in the series.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 6,000 boxes of 10. Unlike the Dragon and Snake, there is one version for all markets. The maker says medium to full; Neptune lists Full.

cigars.about: The milder Connecticut Shade version of Rocky Patel Freedom, a value line named for Rocky Patel's lobbying on behalf of cigar smokers. It is rolled at the TaviCusa factory in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: A milder extension of the 2012 Freedom line. Only the Robusto could be confirmed; other sizes may exist. Strength comes from Neptune alone and no release year was found.

cigars.about: A treasure chest humidor of 60 toros holding three Gurkha blends, 20 each in Connecticut shade, Habano and maduro wrappers, made at Las Villas Cigars in Nicaragua. A follow-up, Grand Age II, came out in 2023 in a 6 x 54 toro.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as a 60-cigar chest of toros in three wrappers (Connecticut shade, Habano, maduro), so there is no single wrapper; binder and filler are not published. Neptune gives the toro as 6 x 50 in its description but 54 ring in its specs; Grand Age II is 6 x 54. Neptune also describes an older Honduran Grand Age with a Cameroon wrapper.

cigars.about: A Gurkha line introduced in 2018 with packaging and a flavor profile modeled on pre-embargo Cuban cigars. Each box of 20 holds 10 box-pressed and 10 round cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Sources do not say where the Sumatra wrapper is grown. The 6 x 60 Magnum was added in 2019. Neptune lists the Toro as discontinued while the Robusto is still offered.

cigars.about: A box-pressed cigar with an unfinished foot, released in 2013 as the third blend under Gurkha's East India Trading Company label. It was priced as an affordable everyday smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Released under Gurkha's East India Trading Company label. Neptune lists it as Full strength but describes it as medium bodied; Cigar Place calls it medium to full.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (Aganorsa Leaf)
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made for Gurkha by Aganorsa Leaf from its own tobaccos, released in September 2020. It replaced an older Dominican-made San Miguel and was discontinued in 2023.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as San Miguel by Gurkha. The original San Miguel was Dominican made with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. Cigar Dojo rated it medium to full, Halfwheel found it just above medium, and Neptune lists Full.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Corojo 99, Criollo 98 from Esteli and Jalapa)
cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (Aganorsa Leaf)
cigars.about: Gurkha's 30th anniversary cigar, marking 30 years since Kaizad Hansotia bought the brand, and one of the first Gurkhas made by Aganorsa Leaf. It came out in September 2019 and was discontinued in 2023.
cigars.researchNote: A Belicoso (6 1/4 x 52) and Figurado (6 3/4 x 52) were sold only in limited Treinta humidors.

cigars.about: A limited Gurkha release from 2018 that is milder and creamier than most of the brand's blends, made at PDR Cigars. It came in a domed box inside a metal lattice cage.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is published only as Ecuadorian Desflorado, with no seed type given. The first run was 300 boxes of 20 per size.

cigars.about: A single-size Cellar Reserve made to mark ten years of Gurkha's Cellar Reserve line. It debuted in 2017 in 50-count humidors and returned in 2018 in boxes of 24.
cigars.researchNote: Gurkha has not said where it is made. The 2017 humidor release listed Nicaraguan binder and filler; the 2018 boxes list Dominican. Gurkha's release called it medium bodied while its website said medium-full; it is still in Gurkha's Cellar Reserve toro sampler.

cigars.about: A value-priced Nicaraguan puro launched in 2011 as the first cigar under Gurkha's East India Trading Company label. It was sold in plain boxes of 50.
cigars.researchNote: Released under Gurkha's East India Trading Company label. Halfwheel and Neptune list an all-Nicaraguan blend; Famous Smoke lists a Dominican-made version with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper in 5 x 52 and 7 x 60. Neptune marks it discontinued.

cigars.about: Released in 2012 to mark 125 years since the 1887 date Gurkha claims as its origin. It is made at the PDR factory in the Dominican Republic with a Brazilian wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Gurkha calls it medium bodied; Famous Smoke lists it as Medium-Full. Famous currently shows only a 6 x 54 Toro.

cigars.about: A Honduran-made Gurkha maduro with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. It is a different cigar from Gurkha's Black Dragon Special Edition Tubo.
cigars.researchNote: Blend is from Famous Smoke only. Do not confuse it with the Black Dragon Special Edition Tubo (7 1/2 x 52, Dominican made, Cameroon binder), which Gurkha lists as Medium with an Ecuadorian maduro wrapper.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan-made Gurkha with a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Not listed on Gurkha's own site; details come from retailers. Retailers say the wrapper is aged nine years or more. Factory is not published; Cigar Place dates the line to 2008.

cigars.about: A milder Gurkha with a Connecticut shade wrapper, introduced at the 2016 trade show in 10-count boxes. It was first made at American Caribbean Tobacco in Esteli, Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel's 2016 launch report gives a Nicaraguan factory and filler. Famous Smoke and Neptune now list it as Dominican made with Dominican filler, so the current version may differ. Famous calls the wrapper Ecuadorian Connecticut and Neptune US Connecticut; Neptune rates it mild.

cigars.about: A Gurkha blend first sold in 2001 and brought back in 2017, made by Fidel Olivas, who blended the original. Gurkha calls the recipe OVB, for Original Vintage Blend.
cigars.researchNote: Gurkha's release calls it mild to medium, while Famous Smoke lists Medium-Full. Halfwheel gives an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper; Famous says Nicaraguan Habano. A Robusto and Perfecto #2 also exist; their sizes are not published.

cigars.about: A Gurkha known for its shaggy, unfinished foot, which lets the filler and binder burn alone before the wrapper joins in. First released in 2001, it returned in 2016 from Fidel Olivas's factory in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Sold without a band. The 2016 return was capped at 4,000 boxes of 25 per size each year. Famous Smoke currently lists only the 6 x 60 as a Gordo.

cigars.about: A mellow Dominican-made Gurkha with a Connecticut shade wrapper, pitched as an easy introduction to the brand.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers disagree on where the Connecticut shade wrapper is grown: Famous Smoke says Ecuador in its description and Dominican in its specs, Neptune says the US. Famous lists it as Medium; Neptune calls it mild. Not listed on Gurkha's own site.

cigars.about: A Honduran-made Gurkha with a Costa Rican maduro wrapper over a filler blend from several countries.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke lists it as Full; Cigar Place lists Medium-Full with a Nicaraguan binder and no Nicaraguan filler. Not listed on Gurkha's own site.

cigars.about: A medium-bodied Dominican-made Gurkha with a dark Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over Dominican binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Blend is from Famous Smoke only. Not listed on Gurkha's own site; factory and release year are not published.

cigars.about: A one-size Halloween release from Lost&Found, the side brand of Robert Caldwell, Tony Bellatto and Jaclyn Sears. It shipped in October 2022 in 10-count bundles.
cigars.researchNote: Lost & Found is Caldwell's sister brand, run by Robert Caldwell with Tony Bellatto and Jaclyn Sears. Only 500 bundles of 10 were made, 5,000 cigars in all.

cigars.line: Lost&Found 22 Minutes to Midnight Connecticut Radiante
cigars.about: One of the two Robert Caldwell blends in Lost&Found's 22 Minutes to Midnight series, with bands that read 23:38. The cigars were rolled in 2020 at William Ventura's El Maestro factory and aged before shipping in May 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Blend is not disclosed; the company says only that the fillers have a combined age of more than 25 years. Strength is Halfwheel's reading, not the maker's. Lost & Found is Caldwell's sister brand; shipped twice a year, about 4,000 cigars per size per year.

cigars.line: Lost&Found 22 Minutes to Midnight Habano de Oro
cigars.about: One of the two Robert Caldwell blends in Lost&Found's 22 Minutes to Midnight series, with bands that read 23:38. The cigars were rolled in 2020 at William Ventura's El Maestro factory and aged before shipping in May 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Blend is not disclosed; the company says only that the fillers have a combined age of more than 25 years. Lost & Found is Caldwell's sister brand, run by Robert Caldwell with Tony Bellatto and Jaclyn Sears. Shipped twice a year, about 4,000 cigars per size per year.

cigars.about: A Lost&Found blend commissioned from William Ventura's El Maestro factory and aged for years before it shipped in May 2022. It is a different blend from the 2020 Instant Classic.
cigars.researchNote: Lost & Found is Caldwell's sister brand, run by Robert Caldwell with Tony Bellatto and Jaclyn Sears. Announced in 2022 as an ongoing line, with a 5 x 50 Robusto, 6 x 46 Corona Gorda and 6 x 52 Toro planned. It is not in the current lineup on Caldwell's site.

cigars.about: A Lost&Found blend commissioned from William Ventura's El Maestro factory and aged for years before it shipped in May 2022. It is a different blend from the 2020 Instant Classic.
cigars.researchNote: Binder is not published. Lost & Found is Caldwell's sister brand, run by Robert Caldwell with Tony Bellatto and Jaclyn Sears. Announced in 2022 as an ongoing line; it is not in the current lineup on Caldwell's site.

cigars.about: A short, fat perfecto in Arturo Fuente's Hemingway series, with a Cameroon wrapper over Dominican tobaccos. The Hemingway series dates to 1983 and revived the old tapered perfecto shapes.
cigars.researchNote: This is one size of the Hemingway line, not its own blend. Fuente lists it as 4 1/2 inches with a 43/55 ring (tapered foot). Also made with a Connecticut broadleaf maduro wrapper.

cigars.about: The largest perfecto in Arturo Fuente's Hemingway series at 9 inches, with a Cameroon wrapper over Dominican tobaccos. It is sold in boxes of 10 rather than the usual 25.
cigars.researchNote: This is one size of the Hemingway line, not its own blend. Also made with a Connecticut broadleaf maduro wrapper. The Hemingway series itself dates to 1983.

cigars.about: A large perfecto in Arturo Fuente's Hemingway series that is sold only with a maduro wrapper. It uses the Hemingway blend of Dominican tobaccos under Connecticut broadleaf.
cigars.researchNote: This is one size of the Hemingway line and comes in maduro only. Fuente lists it as 7 1/2 x 54, while Holt's lists 7 5/8 x 54.

cigars.about: The Hemingway perfecto blend of Dominican tobaccos dressed in an Ecuadorian sun grown wrapper instead of the usual Cameroon. Arturo Fuente ships it only occasionally, in the Signature and Classic sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Fuente lists the Sungrown wrapper only on the Signature and Classic sizes. Neptune says Fuente releases it only on special occasions.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Habano-seed Oscuro grown by Oliva Tobacco Co.
cigars.about: A darker take on the Hemingway perfecto, using a habano-seed oscuro wrapper from Oliva Tobacco Co. over the usual Dominican Hemingway blend. It debuted in October 2024 for retailers in the Tobacconists' Association of America.
cigars.researchNote: Fuente has not confirmed where the wrapper is grown. halfwheel believes it is Ecuador. It has a red ribbon at the foot, which the Hemingway Maduro does not.

cigars.about: A Don Carlos offshoot first shipped in 2015 for Carlos Fuente Sr.'s 80th birthday, said to be based on his personal Senior Blend. It comes as a robusto and as the Eye of the Shark, a belicoso with a box-pressed foot.
cigars.researchNote: Fuente has not published a separate blend; halfwheel lists it as undisclosed and says the wrapper looks like Cameroon. Fuente lists Eye of the Shark at 5 1/4 x 52, halfwheel at 5 3/4 x 52. It launched as a limited edition and can be hard to find.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (including Chateau de la Fuente)
cigars.about: A tribute robusto to the late Carlos Fuente Sr., based on the Don Carlos blend but with some filler from Fuente's Chateau de la Fuente farm. It was first shown at a Holt's event in 2017 and went to retailers nationwide in 2018.
cigars.researchNote: Fuente has not disclosed the wrapper or binder, and halfwheel found it tastes unlike a regular Don Carlos. It is on Fuente's Don Carlos list but ships only occasionally and in small amounts. A 7 1/2 x 41 lancero was shown for holiday 2024.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican, the Chateau de la Fuente leaf used on OpusX
cigars.about: A Dominican puro that Carlito Fuente blended in 2006 to mark 30 years of his father's Don Carlos cigar, swapping the usual Cameroon wrapper for a Dominican leaf. It is aged for years and sold in small batches through Prometheus as part of the Fuente Aged Selection.
cigars.researchNote: Its own blend, not a regular Don Carlos with a new wrapper. halfwheel calls the wrapper sun grown rosado, while Cigar Aficionado and Holt's call it shade grown. Holt's and halfwheel rate it medium, though Cigar Aficionado says it is stronger than regular Don Carlos.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican corojo-seed from Chateau de la Fuente, rolled over a Cameroon wrapper
cigars.about: A Don Carlos made for what would have been Carlos Fuente Sr.'s 90th birthday. It is a standard Cameroon-wrapped Don Carlos that is aged a year, given a second Dominican corojo wrapper on top, then aged another year.
cigars.researchNote: It has two wrappers, one over the other, which Fuente says is a first. The corojo nods to the original 1976 Nicaraguan-made Don Carlos, which did not use Cameroon. Sold in cases of 90 and lightly box-pressed.

cigars.about: A regular production Don Carlos extension launched in October 2025, and the first Arturo Fuente cigar to wear a Mexican San Andrés wrapper. The binder and filler are Dominican, and the name means bull's blood.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is reported differently: halfwheel's review found medium strength with a medium-plus body, while Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.about: A rare OpusX offshoot from Arturo Fuente that first reached stores in late 2011 as ForbiddenX 13, tied to the company's 100th anniversary. It returned for TAA retailers in 2018, and four new sizes with a lighter wrapper arrived in December 2020.
cigars.researchNote: Fuente does not disclose the blend, saying only that the tobacco comes from Chateau de la Fuente. halfwheel writes the name as ForbiddenX 13 and found the 2020 sizes medium-full. The 2020 sizes come in cedar sleeves and are a different blend from the 2011 originals.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican rosado oscuro from Chateau de la Fuente
cigars.about: A dark-wrapped version of OpusX that Arturo Fuente introduced in late 2015. It is a Dominican puro whose OpusX wrapper is aged and fermented longer, and it wears a gold ribbon at the foot.
cigars.researchNote: First sold as Rosado Oscuro Oro in a 15-cigar sampler. Retailers also call it OXO and list the wrapper as maduro because it is so dark. Neptune lists it as full, while halfwheel's 2015 review found medium strength.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican (lighter than the regular OpusX wrapper)
cigars.about: The blue-banded OpusX made to mark 20 years of the brand, which debuted in 1995. It reached stores in December 2016 and uses a lighter Dominican wrapper for a milder, creamier smoke than regular OpusX.
cigars.researchNote: Fuente's site calls it 20th Anniversary, while halfwheel calls it 20 Years Celebration. It wears blue bands instead of the usual red. Fuente has not published the binder and filler; Neptune lists them as Dominican.

sizes.name: Perfecto (La Familia X to the 25th Power)

cigars.about: The green-banded OpusX made for the brand's 25th anniversary. It debuted in November 2021 as a 7 x 50 Churchill sold only inside Elie Bleu humidors, and a perfecto in metal coffins followed in late 2024.
cigars.researchNote: Fuente has not disclosed the blend, which is believed to be an all-Dominican variation of OpusX. Neptune lists it as full, while halfwheel's review found medium to medium-plus strength. The perfecto size is from Neptune.
