cigars.about: An OpusX release marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, shipped in August 2026. Each box of 20 holds 16 Churchills and four fully box-pressed cigars in an American flag wrap, and $11 per box goes to charity.
cigars.researchNote: Fuente has not disclosed the blend, which is believed to be based on the original OpusX with tweaks. The size of the four flag-wrapped pressed cigars has not been published. Fuente has not said whether it is a one-time release.

cigars.line: Fuente Fuente OpusX Templo de Oro
cigars.about: An OpusX blend with a lighter-colored wrapper that arrived in stores in December 2025. Carlito Fuente says he made it to be creamier than any other OpusX, and it wears the black OpusX band with a gold foil sleeve.
cigars.researchNote: Fuente declined to disclose the tobaccos; Neptune lists it as all Dominican. The name means temple of gold. It is unclear how often it will ship.

cigars.about: A collector series from Arturo Fuente that packs aged OpusX and OpusX Forbidden X cigars in five-cigar samplers with playful packaging. Retailers list a Series 2020 OpusX sampler and Series 2021 Forbidden X samplers.
cigars.researchNote: Details come from Neptune Cigar only; Fuente's own Toymaker page gives no cigar details. Neptune describes it as an all-Dominican puro and lists the 2021 Forbidden X Belicoso at 5 3/4 x 54, box-pressed, medium strength.

cigars.about: A Dominican puro OpusX blend created for Expo 2020 in the United Arab Emirates and launched in Dubai in December 2019. It stayed a UAE exclusive until a one-time U.S. shipment in December 2024, and is nicknamed Opus Dubai.
cigars.researchNote: Known as Opus Dubai and wears green bands. Fuente does not say how it differs from regular OpusX. Neptune lists it as full, and halfwheel found it starts gentler than regular OpusX but builds to full by the end.

cigars.line: Fuente Fuente OpusX La Edicion de la Sociedad
cigars.about: The first cigar from The OpusX Society, a project between designer Manny Iriarte's company and Arturo Fuente. It is a single 6 1/4 x 49 size in blue and yellow bands, made by Fuente and first shipped in October 2024.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is undisclosed. It is sold by Manny Iriarte Enterprises at about $90 a cigar with no set MSRP. halfwheel lists it as regular production, though Carlito Fuente called it extremely limited.

cigars.about: The second cigar from The OpusX Society, the collaboration between Manny Iriarte Enterprises and Arturo Fuente. It is a 6 3/4 x 50 parejo sold in boxes of 12 that began shipping in July 2026.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is undisclosed and said to differ from La Edicion de la Sociedad. Production is 2,500 boxes of 12 a year, up from the 1,500 first announced. No MSRP is set, and stores listed it at $125 to $150 a cigar.

cigars.about: A maduro version of Rocky Patel's Freedom line, made as a Nicaraguan puro at the company's own factory in Esteli. It was created for the distributor Santa Clara Inc.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as a maduro, but the wrapper is a dark Nicaraguan habano oscuro leaf rather than broadleaf. Distributed exclusively through Santa Clara Inc. Neptune rates it full, while Cigar Place lists it medium-full.

cigars.about: Rocky Patel's 2020 exclusive for retailers in the Tobacconists' Association of America. It is a single toro with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,000 boxes of 20 and sold only through TAA member shops.

cigars.about: A single toro made to mark the 250th anniversary of the United States. The cigars were rolled in early 2025 and aged at Rocky Patel's Esteli factory before release.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,000 boxes of 20. It was first offered to shops at summer 2026 road show events, with shipping expected in mid to late September 2026.

cigars.about: A version of the Decade that swaps the usual Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper for a Honduran habano leaf. It was Rocky Patel's 2022 exclusive for Tobacconists' Association of America shops.
cigars.researchNote: TAA 2022 exclusive, limited to 1,000 boxes of 20 in one box-pressed size. No published strength rating was found.

cigars.about: A take on the Decade made for the distributor Phillips & King's Reserve Collection. It uses a Cameroon-seed wrapper grown in Ecuador in place of the regular Decade's Sumatra-seed leaf.
cigars.researchNote: Sold through the distributor Phillips & King as part of its Reserve Collection. No published strength rating was found.

cigars.about: A 6 x 60 Connecticut-wrapped cigar made for the Chicago-area distributor Arango Cigar Co. The name comes from Carl Sandburg's nickname for Chicago, the City of Big Shoulders.
cigars.researchNote: Exclusive to the distributor Arango Cigar Co. It is made at Plasencia's Tabacos de Oriente in Danli rather than at Rocky Patel's own factories.

cigars.about: A Honduran puro toro made for the New York Tobacconist Association to help fund its work on New York cigar tax and licensing bills. Rocky Patel said it would donate the proceeds to the group.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as the NYTA Rocky Patel Empire; first run of 1,000 boxes of 10. halfwheel's review lists an all-Honduran blend, though its launch story said Honduran and Nicaraguan tobaccos. The review had it starting at medium strength and finishing full.

cigars.about: Rocky Patel's low-priced bundle line, made at El Paraiso in Honduras. It is a Cuban sandwich style cigar with a whole-leaf wrapper and binder over short filler.
cigars.researchNote: Comes in two wrappers: Classic (Honduran maduro) and Shade (Connecticut-seed grown in Honduras). Uses short filler, not long filler. Famous Smoke calls the line medium-bodied and the Shade mild.

cigars.about: A San Andres-wrapped line made at Rocky Patel's Nicaraguan factory, with part of the proceeds going to The Juneteenth Foundation. The name refers to June 19, 1865.
cigars.researchNote: A portion of sales goes to The Juneteenth Foundation. halfwheel's review found it medium in strength, while Cigars Direct, Mike's Cigars and Cigar Place list it medium-full. Cigars Direct lists the Toro at 6 x 52, but halfwheel and Cigar Place give 6 1/2 x 52.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped version of Rocky Patel's value-priced Catch 22 line, made in Honduras. It was introduced at the 2016 IPCPR trade show.
cigars.researchNote: The binder and filler are undisclosed. Neptune describes it as mild, while Cigars Direct, Mike's Cigars and Cigar Place all list it as medium.

cigars.about: A medium-strength Rocky Patel line with a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and Honduran and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune and Cigar Place say it is made in Honduras with Honduran and Nicaraguan filler, while Cigars Direct says Nicaragua with Nicaraguan filler. Cigar Place lists a Honduran binder; the other two say Nicaraguan. No factory or release year is published.

cigars.about: A medium-strength Rocky Patel line with a Mexican San Andres maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers disagree on where it is rolled: Neptune says Honduras, Cigars Direct says Nicaragua. No factory or release year is published.

cigars.about: A companion to Rocky Patel's Flor de San Andres with a dark Mexican San Andres maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is made in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Cigars Direct calls it a stronger, box-pressed follow-up to Flor de San Andres, though its spec table and Neptune both rate it medium. Also sold as a 52-ring Toro and Torpedo, but Cigars Direct gives their length as both 6 1/4 and 6 1/2 inches. No factory or release year is published.

cigars.about: A medium-strength Honduran-made Rocky Patel with an Ecuadorian Sumatra-seed wrapper and a Honduran binder.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune rates it medium and lists Nicaraguan and Honduran filler, while Cigars Direct rates it medium-full and lists Nicaraguan filler only. Also sold in Churchill and Torpedo.

cigars.about: A single toro blended to mark baseball player Gary Sheffield's 500th home run. It comes in a box made to look and feel like a baseball.
cigars.researchNote: Rocky Patel called it a limited special edition at its 2012 launch, but it is still sold by retailers today. HR500 stands for Homerun 500.

cigars.about: A mild Connecticut-wrapped Rocky Patel made in Honduras and sold through Famous Smoke Shop. It is often shortened to AMS.
cigars.researchNote: Famous's spec table and Neptune both call it mild, though Famous's description also says mellow to medium. The Nicaraguan binder comes from Neptune; Famous does not list one. A cheaper Fumas bundle version is also sold.

cigars.about: A value-priced, box-pressed Rocky Patel made in Honduras with Honduran and Nicaraguan long filler, sold through Famous Smoke Shop.
cigars.researchNote: Famous says the line comes in Corojo or Maduro wrappers, but only the Nicaraguan Corojo version is listed now. The binder is not published.

cigars.about: A value-priced Rocky Patel in big ring gauges with a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan filler, sold through Famous Smoke Shop.
cigars.researchNote: Despite the name, Famous lists the country of origin as Honduras. The binder is not published.

cigars.about: A Rocky Patel line named for its reddish Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, sold by Famous Smoke Shop as an exclusive. It is made in Honduras with Dominican and Nicaraguan long filler.
cigars.researchNote: Famous calls it an exclusive. Rosado describes the reddish color; the leaf itself is Ecuadorian Sumatra. The Dominican binder comes from Neptune; Famous does not list one. A cheaper Rosado Fumas bundle version is also sold.

cigars.about: A full-strength Rocky Patel with a thick Mexican San Andres maduro wrapper over a core of Nicaraguan tobacco, sold through Famous Smoke Shop as RP San Andres.
cigars.researchNote: Listed at Famous as RP San Andres. The binder is not published and no tasting notes are published.

cigars.about: A value-priced Rocky Patel sold through Famous Smoke Shop, with a reddish Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, a Honduran binder and Nicaraguan and Honduran filler.
cigars.researchNote: Famous's spec table says full strength, but its description says medium-bodied and medium to full in strength.

cigars.about: A medium-bodied Honduran-made Rocky Patel sold through Holt's, with a Nicaraguan wrapper, Mexican binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan long filler.
cigars.researchNote: Sold through Holt's. Holt's gives the wrapper only as Nicaraguan, with no leaf type.

cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped Rocky Patel sold through Holt's, made in Honduras with aged Nicaraguan tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Sold through Holt's, which rates it medium. The binder is not published.

cigars.about: A golf-themed bundle line made by Rocky Patel for Holt's. Holt's says the blend was modeled on the Rocky Patel Decade and that it bought the entire production.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's exclusive, sold in bundles of 20. Holt's does not publish the binder, filler or country. Several spin-off Mulligans blends exist, such as Eagle Reserve and Fairway Edition.

cigars.about: The broadleaf maduro version of La Aurora's 107th anniversary blend, made in the Dominican Republic. It reached stores in 2013 after several years of delays.
cigars.researchNote: Renamed 107 USA in a 2023 rebrand, though many shops still list it as 107 Maduro. The maker lists a Dominican binder with Dominican, Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler; halfwheel and Neptune list a Dominican Corojo binder with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler.

cigars.about: A Dominican puro released in 2023 to mark 120 years since La Aurora was founded in 1903. It uses a Dominican-grown Habano 92 wrapper over Cibao Valley binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in the U.S. as 120 Anniversary or 120th Anniversary. A 6 x 58 perfecto Limited Edition and a 6 7/8 x 40 Lancero were also released in limited runs. Neptune lists the Toro as 5 1/2 x 54; halfwheel measured it at 5 3/4.

cigars.about: La Aurora's first all-Dominican blend, created for the company's 100th anniversary and released in 2004. It was planned as a limited run but has kept returning, and came back as a regular production line in 2025.
cigars.researchNote: The 5 x 50 Robusto Especial uses a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper instead of the Corojo. Neptune lists the Churchill as 7 x 50; halfwheel lists 7 x 47. The Belicoso was Cigar Aficionado's No. 2 cigar of 2004.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Cibao Valley), Nicaragua, Brazil, Peru
cigars.about: A La Aurora blend of six tobaccos from five countries, named for the year Santiago de los Caballeros was founded. It pairs an Ecuadorian wrapper with a Brazilian binder.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke sells this original blend as 1495 Ecuador, next to Brazil, Connecticut and Nicaragua versions. Famous lists the Churchill as 7 x 47; older listings at halfwheel and Holt's show 7 x 50. Holt's rates it medium and Famous calls it full-bodied.

cigars.about: A very small batch La Aurora cigar with a Corojo wrapper. It first appeared in 2007 as an unbanded release of 100 cabinets of 50 sold only in Manhattan shops, and the maker still lists it as a yearly limited batch.
cigars.researchNote: The size and the Dominican origin of the wrapper come from halfwheel's account of the 2007 Manhattan release, which also had some Nicaraguan filler. The maker's current page gives no sizes and lists a Habana Corojo wrapper and binder with Dominican filler.

cigars.about: A giant 20 x 80 novelty cigar from La Aurora, sold singly in a wooden coffin with a clear front. It was first made for the factory store and came to the U.S. in 2016.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel calls it La Stravaganza. Halfwheel and Neptune say it uses the 1495 blend: Brazilian Mata Fina binder with Brazilian, Dominican, Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler. The maker's page lists an Ecuador binder and Dominican filler.

cigars.about: The Connecticut Broadleaf version of La Aurora's Preferidos, the double perfecto sold in a shaped black tube. It joined the line in 2012.
cigars.researchNote: The Robusto and Toro are the straight-sided 1903 Edition versions of the same broadleaf blend. The maker lists Dominican and Nicaraguan filler; Neptune lists Brazilian and Dominican.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Cameroon (the maker lists it as grown in Ecuador)
cigars.about: The Cameroon wrapped version of La Aurora's Preferidos double perfecto, sold in a shaped tube.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the wrapper as Cameroon grown in Ecuador, while Famous Smoke calls it African Cameroon. The maker and Neptune rate it medium; Famous calls it full-bodied. Robusto and Toro sizes were added in 2017.

cigars.about: The Dominican Corojo wrapped version of La Aurora's Preferidos double perfecto, sold in a shaped gold tube.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists Dominican, Brazilian and Cameroon filler; Neptune lists Brazilian, Nicaraguan and Peruvian. Robusto and Toro sizes were added in 2017.

cigars.about: A Preferidos double perfecto whose binder and filler are aged in used rum barrels, with the finished cigars then rested in the barrels again. It debuted in 2016, was dropped after about two years, and returned with a new blend in 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Blend shown is the 2026 version, limited to 750 boxes of 8. The 2016 original also had an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper but a different binder and filler, and the maker's product page still shows the older blend.

cigars.about: La Aurora's annual limited edition made from tobacco aged at least 12 years, named after the cognac term for 'beyond age'. It debuted in 2018 and each release carries the year the cigars were rolled.
cigars.researchNote: Some editions are labeled La Aurora Hors d'Age without the Preferidos name. Recent toro releases ran 650 to 700 boxes of 15. The Lancero is new with the 2025 edition shipping in late 2026, and some earlier editions are listed at 6 x 54.

cigars.about: A La Aurora limited series in which each release is blended from a single crop year and named for that vintage. It began in 2008, and recent vintages are a salomon sold in boxes of eight.
cigars.researchNote: Blend shown is the 2014 and 2016 vintages; earlier ones differ (the 2007 had a Dominican wrapper, the 2005 a Cameroon). The salomon is listed as 6 1/2 x 50/60. Neptune rates the 2007 full and the 2009 medium.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andrés (Lot No. 007; each lot differs)
cigars.about: A series of small one-off releases of long-aged cigars from La Aurora's aging rooms, blended by Manuel Inoa. It began in 2023 and each numbered lot has its own blend and shape.
cigars.researchNote: Details shown are for Lot No. 007 (2025, 180 boxes of 10, aged 21 years). Every lot is a different blend and shape: Lot 002 had a corojo wrapper, Lot 003 an Ecuadorian one and Lot 006 a Nicaraguan one. Check the lot number on the box.

cigars.about: A 2022 limited line that La Aurora blended with feedback from about 100 retailers who visited the factory. It uses a Cameroon seed wrapper grown in Ecuador.
cigars.researchNote: Originally limited to 1,000 boxes per size. In late 2025 La Aurora said the remaining stock, about 200 boxes per size, would be the last and it has no plans to keep making it.

cigars.about: The first cigar in La Aurora's Family Creed Series, released in 2025. It is a box-pressed blend built to taste different from the company's usual profile, with a San Andrés wrapper and some Pennsylvania filler.
cigars.researchNote: All sizes are box-pressed. La Aurora describes it as medium to full; Neptune lists it as medium and Famous Smoke as full.

cigars.about: The second cigar in La Aurora's Family Creed Series, released in 2026. It is a full-strength, box-pressed blend with a Pennsylvania Broadleaf wrapper over a San Andrés binder.
cigars.researchNote: All sizes are box-pressed.

cigars.about: A La Aurora cigar with a reddish Dominican Corojo wrapper whose tobacco is aged in Dominican rum barrels.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke lists the strength as full and describes it as medium to full; Holt's lists medium and only Dominican filler. It is not on the maker's site and is sold out at Holt's, so it may be discontinued. Not the same cigar as the Preferidos Double Barrel Aged or Barrel Aged by Karl Malone.

cigars.about: La Aurora's budget-priced long-filler line, introduced in 2018 with an Ecuadorian Connecticut seed wrapper. It became Cazadores Claro when Maduro and Nicaragua versions were added in 2024.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2018 simply as Cazadores in a 5 x 50 Robusto, 6 x 50 Toro and 6 1/4 x 52 Belicoso. The sizes shown are the ones halfwheel listed for all three Cazadores blends in 2024.

cigars.about: The maduro version of La Aurora's budget-priced Cazadores line, added in 2024. It uses an Indonesian maduro wrapper and binder over Dominican filler.
The Nicaraguan version of La Aurora's budget-priced Cazadores line, added in 2024. It has a Nicaraguan wrapper and filler with an Indonesian binder, and is rolled in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper's leaf type is not published, only that it is Nicaraguan.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican, summer-grown at Chateau de la Fuente
cigars.about: An OpusX offshoot made with wrapper from an off-season summer crop that Carlito Fuente planted in 2004 so Andy Garcia could film The Lost City on the farm. It is sold through Prometheus as part of the Fuente Aged Selection, with part of each sale funding a scholarship for Cigar Family school graduates.
cigars.researchNote: Prometheus describes it as medium-to-full; Holt's lists it as Full. Holt's lists the Piramide at 5 3/4 x 52, Prometheus at 6 x 52. The Carlito's A was added in 2023 to mark the line's 15th anniversary.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican Chateau de la Fuente Sun Grown Rosado (Natural); a Maduro version is also made
cigars.about: A large, bulb-footed figurado in the OpusX blend, one of the best known of the rare OpusX shapes. It is sold in Natural and Maduro through Prometheus in the Heaven and Earth series, in travel humidors of 10.
cigars.researchNote: This is one special shape of OpusX, not a separate blend. Blend shown is for the Natural; the wrapper of the Maduro version is not published. The shape predates the Heaven and Earth series, which began in 2017.

cigars.about: A very thick 6 x 74 OpusX perfecto with a flat cap, named for Barry Herbst of BLH Industries, who makes cigar molds for Fuente. It first appeared in 2013 and joined the Heaven and Earth series in 2023, sold in travel humidors of six.
cigars.researchNote: This is one special shape of OpusX. No separate blend is published; halfwheel describes it with the regular all-Dominican OpusX blend. In 2013 only 500 were sold, one in each Opus22 10th release humidor.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican (Natural), with a maduro strip at the foot; a Maduro version is also made
cigars.about: A sharply box-pressed OpusX perfecto with a very pointed head and a contrasting strip of wrapper at the foot. It comes in Natural and Maduro and is sold through Prometheus in the Heaven and Earth series, in travel humidors of 10.
cigars.researchNote: This is one special shape of OpusX, not a separate blend. Blend shown is for the Natural; the wrapper of the Maduro version is not published. The scorpion refers to the birth sign of founder Arturo Fuente.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican, grown at Chateau de la Fuente
cigars.about: A dark-wrapped OpusX lonsdale with an unusual open torpedo head, sold through Prometheus in the Heaven and Earth series since late 2018. It comes in travel humidors of 10 and a share of sales goes to the Cigar Family Charitable Foundation.
cigars.researchNote: Prometheus says the name is not taken from the Prince song. Three diademas in the same blend arrived in 2026 but are branded Carlito's X Rare Purple (7 1/2 x 54, 6 1/4 x 56, 5 1/2 x 60). Early reviews listed the blend as undisclosed.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican, grown at Chateau de la Fuente
cigars.about: An OpusX blend with black bands sold through Prometheus in the Heaven and Earth series. It began in 2019 as a lonsdale with an open torpedo head, gained a Double Corona in 2021 and three diademas in 2026.
cigars.researchNote: The binder and filler have not been disclosed. Strength is taken from halfwheel's review, which had it finishing just under full.

cigars.about: A thick double robusto with OpusX fillers under a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper, named for the birth sign of founder Arturo Fuente. The Scorpio shape first appeared in 2007 in a Prometheus humidor and the Maduro is now sold in the Heaven and Earth series in travel humidors of 10.
cigars.researchNote: The Heaven and Earth series lists only the Scorpio Maduro. Blend, size and strength are from halfwheel's 2012 review of that cigar, which had it finishing at full strength.

cigars.line: Fuente Fuente OpusX Tauros the Bull
cigars.about: A special OpusX shape named for Taurus, the birth sign shared by Carlito Fuente and his father Carlos Fuente Sr. It comes in Natural and Maduro and is sold through Prometheus in the Heaven and Earth series, in travel humidors of 10.
cigars.researchNote: This is one special shape of OpusX, sold in Natural and Maduro. No blend is published for this size; standard OpusX is all Dominican tobacco from the Fuente farm. It was already in Prometheus sets by 2011.

cigars.about: Fuente's 100th anniversary cigar, also called Don Arturo Gran AniverXario Destino al Siglo; the name means destiny of the century. It was planned for 2012 but, after a 2011 fire, shipped at the end of 2013 in book-style boxes, using a Habano-seed Dominican wrapper instead of the seed used for OpusX.
cigars.researchNote: Fuente has not published the binder or filler. Fuente calls it full-flavored and Neptune lists Full, while halfwheel's early review found medium-full. Not a limited edition, but supply is small and stores often cap purchases.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian (Holt's lists it as Ecuador Habano Rosado)
cigars.about: A line of perfectos in Hemingway shapes, launched in December 2020 and led by Liana Fuente to raise money and awareness for breast cancer research. The full name is Rare Pink Vintage 1960's, a nod to the decade that shaped Carlito Fuente.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel's 2021 review listed a Dominican binder; its 2022 report and Neptune say Nicaraguan. halfwheel and Neptune list Queen of Hearts at 3 3/4 x 54, while Fuente's site and Holt's say 4 1/8 x 60. Not a limited edition, but it ships only in small batches.

cigars.about: A darker spin on Fuente's Rare Pink line, with a Connecticut-grown habano-seed wrapper over Dominican fillers. It was teased at the 2024 trade show and began shipping in March 2026.
cigars.researchNote: The binder has not been published. It launched as an exclusive for Tobacconists' Association of America stores for about six months. Strength is from Neptune only.

cigars.about: A series of occasional limited releases from Fuente that began in December 2012, with new versions in 2013, 2014 and 2015 and a return in 2021. The 2021 cigars were rolled in 2016 and limited to 1,000 boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: Each release has its own size, and Fuente says the blend varies from year to year without giving details. Details shown are for the 2021 release, which matches the 2012 size.

cigars.about: A collaboration between Carlito Fuente and Jorge Padrón in which each made a 7 x 50 Churchill honoring the other's father. It reached stores in March 2024 in boxes of 40, 20 of each cigar, at $7,115 a box, with profits going to the two families' charities.
cigars.researchNote: Both blends are undisclosed. Country, factory and tasting notes are for the cedar-wrapped cigar Fuente made; the box-pressed Padrón cigar is rolled in Nicaragua at Tabacos Cubanica. Holt's lists Medium-Full, Neptune lists Medium.

cigars.about: Fuente's value-priced line, made with medium-length aged Dominican filler under a reddish-brown Ecuador Habano wrapper. It arrived in 2012 and comes in three sizes sold in boxes of 30.
cigars.researchNote: This is a medium filler (mixed filler) cigar, not long filler. Fuente calls it medium-bodied; Holt's lists it as Mild-Medium. The binder is from Neptune only.

cigars.about: The golden Connecticut Shade version of Fuente's Gran Reserva, made with Dominican long filler. It comes in three of the longer Gran Reserva sizes and is known as a mellow, creamy smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Fuente lists D'Oro as a wrapper option within Gran Reserva, not as a separate line. Fuente does not say where the wrapper is grown: Neptune says USA Connecticut Shade, Famous says Ecuadorian-grown. Holt's and Famous list Medium, Neptune lists Mild; the binder is from Neptune only.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Fuente's flagship Gran Reserva, with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over aged Dominican tobaccos. It is offered in the same core sizes as the natural Cameroon version.
cigars.researchNote: This is the Maduro wrapper option of Gran Reserva, not a separate blend family. Retailers also file Curly Head Deluxe, Brevas Royales, Exquisitos and Cubanitos Maduro under it.

cigars.about: The green-wrapped version of Fuente's Gran Reserva, using a candela leaf over Dominican tobaccos. It is a mellow, grassy alternative offered in a handful of the Gran Reserva sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's and Famous sell it as Claro and list Medium; Neptune lists Mild. Fuente does not say where the candela leaf is grown: Neptune says Ecuador, Famous lists Connecticut. The binder is from Neptune only, and the Curly Head size comes from retailers, not Fuente's size chart.

cigars.about: Fuente cigars dressed in an Ecuadorian rosado sun grown wrapper over Dominican tobaccos, best known on the Flor Fina 8-5-8. That cigar first appeared in 2002 in a tiny run, returned in 2009 and 2018, and remains hard to find.
cigars.researchNote: Fuente lists Rosado Sun Grown as a wrapper option on the 8-5-8, and King T Rosado Sungrown sits in its Chateau Fuente series. It ships in small batches and is hard to find. halfwheel measured the 2018 8-5-8 at 6 1/4 x 47; the binder is from Neptune only.

cigars.about: Fuente's long-running budget lonsdale, made with medium-length Dominican filler and sold in boxes of 25. It is a smooth, mild everyday cigar that also comes in a Maduro version.
cigars.researchNote: Fuente's site says the wrapper is Connecticut shade, but Famous and Neptune both list the natural version as Cameroon. It is a medium filler (mixed filler) cigar; the binder is from Neptune only. Neptune lists Mild; Famous lists Medium but describes it as mild.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Fuente's Brevas Royales, an inexpensive corona made with medium-length Dominican filler. It is a small everyday smoke with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: This is the Maduro wrapper version of the single-size Brevas Royales, a medium filler (mixed filler) cigar. Retailers spell it Brevas Royale. The binder is from Neptune only.

cigars.about: Two extra sizes added to Tatuaje's Brown Label (Seleccion de Cazador) blend in 2013 to mark the brand's tenth year: a perfecto and a robusto. They are made in Nicaragua by the Garcia family at My Father Cigars.
cigars.researchNote: These are two sizes of the Nicaraguan-made Brown Label line, not a separate blend. Tatuaje and Holt's call it full strength, Atlantic says medium to full and Neptune medium. Limited Tuxtla (San Andres) and Capa Especial (Sumatra) versions came later.

cigars.about: A limited version of the Tatuaje 10th Anniversary cigars that swaps the usual Ecuadorian Habano wrapper for Ecuadorian Sumatra. It shipped in early 2024 in the same perfecto and robusto sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 3,000 boxes of 20 per size. Halfwheel and Atlantic list the Belle Encre at 5 3/4 x 48, while Holt's lists 5 3/8 x 48 like the original. Atlantic lists it as medium to full and Holt's as full.

cigars.about: One of two wrapper shades released in 2018 for Tatuaje's 15th anniversary, reviving two torpedo sizes first sold in 2004. It is rolled in Florida at the Garcia family's small El Rey de los Habanos factory.
cigars.researchNote: Same blend and wrapper varietal as the Rosado Oscuro, just a lighter shade of leaf. Tatuaje rates it 4 out of 5 for strength, Neptune lists it as full, and Halfwheel's reviewer found it closer to medium.

cigars.about: The darker-wrapper version of Tatuaje's 15th anniversary cigars from 2018, offered in the same two torpedo sizes as the Rosado Claro. It is rolled in Florida at the Garcia family's El Rey de los Habanos factory.
cigars.researchNote: Same blend and wrapper varietal as the Rosado Claro, just a darker shade of leaf. Often listed as Habano Oscuro. Tatuaje rates it 4 out of 5 for strength, Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.about: A regular-production line introduced in 2023 for Tatuaje's 20th year, using an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over a double Nicaraguan binder. Both sizes have a covered foot and are made at My Father Cigars in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Also written simply as Tatuaje 20th. Neptune lists it as medium and Halfwheel's reviewer found the strength mild to medium, while Holt's lists it as medium to full.

cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro made to mark Tatuaje founder Pete Johnson's 50th birthday. The cigars were rolled in Florida in late 2019 and early 2020, then aged until they shipped in April 2025.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as Tatuaje 50th, part of the Miami-made Escasos Collection. Only 500 boxes of 10 per size (5,000 cigars each). Neptune lists the origin as Nicaragua, but Halfwheel reports it was rolled at My Father's Doral, Florida factory.

cigars.about: Tatuaje's milder line, named for a tobacco town in central Cuba and wrapped in light Ecuadorian Connecticut leaf over Nicaraguan tobacco. It is made by the Garcia family at My Father Cigars and finished with a small flag cap.
cigars.researchNote: Tatuaje rates the strength 2+ out of 5 and Atlantic lists mild to medium, while Holt's calls it medium.

cigars.about: A darker, fuller version of Cabaiguan with a sun grown Ecuadorian wrapper, made at My Father Cigars. The Toro Grande was Cigar Aficionado's No. 7 cigar of 2011.
cigars.researchNote: Tatuaje only says the wrapper is from Ecuador; Atlantic calls it Ecuadorian sun grown and Holt's lists Ecuador Connecticut. Tatuaje rates it medium (3 of 5), Atlantic medium to full and Cigar Aficionado full. The Junior, 46 and RX sizes have been retired, leaving the Toro Grande.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Cabaiguan Guapos, using a dark Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is made at My Father Cigars in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Tatuaje retired the Junior and 46 maduro sizes in 2023 and the RX in 2026, leaving the Toro Grande. Tatuaje rates it medium (3 of 5), Neptune calls it medium strength but full bodied, and Atlantic lists medium to full.

cigars.about: The red-banded El Triunfador is a milder, box-pressed Tatuaje line with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco. It was first planned for Europe and reached the U.S. in 2010.
cigars.researchNote: Taken off Tatuaje's regular price list in July 2017 but not formally discontinued; it is only offered in small batches and at events. Tatuaje rates the strength 2 to 3 out of 5. The brown-banded El Triunfador Original is a different, broadleaf-wrapped blend.

cigars.about: The brown-banded original El Triunfador, first released in 2008 as a single broadleaf-wrapped lancero with a pigtail cap. A robusto followed in 2018 and a Cazadores size was announced in 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel describes the blend as essentially a Cabaiguan Maduro. Tatuaje calls it strong in flavor but medium in strength, and Neptune agrees, while Holt's lists it as full. Some shops sell it as El Triunfador Broadleaf.

cigars.about: A Tatuaje brand introduced in 2008 with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, made at My Father Cigars. The name means the riches in Spanish.
cigars.researchNote: Off Tatuaje's regular price list since 2017. It now appears as limited La Riqueza SE releases (2022, 2024, 2026), some with a San Andres wrapper under the Tuxtla name. Sizes shown are the original box-pressed line; the flavor notes come from the SE releases.

cigars.about: A Tatuaje brand introduced in 2009 whose name means both worlds. Each of its four sizes comes in two versions: No.1 with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper and No.2 with Ecuadorian Sumatra.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrappers: No.1 is Habano, No.2 is Sumatra. Taken off Tatuaje's regular price list in July 2017; not formally discontinued, but only offered in small batches and at events. Tatuaje rates it 3 out of 5 and describes it as medium to mild in flavor.

cigars.about: A Tatuaje cigar made entirely of U.S. Connecticut Broadleaf, wrapper, binder and filler, in the style of old American cigars. It debuted in 2011 and is rolled at My Father Cigars in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: All Connecticut Broadleaf, though not all of it is dark maduro leaf. Taken off Tatuaje's regular price list in July 2017; not formally discontinued, but only offered in small batches and at events. Tatuaje rates the strength 3+ out of 5.

cigars.about: Tatuaje's value line, a Cuban sandwich cigar that mixes medium and long filler to keep the price down. It wears a white band with red print and is often called the White Label.
cigars.researchNote: Not all long filler. Tatuaje only says the wrapper is from Ecuador: Halfwheel's 2025 report and Atlantic's spec say Ecuadorian Sumatra, but some listings say Ecuadorian Habano. Tatuaje says the line was created in 2006; Halfwheel dates the Nicaraguan-made version to 2011.

cigars.about: A Honduran-made version of Tatuaje's budget Series P, released in late 2025 from My Father Cigars' new factory in Honduras. It pairs a Garcia-grown Nicaraguan Habano wrapper with Honduran binder and mixed filler.
cigars.researchNote: Uses mixed medium and long filler, not all long filler. The band is white with blue print, where the Nicaraguan-made Series P uses red.

cigars.about: A 2022 extension of Tatuaje's Havana VI Verocu that uses a lighter Nicaraguan Corojo 99 Rosado wrapper, making it an all-Nicaraguan cigar. It adds a blue and silver second band and is made at My Father Cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's and Atlantic list it as medium to full, but Halfwheel's reviewer found it lighter than the regular Verocu, with only mild to medium strength. Neptune lists medium.

cigars.about: Escasos, Spanish for scarce, is Tatuaje's name for small-batch cigars rolled at the Garcia family's Florida factory. The best known are versions of the six original Brown Label sizes with a lighter wrapper, first shipped in 2019.
cigars.researchNote: Escasos is a collection; details here are for the six HUNTER-size cigars. They launched in 2019 with an Ecuadorian Habano Rosado Claro wrapper, and Tatuaje switched to Nicaraguan Corojo 99 shade grown for boxes dated April 2020 or later. Neptune still lists Ecuadorian Habano and mild strength.

cigars.about: A limited 2026 Tatuaje release in a single soft-pressed size with a covered foot and a Mexican San Andres wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco. It is made at My Father Cigars in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,000 boxes of 20 (40,000 cigars). Tuxtla is the name Tatuaje puts on its San Andres wrapped releases. Atlantic lists it as medium to full and Neptune as full, while Halfwheel's reviewer found the strength closer to medium.

cigars.about: A 2023 Tatuaje release that puts a Mexican San Andres wrapper on the blend of the 2010 Pork Tenderloin limited edition. It has a pigtail cap and covered foot and comes in 25-count bundles wrapped in butcher paper.
cigars.researchNote: Part of Tatuaje's Tuxtla series; the name is Spanish for pork loin. The original Pork Tenderloin used a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. Halfwheel found the strength building from medium to medium-full, while Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.about: A flavored version of La Aurora's budget Cazadores Claro, with an added light vanilla and cream sweetness. It is one of three Cazadores Flavors cigars announced in September 2026.
cigars.researchNote: This is a flavored cigar, built on the Cazadores Claro blend. No strength rating has been published. The 6 x 60 Gordo stays exclusive to the unflavored Cazadores lines.

cigars.about: A flavored version of La Aurora's budget Cazadores Maduro, with added cocoa and toasted cognac notes. It is one of three Cazadores Flavors cigars announced in September 2026.
cigars.researchNote: This is a flavored cigar, built on the Cazadores Maduro blend. No strength rating has been published. The 6 x 60 Gordo stays exclusive to the unflavored Cazadores lines.

cigars.about: A flavored version of La Aurora's budget Cazadores Nicaragua, with added rum and tropical spice notes. It is one of three Cazadores Flavors cigars announced in September 2026.
cigars.researchNote: This is a flavored cigar, built on the Cazadores Nicaragua blend. No strength rating has been published and the wrapper seed type is not stated. The 6 x 60 Gordo stays exclusive to the unflavored Cazadores lines.

cigars.about: A value-priced bundle cigar from La Aurora's Santiago Collection, brought to the U.S. in August 2026. It is a mixed-filler cigar, combining long filler with smaller pieces of tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed filler, not all long filler like La Aurora's core lines. No strength rating has been published. Sold in bundles, named for Santiago de los Caballeros.

cigars.about: A value-priced bundle cigar from La Aurora's Santiago Collection, scheduled to reach U.S. stores in September 2026. It is a mixed-filler cigar with an Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed filler, not all long filler like La Aurora's core lines. No strength rating has been published. Sold in bundles, named for Santiago de los Caballeros.

cigars.about: The classic Connecticut-wrapped León Jimenes line made by La Aurora in the Dominican Republic. It is a smooth, light cigar that has long sold better abroad than in the U.S.
cigars.researchNote: The maker gives no strength word and its strength gauge reads 65 out of 100, but retailers call it mild. Sizes come from a European retailer, where the line is simply called León Jimenes. Launch year is unclear.

cigars.about: A darker, fuller take on León Jimenes from La Aurora, with a Brazilian maduro wrapper and tobacco aged at least three years. It comes in thicker formats than the classic line.
cigars.researchNote: The maker gives no strength word; its strength gauge reads 75 out of 100. The maker lists a Dominican binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler, while one European retailer lists a Brazilian binder and four-country filler. Sizes come from that retailer.

cigars.about: A León Jimenes blend from La Aurora launched in 2011 to reintroduce the brand in the U.S., originally sold in black and gold tubes. It is a smooth cigar the maker suggests for newer smokers.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it mild to medium bodied. The maker's current blend (Ecuadorian binder, three-country filler) differs from halfwheel's 2011 prerelease listing of a Dominican and Nicaraguan binder over Dominican filler. Sizes are the three launch sizes.

cigars.about: A León Jimenes line La Aurora created in 2007 for the brand's 20th anniversary. The name comes from an extra 300 days of aging.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the wrapper as Cameroon (Ecuador). It gives no strength word; its strength gauge reads 60 out of 100. Sizes come from a European retailer, which also shows a limited Gran Toro (6 x 58).

cigars.about: The personal blend of La Aurora head Guillermo León, introduced in 2010 and also sold as Guillermo León Family Reserve. It is known for its double binder of Dominican and Cameroon leaf.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on strength: the maker calls it full bodied (80 out of 100 on its gauge), Neptune lists it as medium, and halfwheel's reviews ran from medium to strong. halfwheel and Neptune also list Brazilian leaf in the filler, which the maker does not. Also sold as Guillermo León Family Reserve.

cigars.about: A La Aurora line launched in 2012 to honor Fernando León, who ran the company from the 1950s until 2009. It is based on the personal blend once made only for him, his family and friends.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune rates it medium; the maker gives no strength word and its gauge reads 75 out of 100. The maker lists Dominican and Brazilian filler; halfwheel and Neptune add Peru. It is a rebrand of Fernando León's personal Don Fernando cigar. A limited box-pressed 6 x 54 was also made.

cigars.about: A single-size limited lancero from La Aurora released in 2022 for what would have been Fernando León's 100th birthday. Its Dominican corojo wrapper comes from a La Aurora growing project in Bonao, first harvested in 2008.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,000 boxes of 10. It is a separate cigar from the Fernando León Family Reserve and a different blend from the Fernando León Limited Edition. Strength is from the halfwheel review.

cigars.about: A limited belicoso from La Aurora released in 2021 in honor of Fernando León. Its corojo wrapper leaf was bought by León himself before he died in 2009 and sat unused until this project.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel reports 150 boxes of 15. It lists the wrapper origin as undisclosed, while Neptune calls it Dominican-grown corojo. Neptune lists it as medium strength, but halfwheel's reviewer found it mild to barely medium. It is a different blend from the Fernando León Family Reserve.

cigars.about: A low-priced, handmade long-filler line from La Aurora with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker gives no strength word; its strength gauge reads 50 out of 100. Sizes come from a European retailer's listing; the maker says there are seven formats but does not name them. That retailer describes the binder as Dominican, where the maker says Ecuador.

cigars.about: The maduro version of La Aurora's low-priced, handmade Imperiales line. The maker describes it as a sweet, creamy, mild cigar suited to beginners.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists a Brazilian wrapper and calls it mild bodied, though its strength gauge reads 50 out of 100. One European retailer describes the maduro wrapper as Ecuadorian. Sizes come from that retailer's listing.

cigars.about: The handmade, long-filler version of La Aurora's Príncipes, a brand best known in the Dominican Republic for machine-made cigars. It is a budget cigar with a Connecticut-type wrapper grown in Ecuador.
cigars.researchNote: This is the handmade long-filler Príncipes, not the machine-made Príncipes. The maker gives no strength word; its strength gauge reads 50 out of 100. Sizes come from a European retailer, which calls the binder Dominican where the maker says Indonesia.

cigars.about: The maduro version of La Aurora's handmade, long-filler Príncipes line. It is a budget cigar with an Indonesian maduro wrapper that adds a little sweetness.
cigars.researchNote: This is the handmade long-filler Príncipes, not the machine-made Príncipes. The maker gives no strength word; its strength gauge reads 50 out of 100. Sizes come from a European retailer's listing.

cigars.about: A darker, stronger version of Warped's Corto with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco that includes medio tiempo. It is made at NACSA in Esteli instead of Aganorsa, which makes the original Corto.
cigars.researchNote: Warped rates it full; halfwheel found the nicotine strength closer to medium. The X46 is box-pressed. The X54 is sold by Drop Cigar Club, the Warped founder's shop, but is not on Warped's brand page.

cigars.about: A Connecticut broadleaf cigar over Nicaraguan binder and filler, named for Warped founder Kyle Gellis's late Cane Corso. It was the first Warped line made at NACSA in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Warped rates it full; Neptune lists the Toro as medium. Sold in boxes of 14.

cigars.about: A Miami-rolled cigar that Kyle Gellis made to honor his father, blended as a nod to his father's two favorite Cuban brands. It is rolled at El Titan de Bronze in Little Havana at about 100 cigars a day, with entubado bunching and a triple cap.
cigars.researchNote: Warped's site says medium-plus; its Drop shop and Neptune say medium. It debuted in December 2014 as the limited Coronas de Luxe (5.5 x 42); the Regalos became the regular size in 2015. The 70th (6.5 x 48) and Grand Reynaldo 10th Anniversary (6 x 50) were limited.

cigars.about: A Dominican-made Warped line with an Ecuadorian habano desflorada wrapper, a dual binder and Nicaraguan filler. The name means Crocodile Island, a nickname for Cuba based on its shape.
cigars.researchNote: Warped lists the Corona Gorda as 5.5 x 46; halfwheel lists 5 5/8 x 46. Croc Bites is a box-pressed short torpedo, and the 6.5 x 54 Toro Grande is a limited size (1,500 boxes) with Peruvian pelo de oro added to the filler. Warped's site says medium; its Drop shop says medium-plus.

cigars.about: A limited version of Isla del Cocodrilo that swaps the habano wrapper for a light Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed leaf over the same binders and Nicaraguan filler. It came out in one 6.5 x 55 perfecto size.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,500 boxes of 15. Warped's Drop shop and Neptune call it medium; halfwheel found the nicotine strength mild to medium with fuller flavor. halfwheel also noted the wrapper is fragile.

cigars.factory: Aganorsa Leaf (Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A., Esteli)
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made entirely with Aganorsa tobacco and sold in one box-pressed belicoso size. Warped revived the name from a Havana brand dating to 1880 and positions it as one of its fuller blends.
cigars.researchNote: Gellis has said it is full for his portfolio but may not seem powerful to every smoker. The belicoso has a 109-style head.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro from Esteli made only with Aganorsa Leaf tobacco, offered in a single 6 x 44 corona. The filler leans on Esteli farms and the wrapper is shade-grown corojo from Jalapa.
cigars.researchNote: Warped rates it medium-plus to full. It was announced in June 2022 for release that fall.

cigars.about: A single-size Rothschild with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over mostly Dominican tobacco, meant as an everyday carry-along cigar. It was the second Warped cigar made at Tabacalera La Isla in Santiago.
cigars.researchNote: Warped lists it as medium-plus; Neptune lists it as medium. About 80 percent of the filler is Dominican.

cigars.about: An extension of Warped's Cloud Hopper line with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, made at NACSA in Esteli. It comes in the same two sizes as the original Cloud Hopper.
cigars.researchNote: So far it is listed only by Drop Cigar Club, the shop owned by Warped's founder, with no release date or production status published. The original Cloud Hopper has a Nicaraguan corojo wrapper and is made by Aganorsa.

cigars.about: Warped's first Dominican-made cigar and one of the first releases from Tabacalera La Isla, the Santiago factory opened by Hostos Fernandez Quesada. The name is slang for a very small cigar factory.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists it as medium; halfwheel found it medium-plus in strength with medium-full body. It launched in 2021 as regular production, but Drop Cigar Club, the Warped founder's shop, now calls it a discontinued blend.

cigars.about: A thin 6 x 38 petit lancero with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper over Aganorsa-grown Nicaraguan tobacco. The blend is based on one of the earliest Warped cigars, from when the brand was sold mostly through online forums.
cigars.researchNote: Only one size, The First, is confirmed; two more regular sizes were planned in 2018. It launched as regular production, but it is no longer on Warped's brand page and Neptune marks it discontinued.

cigars.about: A 4 x 50 petit robusto offshoot of Warped's La Hacienda that uses higher-priming Aganorsa leaves for more body and spice. The name borrows the top tier of the 1855 Bordeaux wine classification.
cigars.researchNote: This is one size of the La Hacienda line with a tweaked blend. Warped rates La Hacienda medium; halfwheel found First Growth medium-plus. It was announced in 2020 as a 4.5 x 48 but shipped in September 2021 as a 4 x 50.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made as a collaboration between Warped's Kyle Gellis and Max Fernandez Pujals of Casa Fernandez and Aganorsa. Each of them picked one of the two sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Warped announced in January 2025 that Futuro was discontinued. Sources disagree on the filler leaf: halfwheel says corojo 98 and corojo 99, Neptune says criollo 98 and corojo 99. Neptune's text calls it medium to full but its spec says medium; halfwheel found it just over medium.

cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro made by Aganorsa that first appeared as an exclusive for R. Field Wine Co. in Hawaii. It returned in 2022 as a one-time national release with the blend reworked toward more Jalapa tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists it as full; halfwheel found the 2019 release medium-full. The 2019 run was 400 boxes of 10 and the 2022 national release was 1,500 boxes of 25, described as the last for this size.

cigars.about: A limited Miami-rolled cigar that puts the light desflorada wrapper from Warped's La Colmena over the El Oso filler. Warped describes it as a reverse of La Colmena Black Honey.
cigars.researchNote: The seed type of the desflorada wrapper is not published. Neptune lists it as full, but halfwheel found both releases mild to medium. The 2021 release was 600 boxes of 20; the 2025 belicoso was 500 boxes of 10.

cigars.about: A limited version of Warped's La Colmena that uses the darker Ecuadorian habano oscuro wrapper from El Oso over the La Colmena Unico Especial binder and filler. It is rolled at El Titan de Bronze in Miami in one 5 x 48 belicoso size.
cigars.researchNote: Released three times: January 2015 (600 cigars), June 2017 and October 2023. Gellis has said it will be at least six years before it returns. halfwheel found the 2015 release medium-full and the 2023 release medium.

cigars.about: An offshoot of Warped's Flor del Valle, a Nicaraguan puro made by Aganorsa, with medio tiempo leaf added to the filler. It has shipped in small batches because workable medio tiempo is hard to get.
cigars.researchNote: It was announced as regular production but made in small batches: the 5 5/8 x 48 shipped in 2015, 2017 and 2019, and the 7 x 40 Lancero arrived in December 2020. A 5.5 x 52 was a 2016 exclusive for Corona Cigar Co. Neptune shows both sizes sold out.

cigars.factory: Aganorsa Leaf (Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A.)
cigars.about: The limited size of Warped's Maestro del Tiempo line, a Nicaraguan puro made by Aganorsa, with a tweaked blend that adds medio tiempo from Esteli. It is sold in cabinets of 100 with a secondary Seleccion de Warped band.
cigars.researchNote: Released in 2016, 2020 and fall 2026 (400 cabinets of 100), which Drop Cigar Club, the Warped founder's shop, calls the last time. Kyle Gellis calls it medium-plus; halfwheel found the 2016 batch under medium and the 2020 batch medium-full. The regular Maestro del Tiempo line was discontinued in 2025.

cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro made by Aganorsa that Warped shipped around the holidays, sold without bands in cabinets of 50. The name is Spanish for red lily.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel only confirms a Nicaraguan puro; the corojo wrapper and corojo and criollo filler come from Neptune. The 5.5 x 44 corona ran from 2015 to 2018 and the 2019 batch changed to a 6 3/8 x 42 lonsdale with a 109 cap. Neptune's text says medium to full; its spec says medium.

cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro made with Aganorsa tobacco and based on Warped's Flor del Valle blend. It debuted as a lancero and came back in 2023 as a toro called Moon Garden Especial.
cigars.researchNote: The 2018 lancero was limited to 650 boxes of 10. The 2023 Moon Garden Especial (1,000 boxes of 20) adds medio tiempo to the blend and was made at Aganorsa's Esteli factory, by then called Agricola Ganadera Nortena S.A.

cigars.about: A Connecticut Broadleaf robusto extra from Tatuaje, sold in bundles of 25 wrapped in butcher paper. It began in 2010 as a single-store exclusive and came back in 2025 in the original size and blend.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel's review of the 2025 release found medium to medium-plus strength; Neptune lists it as full. The 2010 original was 200 bundles for Gloucester Street Cigars in Boston; the 2025 run is 5,000 bundles of 25. Lomo de Cerdo is the San Andrés wrapped version.

cigars.about: A short, strong robusto from Tatuaje that started in 2009 as an exclusive for R. Field Wine Co. in Honolulu and returned as a national limited release in 2021. Its blend was the starting point for the Fausto and Avion lines.
cigars.researchNote: Every version is 4 3/8 x 52. Other wrappers: Reserva (Connecticut Broadleaf), Capa Especial (Ecuadorian Sumatra), Tuxtla (Mexican San Andrés, 2022) and Corojo (Nicaraguan corojo, 2025, 4,000 boxes of 25). The T stands for Thermonuclear and 110 is the length in millimeters.

cigars.about: A 4 x 50 short robusto based on the Tatuaje Brown Label blend. Cohete is Spanish for rocket, and the cigar started in 2006 as an exclusive for Tower Pipes & Cigars in Sacramento.
cigars.researchNote: Other wrappers: Reserva (Connecticut Broadleaf), Capa Especial (Ecuadorian Sumatra) and Corojo (Nicaraguan corojo, 2025, 2,000 boxes of 25). Neptune lists the Habano and Corojo as medium and the Broadleaf as full; halfwheel's 2013 review ended a bit over medium. Early runs were rolled in Miami.

cigars.about: A limited cigar Tatuaje makes only for retailers who order at the Premium Cigar Association trade show. The size and wrapper change with each edition, and Tatuaje donates 50 cents per cigar to the PCA.
cigars.researchNote: The blend changes by edition. Wrapper, strength and flavors here are the PCA 2025 Exclusive (shipped January 2026); PCA 2022 and PCA 2023 used an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, and Neptune lists the 2023 as full. Each edition ships months after its trade show.

cigars.about: A limited cigar Tatuaje has made since 2011 for members of the Tobacconists' Association of America, sold only through TAA retailers. The size changes each edition and most editions wear a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The blend changes by edition; details here are the TAA 2023 (2,500 boxes of 20, shipped April 2024). Seven of the first ten editions used Connecticut Broadleaf, and the TAA 2020 used Ecuadorian Sumatra. Neptune lists the 2023 as medium; halfwheel's reviewer found it mild in strength.

cigars.about: A lower-priced regular production Tatuaje line made with Los Angeles musician Andreas Contogouris, who performs as Sextooth. Each size is named after one of his songs.
cigars.researchNote: Strength and flavor words come from Neptune only. Began shipping to stores at the start of December 2025.

cigars.line: Old Man and the C Monster
cigars.about: A 2026 limited release that puts the all-Nicaraguan Creature blend from the Monster Series into Tatuaje's Old Man and the C format. Each coffin holds one lonsdale and a culebra of three twisted cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,300 boxes of six coffins. Neither the wrapper varietal nor a strength is published, only that the blend is all Nicaraguan; Neptune lists the full-size Creature from Tatuaje, the same blend, as full. Earlier Old Man and the C releases used the El Triunfador, Black Label and Fausto blends.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Varies by cigar: Nicaraguan Corojo 99, Ecuadorian Habano, Ecuadorian Sumatra or Connecticut Broadleaf
cigars.about: A joint release from My Father and Tatuaje marking 20 years of the García family making Pete Johnson's cigars. Each humidor holds 40 cigars: 20 blended by Johnson for My Father and 20 blended by the Garcías for Tatuaje.
cigars.researchNote: Four blends in two co-branded humidors of 1,500 each; no strength is published. Black (2024): Tatuaje for My Father in Nicaraguan corojo 99, My Father for Tatuaje in Ecuadorian habano. Red (2025): Tatuaje for My Father in Ecuadorian Sumatra, My Father Para Tatuaje in Connecticut broadleaf.

cigars.about: A soft box-pressed Tatuaje line made by José "Pepín" García and Pete Johnson exclusively for Holt's Cigar Company in Philadelphia. It was introduced in 2010.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only at Holt's, which does not publish the binder. Sizes here are as Holt's lists them now; a 2012 halfwheel list gave #2 as 6 5/8 x 54 and #3 as 6 1/4 x 52. The factory is as halfwheel lists it for the Broadleaf version, which shares the same filler.

cigars.about: The Connecticut Broadleaf version of the Tatuaje HCS, a soft box-pressed cigar made exclusively for Holt's Cigar Company. It uses the same Nicaraguan filler as the regular HCS under a darker wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only at Holt's, in one size. halfwheel reviewed the Broadleaf HCS #1 at its October 2012 debut under the name HCS #1 Reserva. Holt's lists it as full; halfwheel's review called it medium-full.

cigars.about: The original line from L'Atelier Imports, the sister company Pete Johnson started in 2012, often called LAT. It was the first known cigar to use an Ecuadorian Sancti Spiritus wrapper and is made by the García family.
cigars.researchNote: L'Atelier Imports was a separate company folded into Tatuaje in 2018. Sancti Spiritus is a Criollo and Pelo de Oro hybrid; Neptune's blurb calls the wrapper Ecuadorian Habano. The LAT46 uses a lighter priming of the wrapper and went only to select stores, and Selection Spéciale is the darker wrapper version.

cigars.about: A San Andrés wrapped line from L'Atelier, introduced in 2015 and described by Pete Johnson as the strongest L'Atelier blend at the time. It is named for the Bordeaux winery Château La Mission Haut-Brion, and the sizes are named for its 100-point vintages.
cigars.researchNote: Launched as La Mission du L'Atelier and now sold as La Mission L'Atelier. Neptune lists it as full strength, and Pete Johnson called it the strongest L'Atelier release at launch. The 1955, 1982 and 2003 sizes are on hiatus.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Sancti Spiritus (Roxy) or Connecticut Broadleaf (Maduro Roxy)
cigars.about: A 3 1/2 x 50 petit robusto added to the L'Atelier and L'Atelier Maduro lines in 2023. K.C. Johnson of L'Atelier named it for his dog Roxy, who died that year.
cigars.researchNote: This is one size of the L'Atelier and L'Atelier Maduro lines, not a separate blend. Boxes of 20 hold 10 of each wrapper. Wrapper category and origin here are for the original Sancti Spiritus version, a Criollo and Pelo de Oro hybrid; the Maduro Roxy is Connecticut Broadleaf.

cigars.about: A limited L'Atelier series built around pelo de oro filler tobacco grown by the García family, first released in 2015. It is named for the Burgundy wine region known for pinot noir, a grape as hard to grow as pelo de oro.
cigars.researchNote: Every size is a separate limited run; the newest is the '19 (2025, 1,500 boxes of 10), named as the next in the sequence, not for a vintage. The La Tâche releases use a lighter wrapper. Sancti Spiritus is a Criollo and Pelo de Oro hybrid, and strength is as Neptune lists it.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro from L'Atelier released once a year from 2013 to 2017, only to retailers who ordered at the industry trade show. It returned in 2022 as the Racine ERB perfecto.
cigars.researchNote: Each year is a different size and a separate limited run; the 2017 and 2022 runs were 500 boxes of 20. Strength varies by year: Neptune lists the ER17 as medium, while halfwheel found the ER16 medium-plus to medium-full. L'Atelier Imports was folded into Tatuaje in 2018.

cigars.about: A Honduran puro in the big-ring Asylum 13 family with a Honduran Corojo wrapper, made at Christian Eiroa's factory in Honduras. It is the Corojo counterpart to the original Nicaraguan Asylum 13.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as Asylum 13 Authentic Corojo. Launched at Tabacos Rancho Jamastran, then production moved to Eiroa's El Aladino factory. Neptune lists it Full; Holt's lists Medium-Full.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Barber pole of Candela and dark Nicaraguan Habano
cigars.about: A barber pole cigar in the Asylum 13 family that twists green candela with a dark habano wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco. The maker says it started as a 70x7 St. Patrick's Day cigar before more sizes were added.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrappers, so no single category fits; Candela is used here for the green stripe. Factory is per Neptune; halfwheel reported it as undisclosed in 2015.

cigars.about: The round version of Asylum's Medulla Oblongata blend, a Honduran puro with fourth and fifth priming Corojo wrapper from the Eiroa farm. The blend is close to Asylum 13 Corojo but uses higher primings.
cigars.researchNote: Medulla is the round cigar and Oblongata is the same blend box-pressed. They first shipped together in 50-count boxes, 25 of each.

cigars.about: The maduro version of the round Medulla, with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over Honduran Corojo binder and filler. It is made by CLE Cigar Co. in Danli, Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Medulla Maduro is the round cigar; Oblongata Maduro is the same blend box-pressed.

cigars.about: The box-pressed version of Asylum's Medulla Oblongata blend, a Honduran puro with a Corojo wrapper. It is the same blend and sizes as the round Medulla.
cigars.researchNote: Oblongata is box-pressed and Medulla is the same blend left round. They first shipped together in 50-count boxes, 25 of each.

cigars.about: The box-pressed maduro in the Medulla Oblongata family, with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over Honduran Corojo binder and filler. It is made by CLE Cigar Co. in Danli, Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Oblongata Maduro is box-pressed; Medulla Maduro is the same blend left round.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro billed at launch as the strongest and boldest Asylum. Every size is 8 1/2 inches long and only the ring gauge changes.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel and Neptune call it a Nicaraguan puro; Mike's Cigars lists an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. Neptune describes it as medium to full, Mike's lists Full. Factory is per Neptune; it was not disclosed at launch.

cigars.about: A flavored Asylum 13 line made to taste like a banana split, with a sweetened cap. CLE Cigar Co. makes it in Honduras and calls it a Honduran puro.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored cigar. The maker has not disclosed the blend beyond Honduran tobacco; Neptune lists the wrapper as Habano. Neptune lists it Medium, while halfwheel and Developing Palates found it mild to mild-medium.

cigars.about: A 2026 Asylum 13 line inspired by One Thousand and One Nights, with a maduro wrapper and packed in 10-count boxes. It is made at CLE's factory in Honduras and launched at an event in Marrakesh.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is secret: Christian Eiroa has only said it has a maduro wrapper. The maker describes it as medium to full; Neptune lists it Full.

cigars.about: The personal blend of Asylum co-founder Tom Lazuka, a maduro that was a runner-up blend from the Asylum Sensorium project. It became a regular release in 2026 and includes the brand's first maduro belicoso.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is secret; the company has only said it is a maduro that uses some Colombian tobacco. The maker gives no strength, and halfwheel's review found it mild to just under medium. Some listings leave the 13 out of the name.

cigars.about: A limited Asylum release named for Tuesday the 13th, the unlucky day in the Spanish-speaking world. It is made entirely of six-year-old Honduran Corojo tobacco and was sold in five-packs.
cigars.researchNote: The 2021 release was limited to 500 five-packs of each size. Neptune lists it Full, while halfwheel's review found it close to medium.

cigars.about: The thin-ring-gauge line in Asylum 867, a set of Honduran puros flavored by a steeping process and finished with a sweetened cap. It was first sold as Deadwood Tobacco Co. Chasing the Dragon Auntie.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored cigar; sources do not say what the flavor is. Renamed from Deadwood Tobacco Co. Chasing the Dragon in 2023 after a trademark dispute; that line began as a 2022 store exclusive. Retailers list the Corona as 5 3/4 x 46.

cigars.about: The large-ring-gauge line in Asylum 867, a set of Honduran puros flavored by a steeping process and finished with a sweetened cap. It was first sold as Deadwood Tobacco Co. Chasing the Dragon Midnight Oil.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored cigar. Renamed from Deadwood Tobacco Co. Chasing the Dragon in 2023 after a trademark dispute; that line began as a 2022 store exclusive. Neptune lists it Medium; halfwheel's review found the strength mild to just under medium.

cigars.about: The maduro-wrapped line in Asylum 867, a set of Honduran puros flavored by a steeping process and finished with a sweetened cap. It was first sold as Deadwood Tobacco Co. Chasing the Dragon Zero.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored cigar; sources do not say what the flavor is. Renamed from Deadwood Tobacco Co. Chasing the Dragon in 2023 after a trademark dispute; that line began as a 2022 store exclusive.

cigars.about: A flavored Asylum line introduced at the 2023 PCA show as a follow-up to Asylum 867. It has a maduro wrapper over Honduran binder and filler and is flavored by steeping.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored cigar. The maker has not said what the flavoring is or where the maduro wrapper comes from; retailers describe it as a Honduran puro.

cigars.about: A mild, budget-priced Asylum with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Honduran tobacco and a sweetened cap. It was made with newer smokers in mind.
cigars.researchNote: Sweet-tipped cigar. Launched as Insidious by Asylum; retailers now list it as Asylum Insidious Connecticut.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Asylum Insidious, using the same Honduran filler blend under a Mexican San Andres wrapper. Like the original it has a sweetened cap.
cigars.researchNote: Sweet-tipped cigar.

cigars.about: The original Asylum line from the brand's 2012 launch, a Nicaraguan puro blended by Christian Eiroa. It sits alongside the fuller Asylum 13.
cigars.researchNote: Often just called Asylum. It launched in 44x4, 50x6, 54x6 torpedo and 60x6; retailers now mainly carry the 44x4, 60x6 and 67x6. Neptune calls the wrapper a Nicaraguan maduro, Holt's a Habano.

cigars.about: Asylum's budget bundle cigar, a Nicaraguan puro made with mixed short and long filler. It was part of the brand's 2012 launch and is priced as an everyday smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed filler, sold in bundles. The maker described it as mild to medium; Neptune lists it Medium. The separate Schizo Maduro is a different blend made in Honduras with a San Andres wrapper.

cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro from Warped that combines elements of its Sky Flower and Moon Garden blends, made by AGANORSA Leaf in Esteli. It comes in one corona size with a rounded 109-style head.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 500 boxes of 50. No maker strength is published; the strength here comes from halfwheel's review, which found it mild to just under medium.

cigars.about: A limited Warped release whose blend and size were chosen by a vote of retailers who smoked three test blends. It is made at Tabacalera La Isla in the Dominican Republic and was sold through only 12 shops.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,000 boxes of 15. The official size is 5 7/8 x 52; Neptune lists it as a 6 x 52 toro. No maker strength is published: halfwheel and Neptune say medium, Atlantic Cigar says medium-full.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Esteli Criollo 98, Jalapa Corojo 99, Condega Corojo 99)
cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro from Warped built on AGANORSA tobacco from Esteli, Jalapa and Condega, with Esteli criollo 98 as the main filler leaf. It was sold only in numbered 200-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 250 numbered boxes of 200 cigars. No maker strength is published; strength and body come from halfwheel's review.

cigars.about: A Warped line that began as an exclusive for DROP Cigar Club, Kyle Gellis's own shop. The store release, Seleccion de Capital, is a box-pressed toro with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over AGANORSA Nicaraguan tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Details are for Seleccion de Capital, the store release: 500 boxes of 25 in 2023 and again in 2024. Strength is from Warped calling it full bodied. The earlier DROP-only Bits of Havana Robusto (5 x 48) is a different blend, a medium Nicaraguan puro with a Corojo 99 wrapper.

cigars.about: A three-part Warped series with one blend from each factory the company works with: El Titan de Bronze, Tabacalera La Isla and AGANORSA. The 4546, made at La Isla with a Dominican corojo wrapper, is the one that went to stores.
cigars.researchNote: Details are for the Seleccion Domain 4546 (red band), which shipped to stores in March 2023. The series has three different blends by band color: green from El Titan de Bronze (sold through DROP Cigar Club in 2022), red from La Isla, black from AGANORSA. Strength is from Cigar Aficionado.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Barber pole of Connecticut Broadleaf and Ecuadorian Desflorada
cigars.about: An event-only Warped cigar whose name is short for Radioactive Waste. It is a box-pressed torpedo with two wrappers rolled in a barber pole pattern, made at NACSA in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only in three-pack boxes at Warped events. It has two wrappers (dark broadleaf and lighter Ecuadorian leaf), so no single wrapper category applies. No strength or tasting notes are published.

cigars.about: An early Gellis Family Cigars release from Warped founder Kyle Gellis, sold through his DROP Cigar Club shop in boxes of 10. It has a closed foot, a Dominican corojo wrapper, and a year of cedar aging after being rolled in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only through Kyle Gellis's DROP Cigar Club shop, in boxes of 10, and now sold out. The shop lists strength as Medium+. Gellis Family Cigars is a separate brand, distributed by Warped.

cigars.about: The third blend in Alec Bradley's Chunk series of short, very thick, value-priced cigars, this one with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. It was scheduled to ship on October 1, 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Cigar Aficionado names the factory as HATSA, STG's plant in Danlí, Honduras; halfwheel listed it as undisclosed at launch. The maker rates it medium bodied and gives no separate strength.

cigars.about: The first stand-alone Chunk line from Alec Bradley, a set of short, very thick cigars with a Mexican maduro wrapper sold at a low price. It is made at STG's factory in Danlí, Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: It launched with two extra limited sizes, L (3 x 58) and 2XL (4 x 64 belicoso), which STG discontinued in August 2025. The maker rates it medium bodied and gives no separate strength.

cigars.about: The mellow member of Alec Bradley's Chunk series of short, very thick cigars, wrapped in Honduran-grown Connecticut seed leaf. It followed the Chunk Maduro in July 2025.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it mellow bodied and gives no separate strength.

cigars.about: A line marking Alec Bradley's 30th anniversary in 2026, blended from Honduran and Nicaraguan tobaccos and rolled at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras. Founder Alan Rubin and his sons Alec and Bradley picked the final blend.
cigars.researchNote: Also written as 30 Years. A fourth size, the Perfecto (6 3/4 x 54), is limited to 2,026 boxes of 10 for brick-and-mortar shops. The maker rates it medium to full bodied and does not publish the wrapper seed.

cigars.about: A lighter Alec Bradley blend with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Dominican and Mexican tobaccos, made in the Dominican Republic. It was introduced in 2025 in three sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it mellow to medium; Neptune lists it as medium. The factory name comes from Neptune and Cigar Dojo, and the maker does not publish it.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro based on a recipe from founder Alan Rubin's blend book, made for Alec Bradley at the Oliva factory in Estelí. It was the first new line chosen from that book after STG bought the brand.
cigars.researchNote: STG told retailers in June 2026 that the Corona size was discontinued, though the maker's site still lists it. The maker rates it medium to full bodied.

cigars.filler: Honduras (Jamastran Corojo, Trojes Criollo), Nicaragua (Jalapa Criollo)
cigars.about: A 2023 revival of Alec Bradley's Post Embargo name with a new, mostly Honduran blend and the packaging first designed for the 2015 original. It is rolled at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras and every size has a pigtail cap.
cigars.researchNote: This is a different blend from the original Post Embargo (2015), which was discontinued in March 2021. The maker rates it medium bodied and gives no separate strength.

cigars.about: A tweaked version of Alec Bradley's Prensado that adds a second, Honduran binder to the blend. The cigars are bunched entubado style, semi-pressed and finished with a triple cap at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: The maker and halfwheel say only that the wrapper is Honduran; Famous Smoke calls it Honduran Corojo. The maker rates it medium to full bodied, while Famous and Neptune list it as full. Halfwheel reported in March 2025 that STG discontinued the Churchill and Torpedo, though the maker still lists them.

cigars.about: A large-format Alec Bradley line introduced in 2005 that blends tobacco from five countries. It is made by Plasencia in Honduras and was given new bands in 2015.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium bodied, but Neptune lists it as full. The maker says only that the wrapper is Nicaraguan; Neptune calls it Nicaraguan Habano. STG discontinued the Nano size in August 2025.

cigars.about: A milder, lower-priced Alec Bradley line released in 2018 with a Honduran shade grown wrapper. Its gold medal band and box earned it the nickname People's Champ.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it mellow to medium; Neptune lists it as medium. The wrapper is shade grown in Honduras and looks like a Connecticut, but no source names the seed.

cigars.about: A tongue-in-cheek Alec Bradley release from 2014: one very thick 7 x 70 cigar with a pigtail cap, named as a joke on the slim lancero shape. It is a regular nationwide release, not a Texas exclusive.
cigars.researchNote: Cigar Aficionado and halfwheel report it is made by Plasencia at Tabacos de Oriente in Honduras, though Neptune lists Nicaragua. The maker does not state where it is rolled or the wrapper seed.

cigars.about: Alec Bradley's longest-running brand, a budget-priced, mellow long-filler cigar first made in the Dominican Republic in the early 2000s. The maker says the blend was reworked in 2023.
cigars.researchNote: The blend shown is the maker's 2023 rework, and the maker does not say where it is rolled; some retailers still list the older Dominican-made version. Halfwheel reports STG discontinued the Corona, Gigante and Torpedo in March 2025 and the Robusto, Toro and Churchill in June 2026, which covers every size listed.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Honduran Candela and Nicaraguan Oscuro (barber pole)
cigars.about: Alec Bradley's yearly St. Patrick's Day cigar, an offshoot of the Black Market line with green candela and dark Nicaraguan leaf rolled in a barber pole. It first came out in 2013 with a plain candela wrapper and became a barber pole in 2016.
cigars.researchNote: Released once a year in limited quantities ahead of St. Patrick's Day. Halfwheel has described the binder as Ecuadorian Sumatra. The maker rates it medium bodied and gives no separate strength.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Honduran Candela, Nicaraguan Oscuro and Nicaraguan Habano (triple barber pole)
cigars.about: The three-wrapper version of Alec Bradley's Filthy Hooligan, adding a Nicaraguan habano leaf to the candela and oscuro barber pole. It has been released each year around St. Patrick's Day since 2019, in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Released once a year in limited quantities. The binder and filler are said to match the regular Filthy Hooligan. The maker rates it medium bodied and gives no separate strength.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: US Broadleaf and Ecuadorian Habano (barber pole)
cigars.about: Alec Bradley's Halloween barber pole, a darker spin-off of the Filthy Hooligan that pairs broadleaf and habano wrappers with no candela. It has come out each fall since 2024.
cigars.researchNote: An annual limited release; the 2026 run is 1,950 boxes of 24. The two wrappers are different leaf types, so it does not fit one wrapper category cleanly. The maker rates it medium to full bodied.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A limited follow-up to Alec Bradley's Kintsugi, named for the Japanese idea of beauty in imperfection. It is a single 6 x 52 toro made by AJ Fernandez in Estelí, limited to 1,500 boxes of 16.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's site rates it medium to full bodied, while the launch press release called it medium to medium-plus. The maker now lists it among its past releases.

cigars.about: A limited size of Alec Bradley's Black Market Estelí, pressed into a diamond shape instead of a normal box press and given an extra leaf of ligero. It is made at the Plasencia factory in Estelí.
