cigars.researchNote: This is one limited size of the Black Market Estelí line, first shipped in October 2020 and brought back in 2021, each time as 1,500 boxes of 16. The wrapper seed is not published. The maker now lists it among its past releases.

cigars.filler: Honduras (Jamastran Corojo and Criollo), Nicaragua (Jalapa Criollo)
cigars.about: A one-size limited edition from 2023 marking five years since Alec Bradley's Magic Toast line was formally launched. It was made at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras in a run of 2,000 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,000 boxes of 10 in one 7 x 54 size. The medium strength rating is Neptune's alone. Neptune also calls the shape a perfecto where halfwheel says double robusto.

cigars.filler: Honduras (Jamastran and Trojes Criollo), Nicaragua (Jalapa Criollo 98)
cigars.about: A limited 6 x 52 toro that Alec Bradley made in 2023 for shops belonging to the Tobacconists' Association of America. It was rolled at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras in a run of 500 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel calls it the Alec Bradley TAA Edition; Neptune sells it as TAA Exclusive LE Toro. Sold only by TAA member shops. Neptune describes the wrapper as a Honduran maduro and lists the binder and filler simply as Honduran; the strength is Neptune's.

cigars.about: A 6 x 52 toro blended by Alec and Bradley Rubin for the My Cigar Pack subscription service and its partner shops. The cigars were rolled at Raíces Cubanas in July 2021 and aged before release in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as MadCap by Alec & Bradley, an exclusive for My Cigar Pack with 5,000 cigars made for 2022. The maker does not list it or give a strength rating.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Asylum's budget Schizo bundle line, made in Honduras by CLE Cigar Co. with a mix of short and long filler. It is sold in bundles of 20.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the blend. halfwheel and Cigars Direct say San Andrés wrapper, Neptune says Habano maduro; halfwheel says Honduran filler, Neptune Nicaraguan, Cigars Direct both. It is a mixed short and long filler cigar (Cuban sandwich).

cigars.about: A high-priced Honduran puro from Asylum built around Pinareño, a disease-prone Cuban-seed tobacco the Eiroa family rarely grows, plus their Jamastran corojo. Each cigar comes in its own coffin.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper varietal is not published; Neptune calls it a maduro. Retailers list it as full strength, but halfwheel's review found it just over medium. About 10,000 cigars per size are made each year, and halfwheel also lists the Asen 18 as 6 1/4 x 52/60.

cigars.about: A 9 x 90 Honduran puro that began as an April Fools' Day joke in 2021 and went into production after fans asked for it. It returns each year, since 2023 with Chinese zodiac packaging.
cigars.researchNote: The maker only says Honduran puro; Neptune describes a dark Honduran maduro wrapper and its 2026 listing says Honduran corojo. The blend is the same every year and only the packaging changes (2026 is Year of the Horse). Neptune rates the 2026 release medium, earlier ones full.

cigars.about: A 13 x 134 novelty cigar from Asylum, two inches across and holding more tobacco than 15 robustos. It is sold in boxes of two with a lighter.
cigars.researchNote: The company does not disclose the blend. Neptune lists it as full strength with an Ecuadorian wrapper, Honduran binder and Colombian and Honduran filler, which the maker has not confirmed. halfwheel lists it as regular production, while Neptune calls it a limited edition.

cigars.about: A yearly Asylum release sold only to shops that order at the PCA trade show. It started in 2021 as a Honduran puro with a habano hybrid wrapper and has come back with a new blend most years since.
cigars.researchNote: The blend changes by year: 2021 and 2022 were Honduran puros with a habano hybrid wrapper, 2023 and 2024 mostly undisclosed with South American tobacco. 2025 is a 6 x 52 only, Honduran habano over Honduran binder and Colombian and Honduran filler. Retailers list it as full; halfwheel found the 2021 medium-plus.

cigars.about: A 13-cigar sampler for Asylum's 13th anniversary holding two aged cigars from each of the six earlier anniversary blends (Seven through 12) plus one new Asylum 13 Anniversary. It closes out the anniversary series.
cigars.researchNote: This is a sampler of seven blends, not one blend. The new 13 Anniversary cigar has a Nicaraguan habano wrapper, Honduran binder and Colombian pinareño and Honduran filler; Neptune calls it medium-full. 500 boxes of the 11/18 version and 250 of the 7 x 70.

cigars.about: The 2024 limited edition marking Asylum's 12th anniversary, sold in two sizes. It was the first in the anniversary series packed in tubes instead of coffins.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is undisclosed beyond binder and filler tobacco from CLE's farm in an unnamed South American country. A 2023 preview said the wrapper and filler included pinareño with a corojo-seed binder, but that was not repeated at release. The 11/18 is a perfecto measuring 48/54/48.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Barber pole of Mexican San Andrés and habano
cigars.about: The 2023 limited edition for Asylum's 11th anniversary. It is a barber pole with two wrappers twisted together over Honduran binder and filler, each cigar in its own coffin.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrappers: Mexican San Andrés and a habano whose origin is not given. It is a clear break from the earlier anniversary blends, which were Honduran puros. The 11/18 is a perfecto measuring 48/54/48.

cigars.about: The 2022 limited edition for Asylum's 10th anniversary, a Honduran puro sold in two sizes with each cigar in a coffin. 1,300 boxes of 20 were made per size.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel and Cigars Direct call it a Honduran puro; Neptune lists a Nicaraguan maduro wrapper. Strength is disputed: halfwheel found it mild rising to medium, Neptune says medium, Cigars Direct lists both medium and full. Wrapper varietal is not disclosed.

cigars.about: The 2021 limited edition for Asylum's ninth anniversary, a Honduran puro made in Danlí and sold in two sizes, each cigar in a coffin. 1,000 boxes of 20 were made per size.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper varietal is not disclosed. Same Honduran puro story as the Asylum 8, but Asylum says the blend is different. Cigars Direct lists the strength as medium-full; the 11/18 is a perfecto measuring 48/54/48.

cigars.about: The 2020 limited edition for Asylum's eighth anniversary, a Honduran puro made in Danlí and sold in two sizes, each cigar in a coffin. 500 boxes of 20 were made per size.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper varietal is not disclosed. halfwheel's news story names the factory El Aladino and its review The CLE Factory. Strength and body are from halfwheel's review; the 11/18 is a perfecto measuring 48/54/48.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Serenity Now: Connecticut-seed; Insanity Later: Mexican San Andrés habano
cigars.about: Two different Asylum blends sold side by side in one 100-count box, 50 of each. Christian Eiroa blended Serenity Now as the smooth one and Insanity Later as the bold one.
cigars.researchNote: Two blends, so no single wrapper. Serenity Now: Connecticut-seed wrapper (origin not given) over Honduran and undisclosed South American tobacco. Insanity Later: Mexican San Andrés habano wrapper over an undisclosed blend.

cigars.about: A limited Asylum release named for the Detroit tradition on the night before Halloween, created by co-founder Tom Lazuka with part of the proceeds going to Detroit firefighters. It is a Honduran puro.
cigars.researchNote: Sizes and the corojo wrapper are from the 2022 release, about 1,000 five-packs per size, sold nationwide. The 2015 original was a Detroit-area exclusive in 6 x 52 and 5 1/2 x 46, made at El Aladino; the 2022 factory is not stated.

cigars.about: A limited Asylum release timed to each Friday the 13th and sold in five-packs. It is a sibling to the Asylum Martes 13, which marks the Latin American version of the superstition.
cigars.researchNote: Asylum does not release any blend information for this one. Sizes shown are the August 2021 release, 700 five-packs per size. The earliest version halfwheel mentions is from November 2020.

cigars.about: The third blend in Steve Saka's Mi Querida broadleaf family, which adds Honduran habano-seed filler to the recipe. It is made at NACSA in Esteli in small yearly runs.
cigars.researchNote: Ongoing but limited: about 3,500 boxes of 10 per size per year. Maker rates strength 8 of 10; halfwheel found the flavor full but the nicotine closer to medium. First sold in 2021 as a JR Cigar 50th anniversary exclusive.

cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A bolder, year-aged take on the original Sobremesa Solita blend, sold in one 6 1/4 x 46 size. Steve Saka built it to replace his discontinued Cervantes Fino vitola.
cigars.researchNote: One size within the Sobremesa Solita line, with the blend tuned a touch stronger. The maker calls it a special limited production, while halfwheel lists it as regular production. Maker rates Solita 5 of 10 and Neptune lists Medium; halfwheel found the Red finishing medium-full.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Esteli hybrid ligero, Condega, La Joya Esteli Criollo 98, Pueblo Nuevo criollo)
cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed shade (G2BW) with a Nicaraguan sun-grown Cuban-seed cap section
cigars.about: A two-wrapper offshoot of Sobremesa Brulee: the body wears Ecuadorian Connecticut shade while the cap and top inch are dark Nicaraguan sun-grown leaf. Made for Dunbarton by Joya de Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Tapa Negra means black lid: the dark leaf only covers the head, so the pepper lands on the lips. Steve Saka calls it a mild smoke and rates the base Brulee blend 3 of 10; Neptune lists Medium and halfwheel found it reaching medium at the end.

cigars.about: A variation on Dunbarton's bundled Umbagog that swaps in a lower-priming 2LS Connecticut broadleaf wrapper for a less sweet, more peppery smoke. Steve Saka made it as a nod to the Henry Clay cigars of the 1980s and 1990s.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists a San Andrés Negro binder for Umbagog; halfwheel lists the binder as Nicaraguan. Maker rates Umbagog 7 of 10 and calls Bronzeback the stronger version. Sold in 10-count bundles; the Robusto was added in 2025.

cigars.about: A spicier, bolder version of the Red Meat Lovers maduro blend in a 6 x 52 box-pressed toro. It is named for Nicaraguan open-flame street grilling and first appeared at a Red Meat Lovers Club dinner in March 2025.
cigars.researchNote: One size of the Red Meat Lovers line with a tweaked, stronger blend. Halfwheel calls it a regular production size; the maker calls it a special limited production. Maker rates the base line 7 of 10 and describes it as full-bodied.

cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The first Muestra de Saka release, a 6 x 52 toro Steve Saka blended around filler from all four of Nicaragua's main growing regions, each aged at least five years. It comes in an individual cedar coffin.
cigars.researchNote: Still made, in small batches. The maker lists a San Andrés Negro binder; halfwheel's 2017 review listed a Nicaraguan binder. The maker calls it medium bodied (5 of 10), while Neptune lists it as Full.

cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The second Muestra de Saka, a 6 x 48 built the old way with all of its filler from one farm in Jalapa. Steve Saka calls it one of his personal favorites.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper sources disagree: the maker lists Nicaraguan sun-grown, while halfwheel lists Ecuadorian habano. Maker rates strength 8 of 10 and Neptune says Full, but halfwheel found it fairly subdued. Still made, in small batches.

cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A 7 x 38 lancero that Steve Saka, no fan of the format, made after years of requests. The name is a hashtag for Now Leave Me The Hell Alone.
cigars.researchNote: Production stopped in August 2023, though the maker's site still lists it. The blend was undisclosed at launch; the leaf listed here is from the maker's current page. Maker rates strength 4 of 10, while Neptune lists it as Medium.

cigars.about: The first Muestra de Saka not blended by Steve Saka: it was created by Raul Disla of the NACSA factory after Saka challenged him to make a personal blend. A 6 x 52 toro built around layered pepper notes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the wrapper as Habano 2000 Sungrown without an origin; halfwheel and Neptune say it is Ecuadorian. Early coverage wrongly called the cigar a Nicaraguan puro. Maker rates strength 9 of 10, the strongest Muestra de Saka.

cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A box-pressed 6 5/8 x 48 with a spiral pigtail cap, first blended as the Owl Shop of Worcester's 75th anniversary cigar and then released nationally in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium-plus (6 of 10) and Neptune lists Medium; halfwheel found it building toward full in the second half. Still made, in small batches.

cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A 6 x 48 finished with a spiral cap shaped like a volcano. Steve Saka spent more than three years on the blend, which pairs an Ecuadorian habano wrapper with Nicaraguan-grown broadleaf, criollo and corojo filler.
cigars.researchNote: Maker rates strength 7 of 10 and halfwheel found it finishing medium-full; Neptune lists it as Full. First planned for 2021 and delayed until September 2023. Still made, in small batches.

cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: Steve Saka's experiment in sparing no expense on a single cigar: a 6 1/4 x 60 double perfecto rolled in molds he carved himself. It retails for about $100 a cigar and is made in very small yearly runs.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists a San Andrés Negro binder; halfwheel's 2018 review listed a Nicaraguan binder. Maker rates strength 7 of 10, while halfwheel put it just over medium. Unicorn versions of Sobremesa Brulee Blue and Mi Querida Black are separate cigars.

cigars.line: Muestra de Saka Lengua de Suegra
cigars.about: Dunbarton's first culebra, a bundle of thin cigars twisted together, shown at the 2026 PCA trade show. The name is Spanish for mother-in-law's tongue, a nickname for the snake plant.
cigars.researchNote: Scheduled to ship in October 2026 at $60 per culebra, in boxes of three. Halfwheel lists the size as 7 1/4 x 40 and Neptune as 7 x 40. Production numbers and strength have not been published.

cigars.about: A shorter, fatter 5 x 60 perfecto sibling to the Muestra de Saka Unicorn, teased by Steve Saka for years and finally shown at the 2026 PCA trade show.
cigars.researchNote: Scheduled to ship in October 2026 at $50 a cigar in 12-count boxes, offered only to retailers who placed PCA orders. The leaf listed is from halfwheel's show coverage; Saka had not confirmed a full blend, production numbers or strength.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua, plus Black Cavendish, Golden Virginia and Burley pipe tobaccos
cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: One of the four original StillWell Star cigars, which blend Cornell & Diehl pipe tobacco into a handmade Nicaraguan cigar. This is the sweet aromatic one, finished with a sweetened cap.
cigars.researchNote: Retired under this name in the 2026 StillWell Star revamp: the same blend continues as StillWell Star Aromatic Dulce Maduro in a toro and a petit robusto. The maker calls it mild-medium (4 of 10), while Neptune lists it as Full. Pipe tobacco blended by Jeremy Reeves of Cornell & Diehl.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua, plus Cavendish Burley and Virginia pipe tobaccos
cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The StillWell Star Holiday 2022 limited edition brought back in 2024 as a regular offering under a new name. An aromatic pipe-tobacco cigar without the sweetened cap used on Aromatic No. 1.
cigars.researchNote: Same blend as the 2022 Holiday release. It is not part of the 2026 revamped StillWell Star line, and Saka said the earlier blends will not be remade once stock is gone. Maker rates it 4 of 10; halfwheel found the Holiday 2022 version medium-plus to medium-full.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua, plus Burley, Turkish and Cypriot Latakia pipe tobaccos
cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: One of the four original StillWell Star cigars, built around an English-style pipe mixture heavy on Cypriot Latakia. Steve Saka has said the English style is his personal favorite.
cigars.researchNote: Dropped in the 2026 StillWell Star revamp; a tweaked version with a sweetened cap replaced it as English Dulce Maduro. The maker's launch sheet called it medium-full (6 of 10 on its site), but halfwheel found the nicotine at medium or less, with the pipe tobacco showing as an accent.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua, plus Bright Virginia, Red Virginia and St. James Parish Perique pipe tobaccos
cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: One of the four original StillWell Star cigars, pairing a Virginia and Perique pipe mixture with Nicaraguan cigar leaf. It starts as the mildest of the set and turns spicy late as the Perique comes through.
cigars.researchNote: Dropped in the 2026 StillWell Star revamp with no direct replacement; it will not be remade once stock is gone. The maker's launch sheet called it medium-plus and its site rates it 7 of 10, while Neptune lists it as Full.

cigars.filler: Dark air-cured cigar leaf, plus stoved Red and Golden Virginia, Oriental and Latakia pipe tobaccos
cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: One of the four original StillWell Star cigars, using a navy-style crumble cake of stoved Virginias with Orientals and Latakia alongside dark cigar leaf.
cigars.researchNote: Dropped in the 2026 StillWell Star revamp with no direct replacement; it will not be remade once stock is gone. The maker calls it medium (5 of 10), while Neptune lists it as Full.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua, plus aromatic pipe tobaccos that change by year (Cavendish Burley and Virginias)
cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed shade (2023 onward; the 2022 edition used Ecuadorian Habano)
cigars.about: A yearly limited StillWell Star made for the holidays since 2022, following the pipe world's habit of one-off holiday mixtures. Each year's cigar is a mild, aromatic pipe-tobacco blend, labeled by year (Y2022, Y2023 and so on).
cigars.researchNote: The blend and wrapper change by year. Y2022 had a habano wrapper and later became Aromatic No. 22; halfwheel found it medium-full. Shade-wrapped editions since 2023 are milder: the maker rates Y2024 3 of 10 and Neptune lists 2023 and 2025 as Mild.

cigars.about: One of three blends in Alec Bradley's triangle-pressed Trilogy series, which first ran from 2002 to 2010 and came back in 2021 as a limited release. This one wears a Honduran corojo wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Specs are for the 2021 return: 2,000 boxes of 10 per blend, close to but not the same blend as the 2002 original. A 5 x 50 robusto was a Smoke Inn store exclusive. Halfwheel found strength building from medium to near full.

cigars.about: The maduro blend in Alec Bradley's triangle-pressed Trilogy series, brought back in 2021 as a limited release. It uses a Nicaraguan Jalapa wrapper over a Honduran binder.
cigars.researchNote: Specs are for the 2021 return: 2,000 boxes of 10, close to but not the same blend as the 2002 original. Strength comes from a single Developing Palates review. A 5 x 50 robusto was a Smoke Inn store exclusive.

cigars.about: The Cameroon-wrapped blend in Alec Bradley's triangle-pressed Trilogy series, brought back in 2021 as a limited release. The wrapper sits over a Honduran binder and Honduran and Nicaraguan fillers.
cigars.researchNote: Specs are for the 2021 return: 2,000 boxes of 10, not the exact 2002 blend. Sources say only that the Cameroon wrapper is grown in Africa, no country named. Strength is from one Developing Palates review, which called it slightly below medium.

cigars.about: A Honduran-made Alec Bradley line named for the Coyol farm in Trojes, Honduras, where its wrapper and part of its binder and filler are grown. It launched at the 2014 trade show.
cigars.researchNote: Discontinued by parent company STG in March 2025, though still shown on the maker's site. The 2014 launch also included a 5 1/2 x 58 Belicoso. Neptune's description calls it medium to full.

cigars.about: An all-Nicaraguan take on Alec Bradley's Tempus line, introduced in 2015 with a Jalapa wrapper and a double binder. Although the tobacco is all Nicaraguan, it was rolled in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Maker's site says medium to full; at launch the company called it medium, and Neptune lists medium. Neptune lists the origin as Nicaragua, but halfwheel says it is rolled in Honduras. Discontinued by STG in March 2025; sizes first carried Tempus names like Medius 6.

cigars.about: A pricier Alec Bradley line from 2013 made only in figurado shapes with a rounded head and tapered foot, all called Punta Lanza. It is remembered for a launch stunt that sent the cigars up on a weather balloon.
cigars.researchNote: Discontinued in March 2021, though still shown on the maker's site. The maker's site lists No. 8 as 6 1/2 x 52 and a Honduran-only binder; halfwheel and Neptune list 6 1/2 x 58 and a Honduran and Nicaraguan binder. Neptune rates it full.

cigars.about: Alec Bradley's birth announcement cigars, sold as It's a Boy and It's a Girl in 20-count keepsake boxes with a picture frame. A mellow toro meant for handing out to friends and family.
cigars.researchNote: Maker says Honduran Connecticut wrapper and mellow to medium; Neptune lists a Habano wrapper, undisclosed filler and mild strength. Both versions were discontinued by STG in August 2025.

cigars.about: A four-country Alec Bradley blend from 2015, put together by Ralph Montero, with a Honduran corojo wrapper over a Costa Rican binder. Cigar Aficionado ranked it No. 15 on its 2015 list.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is disputed: the maker says medium, Cigar Aficionado lists mild to medium, and Mike's and Holt's list medium to full. Still shown on the maker's site but sold out at retailers, with no discontinuation notice found.

cigars.about: A 2015 offshoot of Alec Bradley's all-Nicaraguan Nica Puro that keeps the same binder and fillers but swaps in a lighter rosado wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Where it is rolled is disputed. Blind Man's Puff and Neptune name Raices Cubanas, a Honduran factory, but Holt's and Neptune's origin field say Nicaragua, and halfwheel says the original Nica Puro was made at Plasencia in Nicaragua. Neptune rates it full; the company and Holt's say medium to full.

cigars.about: A Honduran-made Alec Bradley blend from 2009, created to honor the fathers of three company executives and sold in sizes with code names like VR1 and BX2. Cigar Aficionado ranked the original VR1 size No. 16 on its 2009 list.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's cites a 94-point Cigar Aficionado rating, but the magazine's own 2009 Top 25 page shows 92 points. Not on the maker's current site and out of stock at Holt's, with no discontinuation notice found. Not the same cigar as Alec Bradley Family Blend The Lineage.

cigars.about: A budget Alec Bradley cigar made Cuban-sandwich style with mixed filler under an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. It is a mild everyday value smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed filler, not long filler; the binder is not published. The Ecuador wrapper origin and Nicaragua as the country come from Holt's alone. Not on the maker's current site and out of stock at Holt's and Neptune, with no discontinuation notice found.

cigars.about: A 2013 cigar named for the Raices Cubanas factory in Danli, Honduras, which rolled many Alec Bradley lines. The factory's Endemano family led the blend and Alec Bradley distributed it.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel calls it a joint project that Alec Bradley distributes rather than a true Alec Bradley-branded cigar; 1941 is factory owner Romay Endemano's birth year. Mike's lists medium, Holt's medium to full. Sold out at Holt's; no discontinuation notice found.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut (Natural), Nicaraguan Habano or Nicaraguan Corojo, depending on version
cigars.about: A low-priced Alec Bradley line made Cuban-sandwich style with long and short filler at the Raices Cubanas factory in Honduras. It comes in three wrapper versions: Natural, Habano and Corojo.
cigars.researchNote: Three wrapper versions, so there is no single wrapper, and the binder and filler vary by version. Strength is disputed: Mike's lists medium and adds Colombian filler, while Neptune calls the Natural and Habano mild. STG discontinued the Natural Robusto in August 2025; the other sizes were not on that list.

cigars.about: An all-Nicaraguan corojo blend from Gran Habano, rolled at the Rico family's factory in Honduras and built to be stronger than the Corojo #5. It launched in 10-count leather travel cases.
cigars.researchNote: Limited production: Gran Habano's site says 16,000 cigars a year, its 2025 and 2026 catalogs say 60,000. The maker calls it full-bodied, but Neptune lists medium and halfwheel's reviewer found little strength. The 7 x 46 Corona Especial is a limited run of 200 boxes of 10.

cigars.about: George Rico's first blend made outside his own factory, rolled in the Dominican Republic by TabaDom, Davidoff's Dominican operation. It uses Ecuadorian habano wrapper and binder over fillers from three countries.
cigars.researchNote: Gran Habano names TabaDom but not which of its two factories; halfwheel thinks O.K. Cigars is likely. Limited to about 1,000 boxes per size a year and sold through roughly 200 retailers.

cigars.about: Gran Habano's 20th anniversary cigar, made in Danli, Honduras with a four-year-aged Jalapa wrapper and rested two years after rolling.
cigars.researchNote: Sold by most retailers as XX Aniversario Edicion Limitada. Despite the name it is an ongoing release, offered to about 200 retailers; the first batch was 4,000 boxes per size.

cigars.about: A San Andrés maduro follow-up to Gran Habano's 20th anniversary cigar, shown at PCA 2024 in a single 6 x 54 size and sold in 10-count leather travel cases.
cigars.researchNote: Previewed at PCA 2024 and slated to ship that May as 500 leather cases of 10. It is not on Gran Habano's site or in its 2025 and 2026 catalogs, and no source gives the strength or where it is rolled.

cigars.about: A cedar-wrapped George Rico blend in Gran Habano's S.T.K. series, made in Danli, Honduras with a Nicaraguan shade grown corojo wrapper and a dual habano binder.
cigars.researchNote: Gran Habano's spec sheet and Neptune say medium, while the launch announcement called it full-bodied. S.T.K. stands for Stay True Kid.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Connecticut (Black) or Nicaraguan Habano (Habano White)
cigars.about: A limited S.T.K. release from George Rico with box art by Colombian-American street artist Mas Paz. It comes in two versions over the same Nicaraguan binder and filler, one in Ecuadorian Connecticut and one in Nicaraguan habano.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrappers under one name: Gran Habano lists the Connecticut version (Black) as mild and the Habano version (White) as medium. The 2015 release was rolled in Miami; the maker does not say where it is made now.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro from George Rico with an oily, reddish habano hybrid wrapper. It began in 2011 as one of the first S.T.K. small batch projects.
cigars.researchNote: Gran Habano also files it under G.A.R. and does not say where it is rolled. Its site and 2026 catalog disagree on the Gran Robusto size (6 x 52 or 5 x 52), so that size is left out. S.T.K. is billed as limited release, but Opium is still in the 2026 catalog.

cigars.about: A cigar made entirely of American-grown tobacco, including Kentucky fire-cured leaf, and rolled at George Rico's factory in Miami.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper; Blind Man's Puff listed Connecticut Habano in 2013. It launched as regular production and is still on Gran Habano's site, but it is missing from the 2025 and 2026 catalogs. No vitola names are given for the three sizes.

cigars.about: A value-priced Nicaraguan puro in George Rico's G.A.R. series, rolled in Honduras and sold in large ring gauges from 50-count trays.
cigars.researchNote: Gran Habano says medium to full-bodied in its description but Full on the spec sheet; Blind Man's Puff reviewers rated it medium. Still on the maker's site but missing from its 2025 and 2026 catalogs, so it may no longer be made.

cigars.about: A George Rico blend in the G.A.R. series with Ecuadorian corojo wrapper and binder over Nicaraguan filler, sold in boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not say where it is rolled or when it launched. Its site and 2026 catalog disagree on two sizes, so they are left out: Gran Consul (6 x 60 or 4 3/4 x 60) and Robusto Grande (garbled online, 5 x 52 in the catalog).

cigars.about: A budget-minded Nicaraguan puro from Gran Habano, rolled in Honduras and sold in boxes of 50.
cigars.researchNote: Gran Habano has not said which Nicaraguan leaf varieties it uses. Its website lists four sizes, but its 2026 catalog and halfwheel also list the 6 x 66 Czar.

cigars.about: An unbanded, value-priced Nicaraguan puro from Gran Habano, known for its closed foot wrapped in a lighter leaf. It is sold from boxes of 50.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers often list it as Persian King Natural. Halfwheel dates the line to around 2010, so the year is approximate.

cigars.about: The maduro version of the unbanded Persian King, a Nicaraguan puro with a sun grown wrapper and a lighter leaf covering the foot.
Gran Habano's first all-Honduran cigar, made with tobacco from the Rico family's own farms. It is also the first banded cigar in the Persian King family.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,000 boxes of 50; halfwheel's trade show report says that is per year. It does not share the Nicaraguan blend or the unbanded look of the other Persian King cigars.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan Corojo and Ecuadorian Connecticut (barber pole)
cigars.about: An unbanded barber pole offshoot of the Persian King that twists a dark Nicaraguan corojo leaf with a light Ecuadorian Connecticut leaf. It has been released in limited runs.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrappers, so no single wrapper type applies. First run in November 2020 was 500 boxes of 50 per size; it returned in October 2023. Gran Habano lists it as full, though halfwheel's reviewer found it closer to medium.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan Corojo with Ecuadorian Connecticut caps
cigars.about: A double-capped 6 x 60 Persian King with a rounded head at one end and a tapered one at the other, each finished in Ecuadorian Connecticut. It is meant to be lit from either end.
cigars.researchNote: Gran Habano lists the main wrapper as Nicaraguan corojo; halfwheel says Nicaraguan habano. The maker gives the strength only as smooth and bold, depending on which end is lit; halfwheel's reviewer found it medium to medium-full.

cigars.about: An aged, limited version of the Corojo #5 made from the top tenth of that tobacco, aged seven to eight years before rolling and about six years after. The cigars were rolled in 2012 and released in 2018.
cigars.researchNote: Also called Corojo #5 Gran Reserva 2012. The year is when the cigars were rolled, not released. The maker does not name the wrapper variety; about 200,000 cigars were made.

cigars.about: The fourth Gran Reserva release, an aged and limited take on the Corojo #5 made with aged Nicaraguan tobacco at the Rico family's factory in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the filler: the maker and halfwheel say all Nicaraguan, while Blind Man's Puff lists 2005 Costa Rican corojo under a 2002 Nicaraguan corojo wrapper and binder. The maker says full; Blind Man's Puff reviewers rated it medium to medium-strong.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Habano ligero from Jalapa and Esteli)
cigars.about: A limited Gran Reserva release built on aged Nicaraguan tobacco from 2003 to 2005 crops, rolled in Danli, Honduras and rested before it reached stores in late 2012.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,200 boxes of 20 per size. The leaf detail comes from halfwheel; the maker lists only Nicaraguan corojo wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler.

cigars.about: A limited, aged Gran Reserva release using a 2003 Jalapa habano wrapper and binder. The cigars were rolled in Danli, Honduras and rested more than two years before reaching stores in late 2012.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,200 boxes of 20 per size. The maker lists Nicaraguan filler; halfwheel reported aged Colombian tobacco in the filler as well. Halfwheel gave the Churchill as 6 7/8 x 50.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua, plus Cornell & Diehl pipe tobacco (Black Cavendish, Golden Virginia, Burley)
cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A handmade cigar from Steve Saka's Dunbarton Tobacco & Trust that mixes Cornell & Diehl aromatic pipe tobacco into the filler and has a sweetened cap. It is the old StillWell Star Aromatic No. 1 blend under a new name, part of the 2026 revamp of the line.
cigars.researchNote: Same blend as the original Aromatic No. 1 from 2021, renamed in 2026 and sold by Neptune as Aromatic Dulce Dark. Despite the Maduro name the wrapper is Ecuadorian Habano. Dunbarton's own strength meter puts the blend at 4 out of 10, while Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua, plus Cornell & Diehl pipe tobacco (Black Cavendish, Golden Virginia, Red Virginia)
cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A handmade cigar from Dunbarton Tobacco & Trust with Cornell & Diehl aromatic pipe tobacco in the filler, a light Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper and a sweetened cap. It is a new blend for the 2026 StillWell Star revamp, built from the earlier Holiday releases.
cigars.researchNote: New 2026 blend described as a hybrid of the earlier StillWell Star Holiday releases. Contains pipe tobacco and has a sweetened cap, so tell guests it is not a traditional cigar. Neptune lists it as mild and Corona Cigar as mild to medium.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua, plus Cornell & Diehl pipe tobacco (caked Latakia, Turkish, Burley)
cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A handmade cigar from Dunbarton Tobacco & Trust that adds an English style pipe blend with Latakia from Cornell & Diehl to Nicaraguan filler, finished with a sweetened cap. It is a reworked version of the earlier StillWell Star English No. 27.
cigars.researchNote: A tweaked version of the original English No. 27, now with a sweetened cap. Despite the Maduro name the wrapper is Ecuadorian Habano. Neptune sells it as English Dulce and lists it as medium.

cigars.about: The cigar Steve Saka made to mark ten years of Dunbarton Tobacco & Trust, offered in one corona gorda size. It is the company's first national release with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper and was blended to taste different from the rest of the lineup.
cigars.researchNote: Announced in 2025 for the company's 10th anniversary but it did not ship until February 2026. Halfwheel reports it is a regular production cigar, not a limited edition. Neptune lists the binder as Mexican San Andrés.

cigars.binder: Mexico San Andrés Negro (Tom's Blend), Ecuador Habano Rosado (Michelle's Blend)
cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, Nicaragua (Tom's Blend); Nicaragua, USA Pennsylvania (Michelle's Blend)
cigars.factory: Nicaragua American Cigars S.A. (Tom's Blend), Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A. (Michelle's Blend)
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Two blends: Nicaraguan Capa Camaleón (Tom's Blend) and Mexican San Andrés Negro Cultivo Tonto (Michelle's Blend)
cigars.about: The second cigar in Dunbarton's Year of series, which honors friends of the company instead of zodiac animals. Each box of 14 holds seven each of two different 6 x 48 blends made for Alaska couple Tom and Michelle Pauser.
cigars.researchNote: Two different cigars in one box, so there is no single wrapper: Tom's is a Nicaraguan broadleaf and habano 2000 hybrid leaf, Michelle's is a reworked Sin Compromiso Paladin de Saka. Limited to 2,700 boxes of 14. Neptune lists medium, but halfwheel found Tom's Blend medium-plus or stronger.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The first release in Dunbarton's Year of series, named for longtime company volunteer Chris Duque instead of a zodiac animal. Steve Saka built it as a mix of Duque's two favorites, Sobremesa Solita and Todos Las Dias.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,000 boxes of 14 and shipped in April 2025. Strength and body are from halfwheel's review, which called the flavor full.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: Dunbarton Tobacco & Trust's first cigar made only for markets outside the United States, a 6 x 50 toro with a coiled cap. Steve Saka has said later Overseas releases may use different blends.
cigars.researchNote: International exclusive, not officially sold in the US, though Smoke Inn has brought some in from overseas distributors. Strength and body are from halfwheel's review, which found it medium for most of the cigar and stronger in the final third. Smoke Inn lists it as medium-full.

cigars.about: A new corona blend from Steve Saka that is only available inside Dunbarton's Cosmic Corona Sampler, a 14 cigar box of seven different 5 x 44 coronas. Saka developed it as a possible Muestra de Saka release that never came out on its own.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only as part of the Cosmic Corona Sampler, two per box, not on its own. Binder, filler and factory have not been published. Halfwheel listed the sampler as shipping in November 2026.

cigars.about: A new corona blend from Steve Saka that is only available inside Dunbarton's Cosmic Corona Sampler, a 14 cigar box of seven different 5 x 44 coronas. Like its partner the Corona Alpha, it was first developed as a possible Muestra de Saka release.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only as part of the Cosmic Corona Sampler, two per box, not on its own. Binder, filler and factory have not been published. Halfwheel listed the sampler as shipping in November 2026.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro that Steve Saka made for Famous Smoke Shop's 80th anniversary and that is sold only by that retailer. It started as a small 2019 run of box-pressed toros and has been brought back since because of demand.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke Shop exclusive. The 2019 and 2020 runs were limited 6 x 52 toros; it became an ongoing line in four box-pressed sizes in 2024, though Famous currently lists only the robusto. Famous rates it full, while Cigar Coop's review found it medium.

cigars.about: A store exclusive made by Dunbarton Tobacco & Trust for Rocky's Cigars in Syracuse, New York. It is an offshoot of the Muestra de Saka Unstolen Valor with the filler proportions changed, sold in gray-banded boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Rocky's Cigars exclusive released in small batches most years since 2020, including 2026. The Churchill is the main size; the 2022 boxes added two 6 x 54 torpedoes and the 2023 boxes two 4 3/4 x 60 Depth Charge perfectos. Strength is Rocky's own listing of medium to full.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 92), Nicaragua (Condega, Jalapa, Ometepe), USA (Connecticut broadleaf)
cigars.about: A 6 x 48 cigar with a coiled fiddlehead cap that Dunbarton Tobacco & Trust makes only for retail members of the Cigar Association of New Hampshire, its home state. Part of the proceeds goes to the association.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only by New Hampshire shops that belong to the Cigar Association of New Hampshire; the first run was a little over 700 boxes of 10. It was Dunbarton's first cigar with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. No strength rating is published.

cigars.about: A small-batch branch of Steve Saka's Mi Querida broadleaf line. It began as the event-only Pataperro and then came to Smoke Inn in Florida as a 6 x 52 torpedo with a stronger ligero broadleaf wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Smoke Inn exclusive torpedo first sold in November 2024 (600 bundles of 10); it returned in late 2025 renamed Mi Querida The Emerald Fish. The blend details are for the torpedo, which Saka says is revised and stronger than the event-only Pataperro. No strength rating is published.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A box-pressed San Andrés-wrapped line made for Fratello at Joya de Nicaragua. It first appeared in a 2019 sampler and became a regular line in 2020 after smokers picked it over the Sorella blend.
cigars.researchNote: The sizes are box-pressed and were launched under the name Prensado. halfwheel lists the Toro at 6 1/2 x 54, Neptune at 6 1/4 x 54. Neptune rates it medium in strength and calls it medium to full bodied.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped version of the Arlequín, made at Joya de Nicaragua. It keeps the same Ecuadorian binder and Nicaraguan and Peruvian fillers under a lighter Ecuadorian wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Strength and flavor notes come from Neptune, which calls it mild to medium bodied. A 7 x 50 Churchill is sold only in the mixed Edizione di Carnevale box.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A space-themed line from Fratello that flips the make-up of the original Navetta, putting a Nicaraguan wrapper over an Ecuadorian binder. It is made at Joya de Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Fratello ended production of the Corona Gorda size in May 2023, though some retailers still have it. The Boxer is a box-pressed torpedo added in 2019.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano ligero, andullo), Nicaragua (Estelí ligero), USA (Pennsylvania ligero)
cigars.about: A large, ligero-heavy cigar made for Fratello at La Aurora. It launched in 2019 as a Texas-only release and went nationwide in 2021.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on strength: founder Omar de Frias described it as full bodied at launch, while Neptune lists it as medium. The Toro was sampler-only until boxes shipped in 2023.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A Joya de Nicaragua-made blend that debuted alongside the Arlequín in a 2019 sampler. It was kept for markets outside the U.S. from 2020 until the 6 x 50 Toro returned to American stores in 2023.
cigars.researchNote: Only the 6 x 50 Toro is sold in the U.S. The Robusto and the 6 1/2 x 54 Toro are international sizes. No published strength rating was found.

cigars.about: A Dominican puro made at La Aurora and the first release in Fratello's Puro Collection of single-country cigars. The name marks the year the Dominican Republic gained independence from Spain.
cigars.researchNote: Fratello calls it medium to full bodied, while Neptune lists it as medium and halfwheel's reviewer found it milder. Shown at PCA 2025 but first shipped in February 2026, in batches of 3,000 cigars. The wrapper variety is not published.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A reworked take on Fratello's Bianco line with a new binder and filler under the same San Andrés wrapper. It is made at Joya de Nicaragua in one box-pressed perfecto size.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 500 boxes of 10, with 400 for the U.S. The only size is the Riserva, a 6 x 58 box-pressed perfecto.

cigars.about: A Churchill capped at both ends and blended to be smoked from either one, starting milder from one end and stronger from the other. It was made at La Aurora as a one-time release.
cigars.researchNote: Fratello styles the name ViceVersa. One-time release of 2,000 packs of 12, followed in 2026 by Smooth and Strong. Neptune lists it as full, but the strength depends on which end is lit.

cigars.about: The follow-up to Vice Versa: a double-capped Churchill made at La Aurora that can be smoked from either end, with a milder end and a stronger end.
cigars.researchNote: 12,000 cigars were made for 2026, sold in six-packs, and Fratello says it plans to release it annually. No single strength is published because it depends on which end is lit. The darker cap marks the stronger end.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A limited toro made at Joya de Nicaragua for the 250th anniversary of the United States. It comes in boxes of 13 as a nod to the original colonies.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 250 boxes of 13 (3,250 cigars). Neptune's spec table lists a Connecticut Broadleaf binder and Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania filler, while halfwheel lists a Pennsylvania binder and Dominican and Pennsylvania filler. The wrapper variety is not published.

cigars.about: One of three moon-themed cigars made at La Aurora to mark the Fratello logo riding on Intuitive Machines' Nova-C lunar lander. This one wears an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the filler: halfwheel lists Dominican, Nicaraguan and Cameroon-seed leaf, while Neptune lists Nicaragua and USA. It was announced as limited, but halfwheel later listed it as regular production.

cigars.about: One of three moon-themed cigars made at La Aurora to mark the Fratello logo riding on Intuitive Machines' Nova-C lunar lander. This one uses a Cameroon-seed wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel's news coverage says the Cameroon wrapper is grown in Ecuador, while its review and Neptune simply say Cameroon. The U.S. filler leaf is listed in some sources and left out in others. It was announced as limited, but halfwheel later listed it as regular production.

cigars.about: The limited cigar in the Lunar trio, a Dominican puro made at La Aurora with tobaccos aged six years. It was sold in an 18-count humidor shaped like the Nova-C lunar lander.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the size: halfwheel lists a 6 x 50 toro, while Neptune lists a 6 1/2 x 50/60 figurado. 200 humidors of 18 were made, with 175 offered for sale. The wrapper variety is not published.

cigars.about: The maduro-wrapped cigar in Fratello's value-priced Camo bundle line, made at La Aurora. It wears the blue camouflage band.
cigars.researchNote: Also written Blu. Fratello does not officially disclose the Camo blends beyond the wrapper type. The binder and filler shown here come from Neptune.

cigars.about: The habano-wrapped cigar in Fratello's value-priced Camo bundle line, made at La Aurora. It wears the red camouflage band.
cigars.researchNote: Fratello does not officially disclose the Camo blends beyond the wrapper type. The binder and filler shown here come from Neptune.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped cigar in Fratello's value-priced Camo bundle line, made at La Aurora. It wears the green camouflage band.
cigars.researchNote: Fratello only confirms a Connecticut wrapper. The Ecuadorian origin, binder and filler come from Neptune.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut with a sweetened tip (origin not disclosed)
cigars.about: Fratello's first flavored cigar, a sweet-tipped addition to the Camo bundle line made at La Aurora.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is not disclosed. halfwheel lists it among the Camo blends as Connecticut Sweet, and it has a sweetened tip.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan-made version of the Camo Connecticut bundle cigar, rolled at Karen Berger's Estelí Cigars factory in two larger sizes. The original Camo sizes are still made at La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Fratello does not disclose the blend, so only the wrapper type is known. The founder says the Nicaraguan blends are close to the Dominican Camo versions but not identical. No strength rating was found.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan-made version of the Camo Habano bundle cigar, rolled at Karen Berger's Estelí Cigars factory in two larger sizes. The original Camo sizes are still made at La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Fratello does not disclose the blend, so only the wrapper type is known. The founder says the Nicaraguan blends are close to the Dominican Camo versions but not identical. No strength rating was found.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan-made version of the Camo Maduro bundle cigar, rolled at Karen Berger's Estelí Cigars factory in two larger sizes. The original Camo sizes are still made at La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Fratello does not disclose the blend, so only the wrapper type is known. The founder says the Nicaraguan blends are close to the Dominican Camo versions but not identical. No strength rating was found.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan, aged about 8 years, from the La Santa Cruz farm
cigars.about: An aged, limited edition of Gran Habano's #3 blend by George Rico. The cigars were rolled in early 2008 from long-aged Nicaraguan and Colombian tobacco and rested about two years before release.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's spec table lists the wrapper as Colombia, but its 2010 release and Cigar Aficionado both give a Nicaraguan wrapper and binder. The release called it medium to full; the maker's site says medium. 1,200 boxes of each size were made.

cigars.about: A single-size toro from Gran Habano made to raise money for the Women of PCA initiative of the Premium Cigar Association. It was shown at the 2026 PCA trade show and comes in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: One size only. Gran Habano says it donates all of its proceeds from RISE to Women of PCA. halfwheel lists it as regular production, not limited.

cigars.about: Gran Habano's maduro blend, first shown at the 2010 trade show, with a Mexican San Andres wrapper and binder. The maker now sells it as a 20-count bundle.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the binder only as maduro; retailers give San Andres for both wrapper and binder. The maker's table says medium to full, but its blurb says mild to medium and mentions Colombian and Costa Rican filler.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro from Gran Habano with a Corojo wrapper, sold in boxes of 20. Retailers describe it as box-pressed.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium, though retailers pitch it as a bold smoke. halfwheel reported it discontinued in 2010. The maker's site lists it again, but retailers often show it sold out, so check stock before promising it.

cigars.about: A mellow, medium value blend from Gran Habano with a Nicaraguan wrapper and binder over Nicaraguan and Mexican filler. It is sold in bundles of 20.
cigars.researchNote: Bundle cigar, 20 per bundle. The maker does not say what type of Nicaraguan wrapper it uses.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan (Natural), Ecuadorian Connecticut (Sweet Tip), Nicaraguan Maduro (Maduro)
cigars.about: A George Rico line from Gran Habano offered in three versions, Natural, Sweet Tip and Maduro, each in boxes of 20. All three use Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Three wrappers, so no single wrapper type: Natural is Nicaraguan, Sweet Tip is Ecuadorian Connecticut with a sweetened cap, Maduro is Nicaraguan maduro and rated medium to full. The maker gives the sizes without names.

cigars.about: A Cuban sandwich (mixed filler) cigar from Gran Habano aimed at everyday smoking at a low price. The maker describes it as medium to full with a smooth finish.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed-filler value cigar. The maker lists the wrapper only as Ecuador, without naming the leaf type.

cigars.about: Gran Habano's budget bundle cigar, an all-Nicaraguan blend sold 25 to a bundle. A retailer describes the filler as a mix of trimmings and long filler left over from the premium lines.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed-filler bundle cigar, 25 per bundle. The maker lists sizes without names; Cigar King sells the 6 x 50 as a Toro.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan Corojo (Corojo), Ecuadorian Connecticut (Connecticut), Nicaraguan sun-grown Corojo (Maduro), Connecticut and Corojo (Barber Pole)
cigars.about: Gran Habano's house bundles, sold 25 to a bundle in four versions: Corojo, Connecticut, Maduro and Barber Pole. All share the same four sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Four blends, so no single wrapper or strength: Corojo and Maduro are rated full, Connecticut mild to medium, Barber Pole medium. The Barber Pole uses a Nicaraguan Habano binder and Nicaraguan and Costa Rican filler only.

cigars.about: A value bundle blend by George Rico of Gran Habano with an oily Nicaraguan Corojo wrapper, sold in 20-count bundles through retailers. Holt's rates it the strongest of the three Vintage blends.
cigars.researchNote: Retailer bundle line that the maker's own site does not list. Retailers disagree on the filler: Holt's says Nicaraguan and Costa Rican, another says Nicaraguan and Dominican, and Neptune lists all three. Neptune calls it Vintage Corojo 2002.

cigars.about: The Connecticut Shade version of Gran Habano's Vintage bundle series, blended by George Rico and sold in 20-count bundles. Holt's describes it as a mellow, mild to medium smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Retailer bundle line that the maker's own site does not list. The binder and the country the wrapper is grown in are not published.

cigars.about: The Ecuador Habano version of Gran Habano's Vintage bundle series, blended by George Rico and sold in 20-count bundles. Holt's describes it as mild to medium.
cigars.researchNote: Retailer bundle line that the maker's own site does not list; binder is not published. Holt's rates it mild to medium, while Neptune calls it medium. Neptune calls it Vintage Habano 2006.

cigars.line: 1878 Recordando a Santiago Capa Sun Grown
cigars.about: The sun grown version of PDR's 1878 line, made by Abe Flores at the PDR factory in Tamboril. The line was reblended and renamed Recordando a Santiago in late 2020, in honor of the city where PDR is based.
cigars.researchNote: The 2020 date is the Recordando a Santiago reblend and rename; a PDR 1878 Capa Sun Grown existed before that. Neptune rates it medium. When the reblend launched, PDR said production would be capped at 5,000 boxes of each size.

cigars.about: A coffee-infused cigar from PDR, built on the maduro blend of the PDR 1878 line. It is the darkest of the three original Roast Cafe cigars that launched in 2018.
cigars.researchNote: This is a flavored (coffee-infused) cigar. Strength is Neptune's rating; PDR does not publish one. The 2018 launch blend also had Nicaraguan Criollo 98 in the filler, but PDR now lists all Dominican filler.

cigars.about: A coffee-infused cigar from PDR, based on the PDR 1878 Capa Sun Grown blend. It sits in the middle of the three original Roast Cafe cigars that launched in 2018.
cigars.researchNote: This is a flavored (coffee-infused) cigar. Halfwheel's 2018 review listed Dominican and Nicaraguan Criollo 98 filler; PDR lists Dominican Criollo 98 and Corojo. Neptune calls it mild, though halfwheel found it reached medium strength.

cigars.about: A coffee-infused cigar from PDR, based on the Connecticut shade blend of the PDR 1878 line. It is the lightest of the three original Roast Cafe cigars that launched in 2018.
cigars.researchNote: This is a flavored (coffee-infused) cigar. Strength is Neptune's rating; PDR does not publish one. The 2018 launch blend also had Nicaraguan Criollo 98 in the filler, but PDR now lists all Dominican filler.

cigars.about: A 2025 addition to PDR's flavored 1878 Roast Cafe line. It uses the 1878 Sun Grown blend with a French vanilla infusion.
cigars.researchNote: This is a flavored cigar and part of the 1878 Roast Cafe line. No strength is published, and it is not on PDR's own website.

cigars.about: A 2025 addition to PDR's flavored 1878 Roast Cafe line, with a Connecticut shade wrapper and a mint chocolate flavor. Halfwheel found it the lightest of the three new roasts.
cigars.researchNote: This is a flavored cigar and part of the 1878 Roast Cafe line. No strength is published, and it is not on PDR's own website.

cigars.about: A 2025 addition to PDR's flavored 1878 Roast Cafe line, with a Brazilian maduro wrapper. It is flavored with chocolate, a little cherry and dark roast coffee.
cigars.researchNote: This is a flavored cigar and part of the 1878 Roast Cafe line. No strength is published, and it is not on PDR's own website.

cigars.about: The Ecuadorian sun grown Habano version of the Gran Reserva line that PDR makes in honor of its blender, Abe Flores. It was added in 2015 as a slightly milder alternative to the original Corojo version.
cigars.researchNote: Renamed Gran Reserva Premier Cru in 2025 with the same blend, a new 4 x 34 Purito and no paper sleeve. Early on it was also called Gran Reserva Habano. PDR's spec line says "Dominican Corojo & Habano" filler, but its description and halfwheel say the Habano is Nicaraguan.

cigars.about: The San Andres maduro version of the Gran Reserva line that PDR makes in honor of its blender, Abe Flores. It joined the line in 2018 and is described as medium bodied, rich and creamy despite the dark wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Renamed Gran Reserva Premier Cru in 2025 with the same blend, a new 4 x 34 Purito and no paper sleeve. PDR's spec line says "Dominican Corojo & Habano" filler, but its description and halfwheel say the Habano is Nicaraguan.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped version of the Gran Reserva line that PDR makes in honor of its blender, Abe Flores. Desflorado means the wrapper comes from plants that had their flowers removed so more nutrients go to the leaves.
cigars.researchNote: Renamed Gran Reserva Premier Cru in 2025 with the same blend and a new 4 x 34 Purito. Sometimes spelled Deflorado. PDR's spec line says "Dominican Corojo & Habano" filler, but its own description says the Habano is Nicaraguan.

cigars.about: A sharply box-pressed line named for PDR blender Abe Flores and his birth year. Under its earlier name, Capa Habano, the SP 52 scored 93 points and was Cigar Aficionado's number 10 cigar of 2014.
cigars.researchNote: Called Serie Privada Capa Habano until 2019, when it was renamed and reblended. The original used a Nicaraguan Habano binder with Nicaraguan and Dominican filler; PDR now lists all Dominican. PDR launched it as medium bodied, and Neptune rates it medium strength.

cigars.about: The maduro version of the sharply box-pressed Serie Privada line, named for PDR blender Abe Flores and his birth year. It launched alongside the Habano version in 2012.
cigars.researchNote: PDR launched it in 2012 as medium to full bodied; Cigar Coop's 2022 review of the reblend and Neptune both call it medium. Reblended in 2019: PDR now lists all Dominican binder and filler, while Cigar Coop still lists a Nicaraguan Habano binder and part Nicaraguan filler.

cigars.line: A. Flores 1975 Connecticut Valley Reserve Azul
cigars.about: One of PDR's most expensive lines, wrapped in the lighter, lower-priming leaves of Connecticut broadleaf. It first appeared in 2016 under the Flores y Rodriguez name and was reblended and rebranded as A. Flores 1975 in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: PDR lists a Dominican binder and filler, but halfwheel and Cigar Coop report a Nicaraguan Jalapa binder and a filler of Dominican Corojo with some Nicaraguan Criollo. Ongoing production, shipped only a few times a year in boxes of 10. Strength is from Cigar Coop's review.

cigars.line: A. Flores 1975 Connecticut Valley Reserve Roja
cigars.about: One of PDR's most expensive lines, wrapped in the darker, upper-priming maduro leaves of Connecticut broadleaf. It began in 2015 as the Flores y Rodriguez Connecticut Valley Reserve and took the Roja name when the line was reworked in 2020.
cigars.researchNote: PDR lists a Dominican binder and filler, but halfwheel reports a Nicaraguan Jalapa binder and a filler that is about 80 percent Dominican with some Nicaraguan. No strength is published for the current blend.

cigars.about: The lighter San Andres version of AFR-75, PDR's top small-batch line named for blender Abraham Flores Rosario and his 1975 birth year. It was added in 2016, three years after the original maduro.
cigars.researchNote: Despite the name it is not a limited edition, just small production. Relaunched in June 2026 with a reworked Dominican and Nicaraguan blend, boxes of 10 and three slightly thinner sizes; the blend and sizes here are the originals still on PDR's site. Older reports give a Nicaraguan Criollo 98 binder.

cigars.about: The original AFR-75, PDR's top small-batch line named for blender Abraham Flores Rosario and his 1975 birth year. It came out in 2013 and was the first PDR cigar with a San Andres maduro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Cigar Coop found the original medium building to medium-full in both strength and body. Relaunched in June 2026 with a reworked blend, boxes of 10 and three slightly thinner sizes; the blend and sizes here are the originals still on PDR's site. Older reports give a Nicaraguan Criollo 98 binder.

cigars.about: The San Andres maduro version of PDR's El Trovador, whose name means troubadour. It followed the original Ecuadorian rosado blend by a year, arriving in 2017.
cigars.researchNote: PDR lists an all Dominican binder and filler. Halfwheel reports it began as all Nicaraguan under the wrapper and was changed in 2021 to a half Nicaraguan, half Dominican filler. Strength and body are from a 2020 Blind Man's Puff review of the original blend.

cigars.about: A value-priced PDR line built around Criollo tobacco. It was created for the European market in 2016 and reached the United States in 2017.
cigars.researchNote: Strength varies by source: Neptune says mild, halfwheel found it just short of medium. Halfwheel and Neptune also list Nicaraguan Criollo in the filler; PDR lists Dominican only. Sometimes spelled El Criolito.

cigars.about: A PDR line from Abe Flores that comes out in dated yearly batches labeled Cuvee Especial, each rested for a year before release. It debuted in 2023.
cigars.researchNote: Released as dated yearly batches. Flores has said the robusto, belicoso and wide Churchill are mainly for the U.S., with the double corona and salomon aimed at Europe. Strength comes from one retailer (Neptune). It is not on PDR's own website.

cigars.line: Flores y Rodriguez 10th Anniversary Reserva Limitada
cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano seco and ligero aged 7 years, viso)
cigars.about: Made to mark ten years of PDR Cigars, the company Abe Flores founded with the Rodriguez family in 2004. It is built around Dominican Piloto Cubano filler aged seven years.
cigars.researchNote: Regular production despite the Reserva Limitada name. The filler originally included Nicaraguan Jalapa leaf, which halfwheel now reports as Dominican-grown Habano. A 5 x 42 Millefleurs Corona was added for Europe in 2023.

cigars.about: A green candela-wrapped cigar from Espinosa, finished with a dark Nicaraguan habano cap. It began in 2016 as a lounge-only Backroom Series cigar and later became an ongoing line.
cigars.researchNote: Not flavored: the name only nods to the green wrapper. Espinosa lists the Corona as 5 x 42, halfwheel and Neptune as 5 x 46. Neptune rates it Medium, but halfwheel's 2018 review found it medium-full to full, so it can hit harder than most candelas.

cigars.about: A vanilla-flavored, sweet-tipped cigar made with Dominican long filler, and the first flavored cigar from Espinosa. It is made in the Dominican Republic rather than at Espinosa's own factory.
cigars.researchNote: Often written @ZUCAR. Debuted in 2016 and was reblended as an all-Dominican cigar in 2020. In 2026 Espinosa said it is being discontinued and replaced by Entice, though Espinosa's site still lists it.

cigars.about: The third blend in Espinosa's Laranja family, named for a style of blue tile and dressed in blue bands. It pairs an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper with a Brazilian Arapiraca binder and Nicaraguan fillers.
cigars.researchNote: Espinosa's own site calls it Laranja Azulejo and describes it as medium-plus to full bodied. The cigars are box-pressed.

cigars.about: A 2026 addition to Espinosa's Laranja family that swaps the usual Brazilian wrapper for an Ecuadorian habano oscuro leaf and moves the Brazilian tobacco into the filler. It comes in two sizes, with the toro box-pressed.
cigars.researchNote: Strength comes from Neptune only. Neptune lists Brazilian leaf in the binder, while halfwheel and the company put it in the filler.

cigars.about: A vanilla-infused, box-pressed cigar Espinosa introduced in 2026 to replace its Azucar line. It is aimed at newer smokers while still being a handmade cigar.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is not disclosed. halfwheel reports it is made at Victor Calvo's factory in Estelí, while Neptune lists La Zona. Neptune lists the Toro as 6 x 52 where halfwheel has 6 x 50.

cigars.about: A core line Espinosa launched in January 2024, and the first Sumatra-wrapped blend made at its La Zona factory. Erik Espinosa describes it as nutty with a spice note.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is unclear: Famous Smoke describes it as medium bodied and creamy but tags it Full in its spec table.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Three versions: Habano, Connecticut and Maduro
cigars.about: A value-priced Espinosa bundle whose name stands for Cigars, Ready-to-Smoke. The toros come ten to a resealable humidified bag, styled after military MRE packaging, in Habano, Connecticut or Maduro wrappers.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in three wrapper versions, so ask which one the guest has. Wrapper origins, binder and factory are not published. Details here come from Famous Smoke only.

cigars.about: A budget bundle line from Erik Espinosa sold only through Famous Smoke Shop. It uses an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan filler and comes in bundles of 20.
cigars.researchNote: A Famous Smoke Shop exclusive. Famous describes it as medium in body and strength but tags it Full in its spec table. The binder is not published and the factory is not named beyond the line's name.

cigars.about: An Espinosa line built around Jamaican Lengua de Vaca tobacco in the filler, first sold to select lounges in 2016 and released nationally in 2017. Its offshoot, Reggae Dread, has a cap of tobacco strands made to look like dreadlocks.
cigars.researchNote: Reggae Dread (6 x 56, with a dreadlock-style cap) is a different, fuller blend: Ecuadorian Habano wrapper with Nicaraguan, Honduran and Jamaican filler. Launched as regular production, but it is no longer on Espinosa's site, so current status is unclear.

cigars.about: A 2019 collaboration between Erik Espinosa and General Cigar, and the first Espinosa blend to use a Cameroon wrapper. Espinosa made it at La Zona and General Cigar handled sales and distribution.
cigars.researchNote: Sold by General Cigar rather than Espinosa. Strength varies by source: the launch description says medium to full, Neptune tags it Full, and halfwheel found it medium. Each size was a limited run of 1,500 to 3,000 boxes of 20.

cigars.about: A collaboration between Espinosa and the Cigar Dojo community, first released in 2014 as a 1,000-bundle store exclusive. It is named for a sarsaparilla root beer note the makers find in the blend.
cigars.researchNote: Not flavored: the name refers to a natural tasting note. A second version in a 6 x 50 toro came out in 2016, and since 2021 the belicoso has been a seasonal national release in 10-count boxes.

cigars.about: A 2024 limited edition of Espinosa's Murcielago made for retail members of the Tobacconists' Association of America. It trades the line's usual San Andrés maduro wrapper for a light Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed leaf.
cigars.researchNote: TAA exclusive limited to 1,000 boxes of 20. halfwheel found it medium-full in strength despite the light wrapper, while Neptune lists it as Medium.

cigars.about: A reworked version of Espinosa's Murcielago blend with a lighter San Andrés claro wrapper, released in 2023 as the company's first exclusive for the Tobacconists' Association of America.
cigars.researchNote: TAA exclusive limited to 1,500 boxes of 20. Espinosa says it has more body than regular Murcielago but not more strength, and less sweetness. The Medium strength rating comes from Neptune only.

cigars.about: The annual limited edition in Knuckle Sandwich, the brand Guy Fieri runs with Espinosa. Each year brings a new wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, sold in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Called Chef's Special in 2022 and Chef Special since. Wrappers per halfwheel: 2022 Ecuadorian Habano Rosado, 2023 Ecuadorian Sumatra, 2024 Connecticut Broadleaf, 2025 Brazilian Mata Fina, 2026 Mexican Claro. Espinosa's own page lists the original as all Nicaraguan. Strength varies by year, so check the band.

cigars.about: The first Knuckle Sandwich cigar made for the Tobacconists' Association of America, released in late 2025. It is a dark, box-pressed toro with a Pennsylvania Broadleaf wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: TAA exclusive limited to 1,250 boxes of 20. Knuckle Sandwich is Guy Fieri's brand, made and distributed with Espinosa.

cigars.about: An all-Nicaraguan blend added to Guy Fieri's Knuckle Sandwich brand in 2025 as its fourth regular production line. It wears black, silver and red bands with a silver foot ribbon.
cigars.researchNote: The company only says the blend is all Nicaraguan and does not disclose regions or varietals. Neptune alone calls the wrapper Nicaraguan Habano. Espinosa describes it as full-bodied and Neptune rates it Full.

cigars.about: A 2026 Knuckle Sandwich release meant as a milder, more approachable entry point than the brand's usual strong and spicy cigars. It comes in one toro size in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Milder than it looks despite the dark wrapper: halfwheel found it mild to mild-medium, while Neptune lists Medium. Production is undisclosed, and the company says it could become a regular line if demand is there.

cigars.about: The 2026 entry in Knuckle Sandwich's yearly limited edition marking Guy Fieri's birthday, named for the age he turns. It uses the same San Andrés-wrapped blend as the earlier birthday releases in a new oval-pressed size.
cigars.researchNote: Fourth in the birthday series after 55 (2023), 56 (2024) and 57 (2025): same blend, different size each year. halfwheel found it topping out at medium-full, while Neptune lists Medium. Production numbers are undisclosed.

cigars.about: The first release in Espinosa's Las 6 Provincias series honoring Cuba's original six provinces, with LHB standing for La Habana. It debuted in 2018 and is known for its artwork and a limited 20-count box that swings on a stand.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel lists the cigar as regular production with only the 300 swinging boxes limited, though some retailers call it a limited edition. halfwheel found it medium-full building to full, while Neptune describes it as medium.

cigars.about: The second release in Espinosa's Las 6 Provincias series, honoring the Cuban province of Matanzas. It came out in 2019 as a box-pressed Nicaraguan puro in a box built to look like a stained-glass window.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,000 boxes of 10 and 500 boxes of 20, or 20,000 cigars. Unlike LHB, it was made at Espinosa's own La Zona factory.

cigars.about: A bundle cigar in the Connecticut Sweet blend of Fratello's Camo Nicaragua series, made at Karen Berger's Estelí Cigars factory in Nicaragua. It is the Nicaraguan-made counterpart to the Dominican Camo bundles that La Aurora produces.
cigars.researchNote: Fratello does not disclose the blend, so the wrapper type comes from the name only and no strength is published. Sold in bundles of 25. Do not confuse with the Dominican Camo Connecticut Sweet in Robusto and Toro, which La Aurora makes.

cigars.about: The first of six Prohibition-themed releases in Fratello's Concealed Carry sub-brand, a one-time small batch sold in 12-count cans. It is named for the constitutional amendment that began Prohibition.
cigars.researchNote: Blend and factory are secret. Fratello says only that Concealed Carry cigars come from undisclosed factories in the Dominican Republic, Honduras and Nicaragua. About 1,000 cans of 12, sold through no more than 75 stores.

cigars.about: The second release in Fratello's Prohibition-themed Concealed Carry series, a one-time small batch sold in 12-count cans. It is named for the river that bootleggers used to smuggle liquor during Prohibition.
cigars.researchNote: Blend and factory are secret. Fratello says only that Concealed Carry cigars come from undisclosed factories in the Dominican Republic, Honduras and Nicaragua. 1,000 cans of 12, sold through no more than 75 stores.

cigars.about: The third release in Fratello's Prohibition-themed Concealed Carry series, a one-time small batch sold in 12-count cans. It is named for the hidden bars of the Prohibition era.
cigars.researchNote: Blend and factory are secret. halfwheel's Speakeasy story gives the size as 5 1/4 x 54, while Cigar Coop and halfwheel's other series coverage say 5 1/2 x 54. 1,000 cans of 12, sold through no more than 75 stores.

cigars.about: The fourth release in Fratello's Prohibition-themed Concealed Carry series, a one-time small batch sold in 12-count canisters. It is named for the liquor smugglers of the era.
cigars.researchNote: Blend and factory are secret. halfwheel's shipping story gives the size as 5 1/2 x 54, while its PCA 2025 report says 5 1/4 x 54. 1,000 canisters of 12.

cigars.about: The fifth of six releases in Fratello's Prohibition-themed Concealed Carry series of one-time small batches. It came out in 2025, between Bootlegger and the final AA 1935.
cigars.researchNote: Blend and factory are secret. No size or count is published for this release, though Fratello said all six Concealed Carry cigars would share the same 5 1/2 x 54 size. halfwheel lists it as a September 2025 release.

cigars.about: The sixth and final release in Fratello's Prohibition-themed Concealed Carry series, a one-time small batch sold in 12-count jars. The name refers to 1935, the year Alcoholics Anonymous was founded, two years after Prohibition ended.
cigars.researchNote: Blend and factory are secret. 1,000 jars of 12. halfwheel reports $12 per cigar, Cigar Coop reports $10.

cigars.about: A Louisiana-only cigar in Fratello's state exclusive series, made at La Aurora and distributed by PF Importers, the company co-owned by Karl Malone. Its filler includes Dominican andullo, a tobacco cured in tightly wrapped pods and more often used for pipes.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 250 boxes of 20 (5,000 cigars), sold only in Louisiana. Fratello calls it medium to full bodied; no separate strength rating is published.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Corojo seco, Criollo 98, Piloto Cubano ligero)
cigars.about: A Dominican puro in Fratello's state exclusive series, made at La Aurora for retailers in Florida. It debuted at the ABC Fine Wine & Spirits chain.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only through Florida retailers. The first run was 10,000 cigars (500 boxes of 20), and Fratello had not said whether more would follow. No strength rating is published.

cigars.about: A Fratello revival of a Tampa cigar brand dating to 1909, made at La Aurora with an Ecuadorian-grown Cameroon wrapper. It launched through the ABC Fine Wine & Spirits stores in Florida.
cigars.researchNote: First run was 12,000 cigars sold only at ABC Fine Wine & Spirits. Fratello said it planned to make the line ongoing and widen distribution, so it may not be limited. The maker calls it full flavored with a medium body.

cigars.about: The Virginia cigar in Fratello's DMV series, a regional release made at La Aurora for retailers around Washington, D.C., where the company is based. The Pocahontas size was added in 2024.
cigars.researchNote: Blend shown is halfwheel's 2024 description. Its 2018 report gave an Ecuadorian HVA wrapper, Ecuadorian Sumatra binder and Dominican, Nicaraguan and U.S. filler, and the 2019 Virginia used an Ecuadorian corojo wrapper. A separate DMV Virginia Maduro (6 x 50) is made by Joya de Nicaragua.

cigars.about: A pigtail-capped robusto that Fratello made at La Aurora as an exclusive for retailers in Switzerland. It was scheduled to launch on August 1, 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only in Switzerland, 4,000 cigars in boxes of 20. No strength rating is published.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano seco and ligero), Nicaragua (Jalapa viso)
cigars.about: PDR Cigars' 18th anniversary line, a variation on the Flores y Rodriguez 10th Anniversary that swaps the Ecuadorian habano wrapper for an Ecuadorian Sumatra maduro. The filler includes seven-year-old Dominican piloto cubano.
cigars.researchNote: The maker publishes no strength. Famous Smoke lists the strength as full but describes the cigar as medium bodied, so treat the rating as approximate.

cigars.line: Flores y Rodriguez Connecticut Valley Reserve Maduro
cigars.about: A higher-priced PDR release built around a seven-year-old Connecticut broadleaf maduro wrapper over a double binder. It first shipped in late 2015 in wide 15-count boxes and returned in later batches, including 19-count jars.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel's review called strength and body medium, while Famous Smoke lists it as full. The 2017 Gen2 batch dropped the Ecuadorian binder. PDR's site now lists Connecticut Valley Reserve Roja and Azul under A. Flores 1975 instead of this name.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped blend in PDR's sweet-tipped Jose Rey line of value bundles. Jose Rey revives one of the first brands PDR made, originally for the New Orleans retailer Don Leoncio.
cigars.researchNote: Sweet-tipped cap. Sold in bundles or boxes of 25. Strength is from Famous Smoke (mellow to medium); the maker gives none.

cigars.about: The San Andrés maduro blend in PDR's sweet-tipped Jose Rey line of value bundles. Jose Rey revives one of the first brands PDR made, originally for the New Orleans retailer Don Leoncio.
cigars.researchNote: Sweet-tipped cap. Sold in bundles or boxes of 25. No strength is published for this blend; Famous Smoke describes the Jose Rey line overall as mellow to medium.

cigars.about: The Sumatra-wrapped blend in PDR's sweet-tipped Jose Rey line of value bundles. Jose Rey revives one of the first brands PDR made, originally for the New Orleans retailer Don Leoncio.
cigars.researchNote: Sweet-tipped cap. Sold in bundles or boxes of 25. Strength is from Famous Smoke (medium bodied); the maker gives none.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Seco and Ligero), USA (Connecticut Broadleaf)
cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped line that PDR's Abe Flores relaunched for the Pohler family, who are known as cigar sales reps in the southern U.S. It comes in 10-count boxes styled after 1940s and 1950s packaging.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is from Famous Smoke; the maker gives none.

cigars.about: A mixed-filler Connecticut bundle cigar from PDR, usually shortened to VLR Connecticut. PDR used to make it for Thompson Cigar and gave it a wider release to shops in 2023.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel lists it as PDR VLR Connecticut, sold in bundles of 15. Strength is from Famous Smoke, which also calls the smoke mellow; the maker gives none. 2023 is the wider store release, and it was a Thompson exclusive before that.
