cigars.about: A high-priced single-size PDR cigar blended by founders Abe Flores and Luis Rodriguez from tobacco aged more than eight years. It first appeared as a 2026 Procigar Festival auction item before a retail release in 10-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Rests six months in French oak barrels. Cigar Coop reported the Procigar auction version as 6 1/2 x 50 with a Dominican piloto binder and Dominican habano and criollo 98 filler, which differs from the retail specs shown here. No strength is published.

cigars.about: The maduro half of PDR's Small Batch Reserve, a line that dates to 2012 and was among the first cigars from the company's own factory. PDR reintroduced it in 2026 in cabinet-style boxes with new bands and a 4 x 60 Magnum size.
cigars.researchNote: The blend and sizes shown are the 2026 relaunch, which halfwheel lists as Small Batch Reserve Cabinet Maduro. The original 2012 version used a Brazilian Cubra maduro wrapper over a Dominican criollo 98 binder. No strength is published.

cigars.about: The habano rosado half of PDR's Small Batch Reserve line, which shares its Nicaraguan binder and filler with the maduro version. PDR reintroduced it in 2026 in cabinet-style boxes with new bands and a 4 x 60 Magnum size.
cigars.researchNote: The blend and sizes shown are the 2026 relaunch, which halfwheel lists as Small Batch Reserve Cabinet Rosado. The Small Batch Reserve line itself dates to 2012, but no source gives the year the Rosado first appeared. No strength is published.

cigars.about: The maduro version of CAO Gold. It keeps that line's Nicaraguan binder and filler and swaps the Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper for a dark Brazilian maduro leaf.
cigars.researchNote: CAO rates it mild to medium, while Neptune lists it as medium. Neptune marks its three sizes as discontinued, though CAO's site still lists the line, so its current status is unclear.

cigars.about: A flavored cigar from the CAO Flavours family, infused with honey that CAO says comes from Florida orange blossom nectar. It is a mild smoke with a Cameroon wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Sold by retailers as CAO Flavours Gold Honey. It is an infused cigar, not part of the regular CAO Gold line. STG discontinued the 4 x 40 Petit Corona in June 2026. Holt's says it is made in the Dominican Republic, while Neptune lists the Corona as Nicaraguan.

cigars.about: A flavored cigar from the CAO Flavours family, infused with cherry and black currant over a vanilla base. It is a mild smoke with a Cameroon wrapper and Dominican filler.
cigars.researchNote: Sold by retailers as CAO Flavours Cherrybomb. It is an infused cigar.

cigars.about: Introduced in 2011 as one of the first new CAO lines after General Cigar took over the brand. It is named for its wrapper leaf from the Olancho San Agustin valley in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: STG discontinued the line in November 2024 per halfwheel, though CAO's site still lists it. CAO rates it mellow to medium while Neptune and Holt's say medium. Both retailers list Lot 54 as 6 x 54, not CAO's 5.75 x 54.

cigars.about: A motorcycle-themed spin-off of CAO Flathead that debuted in 2015. It keeps the flat head but uses a different blend, with a Connecticut-grown Habano wrapper over a Brazilian Arapiraca binder.
cigars.researchNote: CAO now calls it simply Steel Horse. The small Handbrake (4.5 x 50) was discontinued in August 2025 per halfwheel. Sizes have changed since launch, when Apehanger was 5.5 x 58 and Bullneck 6.5 x 66.

cigars.about: A 2026 addition to CAO's car-themed Flathead family, box pressed with the flat head the line is named for. It swaps the original's broadleaf wrapper for Ecuadorian Habano over a San Andrés binder and is pitched as the everyday, medium-bodied Flathead.
cigars.researchNote: Press coverage calls it Flathead Speed Shop Habano. The 6.5 x 54 Crankshaft is a new size for Flathead.

cigars.about: A 2019 limited edition built as a fuller-bodied take on the original CAO Flathead, box pressed with a flat head. Both the broadleaf wrapper and the habano binder are grown in Connecticut.
cigars.researchNote: Production was 2,350 boxes of 20 in each size. It was rolled in Honduras at STG Danlí, per halfwheel.

cigars.about: The 2021 limited edition in CAO's Flathead series, a soft box press sold only in two large ring gauges. It uses a Mexican San Andrés wrapper where the original Flathead uses Connecticut Broadleaf.
cigars.researchNote: CAO's spec table lists a Honduran Habano binder, but its own description and halfwheel both say Connecticut Broadleaf. Each size was limited to 2,000 boxes of 27.

cigars.filler: Brazil (Mata Fina), Honduras (Jamastran viso), Nicaragua (Jalapa viso, Estelí ligero)
cigars.about: A 2023 limited edition Flathead made to mark 100 years of the 24 Hours of Le Mans, with packaging modeled on the Ford GT40 in Gulf racing colors. It is a single box-pressed 6 x 60 with a Honduran wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: CAO rates it medium to full but also describes it as a full-bodied blend. Production numbers were not disclosed.

cigars.about: The 2020 remake of CAO Vision, a cigar best known for its white box with built-in blue LED lighting. This version is a single Churchill with a Cameroon wrapper, the first Cameroon blend from CAO blender Rick Rodriguez.
cigars.researchNote: The original 2007 Vision was a different, Dominican-wrapped blend made at La Aurora. The 2020 run was 4,500 boxes of 20. CAO's spec table lists a Dominican binder and three-country filler, but its own description, halfwheel and Neptune give the blend shown here.

cigars.about: The third CAO Vision release, a 6 x 52 toro made entirely of habano-seed tobacco with a Honduran wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It came in a 30-count humidor-style box with two touch-opened drawers and orange LED lights.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is left blank because sources conflict: CAO calls it mellow, while halfwheel's review found medium-full to full strength and Neptune's spec says full. Limited to 2,700 boxes of 30.

cigars.filler: Brazil (Bragança, Fuma em Corda), Honduras, Nicaragua
cigars.about: The fourth cigar in CAO's Amazon series, released in 2019 and named for Francisco de Orellana, the first European to travel the length of the Amazon. Like the others it has a twisted tobacco rope in place of a paper band.
cigars.researchNote: Cubra is a Cuban-seed leaf grown in Brazil. CAO's spec table says full, but its description and Holt's say medium to full. Holt's describes the filler as Dominican, Nicaraguan, Brazilian and Colombian, which differs from CAO's list.

cigars.filler: Brazil (Bragança, Fuma em Corda), Colombia, Dominican Republic
cigars.about: The third cigar in CAO's Amazon trilogy, released in 2017. It combines the Bragança tobacco from Amazon Basin with the rope-fermented Fuma em Corda leaf from the second release, under a Brazilian Habano wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists it as discontinued and it is no longer on CAO's site. Strength is left blank: Neptune rates it full, while halfwheel's review found it about medium. Neptune says it was made in Honduras, but halfwheel lists STG Estelí in Nicaragua.

cigars.about: The regular CAO Amazon Basin blend, built around Brazilian Bragança tobacco from the Amazon, with the finished cigars rested for about two extra years in cedar aging rooms. It keeps the tobacco rope band of the original.
cigars.researchNote: First released January 2023 at 5,000 boxes of 18. A second release shipped October 2026 using cigars rolled in 2024.

cigars.about: A follow-up to CAO Pilón that ferments its tobacco in round pilón stacks, then ages the rolled cigars for two more years. It is a different blend from the original Pilón.
cigars.researchNote: A 2022 limited edition made regular in 2023; halfwheel reported STG discontinued it in March 2025, though CAO's site still lists it. CAO's spec table says Ecuadorian Habano wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler, but its own description and halfwheel give the blend shown here.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Andullo, Piloto Cubano), Honduras (Jamastran), Nicaragua (Estelí)
cigars.about: The first release in CAO's Arcana series, which showcases unusual tobacco processing methods. Its filler includes Dominican andullo, leaf fermented by being bound tightly into long palm pod rolls instead of stacked in piles.
cigars.researchNote: Original run was 5,000 boxes of 20 in 2021. It returned in August 2023 with the same blend and size. CAO's site rounds the size to 6 x 50.

cigars.about: The second release in CAO's Arcana series, from 2022. Its Nicaraguan filler was cured with chincagre, an old local method in which the tobacco piles are buried in hot volcanic soil for two months before a second fermentation.
cigars.researchNote: Strength ratings vary widely: CAO's site says mellow, Neptune medium, Holt's full, and halfwheel's review found medium-plus. CAO's story text names a Honduran Corojo wrapper, but its spec table and halfwheel say Ecuadorian Habano Rosado. Limited to 5,000 boxes of 20.

cigars.about: The third release in CAO's Arcana series, from 2024, with a filler made entirely of African tobacco from Cameroon, South Africa and Zimbabwe. The name comes from the local name for Victoria Falls, the smoke that thunders.
cigars.researchNote: Unlike most CAOs it is made in the Dominican Republic, not Nicaragua. General billed it as the first premium cigar with South African and Zimbabwean tobacco. Production numbers were not disclosed.

cigars.about: The fourth Arcana release, from 2025, made with pipe tobacco house Peter Stokkebye, a sister company under Scandinavian Tobacco Group. The filler is split so the first half smokes on Dominican andullo and the second half on fire-cured Latakia from Cyprus.
cigars.researchNote: Size is disputed: CAO's site says 6 x 50, the launch announcement said 6.5 x 52, and halfwheel measured its samples at 6 x 52. Limited to 3,500 boxes of 20.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano), Nicaragua (Jalapa, Estelí, Condega)
cigars.about: A regular production CAO line introduced at the 2024 PCA trade show alongside FASA Noche. The two share a Cameroon binder and the same fillers, and Sol wears the Honduran Olancho San Agustin wrapper CAO first used on OSA Sol.
cigars.researchNote: FASA Sol is made in Honduras at STG Danlí, while its sibling FASA Noche is made in Nicaragua at STG Estelí.

cigars.binder: Nicaragua (Habano, aged in Rabbit Hole Boxergrail rye barrels)
cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A limited Diesel toro made with Rabbit Hole Distillery, the third Diesel and Rabbit Hole collaboration and the first in the Founder's Collection. Its Nicaraguan habano binder was aged in barrels that held Rabbit Hole Boxergrail rye whiskey.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in boxes of 10; production numbers were not disclosed. Strength is from a retailer listing, not the maker. The flavor words are what the maker says the rye barrels add to the binder leaf.

cigars.binder: USA (Connecticut Broadleaf, aged in Rabbit Hole Mizunara oak barrels)
cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A limited Diesel toro made with Rabbit Hole Distillery. The binder leaf was aged in the Japanese Mizunara oak barrels used for Rabbit Hole's Founder's Collection bourbon.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the blend. Diesel's site lists a Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper over a Connecticut Broadleaf binder. Halfwheel's review lists a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over Nicaraguan habano binder and filler.

cigars.binder: Nicaragua (aged in Rabbit Hole Raceking bourbon barrels)
cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A limited Diesel toro made with Rabbit Hole Distillery and released just before the 2025 Kentucky Derby. Its Nicaraguan binder was aged in barrels that held Rabbit Hole Raceking bourbon.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,300 boxes of 10.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The fourth Founder's Collection release from Diesel and Rabbit Hole Distillery. It uses tobacco aged in Rabbit Hole whiskey barrels made of French oak from the Nevers and Allier forests, which is where the name comes from.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel reports the barrel-aged leaf here is the Nicaraguan and Dominican filler, not the binder as in earlier Founder's Collection releases.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The first release in Diesel's limited Backyard BBQ series, a thick robusto blended as a nod to North Carolina barbecue. It is made by AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,000 boxes of 10. The country the Habano Rosado wrapper is grown in has not been disclosed.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The second release in Diesel's limited Backyard BBQ series, a Pennsylvania Broadleaf toro over Nicaraguan tobacco. It is priced to be bought by the box, at about $7.50 a cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Diesel and halfwheel list it as a 6 x 52 toro; Neptune Cigar lists it as 5 x 56 and Full.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The first cigar in Diesel's limited Fool's Errand trilogy, a 5 x 58 perfecto with a broadleaf wrapper. Each box of 10 came with a tarot card and a QR code for an online riddle game with prizes.
cigars.researchNote: First of three Fool's Errand releases, followed by Simple Fool (2023) and Worthy Fool (2024). Production numbers were not disclosed.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The second cigar in Diesel's limited Fool's Errand trilogy, a 5 x 58 perfecto blended by Justin Andrews and AJ Fernandez. Boxes include a collectible card with a QR code for an online riddle game.
cigars.researchNote: Second of three Fool's Errand releases, between Stubborn Fool (2022) and Worthy Fool (2024).

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The third and final cigar in Diesel's limited Fool's Errand trilogy, a 5 x 58 perfecto made by AJ Fernandez. Like the earlier two, boxes include a card with a QR code for an online riddle game.
cigars.researchNote: Third of three Fool's Errand releases. Its listed leaf matches Simple Fool: Ecuadorian Sumatra over Nicaraguan habano.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The second blend in Diesel's Vintage Series, with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper over Nicaraguan filler that the company says is aged five to seven years. It is a regular production line made by AJ Fernandez.
cigars.researchNote: Diesel calls it Medium-Full; Neptune Cigar lists it as Full. The original Pico Gordo (4.5 x 60) and Rabito (6 x 46) sizes were discontinued in 2025, when the 6 x 60 Gigante was added.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A limited edition Diesel toro billed as the boldest blend in the brand when it came out, with ligero and Ometepe leaf in the filler. It is made by AJ Fernandez in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 5,000 boxes of 10 in March 2020. The Delirium name was first used in 2014 on a Cigars International release.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The broadleaf maduro version of Diesel Unlimited, a full-bodied line with a Pennsylvania Broadleaf wrapper over a Mexican San Andres binder. Like the rest of the brand, it is made by AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Diesel's site rounds the d.4 and d.X lengths to 4.7 and 5.7 inches; retailers list them as 4 3/4 and 5 3/4.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: Diesel's tenth anniversary cigar, blended by AJ Fernandez with an Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Some retailers sell it as Diesel 10th Anniversary.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A full-bodied Diesel blended by AJ Fernandez with a dark habano wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. The 2017 version was the first Diesel sold to brick-and-mortar shops after years as a catalog brand.
cigars.researchNote: STG discontinued Grind in November 2024. The 2017 retail version replaced an earlier Grind sold by Cigars International. Diesel's site lists an Ecuadorian Habano Maduro wrapper; STG's Cigar World lists Nicaraguan Habano.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A full-bodied, value-priced Diesel blended by AJ Fernandez with a Pennsylvania Broadleaf wrapper over Nicaraguan long filler.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped follow-up to Diesel Uncut, a medium-bodied blend with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A full-bodied Diesel torpedo with a Pennsylvania Broadleaf Maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan ligero long filler. Like the rest of the brand, it is made by AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Diesel's site lists the length as 6.2 inches; retailers list it as 6 1/4.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A medium to full-bodied Diesel blended by AJ Fernandez with a very dark Ecuadorian Habano Sun Grown Oscuro wrapper over Cuban-seed Nicaraguan long filler.
cigars.researchNote: Diesel describes Rage as a limited edition, though it is still listed in the brand's current lineup in four sizes.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A full-bodied Diesel gordo with an oily Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro wrapper over Nicaraguan long filler from three growing regions, including Esteli ligero.
cigars.researchNote: Diesel describes it as a limited edition, though it is still listed in the brand's current lineup. It comes in one size.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: Diesel's 2024 exclusive for Tobacconists' Association of America (TAA) member shops, a 6 x 52 toro made by AJ Fernandez and packed in boxes that look like books.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,000 boxes of 10, sold only at TAA member retailers. The Tempest name was first announced for the 2022 TAA cigar, which shipped as Diesel Atonement instead.

cigars.about: The third release in Espinosa's Las 6 Provincias series, named for Cuba's old Las Villas province. It is a Nicaraguan puro made by AJ Fernandez and sold in a curio cabinet style box of 10 coffined cigars.
cigars.researchNote: One size only, 1,000 boxes of 10. The wrapper variety is not published. Halfwheel found it starts mild and builds to just under full; Neptune lists it full and Cigars Direct medium-full.

cigars.about: The fourth Las 6 Provincias release, honoring Camaguey and named after the airport code for that city. It is a box-pressed toro made by AJ Fernandez with box art by Edin Gutierrez.
cigars.researchNote: One size only, 1,000 boxes of 20. No maker strength rating. Halfwheel's review found full flavor but little nicotine kick, mild to just under medium; Corona Cigar lists it medium to full.

cigars.about: The fifth Las 6 Provincias release, honoring Pinar del Rio. ZDT stands for Zona de Tabaco, and the cigars come in a painted 20-count ceramic jar.
cigars.researchNote: One size only; production numbers were not disclosed. Neptune lists it medium and Cigars Direct medium-full. Halfwheel found it medium, climbing to medium-full at the very end.

cigars.about: The sixth Las 6 Provincias release, honoring Oriente, Cuba's easternmost original province. It is a box-pressed 6 x 56 made by AJ Fernandez and sold in a hinged display box of 20.
cigars.researchNote: One size only, 1,000 boxes of 20. No maker strength rating; Halfwheel's review and Neptune say full, Corona Cigar says medium to full. It was billed as the last of the six until the Miami (MIA) release was added in 2026.

cigars.about: A seventh Las 6 Provincias release named for Miami, often called Cuba's unofficial seventh province. It is a Nicaraguan puro made by AJ Fernandez, shown at the 2026 PCA trade show.
cigars.researchNote: One size only, 1,000 boxes of 20. Announced April 2026 with a September 2026 target for stores; arrival is not confirmed here. Wrapper variety, strength and tasting notes are not published yet.

cigars.about: An unnumbered offshoot of Espinosa's 601 La Bomba Warhead limited editions, made by AJ Fernandez. The first came out in June 2025 and a second, marking the 250th anniversary of the United States, followed in 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Blend shown is the 2025 release (2,500 boxes of 10). The 2026 '250' release (4,000 boxes) uses an undisclosed Ecuadorian wrapper. Retailers list the 2025 as full, but Halfwheel's reviewer found it closer to medium. Neptune lists the 2026 at 5 1/2 x 56 and medium.

cigars.about: A line Espinosa created in 2023 only for the retailers that have Espinosa-branded cigar lounges. It is a medium-bodied short Churchill made at La Zona in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only at Espinosa-branded lounges (10 shops at launch). Espinosa said it is ongoing production but the blend and size may change from time to time.

cigars.about: A 2022 limited edition marking ten years of the La Zona Cigar Factory in Esteli, where Espinosa began making its cigars. It uses a high-priming version of the Brazilian wrapper found on the Laranja line.
cigars.researchNote: 300 boxes of 30 (9,000 cigars). The wrapper is a higher priming of the Brazilian leaf used on Laranja; no source names the seed variety. The filler includes some pelo de oro. Espinosa describes it as full-flavored but not full strength.

cigars.about: A 2022 limited edition marking Espinosa Premium Cigars' first ten years in business. It is a Nicaraguan puro toro with a hybrid habano seed wrapper, made by AJ Fernandez.
cigars.researchNote: 1,500 boxes of 20 (30,000 cigars). Sources disagree on where the wrapper is grown: Halfwheel's announcement and Developing Palates say Nicaraguan, while Halfwheel's later shipping report and Corona Cigar say Ecuadorian habano hybrid.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano), Nicaragua (Jalapa, Esteli, Condega)
cigars.about: The night half of CAO's value-priced FASA series, launched in 2024 alongside FASA Sol. It shares the Cameroon binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler of its siblings but wears a dark Connecticut broadleaf wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: CAO rates it medium to full; Halfwheel's review and Neptune both put it closer to medium. Each FASA blend is made in a different country: Noche in Nicaragua, Sol in Honduras, Sombra in the Dominican Republic.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano), Nicaragua (Jalapa, Esteli, Condega)
cigars.about: The third and final blend in CAO's FASA series, added in April 2025. It puts an Ecuadorian shade-grown wrapper over the same Cameroon binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler as FASA Sol and Noche.
cigars.researchNote: CAO lists it as medium body. Neptune calls the wrapper Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade; CAO only says Ecuadorian shade-grown. Unlike Noche (Nicaragua) and Sol (Honduras), Sombra is rolled in the Dominican Republic.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: U.S. Broadleaf and U.S. Connecticut Shade (barber pole)
cigars.about: A 2026 limited edition of CAO America for the 250th anniversary of the United States. It keeps the two-tone barber pole wrapper but uses only U.S.-grown tobacco throughout, though it is rolled in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is a barber pole of broadleaf and Connecticut shade, so it is not a pure maduro. CAO rates it medium to full; Halfwheel's reviewer found full flavor but only medium strength. One size, production numbers undisclosed.

cigars.about: A 2021 limited edition and one of the largest cigars CAO has made, an 8 x 60 with a car theme. It was sold in an oil can style tin of eight.
cigars.researchNote: One size only, sold in tins of eight. Production numbers were not disclosed and Neptune shows it sold out. Strength is Neptune's rating. Neptune lists Honduran filler alongside the Nicaraguan.

cigars.about: The maduro member of CAO Surplus, a budget bundle line of handmade long-filler cigars with military surplus styling. It is rolled in Honduras with a Mexican San Andres wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: General Cigar calls the line Surplus by CAO; it is not on CAO's own site. Famous lists it medium-full and the Toro at 6 x 52; Neptune lists medium and a 6 x 50 Toro. Sold in bundles of 25.

cigars.about: The mild member of CAO Surplus, a budget bundle line of handmade long-filler cigars with military surplus styling. It is rolled in Honduras with a Honduran-grown Connecticut wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: General Cigar calls the line Surplus by CAO; it is not on CAO's own site. Famous lists it mild-medium; Neptune lists mild. Sold in bundles of 25.

cigars.about: The sweet-tip member of CAO Surplus, a budget bundle line of handmade long-filler cigars with military surplus styling. It is rolled in Honduras with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper and a sweetened cap.
cigars.researchNote: This is a sweetened-cap cigar. General Cigar calls the line Surplus by CAO; it is not on CAO's own site. Famous lists it mild-medium; Neptune lists medium. Sold in bundles of 20.

cigars.about: A CAO blend released in 2022 for the Canadian market only, named for the northern lights. Its filler includes Cuban-seed dark air-cured tobacco grown in southwestern Ontario.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only in Canada, in plain packaging. General Cigar told Halfwheel it was regular ongoing production, not a limited run; whether it is still made today was not confirmed. CAO calls it medium-bodied.

cigars.about: Villiger's Nicaraguan-made take on its 1888 brand, rolled at the company's own Esteli factory, which is run in partnership with Joya de Nicaragua. It is priced as an everyday box cigar and uses some Pennsylvania ligero in the filler.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in Germany and Switzerland in 2022 and in the U.S. in 2023. Villiger's own pages give the Coronita different lengths; halfwheel and Neptune list the U.S. size as 5 3/4 x 43. A 6 x 58 Perfecto was also shown in 2024.

cigars.about: A box-pressed 6 x 54 limited edition from Villiger's Esteli factory, released in 2025 as the first cigar in a Gran Reserva program. The program requires tobacco aged at least two years and cigars rested a year after rolling.
cigars.researchNote: One size only, 1,000 boxes of 10. Villiger calls it medium-full; Neptune lists it as medium. Villiger also sold an unrelated cigar called 1888 Gran Reserva in 2010.

cigars.about: A San Andres wrapped addition to Villiger's 1888 brand, made at the company's Esteli factory. It began shipping to U.S. stores in June 2026.

The dark, maduro member of Villiger's Cuellar family, made by Jochy Blanco's Tabacalera Palma in the Dominican Republic. It is named for Germany's Black Forest and is the strongest of the three Cuellar blends.
cigars.researchNote: Villiger rates it 4 of 5 and Holt's lists it as medium-full, while Neptune and Famous Smoke's spec table list it as full. Famous lists the Lonsdale as 6 x 44, halfwheel as 6 1/2 x 44.

cigars.about: The mild Connecticut member of Villiger's Cuellar family, made by Jochy Blanco's Tabacalera Palma in the Dominican Republic. It was built to be an especially creamy Connecticut and is named for Diego Velazquez de Cuellar, the first Spanish governor of Cuba.
cigars.researchNote: Villiger bills it as mild-plus and rates it 2 of 5; Neptune lists it as mild. The box spells the name Cuellar Kreme with accents. halfwheel's 2024 list shows the Robusto as 5 x 50, while Villiger and Neptune show 5 x 48.

cigars.about: The third Cuellar blend from Villiger, made at Tabacalera Palma in the Dominican Republic. It is a reworked version of the Villiger TAA Exclusive 2021 and sits between the Kreme and the Black Forest in strength.
A mild Connecticut-wrapped cigar from Villiger's Esteli factory, with teal packaging showing a woman at the helm of a ship. The name is Spanish for a female captain.
cigars.researchNote: This is the 2025 reblend. The earlier La Capitana was a Nicaraguan puro made in the Dominican Republic with red and blue packaging. Villiger calls it mild to medium; Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Jalapa seco, Esteli viso and ligero)
cigars.about: A value-priced Villiger line in red, black and white packaging with the slogan Viva La Libertad. Since 2021 it has been made at the company's own factory in Esteli with a Nicaraguan criollo wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The current blend dates from 2021 and reached the U.S. in January 2022. Older La Libertad cigars used a Brazilian wrapper and were made in Honduras by Plasencia, then at ABAM in the Dominican Republic. Villiger calls it medium-plus and rates it 4 of 5.

cigars.about: A Villiger family of handmade cigars in carbon-fibre style packaging, sold as four separate blends named for their country: Honduras, Dominican Republic, Nicaragua and Brazil. The sizes are slightly thicker than standard, hence the plus in the names.
cigars.researchNote: Four different blends share the name, so there is no single wrapper, country or strength. Villiger rates them 2.5 of 5 (Dominican Republic, Ecuador wrapper), 3.5 (Brazil, Arapiraca wrapper), 4 (Honduras) and 5 (Nicaragua).

cigars.about: A mild, lightly spicy Dominican-made cigar from Villiger with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over an Indonesian binder.
cigars.researchNote: Villiger rates it 2 of 5 for strength. The English page says the wrapper comes from Indonesia, but the German original makes clear that is the binder. Sizes are converted from Villiger's metric figures.

cigars.about: A mild Dominican-made Villiger line named for the year Columbus reached the New World and brought tobacco back to Europe. It is a European-market cigar that also gets limited Discovery Edition releases.
cigars.researchNote: Villiger rates it 2 of 5 and names only tobaccos from Ecuador, Indonesia and the Dominican Republic; trade press gives the binder as Indonesian. The limited Discovery Edition (2023 Gran Toro, 2024 Robusto) uses a Dominican piloto ligero binder and is not sold in the U.S.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped blend in Villiger's three-part San'Doro line, alongside the Colorado and the Brazilian Maduro. It uses Nicaraguan binder and filler and launched in 2015.
cigars.researchNote: Made at Oliva's TABOLISA factory at its 2015 launch; in 2021 Villiger said the line would move to its own factory in Esteli. Neptune lists it as mild, Villiger rates it 2.5 of 5, and halfwheel's review of a 2020 limited size put it between mild and medium.

cigars.binder: Mexican San Andres (No. 049); Dominican Republic (No. 041, No. 051)
cigars.factory: Villiger de Nicaragua (No. 049); ABAM Cigars (No. 041, No. 051)
cigars.about: Villiger's Limited Release (VLR) series is a run of small-batch cigars, each with its own blend, aged six months before release and sold through a small group of retailers. The numbers refer to the aging-room shelf where the cigars rested.
cigars.researchNote: Every release is a different blend of about 4,000 to 5,000 cigars. The first, a 2023 Toro, had a Mexican San Andres wrapper; No. 049 uses a habano oscuro wrapper. Red bands mean made in Nicaragua, blue and gold mean made at ABAM in the Dominican Republic.

cigars.about: A limited Villiger line that began as the cigar handed to visitors at the company's Miami office. Despite the name it is made in the Dominican Republic, at the ABAM factory under blender Jose Matias Maragoto.
cigars.researchNote: Not made in Miami. The blend shown is the 2022 release (500 boxes of 10 per size); the 2023 Canonazo has an Ecuadorian habano wrapper and some Peruvian filler. Villiger rates it 3 of 5, and halfwheel found the 2022 Laguito closer to medium-full.

cigars.factory: Fabrica de Puros Maya Selva Cigars
cigars.about: Villiger's yearly limited edition for retailers in the Tobacconists' Association of America. The company has a different factory make it each year, so every release is a different blend.
cigars.researchNote: Details shown are the 2024 release, a Honduran puro of 500 boxes of 20. Earlier years: 2020 E.P. Carrillo (6 x 54, Ecuadorian Sumatra), 2021 Tabacalera Palma (6 x 54, Ecuadorian habano), 2022 La Zona (6 x 52), 2023 Aganorsa (6 1/4 x 52, Nicaraguan puro).

cigars.about: A limited edition from Villiger's own factory in Esteli, first released in 2022 and offered in a different size each time. The boxes show the Mombacho volcano, and Villiger says the 2026 release is the last.
cigars.researchNote: The blend shown is the 2026 release (2,000 boxes, U.S. launch set for December 2026); the 2022 and 2023 used the same wrapper and binder. Villiger rates the 2022 Torpedo 4 of 5 and the 2023 Perfecto 3.5, while Famous Smoke lists the Torpedo as full.

cigars.about: A limited Villiger release made only for U.S. retailers. The 2022 edition is a box-pressed Nicaraguan puro rolled at the La Zona factory in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Blend and sizes shown are the 2022 edition per halfwheel, which says the first edition came out in 2020 from E.P. Carrillo's factory. Holt's closeout listing has a Robusto 5 x 50, Toro 6 x 50 and Gordo 6 x 60 and dates it to 2021; the strength and flavors come from that listing.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan-made cigar created in 2013 for Villiger's 125th anniversary, with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco. It is now sold by a few retailers as an inexpensive 20-count bundle.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's calls it 125 Habano and Famous Smoke calls it 125th. The 2013 release was 30,000 boxed cigars in three 56-ring sizes (Canton 4 1/2, Lucerne 5 1/2, Mondo 6 1/2); the sizes shown are the current bundles. It is unclear whether it is still being made.

cigars.about: A Brazilian puro from Villiger's own factory in Bahia, wrapped in a Connecticut shade leaf grown in Brazil. It launched in 2020 next to a Maduro version and shares its name with the factory.
The darker of Villiger's two Brazilian puros, made at the company's factory in Bahia with an Arapiraca wrapper. It launched in 2020 alongside the Claro.

A Nicaraguan puro from Aganorsa Leaf named for Arsenio Ramos, the Cuban-born blender who led the company's factory team and died in 2018. It is built on what the company calls his favorite blend, and the Corona was his preferred size.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates strength 3 of 5 and calls it medium to full-bodied; Neptune lists it as full. It is a new blend, not the older Casa Fernandez Arsenio cigars.

cigars.about: The Corojo-wrapped member of Aganorsa Leaf's flagship Aniversario series, a box-pressed Nicaraguan puro made entirely from the company's own tobacco. It was sold as Casa Fernandez Aniversario Corojo until a 2021 rebrand.
cigars.researchNote: Rebranded in 2021 from Casa Fernandez Aniversario Corojo; all sizes are box pressed. The maker rates strength 4 of 5, while Neptune lists it as full. halfwheel places production in Estelí, though Neptune still describes it as rolled in Miami.

cigars.about: The maduro member of Aganorsa Leaf's Aniversario series, a box-pressed Nicaraguan puro under the company's own shade-grown Corojo maduro wrapper. It started as small limited runs and became a regular line in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Began in 2020 as a limited Casa Fernandez Aniversario Cuba 109 Maduro rolled in Miami; regular production since 2022. The maker rates strength 3 of 5, while Neptune lists it as full. The maker's site shows a different size list than halfwheel and retailers.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped third blend in Aganorsa Leaf's Aniversario series, pairing an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper with the company's Nicaraguan binder and filler. It smokes fuller than most Connecticut cigars.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates strength 3 of 5, but halfwheel's review found it building from medium to full with full body, and Neptune lists it as full. The Gran Robusto and Toro are box pressed; the Tubo, added in 2026, is round.

cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro marking 25 years since Eduardo Fernández founded Aganorsa, made entirely from tobacco grown on the company's farms. It came in one toro size.
cigars.researchNote: One size only, limited to 1,000 boxes of 10 (10,000 cigars). halfwheel lists the wrapper only as Nicaraguan; the maker's site specifies Aganorsa Corojo.

cigars.about: The Habano blend in Aganorsa Leaf's core La Validación series, built on the company's Nicaraguan Corojo and Criollo fillers. The series name comes from the company president's habit of calling a test smoke a validation.
cigars.researchNote: Renamed in 2022 from Casa Fernandez Aganorsa Leaf Habano with the same blend. The maker lists an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, while halfwheel and Neptune call it a Nicaraguan puro. The maker lists the Toro as 6 x 52; halfwheel and retailers say 6 1/4 x 52.

cigars.about: The Corojo blend in Aganorsa Leaf's core La Validación series, a Nicaraguan puro wrapped in the company's own Corojo leaf. It is one of four everyday blends sold in the same three sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Renamed in 2022 from Casa Fernandez Aganorsa Leaf Corojo with the same blend. The maker rates strength 4 of 5; Famous lists medium and Neptune full. The maker lists the Toro as 6 x 52; halfwheel and retailers say 6 1/4 x 52.

cigars.about: The maduro blend in Aganorsa Leaf's core La Validación series, with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over the company's Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is the strongest of the four La Validación blends.
cigars.researchNote: Renamed in 2022 from Casa Fernandez Aganorsa Leaf Maduro with the same blend. The maker rates strength 4.5 of 5 and retailers list it as full. The maker lists the Toro as 6 x 52; halfwheel and retailers say 6 1/4 x 52.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Corojo and Criollo, Estelí and Jalapa)
cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA), now called Aganorsa
cigars.about: The maduro follow-up to Guardian of the Farm, a Nicaraguan puro from Aganorsa Leaf named for the dogs that guard its farms. It uses the company's own shade-grown Corojo maduro wrapper and is a fuller smoke than the original.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates strength 4 of 5 and halfwheel found it strong, but Neptune lists it as medium. The Campeon has a 109-style head and the JJ is box pressed. halfwheel listed the JJ at 5 1/2 inches at launch; the maker now lists 5 1/4.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA), now called Aganorsa
cigars.about: A Guardian of the Farm extension from Aganorsa Leaf named for the three-headed dog of Greek myth. It is a Nicaraguan puro and the first Aganorsa blend to use a Corojo 2012 wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Debuted in November 2021 as a limited toro for Cigar.com; the regular sizes shipped in February 2022. The maker rates strength 4 of 5, while Neptune lists it as medium. halfwheel listed the Toro at 54 ring at launch; the maker and retailers list 52.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped version of JFR, Aganorsa Leaf's value brand whose name stands for Just For Retailers. It pairs an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler and is finished with a pigtail cap and tucked foot.
cigars.researchNote: The blend predates 2019, when it was repackaged and put back on the price list; the Junior size was added in 2024.

cigars.about: A box-pressed line from Aganorsa Leaf marking 20 years of its JFR value brand, with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. Each cigar has a pigtail cap and a covered foot.
cigars.researchNote: Strength sources disagree: the maker rates it 3 of 5, but halfwheel's review of the Gordito and Famous both call it full strength.

cigars.about: The big-ring offshoot of Aganorsa Leaf's JFR brand, with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is known for oversized formats, starting with the 8 x 80 Mambo.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates strength 3.5 of 5; Neptune lists it as full. A 10 x 100 novelty size is also sold. The maker lists El Chiquito at 4 1/4 inches, while halfwheel and Neptune say 4 3/4.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA), now called Aganorsa
cigars.about: A brushed-foot Nicaraguan puro in Aganorsa Leaf's JFR Lunatic family. The wrapper stops short of the foot, so the first puffs are binder and filler alone before the Corojo wrapper joins in.
cigars.researchNote: Debuted in 2016 as a single 7 x 50 Churchill and was relaunched in 2020 with new sizes and packaging. The maker rates strength 3.5 of 5; Neptune lists it as medium, while halfwheel's review found it full. It uses a double binder.

cigars.about: A trio of short, fat perfectos in Aganorsa Leaf's JFR Lunatic family, made entirely of Nicaraguan tobacco under a shade-grown Corojo maduro wrapper. The maker bills it as its strongest cigar.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's site labels the line JFR Lunatic Locos; halfwheel and retailers use Loco.

cigars.about: A JFR Lunatic extension that Aganorsa Leaf makes exclusively for Famous Smoke Shop, with a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. Unlike most Lunatic cigars it comes in fairly traditional sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke Shop exclusive, so it is not on the maker's own site. It launched in Robusto and Toro; the Gordo was added later.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andrés Maduro and Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade (barber pole)
cigars.about: A barber-pole version of JFR Lunatic Hysteria, made by Aganorsa Leaf for Famous Smoke Shop. It twists the original San Andrés maduro wrapper together with an Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade leaf over Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke Shop exclusive; Famous is the only source found and the binder is not published. Its spec table lists medium strength, while its description calls the profile full-bodied.

cigars.about: A set of fat perfectos sold under the JFR Lunatic Hysteria name, made by Aganorsa Leaf for Famous Smoke Shop. They are full-strength Nicaraguan cigars with a dark maduro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke Shop exclusive and the only source found. Famous contradicts itself on the wrapper: its spec table says Nicaraguan Corojo maduro, its descriptions say Mexican San Andrés, so the wrapper is left blank. The three sizes match the JFR Lunatic Loco perfectos.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA), now called Aganorsa
cigars.about: A box-pressed, stronger take on the JFR value brand, introduced in 2014 when the company was still called Casa Fernandez. The Maduro version sits alongside a Corojo version in the same sizes.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel reported a Mexican San Andrés wrapper at launch, while Neptune describes a Nicaraguan Aganorsa maduro wrapper. The line is not on the maker's current site and Neptune stocks only the 7 x 70, so current production status is unclear.

cigars.about: The Corojo-wrapped version of New Cuba, Aganorsa Leaf's budget bundle line made in Nicaragua from the company's own tobacco. It is sold in bundles rather than boxes to keep the price down.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune and Famous both list it as medium. The maker's single New Cuba page covers the Corojo, Connecticut and Maduro wrappers together and shows 4 of 5 strength.

cigars.about: The all-Nicaraguan version of Room101's Farce line, launched in late 2022. It is the only Farce blend rolled at Joya de Nicaragua instead of by William Ventura in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper varietal is not disclosed. Room101 lists the Robusto at 5 1/2 x 50, halfwheel at 5 1/4 x 50. Neptune's spec table says Medium while its description says medium to full.

cigars.about: The maduro-wrapped half of Room101's two-blend Doomsayer line, introduced in 2019. It shares its binder and filler with Doomsayer Passive and comes in one 6 x 55 toro sold in 55-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Announced in 2019 as Doomsayer Maduro with the wrapper undisclosed; Room101 now lists it as Ecuadorian Maduro. The sister blend Passive uses an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Criollo '98 from Condega, Jalapa and Esteli)
cigars.about: The Connecticut shade version of Room101's value-priced Big Payback line. It first shipped in 2016 and was brought back in late 2020 with a reworked blend.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree. Halfwheel reported the 2020 relaunch as Nicaraguan binder and filler made at Joya de Nicaragua; Room101 now lists a Mexican binder; Cigars Direct lists Honduras with Dominican filler, which matches the original 2016 version made by Camacho.

cigars.about: A broadleaf-wrapped, value-priced Room101 line that revived the Big Payback name in 2019. It is made at General Cigar's factory in Danli, Honduras and sold in bundles of 20 and boxes of 40.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are from Room101's site. Halfwheel in 2019 and three retailers list a Connecticut Shade binder with Dominican, Honduran and Nicaraguan filler. Neptune and Cigars Direct list it as Medium, Cigars Daily as Medium-Full.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro in Room101's value-priced Big Payback line, added in 2022. It is rolled at Joya de Nicaragua and sold in boxes of 40.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Condega, ASP), Honduras (La Entrada), Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano)
cigars.about: A 7 x 70 Big Payback that returned in June 2023 with a blend used only in this size. It is made at STG Danli in Honduras and sold in boxes of 30.
cigars.researchNote: Room101's site calls it the 70s Original. Its blend is different from the other Big Payback lines. Retailers disagree on strength: Cigars Direct lists Medium-Full, Cigars Daily lists Medium.

cigars.about: The 7 x 70 size of Room101's Big Payback Maduro, released in August 2024 with its own blue and yellow bands. It is made at STG Danli in Honduras and sold in boxes of 30.
cigars.researchNote: This is the 7 x 70 size of Big Payback Maduro with its own branding. Halfwheel says it shares that line's blend, though Room101's site lists the two differently. Retailers disagree on strength: Neptune lists Medium, Cigars Direct Medium-Full.

cigars.about: A stronger 7 x 70 addition to Room101's Big Payback line, shipped in April 2026. It is made at STG Danli in Honduras and sold in boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: Offered only in the 7 x 70 size.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: Room101's space-themed line, made by AJ Fernandez in Esteli with an Ecuadorian Connecticut shade wrapper. The name began as a 2015 limited edition and became a regular line in 2023, when it placed third on halfwheel's Top 25.
cigars.researchNote: The current blend dates from August 2023. The 2015 original was a limited Nicaraguan puro made at Camacho's factory in Honduras. Strength is listed from Mild (Cigars Daily) to Medium (Neptune).

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A maduro-wrapped Nicaraguan puro added to the Johnny Tobacconaut line in June 2026. It is made by AJ Fernandez and sold in boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: Room101 calls it full-bodied. Halfwheel's reviewer found the Robusto topped out at medium-full strength.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro marking ten years since the first Johnny Tobacconaut in 2015. Matt Booth made it with AJ Fernandez in a single 6 x 52 toro that shipped in September 2025.
cigars.researchNote: The tobacco varietals and the production number were not disclosed. Room101 calls it full-bodied and Neptune lists Full, but halfwheel's reviewer found the strength between medium and medium-full.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Criollo '98 and one undisclosed varietal), USA (Pennsylvania)
cigars.about: The third version of Hit & Run, the brand Matt Booth started with Robert Caldwell in 2017. This 2024 Room101 release has a San Andres wrapper and is made by the Ventura family in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers disagree on strength: Neptune lists Medium, Cigars Direct Medium-Full and Cigars Daily Full. Halfwheel calls the Nicaraguan filler corojo 98 where Room101 says Criollo '98. Halfwheel says the Ventura family makes it, but not in their original factory, which burned in 2022.

cigars.about: Room101's second anniversary cigar, a Nicaraguan puro with a maduro wrapper released in December 2020. It came in one 6 x 54 torpedo and was limited to 1,000 boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: The factory was undisclosed at release; halfwheel later named Oliva as the maker when the blend was re-rolled for the 2025 Anniversary Humidor. Neptune lists it as Full, but halfwheel's reviewer found it medium in strength.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: Room101's 2022 anniversary cigar, a 6 x 52 Nicaraguan puro made by AJ Fernandez from his own tobacco. It wears a pink band and was limited to 1,500 boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel lists the wrapper only as Nicaragua; Neptune and Cigars Direct describe it as maduro. Neptune lists it as Full and Cigars Direct as Medium-Full, while halfwheel's reviewer found the strength closer to medium.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: Room101's 2023 anniversary cigar, a 6 x 52 toro made entirely of Nicaraguan tobacco from AJ Fernandez's farms. It shipped in July 2023 in red packaging.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper varietal and the production number were not disclosed. Halfwheel's reviewer found it very strong.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A 6 x 52 Nicaraguan puro made by AJ Fernandez for Room101's 15th year. It shipped in February 2025 and was limited to 2,000 boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper varietal is not disclosed. Cigars Direct calls it a Nicaraguan maduro; Neptune lists the wrapper shade as natural. Neptune lists it as Full and Cigars Direct as Medium-Full, while the launch announcement called it medium-bodied.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: Room101's 2026 anniversary cigar, a 6 x 52 Nicaraguan puro made by AJ Fernandez. It shipped in August 2026 and is limited to 2,500 boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: There was no 16th Anniversary cigar. Neptune and halfwheel's reviewer put the strength at medium, while Cigars Daily lists it as Full. The wrapper varietal is not disclosed.

cigars.about: One of Room101's oldest lines, first released in 2011 and named for the Japanese word for a severed head. It now comes back as occasional limited editions, most recently a 6 1/2 x 50 perfecto in October 2025.
cigars.researchNote: The blend changes by edition; these specs are the 2025 release. The 2011 original had an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper and was made at Camacho in Honduras. Neptune lists Full and Cigars Direct Medium-Full, but halfwheel's reviewer found it mild to medium.

cigars.about: A Room101 sub-brand from 2012 that returned in 2023 as a limited Nicaraguan puro made by Oliva. The revival came in one 6 x 50 toro, limited to 2,000 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: These specs are the 2023 version, whose varietals are undisclosed. The 2012 original was a different blend with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper and Brazilian Mata Fina binder. Neptune lists Full, Cigars Direct Medium-Full.

cigars.about: A perfecto Matt Booth released in December 2014 as a tribute to the uncle who introduced him to cigars. It was made at Davidoff's LAEPE factory in Honduras in a run of 5,000 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: It was a one-time limited run and Room101 now lists it in its vault of retired cigars. Neptune lists it as Medium; halfwheel's reviewer found it built to medium-full.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A single-size Diesel made by AJ Fernandez as the brand's 2022 exclusive for Tobacconists' Association of America (TAA) shops. It came in 10-count boxes made to look like a novel.
cigars.researchNote: TAA exclusive limited to 1,000 boxes of 10. It was announced as Diesel Tempest and renamed before shipping; a different Diesel Tempest came out for TAA in 2024. The maker calls it full-bodied and no separate strength rating is published.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The first of six seasonal Diesel Sunday Gravy blends, made by AJ Fernandez and blended with Justin Andrews. Each blend came in one size priced at about $5.
cigars.researchNote: First of six Sunday Gravy blends. halfwheel and Neptune report an Ecuadorian habano wrapper, while Diesel's own site lists the wrapper only as Nicaraguan. Diesel rates it medium to full; Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The second Diesel Sunday Gravy blend, a thick robusto with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over a Cameroon binder. It is made by AJ Fernandez and was sold for one season at about $5.
cigars.researchNote: Second of six Sunday Gravy blends, each sold in one size. Strength is from Neptune's listing; Diesel's site only rates the San Marzano blend.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The third Diesel Sunday Gravy blend, a Nicaraguan puro in a 6 x 50 toro. It is made by AJ Fernandez and was sold for one season at about $5.
cigars.researchNote: Third of six Sunday Gravy blends. halfwheel's review found it medium in strength and body; Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The fourth Diesel Sunday Gravy blend, a slim 5 1/4 x 45 cigar with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over a Connecticut Broadleaf binder. It is made by AJ Fernandez and was sold in bundles of 10 for one season.
cigars.researchNote: Fourth of six Sunday Gravy blends. No strength rating is published; the maker said the blend deliberately stays away from power in favor of complexity.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The fifth Diesel Sunday Gravy blend, a 5 x 56 robusto extra with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper and Honduran filler. It is made by AJ Fernandez and was sold for one season at about $5.
cigars.researchNote: Fifth of six Sunday Gravy blends, sold in packs of five. The maker called it a medium-plus blend; Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The sixth and final Diesel Sunday Gravy blend, a 6 x 52 toro with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper over Nicaraguan habano binder and filler. It is made by AJ Fernandez and was sold in 10-count boxes at about $5 a cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Sixth and last Sunday Gravy blend. The maker's press release describes it as full-bodied and Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.about: A Dominican-made Villiger with an Ecuador Habano wrapper over Dominican and Nicaraguan long filler. It is sold in 20-count boxes through Holt's.
cigars.researchNote: Sold through Holt's, which calls it an exclusive; Villiger's own site does not list it. The binder and the factory are not published.

cigars.about: A budget Villiger bundle cigar made in Esteli, Nicaragua, with an Ecuador Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos. It is sold in bundles of 20 as an everyday smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's lists it as mild to medium; Neptune calls it mild. The factory is not published.

cigars.about: A budget Villiger bundle cigar made in Nicaragua with a San Andres maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan long filler. It is the stronger partner to Selecto Connecticut and is sold in bundles of 20.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's lists it as medium to full; Neptune calls it medium. The factory is not published.

cigars.about: A Dominican-made Villiger with a Connecticut Shade wrapper over Dominican long filler, described by Holt's as a follow-up to Villiger Black Forest. It is sold in 20-count boxes through Holt's.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's is the only seller found and Villiger's own site does not list it. The binder, the factory name and where the wrapper is grown are not published.

cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro made in 2024 to mark Heinrich Villiger's 94th birthday. It is a 6 x 58 diadema, each in its own gold-lined presentation box.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 500 boxes of five and sold in Switzerland and Germany, not the U.S. The leaf varieties and strength are not published.

cigars.about: Villiger's fourth Chinese zodiac release, a 6 x 52 torpedo made at Villiger de Nicaragua for the 2026 Year of the Horse. It follows the Rabbit, Dragon and Snake editions.
cigars.researchNote: Exclusive to the Asian market and not sold in the U.S. Limited to 1,000 boxes of 10 at $25 a cigar. No strength rating is published.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped version of Aganorsa Leaf's New Cuba value line, sold in bundles. It pairs an Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper with Aganorsa's Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: One of three New Cuba wrappers (Corojo, Maduro, Connecticut) sold in bundles. Neptune and Famous list it as mild; Aganorsa's site shows one strength rating for the whole line, 4 of 5. New Cuba Superior is the separate boxed version.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Aganorsa Leaf's New Cuba value line, a Nicaraguan puro sold in bundles. It is made with tobacco from Aganorsa's own Nicaraguan farms.
cigars.researchNote: Aganorsa's site shows 4 of 5 on its strength scale; Neptune and Famous both list it as full, though their descriptions call it medium-bodied. Famous describes it as a Cuban-sandwich blend.

cigars.about: A boxed, all long filler step up from Aganorsa Leaf's New Cuba bundle line, introduced in 2023. It was built as a mild Connecticut for newer smokers, since most of the company's cigars are much stronger.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers often list it as New Cuba Superior Connecticut. The maker's site shows the Corona as 5 x 44, while halfwheel, Neptune and Famous list 5 1/2 x 44. The 6 x 60 Titan was added in 2024.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro rolled in small batches in Miami, Florida, using Aganorsa-grown tobacco. It is sold under Casa Fernandez, a brand of Aganorsa.
cigars.researchNote: Rolled in Miami, not Nicaragua; the factory name is not published. Neptune and Famous call it full, Holt's lists medium-full. Famous names the wrapper as Corojo, while Neptune and Holt's just say Nicaraguan.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Casa Fernandez Miami Reserva, rolled in Miami, Florida, with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is sold under Casa Fernandez, a brand of Aganorsa.
cigars.researchNote: Rolled in Miami, not Nicaragua; the factory name is not published. Unlike the Corojo version it is not a Nicaraguan puro, since the wrapper is Mexican.

cigars.line: Rare Leaf Reserve Daily Edition Connecticut
cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped take on Aganorsa Leaf's Rare Leaf Reserve, made in 2025 as an exclusive for the Phoenix retailer Cigars Daily. It was developed by Aganorsa's Terence Reilly and Cigars Daily founder Tim Swanson.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only by Cigars Daily in Phoenix, in one 6 x 54 toro. No production cap has been announced. halfwheel says Nicaraguan Corojo 99 and Criollo 98 sit under the wrapper without saying which is binder or filler.

cigars.about: A Connecticut broadleaf cigar made for Crowned Heads by My Father Cigars, created in 2014 as an exclusive for the company's home state of Tennessee. It became a nationwide regular line with three sizes in late 2025.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only in Tennessee from 2014 until November 2025, when it went nationwide and gained the CG and Toro sizes. The maker calls it medium to full bodied; Neptune lists it as medium and halfwheel's review found it around medium.

cigars.line: Four Kicks Mule Kick Limited Edition
cigars.factory: Casa Carrillo (formerly Tabacalera La Alianza S.A.)
cigars.about: An occasional limited edition offshoot of Four Kicks, made by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo's factory in the Dominican Republic. It always comes in one 5 7/8 x 52 size, but the wrapper and blend change from release to release.
cigars.researchNote: The blend changes by year, so no single strength applies. Fields show LE 2025 (2,500 boxes of 10). LE 2023 used an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over a Dominican binder; the 2012 original used a darker Ecuadorian habano wrapper.

cigars.factory: Casa Carrillo (formerly Tabacalera La Alianza S.A.)
cigars.about: A version of Four Kicks with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, made by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo's factory in the Dominican Republic. It is based on a runner-up blend from the original 2011 Four Kicks development.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel and Developing Palates found medium to medium-plus strength with an all-Nicaraguan filler. Neptune lists it as full, says the filler is Dominican and Nicaraguan, and marks the Corona Gorda size as discontinued.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan-made follow-up to Crowned Heads Court Reserve XVIII with an Ecuadorian habano oscuro wrapper. CHC stands for Crowned Heads Court and the E is for Eruption, the Eddie Van Halen guitar solo.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2021 as regular production, but Neptune now marks its sizes as discontinued, so it may no longer be made. The maker described it as medium-plus bodied.

cigars.factory: TacaNicsa (also called D'Hatuey Tabacos S.A.; formerly Tabacalera Pichardo)
cigars.about: A yearly limited edition from Crowned Heads with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper, made in Estelí, Nicaragua. Its filler is 75 percent ligero, which makes it one of the company's stronger blends.
cigars.researchNote: Same blend each year in a different size: 2,000 boxes of 12 in 2024 and 2,500 boxes of 12 in 2025. Neptune lists it as full; Developing Palates' review of the 2025 found it closer to medium.

cigars.factory: TacaNicsa (also called D'Hatuey Tabacos S.A.; formerly Tabacalera Pichardo)
cigars.about: A limited edition from Crowned Heads with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper, made in Estelí, Nicaragua. It began as an event-only cigar and is named after a 19th-century building in Nashville.
cigars.researchNote: The 2015 original was an event-only cigar made by My Father, first announced as Snake Oil. It came back in 2022 from Eradio Pichardo's factory, still event-only, and first went on retail sale in 2024 (1,500 boxes of 12). 2025 had three sizes at 700 boxes of 21 each.

cigars.factory: TacaNicsa (also called D'Hatuey Tabacos S.A.; formerly Tabacalera Pichardo)
cigars.about: A limited edition version of Blood Medicine that swaps the Ecuadorian habano wrapper for a Nicaraguan corojo leaf. It is made in Estelí, Nicaragua, and was blended to be darker and more intense than the original.
cigars.researchNote: Same binder and filler as Blood Medicine. 2025 was a single toro (2,400 boxes of 12); 2026 has three sizes at 800 boxes of 21 each. halfwheel found strength from medium to full across samples; Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.about: A regular production Connecticut broadleaf line made at NACSA in Estelí, named for Nashville's Lower Broadway. It was the first Crowned Heads cigar to wear the company's 2025 rebranded bands.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel and Developing Palates both found medium strength with a fuller body. Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.about: One of two Coroneta blends launched together in 2024, each from a different factory. The Habano is made at NACSA in Nicaragua with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: Sister blend to Coroneta Maduro, which is made in the Dominican Republic at Casa Carrillo.

cigars.about: One of two Coroneta blends launched together in 2024, each from a different factory. The Maduro is made by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo's Casa Carrillo in the Dominican Republic with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Sister blend to Coroneta Habano, which is made in Nicaragua at NACSA. Strength is disputed: Neptune lists it as full, while Cigar Dojo's review rated it medium. No maker rating was found.

cigars.factory: Casa Carrillo (formerly Tabacalera La Alianza S.A.)
cigars.about: A Crowned Heads line made by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo's factory in the Dominican Republic, launched in 2023 as the company's most expensive line to that point. It uses a shade-grown Nicaraguan Jalapa wrapper and fillers aged at least three years.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is shade grown, not sun grown; no seed type is published. halfwheel found medium-full strength with a full body, while Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.about: A Connecticut broadleaf line whose name is French for pastry chef, known for its use of Costa Rican filler. It started as a 2021 limited edition and became a regular Crowned Heads line in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Moved from Tabacalera Pichardo to NACSA in late 2022. It became regular production in 2022, but Neptune now marks every size discontinued and lists the regular sizes as made by Casa Carrillo in the Dominican Republic; no other source confirms either. The No. 2 belicoso was a limited run.

cigars.factory: TacaNicsa (also called D'Hatuey Tabacos S.A.; formerly Tabacalera Pichardo)
cigars.about: A Connecticut broadleaf extension of the Mil Días line, made at Eradio Pichardo's factory in Estelí, Nicaragua. It is a new blend built from scratch, not the original Mil Días with a different wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel found medium strength that rises to medium-full in the final third. Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made by My Father Cigars with tobacco grown on the Garcia family's own farms. It is the first new regular Crowned Heads line from My Father in a decade and is a riff on the discontinued Las Mareas.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel's review found medium to medium-plus strength and a medium body. Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.factory: TacaNicsa (also called D'Hatuey Tabacos S.A.; formerly Tabacalera Pichardo)
cigars.about: A lower-priced regular production cigar from Crowned Heads, sold in bundles of 10 in a single 5 x 54 size. It is made in Estelí, Nicaragua and named after the White Zombie song Thunder Kiss '65.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is Neptune's listing; no maker rating was found.

cigars.about: A box-pressed torpedo made by My Father Cigars as a Crowned Heads exclusive for retailers in Texas. It shares its Connecticut broadleaf blend with Tennessee Waltz.
cigars.researchNote: Texas regional exclusive, occasionally offered to other retailers. It was off shelves from 2019 to 2022 because of a broadleaf shortage, so supply can be spotty.

cigars.factory: TacaNicsa (also called D'Hatuey Tabacos S.A.; formerly Tabacalera Pichardo)
cigars.about: The yearly Crowned Heads cigar sold only through Tobacconists' Association of America member shops. Since 2024 it has carried this plain name in place of The Angel's Anvil and The Lost Angel.
cigars.researchNote: The blend changes each year. Fields show 2025 (750 boxes of 10). The 2024 was made at Casa Carrillo in the Dominican Republic with an Ecuadorian HVA wrapper, Ecuadorian binder and Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania broadleaf fillers (500 boxes of 20).

cigars.factory: Casa Carrillo (formerly Tabacalera La Alianza S.A.)
cigars.about: The name Crowned Heads used from 2021 to 2023 for its yearly cigar sold only through Tobacconists' Association of America shops. It was billed as a prequel to the earlier Angel's Anvil releases.
cigars.researchNote: The blend changed every year. Fields show 2023 (1,000 boxes of 20). The 2021 (San Andrés wrapper) and 2022 (Ecuadorian habano wrapper) were made at Tabacalera Pichardo in Nicaragua. The name was dropped in 2024 for Crowned Heads TAA Exclusive.

cigars.about: A limited edition made by My Father Cigars in 2024 to mark ten years of the Las Calaveras series. The blend recalls the original 2014 Las Calaveras and came back in 2026 in three sizes.
cigars.researchNote: 2024 was one 6 x 52 toro, 2,500 boxes of 10. The 2026 return is sold as Décimo 2026 in three sizes. halfwheel gives the D54 as 5 5/8 x 54, while Neptune lists it as 6 x 54.

cigars.about: A 2022 limited edition toro made at NACSA in Estelí, Nicaragua, the second Crowned Heads blend from that factory. The name means blue and gold and nods to a favorite blended whisky of tobacco man Gustavo Cura.
cigars.researchNote: Single size, limited to 2,500 boxes of 12. halfwheel found medium to medium-plus strength with a medium-full body.

cigars.about: The fifth blend in the box-pressed 2012 by Oscar line, the first line Oscar Valladares brought to market. It puts an Ecuadorian Sumatra-seed wrapper over Honduran and Nicaraguan tobacco and is made at his factory in Danli, Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: All sizes are box-pressed. The maker and Neptune list the Short Robusto at 4 x 50; halfwheel's launch story listed it at 4 x 52.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andrés maduro and candela (barber pole)
cigars.about: A barber pole version of the 2012 by Oscar line that twists a dark Mexican San Andrés leaf with a green candela leaf. It began in late 2017 as an exclusive for The Cigar Shop in the Carolinas and later went nationwide.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrapper leaves: Mexican San Andrés maduro and a candela leaf whose origin is not disclosed. The Toro is box-pressed; the Lancero was added in 2020.

cigars.about: A Honduran puro made to mark ten years of the Leaf by Oscar line, with a criollo-seed wrapper from the company's La Florida Jamastrán farm. Like the rest of the line, each cigar comes wrapped in a tobacco leaf instead of cellophane.
cigars.researchNote: The bands are made from processed plantain leaves.

cigars.line: Leaf by Oscar Broadleaf Limited Edition 2025
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Honduran-grown Connecticut Broadleaf seed, aged three years
cigars.about: The first limited edition in the Leaf by Oscar line and the company's first use of a broadleaf wrapper, which was grown in Honduras from Connecticut broadleaf seed. It was a one-time run of 1,500 numbered boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is broadleaf seed grown in Honduras, not U.S. Connecticut Broadleaf, although Neptune lists it as USA. Neptune also calls it full strength; halfwheel's review found it medium-full.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andrés and Honduran-grown Connecticut Shade (barber pole)
cigars.about: A barber pole Leaf by Oscar that was first sold only in Asia from 2018 to 2020. In October 2023 an aged batch came to the United States as an exclusive for the online retailer Cigora, sold in bundles of 20.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrapper leaves: Mexican San Andrés and Honduran Connecticut Shade. The U.S. release was a Cigora exclusive. The maker describes it as medium-bodied; no strength rating is published.

cigars.about: The original blend of The Oscar line, introduced in 2016. Each cigar is partly covered in a candela leaf that is removed before smoking, and the 11-count boxes are built to look like cigar molds.
cigars.researchNote: First sold simply as The Oscar; it took the Habano name after the Maduro arrived in 2017. Neptune lists it as medium; the maker says medium to full.

cigars.about: The second blend in The Oscar line, added in 2017 with a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper in place of the Habano. It keeps the line's candela leaf sleeve and cigar-mold style boxes of 11.
cigars.researchNote: The candela leaf covering the cigar is packaging and comes off before smoking. The Corona size was added in 2020.

cigars.about: The third blend in The Oscar line, released in 2023 with a Connecticut-seed wrapper grown in Honduras. Like the others it comes partly covered in a candela leaf and packed in mold-style boxes of 11.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists it as mild and halfwheel found the strength mild; Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.about: A 2018 release named for Honduran painter Elmer Ciserón Bautista, whose work appears on five different box lids. It was the first Oscar Valladares cigar blended without any Honduran tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Production was 2,500 boxes of 20: 500 boxes for each of five box paintings. The blend is the same in every box. The maker still lists it on its site.

cigars.about: The Connecticut follow-up to the 1970s-themed Super Fly, sold in pink boxes. It was introduced at the 2020 TPE show and uses a Honduran-grown Connecticut wrapper over tobacco from three countries.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists it as medium; Neptune lists it as mild and halfwheel's first review found it mild to medium. The Super Fly lines were the first Valladares blends to use Dominican tobacco.

cigars.about: A hunting-themed Honduran puro in camouflage packaging, released in 2019. The Natural uses a wrapper from the Copán region over binder and filler from Valladares's own farms.
cigars.researchNote: One of two Wild Hunter blends; the other is the darker Oscuro. The wrapper varietal is not published.

cigars.about: The dark-wrapper version of Wild Hunter, the hunting-themed Honduran puro Oscar Valladares released in 2019. It uses an oscuro leaf from the Copán region over Honduran binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker says medium to full; Neptune lists it as full. The wrapper varietal is not published.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andrés maduro with a Honduran candela foot wrap
cigars.about: Released in 2022 to mark ten years of Oscar Valladares Tobacco & Co. It pairs a dark Mexican wrapper with a band of green candela at the foot and comes in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the filler: the maker's site lists Honduras, while halfwheel and retailers list Nicaraguan filler aged at least five years. Neptune calls it medium and halfwheel's reviewer found it mild to medium. The Salomon is 7 inches with a 52/60 ring.

cigars.about: A 2022 release rolled with only binder and filler and no wrapper leaf, so it looks like an unfinished bunch. It has no cap and a brushed foot, and it is sold in 50-count cabinets.
cigars.researchNote: There is no wrapper: the outer leaf is the Honduran binder. With no cap, it does not need to be cut. The maker says mild to medium; Cigars Direct lists it as medium to full.

cigars.about: A pair of blends from 2021 sold in white and red boxes, with bands that have fold-out wings. It started as a private label for Santa Clara and JR Cigar before Oscar Valladares took over distribution in 2023.
cigars.researchNote: Two different cigars: Claro (Heaven) has a Honduran Connecticut wrapper and is mild to medium; Oscuro (Hell) has a Nicaraguan oscuro wrapper and is medium. Creamy, nutty notes belong to the Claro; chocolate, earth and red pepper to the Oscuro.

cigars.about: A line named for Oscar Valladares's son that debuted in Europe in 2023 and is reblended in small yearly editions. The U.S. version is a 6 x 52 Toro packed in individual coffins, limited to 2,000 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Blend shown is the 2024 U.S. Toro; the 2023 European original (Honduran wrapper, three sizes) is discontinued. Strength is unsettled: the maker's site says mild, but halfwheel's review found it medium-full to full. The 2024 Europe edition uses a Honduran binder.

cigars.about: One of three 2026 Colaboraciones cigars, in which partner factories built a blend around Oscar Valladares's Honduran tobacco. This one is made by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo's Casa Carrillo factory in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,500 boxes of 20. Not made in Honduras: it is rolled at Casa Carrillo. The wrapper was first announced as Connecticut Broadleaf and then corrected to Connecticut Habano.

cigars.about: One of three 2026 Colaboraciones cigars, in which partner factories built a blend around Oscar Valladares's Honduran tobacco. This one is made by Oliva and uses Cameroon leaf for both the wrapper and the binder.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,500 boxes of 20. Not made in Honduras: it is rolled at Oliva's Tabolisa factory in Nicaragua, and the maker labels this version Tabolisa.

cigars.about: The in-house entry in the three-cigar 2026 Colaboraciones release, made at Oscar Valladares's own factory in Danli. It puts an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Honduran binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,500 boxes of 20. The other two Colaboraciones cigars are made by Casa Carrillo and Oliva.

cigars.about: A regular production line made only for the European market, introduced at InterTabac 2024. It is named for the first Mayan king of Copán and made at the Oscar Valladares factory in Danli, Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Made as a European exclusive, so it is not normally stocked in U.S. shops. The maker has not published a wrapper varietal or strength; Neptune describes it as medium to full. A Robusto also exists; halfwheel lists it at 6 x 50, which could not be confirmed.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano), USA (Pennsylvania ligero), Nicaragua (Estelí ligero)
cigars.about: A 2016 limited run of three perfectos from Matt Booth's Room101, the second cigar in the brand's Artist Collection after Johnny Tobacconaut. It was rolled in Danlí, Honduras, while Davidoff distributed the brand.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 3,500 boxes of 20 in 2016 and now retired. Sizes are from Room101's site; halfwheel and Cigar Aficionado listed the 2016 perfectos as 4 1/2 x 52, 5 1/2 x 50 and 8 x 60. Sources say only that the wrapper is Mexican ligero, not which region.

cigars.about: A single-size toro that Room101 made in 2024 with the Massachusetts retailer Sir Louis Cigars. It is rolled at Tabacalera William Ventura and distributed by Forged Cigar Co.
cigars.researchNote: Collaboration with Sir Louis Cigars of Wilbraham, Mass., which sells it as Louis Red Rocket. No strength rating is published. Sir Louis also sells a Connecticut-wrapped Red Rocket, which is a different blend.

cigars.about: A Honduran puro corona that Room101 made in 2021 for retailers in the Limited Cigar Association. It is rolled at Raíces Cubanas in Danlí.
cigars.researchNote: Limited Cigar Association exclusive. The leaf varieties and production numbers were not disclosed.

cigars.about: A 5 x 52 torpedo that Room101 made in 2021 for Pospiech, the distributor behind Powstanie. It was limited to 250 bundles of 20.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is undisclosed; Pospiech only gave a joke description. Limited to 250 bundles of 20 cigars.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The 2020 follow-up to Room101's Death Bucket, named for the band showing Matt Booth's head in a bucket of fried chicken. It is a different blend from the original, made at Joya de Nicaragua and sold through Limited Cigar Association retailers.
cigars.researchNote: Not the same cigar as the 2018 Death Bucket, which was made at Tabacalera William Ventura with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper. halfwheel's review put strength at medium and body at medium-plus. Production numbers were not disclosed.

cigars.about: Crowned Heads' exclusive for retailers who ordered at the 2022 PCA trade show, a lighter Connecticut-wrapped blend named after da Vinci's painting technique. It was made in one size at Tabacalera Pichardo in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: PCA 2022 exclusive with 2,500 boxes of 20 made. The C in the name refers to the Connecticut hybrid wrapper. Strength is from the Developing Palates review, since Crowned Heads only called it smooth and approachable.
