cigars.about: Crowned Heads' recurring exclusive for Hawaii, sold through R. Field Wine Co. since 2015 and named for the Hawaiian word for cowboy. Each release is a different blend and size.
cigars.researchNote: Blend, size and factory change with each release, so ask which year it is. Details here are the 2022 release (400 boxes of 10, made by E.P. Carrillo). The 2015 was a broadleaf from My Father, 2018 used a San Andrés wrapper, and 2019 and 2020 were broadleaf cigars from Drew Estate.

cigars.about: A 2021 Crowned Heads tribute to Grant Kawasaki, the Hawaiian chef and TV host who emceed the company's Paniolo events and died that year. It was sold only through R. Field Wine Co. in Hawaii.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 250 boxes of 10, exclusive to R. Field Wine Co. in Hawaii. Part of the sales went to a culinary scholarship in Kawasaki's name. No strength rating was published.

cigars.about: Crowned Heads' limited edition made only for Canada, developed with its Canadian distributor Brigham Enterprises. The name is a Canadian take on the Four Kicks Mule Kick.
cigars.researchNote: Canada only. The 2024 release was 300 bundles of 10 and halfwheel named the factory as TacaNicsa; the 2025 release was 500 bundles of 10 from D'Hatuey Tabacos, with the same blend and a pigtail cap. No strength rating was published.

cigars.about: Crowned Heads' event-only cigar introduced in September 2026, named after Nashville's old Starwood Amphitheatre. It takes over the event role from Blood Medicine, which became a regular release.
cigars.researchNote: Not for sale: it is given in four-packs with a qualifying purchase at Crowned Heads events. halfwheel lists it as regular production rather than a numbered limited run. No strength rating was published.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Three versions: Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade, Corojo Habano, or Maduro
cigars.about: Oscar Valladares' budget bundle line, rolled in Honduras with a mix of short and long filler left over from his premium cigars. It comes as a toro in Connecticut, Habano and Maduro wrappers.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed-filler bundle cigar sold in 20s, not a long-filler premium. Neptune rates the Connecticut version mild and the Habano and Maduro versions medium. The origin of the Maduro wrapper is not stated.

cigars.about: A 2024 limited edition Honduran puro that Oscar Valladares made to benefit Operation: Cigars for Warriors, which sends cigars to deployed troops. It comes in 10-count boxes built to look like ammo cans.
cigars.researchNote: All profits go to Operation: Cigars for Warriors, and only shops registered as CFW donation centers can carry it. halfwheel reported 1,000 cigars made. Strength is from Neptune's listing.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Honduran Connecticut-seed and Honduran Corojo (barber pole)
cigars.about: The fourth Island Jim blend, added in April 2025, with Connecticut and corojo wrappers twisted in a barber pole. Like the rest of the line it is shaped like a #2 pencil with a shaggy foot and is made by Oscar Valladares in Danlí.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are undisclosed. Neptune lists an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper and 6 1/2 x 52; halfwheel and Cigars Direct say both wrappers are Honduran and the size is 6 x 52. Retailers call it medium, but halfwheel's review found it mild to medium.

cigars.about: The third Island Jim blend, introduced in 2023 with a Connecticut-seed wrapper grown in Honduras. It keeps the line's #2 pencil look, with a shaggy foot and a contrasting cap, and is made by Oscar Valladares.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are undisclosed. Cigars Direct rates it mild-medium and Neptune mild. halfwheel and Cigars Direct give the size as 6 x 52, while Neptune lists 6 1/2 x 52.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Island Jim, added in 2018 as the line's first extension, with a San Andrés wrapper over the same Honduran core. It is the #2 pencil shape with a shaggy foot, made by Oscar Valladares.
cigars.researchNote: Some shops sell it as Island Jim Maduro, and the head is finished with a lighter Ecuadorian Connecticut leaf. Neptune and Smoke Inn rate it medium, Cigars Direct medium-full. halfwheel gives the size as 6 x 52, while retailers list 6 1/2 x 52.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown, offered in natural or maduro
cigars.about: The 6 7/8 x 46 Churchill in Padrón's core Padrón Series, an all-Nicaraguan line made with sun-grown tobacco aged at least two and a half years.
cigars.researchNote: One size of the Padrón Series (often called the Thousand Series), sold in natural and maduro. Padrón calls the line medium to full bodied; Holt's and Neptune list it as medium.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown, offered in natural or maduro
cigars.about: The smallest cigar in the core Padrón Series, a 4 1/4 x 35 short smoke made with the same all-Nicaraguan sun-grown tobacco as the rest of the line.
cigars.researchNote: One size of the Padrón Series, sold in natural and maduro, in boxes and tins. Padrón lists it at 35 ring; Holt's lists 34. Padrón calls the line medium to full bodied; Holt's and Neptune list it as medium.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown, offered in natural or maduro
cigars.about: The largest cigar in the core Padrón Series at 9 x 50, made with all-Nicaraguan sun-grown tobacco aged at least two and a half years.
cigars.researchNote: One size of the Padrón Series (often called the Thousand Series), sold in natural and maduro. Padrón calls the line medium to full bodied; Holt's and Neptune list it as medium.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown, offered in natural or maduro
cigars.about: A long corona size, 6 5/16 x 42, in Padrón's core Padrón Series of all-Nicaraguan sun-grown cigars.
cigars.researchNote: One size of the Padrón Series, sold in natural and maduro. Holt's rounds the length to 6 1/4. Padrón calls the line medium to full bodied; Holt's and Neptune list it as medium.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown, offered in natural or maduro
cigars.about: The slim 6 7/8 x 36 panetela in Padrón's core Padrón Series of all-Nicaraguan sun-grown cigars.
cigars.researchNote: One size of the Padrón Series (often called the Thousand Series), sold in natural and maduro. Padrón calls the line medium to full bodied; Holt's and Neptune list it as medium.

cigars.about: The maduro-wrapped version of Padrón's core Padrón Series, an all-Nicaraguan line of long-filler cigars made with sun-grown tobacco aged at least two and a half years. The line dates back to the company's founding in 1964.
cigars.researchNote: This is the maduro wrapper option of the Padrón Series (Thousand Series), which has fifteen sizes in all. Padrón calls the line medium to full bodied; Neptune and Holt's list it as medium.

cigars.about: The maduro-wrapped version of Padrón's top regular line, an all-Nicaraguan cigar made with tobacco aged ten years. Each size is named for a company anniversary or a birthday of founder José O. Padrón.
cigars.researchNote: This is the maduro wrapper option of the Family Reserve line. Padrón does not disclose the leaf varieties beyond all Nicaraguan tobacco. The No. 45 was Cigar Aficionado's 2009 Cigar of the Year.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown, offered in natural or maduro
cigars.about: A 6 x 52 torpedo and the first cigar in Padrón's Family Reserve line, named for the company's 44th anniversary. It is all Nicaraguan tobacco aged ten years.
cigars.researchNote: One size of the Family Reserve line, sold in natural and maduro. Padrón does not disclose the leaf varieties beyond all Nicaraguan tobacco.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown, offered in natural or maduro
cigars.about: A 5 1/2 x 56 size in Padrón's Family Reserve line, named for the company's 46th anniversary. It is all Nicaraguan tobacco aged ten years.
cigars.researchNote: One size of the Family Reserve line, sold in natural and maduro. Padrón does not disclose the leaf varieties beyond all Nicaraguan tobacco.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown, offered in natural or maduro
cigars.about: A short, thick 4 3/4 x 60 addition to Padrón's Family Reserve line, named for what would have been founder José O. Padrón's 95th birthday. It uses the line's all-Nicaraguan tobacco aged ten years.
cigars.researchNote: One size of the Family Reserve line, sold in natural and maduro. Announced in 2021 and shipped in March 2022, first only to stores that ordered at the 2021 PCA trade show.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown, offered in natural or maduro
cigars.about: A 5 3/4 x 52 robusto extra in Padrón's Family Reserve line, named for what would have been founder José O. Padrón's 96th birthday. It uses the line's all-Nicaraguan tobacco aged ten years.
cigars.researchNote: One size of the Family Reserve line, sold in natural and maduro. Shown at the 2022 PCA trade show but not shipped until April 2023. halfwheel found the Natural full strength and the Maduro milder until the final third.

cigars.about: The two fuller-flavored sizes of Padrón's Dámaso, the company's round Connecticut-wrapped line named for the founder's grandfather. They carry a red band to set them apart from the milder sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Red Label means the Dámaso No. 32 and No. 34, not a separate line. Padrón calls Dámaso mild to medium and these two more robust; halfwheel found the No. 34 medium at most, while Holt's lists the line as mild-medium.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown, offered in natural or maduro
cigars.about: A 5 1/2 x 52 robusto extra made for founder José O. Padrón's 90th birthday. It was the first round cigar in the box-pressed 1926 Serie and Padrón's first cigar sold in a tube.
cigars.researchNote: One size of the 1926 Serie, sold in natural and maduro in 10-count boxes of tubes. Cigar Aficionado named it No. 5 Cigar of the Year for 2016.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown, offered in natural or maduro
cigars.about: A 6 1/2 x 52 cigar made for Padrón's 50th anniversary, first sold in 1,000 numbered humidors of 50 cigars each. The tobacco is all Nicaraguan and aged at least ten years.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in natural and maduro. Humidor owners can buy 50-count refill boxes; cigars from the original humidors have red serial numbers matching the humidor, and refills have black ones.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan sun-grown, offered in natural or maduro
cigars.about: A round perfecto made for Padrón's 60th anniversary. Each cigar comes in its own coffin inside a ten-count box.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in natural and maduro. Padrón and Holt's list it at 6 1/2 x 56, tapering to 48; halfwheel lists 6 x 48/56. Padrón calls it limited in production, though halfwheel lists it as regular; the Natural was Cigar Aficionado's 2025 Cigar of the Year at 97 points.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan, offered in natural or maduro
cigars.about: A round 6 3/4 x 54 belicoso in the black-banded Padrón Black line, named for what would have been founder José O. Padrón's 97th birthday. It was offered to stores that ordered at the 2023 PCA trade show and shipped in March 2024.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in natural and maduro and described as a one-time release. Padrón says only that it is a Nicaraguan puro, with Jorge Padrón placing the blend between the 1926 Serie and Family Reserve. halfwheel found the Natural full strength and the Maduro medium-full.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan, offered in natural or maduro
cigars.about: A round 6 3/4 x 60 gordo in the black-banded Padrón Black line, named for what would have been founder José O. Padrón's 99th birthday. It is one of the largest cigars Padrón has made.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in natural and maduro and shipped in August 2025. halfwheel lists it as regular production, unlike the one-time PB-97. Leaf details beyond all Nicaraguan tobacco are not published.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan, offered in natural or maduro
cigars.about: A round 6 x 46 cigar with Padrón's black band, first made in 2016 as the José O. Padrón 89 Birthday Blend for Smoke Inn. It returned in 2019 as an exclusive for Tobacconists' Association of America stores.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as the TAA Black No. 89 and, originally, the José O. Padrón 89 Birthday Blend (200 boxes). Sold in natural and maduro. halfwheel lists the blend as not disclosed and found the TAA Maduro medium; Neptune lists all Nicaraguan tobacco and full strength.

cigars.about: A 5 1/2 x 56 robusto gordo in the black-banded Padrón Black line, made for the Cigar Rights of America Freedom Sampler. It appeared in the 2019 sampler and again in 2020.
cigars.researchNote: Padrón has not disclosed the blend. Sold only inside CRA Freedom Samplers, not on its own. The 2019 cigar looked like a maduro and the 2020 one a natural, though Padrón did not confirm either.

cigars.about: A 5 1/2 x 52 belicoso in the black-banded Padrón Black line, made for the 2021 Cigar Rights of America Freedom Sampler. It is round rather than box-pressed.
cigars.researchNote: Padrón has not disclosed the blend. Sold only inside the 2021 CRA Freedom Sampler, not on its own.

cigars.about: A 5 1/2 x 50 robusto extra in the black-banded Padrón Black line, made for the Spring 2022 Cigar Rights of America Freedom Sampler.
cigars.researchNote: Padrón has not disclosed the blend or the wrapper type; halfwheel's reviewer believed it was the maduro. Sold only inside the Spring 2022 CRA Freedom Sampler, and not every sampler included it.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan, offered in natural or maduro
cigars.about: A 6 x 54 box-pressed toro made by Padrón only for Tobacconist of Greenwich in Connecticut. The name refers to the small hammer José O. Padrón used to earn the money that started the company.
cigars.researchNote: A Nicaraguan puro sold in natural and maduro, 500 boxes of 10 of each, released June 11, 2025. halfwheel found the Natural reached full strength and the Maduro medium-full. The two took first and third on halfwheel's Top 25 for 2025.

cigars.about: A round 5 3/4 x 56 cigar made by Padrón for the 40th anniversary of Two Guys Smoke Shop in New Hampshire. It comes in numbered 40-count boxes designed by Nelson Alfonso.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is undisclosed. Sold in natural and maduro only at Two Guys Smoke Shop: 200 boxes in all, 150 maduro and 50 natural, released August 1, 2025.

cigars.about: A joint project between Arturo Fuente and Padrón in which Jorge Padrón made a cigar honoring Carlos Fuente Sr. and Carlito Fuente made one honoring José O. Padrón. It is sold in 40-count humidors holding 20 of each.
cigars.researchNote: Blends are undisclosed. Country, factory, strength and flavors here are for the Padrón-made cigar, which is box-pressed; the Fuente-made one is round, and both are 7 x 50. MSRP was $7,115 per box of 40, with profits going to the two families' charities.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: A Honduran puro from the Eiroa family's JRE Tobacco with a Habano wrapper over Corojo binder and filler, all grown on their own farm. The first cigars were rolled in 2015 and 2016 and aged four to five years before release.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers sell it as Aladino Habano or Aladino Vintage Selection. halfwheel found it closer to mild-medium, building to medium; Neptune and Famous list it as medium.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: A Honduran puro from JRE Tobacco built on Habano-seed leaf instead of the Corojo the Eiroa family is known for. JRE says the Habano makes it a more medium blend than its Corojo lines.
cigars.researchNote: The Habano wrapper is a dark shade that Neptune describes as maduro. Neptune's description lists a Habano-seed filler; halfwheel lists Habano and Corojo.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: A fuller-bodied Aladino blend made by JRE Tobacco in Honduras; the name is Spanish for night smoke. It comes in one size with a maduro wrapper JRE will not identify over Eiroa-grown Honduran binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: JRE only calls the wrapper maduro and does not disclose its variety or origin; Famous Smoke lists it as Honduran. Sold in boxes of 16.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: A Honduran puro made for Julio Eiroa's 85th birthday using only Pinareño-seed tobacco, a delicate, low-yield Cuban-seed variety, rather than the family's usual Corojo. It comes in yellow boxes showing Julio's Buick.
cigars.researchNote: Regular production, but retailers can order only four boxes of each size per month. A Lancero was shown at PCA 2026 for release late in 2026. Pinareño does not fit a standard wrapper category.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: An Aladino blend wrapped in Sumatra-seed leaf the Eiroas began planting on their Honduran farm in 2016. The binder and filler are undisclosed varieties from the same farm.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel lists it as regular production while Neptune calls it a limited production release and shows it sold out. Neptune describes the wrapper as a maduro shade.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: A green candela-wrapped Honduran puro that JRE Tobacco ships in small batches early each year ahead of St. Patrick's Day. It honors Julio Eiroa's past as a major candela grower.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel rated the strength medium while Neptune lists it as mild. The Robusto was the 2023 batch and the Toro followed in 2024; the 2025 Toro was 6 x 52. A 2025 sales sheet lists the blend as undisclosed.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: Billed as the first cigar made entirely of Cameroon-seed tobacco grown in Honduras, from wrapper to filler. JRE Tobacco ships it in limited yearly batches in boxes of 12.
cigars.researchNote: Not the same as the regular Aladino Cameroon, which pairs the Cameroon-seed wrapper with Corojo binder and filler. halfwheel found the strength a little under medium.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: A limited Aladino toro with a Honduran-grown Cameroon-seed wrapper over undisclosed Honduran tobaccos aged five to six years. It debuted as a 2023 PCA trade show exclusive and returned in a larger batch in 2024.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune sells it as Aladino Limited Edition Cameroon. The 2023 run was 600 boxes of 20 and the 2024 run was 1,200 boxes. Binder and filler varieties are not disclosed.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: A limited Aladino toro made for the 250th anniversary of the United States, packed in boxes of 13 for the original colonies. JRE says it is made entirely of tobacco the company grew but will not name the leaves.
cigars.researchNote: Blend is undisclosed. It was announced as Aladino Declaration and renamed over a trademark concern. Limited to 1,000 boxes of 13.

cigars.line: Aladino Year of the Horse 2026 Limited Edition
cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: JRE Tobacco's first Chinese zodiac cigar, a torpedo made of Honduran tobaccos grown by the Eiroa family. It is sold only in Asia.
cigars.researchNote: Asia exclusive that JRE says will not be sold in the U.S. Limited to 600 boxes of 20; it went on sale in December 2025. Leaf varieties and strength are not published.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: A Honduran puro lancero that JRE Tobacco made for Limited Cigar Association retailers in 2021. It was tied to a longest ash contest with a customized Dodge Charger as the prize.
cigars.researchNote: Limited Cigar Association release with an initial run of 8,000 cigars. Filler varieties were not disclosed and no strength rating was published.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: The 2026 entry in JRE Tobacco's Camp Aladino series, which is reserved for shops that have visited the company's farms and factory in Honduras. It is a single toro with an undisclosed blend.
cigars.researchNote: JRE has not disclosed anything about the blend. For its first year it is sold only by retailers that have visited JRE in Honduras. Medium strength is Neptune's listing.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Honduran maduro (per Neptune; not disclosed by JRE)
cigars.about: One of three short, thick Gorbusto cigars from JRE Tobacco, each named for a primate character. Gori the gorilla is pitched as the bold, full-bodied one.
cigars.researchNote: This is one of the three 2025 Camp Aladino blends (Cameroon, Corojo, Maduro) renamed in 2026. JRE will not say which blend each primate is and does not disclose the blend. Neptune lists Gori with a maduro wrapper and full strength.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: One of three short, thick Gorbusto cigars from JRE Tobacco, each named for a primate character. Chimp the chimpanzee is pitched as the refined, complex one.
cigars.researchNote: This is one of the three 2025 Camp Aladino blends (Cameroon, Corojo, Maduro) renamed in 2026. JRE will not say which blend each primate is and does not disclose the blend. Neptune lists Chimp as medium with a natural-shade Honduran wrapper.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: One of three short, thick Gorbusto cigars from JRE Tobacco, each named for a primate character. Orang the orangutan is pitched as the creative one with unexpected flavors.
cigars.researchNote: This is one of the three 2025 Camp Aladino blends (Cameroon, Corojo, Maduro) renamed in 2026. JRE will not say which blend each primate is and does not disclose the blend. Neptune lists Orang as medium with a natural-shade Honduran wrapper.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: One of three 2025 Camp Aladino cigars from JRE Tobacco, all in a short 60-ring Gorbusto size and told apart by wrapper. This one wears a Honduran-grown Cameroon-seed wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Sold under this name only in 2025, at shops that had visited JRE in Honduras. In 2026 the same blend was renamed as one of the Gorbusto by Aladino cigars. Binder and filler are not disclosed.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: One of three 2025 Camp Aladino cigars from JRE Tobacco, all in a short 60-ring Gorbusto size and told apart by wrapper. This one wears the Eiroa family's Honduran Corojo wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Sold under this name only in 2025, at shops that had visited JRE in Honduras. In 2026 the same blend was renamed as one of the Gorbusto by Aladino cigars. Binder and filler are not disclosed.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: One of three 2025 Camp Aladino cigars from JRE Tobacco, all in a short 60-ring Gorbusto size and told apart by wrapper. This one wears a Honduran maduro wrapper and is the strongest of the three.
cigars.researchNote: Sold under this name only in 2025, at shops that had visited JRE in Honduras, then renamed in 2026 as one of the Gorbusto by Aladino cigars. Binder and filler are not disclosed. Full strength is Neptune's listing.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: One of JRE Tobacco's original value lines, a Honduran cigar with a Habano-seed wrapper grown on the Eiroa farms. JRE took it off its price list in 2022 and brought it back in 2025 as a $6 mixed-filler toro sold in bundles of 20.
cigars.researchNote: The 2025 version is mixed filler made from trimmings of JRE's other cigars, and no strength is published for it. The earlier long-filler version had a Corojo binder and Neptune rated it medium. It is the red-banded one; the 7 x 64 and 7 x 70 sizes are the separate Rancho Luna Grandes line.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: The blue-banded half of JRE Tobacco's reworked Rancho Luna value line, with a Connecticut-seed wrapper grown on the Eiroa farms in Honduras. It is a $6 mixed-filler toro sold in bundles of 20.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed filler made with trimmings from JRE's other cigars, under a whole-leaf wrapper and binder. No strength rating or tasting notes are published. 2025 is the relaunch date for the line.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: A maduro version of JRE Tobacco's Rancho Luna, blended by Julio and Justo Eiroa and introduced at the 2016 trade show. JRE took Rancho Luna off its price list in 2022, and the 2025 relaunch did not include the Maduro.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the wrapper: halfwheel's show report and Neptune say Mexican San Andrés, while halfwheel's earlier announcement said Honduran maduro. The 2025 Rancho Luna relaunch has only Habano and Connecticut.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: An affordable everyday Honduran puro from Julio and Justo Eiroa's JRE Tobacco, with a Habano wrapper over Corojo binder and a Corojo and Habano filler.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel reports that Tatascan cigars come with a sweetened tip, apart from the Yellow Series. Launch year is not published.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: An affordable everyday cigar from the Eiroa family's JRE Tobacco, made in Honduras with a Connecticut Shade wrapper and a sweetened cap. The name is said to mean head boss, a nod to Julio Eiroa.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on where the wrapper is grown: halfwheel says Honduras, Neptune and Cigar Coop say Ecuador. Neptune's text says mild-medium but its spec table says medium. It has a sweetened cap.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: JRE Tobacco's budget bundle cigar, a mixed-filler Honduran puro with a Habano wrapper. Unlike the other Tatascan cigars it does not have a sweetened tip.
cigars.researchNote: Introduced in 2016 as Tatascan Yellow Label. Mixed filler, sold in bundles of 20. Neptune describes the wrapper as a Habano maduro.

cigars.about: A medium-bodied Nicaraguan puro from Curivari, built on Cuban-seed Criollo and Corojo tobacco and finished with a triple cap. Halfwheel notes its band is styled after Partagas.
cigars.researchNote: Curivari only says the tobacco is Nicaraguan Cuban-seed Criollo and Corojo; Smokingpipes lists the wrapper as Corojo. A darker Maduro version is sold separately, and limited lanceros were released in 2021 and 2022.

cigars.about: The darker-wrapped version of Curivari's Seleccion Privada, a Nicaraguan puro sold in the larger Eminentes, Magnificos and Fabulosos sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is listed differently everywhere: halfwheel's Eminentes review and Neptune say medium, Cigar Place medium-full, Smokingpipes full. Halfwheel dates the Eminentes size to November 2011; the Seleccion Privada name dates to 2010.

cigars.about: One of Curivari's original Cuban-styled lines, a Nicaraguan puro with a reddish brown wrapper. Halfwheel says it was blended to recall Romeo y Julieta.
cigars.researchNote: Curivari only says the tobacco is Nicaraguan Cuban-seed Criollo and Corojo; Smokingpipes lists the wrapper as Criollo with a Rosado shade and rates strength 4 of 5. Smokingpipes also sells a Gloria de Leon Gran Dominio in three smaller sizes.

cigars.about: One of the three Curivari Reserva Limitada blends, a Nicaraguan puro with a dark, oily wrapper that the maker describes as full-bodied. It sits alongside the Cafe and 1000 Series.
cigars.researchNote: Curivari calls it full-bodied and Cigar Place lists it as full, but Smokingpipes rates the strength only medium. Curivari itself just says Nicaraguan Cuban-seed Criollo and Corojo; Habano is the Smokingpipes wrapper label.

cigars.about: One of the three Curivari Reserva Limitada blends, a Nicaraguan puro with a dark Colorado wrapper sold in three sizes numbered 2000 to 4000.
cigars.researchNote: Curivari calls it full-bodied, but halfwheel's 2011 review found medium strength and Smokingpipes rates it 4 of 5. Smokingpipes lists the wrapper as Criollo.

cigars.about: A semi-pressed Nicaraguan puro with a near-black wrapper, added to Curivari's Reserva Limitada group at the 2013 IPCPR show. The 62 size scored 90 points in Cigar Insider.
cigars.researchNote: Cigar Aficionado rates it medium-full, Neptune medium; the 62 size is actually a 60 ring gauge. It is separate from the original Reserva Limitada Cafe, which comes in different sizes. Neptune names Plasencia as the factory, while halfwheel says Curivari's cigars are made at Tabacalera de Nicaragua S.A.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Curivari's value-priced Buenaventura, with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over all-Nicaraguan binder and filler. It debuted at the 2023 PCA show, eleven years after the original.
cigars.researchNote: Cigar Aficionado rated the BV600 medium-full and the smaller Petit BV full; Neptune lists the line as medium.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped member of Curivari's value-priced Buenaventura family, with an Ecuadorian shade wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It was introduced at the 2016 IPCPR show.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune and Cigar Place list it as medium; Smokingpipes rates it milder, 2 of 5. Both retailers name Plasencia as the factory, while halfwheel says Curivari's cigars are made at Tabacalera de Nicaragua S.A.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro extension of Curivari's value-priced Buenaventura family, sold in three sizes labeled D4, D6 and D8.
cigars.researchNote: Cigar Aficionado rated the D8 medium-full and gave it 90 points in 2026; Neptune lists the line as medium. Neptune names Plasencia as the factory, while halfwheel says Curivari's cigars are made at Tabacalera de Nicaragua S.A.

cigars.about: The yellow-band member of Curivari's low-priced Buenaventura Favoritos trio, with an Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It began shipping in October 2024 at under $6 a cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune and Smokingpipes both list it as medium, but halfwheel's review found the nicotine strength mild with medium-full flavor.

cigars.about: The red-band member of Curivari's low-priced Buenaventura Favoritos trio, a Nicaraguan puro with a habano-seed wrapper from Jalapa. The 56 size placed 23rd on halfwheel's Top 25 of 2024.
The blue-band member of Curivari's low-priced Buenaventura Favoritos trio, with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It began shipping in October 2024 at under $6 a cigar.
A maduro-wrapped member of Curivari's value-priced Buenaventura family, with a dark Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan Cuban-seed binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune and the Smokingpipes description both say the wrapper is Mexican San Andrés, though the Smokingpipes spec table lists Nicaragua. Smokingpipes rates the strength 4 of 5.

cigars.about: The lowest-priced version of Curivari's Buenaventura, a Nicaraguan puro made with a blend of long and mixed filler.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed filler, not all long filler. Neptune calls the wrapper a dark habano and the cigar medium strength; Smokingpipes lists the wrapper as Rosado and rates strength 4 of 5.

cigars.about: Two limited sizes of Curivari's Buenaventura, both Nicaraguan puros, released in late 2021 in boxes of 10 with 5,000 cigars made per size. Both sizes first appeared in 2014 as short runs.
cigars.researchNote: Curivari described it as an outtake blend from the Buenaventura sessions, not the regular blend. A 2022 edition followed with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper in 5 x 54 and 6 x 54.

cigars.about: A single-size Nicaraguan puro made by Curivari for the Limited Cigar Association and released to LCA retailers in March 2021. It wears the Buenaventura band but is a different blend.
cigars.researchNote: Not the regular Buenaventura blend: it uses higher primings and some different tobaccos. Halfwheel lists the factory as undisclosed and production numbers were not released.

cigars.about: A version of Curivari's Achilles, a Nicaraguan puro that keeps the original Achilles fillers under a lighter habano wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Part of the Achilles family, launched in 2013 as one of Curivari's strongest blends; Smokingpipes rates this version 3 of 5. Cigar Aficionado spelled it Invensibles and reported a September 2015 release. Factory is unclear: 2015 reports name Plasencia for Achilles, while halfwheel now says Tabacalera de Nicaragua S.A.

cigars.about: One of Curivari's Greek-themed lines, named for the Cyclops of the Odyssey. It pairs a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Strength sources disagree: Neptune calls it full strength, Smokingpipes rates it 3 of 5. It was previewed in 2016 ahead of the FDA deadline; halfwheel lists the launch as August 2017.

cigars.about: One of Curivari's Greek-themed lines, named for the philosopher. It pairs a dark Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper with Nicaraguan Cuban-seed binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Strength sources disagree: Neptune describes it as medium-bodied, Smokingpipes rates it 5 of 5. It was previewed in 2016 ahead of the FDA deadline; halfwheel lists the launch as August 2017.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro from Curivari's Micro Blend Series with a sun-grown habano wrapper. A Maduro version is sold alongside it.
cigars.researchNote: A torpedo (T) also exists; halfwheel prints it as 6 x 52, the same as the 652, so it is left out here. Previewed in 2016 ahead of the FDA deadline; halfwheel lists the launch as August 2017.

cigars.about: The dark-wrapped partner to Curivari's Sun Grown. Smokingpipes describes it as slightly sweeter than the regular version.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper sources disagree: halfwheel's 2017 trade show report lists Mexican San Andrés, while Smokingpipes and Neptune describe a Nicaraguan puro with a habano maduro wrapper. Halfwheel lists the launch as August 2017.

cigars.about: One of Curivari's Greek-themed lines, named for the centaur of mythology. It is a Nicaraguan puro of Cuban-seed Criollo and Corojo tobacco with a triple cap.
cigars.researchNote: Smokingpipes rates the strength 4 of 5. Previewed in 2016 ahead of the FDA deadline; halfwheel lists the launch as August 2017. Smokingpipes lists the 44 as 4 x 44 and the T as 6 x 52, shorter than halfwheel's figures.

cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro made with vintage tobacco from Curivari's own farm in Jalapa, a project owner Andreas Throuvalas says took ten years. Only 1,000 boxes of 10 were made across five sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Shown at the 2025 PCA show but it did not ship until April 2026. Halfwheel's review found mild nicotine strength with medium body and medium-plus flavor; Smokingpipes rates it medium.

cigars.about: A limited-edition spin-off of Curivari's Virtudes line, a Nicaraguan puro with a Jalapa wrapper. About 200 boxes of 10 were planned for each of its five sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Announced at the 2026 PCA show with shipping scheduled for August 2026. The original Virtudes was one of the lines Curivari previewed in 2016 and 2017.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Maduro with Candela accents on the cap and closed foot
cigars.about: A stronger sibling of the Killer Bee from James Brown's Black Works Studio, with a dark Ecuadorian maduro wrapper and green candela on the cap and closed foot. It is a core line cigar made at Fabrica Oveja Negra in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2016 as the Green Hornet and now sold as The Hornet; the Corona Larga was added in 2023. Neptune gives 2023 as the release year.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Connecticut with an Ecuadorian Maduro swirl cap and closed foot
cigars.about: A Killer Bee line extension with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper and maduro accents on the cap and closed foot. It began as a small batch in 2018 and became a core line cigar in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium strength, but halfwheel and Atlantic Cigar call it medium-full, and halfwheel found the body full. First released as a limited batch in 2018, regular production since 2022.

cigars.about: A Sumatra-wrapped extension of the Rorschach line from Black Works Studio, added to the core range in 2023. The maker describes it as a lighter profile than the original that highlights Jalapa tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: The maker only says Sumatra wrapper. halfwheel reported it as Indonesian-grown in 2023 and as Sumatra-seed grown in Ecuador in 2026. The maker rates it medium strength and calls it mild to medium, though Atlantic Cigar lists it as full.

cigars.about: A limited Black Works Studio blend with a Pennsylvania broadleaf wrapper over Nicaraguan, Pennsylvania and Connecticut fillers. It comes back in occasional batches and returned in 2026 after a seven year gap.
cigars.researchNote: Originally sold as Boondock Saint, now just Boondock. Soft launched in 2016, with full releases in 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2026, when the Lancero was added. Retailers list it as full; halfwheel's 2026 review found it medium-full to full.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Maduro with Connecticut and Candela
cigars.about: A 2026 limited edition from Black Works Studio whose wrapper combines Ecuadorian maduro, Connecticut and green candela leaf. James Brown calls it the boldest profile the brand has made.
cigars.researchNote: Multi-leaf wrapper: Ecuadorian maduro with Connecticut and candela. Limited to 800 boxes each of the Robusto and Toro and 500 of the Panatela. Neptune lists it as full strength, Atlantic Cigar as medium-full.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Pennsylvania Broadleaf, Connecticut Broadleaf and Candela
cigars.about: The first limited release in the Black Works Studio Tiger Series, made for the brand's tenth anniversary in 2025. It is a bigger, darker take on the Tiger with broadleaf and candela wrappers.
cigars.researchNote: Triple wrapper of two broadleafs plus candela. halfwheel found the strength built from medium to medium-full; Neptune lists it as medium. Sold in 15-count boxes.

cigars.about: A small batch Black Works Studio release from 2024 built around an Ecuadorian Connecticut Desflorado wrapper. The maker describes it as medium strength with full flavor, both sizes box pressed.
A small batch Black Works Studio cigar with a Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper, offered only to retailers who attended the 2023 PCA trade show. Each size was limited to 500 boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Strength and body are from halfwheel's review; the maker only calls it bold yet refined.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Sumatra with Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade (barber pole)
cigars.about: A limited Black Works Studio blend and the first in the brand to use Dominican filler and a Sumatra wrapper. The 2023 release added Connecticut shade stripes to the dark Sumatra wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Specs shown are the 2023 release. The 2018 to 2020 batches used a plain Sumatra wrapper, a Nicaraguan habano binder and Corona Gorda (5.5 x 46) and Lancero (6.75 x 42) sizes. Announced in 2016 with a full debut in February 2018.

cigars.about: A limited Black Works Studio cigar that pairs a Cameroon wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler. James Brown made it as a tribute to the years he and his wife lived in Africa.
cigars.researchNote: Released in 2021 and again in 2022, the second batch described by the maker as a touch more intense. halfwheel rated strength and body medium-plus with full flavor.

cigars.about: A 2022 limited edition from Black Works Studio with a dark Sumatra wrapper over an Ecuadorian habano binder and Nicaraguan filler. The maker calls it a more traditional profile for the brand.
cigars.researchNote: The maker says Dark Sumatra; halfwheel lists the wrapper as Indonesian. Strength is from halfwheel's review.

cigars.about: The darker follow up to Intergalactic, released in 2024 with a Pennsylvania broadleaf wrapper in place of the original Sumatra. A limited edition made at Fabrica Oveja Negra.
cigars.researchNote: Strength and body are from halfwheel's review; the maker only calls it bold. Each size was limited to 900 boxes.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andrés with Connecticut and Candela
cigars.about: A tweaked version of the Killer Bee blend in a three-leaf wrapper of San Andrés, Connecticut and candela. It was a small batch for retailers who ordered at the 2022 PCA trade show.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it bold but elegant, while halfwheel's review found it medium bodied and mild in strength. halfwheel reports 1,000 boxes of 24.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Maduro and Ecuadorian Rojiso barber pole
cigars.about: A barber pole version of the Black Works Studio NBK, first released in 2019 for retailer events. The maker describes it as an amped up NBK with more strength and spice.
cigars.researchNote: Launched as an event-only cigar. Full strength is Neptune's listing; the maker says only that it has more strength and spice than the regular NBK.

cigars.about: One of the three Tiger Series cigars from Black Works Studio, each striped with three different wrapper leaves. On the Neon Tiger the green candela is the most visible leaf.
cigars.researchNote: Part of the Tiger Series. The maker says the series was sold only in Europe and as factory exclusives from 2017, then as event-only 13-count boxes in the US from 2022. Candela is the dominant wrapper.

cigars.about: The toro of the Black Works Studio Tiger Series, striped with three wrapper leaves. It shows more of the Connecticut wrapper than the other two Tigers.
cigars.researchNote: Part of the Tiger Series. The maker says the series was sold only in Europe and as factory exclusives from 2017, then as event-only 13-count boxes in the US from 2022. Connecticut is the dominant wrapper.

cigars.about: A robusto in the Black Works Studio Tiger Series with a coiled cap and three striped wrapper leaves. The Ecuadorian maduro is the most visible leaf on this one.
cigars.researchNote: Part of the Tiger Series. The maker says the series was sold only in Europe and as factory exclusives from 2017, then as event-only 13-count boxes in the US from 2022. Maduro is the dominant wrapper.

cigars.about: A limited Black Works Studio blend with a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper, a rabito cap and a closed foot. James Brown called it the boldest of the brand's 2016 additions.
cigars.researchNote: James Brown described it as full in flavor and strength. Soft launched at four shops in 2016, with full releases in 2017 and 2018. The Robusto and Lancero returned in the 2025 BOOMBOX anniversary sampler.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dual wrapper of Mexican San Andrés and Ecuadorian Sun Grown
cigars.about: A dual wrapper Black Works Studio cigar made as a shop exclusive for R. Field Wine Co. in Honolulu. It has come out in several small batches in 10-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: R. Field Wine Co. (Honolulu) exclusive. The maker called the 2022 batch the second release and the 2024 batch the third; the year of the first release was not confirmed.

cigars.about: A three-leaf wrapper Black Works Studio robusto made as an exclusive for R. Field Wine Co. in Honolulu. The maker describes it as a spin-off of the Kato Hawaii with a rich, dark, earthy profile.
cigars.researchNote: R. Field Wine Co. (Honolulu) exclusive in 10-count boxes. Released in September 2023 and again in January 2026. The maker also calls it the Hawaiian Hornet.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Triple wrapper of Mexican San Andrés, Connecticut and Candela
cigars.about: The first shop exclusive in the Black Works Studio Tiger Series, made for R. Field Wine Co. in Honolulu in 2024. It uses a striped triple wrapper led by Mexican San Andrés.
cigars.researchNote: R. Field Wine Co. (Honolulu) exclusive in 10-count boxes, first offered at a store event on August 3, 2024.

cigars.about: A perfecto version of the Killer Bee made as an exclusive for Smoke Inn in South Florida in 2024. The shape first appeared in the 2021 Hive sampler.
cigars.researchNote: Smoke Inn exclusive in 10-count boxes. It is a Killer Bee in a perfecto shape. The maker calls it bold and very intense but gives no strength rating.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andrés and African Cameroon
cigars.about: A dual wrapper NBK variant made in 2024 for the tenth anniversary of Hogshead Cigar Lounge in Fredericksburg, Virginia. The maker describes it as full bodied with dark, earthy notes.
cigars.researchNote: Hogshead Cigar Lounge (Fredericksburg, Virginia) exclusive in 10-count boxes.

cigars.about: A dual wrapper Black Works Studio cigar made in 2025 as a shop exclusive for Tooth & Bear Cigar Lounge in Woodland Park, Colorado. James Brown says it is very different from the brand's earlier cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Tooth & Bear Cigar Lounge (Woodland Park, Colorado) exclusive in 10-count boxes. No strength or tasting notes are published.

cigars.about: The first blend released by Litto Gomez Jr., made as the daytime counterpart to his brother Tony's La Nox. It comes in one size, sold in a round wooden box.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it powerful and Neptune lists it as full. halfwheel's reviewer found it medium-full to full in strength.

cigars.about: La Flor Dominicana's first full-bodied line, built on aged ligero grown on the company's own farm under an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. The sizes carry L numbers such as L-300 and L-500.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers often list it as Ligero Natural. The darker wrapped version is sold as Ligero Oscuro or Cabinet Oscuro. Neptune's spec table says Ecuadorian Habano, but its write-up, Holt's and the maker all say Ecuadorian Sumatra.

cigars.about: A box-pressed, oversized Chisel that was the first cigar blended by Tony Gomez, son of founder Litto Gomez. It pairs a very dark Brazilian wrapper with Dominican ligero filler.
cigars.researchNote: Also written Chapter One. The maker calls the wrapper Brazilian Habano; halfwheel lists it as Brazilian ligero oscuro. Holt's rates it full, halfwheel's reviewer found it medium-full. It launched in 2013 as a limited run of 100,000 cigars.

cigars.about: The follow-up to Chapter 1, in the same box-pressed 6 1/2 x 58 Chisel but with a Nicaraguan wrapper and Ecuadorian binder. The name is Spanish for chapter two.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's rates it full; halfwheel's reviewer found it closer to medium. It was announced in 2014 as a limited edition but the maker still lists it.

cigars.about: A stronger take on the Coronado blend that uses higher-priming Nicaraguan habano wrapper over Dominican tobacco from the company farm. It is best known for its gold tubes and comes in Natural and Maduro.
cigars.researchNote: The Maduro also uses a Nicaraguan habano wrapper. No. 6 comes in Natural and Maduro, with or without tubes. Nos. 5, 7 and 8 were added in 2025 in Natural only. Neptune lists it as full; halfwheel's 2012 review found it medium-bodied.

cigars.about: La Flor Dominicana's flagship limited release, a Dominican puro made from a single harvest grown on the company's La Canela farm. Eight batches came out between 2006 and 2019, sold in 105-count cabinets.
cigars.researchNote: Each batch differs in size and blend. The size, strength and flavors here are for the 2019 release, the most recent. Earlier batches ran from 6 1/2 to 7 inches, and halfwheel found No. 6 closer to medium.

cigars.about: The Air Bender blend of estate-grown Dominican binder and filler finished in a darker, oilier Ecuadorian habano wrapper. The maker offers Air Bender in both natural and maduro.
cigars.researchNote: Regular production since 2015 with a dark Ecuadorian habano wrapper. The limited versions of 2011 and 2012 used Brazilian habano, so older write-ups may say Brazil.

cigars.about: The maduro-wrapped version of Double Ligero, a ligero-heavy blend of Dominican binder and filler grown on the company farm. It is among the strongest regular La Flor Dominicana cigars and is closely tied to the Chisel shape.
cigars.researchNote: This is the maduro wrapper option of the Double Ligero line. Neptune's write-up and a 2008 Cigar Aficionado rating call the wrapper Connecticut Broadleaf, but Neptune's spec table and halfwheel say Ecuadorian maduro, and the maker describes Ecuadorian sun grown leaf.

cigars.about: The Connecticut Broadleaf version of Reserva Especial, sold as the small bulging El Jocko perfecto. Reserva Especial is the milder side of the La Flor Dominicana range.
cigars.researchNote: This is one size, the El Jocko Maduro, within the Reserva Especial line. The maker and halfwheel give a Dominican binder for the line, while Neptune lists Nicaraguan. Holt's and halfwheel call the line medium; Neptune tags this cigar full.

cigars.about: The maduro half of the Suave line that La Flor Dominicana rebuilt in 2025, sold in two box-pressed sizes. Suave traces back to the company's very first blend from 1994.
cigars.researchNote: The blend and release year are for the 2025 relaunch; an older Suave Grand Maduro blend was sold before it. The No. 6 is a torpedo.

cigars.about: A Connecticut Broadleaf maduro over Dominican binder and filler from La Flor Dominicana, offered in two sizes. Retailers describe it as a limited release.
cigars.researchNote: Details come from retailer listings only; the maker's site does not list it. Some shops call it Cabinet Maduro. Neptune rates it full, Corona medium to full. The No. 6 is a torpedo.

cigars.about: A box-pressed 6 x 52 toro from La Flor Dominicana with a dark Ecuadorian habano wrapper over Dominican binder and filler. Retailers sell it as a limited edition.
cigars.researchNote: Details come from retailer listings; the maker's site does not list it. Neptune's write-up calls it a maduro, but Neptune and Corona both list an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. A separate Double Press Maduro with Connecticut Broadleaf was a 2013 TAA exclusive.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mix of candela, maduro and Connecticut-seed leaves cut into designs
cigars.about: The La Flor Dominicana Salomon dressed with hand-applied tobacco artwork. One roller at the factory created roughly 100 designs, and each box of 10 holds a mix of them.
cigars.researchNote: Every cigar has a different wrapper design made from several leaves, so there is no single wrapper to quote. No source publishes a strength rating or tasting notes. halfwheel reported a planned run of 4,000 boxes of 10.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican Habano with a maduro foot and cap
cigars.about: A 7 x 54 perfecto with a contrasting dark foot and cap, originally called Mysterio. It was renamed in 2014 after a trademark dispute; the letters stand for The Cigar Formerly Known As M.
cigars.researchNote: 2014 is the year of the rename; it was sold before that as Mysterio. halfwheel calls the Natural wrapper Dominican habano, while Neptune lists Nicaraguan with Connecticut Broadleaf tips. A Maduro version also exists. Neptune lists it full; halfwheel's 2011 review found it medium.

cigars.about: A single 7 x 52 Churchill released in 2019 to mark 25 years in the cigar business for founders Litto and Ines Gomez. The La Flor Dominicana brand itself dates to 1996.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel's reviewer found the strength between medium and full; Neptune lists it as full. Production numbers were not disclosed.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Chisel sold in 60-count humidors to mark 30 years in cigars for founders Litto and Ines Gomez. Production was limited to 2,000 humidors.
cigars.researchNote: Some retailers list it as 30th Anniversary. halfwheel's reviewer called it medium-full; Neptune lists it as medium. It marks the founders' 30 years in the business, not the brand's, which started in 1996.

cigars.about: A 6 x 54 toro in the Litto Gomez Diez family, made entirely from tobacco grown on the company's La Canela farm and sold only through TAA member shops. The name is French for emerald, a nod to the TAA's 55th anniversary.
cigars.researchNote: A Dominican puro. It was planned as the 2023 TAA exclusive but did not reach stores until late 2024. halfwheel found it medium-full to full; Neptune lists it as full. Production numbers were not disclosed.

cigars.about: La Flor Dominicana's 2025 exclusive for TAA member shops, a box-pressed 6 1/2 x 44 lonsdale with a Cameroon wrapper over Dominican tobacco. Limited to 1,500 boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: Shipped to stores in mid-December 2025. Strength is from halfwheel's review, which had it topping out a little above medium.

cigars.about: A 2026 collaboration with accessory maker ProjectCarbon: a 6 x 54 pigtailed toro sold only in five-count carbon fiber travel cases. Limited to 1,500 sets.
cigars.researchNote: The maker bills it as full-bodied and Neptune lists it as full, but halfwheel's reviewer found it only mild to medium in strength with a medium body. A set of five with the case has an MSRP of $200.

cigars.about: A 2026 limited edition marking ten years of the Andalusian Bull. It keeps the original's unusual 6 1/2 inch perfecto shape but swaps the Ecuadorian wrapper for Connecticut Broadleaf maduro.
cigars.researchNote: New in October 2026 with no published reviews; the full strength rating comes from Neptune's listing alone. The maker calls it sweeter, richer and darker than the original. Binder and filler are from the 2016 La Canela crop. Limited to 5,000 boxes of 10. The size is listed as 6 1/2 x 52/64.

cigars.about: The last of La Flor Dominicana's Golden Blend exclusives for TAA member shops, a 7 x 64 salomon that shipped in December 2022. It came in Natural and Maduro versions.
cigars.researchNote: The maker did not disclose this blend. Earlier Golden Blend cigars used Nicaraguan sun grown (Natural) or Connecticut Broadleaf (Maduro) over Dominican tobacco. halfwheel found the Natural about medium and the Maduro just under full. 700 boxes of Maduro and 400 of Natural, 10 per box.

cigars.about: The third release in La Flor Dominicana's Golden Blend series for TAA member shops, a 6 1/2 x 58 box-pressed Chisel. The filler includes a Dominican criollo 99 leaf the company keeps for its TAA cigars.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper, strength and flavors here are for the Natural. A Maduro version uses Connecticut Broadleaf over the same blend. It was announced in 2020 as TAA 52nd Oro Tercera Edicion, then renamed and shipped in early 2022.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Habano through 2024 (Ecuadorian Sumatra in 2025), with a football made from contrasting leaf
cigars.about: An annual limited edition released ahead of the Super Bowl and usually sold only by retailers in the state hosting the game. Each cigar has a football worked into the wrapper in contrasting tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Size and blend change every year, so sizes and strength are left blank; halfwheel found 2024 full and 2025 mild. The wrapper was Ecuadorian habano through 2024; the 2025 pair was based on the Ligero blend with Ecuadorian Sumatra and Connecticut Broadleaf. 2025 was the first year with two cigars.

cigars.about: A Dominican puro blended by Eladio Díaz from 2000 and 2001 harvest tobacco that was aged more than 12 years before rolling. It launched in 2014 at $500 a cigar and comes in one 6 x 54 size.
cigars.researchNote: Davidoff said in 2024 that the tobacco for this blend is almost gone and launched the Oro Blanco Special Reserve 111 Years as its successor. Leaf varietals are not published. halfwheel found medium strength, rising near full at the end.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (five fillers aged 17 to 18 years)
cigars.about: The 2024 follow-up to Oro Blanco, a Dominican puro in the same 6 x 54 size. The name refers to the combined 111 years of age of the seven tobaccos in each cigar, and it carries a $750 price.
cigars.researchNote: Davidoff has not named the filler varietals, only that one has never been used in a Davidoff before. Davidoff describes it as medium intensity, while halfwheel found medium-full strength. halfwheel lists it as regular production.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Mao, Villa González, Piloto, Navarrete)
cigars.about: An all-Dominican line added to the Black Band Collection in 2026, using tobacco from six Dominican regions with a combined age of 32 years. It reuses the name of a 2009 limited edition but is a new blend.
cigars.researchNote: Davidoff names the six regions but not which leaf comes from where; the wrapper and binder regions are from Neptune. Neptune lists it as full and Famous Smoke as medium-full. Not the same cigar as the 2009 Puro Dominicano belicoso.

cigars.about: The 2024 return of the Davidoff Maduro, which ran from 2008 to 2016, now with a new blend. The Ecuadorian wrapper is a high-priming leaf fermented for 16 months, twice the usual time.
cigars.researchNote: Davidoff describes it as full-bodied with medium intensity, and Neptune lists medium. halfwheel found mild strength and medium body. Production numbers are not disclosed.

cigars.line: Grand Cru Diademas Finas Limited Edition Collection
cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (includes San Vicente seco aged six months in Bordeaux red wine casks)
cigars.about: A 2024 limited edition that puts the Grand Cru blend idea into the Diademas Finas shape, with one filler leaf aged in Bordeaux wine casks. It was the fourth and last release in Davidoff's History Re-Rolled series.
cigars.researchNote: Davidoff did not publish the blend beyond an Ecuadorian wrapper and Dominican binder and filler. Strength is Neptune's rating. About 4,000 boxes went to the U.S.

cigars.about: A 6 x 56 limited edition marking ten years of the Brazilian-influenced Escurio line. One of its four Dominican filler leaves was aged in bourbon barrels.
cigars.researchNote: 15,750 boxes of 12 were made, 3,750 of them for the U.S. Neptune describes the cask-aged filler as whisky cask; Davidoff's press quote says bourbon cask.

cigars.about: A 2023 limited edition for the tenth year of Davidoff Nicaragua, sold only in a 6 x 56 size. The tobaccos have a combined 45 years of age and one Estelí filler spent six months in rum casks.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is Ecuadorian, so it is not a Nicaraguan puro. Neptune calls the wrapper maduro and rates the cigar full; halfwheel found medium body with little nicotine strength. 3,300 boxes of 12.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (hybrid leaf, 15-year-old San Vicente, piloto aged five years in yagua leaves)
cigars.about: The fifth Chefs Edition, a 6 1/4 x 52 toro blended with five chefs who hold 11 Michelin stars between them. It is the first Davidoff to use piloto tobacco aged in yagua palm leaves.
cigars.researchNote: 17,500 boxes of 10 worldwide. Neptune lists it as medium; halfwheel found mild to just under medium strength with medium body.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Hybrid 192 seco, piloto seco, piloto viso, San Vicente ligero)
cigars.about: A 7 x 48 Churchill blended with four well known chefs: Juan Amador, Norbert Niederkofler, Masa Takayama and Jorge Vallejo. It was the fourth Chefs Edition and the first not made as a 6 x 54 toro, limited to 9,700 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Strength and body are from the halfwheel review, which found little nicotine strength until the final third.

cigars.line: Winston Churchill Limited Edition 2025 The Artist
cigars.about: A 7 x 48 Churchill honoring Winston Churchill as a painter. The box shows his painting Cork Trees Near Mimizan and has a wooden inlay shaped like a palette.
cigars.researchNote: 18,000 boxes of 10 worldwide. Neptune lists it as medium; halfwheel found it starts medium and reaches medium-full in the final third.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (piloto mejorado viso, San Vicente mejorado seco and viso), Nicaragua (Condega seco, Estelí seco)
cigars.about: A 5 7/8 x 61 double perfecto, the first Winston Churchill made in a perfecto shape. It came in a box styled after one of Churchill's briefcases, with 5,000 boxes of 10 for the U.S.
cigars.researchNote: Strength and body are from the halfwheel review (medium-plus strength, medium-full body). Total worldwide production was not disclosed.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (piloto ligero, Hybrid 20-20 seco, San Vicente mejorado ligero, San Vicente viso), Nicaragua (Estelí viso)
cigars.about: A 6 x 52 toro released in February 2021 as the third Winston Churchill limited edition. The box artwork is styled after a chessboard, and 4,500 boxes of 10 were made.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel's review gives the size as 6 x 52, but its later release lists show 6 x 56. Strength is from that review, which found it starts mild and ends just above medium.

cigars.about: The Zodiac series release for 2026 and the first Davidoff blend made entirely from the company's own hybrid seed tobaccos, with a combined age of 43 years. The standard cigar is a 6 1/2 x 55 toro.
cigars.researchNote: Went on sale in November 2025; 17,500 boxes of 10. The same blend also comes as a 6 x 52 Flagship Exclusive Torpedo and a 6 x 56 toro sold only in a Masterpiece humidor. Not the 2014 Year of the Horse, which was a Dominican puro. The Colorado wrapper shade is Neptune's label.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (San Vicente), Mexico (San Andrés negro)
cigars.about: The 2025 Zodiac release, which started Davidoff's second trip through the Chinese calendar. The standard cigar is a slim 7 x 43, and it is only the second Davidoff blend to use Mexican tobacco in the filler.
cigars.researchNote: 17,500 boxes of 10, 4,200 for the U.S. Neptune calls the wrapper maduro and the strength medium; halfwheel found mild to just under medium. Davidoff says the blend uses a Dominican hybrid seed 98 leaf from Martín García for the first time. Also made as a 6 x 52 flagship toro and a 6 x 56 humidor toro.

cigars.about: The 2024 Zodiac release, a 7 1/2 x 50 double corona with a brushed foot that leaves the filler exposed. Its tobaccos have a combined age of 60 years.
cigars.researchNote: Went on sale in November 2023; 19,500 boxes of 10 worldwide. Neptune describes the wrapper as Ecuadorian maduro; halfwheel lists only Ecuador. A 6 x 56 Flagship Edition was also made.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (piloto seco, San Vicente ligero, San Vicente seco, Yamasá viso), Nicaragua (Estelí seco)
cigars.about: The 2023 Zodiac release, a 5 15/16 x 54 double perfecto finished with a small pigtail cap.
cigars.researchNote: Went on sale in November 2022; 6,500 boxes of 10 went to the U.S. Neptune calls it full bodied, but halfwheel found medium-plus body and little nicotine strength. A 6 x 56 Flagship Edition was also made.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Hybrid 254 viso, Hybrid 259 seco, piloto ligero, San Vicente mejorado seco, San Vicente mejorado viso)
cigars.about: The 2022 Zodiac release and the first in the series with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. Darker veins were pressed onto the wrapper for 48 hours to leave tiger-like stripes.
cigars.researchNote: Went on sale in November 2021; 17,350 boxes of 10. halfwheel gives the size as 5 x 52, while Neptune lists 5 1/2 x 52.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto, San Vicente Mejorado, Yamasá), Nicaragua (Condega, Estelí)
cigars.about: The 2021 Zodiac release, a 6 x 60 gordo with a Dominican wrapper over an Ecuadorian Sumatra binder and five viso fillers. 13,500 boxes of 10 were made.
cigars.researchNote: Went on sale in November 2020. Neptune rates it full; halfwheel found medium strength with medium-full body.

cigars.filler: Brazil (Mata Fina seco), Nicaragua (Estelí viso, Jalapa viso), Dominican Republic (Hybrid 2020 seco, San Vicente mejorado seco)
cigars.about: A single-size limited edition that combines tobaccos from the three Black Band lines, Nicaragua, Escurio and Yamasá, in one blend. 13,500 boxes of 12 were made.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as "Davidoff Limited Edition 2022 Gran Toro" or the Black Band Limited Edition. Neptune calls the wrapper Ecuadorian maduro and rates it full; halfwheel lists only Ecuador and found it medium rising to medium-full.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (piloto viso, San Vicente mejorado ligero, Semilla 254 viso, Yamasá viso)
cigars.about: A 2020 re-creation of the Robusto Intenso limited edition from 2005, built from six tobaccos. 10,100 boxes of 10 were made, plus 1,960 five-count boxes for travel retail.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune rates it full bodied, but the halfwheel review found medium strength and medium-plus body with the intensity in the flavor. halfwheel's text gives 5 1/8 inches and its spec table 5 1/4.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (olor seco, piloto ligero, San Vicente seco)
cigars.about: A 2020 re-release of the 2002 Special 53, Davidoff's first all-Dominican cigar, in the same 6 1/8 x 53 perfecto. 9,700 boxes of 10 were made, 4,500 of them for the U.S.
cigars.researchNote: A Dominican puro. Neptune lists it as mild; halfwheel found it starts mild and only reaches medium at the very end.

cigars.line: The Boutique Selection New York Madison
cigars.about: A 6 x 54 toro sold only at the Davidoff of Geneva flagship store on Madison Avenue in New York, developed with the store's staff. It launched in September 2026 alongside sister blends for Geneva and Hong Kong.
cigars.researchNote: A store exclusive that Davidoff calls a permanent offering released in limited batches, so it is not sold at other retailers. Davidoff lists its intensity as medium-full. No tasting notes or leaf varietals are published.

cigars.about: Davidoff's range of handmade small cigars, all 4 1/8 x 34 with short or mixed filler and sold in tins of six. Each version is a small take on one of the main lines.
cigars.researchNote: Not one blend: versions include Dominican, Dominican Maduro, Nicaragua, Nicaragua Maduro and Escurio, each with its own wrapper, so ask which tin. The Dominican is the mild one with a Connecticut wrapper; the Escurio (2016) uses Ecuadorian Habano over Brazilian binder.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped version of Legacy, the line Nick Perdomo III blended as a 60th birthday tribute to his father. Its binder is Perdomo's own shade-grown hybrid leaf and the wrapper is aged in bourbon barrels.
cigars.researchNote: The Gran Belicoso is box-pressed and sold in boxes of 10. halfwheel scored the Epicure 91.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan Shade Grown (Cuban-seed/Cameroon-seed hybrid, aged 10 years)
cigars.about: The headline blend of the Legacy line: a Nicaraguan puro wrapped in a shade-grown hybrid leaf Perdomo developed and grows at its Finca Natalie farm in Esteli. The wrappers are bale-aged 10 years and then rested in bourbon barrels.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is a Cuban-seed (habano) and Cameroon-seed hybrid grown under shade, so it does not fit one wrapper type cleanly. Perdomo says this top-priming leaf shows more of the habano side. The Gran Belicoso is box-pressed and sold in boxes of 10.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Legacy, a Nicaraguan puro with a dark Nicaraguan wrapper over Perdomo's shade-grown hybrid binder. The wrapper spends at least 14 months in bourbon barrels after 10 years of aging.
cigars.researchNote: Perdomo calls it medium to full; halfwheel's review found the nicotine strength lighter than that. The Gran Belicoso is box-pressed and sold in boxes of 10.

cigars.about: A limited follow-up to Legacy in which Nick Perdomo Jr. and Nick Perdomo III blended the Connecticut version together. It uses aged tobaccos from the 2011 to 2016 harvests and comes in a single box-pressed figurado.
cigars.researchNote: One size only: a 6 inch box-pressed gran figurado with a 48/60/52 ring, sold in 50-count chests. Perdomo gives no strength and retailers disagree, from mild-medium to medium. Perdomo plans one or two shipments a year.

cigars.about: The Father & Son blend made by Nick Perdomo Jr., a Nicaraguan puro that uses Perdomo's shade-grown hybrid leaf for both wrapper and binder. It is a limited release built on tobaccos from the 2011 to 2016 harvests.
cigars.researchNote: One size only: a 6 inch box-pressed gran figurado with a 48/60/52 ring. The wrapper is a habano and Cameroon hybrid grown in Nicaragua; this lower priming leans Cameroon. Perdomo gives no strength; Corona Cigar lists medium and halfwheel found it just under medium.

cigars.about: The Father & Son blend made by Nick Perdomo III, a Nicaraguan puro with a maduro wrapper over Perdomo's shade-grown hybrid binder. It is a limited release built on tobaccos from the 2011 to 2016 harvests.
cigars.researchNote: One size only: a 6 inch box-pressed gran figurado with a 48/60/52 ring, sold in 50-count chests. Perdomo gives no strength; retailers list it medium to full, while halfwheel's review found it medium. Perdomo plans one or two shipments a year.

cigars.about: Perdomo's value-priced bundle cigar in its Connecticut wrapper, made with long-filler tobaccos from the company's farms in Esteli. It is sold as an everyday smoke in bundles of 25.
cigars.researchNote: Some retailers list this version simply as Perdomo Fresco. It is a bundle cigar, not a boxed line.

cigars.about: The sun grown version of Perdomo's value-priced Fresco bundle, a Nicaraguan puro made with long-filler tobaccos from the company's Esteli farms. It is sold as an everyday smoke in bundles of 25.
cigars.researchNote: Perdomo's own page is inconsistent: the description calls it medium bodied, while the spec box says medium to full. Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Perdomo's value-priced Fresco bundle, a Nicaraguan puro made with long-filler tobaccos from the company's Esteli farms. It is sold as an everyday smoke in bundles of 25.
cigars.researchNote: It is a bundle cigar, not a boxed line.

cigars.about: A line of 70 ring gauge Nicaraguan puros from Perdomo, made with five-year-aged tobaccos and priced affordably. It revives the Inmenso name the company used for big ring cigars in the early 2000s.
cigars.researchNote: Every size is a 70 ring gauge. There is no Connecticut version, which is unusual for Perdomo.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Perdomo's 70 ring gauge line, a Nicaraguan puro made with five-year-aged tobaccos and priced affordably. It revives the Inmenso name the company used for big ring cigars in the early 2000s.
cigars.researchNote: Every size is a 70 ring gauge. Perdomo calls it medium to full; Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.about: A Perdomo line made from 12-year-old tobaccos: bale-aged for ten years, then aged two more in charred oak bourbon barrels. This is the Ecuadorian Connecticut version.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2014 as a limited yearly production; it is now a standing line on Perdomo's site. Perdomo lists the Salomon at 6 1/8 x 54, halfwheel at 50/60.

cigars.line: Double Aged 12 Year Vintage Sun Grown
cigars.about: A Perdomo line made from 12-year-old tobaccos: bale-aged for ten years, then aged two more in charred oak bourbon barrels. This is the Nicaraguan puro sun grown version.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2014 as a limited yearly production; it is now a standing line on Perdomo's site. Perdomo lists the Salomon at 6 1/8 x 54, halfwheel at 50/60. Perdomo calls it medium to full; halfwheel's Salomon review found it under medium.

cigars.about: A Perdomo line made from 12-year-old tobaccos: bale-aged for ten years, then aged two more in charred oak bourbon barrels. This is the Nicaraguan puro maduro version.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2014 as a limited yearly production; it is now a standing line on Perdomo's site. Perdomo lists the Salomon at 6 1/8 x 54, halfwheel at 50/60.

cigars.about: Perdomo's ESV line, first released in 2005 as a tribute to Nick Perdomo Sr. and reblended in 2016 around tobacco from the first crops of the Finca Natalie farm. The Connecticut is the one version that is not a Nicaraguan puro.
cigars.researchNote: Often called ESV. Box-pressed since 2019. Perdomo no longer lists it and Neptune marks every size discontinued. Perdomo rated it mild to medium; Neptune lists it as mild.

cigars.about: Perdomo's ESV line, first released in 2005 as a tribute to Nick Perdomo Sr. and reblended in 2016 around tobacco from the first crops of the Finca Natalie farm. The sun grown version is a Nicaraguan puro.
cigars.researchNote: Often called ESV. Box-pressed since 2019. Perdomo no longer lists it and Neptune marks every size discontinued. Perdomo rated it medium to full; Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.about: Perdomo's ESV line, first released in 2005 as a tribute to Nick Perdomo Sr. and reblended in 2016 around tobacco from the first crops of the Finca Natalie farm. The maduro version is a Nicaraguan puro.
cigars.researchNote: Often called ESV. Box-pressed since 2019. Perdomo no longer lists it and Neptune marks every size discontinued. Perdomo rated it medium to full; Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.about: A Perdomo line of shorter sizes made with 10-year-aged tobaccos and bourbon barrel-aged wrappers, released in three wrappers during 2015. The Connecticut shipped first, in March 2015.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as Small Batch 2005. Perdomo no longer lists it and Neptune marks every size discontinued. Perdomo rated it mild to medium; Neptune lists it as mild.

cigars.about: A Perdomo line of shorter sizes made with 10-year-aged tobaccos and bourbon barrel-aged wrappers, released in three wrappers during 2015. The sun grown version is a Nicaraguan puro that shipped in April 2015.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as Small Batch 2005. Perdomo no longer lists it and Neptune marks every size discontinued. Perdomo rated it medium to full; Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.about: A Perdomo line of shorter sizes made with 10-year-aged tobaccos and bourbon barrel-aged wrappers, released in three wrappers during 2015. The maduro version is a Nicaraguan puro that shipped last, in May 2015.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as Small Batch 2005. Perdomo no longer lists it and Neptune marks every size discontinued. Perdomo rated it medium to full; Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan Sun Grown (same wrapper as Perdomo 20th Anniversary Sun Grown)
cigars.about: Perdomo's entry in the Firecracker series from Two Guys Smoke Shop and United Cigars: a short Nicaraguan puro with a long pigtail cap shaped like a fuse. It is a strong, ligero-forward smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Made for Two Guys Smoke Shop and distributed by United Cigars. 1,000 boxes of 20 in 2020 and 500 boxes in 2021. Nick Perdomo Jr. described it as full-bodied.

cigars.about: A shade-wrapped companion to Angel Cuesta Rosado, hand rolled at J.C. Newman's El Reloj factory in Tampa. The name revives an early 1900s Cuesta-Rey brand.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are undisclosed. It first appeared in a TAA sampler in December 2024 and went to wider release in September 2025. Halfwheel reported in March 2026 that only the Toro had shipped, not the other two sizes.

cigars.about: An annual fall limited edition of Brick House, released for Oktoberfest alongside a beer stein promotion at participating stores.
cigars.researchNote: The blend and size have changed over the years. Specs here are the 2025 and 2026 releases, which are the same cigar. The 2023 and 2024 releases were 6 x 52 toros.

cigars.line: Brick House Is On Fire TAA Exclusive
cigars.about: A 2025 exclusive for Tobacconists' Association of America member stores. It is the regular Brick House blend in a 6 x 50 toro with an uncovered foot, so the filler lights first.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,000 boxes of 10, sold only at TAA retailers. Strength is the maker's rating for the regular Brick House blend, which this cigar uses.

cigars.about: A mild Dominican cigar made for J.C. Newman by the Fuente family, created to mark the 100th anniversary of the Cuesta-Rey brand. The cigars are aged in cedar for up to five years.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the wrapper as Connecticut Shade without a country, while Neptune calls it Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade. The maker rates it Mild, while retailers say mild to medium. Also sold with a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Cuesta-Rey Centenario, with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over Dominican tobacco. It is made for J.C. Newman at the Fuente factory.
cigars.researchNote: This is the maduro wrapper option of the Centenario line, not a separate blend. The maker does not say which sizes come in maduro, so the sizes here are the ones retailers list. The maker rates the line Mild, while Holt's says mild to medium and Neptune says medium.

cigars.about: A long-running Cuesta-Rey line first introduced in 1958 and now made at the Fuente factory. Its No. 95 is known as an early premium cigar to use an African Cameroon wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's spec lists African Cameroon for the line, but its own description calls the No. 898 Connecticut-wrapped. Check the box before telling a guest which wrapper a No. 898 has.

cigars.filler: Five fillers from the Caribbean and Central America
cigars.about: The maduro version of J.C. Newman's Diamond Crown, made by the Fuente family with a double-fermented Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. Most sizes have a 54 ring gauge.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists No. 6 as a 6 x 46/54 figurado, while Neptune lists it with a 64 ring. The maker says the filler comes from the Caribbean and Central America, while Neptune lists it as Dominican. Neptune also lists a Pyramid No. 7 (6 3/4 x 54) in maduro.

cigars.filler: Five fillers from the Caribbean and Central America
cigars.about: A Diamond Crown blend that honors J.C. Newman's home city, made by the Fuente family in the Dominican Republic. It is the first cigar from the Fuente factory to use Florida Sun Grown tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists 6 1/2 x 52 with a Florida Sun Grown binder. Halfwheel lists it as 6 x 52 with a Dominican binder and the Florida tobacco in the filler. Launched July 15, 2025 and aimed at Tampa stores.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Nicaraguan cigar with an Ecuadorian Corojo-seed wrapper, added in 2020 when J.C. Newman reworked the Perla del Mar brand. It is a value-priced line from the company's factory in Esteli.
The mild, shade-wrapped version of Quorum, J.C. Newman's value-priced bundle cigar made in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists a Sumatra Sungrown binder, while retailers describe the binder as Nicaraguan or Nicaraguan and Dominican. Neptune lists the Torpedo as 6 x 52 and the Tres Petit Corona as 4 1/2 x 38.

cigars.about: A value-priced Nicaraguan cigar that J.C. Newman calls a cousin of Quorum, made in larger ring gauges with a Havana-seed wrapper grown in Ecuador. It is sold in resealable humidified bags of 20.
cigars.researchNote: Despite the name it contains no Cuban tobacco.

cigars.about: A Tampa-rolled cigar named for the Tampa Smokers, the city's baseball team from 1919 to 1954. It is hand rolled at J.C. Newman's El Reloj factory and includes a size shaped like a baseball bat.
cigars.researchNote: The Grand Slam is a baseball bat shape that halfwheel lists as 7 x 52/42, and boxes hold 10 Toros and one bat. The Toro first shipped in a TAA sampler in December 2024, with nationwide release in April 2025. The maker rates it Mild, but halfwheel's review found medium strength and full flavor.

cigars.about: An annual limited edition rolled at El Reloj in Tampa with the LeRoy Neiman foundation. Each year features a different Neiman painting on the band and a lithograph in the box.
cigars.researchNote: Same blend each year in a new size: 2023 was a 6 x 52 toro, 2024 a 7 x 50 churchill, 2025 a 6 1/4 x 52 torpedo, 2026 a 6 1/2 x 56 toro grande (750 boxes of 20). Halfwheel's review lists the wrapper as Ecuadorian. The maker does not state its origin.
