cigars.about: A mild, value-priced Dominican cigar made at the Fuente factory since 1986. It came out of a partnership between Stanford Newman and Carlos Fuente Sr. and was originally sold in cellophane bundles instead of boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold with a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper. The maker lists No. 300 as 6 7/10 x 44, while retailers list it as 6 3/4 x 44.

cigars.about: The maduro version of La Unica, with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over the same Dominican blend. It is a mild, value-priced cigar made at the Fuente factory.
cigars.researchNote: This is the maduro wrapper option of La Unica, not a separate blend. Mike's lists all six sizes in maduro, while Holt's shows only No. 100, No. 500 and No. 600. Flavor words are the maker's for the whole line.

cigars.about: A mild cigar billed as "The Aromatic Cigar", reviving a J.C. Newman brand first rolled in 1900. It is made in Esteli with an Ecuadorian shade wrapper and began shipping in December 2025.
cigars.researchNote: The maker labels the strength "Mild Aromatic". Halfwheel's review found a sweetened cap and a very sweet profile, so tell guests it smokes like an aromatic. The maker lists the Robusto as 5 x 50, while halfwheel lists it as 4 3/4 x 52.

cigars.about: An annual limited release for Tampa's Gasparilla pirate festival, named for the legendary pirate Jose Gaspar. It is sold each January only at stores around Tampa.
cigars.researchNote: Specs are the 2026 release, which halfwheel says is a new blend, limited to 2,000 boxes of 10. The size and blend have changed over the years. The 2022 original was a 7 x 50 churchill.

cigars.about: A value-priced maduro bundle cigar made in Nicaragua with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. J.C. Newman revived the name from an 1898 brand that was named after a champion racehorse.
cigars.researchNote: Often listed by retailers as Alcazar Maduro. The maker rates it Full, while Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.about: A long-standing value cigar from J.C. Newman, made with Cuban-seed long filler at the company's factory in Nicaragua. It comes in natural and maduro versions.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's spec table lists Nicaraguan binder and filler, but its own intro and Neptune both say the tobacco is grown in Honduras. Neptune calls it medium to full bodied. The maker does not say where the Sumatra wrapper is grown.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Don Jose, J.C. Newman's value cigar made with Cuban-seed long filler in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The maker says Don Jose comes in Natural and Maduro but does not publish the maduro wrapper or its sizes. Neptune describes the wrapper as Brazilian maduro and the cigar as medium to full, which no other source confirms. Binder, filler and strength are the maker's specs for the line as a whole.

cigars.about: A regular production Punch line named after the brand's puppet mascot, made in Nicaragua with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It comes only in large ring gauges.
cigars.researchNote: Also written as Mr. Punch by Punch Cigars. The 7 x 70 Big Slapper is the largest size Punch has released.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: An all-Honduran toro released to mark 25 years of Punch Rare Corojo. It is made for Punch at the Aladino factory of JRE Tobacco rather than at the brand's usual factory.
cigars.researchNote: A different blend from the regular Rare Corojo, which uses an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. Punch calls it a full-time release, though halfwheel's review labels it a limited edition. Punch rates it medium and halfwheel agreed, but Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.about: The maduro version of the core Honduran Punch Clásico line, with a dark Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper in place of the Ecuadorian Sumatra. It is known for an earthy, sweet profile.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke sells it as Clasico Broadleaf, lists a Connecticut Broadleaf binder and rates it full. Punch lists a Connecticut Shade binder and a medium profile.

cigars.about: A full-bodied extension of the Punch Gran Puro line built on Nicaraguan binder and filler under a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper. It is regular production from General Cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Despite the name it is not a Nicaraguan puro: the wrapper is Connecticut Broadleaf. Halfwheel says it is rolled at STG Danlí in Honduras, while Neptune lists Nicaragua as the origin.

cigars.about: A mellower Honduran-made Punch line with a Connecticut Shade wrapper over a broadleaf binder and filler from three countries. Cigar Aficionado named it one of its 25 best cigars of 2010.
cigars.researchNote: Punch says the No. II wears an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, and a No. II Maduro is also sold. Halfwheel reported in March 2025 that the Diadema, Britania and Robusto sizes were discontinued, though Punch's site still lists them. Neptune rates the natural mild and the maduro medium.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: A Honduran puro made with Corojo tobacco grown by the Eiroa family, who roll it for Punch at their Aladino factory. Punch rates it mellow to medium.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is listed very differently: Punch rates it mellow to medium and halfwheel's review found it mild to medium, but Neptune lists medium and Famous Smoke lists full. The Lancero was added in 2024.

cigars.about: The second blend in Punch's budget-priced Knuckle Buster family, with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over an Indonesian binder and Nicaraguan filler. It is made in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Punch and Neptune rate it medium; Famous Smoke lists it as full. The Stubby size was added in 2024.

cigars.about: The third and lightest Knuckle Buster blend, a budget-priced Honduran-made cigar with an Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper. It uses tobacco from six countries.
cigars.researchNote: Punch rates it mellow to medium; Neptune and Famous Smoke both list medium.

cigars.about: A Honduran-made Punch blend sold by Holt's that is aged in cedar cabinets for more than a year before it ships. Every size comes in a natural and a maduro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Each size also comes in a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro. Only Holt's lists this line; Punch's own site does not.

cigars.about: The 2026 entry in Punch's Lunar New Year series, a 6 x 60 version of the 2019 Egg Roll with the same blend. It has an unfinished foot and comes in a box styled like a Chinese takeout container.
cigars.researchNote: A larger remake of the original 4.5 x 50 Egg Roll from 2019. Production numbers were not disclosed.

cigars.about: Punch's 2025 Father's Day limited edition, packaged to look like a pack of hot dogs. The toro is capped at both ends and one half contains Dominican andullo tobacco, so it smokes differently depending on which end is lit.
cigars.researchNote: Can be lit from either end. Punch rates it medium to full; Neptune lists it as full. Sold in packs of 10.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Estelí, Condega), Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano), Honduras (Jamastran)
cigars.about: Punch's 2025 Lunar New Year limited edition, a short belicoso with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper. Each cigar has a wooden stick attached to its cellophane so it looks like a bottle rocket.
cigars.researchNote: Punch's site says Bottle Rockets; Cigar World and halfwheel call it Bottle Rocket. Punch and Neptune rate it full, but halfwheel's review found the strength mild to medium.

cigars.about: Punch's 2024 Father's Day limited edition, a box-pressed toro with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over all-Nicaraguan binder and filler. It comes in packaging styled like a 1980s VHS tape set.
cigars.researchNote: Punch rates it medium; Neptune lists it as full. Halfwheel's review put the strength a little above medium.

cigars.filler: Honduras (La Entrada), Nicaragua (Estelí), Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano)
cigars.about: Punch's 2024 Lunar New Year limited edition for the Year of the Dragon, a 5 x 60 flat-headed cigar with a dark Mexican wrapper. It is one of the few Punch cigars rolled in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Punch describes the wrapper only as Mexican, without naming a region. Punch rates it full; Neptune lists medium and halfwheel's review landed at medium to medium-full.

cigars.filler: Brazil (Mata Fina), Nicaragua (Condega), Honduras (La Entrada), Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano)
cigars.about: Punch's 2023 Father's Day limited edition, a short, fat perfecto with a Cameroon wrapper and tobacco from six countries. The cigars were packed in reusable cans made to look like a four-pack of beer.
cigars.researchNote: Part of Punch's Father's Day limited edition series. Production numbers were not disclosed.

cigars.about: Punch's 2023 Lunar New Year limited edition, a short robusto with a shaggy foot that revisits the original Egg Roll with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. It was sold in boxes styled like Chinese takeout containers.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 5,000 boxes of 25. Halfwheel's review found the strength below medium.

cigars.about: Punch's 2022 Lunar New Year limited edition for the Year of the Tiger, a box-pressed toro with a Honduran Habano wrapper and a long pigtail cap. It uses tobacco from five countries.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 6,400 boxes of 20.

cigars.about: A limited double corona released in 2021 to mark the 180th anniversary of the Punch brand. It has a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper and binder over filler from three countries.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 3,400 boxes of 10, which General Cigar called its most limited Punch release at the time.

cigars.about: Punch's 2021 Lunar New Year limited edition for the Year of the Ox, a toro with a dark broadleaf wrapper over a Honduran Habano binder. It is the third cigar in the series that began with Egg Roll.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 4,500 boxes of 20.

cigars.about: Punch's 2020 Lunar New Year limited edition, a long, thin panatela with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. It was packaged with chopsticks and has a fortune printed inside each band.
cigars.researchNote: Made in the Dominican Republic, unlike most Punch cigars. Limited to 3,650 boxes of 25. Punch rates it medium, but halfwheel's review found it medium-full to full.

cigars.about: A collaboration between Punch and Tampa's Cigar City Brewing, blended to pair with the brewery's beers. It is an all-Honduran cigar with a maduro Habano-seed wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Full name is Cigar City Brewing Maduro by Punch. It launched in late 2021 at select liquor chains ahead of a wider rollout. No source says whether it is still in production.

cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped cigar over Nicaraguan binder and filler, made by Esteban Carreras at its own factory in Esteli. It arrived quietly in stores in August 2020.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium to full-bodied, but Neptune lists it as medium and reviews by halfwheel and Cigar Coop found it mild to medium in strength. A 4 x 38 tin size was added in 2026.

cigars.about: A box-pressed offshoot of the Chupacabra line with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It debuted at the 2016 trade show, and the small Hellcatito size followed in 2018.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's site lists it simply as Hellcat. Neptune rates it medium, Atlantic medium to full. The line is box-pressed.

cigars.line: Taken From The Dictator's Hand Maduro
cigars.about: The maduro version of the Dictator's Hand line, built around a corojo-seed wrapper given a long, low-heat extra fermentation. The story behind it is corojo seed smuggled out of Cuba in the 1990s by the man who now runs the Esteban Carreras factory.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2023 as Taken From the Devil's Hand Corojo Maduro and renamed in 2024 after a trademark dispute. The maker lists an Ecuadorian corojo maduro wrapper, but Atlantic calls it Nicaraguan. Neptune and Cigar Coop rate it medium, Atlantic medium to full, and halfwheel found it mild.

cigars.about: A barrel-aged blend from Esteban Carreras: the tobacco and then the finished cigars rest in barrels that held Flor de Cana 18 year rum. It includes the company's first 70 ring gauge size.
cigars.researchNote: Released in 2019 as Unforgiven and renamed Unforsaken in 2020. Strength varies by source: Atlantic says medium to full, Neptune full, and Cigar Coop's review medium. The maker lists four sizes with the toro at 6 x 50, while halfwheel and Atlantic list it as 6 x 52.

cigars.about: The natural-wrapper follow-up to Mr. Brownstone, an all-Nicaraguan blend under a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper. It was added at the 2018 trade show.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's site shows the Maduro's broadleaf blend under this name, which looks like a copy error: halfwheel, Neptune and Atlantic all list a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper. Atlantic sells it as Mr. Brownstone Habano. Neptune rates it medium, Atlantic medium to full.

cigars.about: The original Mr. Brownstone, a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro over an Ecuadorian Habano binder and Nicaraguan filler. It launched at the 2017 trade show, with the small Boolit size added in 2018.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is listed differently by source: Neptune says medium, Atlantic medium to full, and Cigar Coop's review called it full. It launched simply as Mr. Brownstone.

cigars.about: The second cigar in the Esteban Carreras Cross series, following Black Cross with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco. It was shown at the 2015 trade show.
cigars.researchNote: The toro's ring gauge differs by source: the maker lists 5 1/2 x 50, Cigar Coop 52 and halfwheel 54. Atlantic and Neptune both call it medium to full. Atlantic says it is box-pressed.

cigars.about: The first of the Esteban Carreras Cross series, a Habano Café wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. The name refers to a mark put on the doors of supporters of the brand's namesake during the Cuban revolution.
cigars.researchNote: No source says where the Habano Café wrapper is grown. The Bonita and Cervantes are figurados.

cigars.about: A San Andrés-wrapped cigar with Nicaraguan binder and filler, listed in the Esteban Carreras catalog in four sizes sold in boxes of 24.
cigars.researchNote: The maker publishes no strength or release year for this line. Neptune lists a 10 Anos Maduro with the same San Andrés over Nicaraguan blend, likely the same cigar, and calls it medium to full bodied. It is a different cigar from the Chupacabra 10 Year Anniversary.

cigars.about: A dark Habano Oscuro-wrapped cigar with Nicaraguan binder and filler. The maker's About page names Covenant alongside Chupacabra as one of its popular lines.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not say where the wrapper is grown. Neptune calls the cigar a Nicaraguan puro with a Habano maduro wrapper. Strength is from Neptune, the only source that gives one, and no release year is published.

cigars.about: The broadleaf maduro version of the Esteban Carreras Bloodline series, with Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is listed in the maker's catalog in five sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not say where the broadleaf wrapper is grown. Neptune calls the cigar a Nicaraguan puro. Strength is from Neptune, the only source that gives one, and no release year is published.

cigars.about: The Nicaraguan puro in the Esteban Carreras Bloodline series, with a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper. Its sizes carry family-tree names such as Lineage, Stemma and Progeny.
cigars.researchNote: Strength and tasting notes are from Neptune, the only source that gives them, and no release year is published. The maker's catalog spells the 5.2 x 56 size Grodito.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped member of the Esteban Carreras Bloodline series, with Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is listed in the maker's catalog in six sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not say where the Connecticut wrapper is grown. Strength is from Neptune, the only source that gives one. The catalog lists Progeny as 6 x 60 here but 7 x 56 in the other Bloodline blends.

cigars.about: An older Esteban Carreras blend from 2008, a Nicaraguan puro with a natural Habano wrapper. It is the lighter-wrapped partner to the Habano Maduro.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune describes it as medium to full bodied, while Blind Man's Puff's panel called it medium. The release year comes from Blind Man's Puff. Neptune's sampler lists it as 13 Year Aged Habano.

cigars.about: The dark-wrapped half of the Esteban Carreras Habano series, a Nicaraguan puro that Neptune and Cigar Coop both rate full strength. It has been on the market since at least 2009.
cigars.researchNote: No source gives an exact release year. Neptune sells it in a sampler as 13 Year Aged Habano Maduro. Cigar Coop's 2011 review called the 4 x 54 size the Rothman.

cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped cigar from Esteban Carreras with a Nicaraguan binder. Its filler mixes Nicaraguan and Dominican tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not say where the Connecticut wrapper is grown. Strength is from Neptune, the only source that gives one: it says the cigar starts mild and peaks at medium. No release year is published.

cigars.about: A sweetened Nicaraguan puro with a Habano maduro wrapper. Instead of only sweetening the cap, every leaf is sprayed with sugar water so the sweetness carries through the cigar, and the owner says it is now the company's number two seller.
cigars.researchNote: This is a sweetened cigar, so tell guests up front. Neptune lists it as full, but halfwheel's review found the nicotine strength mild to just under medium with medium-full flavor. The binder and filler regions are not disclosed.

cigars.about: The lighter follow-up to Las Cañas, with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It uses the same method of sweetening every leaf with sugar water.
cigars.researchNote: This is a sweetened cigar. It was introduced at the 2026 trade show with a May 2026 release date, and no strength rating or tasting notes are published yet.

cigars.about: A small-production San Andrés maduro from Esteban Carreras, named rope of gold for the twist of tobacco it wears in place of a band. The cigars get an extra year of rest in their boxes before shipping.
cigars.researchNote: Regular production but limited to about 50 boxes of each size a month. Also sold as Soga de Oro Maduro or Black Maduro. Strength is from Atlantic, and no tasting notes are published.

cigars.about: The second Soga de Oro blend, with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper aged three years over Nicaraguan binder and filler. Like the original it wears a twist of tobacco instead of a band and is made by a single pair of rollers.
cigars.researchNote: Regular production but limited to about 50 boxes of each size a month. Atlantic sells it as Soga de Oro Red Sumatra. Strength is from Atlantic, and no tasting notes are published.

cigars.about: An older Esteban Carreras blend, a Nicaraguan puro with a maduro wrapper that came out in 2010. It is still in the portfolio and was one of five lines given a small tin size in 2026.
cigars.researchNote: The blend, strength and the toro and torpedo sizes come from a 2010 Cigar Coop review. The maker's current site does not list this line, so those two sizes may no longer be made. Neptune calls it medium bodied, and the 4 x 38 tin was announced for May 2026.

cigars.about: An extension of the Perez-Carrillo Pledge line from Casa Carrillo, launched in 2026 with purple bands and boxes. It keeps the Pledge's Connecticut Havana-seed wrapper, now aged close to ten years, over a new Mexican binder and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 3,500 boxes of 10 per size, shipped in batches through the year. The toro came out in March 2026 and the box-pressed robusto in October 2026. Sold under the Perez-Carrillo name by Casa Carrillo, the company formerly called E.P. Carrillo.

cigars.about: A patriotic limited edition from Casa Carrillo that has shipped each year around Flag Day and the Fourth of July since 2023. The name joins two other Perez-Carrillo lines, Pledge and Allegiance.
cigars.researchNote: The blend changes by year, and the details listed are the 2026 toro. The 2023 to 2025 editions used a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. The toro is 1,776 boxes of 10 each year, and the 2026 Rockets is a separate blend not yet announced.

cigars.about: An ocean-themed limited edition in the Perez-Carrillo brand from Casa Carrillo, released in 2026 in one 6 x 56 size. It pairs a Jalapa wrapper with a Honduran binder and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists strength as Medium Plus and Neptune lists Medium. Limited to 2,500 numbered boxes of 20. It previewed at Smoke Inn's Great Smoke in March 2026 and shipped nationally in May.

cigars.about: A stronger, broadleaf-wrapped offshoot of the Perez-Carrillo Encore from Casa Carrillo. The wrapper is fermented for 18 months and aged three years, and the cigar is box-pressed.
cigars.researchNote: Regular production, first sold on Black Friday 2023 at Fox Cigar Bar in Arizona and shipped nationally in March 2024. The Bulwarks perfecto was added in July 2025. The original Encore is a Nicaraguan puro, so this is a different blend.

cigars.about: A limited Perez-Carrillo Encore extension from Casa Carrillo made mainly for markets outside the United States. It looks much like Encore Black but is a different blend.
cigars.researchNote: The blend listed is the original 2024 Noir, 3,000 boxes of 10 a year with only 500 for US events. Encore Noir II (July 2026) is a different, all-Nicaraguan blend in a 6 1/8 x 50 toro called Celestial No. 2, limited to 1,500 boxes of 10. The wrapper variety and strength are not published.

cigars.about: A limited Perez-Carrillo Encore release from Casa Carrillo built from well-aged tobacco and sold only outside the United States. Each edition is a single size.
cigars.researchNote: International markets only, and no strength is published. The blend listed is the 2024 original, 1,500 boxes of 10. Edición Unica II (July 2026) is all Nicaraguan tobacco aged at least five years, a 6 1/4 x 54 toro extra with a 109 head called Amigos, limited to 1,100 numbered boxes of 10.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Estelí), USA (Pennsylvania Broadleaf), Dominican Republic (La Canela, Pelo de Oro), Mexico (San Andrés)
cigars.about: A sub-line of Perez-Carrillo La Historia blended by Lissette Perez-Carrillo and inspired by women. The final blend was picked by a panel of retailers and women cigar smokers from three wrapper options.
cigars.researchNote: Made in limited batches: 1,500 boxes of 10 in August 2025 and 2,500 boxes in August 2026. The binder and filler were undisclosed at launch and published with the second batch. Part of the 2026 proceeds go to Dress for Success Miami.

cigars.about: A regular production Perez-Carrillo line from Casa Carrillo introduced at the 2026 PCA trade show. The three sizes are named for mountain landforms and the blend is meant to change as it burns.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists strength as Medium Plus and Neptune lists Medium. The Ridge size has an oval press, and all sizes come in boxes of 20.

cigars.about: The first blend in the E.P. Carrillo Essence Series, a group of lower-priced lines that each showcase a different wrapper. This one is built around an Ecuadorian Sumatra leaf with two binders.
cigars.researchNote: The band and box read E.P. Carrillo Sumatra. Essence Series is the name of the collection. The maker rates it medium in strength and body but full in flavor.

cigars.about: The second blend in the E.P. Carrillo Essence Series, positioned as an everyday maduro. It uses a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over a Honduran binder and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: The band and box read E.P. Carrillo Maduro. Essence Series is the name of the collection. The maker rates it medium in strength and body but full in flavor.

cigars.about: The third blend in the E.P. Carrillo Essence Series, centered on Honduran tobacco. It is made for the company by the Plasencia family in Honduras rather than at the Carrillo factory.
cigars.researchNote: The band and box read E.P. Carrillo Honduras. It is not rolled in the Dominican Republic like most Carrillo cigars. The wrapper gets a two-year fermentation and its seed variety is not published.

cigars.about: The fourth blend in the E.P. Carrillo Essence Series and the mildest of the group. It has an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper and is made in Danlí, Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: The band and box read E.P. Carrillo Connecticut. It is rolled in Honduras, not at the Carrillo factory. It has a corona in place of the gordo the other Essence blends carry.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro in E.P. Carrillo's large ring gauge INCH series, made by the Plasencia family in Estelí with tobacco from their own farms. It was the first INCH made outside the company's Dominican factory.
cigars.researchNote: Tobaccos come from Jalapa, Condega and Estelí. The No. 62 scored 91 in Cigar Aficionado. The INCH name refers to the 64 ring gauge size, which is one inch across.

cigars.about: E.P. Carrillo's series of small-batch limited editions, started in 2010, with a new blend for each release. The 2023 edition was made with Oscar Valladares in Honduras and uses Copán tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Every Short Run is a different blend, and the details listed are the 2023 edition, the first made outside the Dominican Republic. Editions ran yearly from 2010 to 2016, paused, and returned in 2021. The 2023 run was 1,250 boxes of 24 each for the robusto and toro and 625 for the gordo.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Estelí, Jalapa, Condega), Dominican Republic (La Canela)
cigars.about: A limited edition released in November 2024 to mark 15 years since the Perez-Carrillo family started the E.P. Carrillo brand in 2009. It is a single size built on long-aged wrapper and binder leaf.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 5,000 boxes of 15, with 3,500 for the US. The maker does not publish a strength: Neptune lists Medium, while halfwheel's review found it building to medium-full. The filler is eight tobaccos aged five to seven years.

cigars.about: Casa Carrillo's 2025 limited edition for shops that belong to the Tobacconists' Association of America. It is a box-pressed toro with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Details are for the 2025 edition, 1,000 boxes of 10, the first one branded Casa Carrillo. The company made TAA exclusives in earlier years with different blends. Strength is Neptune's listing, and Neptune lists only Nicaraguan filler where halfwheel lists Nicaragua and the US.

cigars.about: A limited Perez-Carrillo release from Casa Carrillo that honors US military veterans, inspired by Navy veteran Lionel McKoy, the company's shipping manager. Part of the sales goes to veteran and first responder charities.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,500 numbered boxes of 20, each with a Battleborn dog tag. It uses two binders. The maker calls it full strength and full bodied, though halfwheel's reviewer found the strength closer to medium.

cigars.about: A small limited edition marking Ernesto Perez-Carrillo Jr.'s 70th birthday. Smokers voted on three unbanded blends from an event pack in 2022 and the winner shipped to stores in May 2023.
cigars.researchNote: Only 500 boxes of 10 were made, so it is very hard to find now. Halfwheel says only that the wrapper is Mexican and Neptune calls it a Mexican maduro, with no growing region published. Strength is from Neptune alone, and halfwheel's reviewer found it mild to medium.

cigars.about: An infused cigar Drew Estate released in 2019 to mark 20 years of the ACID brand. The original has a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over an Indonesian binder and Nicaraguan filler, with a sweetened tip.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as ACID 20 Connecticut (2022) with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over the same binder and filler. Drew Estate lists the Connecticut Toro at 6 x 50, halfwheel and retailers list 6 x 54. Halfwheel gave the launch robusto as 5 x 52.

cigars.about: A darker-wrapped version of the small ACID Blondie, added by Drew Estate in 2014. It is an infused 4 x 38 petit corona.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the ACID Blue line. Halfwheel and Famous give a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper, while Neptune lists Connecticut Broadleaf. Strength is listed as Medium by Famous and Mild by Neptune.

cigars.about: A larger 5 x 54 belicoso version of the ACID Blondie from Drew Estate. It is an infused cigar in the ACID Blue line.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the ACID Blue line. Neptune and Atlantic list a Connecticut Shade wrapper and Mild strength, while Famous lists Cameroon and Medium.

cigars.about: A thick 5 x 58 box-pressed infused cigar in Drew Estate's ACID Blue line. Retailers describe it as creamy with a sweet finish.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the ACID Blue line. Famous and Atlantic list a Sumatra wrapper and Medium strength, while Neptune lists Cameroon and Mild. Drew Estate does not publish the blend.

cigars.about: A 6 x 50 toro version of the ACID Kuba Kuba from Drew Estate, sold in individual tubes. It is an infused cigar with sweet, herbal notes.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the ACID Blue line, sold in tubos. Famous and Neptune list a Sumatra wrapper, Atlantic lists Connecticut Shade. Strength varies by retailer: Mild (Neptune), Mild-Medium (Atlantic), Medium (Famous).

cigars.about: A 6 x 60 version of the ACID Kuba Kuba that Drew Estate added in 2013. It is an infused cigar with a Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the ACID Blue line. Neptune and Atlantic list Mild strength, Famous lists Medium.

cigars.about: A Sumatra-wrapped version of the 4 x 38 ACID Blondie that Drew Estate added in 2017. It is an infused cigar in the ACID Gold line.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the ACID Gold line. Famous describes an Indonesian wrapper and binder, while Atlantic lists a Nicaraguan binder. Famous and Atlantic list Medium strength, Neptune lists Mild.

cigars.about: A 5 x 50 maduro robusto in Drew Estate's ACID Gold line. It is an infused cigar with a dark wrapper over Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the ACID Gold line. Famous and Atlantic describe a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper, though Famous's spec table says undisclosed and Neptune lists a Nicaraguan maduro. Neptune also lists it as Mild. Drew Estate does not publish the blend.

cigars.about: A tiny 2 1/2 x 50 infused cigar in Drew Estate's ACID Purple line, released in 2019 during the brand's 20th anniversary. It is packed two to a glass tube.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the ACID Purple line. Sold two cigars per glass tube. Retailers list Medium, but halfwheel's reviewer found almost no nicotine strength.

cigars.about: A 5 1/2 x 50 broadleaf maduro cigar added to Drew Estate's ACID Purple line in 2019. It is an infused cigar that sits alongside Extra Ordinary Larry.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the ACID Purple line.

cigars.about: The 6 x 60 maduro in Drew Estate's ACID Purple line. It is an infused cigar that retailers describe as creamy with a floral aroma.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the ACID Purple line. Famous and Atlantic list a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper, Neptune lists a Nicaraguan maduro. Strength varies by retailer: Medium (Neptune), Medium-Full (Atlantic), Full (Famous).

cigars.about: A green candela-wrapped version of the 4 x 38 ACID Blondie, added to regular boxes by Drew Estate in 2017. It is a mild infused cigar with grassy notes.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the ACID Green line. Launched as Blondie Green, and many retailers still use that name. Drew Estate does not say where the candela leaf is grown; Neptune lists it as Nicaraguan.

cigars.about: A green candela-wrapped version of the 5 x 54 ACID Kuba Kuba, introduced by Drew Estate in 2017. It is a mild infused cigar with grassy notes.
cigars.researchNote: One size in the ACID Green line. Launched as Kuba Kuba Green, and many retailers still use that name. Drew Estate does not say where the candela leaf is grown; Neptune lists it as Nicaraguan.

cigars.about: An infused 5 x 50 robusto in Drew Estate's ACID Subculture series, whose blends are made for specific retailers. Malta is sold by Neptune Cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Part of the ACID Subculture series and found only at Neptune Cigar. Neptune lists a USA Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper but a Natural color, so the wrapper is left blank. Drew Estate does not publish the blend.

cigars.about: An infused 5 1/2 x 52 robusto in Drew Estate's ACID Subculture series, made as a Famous Smoke Shop exclusive. The Subculture cigars get an extra year of aging.
cigars.researchNote: A Famous Smoke Shop exclusive in the ACID Subculture series. Famous calls the wrapper a proprietary natural leaf and does not say what it is.

cigars.about: An infused 5 1/2 x 46 corona in Drew Estate's ACID Subculture series, made as a Famous Smoke Shop exclusive. It has a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco and an extra year of aging.
cigars.researchNote: A Famous Smoke Shop exclusive in the ACID Subculture series.

cigars.about: An infused 5 1/2 x 52 robusto with a sweetened tip that Drew Estate made for the Smoker Friendly chain. It debuted at the 2021 Rocky Mountain Cigar Festival.
cigars.researchNote: A Smoker Friendly store exclusive, announced as ongoing production. The wrapper is described only as Indonesian, and the maker gives body (medium) but no strength.

cigars.about: An infused 5 x 54 cigar Drew Estate released in 2023 in memory of Allan Blatt, the founder of Best Cigar Prices. It has an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Made for Best Cigar Prices. No source says whether it is a limited run or ongoing. The blend under the wrapper is given only as Nicaraguan tobaccos.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: An all-Nicaraguan version of the Reserva Real, blended by Rafael Nodal and AJ Fernandez and rolled at Fernandez's factory in Esteli from tobacco grown on his farms. It wears a blue and gold band.
cigars.researchNote: Nicaraguan puro; the wrapper varietal is not published. The maker calls it medium-bodied, while Neptune describes it as full strength. It launched in four sizes in May 2020; the Corona and No. 2 were added later.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A darker take on the Reserva Real Nicaragua from AJ Fernandez and Rafael Nodal, using a Nicaraguan oscuro wrapper that gets its color from extended fermentation. It is a Nicaraguan puro rolled at Fernandez's factory in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: The company describes it as medium to full-bodied; halfwheel's review found the strength closer to mild to medium. Beyond the oscuro wrapper grown by AJ Fernandez, blend details are not published.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Two Nicaraguan wrappers in a barber pole
cigars.about: A barber pole version of the Reserva Real Nicaragua, with two Nicaraguan wrappers of different shades striped over the same all-Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is made at AJ Fernandez's factory in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Dual wrapper cigar, so no single wrapper category applies. The Twisted Love Story is a small perfecto; the Twisted Toro is a straight-sided parejo.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Habano and Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade in a barber pole
cigars.about: A barber pole extension of the Reserva Real, with alternating stripes of Ecuadorian Habano and Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. It is made in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Dual wrapper cigar, so no single wrapper category applies. The Twisted Love Story is a short perfecto often compared to Arturo Fuente's Hemingway Between the Lines.

cigars.about: Altadis U.S.A.'s cigar for the 150th anniversary of the Romeo y Julieta brand, dated from 1875. It pairs an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper aged by AJ Fernandez with a Turrent family San Andres binder and filler from Peru, Honduras and the Dominican Republic, sold in 16-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's site lists the Balconet as 6 x 52; halfwheel, Cigar Aficionado's launch report and Neptune give 6 x 54. The three sizes are regular production; only the Reconciliation belicoso sold in the 150th Anniversary Humidor is limited. The filler also includes an undisclosed aged leaf.

cigars.about: A Honduran-made Romeo y Julieta blended by Rafael Nodal and Altadis U.S.A.'s Grupo de Maestros as a tribute to the people who grow and roll cigars. It has an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over a U.S. binder and Dominican and Honduran filler.
cigars.researchNote: Devocion is Spanish for devotion. The published blend and factory match the JR Cigar exclusive Romeo y Julieta Pasion.

cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro made for Altadis U.S.A. by Plasencia in Esteli, released as a follow-up to the Romeo y Julieta Eternal. It comes in one size, the Amulet, in boxes of 11 with a green band and an evil eye symbol.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 100,000 cigars in one size, the 6 x 55 Amulet. Neptune lists it as Medium and Famous as Full; halfwheel's review found medium strength building to medium-full. Cigar Aficionado and Famous say the wrapper is aged leaf from Jalapa.

cigars.about: A limited Romeo y Julieta made in partnership with Churchill Downs for the 151st running of the Kentucky Derby in 2025. It is an all-Nicaraguan blend rolled in the Dominican Republic, sold in 20-count boxes and single coffins.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,350 boxes of 20, plus single coffins sold only at Churchill Downs during Derby Week. All-Nicaraguan tobacco but rolled in the Dominican Republic. Also called the 2025 Limited Edition Run For The Roses; a different Derby cigar came out in 2024.

cigars.about: The 2026 Romeo y Julieta made with Churchill Downs for the 152nd Kentucky Derby. It is an all-Nicaraguan blend rolled at the Plasencia family's Tabacos de Oriente factory in Danli, Honduras, sold in 10-count boxes and single coffins.
cigars.researchNote: Third Romeo y Julieta release for the Kentucky Derby. All-Nicaraguan tobacco but rolled in Honduras. Coffin singles were sold at Churchill Downs during Derby Week.

cigars.about: A Romeo y Julieta line made for JR Cigar at the Flor de Copan factory in Honduras. It uses an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, an American binder and Dominican and Honduran filler in a medium-bodied blend.
cigars.researchNote: JR Cigar exclusive, launched May 1, 2020. Properly spelled Pasión. Current availability at JR was not confirmed.

cigars.about: A limited Romeo y Julieta made by Altadis U.S.A. in 2021 to mark the 50th anniversary of retailer JR Cigar. It is a single 5 x 54 size with a Mexican criollo wrapper, sold only through JR.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 500 boxes of 12 and sold only by JR Cigar. No strength rating was found.

cigars.about: A full-bodied Nicaraguan puro sold only by Famous Smoke Shop, named for the cigar-making city of Esteli. It uses sun-grown Nicaraguan tobacco under a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke Shop exclusive. Famous calls it a Nicaraguan puro but does not name the factory or itemize binder and filler.

cigars.about: A value-priced, medium-bodied Romeo y Julieta sold by Famous Smoke Shop as a companion to its Capulet and Montague lines. It has a dark Mexican San Andres wrapper over Dominican, Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler and is made in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Famous's spec table labels the wrapper leaf as Habano with Mexican origin, while its description calls it San Andres. The binder and factory are not published.

cigars.about: A Famous Smoke Shop exclusive that rounds out the retailer's House of collection alongside Capulet and Montague. It was blended by Altadis U.S.A.'s Grupo de Maestros with Rafael Nodal and is rolled at Flor de Copan in Honduras with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only at Famous. Famous rates it Medium but describes it as dark and full-bodied.

cigars.about: A fuller version of the House of Romeo sold only by Famous Smoke Shop, with a dark Mexican San Andres wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. The blend was developed with Altadis U.S.A.'s Grupo de Maestros.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke Shop exclusive. Nicaragua refers to the binder and filler: Famous lists the country of origin as Honduras and does not name the factory.

cigars.about: A richer take on Famous Smoke Shop's House of Capulet that swaps the original Connecticut Shade wrapper for a Nicaraguan Habano 2000 leaf over all-Nicaraguan tobaccos. It is rolled at La Flor de Copan in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Famous lists it as Capulet Nicaragua. Despite the name it is rolled in Honduras. The binder is not itemized beyond an all-Nicaraguan core.

cigars.about: A cabinet-boxed offshoot of the Reserva Real carried by Famous Smoke Shop, with an Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper, Nicaraguan binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. The cigars come bundled in wooden cabinet boxes without individual sleeves.
cigars.researchNote: Found only at Famous, which rates it Medium but describes it as leaning medium to full. Some sizes differ from the regular Reserva Real. The factory is not stated.

cigars.about: The core VegaFina blend, a Connecticut Shade cigar made by Altadis at Tabacalera de García. The brand dates to 1998 and is far better known in Europe than in the U.S.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as VegaFina Classic or just VegaFina. Altadis calls it medium body; Neptune lists it as mild and Holt's as mild to medium.

cigars.about: A limited series under the VegaFina 1998 name that honors historical wonders of the world. The first release, Nabateos, is a Churchill launched in the U.S. in 2025 and named for the Nabataeans, whose capital was Petra.
cigars.researchNote: The blend shown is for Nabateos, the first release. Neptune describes the series as annual with a new blend each year, so later releases may differ.

cigars.about: The first VegaFina made only for the U.S. market, part of the brand's country exclusive series. The tobaccos were aged two years and the run was 1,776 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper seed type is not published, only that it is Ecuadorian.

cigars.about: VegaFina's Chinese New Year release for 2022 and the first of the zodiac series sold in the U.S. It came in red and gold boxes of 16.
cigars.researchNote: Two versions were made with the same blend: a 6 1/8 x 52 for the U.S. (500 boxes) and a 6 5/8 x 52 for other markets.

cigars.about: VegaFina's Chinese New Year release for 2024, a long toro in red and gold packaging. Of 6,888 boxes made, 500 went to the U.S.
cigars.researchNote: Launched abroad in December 2023 and reached the U.S. in February 2024. Halfwheel only says Ecuadorian wrapper; the Habano detail comes from Neptune, which also lists only Dominican filler.

cigars.about: VegaFina's Chinese New Year release for 2023, a torpedo sold in red boxes of 16. The U.S. received 1,500 boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis says the blend is built to start mild and grow to full-bodied by the end, so no single strength is given. It reached U.S. stores in December 2022.

cigars.about: VegaFina's Chinese New Year release for 2021, the fourth in its zodiac series. It was limited to 4,300 boxes of 16 and was not sold in the U.S.
cigars.researchNote: VegaFina calls it full-bodied, but halfwheel's review found it medium at most. Not sold in the U.S.

cigars.about: VegaFina's Chinese New Year release for 2025, with a long pigtail cap meant to look like a snake's tongue. Production was 5,750 boxes of 16.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper seed type is not published, only that it is Ecuadorian. Strength comes from Neptune, which calls it medium-bodied.

cigars.about: VegaFina's Chinese New Year release for 2026, which also honors the Paso Higüeyano horse breed of the Dominican Republic. It has a long pigtail cap and was limited to 4,300 boxes of 16.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper seed type and strength are not published. It debuted in China before other international markets.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dual wrapper: Dominican with a lighter Ecuadorian leaf on top
cigars.about: A limited belicoso in VegaFina's Series 2 line that pays tribute to winemaking and uses two wrappers. Production was 5,900 boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: Series 2 is the new name for the Fortaleza 2 line. The change was made because buyers took Fortaleza, Spanish for strength, to mean a strong cigar.

cigars.line: Serie 2 San Juan de la Maguana
cigars.about: An all-Dominican double perfecto in VegaFina's Serie 2 line, named for a city in the San Juan Valley. It went on sale in Spain in early 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel does not say whether this is a limited edition or give a production number.

cigars.about: A limited Fortaleza 2 release named for its 20-year-old Mexican wrapper. It was limited to 4,500 boxes of 12 and was not sold in the U.S.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel only says the wrapper is Mexican; Cigar Coop's review calls it Mexican Habano. Strength is from that review, since the maker gives none. Not sold in the U.S.

cigars.about: A limited Fortaleza 2 release built around two binders, each aged four years. It was the first box-pressed VegaFina, with 3,960 boxes of 12 made.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper seed type is not published, only that it is Ecuadorian. Not sold in the U.S.

cigars.about: VegaFina's first Reserva, a Nicaraguan puro with a pigtail cap made from tobaccos aged at least three years. It was limited to 8,000 boxes of 12.
cigars.researchNote: It is a different blend from the regular VegaFina Nicaragua. All Nicaraguan tobacco but rolled in the Dominican Republic. Not sold in the U.S.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro marking ten years of the VegaFina Nicaragua line, which launched in 2014. It was limited to 6,700 boxes of 20 that double as humidors.
cigars.researchNote: Described as medium to medium-full. All Nicaraguan tobacco but rolled in the Dominican Republic. Not sold in the U.S.

cigars.about: A limited VegaFina whose cigars rested for ten years after they were rolled. It was limited to 3,930 boxes of 10 and debuted in Spain.
cigars.researchNote: The ten years refers to aging of the finished cigars, not just the leaf. The maker gives no strength; CigarsLover found it light, building to medium. Some outlets list it under the Fortaleza 2 line, and it is not sold in the U.S.

cigars.about: A limited edition in the VegaFina Classic family that honors the brand's home country, the Dominican Republic. It is made entirely of Dominican tobacco aged three years and was sold in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: All Dominican tobacco, with the leaf types not published. Strength is from Cigar Coop's review (mild, building to mild-medium), since the maker gives none. Not sold in the U.S.

cigars.about: A VegaFina made only for Austria, named for the Roman camp that became Vienna. It is a pigtail toro limited to 1,230 numbered boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only in Austria. The wrapper seed type is not published, only that it is Ecuadorian. Strength is from Cigar Coop's review, since the maker gives none.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro Reinier Lorenzo released in 2021 to mark ten years of HVC. It was the first HVC blend to use Corojo 2012 tobacco in the filler.
cigars.researchNote: The original 6 1/2 x 50 was limited to 2,000 boxes of 10. The 5 x 54 added in 2023 is made at HVC's own factory in Esteli. Neptune and Atlantic list it as full, but halfwheel's reviewer found the strength closer to medium.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Criollo 98 and Corojo 99 from Esteli and Jalapa)
cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos HVC S.A. de Reinier Lorenzo
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro of AGANORSA tobacco made to mark the 500th anniversary of the founding of Havana, the city HVC is named for. It began as a limited edition and is now a regular line.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2019 as a limited edition made at TABSA and became regular production in 2021. Retailers list it as full, though halfwheel's reviewer found the Tesoros closer to medium. A 7 1/2 x 38 Lancero Only Legends was a 5,000-cigar limited release in 2026.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Cerro, one of HVC's original lines, named for a Havana neighborhood. It keeps the Nicaraguan binder and filler and swaps the wrapper for Mexican San Andrés.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists medium and Atlantic medium-full. It launched at TABSA; HVC opened its own Esteli factory in 2022 and Atlantic now names that one. Retailers still stock all four sizes, but whether it is still being made is not confirmed.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos HVC S.A. de Reinier Lorenzo
cigars.about: A San Andrés wrapped HVC line over Nicaraguan tobaccos, introduced in 2015. It was relaunched in 2025 as a soft box-pressed cigar with new packaging.
cigars.researchNote: The original round version, made at TABSA, was dropped in early 2025 and replaced by the soft box-pressed version listed here; halfwheel says the blend is essentially the same. A 6 1/2 x 48 Especiales is a limited size sold in boxes of 10. Neptune lists medium, Atlantic medium-full.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos HVC S.A. de Reinier Lorenzo
cigars.about: The third Selección No. 1 blend, after the Maduro and Natural, with an Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos. It is made at HVC's own factory in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists it as medium; Atlantic lists mild-medium, which matches halfwheel's review (full flavor, mild to mild-medium strength).

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos HVC S.A. de Reinier Lorenzo
cigars.about: The first line made at HVC's own factory in Esteli, which opened in 2022. Reinier Lorenzo built it as a tribute to the old Cuban style and it is known for being strong.
cigars.researchNote: Originally released as just Selección No. 1; Maduro was added to the name once the Natural and Connecticut followed. Lorenzo pitched it as an after-dinner cigar and halfwheel found it very full in strength, but Neptune lists medium and Atlantic medium-full.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos HVC S.A. de Reinier Lorenzo
cigars.about: The lighter version of HVC's Hot Cake, trading the San Andrés wrapper for Ecuadorian Connecticut over Nicaraguan tobaccos. It was the first Hot Cake with a Connecticut shade wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: HVC describes it as mild to medium and Atlantic agrees; Neptune lists medium. The Half Corona was added in 2024 with an adjusted blend.

cigars.line: Hot Cake Fresh Out of the Oven Broadleaf
cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos HVC S.A. de Reinier Lorenzo
cigars.about: The dark Connecticut broadleaf version of HVC's Hot Cake, the fourth blend in the Pan Caliente family. It uses Nicaraguan binder and filler and is made at HVC's own factory.
cigars.researchNote: Every size so far has shipped in a capped run of 240 to 500 boxes of 25, though retailers sell it alongside the regular Hot Cake lines. Neptune lists medium and names Aganorsa as the maker; Atlantic lists medium-full and halfwheel reports HVC's own factory.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos HVC S.A. de Reinier Lorenzo
cigars.about: A regular production HVC line introduced in 2026 that revives the name of a defunct 19th-century Cuban brand. It is a soft box-pressed cigar with an Ecuadorian Habano 2000 wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: Properly spelled La Decoración. HVC describes it as medium-bodied and Neptune lists medium; Atlantic lists medium-full. All four sizes are box-pressed.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos HVC S.A. de Reinier Lorenzo
cigars.about: A 2025 limited edition marking ten years of La Rosa 520, the line named for Reinier Lorenzo's childhood address in Havana. It is a new blend, not a remake of the 2015 original.
cigars.researchNote: Each size is limited to 1,000 boxes of 10; the Magnificos is a figurado. Atlantic lists medium-full and calls the wrapper Nicaraguan Habano, while halfwheel reports Ecuadorian Habano 92 and its reviewer found the strength about medium.

cigars.about: A limited maduro take on HVC's La Rosa 520, replacing the all-Nicaraguan blend's Corojo 99 wrapper with Mexican San Andrés. It has only been released in small occasional runs.
cigars.researchNote: First sold in December 2018 as a 300-box Small Batch Cigar exclusive (4 1/2 x 52). Exquisitos and Mágicos followed in 2019, and Exquisitos returned in 2021 at 500 boxes of 10. Neptune lists medium; halfwheel's reviewer put it at medium-plus to medium-full.

cigars.about: A limited HVC belicoso rolled at El Titan de Bronze in Miami. It was the first HVC cigar made in the United States and the first to use Dominican and medio tiempo tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 500 boxes of 10 and a completely different blend from the Nicaraguan La Rosa 520. Neptune lists medium; halfwheel's reviewer found medium to medium-plus. Neptune shows a 5 1/2 x 54 torpedo, while halfwheel reports a single 6 x 52 belicoso.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos HVC S.A. de Reinier Lorenzo
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro of AGANORSA tobacco with a Criollo 98 wrapper, introduced in 2016. The name is Cuban slang for something that sells like hot cakes, and the line led to HVC's Hot Cake cigars.
cigars.researchNote: First made at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras. halfwheel reports it moved to TABSA in Nicaragua in 2019 and that HVC now makes its cigars at its own Esteli factory, but Neptune and Atlantic still list it as made in Honduras. The Hot Cake lines share the name but are different blends.

cigars.about: A budget mixed-filler bundle cigar from HVC, sold in bundles of 25 under the Pan Caliente name. It pairs Nicaraguan short and long filler with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Atlantic sells the same cigar as Pan Caliente Connecticut Bundles and also has a Maduro version. Neptune says it is made in Honduras at Raíces Cubanas; Atlantic says HVC's factory in Nicaragua. Neptune lists mild and a Habano binder, Atlantic mild-medium.

cigars.line: Pan Caliente de HVC 10th Anniversary Limited Edition 2026
cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos HVC S.A. de Reinier Lorenzo
cigars.about: A 2026 limited edition marking ten years of HVC's Pan Caliente. It is an all-new blend and the first HVC cigar to use Peruvian tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 500 boxes of 25 in a single 6 7/8 x 54 size. The blend is not the same as the regular Criollo 98 wrapped Pan Caliente.

cigars.about: A box-pressed HVC line with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos, introduced in 2016. It is named for the Havana street where the gangster Alberto Yarini was killed in 1910.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists medium and Atlantic medium-full; halfwheel found it medium-full when new and medium on a 2022 revisit. Neptune marks the Hermoso as discontinued. Atlantic names HVC's own factory rather than TABSA.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Raíces Cubanas S. de R.L.
cigars.about: A limited HVC figurado made entirely of AGANORSA Nicaraguan tobacco from the 2010 harvest, aged five years. It followed the Vieja Cosecha No. 1, which used 2009 tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: First run was 200 boxes of 20, with 250 more boxes in 2016; Atlantic says it now comes back about once a year in small quantities. Neptune lists medium, Atlantic medium-full. Rolled in Honduras from Nicaraguan tobacco.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped version of Oliva's value-priced Flor de Oliva bundle line, made with Nicaraguan long filler. It is the milder blend in the Flor de Oliva family.
cigars.researchNote: Famous and Neptune list it as mild, Holt's lists it as medium. Oliva only says it is lighter on the palate. Sold in bundles of 20.

cigars.about: The Corojo-wrapped version of Oliva's value-priced Flor de Oliva bundle line, built on Nicaraguan long filler. Oliva describes it as medium bodied with toasty cedar notes.
cigars.researchNote: Oliva calls it medium bodied and lists the wrapper as Ecuador. Famous lists the Corojo wrapper as Nicaraguan. Famous and Holt's rate it full, Neptune medium. Sold in bundles of 20.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Oliva's value-priced Flor de Oliva bundle line, with a dark wrapper over Nicaraguan long filler. It is a sweet, medium-bodied everyday smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the wrapper: Oliva's own page lists Ecuador, while Famous and Holt's list Connecticut Broadleaf maduro. Sold in bundles of 20.

cigars.about: Oliva's yearly limited edition of the Serie V Melanio blend, released in a different size each year in boxes of 10. Most editions are round, unlike the box-pressed regular Melanio.
cigars.researchNote: Same blend as the regular Serie V Melanio in a new size each year. The series began in 2017 as Edición Limitada and was renamed Edición Año in 2022. The 2022 edition was not sold in the U.S.; 2023 was the first U.S. release.

cigars.line: Serie V Melanio Gran Reserva Limitada World Cup 2026 Edition
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Varies: Ecuadorian (Melanio) and Mexican maduro (Melanio Maduro)
cigars.about: A soccer-ball-shaped box of 24 cigars that Oliva released for the 2026 World Cup. It holds 12 Serie V Melanio Double Toros and 12 Serie V Melanio Maduro Double Toros with a special second band.
cigars.researchNote: This is special packaging, not a new blend: the cigars are the regular production box-pressed 6 x 60 Melanio and Melanio Maduro Double Toro. MSRP is $680 per box and production is 5,000 boxes, 4,250 of them for the U.S.

cigars.about: A limited perfecto in the regular Serie V blend with a rounded cap and a tapered foot, sold in boxes of 12 arranged like a fan. It marks 135 years since Melanio Oliva first grew tobacco in Cuba's Pinar del Río.
cigars.researchNote: Some halfwheel posts give the size as 6 1/2 x 54, but its review spec table and Neptune list 5 1/2 x 54. Neptune calls the wrapper Ecuadorian Sumatra seed. First run was 15,000 boxes of 12; Oliva made it an annual limited release in 2022.

cigars.line: Serie V Roaring Twenties Super Limited Edition
cigars.about: A $300 double perfecto in the Serie V blend, the most expensive cigar Oliva has released, sold in boxes of 10 with a gold Les Fines Lames cigar knife. Oliva says proceeds go to its Helping Hands Foundation in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Announced in mid 2023, shipped November 2024. Limited to 300 boxes of 10, about 200 for the U.S., at $3,000 per box. Sources only agree the wrapper is Ecuadorian: one halfwheel listing says Sumatra, but the regular Serie V blend it uses is usually listed as Habano sun grown.

cigars.line: Limited Edition Helping Hands Foundation Corona
cigars.about: A charity cigar based on the Serie V Melanio blend with a lighter Sumatra wrapper, sold in six-count boxes. Proceeds go to the Oliva Helping Hands Foundation, which supports schooling for children in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: A special version of the Serie V Melanio, not a separate line. Launched December 2022 at Casa de Montecristo in Boca Raton at $75 for a box of six. Oliva did not publish a production number.

cigars.about: A maduro take on Oliva's Master Blends 3 made for Atlantic Cigar Co. It swaps the original's Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper for an Ecuadorian Habano maduro leaf over the same Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Exclusive to Atlantic Cigar Co. and sold in bundles of 20. The first batch was 1,500 bundles of each size and it was planned as a yearly release. Atlantic lists it as full strength and spells it Master Blend 3 Maduro.

cigars.about: A soft box-pressed Nicaraguan puro with a dark maduro wrapper, made by Oliva in Estelí from aged tobaccos. It is sold only through Holt's.
cigars.researchNote: A Holt's exclusive that does not appear on Oliva's own site. Holt's rates it medium-full.

cigars.about: The mild, Connecticut-wrapped member of the Baptiste family, a value-priced Nicaraguan brand sold only by Famous Smoke Shop. It pairs an Ecuadorian shade wrapper with Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: Famous calls Baptiste Maduro an Oliva exclusive, but the Connecticut page names no maker or factory, so the Oliva link is not confirmed for this blend. The binder is not published. It is not on Oliva's own site.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro with a Habano wrapper, made with Oliva for Famous Smoke Shop's Inferno brand. Famous lists it as full strength with pepper, earth and coffee notes.
cigars.researchNote: Inferno is a Famous Smoke Shop house brand made with Oliva, not on Oliva's own site. Famous lists strength as full, though its description says medium to full. Described as 100% Nicaraguan tobacco; the binder is not listed separately.

cigars.about: The Cameroon-wrapped blend in Famous Smoke Shop's Inferno family, made by Oliva with Nicaraguan binder and filler. Famous lists it as medium strength.
cigars.researchNote: A Famous Smoke Shop exclusive made by Oliva, not on Oliva's own site. Famous lists the wrapper origin only as African.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro with a sun grown wrapper in Famous Smoke Shop's Inferno family, which is made by Oliva. It comes in boxes of 20 and leans on leather, earth and pepper.
cigars.researchNote: A Famous Smoke Shop brand made by Oliva, not on Oliva's own site. Famous's spec sheet says full strength, but its Inferno overview page calls Singe medium bodied.

cigars.about: The second blend in Famous Smoke Shop's Inferno series, made with Oliva in small batches. It puts an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan Habano ligero and Jalapa filler.
cigars.researchNote: A Famous Smoke Shop exclusive made with Oliva. Famous says it is made in limited quantities and released a few times a year, so it is recurring but often out of stock. It launched in Churchill, Robusto and Torpedo; other sizes came later. Binder is not published.

cigars.about: The maduro follow-up to Inferno Flashpoint, sold by Famous Smoke Shop and made by Oliva. It wraps a Nicaraguan core in Mexican San Andrés leaf and comes in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: A Famous Smoke Shop brand made by Oliva, not on Oliva's own site. Famous lists strength as full, though its description says medium to full. Binder is not published. Both sizes were out of stock when checked.

cigars.about: A full-bodied Nicaraguan puro with a dark broadleaf wrapper, made at the Oliva factory only for Famous Smoke Shop's Inferno brand. It is sold in boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: A Famous Smoke Shop exclusive made by Oliva, not on Oliva's own site. Famous calls it a Nicaraguan puro; the binder is not listed separately. All sizes were out of stock when checked.

cigars.about: The first extension of Illusione's Epernay line, putting a Mexican San Andrés wrapper on a Criollo and Corojo blend. It is rolled at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras in four of the regular Epernay sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Illusione's spec table lists the wrapper as Nicaragua, but its own description and halfwheel both say Mexican San Andrés. Halfwheel lists the binder and filler as undisclosed; Nicaragua here is from Illusione's page. Le Taureau is the pressed size.

cigars.about: A single 6 x 50 toro released in 2019 to mark ten years of Illusione's Epernay line. It is made at the same Honduran factory as Epernay but with a slightly different blend, sold in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Illusione did not disclose the blend. Halfwheel's articles call it a Nicaraguan puro, but its review spec box and Blind Man's Puff list Dominican and Nicaraguan filler, so filler is left blank. Production was limited but the number was not given.

cigars.about: A regular production Illusione line launched in 2024 and planned as five sizes of one blend, made by AGANORSA in Nicaragua. The company keeps the blend deliberately mysterious.
cigars.researchNote: Blend is mostly secret: Illusione confirms Nicaraguan Criollo 98, Corojo 99 and a high-priming viso of an unnamed varietal. Halfwheel lists the wrapper and binder as undisclosed. Reviews of the RB found it medium; Neptune lists it as full, and halfwheel found the SE medium-full to full.

cigars.factory: Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A. (AGANORSA, formerly TABSA)
cigars.about: The maduro version of Illusione's core line: Nicaraguan binder and filler under a Mexican San Andrés wrapper. It was sold as Illusione Maduro until the core lines were renamed Original Documents.
cigars.researchNote: Formerly sold as Illusione Maduro under the old size names such as ~cg:4~ and ~mj12~. Renamed in the 2022-23 repackaging with the same blend. Illusione calls it medium to full bodied; Famous and Neptune list strength as full.

cigars.about: A core Illusione line that began shipping in 2023 and the brand's first cigar made with AJ Fernandez, at his San Lotano factory. It is a Nicaraguan puro with a sun-grown Habano wrapper and is stronger than most Illusione blends.
cigars.researchNote: Illusione's spec table says the wrapper is from Ecuador, but halfwheel, Famous and Neptune all say Nicaraguan Habano grown by AJ Fernandez. Illusione lists the Lancero at 7 1/2 inches; halfwheel and Neptune say 7 1/4. Retailers list it as full; halfwheel found it just under full.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA, now Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A.)
cigars.about: The green-wrapped version of Illusione's core line, pairing Nicaraguan Criollo 98 and Corojo 99 tobaccos with a candela wrapper. It comes in four sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Formerly sold under the old size names (~hl~, ~88~, ~888~ Candela). Illusione calls it mild to medium bodied, but sources vary: Neptune lists mild, Famous full, and reviews of single sizes found medium or stronger. Neptune still shows Honduras as the origin; Illusione says Nicaragua.

cigars.factory: Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A. (AGANORSA, formerly TABSA)
cigars.about: A regular production take on Illusione's Singulare series, which used to be a yearly limited edition with a new blend each time. Dion Giolito built this all-Nicaraguan blend from what he liked best in past Singulare releases.
cigars.researchNote: Illusione gives no strength. Cigar Dojo and Developing Palates found it medium-light to medium, while Neptune lists it as full. The Corojo Cafe Rosado wrapper detail comes from Cigar Dojo and Neptune; Illusione and halfwheel only say Nicaraguan.

cigars.factory: Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A. (AGANORSA, formerly TABSA)
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andrés Maduro (also offered in Ecuadorian Connecticut)
cigars.about: A value-priced 6 1/2 x 56 cigar from Illusione, the big brother to its Rothchildes. It launched in 2014 with a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper and gained an Ecuadorian Connecticut version in 2016.
cigars.researchNote: One size in two wrappers: San Andrés maduro and Ecuadorian Connecticut (CT). Illusione gives no strength: Neptune lists the maduro as full, while Developing Palates found both versions medium.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA, now Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A.)
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andrés Maduro or Nicaraguan Corojo (Natural)
cigars.about: Cigares Prive started in 2014 as the name for Illusione's single-store exclusive cigars and became a nationally sold line in 2016. It comes in three sizes, each offered with a San Andrés maduro or a Nicaraguan natural wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrapper options: Maduro (Mexican San Andrés) and Natural (Nicaraguan, which halfwheel calls Corojo); the wrapper fields here describe the Maduro. The name also covers Illusione's store exclusives, such as MC Slam. Illusione calls it full bodied.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA, now Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A.)
cigars.about: A small petit corona from Illusione sold in gold foil bundles of 25, blended for and named after a friend of founder Dion Giolito. It grew out of two earlier exclusives for Giolito's own Reno shop and went national in 2017.
cigars.researchNote: Illusione calls it full bodied, but Famous lists medium strength and halfwheel found it just under medium. Illusione and Famous give the size as 4 5/8 x 40; halfwheel lists 4 7/8 x 40. Illusione spells it La Grand Classe on its own site.

cigars.factory: Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A. (AGANORSA, formerly TABSA)
cigars.about: An offshoot of OneOff, the old cult brand Dion Giolito of Illusione bought in 2017 and relaunched as a Nicaraguan puro made by AGANORSA. The +53 is named for Cuba's phone country code and uses a slightly different blend from the main OneOff line.
cigars.researchNote: OneOff is its own brand, owned by Illusione. The Super Robusto came out in 2018; the Robusto and the 6 x 56 (Toro to Illusione, Gordo to halfwheel and retailers) were added in 2022. Famous's spec table lists it as mild; halfwheel and Neptune say medium.

cigars.about: A limited release under Illusione's OneOff brand built around tobacco from a seed unique to AGANORSA's Nicaraguan farms, aged in bales for three years. It debuted in 2024 as a robusto limited to 1,000 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as OneOff Black and Tan, the name used since 2025. Illusione lists all-Nicaraguan tobacco but has not named the varietal; halfwheel lists the blend as undisclosed. Halfwheel rated it medium-full; Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.factory: Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A. (AGANORSA, formerly TABSA)
cigars.about: The sister brand to OneOff, which Illusione's Dion Giolito acquired along with it and reblended as a Nicaraguan puro. It launched in 2022 in five sizes using farm-specific Criollo 98 and Corojo 99 tobaccos, priced below OneOff.
cigars.researchNote: Illusione and halfwheel only say the wrapper is Nicaraguan; Corojo 99 comes from Developing Palates. Neptune lists a Honduran wrapper, which does not match the maker. The Allegria name dates to 2004 under OneOff's founder; Illusione's version came out in 2022.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA, now Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A.)
cigars.about: A collaboration between Illusione's Dion Giolito and actor Jeremy Piven, sold as part of The Jeremy Piven Collection. It is a single 5 x 52 Nicaraguan puro robusto that began shipping in November 2021 in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Only one size, the PIV Robusto. Halfwheel and Developing Palates found it medium; Neptune lists it as full and shows Honduras as origin, but halfwheel says it is made in Estelí, Nicaragua. Neptune calls the wrapper Nicaraguan Corojo.

cigars.factory: Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A. (TABSA, now Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A.)
cigars.about: Illusione's first exclusive for Tobacconists' Association of America member shops, a Nicaraguan puro toro built around an AGANORSA viso leaf. It shipped in September 2021, limited to 3,500 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Size sources disagree: halfwheel and Cigar Coop say 6 3/4 x 52, while Developing Palates and Neptune list 6 1/4 x 54. Halfwheel's review climbed from medium to medium-full strength; Neptune lists it as full. Sold only through TAA member retailers.

cigars.about: Illusione's second exclusive for Tobacconists' Association of America member shops, a 6 x 56 Nicaraguan puro made with AGANORSA tobacco. It shipped in September 2022, limited to 1,500 boxes of 10, with a blend unrelated to the 2021 release.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only through TAA member retailers. Strength and body come from a single halfwheel review, which found little nicotine strength and a medium-plus body.

cigars.about: A 6 x 50 toro made only for retailers who placed orders in person at the 2023 PCA trade show. It is rolled at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras, the factory that made Illusione's early cigars, and was limited to 750 bundles of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Blend is undisclosed: Illusione only says it uses tobacco from Nicaragua and Honduras. It shipped in November 2023 and falls under Illusione's Cigares Prive group. Strength and body come from a single halfwheel review.

cigars.about: The maduro version of La Gloria Cubana's original Classic line. It keeps the Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers and Nicaraguan binder and swaps in a dark Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper.
The Connecticut Broadleaf maduro version of Serie R, the large ring gauge line La Gloria Cubana introduced in 1999. Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers sit under a Nicaraguan binder.
cigars.researchNote: Strength varies by source: the maker's scale puts it between medium and full, Famous Smoke lists Full and Holt's lists Medium.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro extension of Serie R, rolled in Esteli with ligero and viso from several farms under an oily Jalapa wrapper. It launched in 2013 as one of the brand's first two Nicaraguan-made lines.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's scale and Famous Smoke say Full; Holt's lists Medium-Full. It launched as a brick-and-mortar exclusive.

cigars.about: The Serie R Esteli blend of Nicaraguan binder and fillers finished in a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper. It shipped in July 2016 alongside a maduro version of Serie R Black.

A Nicaraguan puro in the Serie R family with a dark Jalapa ligero wrapper that was fermented for a year and aged two and a half more. It debuted in 2013 as one of the brand's first Nicaraguan-made cigars.
cigars.researchNote: It launched as a catalog and internet exclusive in No. 58, No. 60 and No. 64. The maker now lists No. 48, No. 52 and No. 60.

cigars.about: Serie R Black's Nicaraguan binder and fillers under an aged Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper. It was added in July 2016.
cigars.researchNote: It launched in No. 58, No. 60 and No. 64 as a catalog and internet exclusive. The maker now lists No. 54, No. 56 and No. 60.

cigars.about: A large ring gauge line that was the first La Gloria Cubana to use a Mexican San Andrés wrapper, over a Nicaraguan binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers. It began shipping in August 2022.
cigars.researchNote: The maker places it between medium and full; Famous Smoke lists it as Full. The wrapper is San Andrés but not a maduro leaf; the darker version is Serie S Maduro.

cigars.about: The second Serie S blend, using a longer-matured Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and Nicaraguan and Dominican fillers. It launched July 1, 2023 in the same three sizes as Serie S.

A Miami-made limited edition named for Calle Ocho, rolled at El Titan de Bronze across the street from the brand's original El Credito factory. It came out in 2022 and returned in 2023 with the same blend in a new size.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls the wrapper Ecuadorian Habano Maduro; halfwheel lists Ecuadorian habano. 2022 was 5,000 boxes of 10 and 2023 was 3,500 boxes of 10.

cigars.about: The second limited edition blended with input from La Gloria Cubana's fan community, the La Gloria Cubana Society. It is a single 6 x 50 toro that shipped in November 2023.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's site lists it as the 2023 Society Cigar. Sold in boxes of 10; production numbers were not disclosed.

cigars.about: A limited salomon made as a tribute to the brand's workers, rolled by 20 rollers and bunchers who each have at least 15 years of experience. It uses higher-priming fillers under a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,900 boxes of 10. A secondary band carries the signature of the person who made each cigar.

cigars.about: A regular production line made for the brand by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo Jr., whose family built La Gloria Cubana at El Credito before selling it in 1999. It is rolled at his Casa Carrillo factory and shipped in April 2025.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the binder as Jalapa and Esteli; halfwheel lists Jalapa only.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Estelí ligero and viso), Honduras (Jamastran viso, La Entrada ligero)
cigars.about: A value-priced four-country blend released in April 2026 and pitched as a return to the brand's bolder blends and larger ring gauges. It is made at STG Estelí in Nicaragua.

cigars.binder: Dominican Republic (Corojo de Oro hybrid, grown in Mao)
cigars.filler: Brazil (Mata Fina), Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano), Nicaragua (Ometepe)
cigars.about: A limited edition built around a proprietary hybrid of corojo 97-98 and pelo de oro grown in Mao, Dominican Republic. It had a small preview release in March 2023 and a wider second release in February 2024.
cigars.researchNote: The cigar is named for its binder, not its wrapper: the Corojo de Oro leaf is the binder under an Ecuadorian habano wrapper.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican sun grown Criollo de Oro (grown in Mao)
cigars.about: A 2021 limited edition wrapped in a proprietary hybrid of criollo 98 and pelo de oro grown in Mao, Dominican Republic. It came in two sizes with 3,100 boxes made in total.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is a hybrid seed, a cross of criollo 98 and pelo de oro.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Honduran Olancho San Agustín, aged seven years
cigars.about: A box-pressed 2021 limited edition honoring the rollers of the El Credito room, and the first release under Forged Cigar Co. It uses a seven-year-old Honduran wrapper over a Cameroon binder.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 600 boxes of 20 per size. Neptune describes the wrapper as a maduro leaf; halfwheel does not.

cigars.about: A single-size 2023 release sold only through Tobacconists' Association of America member shops. The cigars were rolled in 2019 and aged four years before release.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 850 boxes of 10. halfwheel lists Dominican and Honduran fillers; Cigar Aficionado and Neptune say Dominican and Nicaraguan. The maker gave no strength; Neptune lists Medium.

cigars.filler: Brazil (Arapiraca), Nicaragua (Habano Jalapa, Habano Ometepe), Dominican Republic
cigars.about: A core line from the Freemason-themed Hiram & Solomon brand, blended with tobaccos from five countries under an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. Part of the proceeds goes to Shriners Hospitals for Children.
cigars.researchNote: Made at Plasencia in Esteli, Nicaragua until the brand moved all production to PDR Cigars in the Dominican Republic in 2022, so older boxes are Nicaraguan-made. Neptune and Atlantic currently list only the robusto, toro and gran toro.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Habano Esteli, Habano Jalapa ligero), Paraguay
cigars.about: A core Hiram & Solomon line with a Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper, named for a Masonic order. It began as the 7 x 60 Grand Monarch and later added a toro and a lancero.
cigars.researchNote: The maker gives no strength; halfwheel's review put it at medium-plus to medium-full, while Neptune lists it as Mild. Made at Plasencia in Nicaragua until production moved to PDR Cigars in 2022. The 6 x 54 Monarch launched in 2018 as a 500-box run.

cigars.about: A regular production Hiram & Solomon line with a Nicaraguan Corojo wrapper and Paraguayan tobacco in the filler. The name refers to the Masonic term for the Creator.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium to full and Atlantic lists Medium-Full, while Neptune lists Medium. Launched from Plasencia in Nicaragua; production moved to PDR Cigars in the Dominican Republic in 2022.

cigars.about: A 6 x 52 toro from Hiram & Solomon made at PDR Cigars with an undisclosed blend. It was first sold only in the brand's four-cigar Unity sampler and got its own 20-count boxes in 2023.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is undisclosed. It was part of the Unity Pack sampler before standalone boxes arrived in July 2023; the original release year is not published. Neptune now marks the standalone toro as discontinued, and the maker's site shows only the Unity Pack.
