cigars.filler: HVA seco, HVA ligero, broadleaf (origins undisclosed)
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Hybrid Premium Connecticut (habano and Connecticut-seed hybrid, origin undisclosed)
cigars.about: The limited edition marking Hiram & Solomon's 10th anniversary, a 6 x 52 toro with a hybrid habano and Connecticut-seed wrapper. It was shown in 2025 but did not ship until April 2026.
cigars.researchNote: The maker has not disclosed the factory or where the wrapper and filler were grown; Neptune lists it as made by PDR in the Dominican Republic. The wrapper is a habano and Connecticut-seed hybrid, not a classic Connecticut Shade. 1,025 boxes of 10, including 25 collector's boxes with a knife.

cigars.about: A limited 6 x 52 toro in Hiram & Solomon's Grand Lodge series, made at PDR Cigars for the Grand Secretary of Masons in Arkansas. It uses an Indonesian Sumatra wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,000 boxes of 10.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (corojo seco and ligero, criollo 98 ligero), USA (Pennsylvania Broadleaf)
cigars.about: A limited 6 x 52 toro made for a Grand Master of Masons in New Jersey, with a dark Pennsylvania Broadleaf wrapper. The name is Latin for 'we care', and it was the first Hiram & Solomon cigar made at PDR Cigars.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium to full body; halfwheel found the strength a solid medium. Halfwheel reported 450 boxes of 20 at launch and 500 in its later review.

cigars.filler: USA (Pennsylvania Broadleaf), Dominican Republic (FDR2 corojo seco and ligero)
cigars.about: A 6 x 52 toro made at PDR Cigars for the Grand Master of Masons in North Carolina, named for his hope of a Masonic revival after the pandemic. It pairs an Ecuadorian Habano Claro wrapper with Dominican and Pennsylvania Broadleaf filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker gives no strength. Neptune lists Medium; Atlantic's spec table says Full but its description says moderate strength. No production number has been published.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Barber pole of Ecuadorian Connecticut and Mexican San Andrés Maduro
cigars.about: A limited 6 x 52 barber pole toro made at PDR Cigars for a Grand Master of Masons in New Jersey. Its two wrappers, a light Ecuadorian Connecticut and a dark San Andrés, are meant to stand for duality and connection.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrappers, so no single wrapper category applies. Halfwheel's review found it medium-full building to full, while Neptune lists it as Medium. Limited to 1,000 boxes of 10.

cigars.filler: USA (Broadleaf), Dominican Republic (ligero, seco, seco HVA)
cigars.about: A limited 6 x 52 toro made at PDR Cigars for a Past Grand Master of Masons in Pennsylvania, built around the theme 'Ignite the Light Within'. It wears a light Ecuadorian claro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is from Neptune only; the maker does not give one. Limited to 1,000 boxes of 10.

cigars.about: A limited 6 x 52 toro made at PDR Cigars for a Grand Master of Masons in New Jersey. It uses an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Ecuadorian binder and Dominican filler.
cigars.researchNote: Announced in December 2023 as 1,000 boxes of 10. Neptune now lists it as discontinued.

cigars.about: A limited 6 x 52 toro in Hiram & Solomon's Grand Lodge series, made at PDR Cigars in tribute to a Grand Master of Masons in New Jersey. It uses an Ecuadorian Criollo wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,000 boxes of 10. Strength is from Neptune only, which now lists the cigar as discontinued.

cigars.about: A limited 6 x 52 toro honoring the 91st Grand Master of Masons in Massachusetts. It is made in the Dominican Republic with an Ecuadorian Habano Claro wrapper over Dominican binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel and the maker's release call it Patriot Cigar. The factory was not disclosed, though Neptune lists PDR. The maker calls it medium to full bodied, Neptune lists Medium; limited to 1,000 boxes of 10.

cigars.about: A 6 x 52 toro made at PDR Cigars and named for the 32nd degree of the Scottish Rite. It was created for the Scottish Rite Northern Masonic Jurisdiction, with sales supporting its charities.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel calls it Sublime Prince 32. The 2022 launch gave a Habano Rosado wrapper and Dominican binder, while the maker's page now says Habano Claro. The page is off the maker's menu and Neptune marks boxes as discontinued.

cigars.about: A 6 x 52 toro made at PDR Cigars for the Grand Master of Masons in Georgia. The name comes from a Hebrew word meaning to bind or join together.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it a medium body cigar, while Neptune lists it as Full. Its page is off the maker's site menu but still up, and Neptune still sells it. No source says whether it is limited or discontinued.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (corojo ligero and seco, criollo 98 ligero), Panama (broadleaf)
cigars.about: A limited 6 x 52 toro made at PDR Cigars as a collaboration with Operation: Cigars for Warriors. All profits went to the charity, which sends cigars to deployed troops.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 500 boxes of 20 and sold only through Cigars for Warriors donation center retailers. No strength rating or tasting notes were published.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto), Honduras (Broadleaf, Jamastran Valley), Nicaragua (Habano, Jalapa), USA (Pennsylvania)
cigars.about: A regular production line from Cavalier Genève, launched in 2022 as a tribute to the people who helped build the brand. It is rolled at the company's own factory in Danli, Honduras, and does not carry the gold diamond found on most Cavalier cigars.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel rated the Petit Robusto medium-plus in strength and medium-full in body. Cigar Coop and Developing Palates found the Toro lighter, around medium or just under.

cigars.filler: Honduras (Habano, Jamastran Valley), Nicaragua (Habano, Jalapa), Paraguay
cigars.about: The second line in Cavalier Genève's Inner Circle family, released in 2023 as a tribute to founder Sébastien Decoppet's late father, Pascal. The winery-style packaging nods to the wine and cigars the two enjoyed together.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Domaine Rouge by Cavalier Genève and part of the Inner Circle family, so some sites call it Inner Circle Domaine Rouge. Strength comes from two review panels, not the maker.

cigars.about: The Connecticut version of Tres Delincuentes, a lower-priced Cavalier Genève brand launched in 2023 in three wrapper options. Each blend is tied to one of the company's three principals, and this one carries sales director Brian Motola's portrait on the box lid.
cigars.researchNote: No published strength rating was found. The name comes from a 1996 Delinquent Habits song.

cigars.about: The Habano version of Tres Delincuentes, a lower-priced Cavalier Genève brand launched in 2023 in three wrapper options. Each blend is tied to one of the company's three principals, and this one carries Eylin Decoppet's portrait on the box lid.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the binder: halfwheel and Cigar Aficionado say Ecuadorian Habano for all three blends, while Cigar Coop and Developing Palates list a Honduran Connecticut-seed binder for the Habano. Strength is from the Developing Palates review panel.

cigars.about: The Maduro version of Tres Delincuentes, a lower-priced Cavalier Genève brand launched in 2023 in three wrapper options. Each blend is tied to one of the company's three principals, and this one carries founder Sébastien Decoppet's portrait on the box lid.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the binder: halfwheel and Cigar Aficionado say Ecuadorian Habano for all three blends, while Cigar Coop lists a Honduran Connecticut-seed binder for the Maduro. No published strength rating was found.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan Jalapa Viso, two wrappers in a barber pole
cigars.about: A barber pole cigar from Cavalier Genève that began in 2019 as a store exclusive for Underground Cigar Shop in Fort Worth. It came back in 2021 with a new blend as a 6 x 54 sold nationwide.
cigars.researchNote: The blend listed is the 6 x 54 that went nationwide in 2021; a separate Limited Release Prospektor 2025 (4 3/4 x 58, 500 boxes of 15) uses Jalapa and Jamastran wrappers. halfwheel called it regular production in 2021 but a limited release in 2025. Strength is one retailer's rating (Neptune).

cigars.about: The first of four blends in Cavalier Genève's Project Broadleaf series, each built around a long-fermented Connecticut broadleaf wrapper. It debuted in April 2025 and returned in 2026 with the same blend and size.
cigars.researchNote: One blend in the Project Broadleaf series. Limited to 100 boxes of 50 in 2025 and 200 boxes of 50 in 2026. Neptune lists the series as full strength, while the Developing Palates panel found it medium to medium-full.

cigars.about: The second blend in Cavalier Genève's Project Broadleaf series, shipped in June 2025 in 10-count bundles. It pairs a Connecticut broadleaf wrapper with a Jalapa binder.
cigars.researchNote: One blend in the Project Broadleaf series, limited to 500 bundles of 10. It is the only Project Broadleaf blend Cavalier chose not to bring back in 2026. Strength and body come from the Developing Palates panel, which put it between medium and medium-full.

cigars.about: The third blend in Cavalier Genève's Project Broadleaf series and the only one sold in two sizes, including a 9-inch A. It shipped in October 2025 in 10-count boxes with a broadleaf wrapper aged five years.
cigars.researchNote: One blend in the Project Broadleaf series, returning for 2026. Neptune lists the series as full strength, while the Developing Palates panel found the Robusto Extra about medium. The filler includes tobacco from India.

cigars.about: The fourth and final 2025 blend in Cavalier Genève's Project Broadleaf series, inspired by founder Sébastien Decoppet's home country of Switzerland. It shipped in November 2025 in 10-count bundles.
cigars.researchNote: One blend in the Project Broadleaf series, limited to 500 bundles of 10 in 2025 and due back in 2026. Neptune lists it as full, but it gives every Project Broadleaf blend that rating and reviews of the other blends came in lower, so strength is left blank. The wrapper is more than five years old.

cigars.filler: Honduras (Copán, Jamastran Valley, Broadleaf), Nicaragua (Estelí, Jalapa), India, Paraguay
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Honduran Habano (Jamastran Valley), in Claro and Oscuro versions
cigars.about: Cavalier Genève's 10th anniversary cigar, built from 10 tobaccos: a wrapper, a binder and eight fillers. It comes in one size with two wrapper shades of the same Honduran habano leaf, packed seven of each in a 14-count box.
cigars.researchNote: Not a numbered limited edition, but Cavalier only takes orders through the end of 2026 and then discontinues it. Claro and Oscuro are not sold separately. halfwheel rated the Claro medium in strength, rising late.

cigars.about: Two hard-to-roll sizes, a lancero and a salomon, sharing a new blend that Cavalier Genève introduced in 2026. They replaced the older Small Batch cigars, which were limited sizes of the Black Series II and White Series.
cigars.researchNote: Before 2026, Small Batch meant lancero and salomones sizes of Black Series II and White Series, now discontinued. The new blend shipped September 30, 2026, and no strength is published. Small Batch is also the umbrella for Project Broadleaf and Project 10th Anniversary.

cigars.about: Cavalier Genève's annual limited release, made every year since 2018 with a new blend that is never repeated. Recent editions run 1,948 boxes of 10, a nod to the melting point of gold in degrees Fahrenheit.
cigars.researchNote: Cavalier no longer discloses the blend, which changes every year, and the size often changes too. Strength, body and flavors here describe the 2026 edition (6 1/2 x 47) only. The 2025 edition was 6 1/4 x 50.

cigars.about: A yearly golf-themed limited release timed to The Masters, started in 2024 as a single-store cigar for The Vault in Meridian, Idaho. Each 11-count box holds 10 of that year's Churchill plus one preview of the next year's blend.
cigars.researchNote: The blend changes every year; the one listed is 2026, and its strength is Neptune's rating. The 2025 edition used a Honduran Jamastran claro wrapper, a Honduran habano binder and Honduran, Indonesian, Nicaraguan and Paraguayan filler. Sold by pre-order only.

cigars.about: A San Andrés-wrapped line that Cavalier Genève sells only in the United States. It replaced the older USA Exclusive in December 2022 with a new blend and new packaging, and carries the brand's gold diamond on the wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Formerly called USA Exclusive. Only the wrapper carried over from the old blend, so retailer pages still describing a Brazilian binder refer to the earlier version. halfwheel rated the Petit Robusto medium to medium-plus in strength.

cigars.about: An event-only cigar from Cavalier Genève, announced in May 2022 and sold in 10-count bundles at stores hosting Cavalier events. As the name says, the company does not disclose the blend.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is secret, and no source names the factory or a strength for this cigar. It is only offered at Cavalier Genève store events and does not carry the gold diamond.

cigars.factory: Nueva Matacapan de Tabacos S.A. de C.V.
cigars.about: A blend of Mexican San Andrés criollo and Nicaraguan tobacco from the Turrent family, named for Alejandro Turrent's birth year. The Torpedo was Cigar Aficionado's No. 14 cigar of 2020.
cigars.researchNote: Maker lists a Nicaraguan binder; halfwheel listed a San Andrés criollo binder at launch. The maker's chart now shows only the Gran Robusto (6 x 52, launched at 5 3/4 x 52) and Robusto; the Torpedo and Gran Toro are launch sizes.

cigars.filler: Mexico (San Andrés Habano Criollo, San Andrés Negro)
cigars.about: The lightest of the four 1880 blends Casa Turrent added in 2020, made by the Turrent family with aged Mexican tobacco they grow themselves. The maker rates it mild to medium.
cigars.researchNote: Maker now lists an all-Mexican blend; halfwheel listed a habano criollo claro wrapper with Mexican and Dominican filler. Launched as a 6 1/2 x 55 toro gordo; the maker's chart now shows three shorter sizes.

cigars.filler: Mexico (San Andrés Habano Criollo, San Andrés Negro)
cigars.about: A Mexican puro in Casa Turrent's 1880 series, named for the colorado shade of its San Andrés Negro wrapper. The Turrent family grows all of the tobacco in it.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's text calls it medium to full, but the strength scale beside it on the same page shows mild to medium. Launched as a 6 1/2 x 55 toro gordo; the maker's chart now shows three shorter sizes.

cigars.filler: Mexico (San Andrés Habano Criollo, San Andrés Negro)
cigars.about: A dark-wrapped Mexican puro in Casa Turrent's 1880 series, built on habano-seed and Negro tobacco from the San Andrés Valley. It is one of the stronger blends in the series.
cigars.researchNote: Maker's text says full-bodied while its strength scale shows medium to full; halfwheel's review found full strength. Halfwheel lists the wrapper as San Andrés habano criollo. Launched as a 6 1/2 x 55 toro gordo.

cigars.about: The maduro blend in Casa Turrent's 1880 series, with a dark San Andrés Negro wrapper over a habano criollo binder. It was one of the four 1880 blends added in 2020.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's page repeats the Colorado description under Maduro, so wrapper and filler here follow halfwheel. The maker's strength scale shows full, while Neptune lists medium. No tasting notes specific to the Maduro are published by the maker.

cigars.filler: Mexico (San Andrés Habano México, Habano Criollo, Habano 2000)
cigars.about: A Mexican puro in Casa Turrent's 1880 series made from three Cuban-seed tobaccos grown in the San Andrés Valley. It joined the series in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Maker's text says medium strength while its strength scale shows medium to full. Halfwheel's launch report listed a habano 2000 binder. Launch sizes ran up to 7 1/2 inches; the maker's chart now shows three shorter sizes.

cigars.filler: Mexico (San Andrés Habano Criollo, San Andrés Negro)
cigars.about: The lightest of the three 1880 blends Casa Turrent added in 2022, a Mexican puro wrapped in Connecticut-seed leaf grown in the San Andrés Valley.
cigars.researchNote: The Connecticut-seed wrapper is grown in Mexico, not the U.S. or Ecuador. Maker lists a habano criollo claro binder; halfwheel's launch report listed San Andrés Negro.

cigars.filler: Mexico (San Andrés Habano Criollo, San Andrés Negro)
cigars.about: The fullest of the three 1880 blends Casa Turrent added in 2022, a Mexican puro with San Andrés Negro leaf as both wrapper and binder.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel's launch report described San Andrés Negro for the filler as well; the maker now lists habano criollo with it.

cigars.about: The original Casa Turrent 1880 blend from 2017, which took the Edición Limitada name in 2020 when the wrapper-named 1880 lines arrived. It uses long-aged Mexican tobacco from the Turrent farms with some Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: Also known as 1880 Sui Generis. Sources list the original 2017 toro anywhere from 6 1/4 x 52 to 6 1/2 x 54; the 2022 version is 6 1/2 x 55. Made in small ongoing batches, not a fixed run; strength and flavors here come from reviews of the original.

cigars.factory: Nueva Matacapan de Tabacos S.A. de C.V.
cigars.about: One of four Casa Turrent Origins blends named for places in the Turrent family's history. It pairs a Connecticut-seed wrapper grown in Mexico with Mexican and Dominican filler.
cigars.researchNote: No maker strength rating; halfwheel's two reviews put strength between medium and medium-full, with full body. Halfwheel lists a San Andrés criollo binder plus Nicaraguan filler. Shown in Europe in 2018, U.S. release August 2019; launched at 5 1/2 x 54, the maker now lists 5 1/4 x 55.

cigars.about: One of four Casa Turrent Origins blends named for places in the Turrent family's history. This one puts Nicaraguan filler under a Mexican criollo wrapper and San Andrés Negro binder.
cigars.researchNote: Rolled in Mexico despite the name. The maker publishes no strength rating; a UK retailer rates its flavour medium to full. Shown in Europe in 2018, U.S. release August 2019; launched at 5 1/2 x 54, the maker now lists 5 1/4 x 55.

cigars.about: One of four Casa Turrent Origins blends named for places in the Turrent family's history. It is a Mexican puro made entirely from Cuban-seed habano tobacco grown in San Andrés.
cigars.researchNote: Contains no Cuban tobacco: the name refers to the Cuban-seed leaf, all grown in Mexico. The maker publishes no strength rating or tasting notes. Shown in Europe in 2018, U.S. release August 2019; launched at 5 1/2 x 54, the maker now lists 5 1/4 x 55.

cigars.factory: Nueva Matacapan de Tabacos S.A. de C.V.
cigars.about: One of four Casa Turrent Origins blends named for places in the Turrent family's history, this one built on the family's own San Andrés Negro tobacco. It placed in Cigar Journal's Top 25 for 2020 and 2021.
cigars.researchNote: The band reads San Andrés and it is often sold as Origins San Andrés. Maker lists all San Andrés Negro, while Cigar Journal adds Nicaraguan filler and scored its strength 8 of 10; the maker gives no strength rating. Launched at 5 1/2 x 54; the maker now lists 5 1/4 x 55.

cigars.about: A limited Mexican puro from Casa Turrent marking Alberto Turrent's 60 harvests as a tobacco grower. It uses aged San Andrés Negro tobacco under a maduro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 3,000 boxes of 15. Announced in September 2021 for a November 2021 release; the actual ship date is unconfirmed. The blend was not disclosed beyond a puro of Mexican San Andrés Negro, with wrapper and binder aged 5 to 7 years and filler 5 to 15.

cigars.about: An everyday cigar from the Turrent family in Mexico, sold by UK retailers under the Casa Turrent name. It is described as a smooth, milder smoke.
cigars.researchNote: The maker shows Macarena as its own brand beside Casa Turrent and Te-Amo and publishes no blend. One UK retailer lists a Sumatra wrapper, Mexican binder and Dominican Criollo 98 filler, light to medium; treat that as unconfirmed.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Connecticut Broadleaf cigar that Luciano Meirelles named for his late mother. The band art is a drawing by his daughter Deborah.
cigars.researchNote: Debuted in 2022 as a limited single size (5 1/4 x 54), then became a regular four-size line in 2023. The maker calls it medium-full; Neptune Cigar lists it as full.

cigars.filler: Brazil (Mata Fina), Nicaragua, Peru, South Africa
cigars.about: A limited round version of Maria Lucia with a different blend, built around a San Andrés wrapper and some South African filler. It was offered to retailers who attended the 2025 PCA trade show.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,000 boxes of 10. Strength is disputed: halfwheel's reviewer found it mild in strength, while Neptune Cigar lists it as full. Halfwheel gives the size as 6 x 52; Neptune lists 6 x 54.

cigars.about: A Luciano Cigars line blended to pair with red wine from the Mas Igneus winery in Priorat, Spain, where Luciano Meirelles is a partner. The filler was chosen by testing tobacco pH to match the wine.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2022 when the company was still called ACE Prime. No tasting notes are published; Meirelles describes it as a dense, meaty blend.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Honduran Habano from Plasencia's San Agustin farm, plus Ecuadorian Sumatra (two wrappers)
cigars.about: A limited edition of the Fiat Lux line made for Luciano Cigars by Plasencia in Danli, Honduras. It uses two wrapper leaves that were both fermented for more than five years.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,500 boxes of 10. It has two wrappers: a Honduran habano and the Ecuadorian Sumatra used on regular Fiat Lux. Tenebrus comes from the Latin for darkness.

cigars.about: A core line from Luciano Meirelles and Constella Group that follows Luciano The Traveler and The Dreamer. It is themed around people who actually do the work rather than talk about it.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Luciano The Maker. The wrapper's country of origin is not disclosed. It is unrelated to the 2023 store-exclusive The Maker that Meirelles made with West Tampa Tobacco's Rick Rodriguez.

cigars.about: A regular production line from Luciano Cigars and Constella Group that honors working tradespeople. It was inspired by Jack Beaver, a machinist and the grandfather of a company account manager.
cigars.researchNote: Made at an undisclosed factory in the Dominican Republic. The maker gives no strength rating: Neptune Cigar lists it as full, while Stogie Press calls it medium to full.

cigars.filler: USA (Connecticut Broadleaf), Ecuador (HVA), Nicaragua (Pueblo Nuevo medio tiempo)
cigars.about: A value-priced Luciano Cigars line made in Esteli with former NBA player Ron Harper as a partner. Its filler uses broadleaf and Ecuadorian leaves normally reserved for wrappers, plus Nicaraguan medio tiempo.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium-full with a candied sweetness; Neptune Cigar lists it as full. Neptune shows the Toro Especial as 6 x 52 where halfwheel has 6 1/4 x 52.

cigars.about: A limited 6 x 54 cigar released to mark the launch of Constella Group, the joint venture between Luciano Cigars and the Azores tobacco company EMT. The name is French for elevated.
cigars.researchNote: The blend and the factory are both undisclosed; the company only says the tobaccos come from several growing regions. Limited to 1,420 boxes of 10. Released as a Constella Group cigar to mark the merger.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Esteli ligero, Jalapa and Pueblo Nuevo viso)
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan cigar Luciano Meirelles blended as a tribute to his friend, US Marine Sgt. Brian Acevedo, and to service members generally. It began as a 2021 trade show exclusive in one 5 x 58 size.
cigars.researchNote: Launched under the ACE Prime name before the company became Luciano Cigars. The company called it medium to full bodied; Neptune Cigar lists strength as medium. The binder is a Connecticut-grown hybrid seed, not broadleaf.

cigars.about: A Constella Group cigar created by Luciano Meirelles with former MLB first baseman Adrian Gonzalez, who is a partner in the company. It launched in a single toro size.
cigars.researchNote: A Constella Group release. The company names a Costa Rican binder, but halfwheel's review lists Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed. Halfwheel's review lists the country as undisclosed, but its news coverage says the cigar comes from the same Dominican factory as The Machinist.

cigars.about: A line co-blended by Luciano Meirelles and Linxu "Panda" Yan, a former intern at the Luciano factory in Esteli. It is made and distributed by Luciano Cigars.
cigars.researchNote: No maker strength rating; strength and body here come from halfwheel's review of the Sublime. The launch release names the Brazilian binder as Arapiraca, while halfwheel's review lists Mata Fina.

cigars.about: The first limited edition in the Y Panda line, a 6 x 52 toro with a Connecticut wrapper in place of the regular corojo. It was sold only to retailers who ordered at the 2024 PCA trade show.
cigars.researchNote: Initial run was 300 boxes of 18, with a possible reorder for the same retailers. The blend differs from regular Y Panda in both the wrapper and one of the two binders.

cigars.about: The third blend in the Tiago Clasico family from Luciano Cigars, with a sun grown habano wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos. The brand is named for co-founder and former NBA player Tiago Splitter.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Pichardo Clasico Natural until the 2023 rebrand to Tiago; the blend did not change. It is a distinct blend, not just a new wrapper on the other Clasico cigars.

cigars.about: The maduro member of the Tiago Clasico family from Luciano Cigars, using a Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It comes in one box-pressed toro size.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2020 as Pichardo Maduro (Pichardo Clasico Maduro) under ACE Prime, then renamed Tiago in 2023 with the same blend. Strength is Neptune Cigar's listing; the maker does not state one.

cigars.about: The original Tiago Clasico from Luciano Cigars, an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos made to taste like a Cuban cigar. It dates to the company's 2019 debut as ACE Prime.
cigars.researchNote: This is the original Clasico blend; retailers add Sumatra to tell it apart from the Maduro and Natural. Sold as Pichardo Clasico until the 2023 rebrand. Strength is Neptune Cigar's listing.

cigars.about: Kristoff's 20th anniversary line, named with the Spanish word for twenty. It pairs a dark Brazilian wrapper with an Indonesian binder and Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania filler.
cigars.researchNote: Kristoff rates it 4 out of 5 for strength; Neptune lists it as full. Kristoff only says the wrapper is Brazilian; halfwheel and Neptune name it Arapiraca. Sizes are Kristoff's; halfwheel lists the Toro at 6 1/2 x 54 and the perfecto at 6 x 60.

cigars.about: An all-Nicaraguan blend that Kristoff founder Glen Case made as a tribute to two late friends, factory manager Rolando Villamil and Chuck Finch. It is meant to be sweeter and creamier than the usual peppery Nicaraguan puro.
cigars.researchNote: All Nicaraguan tobacco but rolled in the Dominican Republic. Kristoff's site rates it 3 out of 5 for strength; Glen Case told halfwheel at launch it was a 2 out of 5.

cigars.about: Kristoff's Nicaraguan puro, with filler from Condega, Esteli and Jalapa and a Corojo binder that adds spice. It launched alongside Tres Compadres as the stronger, spicier of the two.
cigars.researchNote: All Nicaraguan tobacco but rolled in the Dominican Republic. Kristoff rates it 4 out of 5 for strength; its site only says the wrapper is Nicaraguan, and halfwheel identifies it as Habano.

cigars.about: Named for the motorcycle crash into a guardrail that put Kristoff founder Glen Case in the hospital. It is notable for using tobacco from Zimbabwe in the filler under a Brazilian maduro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Kristoff rates strength 3 out of 5 but describes the cigar as medium-full bodied.

cigars.about: A stronger take on Kristoff's Original Criollo, with twice as much ligero leaf in the filler. All of the tobacco is Cuban-seed, grown in Honduras and the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Kristoff rates strength 4 out of 5 and calls it full-bodied; Neptune lists it as full strength.

cigars.about: Kristoff's nearly all-Nicaraguan blend under a Corojo wrapper, described by founder Glen Case as the spiciest cigar in his range. The Torpedo was Cigar Aficionado's No. 11 cigar of 2012 with 93 points.
cigars.researchNote: Despite the name it is a regular production line. Kristoff rates strength 4 out of 5 and Cigar Aficionado calls it medium-full; Neptune lists medium. Older sources name the factory Charles Fairmorn, the former name of Tabacalera Von Eicken.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Kristoff's value-priced Kristania line, swapping the original's Nicaraguan wrapper for Brazilian maduro over Dominican Habano binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Kristoff rates strength 3 out of 5. The 2014 announcement named the factory Charles Fairmorn, the former name of Tabacalera Von Eicken.

cigars.about: A small-batch perfecto named for the address of the suburban Chicago house where Kristoff founder Glen Case grew up. It first went to TAA retailers in 2013 before a wider release.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree. Kristoff lists a Brazilian Sumatra binder, 6.25 x 60 and strength 3 of 5; halfwheel and Neptune list a Nicaraguan binder with one undisclosed filler leaf and 6 1/2 x 60, and Neptune calls it full. Kristoff calls it limited production, but it is still sold.

cigars.about: A single-size box-pressed toro named for Jarrid Trudeau, Kristoff's executive vice president. It began in 2019 as an event cigar and follows the earlier GC Signature Series named for founder Glen Case.
cigars.researchNote: Kristoff rates strength 3 out of 5. Its site does not give the wrapper's country; halfwheel lists it as Ecuador. The binder is described only as Sumatra, with no country given.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Connecticut with a sweet tip
cigars.about: A mild, sweet-tipped Connecticut-wrapped cigar from Kristoff, sold in bundles as one of its lower-priced lines.
cigars.researchNote: Sweet tipped, and contains no Cuban tobacco. Kristoff and Neptune both call it mild, though Kristoff's strength chart shows 3 out of 5. Neptune lists the wrapper, binder and filler as all Dominican, which differs from Kristoff's own blend.

cigars.about: Kristoff's value line, sold in two wrappers over the same Dominican binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler: a mild, creamy Ecuadorian Connecticut and a richer Brazilian Maduro.
cigars.researchNote: Comes in two versions: Natural (Ecuadorian Connecticut, mild and creamy) and Maduro (Brazilian, coffee and cocoa). Kristoff gives one strength rating of 3 out of 5 for both. Sold in bundles.

cigars.about: An annual limited cigar that Kristoff sells only to retailers who order at the PCA trade show, with part of the sales supporting the association. The 2026 edition is a box-pressed Cameroon-wrapped toro extra with a pigtail cap.
cigars.researchNote: Blend details are for the 2026 edition: 500 boxes of 20, rated 3 out of 5 by Kristoff. The series has run every year since 2022 with a different blend each time, for example Brazilian maduro in 2023 and Mexican San Andres in 2024 and 2025.

cigars.about: A limited cigar Kristoff makes only for retailers in the Tobacconists' Association of America. The 2026 edition is a toro with a Connecticut broadleaf maduro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Details are for the 2026 edition: 500 boxes of 20, due to ship in late October or November 2026. Kristoff calls it medium-plus bodied and gives no separate strength rating. Earlier TAA exclusives were different cigars: a Brazilian maduro cut perfecto in 2024 and an Ecuadorian shade perfecto in 2023.

cigars.about: A Kristoff robusto made only for the Canadian market, launched in July 2026 through distributor JB Cigar Co. The name refers to the 49th parallel north, which forms much of the border between the United States and Canada.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only in Canada, in boxes of 20. The binder's country is not disclosed, and no strength, factory or production limit has been published.

cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped version of the Pistoff Kristoff, keeping the same Indonesian binder and Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania broadleaf filler as the San Andres original. Founder Glen Case calls it a Connecticut with an attitude.
cigars.researchNote: Glen Case rates it 4 out of 5 for strength, so it is stronger than a typical Connecticut. It goes first to TAA retailers, shipping in late October or November 2026, with a wide release planned for the PCA show in March 2027.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano, Olor), Nicaragua (Condega, Esteli)
cigars.about: A box-pressed Macanudo with an Ecuadorian shade wrapper, launched in April 2026 alongside the Sumatra version of the same blend. Unlike most Macanudos it is rolled in Esteli, Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: All sizes are box-pressed. Macanudo rates it Mellow to Medium in body and gives no separate strength; Neptune lists it as Medium.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano, Olor), Nicaragua (Condega, Esteli)
cigars.about: A box-pressed Macanudo with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, launched in April 2026 as the richer partner to the Ecuadorian Shade. It shares that cigar's binder and filler and is rolled in Esteli, Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: All sizes are box-pressed. Macanudo rates it Medium in body and gives no separate strength rating.

cigars.filler: Brazil (Mata Fina), Nicaragua (Jalapa), Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano seco and ligero)
cigars.about: A Macanudo built around a Connecticut broadleaf wrapper from the hot, wet 2013 growing season, aged about ten years. General Cigar began shipping it in July 2023.
cigars.researchNote: 2013 is the wrapper's crop year, not the release year. Macanudo rates it Medium in body and gives no separate strength rating.

cigars.about: A Macanudo made with Honduran wrapper and binder over aged Honduran and Nicaraguan filler, rested two years after rolling. It is not on Macanudo's own site and only turns up at a few retailers.
cigars.researchNote: Retailer information only; the maker does not list it. Neptune's spec table says Dominican Republic, but its own description and Cigar Place both say it is made in Honduras. Neptune marks it discontinued.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican Jamao (Habano seed from Jamastran, Honduras, grown in Mao)
cigars.about: A limited Inspirado whose wrapper is a Honduran Jamastran habano seed grown in the Mao region of the Dominican Republic. The name joins Jamastran and Mao.
cigars.researchNote: Limited edition; halfwheel reports 46,000 cigars in total. Pronounced hah-mau. Macanudo rates it Medium in body and gives no separate strength rating.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano seco and ligero), Colombia (seco)
cigars.about: A limited Inspirado built around Dominican piloto filler aged six months in tercios, bales wrapped in royal palm bark. It shipped in April 2023.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,700 boxes of 10 per size in the U.S. Macanudo rates it Medium in body and gives no separate strength rating.

cigars.about: A limited Lunar New Year edition of Macanudo Inspirado made for markets in Europe and Asia, not for the U.S. It came in one 6 x 50 toro.
cigars.researchNote: Not a U.S. release: 3,900 boxes of 10 for France, Spain, the UAE, Macau and other markets. Announced December 2022, on sale from early January 2023. No strength rating was published.

cigars.line: M by Macanudo Espresso with Cream
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Indonesian shade and Indonesian maduro (barber pole)
cigars.about: A flavored Macanudo with a two-tone barber pole wrapper, infused with espresso and cream flavor. It launched in August 2021.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored (infused) cigar; launched as M by Macanudo Espresso. Macanudo rates it Medium in body, while Neptune lists it as Full. Factory is as halfwheel reported at the 2021 launch.

cigars.about: A flavored Macanudo modeled on the Old Fashioned cocktail, with bourbon, cherry and bitters flavoring over an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. It launched in August 2019.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored cigar, also sold as M Bourbon by Macanudo. Launched with a Toro (6 x 50) and Churchill (7 x 47); Macanudo now lists only the Robusto. Where it is rolled is unclear: Neptune says Nicaragua, halfwheel says the M flavored lines are made at General Cigar Dominicana.

cigars.about: A flavored Macanudo with Irish cream flavoring over a Cameroon wrapper, one of three M by Macanudo flavors added in March 2025. It comes in one robusto size.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored (infused) cigar. Halfwheel lists the factory as General Cigar Dominicana, while retailer Cigar Place says it is made in Nicaragua. Macanudo rates it Medium in body.

cigars.about: A flavored Macanudo with vanilla and bourbon flavoring over a Cameroon wrapper, one of three M by Macanudo flavors added in March 2025. It comes in one robusto size.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored (infused) cigar; separate from the older M Bourbon. Halfwheel lists the factory as General Cigar Dominicana, while retailer Cigar Place says it is made in Nicaragua. Macanudo rates it Medium in body.

cigars.about: A flavored Macanudo with honey flavoring, one of three M by Macanudo flavors added in March 2025. It comes in one robusto size.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored (infused) cigar. Macanudo and Cigar Place list an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper; halfwheel's launch report said Cameroon for all three 2025 flavors. Halfwheel lists General Cigar Dominicana as the factory, while Cigar Place says Nicaragua.

cigars.about: A flavored Macanudo made in partnership with Sazerac's Myers's Rum, a nod to both brands' Jamaican roots. It began shipping in April 2026 in one robusto size.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored cigar. Halfwheel reports it is flavored to go with rum rather than infused with actual rum. Macanudo rates it Mellow to Medium in body and gives no separate strength rating.

cigars.about: The first Macanudo Emissary, released in March 2024, built around 10-year-old filler tobacco grown near Riolobos, Spain. It blends tobaccos from five countries and is rolled in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is a lighter claro broadleaf, though Neptune lists it as maduro. The Perfecto tapers from 40 to 54 ring. A limited box-pressed Torpedo (6 x 52, 1,500 boxes of 16) shipped in October 2024.

cigars.about: The second Macanudo Emissary, released in March 2025, featuring four-year-old French filler tobacco grown in the Mugron valley between Bordeaux and the Spanish border. It is rolled in Honduras with tobaccos from five countries.
cigars.researchNote: Every leaf is aged four to ten years; the French leaf is the youngest at four. Macanudo rates it Medium in body and gives no separate strength rating.

cigars.about: A box-pressed San Andrés-wrapped blend from AJ Fernandez that marks ten years of the New World brand. It is made at the company's San Lotano factory in Ocotal, Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's and Corona Cigar list it medium-full; Neptune lists it full. Halfwheel's review put strength at medium building to medium-full.

cigars.about: The mild Connecticut-shade blend in San Lotano Requiem, the core three-blend line of AJ Fernandez's first brand. It is made in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists a Honduran binder with Nicaraguan and Dominican filler. Neptune's copy says Nicaraguan binder with Honduran leaf in the filler. It launched in 2010 as San Lotano Connecticut; the maker now calls it Requiem Connecticut.

cigars.about: A collaboration between AJ Fernandez and Jochy Blanco, made at Blanco's Tabacalera Palma in the Dominican Republic rather than in Nicaragua. It pairs a Brazilian wrapper with Dominican and Nicaraguan tobaccos from both makers' farms.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel and Cigar Aficionado rate strength medium-full; Holt's and Neptune list it as medium. The wrapper is Cuban-seed leaf grown in Brazil, so Habano is the closest category rather than an exact one.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The Connecticut-shade version of San Lotano Oval, AJ Fernandez's line pressed into an oval shape. It was added in 2013 as the third Oval blend.
cigars.researchNote: In 2018 AJ Fernandez dropped the Oval line from general distribution and it became a Cigars International exclusive, so it is not on the maker's site. Part of the filler is undisclosed.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The maduro version of San Lotano Oval, AJ Fernandez's oval-pressed line, using the same binder and filler as the original Oval under a darker wrapper. It followed the original by a year.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the wrapper: halfwheel says Ecuadorian Habano Maduro, Holt's says Connecticut Broadleaf, Neptune says San Andrés. Holt's lists medium-full; halfwheel's 2012 review found it medium. Since 2018 the Oval line has been a Cigars International exclusive.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: AJ Fernandez's Nicaraguan-made take on the old Cuban Ramon Allones name, which he makes and sells in the U.S. under an arrangement with trademark owner General Cigar. It is known for its very dark wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker says the wrapper is a medio tiempo leaf grown on AJ's farm in Nicaragua; halfwheel lists it as Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro. Neptune lists strength as full, Corona Cigar as medium to full. This is not the Cuban Ramon Allones.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro with a habano wrapper that AJ Fernandez released as a thank-you for the support he received after the 2025 fire at his main factory in Estelí. It is made at the company's San Lotano factory in Ocotal.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's and Corona Cigar list it medium-full; halfwheel's review found the strength reaching full by the end. Amar means to love in Spanish and moon in Arabic, a nod to AJ's Cuban and Lebanese heritage.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro marking 20 years since AJ Fernandez started his cigar company, blended from what he calls the best leaf from his farms. It is rolled at his main factory in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: The Toro was limited to 7,500 numbered boxes of 20 and the Belicoso came only in 250 numbered 50-count humidors. The wrapper variety is not named; Neptune lists its color as maduro. Halfwheel calls it AJF 20th Anniversary.

cigars.about: An Enclave blend that AJ Fernandez had made by former Davidoff blender Eladio Díaz at Díaz's own factory in the Dominican Republic, using Díaz's tobacco. It contains no Nicaraguan leaf, which is unusual for an AJ Fernandez brand.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel's review and trade show report list the wrapper as Ecuadorian Criollo 99; an earlier halfwheel news story and Neptune call it Corojo 99. Neptune lists strength as medium; halfwheel's reviewer found it milder than that.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped version of AJ Fernandez's Enclave line, with binder and filler from his Nicaraguan farms. It was created for retailers outside the United States.
cigars.researchNote: Released in 2021 for international markets such as Germany, the UK and Switzerland, so it is rarely seen in U.S. shops. No published strength rating was found; Neptune describes it as aimed at smokers who want a milder cigar.

cigars.about: An AJ Fernandez blend with an Ecuadorian Habano 2000 wrapper over a Mexican binder and Nicaraguan filler. It is sold by Famous Smoke Shop.
cigars.researchNote: Only Famous Smoke Shop lists this blend, so the details are the retailer's. Famous rates it full strength, though its Toro description calls it medium-bodied. Factory and release year are not published.

cigars.about: A budget-priced AJ Fernandez blend with a dark Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. It is sold by Famous Smoke Shop.
cigars.researchNote: Only Famous Smoke Shop lists this blend, so the details are the retailer's. Its specs say full strength while its description says medium to full. Factory and release year are not published.

cigars.about: The core non-Cuban Montecristo, sold by Altadis U.S.A. and made in the Dominican Republic with a Connecticut Shade wrapper. It is the mild yellow-band line that most people think of as the standard Montecristo.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers often call this Montecristo Yellow. Famous lists the No. 1 at 6 1/2 inches and mentions some Nicaraguan filler; Altadis lists 6 5/8 and Dominican filler only.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade (Connecticut seed, aged 20 years)
cigars.about: A Montecristo made by AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua around a 20-year-old Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper grown by A.S.P. Enterprises. The Nicaraguan binder and filler were blended at medium body to show off the aged wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Not a limited edition, but halfwheel reports it is made in small batches because the aged wrapper is in short supply. The No. 2 is a torpedo.

cigars.about: A soft-pressed Nicaraguan puro made by AJ Fernandez for Altadis U.S.A. It began as an alternate blend for the Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua and was released later as the milder sibling of that line.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis and Cigar Aficionado call it medium; Famous Smoke lists it medium-full. halfwheel names the factory as AJ Fernandez's San Lotano factory.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A $150 limited edition Nicaraguan puro made by AJ Fernandez for Altadis U.S.A., using tobacco from his El Dorado, La Lilia and San Lotano farms that was aged at least 10 years before rolling. Only 250 numbered boxes of 20 were made, and the boxes double as humidors.
cigars.researchNote: One size only, 5,000 cigars total. Altadis has not published a strength; Neptune lists it Full and calls the wrapper maduro, and halfwheel's reviewer found it full in body and strength by the end.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The 2026 follow-up to the $150 Doble Diamante, made by AJ Fernandez with aged tobacco from his Finca La Lilia and San Lotano farms in Esteli. It is box-pressed, blended to be stronger than the first one, and limited to 250 boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: One size only, 5,000 cigars total at $150 each. Altadis calls it medium-to-full; Neptune lists it Full and halfwheel's reviewer found it medium-plus.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made by Plasencia for Altadis U.S.A. to mark 90 years since Montecristo was founded in Cuba in 1935. It uses aged Plasencia tobacco from Esteli, Condega, Jalapa and Ometepe and comes in 12-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Described as a small-production release; no production number has been published. Strength is from Neptune's listing; halfwheel's reviewer found medium-plus body with mild nicotine strength. The No. 2 is a torpedo.

cigars.about: An extension of the Montecristo Epic line made at Tabacalera de Garcia in the Dominican Republic. The name refers to Dominican tobacco from the 2012 harvest used in the blend, not to the age of the cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis lists a Dominican and Nicaraguan binder with Dominican filler; Cigar Aficionado and halfwheel list a Dominican binder with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. The Blue No. 2 is a torpedo.

cigars.about: A darker follow-up to the original Espada, a Nicaraguan puro made for Altadis U.S.A. by the Plasencia family with tobacco they also grow. Cigar Aficionado describes it as more powerful than both the original Espada and the Espada Conquistador.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis does not publish a strength; Famous Smoke lists it medium-full and Neptune lists it medium. The 6 x 60 Magnum Especial started as a JR Cigar exclusive and went nationwide in 2021.

cigars.about: A limited edition in the Plasencia-made Espada series, built from aged tobacco in the Plasencia family's reserves. It is a Nicaraguan puro sold in one 6 x 55 size called Valiente.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis calls it Espada Signature Limited Edition and describes it as medium-bodied; halfwheel's reviewer found it closer to medium-full. Production numbers were not disclosed.

cigars.about: The fifth Espada release, a Nicaraguan puro made by Plasencia in Esteli for Altadis U.S.A. with tobacco from all four Nicaraguan growing regions. It sits between the original Espada and the Espada Oscuro in strength.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis, halfwheel and Cigar Aficionado all say all Nicaraguan and medium-to-full; Neptune lists it medium.

cigars.about: A collaboration between Altadis U.S.A. and Crowned Heads, named for Nashville, the city of music. It was blended with Ernesto Perez-Carrillo Jr. and rolled at his Tabacalera La Alianza factory in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Production was capped at 100,000 cigars per size. The Piramide was exclusive to Casa de Montecristo lounges. Strength is from Neptune's listing.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made by Plasencia as a collaboration between Montecristo and Bardstown Bourbon Co. It is the first cigar in the Distillers Select Series and is meant to be paired with Bardstown's Origin Series bourbon.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 7,000 boxes of 10 and sold through Santa Clara, Inc., the JR Cigar distribution arm. It is not barrel-aged or infused. No strength or tasting notes were published in the sources used.

cigars.about: The second cigar in the Montecristo Volume Series, made at Flor de Copan in Honduras and sold only through the distributor Santa Clara, Inc. The name comes from a chapter in the second volume of The Count of Monte Cristo.
cigars.researchNote: A distributor exclusive for Santa Clara, Inc., a sister company to Altadis U.S.A. The company describes it as medium-bodied.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Nicaraguan puro with a maduro wrapper, made by AJ Fernandez and aged five years after rolling. It comes in the Follow The Stars Tribute Humidor, a lighted humidor built with Hernandez Humidores that holds 50 cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Only 20 humidors at $15,000 each, plus 40 refill packs of 50 cigars, for 3,000 cigars total. Neptune also lists single cigars at $150. Strength is from Neptune's listing only.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped third blend in Southern Draw's value-priced 300 Hands project, made by AJ Fernandez and sold in bundles. A quarter of the profits goes to charitable causes in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The maker gives no strength rating; Famous Smoke lists it as medium. The name refers to the roughly 300 hands said to touch a cigar as it is made.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A fuller variation on the Rose of Sharon blend, made by AJ Fernandez and introduced at the 2019 trade show in Las Vegas. It uses an Ecuadorian claro wrapper and a different filler blend from the original.
cigars.researchNote: Maker calls it medium body and medium flavor; Neptune lists it as mild. The maker's spec line says the Corojo 99 filler is Nicaraguan, while halfwheel and Neptune say Honduran. The Perfecto is 5.5 x 58 per the maker and 5 x 58 per halfwheel.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A stronger offshoot of Jacobs Ladder made by AJ Fernandez, with broadleaf wrapper and binder and three ligeros in the filler where the original uses two.
cigars.researchNote: Maker rates it Full Body+ and Full Flavor+. halfwheel also reports a 5 x 58 Perfecto that began as a Cigar Federation exclusive called Oblivion; the maker's page does not list it.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A limited Jacobs Ladder release marking the 21st birthday of Ethan Jacob Holt, the line's namesake. It uses an early prototype blend with a San Andrés wrapper, rolled in 2016 and aged before release.
cigars.researchNote: Not the regular Jacobs Ladder blend: San Andrés wrapper here versus Pennsylvania broadleaf, and an open foot. Debuted at Famous Smoke Shop in September 2021 with a wider release planned for January 2022. Billed as full bodied; no tasting notes were published.

cigars.filler: Pelo de Oro, Corojo 99, Ligero (origins undisclosed)
cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A Southern Draw line made by AJ Fernandez with a reddish habano hybrid wrapper, named for the manzanita tree. Part of the proceeds goes to the First Nations Development Institute.
cigars.researchNote: The maker names the leaf varieties but not where they are grown; a 2022 halfwheel news story called it a Nicaraguan puro. Strength varies by source: Famous and halfwheel's review put it at full, Neptune lists medium.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: Southern Draw's gentlest core blend, made by AJ Fernandez with a U.S.-grown Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos. It is the lighter partner to Evening Primrose.
cigars.researchNote: Maker calls it mellow to medium bodied; Neptune lists it as medium. Announced in 2022 in different sizes, then relaunched in late 2024 in these three sizes and 20-count boxes.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A San Andrés maduro core line from Southern Draw, made by AJ Fernandez as the darker partner to Morning Glory. The filler is half Honduran, with Nicaraguan leaf and U.S. ligero making up the rest.
cigars.researchNote: The maker gives no strength rating but said at launch it would likely be seen as more robust than Jacobs Ladder; Neptune lists medium strength and medium to full body. Debuted in 2022 in other sizes and relaunched in late 2024 in these three.

cigars.about: Southern Draw's 10th anniversary cigar, rolled at El Titan de Bronze in Miami's Little Havana instead of at AJ Fernandez. It comes in one size and is sold in three-packs.
cigars.researchNote: Made in Miami, unlike nearly everything else from the brand. The first run was 5,000 three-packs and the maker has left the door open to more. halfwheel calls the 6 x 46 size a corona extra; the maker calls it a lonsdale.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: One of three cigars in Southern Draw's 2022 IGNITE charity series, made by AJ Fernandez. It is a variation on the Hyacinth blend from the company's Peccadilloes test project.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only in a five-pack with the Pennyroyal (three Hyacinth, two Pennyroyal), 10,000 packs, benefiting Warriors on the Fly. No strength rating or tasting notes were published.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: One of three cigars in Southern Draw's 2022 IGNITE charity series, made by AJ Fernandez with a San Andrés maduro wrapper. The filler is half Nicaraguan, a quarter Honduran and a quarter U.S. broadleaf ligero.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only in a five-pack with the Hyacinth (three Hyacinth, two Pennyroyal), 10,000 packs, benefiting Warriors on the Fly. No strength rating or tasting notes were published.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: One of three cigars in Southern Draw's 2022 IGNITE charity series, a Churchill made by AJ Fernandez with a dark Ecuadorian habano wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in five-packs, 10,000 packs, benefiting the U.S. Border Patrol Fallen Officers Scholarship Fund. halfwheel says it is a variation on the 2021 Ladykiller; the maker's page calls it a variation of the Peccadilloes Hyacinth. No strength rating was published.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Criollo 98 from Estelí, Jalapa and Condega)
cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A 2021 Southern Draw release made by AJ Fernandez for retail members of the Limited Cigar Association. It is named for a variety of crocus flower and came in a single lonsdale size.
cigars.researchNote: An exclusive for the Limited Cigar Association and Privada Cigar Club; production numbers were not disclosed. The 2022 IGNITE Crocus is a variation on this blend. No strength rating or tasting notes were published.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped blend in Southern Draw's QuickDraw line of small, quick-smoking cigars, made by AJ Fernandez. It joined the Habano and Pennsylvania Broadleaf versions in 2016.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper origin disagrees: the maker's site lists Connecticut, USA, while halfwheel, Neptune and Famous all say Ecuadorian Connecticut. The maker's line-wide filler listing is Nicaragua and Honduras. The original Petit Corona and Short Panatela sizes are gone; only the Corona Gorda remains.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: The dark habano blend in Southern Draw's QuickDraw line of small, quick-smoking cigars, made by AJ Fernandez. It was one of the line's first two blends, alongside the Pennsylvania Broadleaf.
cigars.researchNote: Often sold as QuickDraw Dark Habano. Neptune lists it as medium; Famous describes it as medium to full bodied. It predates the 2016 Connecticut version but no source checked gives the launch year.

cigars.about: One of the core Graycliff blends, rolled in Nassau with an Ecuadorian wrapper and a small amount of Greek leaf in the mix. It is also known as the White Label.
cigars.researchNote: Cigar Aficionado listed an Ecuadorian binder with Nicaraguan, Honduran, Costa Rican and Greek filler through 2020, then an Indonesian binder with Costa Rican, Dominican and Nicaraguan filler in late 2025. It rated the cigar medium earlier and full in 2025. Corona Cigar lists Brazilian, Nicaraguan and Honduran filler.

cigars.about: A stronger take on the Graycliff Espresso, made by adding extra ligero to the blend. It began as a single short, thick size sold through Cigars International and is now counted among the core Graycliff lines.
cigars.researchNote: The filler is described as Cuban-seed Corojo, Ecuadorian ligero and Nicaraguan leaf. The 4 1/2 x 54 size comes from a 2010 review, so current sizes may differ. No strength rating is published. The regular Espresso is sold as full bodied.

cigars.about: The strongest version of the Graycliff Espresso blend, introduced at the 2019 IPCPR trade show as a step up from the Double Espresso.
cigars.researchNote: No strength rating or tasting notes are published. It is billed as stronger than the Double Espresso. The source does not say where it is rolled, though Graycliff's own factory is in Nassau, Bahamas.

cigars.about: A core Graycliff line rolled in Nassau, sometimes spelled Chateau Gran Cru. It is the milder relative of the Heritage Royale.
cigars.researchNote: The blend and sizes come from a January 2015 review, before Graycliff reworked its blends and cut sizes later that year, so treat them as unconfirmed. That review called it medium. No current strength rating was found.

cigars.about: A full-bodied Graycliff line introduced in 2010, described as similar to the Chateau Grand Cru but a bit stronger.
cigars.researchNote: Corona Cigar says the blend uses tobacco from Costa Rica, Ecuador, Honduras and Nicaragua but does not say which is wrapper, binder or filler. Sizes were not confirmed.

cigars.about: Released in 2022 to mark 50 years since the Garzaroli family bought the Graycliff property in Nassau in 1973. It is a regular production line, not an anniversary of the cigar company itself, which dates to 1997.
cigars.researchNote: Corona Cigar lists the strength as medium. Corona lists its Uncut Toro at 5 3/4 x 54, which differs from the 7 x 52 halfwheel gives.

cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro marking 30 years since Graycliff began making cigars in 1997. It comes in one size and was capped at 3,000 cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 125 boxes of 24 in a single 6 x 52 size. No published strength rating, tasting notes or factory details were found.

cigars.about: A regular production Graycliff line from 2025 named for the predators found in Bahamian waters, with sizes called Shark and Barracuda.
cigars.researchNote: No published strength rating, tasting notes or factory details were found.

cigars.about: A Graycliff-branded line sold by Cigars Direct, described there as a limited annual release made in Honduras rather than at the Nassau factory.
cigars.researchNote: Only one retailer lists it, so the blend is left blank. Cigars Direct describes an Ecuadorian Habano sun grown wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, medium to full, made in Honduras, in Robusto, PGX, Pirate and Presidente sizes. Graycliff does not list it.

cigars.about: Introduced in 2012 and packed in a box styled like a bar of silver, with tobacco aged at least five years. It is rolled in Nassau and, unlike most Graycliff sizes, has a trimmed foot.
cigars.researchNote: Graycliff launched it in 2012 as a limited edition and still showed it in 2015, so its current status is unclear. The 2012 press release includes Philippine filler, which Corona Cigar leaves out. Corona calls it medium to full.

cigars.about: One of the five cigar brands the Graycliff Cigar Company in Nassau says it produces. The maker gives no blend or size details for it.
cigars.researchNote: Graycliff names this brand on its site but publishes no blend, strength or sizes, and no retailer listing was found.

cigars.about: One of the five cigar brands the Graycliff Cigar Company in Nassau says it produces. The maker gives no blend or size details for it.
cigars.researchNote: Graycliff names this brand on its site but publishes no blend, strength or sizes, and no retailer listing was found.

cigars.about: A lower-priced Graycliff blend launched in 2012 as an entry point to the brand, sold in bright orange boxes of 21.
cigars.researchNote: Launched at $7.50 to $7.95 a cigar. Graycliff still names it on its site, but no current retailer listing was found, so availability is unclear.

cigars.about: A collaboration between Graycliff and the DJ and musician P La Cangri, who picked the blend in a blind tasting at the Graycliff hotel. It debuted at the 2022 PCA trade show and is made by Graycliff.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Boss of the Block by Graycliff. It is P La Cangri's own brand, made and shown by Graycliff, with its own blend. No published strength rating was found.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped cigar in Black Label Trading Co.'s core line, made at the company's own Fabrica Oveja Negra in Esteli. It is known as a spicier, fuller take on a Connecticut than the style usually gives.
cigars.researchNote: Debuted in December 2018 as a limited Deliverance Porcelain and joined the core line in 2019. Halfwheel lists the wrapper as Ecuadorian Connecticut seed; the maker only says Connecticut and Neptune lists US Connecticut Shade.

cigars.about: A Day of the Dead themed cigar from Black Label Trading Co. with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper and six filler tobaccos. It started as an annual limited edition and became part of the core line in 2023.
cigars.researchNote: Limited annual release from 2016 to 2019, then relaunched in 2023 as regular production with new white packaging. The maker rates it medium; Neptune lists it as full and Cigars Direct as medium-full.

cigars.about: A small 5 x 40 petite corona from Black Label Trading Co., sold in flip-top boxes of 10. The idea was a big, bold cigar in a small format.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's tasting notes page lists an Ecuadorian binder and all-Nicaraguan filler, while its press release and halfwheel give a Honduran binder with Nicaraguan and Honduran filler. The maker rates it medium-plus to full; Neptune lists it as medium and Cigars Direct as full.

cigars.about: A limited release from Black Label Trading Co. that debuted at the 2026 PCA trade show, with a San Andrés wrapper and a rabito cap on every size. Production was 800 boxes each of the Robusto and Toro and 650 of the Corona Gorda.
cigars.researchNote: Cigars Direct lists it as medium-full and Atlantic Cigar as full, but halfwheel's reviewer found the strength only mild to medium. The maker gives no strength rating. The maker and halfwheel give the Toro as 6 x 50; Neptune lists it as 6 x 48.

cigars.about: A small batch 2024 release from Black Label Trading Co., offered to retailers who attended that year's PCA trade show. The maker describes it as a return to the brand's roots of bold Nicaraguan tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 900 boxes of each size. Neptune and Cigars Direct list it as full and the maker calls it one of its boldest blends, but halfwheel's reviewer found the nicotine strength only mild to medium.

cigars.about: A 2025 limited release from Black Label Trading Co. made to mark the 10th anniversary of its factory, Fabrica Oveja Negra. The name is Italian for chosen one.
cigars.researchNote: 800 boxes each of the Short Robusto and Toro and 400 of the Corona Gorda. Cigars Direct lists it as medium-full and Atlantic Cigar as full, but halfwheel's reviewer found the strength mild to just under medium. The maker gives no strength rating.

cigars.about: A limited Pennsylvania broadleaf cigar from Black Label Trading Co. that has traditionally come only in figurado shapes. It returns every few years and is one of the brand's most requested blends.
cigars.researchNote: Sizes shown are the 2025 release, the first since 2020 and the first with straight-sided Robusto and Toro sizes. The Short Salomon tapers from 40 to 56 ring. Neptune lists it as full; Cigars Direct lists it as medium-full.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andrés and Ecuadorian Maduro (dual wrapper)
cigars.about: A near-annual limited release from Black Label Trading Co. that first appeared in 2014. Recent versions use two wrapper leaves, San Andrés and Ecuadorian maduro, rolled in a subtle barber pole.
cigars.researchNote: Sizes and blend shown are the 10th anniversary release shipped in November 2024; the blend and sizes have been tweaked from year to year. Retailers list it as full, while halfwheel's reviewer put the strength at medium-full.

cigars.about: A box-pressed San Andrés limited release from Black Label Trading Co. that debuted in 2020 and came back for a second run in 2025. The maker calls it the most requested cigar in the brand's history.
cigars.researchNote: Sizes shown are the 2025 release, 750 boxes of each. The 2020 original came as a petite corona, a 5 1/4 x 52 robusto and a 7 x 42 lancero. Cigars Direct describes it as medium-full but also tags it full.

cigars.about: The 10th anniversary cigar of Black Label Trading Co., released in 2023 in three box-pressed sizes. It pairs a Connecticut broadleaf wrapper with Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania filler.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 900 boxes of each size, plus 50 mixed 32-count collection boxes. Strength is from Cigars Direct and halfwheel's review, not the maker.

cigars.about: A limited offshoot of Black Label Trading Co.'s Last Rites blend that uses most of the same tobaccos in different proportions and primings. All sizes are box pressed.
cigars.researchNote: First released in 2019 as a single 5 x 54 robusto for trade show retailers (500 boxes), then in 2021 in three sizes at 800 boxes each. The maker now usually calls it just Viaticum and gives no strength rating. Cigars Direct lists it as full, while Cigar Coop's review found it medium.

cigars.about: A dark Pennsylvania broadleaf cigar from Black Label Trading Co. that began as a factory exclusive at Fabrica Oveja Negra and reached stores in March 2022. The name is Latin for remember you must die.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 850 boxes of each size for the US. Strength and body are from halfwheel's review, not the maker. Cigars Direct lists it as full.

cigars.about: A 2023 special edition of Black Label Trading Co.'s Bishops Blend, made for the brand's 10th anniversary. It swaps the usual Ecuadorian maduro wrapper for Pennsylvania broadleaf.
cigars.researchNote: A one-time variant of the regular Bishops Blend limited release, 900 boxes of each size. Strength and body are from halfwheel's review, not the maker.

cigars.about: One of Black Label Trading Co.'s original 2013 core lines, shelved in 2019 when Porcelain took its place. It came back in December 2021 as a tweaked Nicaraguan puro sold only at Smokers Abbey shops.
cigars.researchNote: Blend and sizes shown are the 2021 Smokers Abbey exclusive (Austin, Memphis, Nashville), 150 boxes per size per store. It is no longer a core line. The maker gives no strength rating; Neptune described the original as medium bodied.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: Joya de Nicaragua's 55th anniversary cigar, a soft-pressed blend with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. The blend was built from the records of hundreds of blending sessions held with factory visitors, and it sits in the company's top Obras Maestras tier.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's page rates strength 4 out of 5 and calls it medium to full-bodied, but its launch release said full-bodied with medium strength, and halfwheel found the strength mild to medium. A 6 x 60 size was made in 2024 as a TAA exclusive.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A bolder take on Joya de Nicaragua's original Clásico, made as a Nicaraguan puro with a habano criollo wrapper. It came out in 2021 to mark 50 years of the Clásico and reached the U.S. in 2024.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it 2 out of 5 and has called it both mild to medium and medium-bodied. In the U.S. it is sold only through Club de Amigos retailers. The Gordo is a U.S. size, and the Selección B and Gordito are sold abroad.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped version of Rosalones, Joya de Nicaragua's value-priced line that was long sold only outside the U.S. It pairs an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's page lists the wrapper as Nicaraguan habano criollo Colorado and the binder as Ecuador Connecticut, which looks swapped; halfwheel reports an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder. It reached U.S. stores in 2026. The maker rates strength 2 out of 5.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A step up within Rosalones, Joya de Nicaragua's affordable Nicaraguan puro line, using a more selective choice of tobacco. It launched in Europe in 2016 and came to U.S. stores in 2026.
cigars.researchNote: In the U.S. it is sold in two sizes, called Robusto (5 x 50) and Toro (6 x 50). The maker rates strength 3 out of 5.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: One of Joya de Nicaragua's oldest brands, an everyday Nicaraguan puro with a light habano criollo wrapper. For many years it was sold only in northern Europe.
cigars.researchNote: Details come from the maker's page only, which rates strength 2.5 out of 5 and calls it medium-bodied. The maker lists a single Robusto size.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A limited U.S.-only toro in the JOYA series, made to mark the 250th anniversary of American independence. It uses an Ecuadorian habano wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler with extra aging.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 500 boxes of 10, sold only in the U.S. and shipped in June 2026. The maker describes it as medium-bodied.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A limited diadema in the Clásico Original blend, named for the White House Green Room, where Joya de Nicaragua cigars were offered to guests in the 1970s. It has an Ecuadorian Connecticut shade wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: This is one limited size of the Clásico Original line: 1,200 boxes of 20, with 700 for the U.S. The maker calls it mild, while halfwheel's review found medium strength with full flavor.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A limited return to the all-Nicaraguan blend of the original 2013 Cuatro Cinco Edición Limitada, using tobacco aged since 2013 in charred oak barrels that once held spirits. It comes in the same 6 x 54 box-pressed size as the original.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,500 boxes of 10, with 700 for the U.S. The maker calls it medium to full-bodied, while halfwheel's review found the strength below medium. The wrapper is published only as Nicaraguan, with no seed type given.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A limited 2021 release marking 200 years of Central American independence, blended from tobaccos of five countries. It is part of Joya de Nicaragua's Obras Maestras tier and was halfwheel's number 4 cigar of 2021.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 3,000 boxes of 21, with 2,000 for the U.S.; one cigar in each box came wrapped in tissue paper. The maker calls it medium-bodied (2.5 out of 5), but halfwheel's reviewer put it closer to 3.5 to 4 out of 5.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A Brazil-only version of the Antaño Original, made with distributor Reality Cigars, that adds Brazilian Mata Fina leaf to the otherwise all-Nicaraguan filler. It was the first time Joya de Nicaragua changed a blend for a regional exclusive.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only in Brazil, limited to 2,000 boxes of 10. No strength rating is published for this edition. The Antaño Original line was called Antaño 1970 until 2024.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A value-priced bundle cigar made by Joya de Nicaragua in Estelí as a Famous Smoke Shop exclusive. It has a dark Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: A Famous Smoke Shop exclusive sold in bundles of 10; the retailer is the only source for the blend. Sizes are listed as Carnage San Andres.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A value-priced bundle cigar made by Joya de Nicaragua for Famous Smoke Shop. It has an Ecuadorian Connecticut shade wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Sold by Famous Smoke Shop as Cunning by Joya de Nicaragua, in bundles of 10. The retailer is the only source for the blend.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A value-priced bundle cigar made in Estelí by Joya de Nicaragua as a Famous Smoke Shop exclusive. It uses an Ecuadorian habano wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: A Famous Smoke Shop exclusive sold in bundles of 10; the retailer is the only source for the blend. Its spec table says Full, while its own description says medium to full-bodied.

cigars.about: One of Blackbird Cigar Co.'s core lines, a medium-bodied Dominican cigar with a dark Cuban-seed Brazilian wrapper. It is made at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the filler only by leaf type (Criollo 98, HBA, Corojo, Pennsylvania), not by country. The maker's page shows three sizes; the Corona is in retailer listings. Neptune calls the wrapper a Brazilian maduro and rates it medium; Atlantic Cigar rates it medium-full.

cigars.about: Blackbird's Connecticut-wrapped core line and one of the lightest blends in its portfolio. It debuted at the 2019 IPCPR trade show and is made at the company's Dominican factory.
cigars.researchNote: The maker spells it JackDaw and calls it mild to medium bodied; Neptune lists it as mild. The maker lists Corojo 99, USA and Dominican filler, while halfwheel's 2019 listing gave Dominican, USA and Nicaraguan. The Corona (6 x 44) is listed by Cigars Direct and Smokingpipes, not by the maker.

cigars.about: A core line introduced in 2024 and the first regular Blackbird cigar with a habano wrapper. It is made at the company's Dominican factory, and a box-pressed toro and a lancero were added in 2025.
cigars.researchNote: The binder and filler are undisclosed. Retailers describe the wrapper as an Ecuadorian Habano maduro; halfwheel lists it simply as Ecuadorian habano.

cigars.about: A San Andres maduro-wrapped Blackbird cigar named after Arizona's state bird. Retailers describe it as a short-run, limited release made at the company's factory in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers call this a short-run or limited-edition cigar, so supply can be spotty. The filler is published only by leaf type, not by country. Neptune calls it medium bodied; Smokingpipes says medium-full bodied.

cigars.about: A single-size toro with a Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper, shown at the 2025 PCA trade show as part of Blackbird's limited Short Run Line. It is made at the company's factory in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: The binder and filler are undisclosed. It was announced as a limited Short Run Line release with an initial run of 500 boxes of 20. Neptune rates it medium; Atlantic Cigar rates it medium-full.

cigars.about: The Connecticut Shade version of Blackbird's value-priced Nest line, sold in bundles of 25. It is a mild to medium cigar made at the company's Dominican factory.
cigars.researchNote: Nest is Blackbird's bundle line, in Connecticut and Maduro versions. Neptune rates it mild; Atlantic and Cigars Daily say mild to medium. Atlantic lists an Indonesian binder and mixed filler; Neptune and Cigars Daily list a Dominican binder.

cigars.about: The San Andres maduro version of Blackbird's value-priced Nest line, sold in bundles of 25. It is a medium-strength cigar made at the company's Dominican factory.
cigars.researchNote: Nest is Blackbird's bundle line, in Connecticut and Maduro versions. Neptune and Cigars Daily rate it medium; Atlantic says medium-full. Atlantic lists an Indonesian binder and mixed filler; Neptune and Cigars Daily list a Dominican binder.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped blend in Blackbird's value-priced GLITCH line, which shipped in June 2023. The line grew out of a factory mix-up in which mislabeled tobacco produced a blend the team decided to keep.
cigars.researchNote: One of three GLITCH blends (Claro, Habano, Oscuro) that share the same two sizes. The maker publishes no strength: Atlantic Cigar rates it mild and Smokingpipes 3 out of 5. Atlantic sells it as GLITCH Connecticut and lists a Dominican binder; halfwheel reports Mexican.

cigars.about: The habano-wrapped blend in Blackbird's value-priced GLITCH line, which shipped in June 2023. It uses the same binder and filler as the Claro with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: One of three GLITCH blends (Claro, Habano, Oscuro) that share the same two sizes. Strength comes from retailer listings (Atlantic Cigar, Smokingpipes), not the maker. Atlantic sells it as GLITCH Natural and lists a Dominican binder; halfwheel reports Mexican.

cigars.about: The San Andres-wrapped blend in Blackbird's value-priced GLITCH line, which shipped in June 2023. Unlike the other two GLITCH blends, it uses a Dominican binder instead of a Mexican one.
