cigars.researchNote: One of three GLITCH blends (Claro, Habano, Oscuro) that share the same two sizes. Strength comes from retailer listings (Atlantic Cigar, Smokingpipes), not the maker. Atlantic sells it as GLITCH Maduro.

cigars.about: A box-pressed toro released in April 2026 as the first of three cigars marking Blackbird's 10th anniversary. It honors the company's master blender, known as Papo "El Caballo", and is planned as an annual limited release.
cigars.researchNote: The binder and filler are undisclosed, and the 2026 run is 500 boxes of 10 at $16 per cigar. The company calls it mild to medium bodied; halfwheel found the strength reached medium by the end. halfwheel names the factory as Tabacalera Robles in Tamboril, the company's own factory.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Corojo, Criollo 98, Piloto Cubano), USA (Pennsylvania)
cigars.about: Blackbird's first limited edition, a box-pressed robusto gordo that shipped in August 2021 after being announced as the "Unknown Limited Edition". The company says it uses the best versions of tobaccos found in its other blends.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 500 boxes of 14 (7,000 cigars) in one size. The wrapper is a Cuban-seed Brazilian leaf similar to the one on Unkind and Cuco. Strength and body are halfwheel's review ratings, not the maker's.

cigars.about: A box-pressed 6 x 54 toro made by Blackbird as a collaboration with The Cigar Culture, shipped in November 2021. It was the second cigar in The Cigar Culture's series.
cigars.researchNote: This is a collaboration release for The Cigar Culture, made by Blackbird; Neptune sells it as Blackbird Hawk Cigar Culture. Limited to 600 boxes of 14 in one size. Neptune lists the wrapper shade as natural.

cigars.about: A regular-production Quesada line named for the year the family started making its own cigars after generations as leaf brokers. It is known for an uncommon Cameroon-seed wrapper grown in Ecuador, and Quesada grew the Dominican tobacco in it.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers list the wrapper only as Ecuadorian; halfwheel specifies Cameroon-seed. It went on sale in Spain in February 2019 and reached the U.S. that fall. The Toro was added in 2021.

cigars.about: A limited edition released in 2024 to mark 50 years since the Quesada family opened its cigar factory in the Dominican Republic. It came in a box-pressed toro and a much scarcer perfecto, both in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: About 2,000 to 2,200 boxes of the Toro Prensado and only 200 boxes of the Perfecto were made. Neptune lists it as medium with a maduro-colored wrapper; halfwheel found the nicotine strength mild.

cigars.about: A 2026 limited edition marking Manolo Quesada Jr.'s 79th birthday, blended by his daughters Raquel and Patricia. It is the third Quesada birthday cigar and the first one he did not blend himself.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,000 boxes of 10, with 700 for the U.S. Neptune lists the filler as Dominican only; halfwheel says Dominican and Nicaraguan. Medium and the Colorado wrapper shade are Neptune's listing; the wrapper variety is not published.

cigars.about: A single-size limited edition from 2022 that Manolo Quesada Jr. blended for his own 75th birthday. It followed the Manuel Quesada 70th and came in numbered boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: The shipping announcement said 1,200 numbered boxes of 10; halfwheel's review table says 1,500. Cigar Coop and Mike's Cigars rate it medium, while halfwheel found it mild to medium. Neptune describes the filler as Nicaraguan only.

cigars.about: A seasonal limited release for the winter holidays, a spin-off of the St. Patrick's Day Keg. It is a single toro sold in small wooden boxes shaped like barrels.
cigars.researchNote: The blend shown is the 2022 edition, limited to 500 boxes in the U.S. The 2016 original used a Dominican wrapper, which is what Neptune still lists (Dominican Corojo). Medium is Neptune's rating.

cigars.about: A St. Patrick's Day limited edition blended to pair with Irish stout and packed in wooden kegs. Plasencia rolls it in Nicaragua, which made it the first Quesada-branded cigar produced outside the family's Dominican factory.
cigars.researchNote: Editions came out in 2015 (toro only), 2016 and 2017, all with the same blend. Neptune shows it sold out and not expected back. Medium is Neptune's rating; halfwheel's 2015 review found it milder.

cigars.about: The broadleaf-wrapped follow-up to the Quesada Reserva Privada, built around a Dominican criollo binder from the 1997 harvest. It uses more Pennsylvania ligero than the original and smokes stronger than most Quesadas.
cigars.researchNote: Launched as a limited edition of 1,400 boxes per size; the Robusto was a TAA exclusive. Neptune rates it full and now marks it discontinued. halfwheel called it medium-full.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Connecticut and Dominican Criollo 98 Oscuro (barber pole)
cigars.about: A two-tone version of the Quesada Reserva Privada with a light and a dark wrapper leaf twisted together over the line's 1997-crop Dominican binder. It began as a Procigar charity auction cigar before going on sale in 2017.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the wrappers: halfwheel says Ecuadorian Connecticut and Dominican Criollo 98 Oscuro, Neptune says U.S. Connecticut shade and broadleaf. Neptune also rates it full; halfwheel found it medium. Launched as 300 boxes per size but still stocked in 2026.

cigars.about: One of two sweet-capped blends Quesada introduced in 2026 under the Suspiro name, which is a Spanish meringue dessert and also means sigh. This one wears a Connecticut-seed wrapper and comes in boxes of 15.
cigars.researchNote: The cap is sweetened. Quesada has not said where the Connecticut-seed wrapper is grown, and no strength rating or tasting notes were published in the sources checked. It reached stores in August 2026.

cigars.about: The darker of the two sweet-capped Suspiro blends Quesada introduced in 2026. It uses a Cameroon-seed wrapper grown in Ecuador over a Dominican binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler, in boxes of 15.
cigars.researchNote: The cap is sweetened. Despite the Oscuro name, the wrapper is a Cameroon-seed leaf from Ecuador. No strength rating or tasting notes were published in the sources checked. It reached stores in August 2026.

cigars.about: One of the most expensive lines Quesada has made, launched in 2018 with Dominican filler that had been aging in palm-leaf tercios since 2001. Each box of 10 has a removable sketch by Dominican artist Pragmy Marichal built into the bottom.
cigars.researchNote: Sold under the Vega Magna name rather than as a Quesada-banded cigar. One roller and buncher pair makes all of it, so supply is small. Quesada calls it full-bodied; Neptune and halfwheel put strength around medium and Cigars Direct lists medium-full.

cigars.about: A short, fat perfecto with a pigtail cap, a shape often called a pig, that Quesada made in 2021 for Privada Cigar Club's Limited Cigar Association. It was a one-time release sold in bundles of 20.
cigars.researchNote: The blend was never disclosed. Its full name is Quesada BBQ Pig LCA Exclusive and it was sold only through LCA member shops. halfwheel rated strength medium-plus; flavors are from its review.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto), Nicaragua (Esteli), Honduras (La Entrada Corojo 2012, Jamastran Broadleaf)
cigars.about: A Honduran-made Hoyo de Monterrey from General Cigar (Scandinavian Tobacco Group), rolled in Danli with a Honduran OSA wrapper over a broadleaf binder. It first appeared in September 2026 as the toro in the Hoyo New Legends Sampler.
cigars.researchNote: As of September 2026 only the 6 x 52 Toro was on sale, and only inside the Hoyo New Legends Sampler. Rothschild (4.5 x 50) and Gigante (6 x 60) boxes were announced without a date. This is not the Cuban Le Hoyo series from Habanos.

cigars.about: An all-Honduran blend from General Cigar finished with a shade-grown wrapper and made in Danli. It followed Rojo and Oscuro in 2025 as the mildest of the relaunched Hoyo de Monterrey lines.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it Mellow to Medium; Famous Smoke and Neptune list it as Mild. The maker and halfwheel say the wrapper is Honduran shade-grown, while Famous Smoke's description says the leaf is grown in Ecuador.

cigars.about: One of two blends General Cigar used to relaunch the Honduran Hoyo de Monterrey in 2024. It pairs a wrapper from Honduras' Jamastran Valley with a Nicaraguan binder and three-country filler at an everyday price.
Released alongside Rojo in 2024 as part of General Cigar's relaunch of the Honduran Hoyo de Monterrey. The company says it is the first Hoyo de Monterrey to use a Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: General Cigar's launch release called it medium-plus and its site lists body as Medium. Famous Smoke lists the strength as Full.

cigars.about: A Honduran puro from General Cigar made entirely of Cuban-seed tobacco grown in Honduras. The name and packaging echo the Cuban Epicure cigars, but it is an unrelated blend sold only in the U.S.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates body Medium to Full; halfwheel's review and Neptune put the strength at Medium. Not the Cuban Hoyo de Monterrey Epicure from Habanos.

cigars.about: The dark-wrapper version of the classic Honduran Hoyo de Monterrey from General Cigar, finished in Connecticut Broadleaf. It is a long-running line sold in traditional sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it Medium; Holts says Medium-Full and Famous Smoke, which sells it as Hoyo de Monterrey Broadleaf, says Full. Neptune calls the wrapper Ecuadorian maduro, which disagrees with the maker. The Sultans (7.25 x 54) size was discontinued in August 2025.

cigars.about: A darker, fuller extension of General Cigar's Excalibur line, introduced in 2021 with a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper. It is made in Danli, Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's site now lists a Nicaraguan binder with Dominican and Nicaraguan ligero; the 2021 launch announcement gave an Ecuadorian Sumatra binder with Honduran and Nicaraguan fillers. The maker rates it Medium to Full; Famous Smoke and Neptune say Full.

cigars.about: The Cameroon-wrapped member of General Cigar's Honduran Excalibur family. The maker calls it the people's choice cigar because the blend was picked by consumers.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel's August 2025 list of items STG discontinued includes Excalibur Cameroon without naming a size; the maker's site still shows three sizes and some retailers still had stock. The maker rates it Mellow to Medium; Famous Smoke lists it as Medium.

cigars.about: A dark Excalibur from General Cigar that uses a Connecticut-grown Havana Seed wrapper over a Connecticut Broadleaf binder. It was sold in two thick sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Both sizes were on STG's August 2025 list of discontinued items, though the maker's site still shows the line. The maker rates it Medium to Full; Mike's Cigars lists it as Full. STG's Cigar World site lists the wrapper as Connecticut Broadleaf in its spec box but Connecticut Havana Seed in its description.

cigars.about: A General Cigar tribute to Hoyo de Monterrey's heritage, wrapped in a reddish viso rosado leaf from Honduras' Jamastran Valley. Scandinavian Tobacco Group discontinued the line in March 2025.
cigars.researchNote: Discontinued in March 2025, though the maker's site still shows it. Cigar Aficionado ranked the Toro Grande No. 23 in its Top 25 of 2008.

cigars.factory: Agricola Ganadera Nortena S.A. (AGANORSA Leaf, formerly TABSA)
cigars.about: A 2022 limited edition blended by Dion Giolito of Illusione with General Cigar's Justin Andrews, modeled on the Excalibur #1. It is a Nicaraguan puro made at the AGANORSA factory rather than in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: One size only, limited to 4,960 boxes of 10, and made in Nicaragua unlike the rest of the Excalibur family. Some sources call it The Illusione of Excalibur. Developing Palates and Neptune call it medium; halfwheel's review found the strength mild.

cigars.about: A limited-release Hoyo de Monterrey perfecto from General Cigar with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, a Nicaraguan binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers. It was introduced at the 2019 trade show.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on size: STG's Cigar World and Cigar Coop list a 6.5 x 49 perfecto, Neptune and Mike's a 7.25 x 54 Selectos Regalo. Cigar Coop and Neptune's text say made in Honduras, but Neptune's and Mike's spec tables say Dominican Republic, so country is blank. Neptune says it will not return once sold out.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (criollo and corojo viso from Jalapa, ligero from Estelí), Dominican Republic (ligero from Peñuela)
cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.about: The third Intemperance blend from RoMa Craft, named for the Whiskey Rebellion of 1794. It pairs a dark Ecuadorian Habano wrapper with an Indonesian Besuki binder and is rolled with the line's usual brushed foot.
cigars.researchNote: WR stands for Whiskey Rebellion. It debuted in 2016 as a Famous Smoke Shop exclusive made with Cigar Dojo and went to other stores in 2019. Retailers list it as full; halfwheel's review found it closer to medium-full.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (ligero from Condega, corojo seco from Jalapa, criollo viso from Pueblo Nuevo), Dominican Republic (corojo seco)
cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Sumatra hybrid (maker: dark Ecuador Sumatra/Cameroon/Habano hybrid)
cigars.about: The fourth Intemperance blend from RoMa Craft, named for the Volstead Act that put Prohibition into law in 1920. It uses an Ecuadorian Sumatra hybrid wrapper over a Mexican San Andrés binder, with sizes named after Prohibition figures.
cigars.researchNote: VO stands for Volstead. The maker calls the wrapper a Sumatra/Cameroon/Habano hybrid; halfwheel and retailers shorten it to Ecuadorian Sumatra. Retailers list it as medium; halfwheel's review put strength at medium-plus.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (criollo from Condega, Jalapa and Pueblo Nuevo), Dominican Republic (corojo)
cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.about: A regular production RoMa Craft line sold only in the United States, named with a word the company translates as the people around you helping. It has a dark Mexican San Andrés wrapper over a Brazilian binder.
cigars.researchNote: U.S. only because Meerapfel also sells a cigar named Maestranza; it is the counterpart to the overseas Wunder|Lust. Neptune lists it as medium; Cigars Direct and halfwheel's review say medium-full. Halfwheel and retailers also list Honduran filler, which the maker's page does not.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Criollo 98 from Jalapa and Pueblo Nuevo), Dominican Republic (ligeros from La Canela and Santuario)
cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.about: The reworked version of RoMa Craft's first blend, introduced in 2024 with a Pennsylvania broadleaf wrapper in place of the original Connecticut broadleaf. The binder and filler were changed too, and it comes in the same seven core sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Sold simply as CroMagnon; PA marks the Pennsylvania broadleaf blend that replaced the Connecticut broadleaf original. PA bands have white text, the old blend dark gray. Holt's lists it as medium-full, Neptune as full.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.about: RoMa Craft's occasional showpiece release, started in 2013 to show off what the Nica Sueño rollers can do with patterned multi-leaf wrappers. It has no fixed blend, and each release is a different size and set of tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is undisclosed and changes every release; this is a separate series from CRAFT Maquette. CRAFT 2026 is a 5 x 60 gordo with nine tobaccos from six countries, 2,000 boxes of 10, and every cigar in a box looks different. Neptune and Cigars Direct list the 2026 release as medium.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (corojo from La Canela), Nicaragua (criollo from Condega, Estelí and Jalapa)
cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.about: A 2026 limited release in RoMa Craft's CRAFT Maquette series, sold in paper bundles of 10 with ribbons instead of bands. It is the company's first cigar to use tobacco from Ometepe and is named in honor of Estelí tobacco man Carlos Sanchez.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,000 bundles of 10. The blend became the basis for the Marinero bundle line. Neptune's spec lists it as full, though its description says medium to full.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.about: A 2026 limited release in RoMa Craft's CRAFT Maquette series, described as a lighter take on the Intemperance Whiskey Rebellion 1794 blend. It comes in paper bundles of 10.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is undisclosed. Limited to 1,800 bundles of 10 (18,000 cigars). Neptune lists it as medium; no other strength rating was found.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.about: A 2025 limited release in RoMa Craft's CRAFT Maquette series, a short, thick cigar with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over a Cameroon binder. It was sold in paper bundles of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 796 bundles of 10. Neptune lists it as medium; Cigars Direct lists it as mild-medium.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Connecticut with Ecuadorian Habano accents (barber pole)
cigars.about: A 2024 limited release in RoMa Craft's CRAFT Maquette series. It is a corona gorda version of the Aquitaine EMH Frenchy, a barber pole with a Connecticut main wrapper and Habano stripe.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 650 bundles of 10. Halfwheel's review had strength finishing at medium-full; Neptune lists it as full. Halfwheel lists a Nicaraguan binder, Neptune a Cameroon one.

cigars.filler: Honduras (corojo and criollo from Jamastrán), Nicaragua (Condega)
cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.about: A small box-pressed petite corona in RoMa Craft's CRAFT Maquette series, first released in 2025 and the first Maquette to get a second run. It shares its binder and filler with the Riverside 15th Anniversary and the planned CroMagnon Visigoth, with a slightly different wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: First run was 500 bundles of 10; a second run of 1,200 bundles was announced for fall 2026. The blend was kept secret at launch and disclosed later. No maker strength is published; Cigars Direct lists it as full.

cigars.filler: Boatswain: Dominican Republic, Nicaragua. Cockswain: not published
cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Boatswain: Mexican San Andrés. Cockswain: Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed
cigars.about: A bundle line RoMa Craft announced in 2026, built on the CRAFT Maquette El Marinero blend. It comes as one 6 x 60 gordo in two blends, sold in bundles of 25.
cigars.researchNote: Two blends, so there is no single wrapper: Boatswain is San Andrés like El Marinero, Cockswain is Ecuadorian Connecticut over a broadleaf binder. Announced in July 2026 for an August launch at two stores, Caribbean Cigars in Miami and Pipe World in Austin, with others to follow. No strength is published.

cigars.about: A limited robusto made for RoMa Craft co-founder Skip Martin's 50th birthday, blended with Ernesto Perez-Carrillo Jr. and rolled at his factory in the Dominican Republic. It was the first RoMa Craft cigar not made at Nica Sueño.
cigars.researchNote: About 50,000 cigars were made, mostly in boxes of 24. Neptune lists it as medium, Cigars Direct as medium-full. A second Quinquagenario for co-founder Mike Rosales is planned from the Vegas Santiago factory in Costa Rica, with details not yet announced.

cigars.about: Summa is the first all-new regular production blend from Ferio Tego, the company Michael Herklots and Brendon Scott built from the old Nat Sherman cigar portfolio. It is made by the Quesada family in the Dominican Republic and sold in boxes of ten.
cigars.researchNote: Strength varies by source: Cigar Aficionado rates it Medium-Full, Neptune and Famous Smoke list Medium, and Atlantic and Corona list Full. The maker calls it full-bodied, and halfwheel's review found medium to medium-plus strength.

cigars.about: A limited edition toro made with the Miles Davis Estate for the centennial of the musician's birth, named after his 1958 album. Each box of ten includes a reproduction of one of four Miles Davis sketches.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,600 boxes of 10. Strength varies by source: halfwheel's review calls it mild with medium body, Atlantic lists Mild-Medium and Neptune lists Medium. The maker names the producer as Agroindustrias; halfwheel says that is Davidoff's Diadema (Camacho) factory in Honduras.

cigars.about: A limited Ferio Tego line in a 7 x 50 diadema shape, made by the Quesada family in the Dominican Republic. Its first batch was made for the 30th anniversary of World Famous Cigar Bar in Florida.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is undisclosed; Michael Herklots has only said it is completely new. It debuted in December 2025 as 250 boxes of 10 for World Famous Cigar Bar, with a wider release planned for 2026 at select retailers and events.

cigars.about: A full-bodied blend made by Plasencia in Nicaragua with Nicaraguan and Costa Rican filler under an Ecuadorian wrapper. It began as a Nat Sherman Townhouse exclusive and now sits in Ferio Tego's Timeless Collection.
cigars.researchNote: First released by Nat Sherman in 2014; Ferio Tego brought it back in November 2021 with the same blend. The maker lists the wrapper only as Ecuador, while halfwheel names it Ecuadorian Sumatra. halfwheel lists the Belicoso Fino as 5 x 52 and the Secreto as 4 1/2 x 40.

cigars.about: A six-tobacco blend from three countries with a Honduran wrapper, made by the Quesada family in the Dominican Republic. It is the original Nat Sherman Timeless blend, now sold under Ferio Tego in boxes of twenty.
cigars.researchNote: Began as Nat Sherman Timeless in 2011-12, renamed Timeless Prestige in 2018, relaunched by Ferio Tego in September 2021. Strength listings disagree widely: Neptune Medium, Corona Medium to Full, Famous Smoke Full, while halfwheel's review found it mild. The Divino is a short perfecto with a 32/50/36 ring.

cigars.about: A black-banded Nicaraguan puro that Ferio Tego makes each year only for retailers in the Tobacconists' Association of America. It is rolled by Plasencia in Estelí and comes in a single toro size.
cigars.researchNote: An annual release with 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 editions, all 6 x 50 with an Estelí wrapper and Jalapa fillers; the 2025 edition was 900 boxes of 10. It follows the Nat Sherman Timeless TAA 2020. Corona Cigar lists Medium to Full and Neptune lists Full; flavor notes come from halfwheel's review of the 2022 edition.

cigars.about: A limited edition robusto extra made by Quesada in the Dominican Republic to mark ten years of the Timeless line. It shipped in August 2022 in boxes of ten.
cigars.researchNote: The name marks ten years of the Timeless line (a former Nat Sherman brand), not of Ferio Tego. Limited to 2,500 boxes of 10; the band reads Limited 10 Years and some shops list it as Timeless Limited 10 Years. An early trade show preview listed a different blend than the shipped cigar.

cigars.about: A mellow Dominican cigar with a Connecticut shade wrapper, made by the Quesada family. It is one of the original Nat Sherman Metropolitan blends from the mid-1990s, now sold under Ferio Tego.
cigars.researchNote: A Nat Sherman blend from 1995-96, relaunched by Ferio Tego in January 2022. The maker and Famous Smoke give the wrapper as Connecticut, but Neptune calls it Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade. Famous Smoke and Mike's list Mild strength, Corona lists Mild-Medium and Neptune lists Medium.

cigars.about: A smooth Dominican cigar with a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper, made by the Quesada family. Like the Metropolitan Connecticut, it is a Nat Sherman blend from the mid-1990s carried on by Ferio Tego.
cigars.researchNote: A Nat Sherman blend from 1995-96, relaunched by Ferio Tego in January 2022. Neptune and Corona Cigar list Medium strength; Mike's Cigars lists Mild.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro with a habano wrapper, made by Plasencia in Estelí. It joined the Metropolitan family under Nat Sherman in 2016 and continues under Ferio Tego.
cigars.researchNote: First released by Nat Sherman in 2016 and relaunched by Ferio Tego in January 2022. Neptune lists Medium strength and Mike's Cigars lists Full; halfwheel's review of the Nat Sherman version found medium strength. Flavor notes come from that earlier review.

cigars.about: A smooth Honduran cigar with a Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper and a sweetened cap, made at Davidoff's factory in Honduras. It is the maduro version of the long-running Host line that Ferio Tego took over from Nat Sherman.
cigars.researchNote: Has a sweetened cap. A former Nat Sherman Host blend, folded into the Metropolitan Selection in 2018 and relaunched by Ferio Tego in January 2022. The Hudson toro was added in boxes in September 2025.

cigars.about: A limited edition toro marking thirty years of the Metropolitan brand, which began under Nat Sherman in the mid-1990s. It is made by the Quesada family in the Dominican Republic with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,500 boxes of 10. halfwheel's review found medium strength with full flavor; Atlantic Cigar lists it as Medium-Full.

cigars.about: The first cigar in the Y Nada Mas series from the non-Cuban Partagas brand, named for the Dominican city of Santiago. It is rolled at Tabacalera William Ventura rather than at General Cigar Dominicana, where most Partagas are made.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not say where the Habano 2000 wrapper is grown. The maker rates it medium; Famous Smoke lists medium-full. The 6 x 60 is called Gigante by the maker and Gordo by halfwheel and Famous.

cigars.filler: Dominican Habano Vuelta Abajo (HVA), Criollo, Pennsylvania Broadleaf
cigars.about: The second cigar in the Y Nada Mas series from the non-Cuban Partagas brand, named for the Cibao Valley growing region of the Dominican Republic. It is made at Tabacalera La Isla in Santiago and followed the 2025 Santiago blend.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium-full; Neptune lists it as medium. Reached stores in May 2026.

cigars.about: A limited edition non-Cuban Partagas made entirely of Nicaraguan tobacco and rolled at El Titan de Bronze in Miami, the factory the name honors. It came in one corona gorda size, in numbered boxes of 10 signed by the roller.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 5,000 numbered boxes of 10, shipped April 2023. Neptune lists it as medium; halfwheel and Cigar Coop reviews found it starting medium and building to medium-full by the end.

cigars.about: A short, thick Cuban Partagas in the Serie D family, one size down from the well known Serie D No. 4. It began as a 2008 Edicion Limitada and joined the regular range in 2011.
cigars.researchNote: Cuban puro. First sold as a 2008 Edicion Limitada, then made a regular size in 2011. Measures 110 mm by 50.

cigars.about: The smallest cigar in the Cuban Partagas Serie D family, a 50 ring gauge smoke only 90 mm long. It was made as a quick smoke with the full Partagas character, roughly 15 minutes by the maker's account.
cigars.researchNote: Cuban puro. Announced at the Habanos Festival in February 2014. Launched in boxes of 20 and packs of 5.

cigars.about: A thick Cuban Partagas in the Duke format, introduced in 2011 as the first of the Serie E line. The E marks its 54 ring gauge.
cigars.researchNote: Cuban puro. Habanos rates the brand full strength; a 2012 halfwheel review found this cigar medium-plus. A limited Gran Reserva Cosecha 2015 version also exists.

cigars.about: The pyramid of the Cuban Partagas range, added in 2005. Habanos says it quickly became a favorite of smokers who like full flavored cigars, and the P stands for Piramide, its factory name.
cigars.researchNote: Cuban puro. Measures 156 mm by 52. The same pyramid size was first sold as a Partagas limited edition in 2000.

cigars.about: The double corona of the Cuban Partagas brand and one of its classic sizes, named by Habanos among the best known Partagas vitolas. It is a long, full flavored smoke sold in cabinets of 50 as well as smaller boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Cuban puro. Measures 194 mm by 49. A limited Lusitanias Gran Reserva Cosecha 2007 was released in 2013.

cigars.about: A long, slim Cuban Partagas in the Dalia format and one of the classic sizes of the brand. It is named for the way the 25 cigars sit in the box, in rows of eight, nine and eight.
cigars.researchNote: Cuban puro. Measures 170 mm by 43. Sold in boxes of 25, packed in rows of eight, nine and eight.

cigars.about: The first cigar in the Cuban Partagas Linea Maduro, a slightly longer and thicker robusto with a dark, naturally fermented maduro wrapper. It launched in 2015 for La Casa del Habano shops and later became a standard size.
cigars.researchNote: Cuban puro, part of the Linea Maduro. Launched in 2015 as a La Casa del Habano and Habanos Specialist exclusive; Habanos now counts it in the standard range, though the UK distributor still limits it to those shops. Measures 130 mm by 52.

cigars.about: The only figurado in the Cuban Partagas Linea Maduro, a short pyramid and the shortest and thickest of the three sizes. It was launched in 2018 with a dark, naturally fermented maduro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Cuban puro, part of the Linea Maduro. Measures 120 mm by 55, a size created for this cigar. The pepper, toast, berry and nut notes come from a halfwheel review of preproduction samples.

cigars.about: The longest of the three cigars in the Cuban Partagas Linea Maduro, launched in 2018 in a size that was new at the time. Its dark maduro wrapper adds a light sweetness to the usual full Partagas taste.
cigars.researchNote: Cuban puro, part of the Linea Maduro. Measures 145 mm by 50; the factory name of the size is also Maduro No. 3.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Sumatra (the maker calls it Sumatra Maduro)
cigars.about: The fourth regular production line from Stolen Throne, named for the company's headquarters town of Yorktown, Virginia. It is rolled at Noel Rojas' factory in Esteli and sold in 20-count bundles.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the wrapper as Sumatra Maduro, while halfwheel lists Ecuadorian Sumatra. Cigar Federation sells it as medium-full and Famous Smoke as full, but halfwheel and Developing Palates both found it closer to medium.

cigars.about: A regular production line from Stolen Throne that shipped in June 2025. The name and band refer to founder Lee Marsh's childhood address in the Essex area of Baltimore.
cigars.researchNote: Strength, body and flavors come from the Developing Palates team review of the Belicoso, not from the maker. Famous Smoke also lists it as medium.

cigars.about: Stolen Throne's first nationwide limited edition, a single petit belicoso shown at PCA 2022 and shipped that December. It was limited to 1,500 boxes of 10 and is named for a Celtic deity of war and death.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists a Mexican binder, while halfwheel, Neptune and Cigar Federation list a Nicaraguan binder. Cigar Federation sells it as full-bodied and medium strength, and the halfwheel reviewer found the strength mild.

cigars.about: A Stolen Throne limited cigar that began as an exclusive for the shop Winston's Humidor, with proceeds going to animal rescue groups. It was the first cigar dedicated to founder Lee Marsh's family dog.
cigars.researchNote: Shop exclusive for Winston's Humidor. The maker does not publish the size, strength, release year or the origin of the wrapper.

cigars.about: A Stolen Throne shop exclusive made for Up Down Cigar in Chicago. The maker describes it as a Habano-wrapped cigar with sweetness, spice and a long savory finish.
cigars.researchNote: Shop exclusive for Up Down Cigar in Chicago. The maker only says it is a Habano cigar and does not publish the binder, filler, size, strength or release year.

cigars.about: A limited edition 6 x 46 that Stolen Throne made as an exclusive for the Cigar Federation store, blended with Noel Rojas. The maker describes it as full-bodied and medium in strength.
cigars.researchNote: Cigar Federation exclusive, limited to 1,895 cigars. The binder and filler are only described as Nicaraguan plus other undisclosed tobaccos. The maker calls the size a corona and the retailer calls it a skinny toro.

cigars.about: A limited edition toro that Stolen Throne made as an exclusive for the Cigar Federation store, blended with Noel Rojas. It pairs Nicaraguan and Peruvian fillers with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Cigar Federation exclusive, limited to 910 cigars. The binder is not published. Size, strength and tasting notes come from the Cigar Federation listing, which calls it full-bodied and medium strength.

cigars.about: A limited edition corona made to mark the 150th running of the Preakness Stakes in Baltimore, founder Lee Marsh's hometown. It shipped in April 2025 and was limited to 3,000 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Strength and body are from the halfwheel review, which found it mild in strength and medium in body. Famous Smoke lists it as medium-full. No maker strength rating was found.

cigars.about: A 2026 limited release toro and the first Stolen Throne cigar made with a shaggy foot. It comes in 10-count bundles, with 10,000 cigars made.
cigars.researchNote: Shown at PCA 2026 and shipped to stores in September 2026. No strength rating or tasting notes have been published.

cigars.about: A 2026 limited release built on the Preakness 150 blend, reworked for more strength and body. It comes in a single 5 x 54 size in 10-count bundles, with 10,000 cigars made.
cigars.researchNote: Based on the Preakness 150 blend but stronger, per the company. Announced at PCA 2026 for a May 2026 release. halfwheel gives the size as 5 x 54 with no vitola name, and no strength rating or tasting notes have been published.

cigars.about: A 2026 limited release belicoso named after founder Lee Marsh's family dog, the second cigar dedicated to him after Argos. Production was announced at 10,000 cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Announced at PCA 2026 with a September 2026 release date. No strength rating or tasting notes have been published.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro from Plasencia that puts a lighter, long-aged Colorado Claro wrapper from Jalapa on the Alma Fuerte line. It began in late 2020 with the six-sided Sixto I Hexagon and has since grown to four sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The brand is spelled Plasencia. The maker's site also calls this line Alma Fuerte Natural. The maker calls it medium to full-bodied and shows 3.5 of 5 on its strength meter, Neptune lists medium strength, and halfwheel found the strength just under medium.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro from Plasencia made entirely with tobacco certified organic by the OCIA, which the maker says no other cigar can claim. It was introduced in 2017 when the family launched its own brand in the U.S.
cigars.researchNote: The brand is spelled Plasencia. The maker only gives the wrapper as Nicaraguan, while Neptune calls it a maduro. Retailers and halfwheel call it medium, though the maker's own strength meter shows 2 of 5. Neptune also lists a Corona (6 1/4 x 44) and a Churchill (7 x 48) that are not on the maker's current size list.

cigars.about: A 2026 limited edition from Plasencia tied to the 2026 World Cup and the second cigar in its Mundial series after Ehtefal. It is the first Plasencia blend to combine certified organic tobacco from both Honduras and Nicaragua, and 5,000 numbered boxes of 10 were made.
cigars.researchNote: The brand is spelled Plasencia. The maker rates strength and body as medium, halfwheel found both a little above medium, and Famous Smoke lists medium-full. Neptune lists the wrapper shade as Colorado, and the maker does not name the seed.

cigars.about: A limited edition Plasencia toro that debuted in Doha, Qatar in November 2022, the night before the World Cup opened there. The name is Arabic for celebration, the fillers were aged 10 years, and 5,000 boxes of 10 were made with half going to the U.S.
cigars.researchNote: The brand is spelled Plasencia. Neptune and the halfwheel article text say the filler is Honduran and Nicaraguan, while halfwheel's spec table lists Nicaragua only. It was the first cigar in what Plasencia now calls its Mundial series.

cigars.about: The first of Plasencia's yearly Lunar New Year cigars, a Nicaraguan puro salomon released in February 2021. It was limited to 2,500 boxes of eight and was sold only outside the United States.
cigars.researchNote: The brand is spelled Plasencia. This release was an international exclusive and was not sold to U.S. retailers. Strength and flavors come from the halfwheel review.

cigars.about: Plasencia's second Lunar New Year cigar and the first one sold in the U.S., a Nicaraguan puro using tobacco aged up to 10 years. It came out in early 2022 in eight-count boxes, with 6,250 boxes made and 2,500 of them for U.S. stores.
cigars.researchNote: The brand is spelled Plasencia. The maker called it medium strength and medium-bodied, but the halfwheel reviewer found the strength built to full by the end. Neptune describes a dark maduro wrapper, while halfwheel saw a standard brown one.

cigars.about: Plasencia's third Lunar New Year cigar, a Nicaraguan puro built mainly on tobacco from Jalapa. It was released in January 2023 and limited to 6,000 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: The brand is spelled Plasencia. Neptune lists medium strength and a Colorado shade wrapper. The halfwheel review found the strength growing from medium to medium-full.

cigars.about: Plasencia's fourth Lunar New Year cigar, a torpedo made entirely from Nicaraguan tobacco grown on the family's own farms. It shipped in February 2024 and was limited to 3,000 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: The brand is spelled Plasencia. Sources disagree on length: halfwheel's news story says 6 1/4 x 54, while Neptune and halfwheel's series list say 6 1/2 x 54. Strength is Neptune's rating, and no tasting notes were published by a source checked.

cigars.line: El Año de la Culebra Edición Limitada 2025
cigars.about: Plasencia's fifth Lunar New Year cigar, a Nicaraguan puro for the 2025 Year of the Snake. Each box holds eight straight lanceros plus two twisted into a culebra, and 6,000 boxes were made with half going to the U.S.
cigars.researchNote: The brand is spelled Plasencia. It shipped in December 2024 for the 2025 lunar year. Famous Smoke lists it as medium-full and Neptune as full, but the halfwheel reviewer found the strength under medium, with medium body.

cigars.about: Plasencia's sixth Lunar New Year cigar, made for the 2026 Year of the Horse. It is a large 7 x 58 with a braided strand of tobacco at the cap meant to look like a horse's tail, limited to 6,000 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: The brand is spelled Plasencia. It shipped in late 2025 for the 2026 lunar year. Famous Smoke lists it as medium-full and Neptune as full, while the halfwheel review found the strength medium rising to just above, with medium body.

cigars.line: Alma del Fuego Ometepe Edición Limitada
cigars.about: A 2024 limited edition of Plasencia's Alma del Fuego that the company says is the first cigar with a wrapper grown on the volcanic island of Ometepe. It is a box-pressed torpedo sold in glass tubes at $100 each, with 1,000 boxes of 20 made.
cigars.researchNote: The brand is spelled Plasencia. This is a limited edition of the regular Alma del Fuego line. halfwheel gives the size as 6 x 54 while Neptune lists 6 1/2 x 54. The binder and filler regions are not disclosed.

cigars.about: A sweet-tipped Connecticut Shade cigar from Dapper Cigar Co., reworked from a house blend made for Cigars Ltd. in Fresno. It is rolled at NACSA in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: The cap is sweetened, and Dapper's site calls it Cubata Cru Shade. A rum-sweetened Cubata Cru made at La Aurora came out in 2018; this NACSA version launched in 2022. Dapper's site labels the 4 1/2 x 40 Bumbo, halfwheel calls it Blimey.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Jalapa, Esteli), USA (Connecticut Broadleaf), one undisclosed leaf
cigars.about: Dapper Cigar Co.'s fuller blend, developed by founder Ian Reith with Raul Disla of NACSA and Oliva Tobacco Co. The name is Cuban Spanish for those without hope.
cigars.researchNote: Dapper rates it full in strength; halfwheel's reviewer found it closer to medium. One filler leaf and the binder variety are undisclosed.

cigars.about: A remake of Dapper's Desvalido blended by Raul Disla, production manager at NACSA, to suit his own taste. It is described as more Nicaraguan and bolder than the original.
cigars.researchNote: Dapper has not published the blend. Halfwheel reported Ecuadorian Habano over Nicaraguan binder and filler at the 2022 trade show, then listed it as undisclosed in its review. Neptune shows a USA binder and is the source for strength.

cigars.about: The broadleaf-wrapped version of Dapper's El Borracho, built on the original San Andres blend with extra Nicaraguan ligero. All sizes are box-pressed.
cigars.researchNote: Launched as El Borracho Maduro and renamed El Borracho Broadleaf in 2022, so older boxes and some retailers still say Maduro.

cigars.about: The Connecticut Shade follow-up to La Madrina, Dapper's most requested cigar, built on the original blend with a few components changed. It is fuller than a typical shade cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Dapper lists the binder as undisclosed; halfwheel and Neptune report Mexican San Andres. Dapper rates it medium-full to full, but halfwheel's reviewer found the nicotine strength mild-medium with full flavor.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Jalapa and one undisclosed), USA (Connecticut Broadleaf and one undisclosed)
cigars.about: A bolder extension of Dapper's Siempre Sun Grown, first released through Small Batch Cigar in 2020. It was blended by Ian Reith with Raul Disla at NACSA.
cigars.researchNote: The 5 5/8 x 46 corona gorda is a Small Batch Cigar exclusive; the other three sizes go to all retailers.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade, U.S. Connecticut Broadleaf, or a barber pole of both
cigars.about: A small 4 x 38 long-filler cigar from Dapper with a lightly sweetened tip, sold from a 150-count display in three wrapper options. It was made as a quick break-time smoke.
cigars.researchNote: One size in three wrappers, so there is no single wrapper type. All three have a sweetened tip. Dapper has not published tasting notes.

cigars.about: Dapper's budget mixed-filler bundle cigar, named for founder Ian Reith's father, a retired Air Force major. This is the Connecticut Shade version.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed long and short filler made from tobaccos used in Dapper's other blends plus some Honduran leaf; the exact filler is proprietary. Sold unbanded in bundles of 20. The Habano version shares the same binder and filler.

cigars.about: Dapper's budget mixed-filler bundle cigar in its Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. The artwork honors founder Ian Reith's grandfather, an Army major.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed long and short filler made from tobaccos used in Dapper's other blends plus some Honduran leaf; the exact filler is proprietary. Sold unbanded in bundles of 20. The Connecticut Shade version shares the same binder and filler.

cigars.about: A limited cigar marking Dapper Cigar Co.'s tenth year, aged about a year after rolling. Unlike Dapper's Nicaraguan lines, it is made in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,000 boxes of 10. A 4 1/2 x 54 Robusto Grande (200 boxes) was also made; half went to the anniversary party at Cigars Ltd. in Fresno. Strength and flavors are from halfwheel's review, which put strength at medium-plus.

cigars.about: A box-pressed perfecto made by Dapper Cigar Co. with HolySmoke, a cigar-themed Bible study group. It was Dapper's first limited edition and first figurado.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 10,000 cigars in boxes of 12. The perfecto tapers from a 28 ring foot to 52 at its widest. Strength, body and flavors are from halfwheel's review.

cigars.about: La Palina's 125th anniversary cigar, a Nicaraguan puro made by Oliva from its private stock of vintage tobacco. It debuted in glass jars of 37 and later came in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: La Palina keeps the blend secret beyond saying it is all Nicaraguan. Halfwheel and retailers list the toro at 6 1/2 x 52; La Palina's site shows 6 1/4 x 54. It debuted as 300 jars of 37 and now returns in small boxed batches (500 boxes in 2025), though halfwheel calls it ongoing production.

cigars.about: A box-pressed line made by Oliva for La Palina to mark chairman Bill Paley's 75th birthday; 1948 is his birth year. The binder and filler come from Oliva's farms.
cigars.researchNote: La Palina also calls it El Año 1948. Halfwheel lists the three sizes as regular production, but La Palina says it is released yearly in limited quantities. A 6 x 46 Diadema was a 500-box exclusive for retailers at the 2023 trade show.

cigars.about: One of the blends in La Palina's value-priced Classic line, with a reddish Honduran wrapper. It arrived when the Classic line was revamped in 2017.
cigars.researchNote: It launched at General Cigar Dominicana in 2017; by late 2019 halfwheel reported the Classic line was made at STG's Danli factory in Honduras, and Neptune lists Honduras. La Palina calls it medium-bodied while Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.about: La Palina's value-priced 6 x 60, sold in boxes of 50. It comes in one size only.
cigars.researchNote: Blend is from La Palina's site. Halfwheel lists Dominican and Nicaraguan filler with an undisclosed binder. La Palina never named the factory; Honduras and Raices Cubanas come from Neptune's listing only, so treat them as unconfirmed.

cigars.about: The reblended return of La Palina's first line, rolled at El Titan de Bronze in Miami. The sizes are named for Bill Paley's mother, wife and father.
cigars.researchNote: The original Family Series (2009) was made at Graycliff in the Bahamas; the Miami version replaced it in 2015. Halfwheel listed the Pasha at 7 1/4 x 50 at launch; La Palina and Neptune now show 7 x 50. Strength is from Neptune.

cigars.about: The first in a new La Palina Family Series of limited editions honoring people the company has worked with over the years. It is made at Hostos Fernandez's Tabacalera La Isla.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,000 boxes of 10 in one size. Strength is from Neptune's listing, which shows Dominican filler only; halfwheel lists Dominican and Nicaraguan. No tasting notes have been published yet.

cigars.about: La Palina's green candela-wrapped cigar, whose name means green fire. It comes in a single robusto size and is tied to St. Patrick's Day.
cigars.researchNote: Made in limited seasonal runs around St. Patrick's Day rather than year-round; the 2018 run was 500 boxes of 20. Strength is from Neptune's listing. Halfwheel reported it as new in 2017, while Cigar Aficionado dates it to 2016.

cigars.about: La Palina's Kill Bill line, named after owner Bill Paley could not finish the strong first prototype. It began in 2012 as a petit corona in the El Diario line and was relaunched in 2021 as a four-size series.
cigars.researchNote: KB stands for Kill Bill, and Parts Three and Four have extra ligero. La Palina's site calls the wrapper Honduran Rosado, halfwheel Honduran Corojo. Neptune tags it medium but describes it as full strength, and halfwheel's review found it building to full.

cigars.about: Named for La Palina founder Sam Paley, whose factory workers called him Mr. Sam. It is rolled in Miami at El Titan de Bronze.
cigars.researchNote: It began in 2013 as a limited 850-box robusto and became regular production in 2014, though output from the small Miami factory stays limited. La Palina calls it medium to full; Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.about: The fullest cigar in La Palina's Label Series, made in Danli, Honduras. It started as a 2019 exclusive for Tobacconists' Association of America shops and went to all retailers in 2020.
cigars.researchNote: La Palina describes the wrapper as Cuban-seed Honduran Oscuro; halfwheel called it Honduran habano. The original 2019 TAA release was a single 6 x 52 toro limited to 1,000 boxes.

cigars.about: The mild, creamy entry in La Palina's Label Series. It began in 2021 as a toro exclusive to Tobacconists' Association of America shops and was opened to all retailers in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: La Palina's site gives the blend above; the 2021 launch version had a Honduran-grown Connecticut wrapper and San Andres binder. Halfwheel placed it at an undisclosed Nicaraguan factory, while Neptune says Honduras. Sizes follow halfwheel, and La Palina's site lists different ones.

cigars.about: A medium-strength Corojo-wrapped line from Noel Rojas, named after the Texas bluebonnet flower. Rojas keeps the line to ring gauges of 50 and under.
cigars.researchNote: Famous and Neptune list an Ecuadorian Corojo wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, while Atlantic calls the cigar a Corojo puro. Atlantic also lists the Toro at 6 x 52 instead of 6 x 50.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped version of Rojas Breakfast Tacos, a small perfecto made as a roughly 30 minute smoke. The binder and filler are Nicaraguan tobaccos grown by Rojas.
cigars.researchNote: One of three Breakfast Tacos wrappers (Connecticut, Maduro, Sumatra). It launched at 4 1/2 x 46 and moved to a 50 ring gauge in late 2023; Famous still lists 4 1/2 x 44. Strength is the Famous rating.

cigars.about: The San Andrés maduro version of Rojas Breakfast Tacos, a small perfecto made as a roughly 30 minute smoke. The binder and filler are Nicaraguan tobaccos grown by Rojas.
cigars.researchNote: One of three Breakfast Tacos wrappers. It launched at 4 1/2 x 46 and moved to a 50 ring gauge in late 2023; Famous still lists 4 1/2 x 44. Famous rates it full and the halfwheel review found the strength medium-full to full.

cigars.about: The Sumatra-wrapped version of Rojas Breakfast Tacos, a small perfecto made as a roughly 30 minute smoke. The binder and filler are Nicaraguan tobaccos grown by Rojas.
cigars.researchNote: One of three Breakfast Tacos wrappers. It launched at 4 1/2 x 46 and moved to a 50 ring gauge in late 2023; Famous still lists 4 1/2 x 44. Strength is the Famous rating.

cigars.about: The fourth blend in the Rojas Street Tacos series and the third in regular production, named after the spit-roasted pork taco filling. It pairs an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper with a Mexican San Andrés binder.
cigars.researchNote: No strength is published. The halfwheel review had it starting at medium and finishing full, with medium-full body.

cigars.about: An annual limited edition in the Rojas Street Tacos series, released each spring for Cinco de Mayo since 2024. Rojas says about 80 percent of the filler is Connecticut broadleaf aged seven years.
cigars.researchNote: Released yearly: 2024 was 6 x 52 (35,000 cigars), 2025 was 6 x 54 (50,000) and 2026 is 6 x 54 (40,000). No strength is published. The halfwheel reviews found the 2024 mild and the 2025 medium to medium-full.

cigars.about: A single-size limited edition marking ten years since Noel Rojas opened his own factory. It uses an Ecuadorian Habano Maduro wrapper from Oliva Tobacco Co. over filler Rojas grew in three regions of Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 3,500 boxes of 10. Rojas described it as medium to full, while Famous lists it as full. halfwheel reports all-Nicaraguan filler, but Famous also mentions tobacco from Costa Rica and Panama, and the binder is not published.

cigars.about: A regular production Connecticut-wrapped line Rojas introduced at the 2026 PCA show, blended to be the first cigar of the day. It comes in the same core sizes as the main Rojas line.
cigars.researchNote: Famous calls it mild to medium. The halfwheel review found the strength mild with medium body.

cigars.about: KSG stands for King of the Small Gauge, a limited Rojas line kept to thin ring gauges. The blend is built around tobacco from the Somoto region of Nicaragua under an aged Ecuadorian maduro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Released in small runs: a 7 1/2 x 38 Lancero in 2020 (5,000 cigars) and a 6 1/4 x 42 Lonsdale in 2022 (1,000 boxes). The 2020 run was made at Tabacalera Flor de San Luis and the 2022 run at Rojas Cigar Factory. Neptune lists medium strength, and halfwheel found medium to medium-plus with full body.

cigars.about: Budget-priced factory overrun cigars sold under the Rojas name by Famous Smoke Shop. Famous says they come from the same maker as Street Tacos and Unfinished Business, and the blends are not named.
cigars.researchNote: Only Famous Smoke Shop lists these, and its specs are the only source. The blends are not named, so the binder is unpublished and the cigars may vary from batch to batch.

cigars.about: The second line from My Father's Honduran factory, after My Father Blue. The name means loyalty, and the blend uses an Ecuadorian Rosado Oscuro wrapper over Honduran and Nicaraguan tobaccos from the Garcia family farms.
cigars.researchNote: My Father calls the wrapper Ecuador Rosado Oscuro and rates the blend 3/4 to full body; halfwheel calls the wrapper Habano Oscuro Rosado. Holt's lists medium-full, while the halfwheel review found the strength closer to medium.

cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped extension of the broadleaf Jaime Garcia Reserva Especial, made by My Father Cigars. It began in 2012 as a New England regional release and went nationwide in 2024.
cigars.researchNote: My Father describes it as a full flavor, mild to medium blend, while Holt's lists it as medium. The 2012 regional release used slightly different sizes.

cigars.line: Jaime Garcia Reserva Especial Sucesor Limited Edition 2024
cigars.about: A 2024 limited edition under the Jaime Garcia Reserva Especial brand from My Father Cigars. It comes in two box-pressed sizes that each use a different wrapper over the same Nicaraguan blend.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper depends on the size: the 6 x 56 Toro is Sumatra-seed and the 6 1/8 x 52 Torpedo is Habano-seed, both grown in Nicaragua per Neptune. Retailers disagree on strength: Holt's says medium-full and Neptune says medium.

cigars.line: Flor de Las Antillas San Andres
cigars.about: A Mexican San Andrés-wrapped version of My Father's Flor de las Antillas that first reached Tobacconists' Association of America member stores in November 2025. It comes in two pressed sizes.
cigars.researchNote: My Father has not published the blend or where it is made. Atlantic and Neptune list Nicaraguan binder and filler, but halfwheel found another retailer listing Honduran. Atlantic rates it medium-full and Neptune full, and Atlantic calls it limited while halfwheel lists regular production.

cigars.line: Flor de las Antillas 10th Anniversary Limited Edition 2022
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan (a darker, higher priming than the regular line)
cigars.about: A limited edition Nicaraguan puro marking ten years of My Father's Flor de las Antillas. It uses a modified version of the original blend with a darker, higher priming wrapper, all from Garcia family tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 5,000 numbered boxes of 12, each cigar in its own coffin. It carries a 2022 name but did not ship until January 2023. Holt's lists it as full, while the halfwheel review found it starting near medium and ending just under full.

cigars.about: A limited edition of My Father Le Bijou 1922 created for what would have been the 100th birthday of Pepin Garcia's father, born in 1922. It first shipped in 2022 and has returned every two years.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel reports an all-Nicaraguan blend with a dark wrapper My Father calls Habano My Father, while Holt's lists the wrapper as Ecuador Habano Oscuro. Released in 2022, 2024 and 2026, limited to 1,922 boxes of 22 per size. Strength is the Holt's rating.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Varies by blend: Ecuadorian Habano and Connecticut Broadleaf (My Father blends), Nicaraguan Corojo 99 and Ecuadorian Sumatra (Tatuaje blends)
cigars.about: A limited collaboration between My Father and Tatuaje marking 20 years of the Garcia family making Pete Johnson's cigars. Each side blended two cigars for the other, sold together in 40-count humidor boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Four blends, all 7 1/4 x 50 with a 109-style cap. Black Humidor (2024): Ecuadorian Habano from My Father and Nicaraguan Corojo 99 from Tatuaje. Red Humidor (2025): Connecticut Broadleaf from My Father and Ecuadorian Sumatra from Tatuaje, with 1,500 boxes per color at $2,400.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made for the 70th birthday of Jose Pepin Garcia and sold only with an Elie Bleu humidor. All the tobacco comes from My Father's own farms, under a Corojo 99 wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Only 75 numbered humidors were made, 70 of them for retail, each sold with 100 cigars for $10,000. My Father describes the cigar as 3/4 to full body.

cigars.about: A small-batch soft-pressed toro blended by Jose Pepin Garcia for Holt's annual Pepin Mania events. It uses a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over Nicaraguan filler from Garcia family farms and is aged three extra years.
cigars.researchNote: A Holt's exclusive, and Holt's is the only source for the blend. The binder, the wrapper's growing country and the release year are not published.

cigars.about: A limited toro blended by Jose Pepin Garcia to mark ten years of Holt's annual Pepin Mania events. It has a San Andrés Oscuro wrapper over Nicaraguan filler from Garcia family farms and is aged three years after rolling.
cigars.researchNote: A Holt's exclusive, and Holt's is the only source for the blend. The binder, factory and release year are not published.

cigars.about: The second Protocol line from Cubariqueño Cigar Co., a Mexican San Andrés maduro over Nicaraguan binder and filler made at Erik Espinosa's La Zona factory in Estelí. It is known by its red band and is the darker counterpart to the original Protocol Blue.
cigars.researchNote: Often sold as Protocol Red. The maker calls it medium strength with full flavor; halfwheel's reviewer found it closer to medium-full. A Lancero was added in 2017 and a Corona Gorda in 2018; some retailers no longer list the Robusto.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro with a habano rosado wrapper, made at La Zona in Estelí as the fifth core Protocol line. It is named for co-owner Kevin Keithan's work in internet security and wears a neon green band.
cigars.researchNote: Smoke Inn lists it Medium-Full; Cigar Dojo's review called it medium-plus in strength and medium-full in body.

cigars.about: A 2025 Protocol release honoring forensic investigators and the brand's first cigar with a Connecticut broadleaf wrapper. It is made at La Zona in a single 6 1/2 x 50 size.
cigars.researchNote: First run was 150 boxes of 10. The maker says more may follow if it can get enough broadleaf wrapper. Strength is from one retailer listing only.

cigars.about: The natural-wrapper half of the second release in Protocol's Lawmen Series, named for the Prohibition agent who pursued Al Capone. It is a Nicaraguan puro rolled at AJ Fernandez's San Lotano factory and was the first Protocol blend made without ligero.
cigars.researchNote: The maker gives no strength rating. halfwheel's review found it between mild and medium, which fits the no-ligero blend. Announced in 2020, shipped March 2021.

cigars.about: The maduro half of Protocol's Eliot Ness, part of the Lawmen Series. It uses a rarely seen Nicaraguan-grown broadleaf wrapper over Nicaraguan habano binder and corojo filler, with no ligero, and is rolled at AJ Fernandez's San Lotano factory.
cigars.researchNote: The maker gives no strength rating. Strength and body are from Cigar Dojo's review, which put it at medium, building to medium-full at the end.

cigars.about: The natural version of the third Lawmen Series release, named for Bass Reeves, one of the first Black deputy U.S. Marshals, who served west of the Mississippi. It pairs an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler and is rolled at AJ Fernandez's San Lotano factory.
cigars.researchNote: Smoke Inn lists Medium-Full for the line but describes the Natural as medium-plus, so it sits a touch under the Maduro. No maker strength rating was found.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Protocol's Bass Reeves in the Lawmen Series, a Nicaraguan puro with a dark habano wrapper. It is rolled at AJ Fernandez's San Lotano factory in Ocotal.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is from one retailer listing only. A 5 x 52 robusto called Oklahoma Territory was a 2024 limited exclusive for Omerta Cigar Co.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Estelí ligero, Estelí corojo viso, Condega viso)
cigars.about: The natural version of the fourth Lawmen Series release, honoring Phoebe Couzins, the first woman to serve as a U.S. Marshal. It has an Ecuadorian Sumatra rosado wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos and is rolled at the San Lotano factory.
cigars.researchNote: Strength and body are from Cigar Dojo's review (medium). Smoke Inn lists the line as Medium-Full and describes the Natural as medium-plus.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Condega ligero, Estelí viso, Jalapa corojo viso)
cigars.about: The maduro version of Protocol's Phoebe Couzins in the Lawmen Series, a Nicaraguan puro with a habano oscuro wrapper. It is rolled at the San Lotano factory in Ocotal.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is a dark habano oscuro, not broadleaf. Strength is from one retailer listing only.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Estelí viso, Ometepe viso), USA (Pennsylvania ligero)
cigars.about: The third Protocol and Cigar Dojo collaboration, after K9 and Night Stick, sold only through Smoke Inn in March 2021. It is a 5 x 52 robusto with a double pigtail cap meant to look like a taser's two electrodes.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 500 bundles of 10, which sold out on release day. No strength rating was published; Cigar Dojo described it as medium-full in body and full in flavor.

cigars.about: The fifth blend in Micallef's value-priced Color Series, built around a Brazilian mata fina wrapper. It is made at the company's own factory in Estelí in the series' two standard sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker says medium to full; Smoke Inn lists Medium and Neptune lists Full. The maker and halfwheel give Nicaraguan filler, while Smoke Inn adds Dominican and Mexican. Smoke Inn also has an exclusive 6 1/2 x 54 box-pressed toro.

cigars.about: The seventh blend in Micallef's Color Series, with a Connecticut-seed wrapper over a Mexican San Andrés binder and Nicaraguan and Dominican filler. It launched at Two Guys Cigars in late August 2026 and reached stores nationwide in early September.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not say where the wrapper is grown; Neptune lists it as Ecuadorian Connecticut. The maker says medium strength, while Smoke Inn lists Mild-Medium. No tasting notes have been published yet.

cigars.about: The fourth blend in Micallef's Color Series, introduced at PCA 2025. It uses the same San Andrés Sumatra wrapper type as the Blue and a broadleaf binder like the Red.
cigars.researchNote: The maker and Neptune say medium; Smoke Inn lists Medium-Full. The wrapper is Sumatra seed grown in Mexico's San Andrés valley. The maker lists the binder only as broadleaf, while Neptune calls it Nicaraguan broadleaf.

cigars.about: The mildest blend in Micallef's Color Series, a Connecticut-seed wrapper over a Connecticut broadleaf binder, released in early 2026. It is made at the company's factory in Nicaragua in the series' two standard sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not say where the wrapper is grown; Neptune lists Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade. The maker says mild, while Smoke Inn lists Mild-Medium. Smoke Inn has an exclusive 6 1/2 x 54 box-pressed toro.

cigars.filler: Mixed filler from trimmings of the other Color Series blends
cigars.about: A budget, mixed-filler cigar in Micallef's Color Series, released in 2026 and sold in bundles of 20. The filler is made from the leftover cuts of the other Color Series blends under a Sumatra-seed wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: It is a mixed-filler (Cuban sandwich) cigar sold in bundles of 20, not long filler. The maker says mild to medium; Neptune and Smoke Inn list Medium. The maker calls the wrapper San Andrés Sumatra, while halfwheel lists its origin as undisclosed.

cigars.about: Micallef's Ecuadorian Connecticut blend, made with the Gomez Sanchez family in Estelí using a wrapper aged four years. It smokes fuller and spicier than most Connecticut-wrapped cigars.
cigars.researchNote: The maker says medium, Smoke Inn lists Mild-Medium, and halfwheel's reviewer found it closer to medium-full with a lot of spice. The maker's site now shows only 5 x 40 and 5 x 52; the Toro and Gordo are still at some retailers.

cigars.about: A medium, creamy Micallef blend with a Sumatra-seed wrapper grown in San Andrés, Mexico, over an Ecuadorian habano binder. It is one of the company's core lines and is notable for using Panamanian tobacco in the filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's site lists Honduran, Dominican and Panamanian filler; halfwheel and Smoke Inn list Nicaraguan, Dominican and Panamanian. Some retailers also carry a 6 x 60 Gordo. Neptune lists the line simply as Experiencia.

cigars.about: Micallef's highest-priced blend and the cigar the brand started with, first made for founder Al Micallef by the Gomez Sanchez family. It has a San Andrés habano wrapper and sells in five-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as Reserva Limitada Privada (Smoke Inn) or Reserva Privada (Neptune). It began as a 7 x 52 only; the Toro was added in 2019 and the 5 x 40 Londres came from the 2022 Collectors Edition sampler.

cigars.about: Micallef's value-priced, box-pressed line, named for the cigar rollers. It is a mild to medium smoke with a Sumatra-seed San Andrés wrapper over a Honduran binder.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune describes it as a mixed-filler cigar and lists it as Mild; the maker says mild to medium. No release year was found in a reliable source.

cigars.about: The box-pressed Sumatra-wrapped blend in Micallef's five-line Grande Bold series from 2018, and the only one the maker rated medium-full instead of full. Micallef discontinued the whole Grande Bold family in January 2023.
cigars.researchNote: Discontinued in January 2023; only leftover retail stock remains. The maker rated it medium-full, while Neptune lists Medium. halfwheel gives a Honduran binder and Neptune a broadleaf binder.

cigars.about: A box-pressed version of the Camacho Connecticut, made by Davidoff's Camacho factory in Honduras. Pennsylvania broadleaf was added to the filler to give the blend more intensity.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists the wrapper as USA Connecticut Shade, but Cigar Aficionado and Cigar Coop both say Ecuadorian Connecticut.

cigars.about: A box-pressed version of the Camacho Corojo, the all-Honduran corojo blend the brand is known for. Pennsylvania broadleaf ligero was added to the filler for extra punch.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers list it as full strength, but halfwheel's review called it medium-plus.

cigars.about: A box-pressed version of the Camacho Ecuador, made by Davidoff's Camacho factory in Honduras. Pennsylvania broadleaf was added to the filler to make the blend more intense.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on strength: Mike's Cigars lists it as medium to full, Neptune lists it as full. It launched in three sizes, but Neptune now shows only the Toro.

cigars.about: The first release in Camacho's limited Factory Unleashed series, a toro with an unfinished shaggy foot so the filler burns on its own before the wrapper. It was sold in 10-count bundles and 100-count crates.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 125,000 cigars. Halfwheel's review put strength at medium-full; Neptune lists it as full. Each Factory Unleashed release is a different blend.

cigars.about: The second Factory Unleashed release, a shaggy-foot toro with a completely different blend from the first: an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over corojo fillers. It was sold in 10-count bundles and 100-count crates.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 125,000 cigars. Sources disagree on strength: Neptune lists it as full, but halfwheel's review found it mild to medium.

cigars.about: The third Factory Unleashed release, a shaggy-foot toro with a Mexican San Andres wrapper. Like the first two, it was sold in 10-count bundles and 100-count crates.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 125,000 cigars. Halfwheel's review had it starting at medium and finishing just under full; Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.about: Camacho's annual limited edition, released around the Fourth of July from 2002 through 2021 and usually sold in individual coffins. Most years used the brand's 11/18 perfecto shape.
cigars.researchNote: This is a series, not one blend: the blend changed with each year's release, so there is no single wrapper or strength. The 11/18 perfecto measures 6 x 48/54/48. Davidoff called the 2021 release the last, then brought the name back in 2026 with the Liberty 250.

cigars.about: A 2026 return of the Camacho Liberty name, made for the 250th anniversary of the United States. It comes in red, white or blue bundles of 10, all holding the same cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Not sold at retail: it is only handed out at Davidoff's Red, White & Beef Experience events, with a pairing or a qualifying purchase. The type of American wrapper leaf and the production number have not been published.

cigars.about: The first cigar in Camacho's Limited Edition series, which launched after the Liberty Series ended. It is a single toro packed in aluminum tins and dedicated to the blenders at the Camacho factory.
cigars.researchNote: Production numbers were not disclosed. Halfwheel's review had strength building from medium-plus to full by the end.

cigars.about: The second release in Camacho's yearly Limited Edition series, with a new blend in the brand's 11/18 perfecto shape. It is dedicated to the master blenders at the Camacho factory.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 60,000 cigars in boxes of 15. Davidoff calls it medium intensity and the press release says medium-plus. The exact wrapper varietal is not published, only that it is Ecuadorian.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano from Jacagua, Criollo 98 from La Canela)
cigars.about: La Galera's first Cameroon-wrapped line, made by Jochy Blanco at Tabacalera Palma with Dominican binder and filler from the family's own farms. It wears a jade green biodegradable band.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel lists the Robusto at 5 1/2 x 50; Neptune lists it at 5 1/8 x 50. The Chiquito Perfecto is 4 x 40/52 and was added in 2022.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98 and Piloto Cubano from La Canela)
cigars.about: A Connecticut broadleaf line from Jochy Blanco's Tabacalera Palma, named for the Greek gods of the wind. Four of the five sizes are named for the north, south, east and west winds.
cigars.researchNote: At launch the four wind-named sizes were each sold only in matching regions of the U.S., with the Anemoi size available nationwide.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Corojo ligero from Jacagua, Criollo 98 ligero from La Canela, Criollo 98 seco from Gurabo, Piloto Cubano seco from La Canela)
cigars.about: La Galera's first Dominican puro, made for the 90th anniversary of the Blanco family's factory, registered in 1936. All of the tobacco, including the wrapper, comes from the company's own farms, and both sizes are box-pressed.
cigars.researchNote: Regular production despite the anniversary name. The Nanan is a new box-pressed perfecto that halfwheel lists at 6 3/4 x 44/58; Neptune lists it as 62 ring and calls the Lector a Toro. Strength is from Neptune only.

cigars.about: One of two toros made for Tabacalera Palma's 85th anniversary, this one blended by owner Jochy Blanco and inspired by his father's love of Connecticut wrapper. It was sold in a shared box with his son's blend.
cigars.researchNote: One half of the 85th Anniversary release: 2,021 boxes of 20, with 10 of each blend. Announced in 2021 but reached stores in January 2022. Halfwheel found it mild to mild-medium; Neptune lists the box as medium.

cigars.about: One of two toros made for Tabacalera Palma's 85th anniversary, this one blended by Jochy Blanco's son Jose Manuel, his first blend sold to the public. It uses a Connecticut broadleaf wrapper and came in a shared box with his father's blend.
cigars.researchNote: One half of the 85th Anniversary release: 2,021 boxes of 20, with 10 of each blend. Announced in 2021 but reached stores in January 2022.

cigars.about: La Galera's first Chinese New Year cigar, a toro with a coiled bun cap and covered foot released for 2024. The Dominican tobaccos come from the company's Canela and Jacagua farms and were aged at least five years.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,024 boxes of 10. Sources disagree on strength: Neptune lists it as full, but halfwheel's review found it mild to medium. The Dominican binder and filler include criollo 98 and piloto cubano.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98, Olor, Pelo de Oro, Piloto Cubano)
cigars.about: La Galera's 2025 Chinese New Year release, a Churchill with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over Dominican tobaccos. Each 10-count box came with a two-cigar leather case.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,025 boxes of 10, with 1,000 sent to Asia and about 700 to the U.S. No strength rating or tasting notes have been published.

cigars.line: Year of the Horse Limited Edition 2026
cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98, Olor, Pelo de Oro, Piloto Cubano)
cigars.about: La Galera's 2026 Chinese New Year release and its third zodiac cigar, a 6 x 56 toro with a Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper. It comes in an ornate 12-count box that also holds a cutter, lighter and ashtray.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,026 numbered boxes of 12. Arapiraca is a Brazilian leaf, not Mata Fina; Neptune lists the wrapper color as Colorado.

cigars.about: A La Galera toro with a pigtail cap and covered foot, made as a regional exclusive for the Middle East. The name refers to the majlis, the sitting room at the center of Arab hospitality.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only in the Middle East, starting with Bahrain, Qatar and the UAE, so guests are unlikely to find it in the U.S. It is not a limited edition. No strength rating or tasting notes were found.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made for Aging Room by AJ Fernandez, added in 2023 as the second blend in the Quattro Nicaragua family. It is blended to be a little lighter than the original Quattro Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper varietal is not published; Neptune calls it a maduro. The 2019 Cigar of the Year was the original Quattro Nicaragua Maestro, not the Sonata. Mike's Cigars lists it as medium to full.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The third Quattro Nicaragua blend, a box-pressed Nicaraguan puro made by AJ Fernandez and released in 2025. It uses a hybrid Criollo 98 wrapper from the Finca La Lilia farm in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: Concerto is also the name of the 7 x 50 size in every Quattro line, so check which one a guest means. Altadis lists the Impromptu at 6 1/2 x 52, while halfwheel and Neptune list 6 x 52. Neptune rates it medium, Cigars Direct and Mike's medium to full.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: Rafael Nodal's opera-themed line, relaunched in January 2025 with a new blend made by AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua. It pairs a Connecticut-grown broadleaf and habano hybrid wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: The original La Boheme of 2014 was a different cigar: Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Dominican binder and filler, made at Tabacalera Palma. Altadis simply calls the current wrapper Connecticut Broadleaf. Shops list it medium to full, but halfwheel's reviewer found the strength just under medium.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro from Aging Room built around tobacco from the volcanic island of Ometepe, made at the Plasencia factory in Estelí. It followed the Dominican Bin No. 1 and came out in 2019.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune calls it medium strength, Mike's Cigars lists it as full. Neptune now flags it discontinued, though some shops still have the C Major. The wrapper varietal is not published.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: Aging Room's 15th anniversary cigar, made by AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua and named for the blue amber mined in the Dominican Republic. It was announced in late 2025 and reached stores in April 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Made in limited annual batches with no numbers given. The Blue Maestro is a torpedo and the Blue Turquoise is a perfecto. Neptune and Mike's list it as full, Cigars Direct as medium to full.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped cigar in Aging Room's core trio, launched in 2018 as Aging Room by Rafael Nodal Connecticut. It is a Dominican cigar made at Jochy Blanco's Tabacalera Palma.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2018 as Aging Room by Rafael Nodal Connecticut and now sold as Core Connecticut. Mike's Cigars lists it as mild, Cigars Direct as mild to medium.

cigars.about: The maduro cigar in Aging Room's core trio, launched in 2018 as Aging Room by Rafael Nodal Maduro. It is a Dominican cigar made at Tabacalera Palma.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2018 as Aging Room by Rafael Nodal Maduro. halfwheel's launch coverage, Cigars Direct and Mike's spec table give a Mexican San Andrés wrapper, while an earlier halfwheel report and Mike's description say Nicaraguan.

cigars.about: A 2014 Aging Room release built on long-aged Dominican binder and filler from Jochy Blanco's reserves, under an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. It was made at Tabacalera Palma in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis no longer lists it and no source says outright that it is discontinued. halfwheel dates the aged tobacco to 1999 and 2001, Mike's Cigars to 1997 to 1999. The D Major is a box-pressed toro added in 2015.

cigars.about: The original Aging Room Maduro from Boutique Blends, released in 2013 with a five-year-old Nicaraguan maduro wrapper over Dominican Habano tobacco. A separate maduro line was added in the 2018 portfolio overhaul.
cigars.researchNote: This is the 2013 blend. The maduro mostly sold today is Core Maduro, a 2018 cigar that reuses the Rondo, Mezzo and Major size names. No source says outright that the 2013 blend was discontinued, and Mike's Cigars still lists it.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.about: Powstanie's third regular line, released in 2023 by the Szczepankiewicz brothers of Cigar Hustler. It is made at the Nica Sueño factory in Estelí, the home of RoMa Craft Tobac.
cigars.researchNote: The Corona Gorda, nicknamed Justice, was added in April 2024. Cigar Hustler, the owners' shop, rates it mild to medium, while Luxury Cigar Club calls it medium.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.about: Powstanie's fourth regular line, released in early 2025 and made at the Nica Sueño factory in Estelí. The Belicoso placed second on halfwheel's Top 25 for 2025.
