cigars.researchNote: The Corona Gorda was added in January 2026. Cigar Hustler, the owners' shop, rates it medium to full, while Luxury Cigar Club calls it full.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.about: Powstanie's fifth regular line, released in spring 2026 in four box-pressed sizes. It is made at the Nica Sueño factory in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: Same blend as the limited Catastrophic Failure of 2024. Cigar Hustler's own listing says Indonesian Sumatra wrapper, while halfwheel and Luxury Cigar Club say Ecuadorian Sumatra-seed. Cigar Hustler rates it medium, Luxury Cigar Club medium-plus.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Barber pole of Ecuadorian Habano and Brazilian Mata Fina
cigars.about: The third Surrounded by Champions release from Powstanie, a barber pole corona gorda made at the Nica Sueño factory. It shipped in January 2022 and was limited to 250 boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: Named for 2020 but released in January 2022. Ecuadorian Habano is the main wrapper, with Brazilian Mata Fina as the accent stripe. Strength is the halfwheel reviewer's reading of slightly over medium.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.about: The fourth Surrounded by Champions release from Powstanie, a barber pole corona gorda made at the Nica Sueño factory. It shipped in December 2023 and was limited to 500 boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is undisclosed. Named for 2022 but released in December 2023. halfwheel's reviewer found the strength a little under medium.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.about: The fifth Surrounded by Champions release from Powstanie, a barber pole corona gorda made at the Nica Sueño factory. It shipped in June 2025 and was limited to 500 boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: The blend was not officially disclosed; Cigar Hustler, the owners' shop, describes a Mexican Habano and Ecuadorian Connecticut shade barber pole over Nicaraguan binder and filler. Named for 2024 but released in June 2025. Shops rate it from medium-plus to full.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Mejorado ligero), Nicaragua (Condega, Estelí viso, Pueblo Nuevo ligero)
cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Barber pole of Ecuadorian Sumatra-seed and Mexican San Andrés
cigars.about: The sixth Surrounded by Champions release from Powstanie, a barber pole corona gorda with tobacco from five countries. It shipped in August 2026 and is limited to 500 boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is two leaves, Ecuadorian Sumatra-seed and Mexican San Andrés. It is the first SBC said to use Dominican tobacco. Luxury Cigar Club lists a different blend (Ecuadorian Habano and Brazilian wrappers, San Andrés binder), which does not match halfwheel or Cigar Hustler.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.about: A limited Powstanie release from late 2024, a box-pressed robusto extra made at the Nica Sueño factory. Only 500 bundles of 10 were made.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in bundles of 10 as a one-time run. The same blend returned in 2026 as the regular Powstanie Sumatra line. Strength is the halfwheel reviewer's reading of medium-full; no maker rating was found.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Nica Sueño S.A.
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Barber pole of Ecuadorian Habano and Mexican San Andrés
cigars.about: The 2025 cigar in Powstanie's Wojtek series, named for the bear adopted by Polish soldiers in World War II. It is a barber pole perfecto in the Wojtek blend, made at the Nica Sueño factory and limited to 1,000 boxes of eight.
cigars.researchNote: Fifth cigar in the Wojtek series, same blend, renamed War Bear for 2025 and nicknamed War Bear of Mass Destruction. A 250th American Anniversary War Bear (250 boxes) followed in 2026. Cigar Hustler rates it medium to full, Luxury Cigar Club full.

cigars.about: A thick broadleaf-wrapped robusto and one of the two original Surrogates cigars, created by Dan Welsh of New Havana Cigars and now part of Tatuaje. It is built on a ligero-heavy Nicaraguan filler and is meant to be strong.
cigars.researchNote: Each Surrogates name is a single size with its own blend. It launched in 2011 as 5 1/4 x 54; the maker and retailers now list 5 1/4 x 55. Skull Breaker is the belicoso sibling.

cigars.about: A 6 x 60 Surrogates cigar with a dark Ecuadorian habano oscuro wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco, made at My Father for Tatuaje's Surrogates brand. A 5 x 50 robusto called AC550 was added in 2016.
cigars.researchNote: Famous and Holt's list it as full; Famous's own description calls it medium-full. Cracker Crumbs is the same blend in a 4 1/2 x 38 size.

cigars.about: A box-pressed 7 x 47 churchill with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco, made at My Father for the Surrogates brand. A 6 x 54 toro called SG654 followed in 2018.
cigars.researchNote: Tatuaje retired the 7 x 47 from its U.S. list in February 2023, though some retailers still show stock. Retailers disagree on strength: Famous lists medium and describes it as medium to full, Corona Cigar lists full.

cigars.about: A box-pressed 5 3/4 x 56 Surrogates cigar that takes the Crystal Baller blend and swaps its Ecuadorian habano wrapper for Connecticut broadleaf. It is made at My Father in Nicaragua for Tatuaje.
cigars.researchNote: One size only. Halfwheel's review put strength at medium-full with full body; Famous lists it as full.

cigars.about: A small 4 1/2 x 38 version of the Surrogates Animal Cracker blend, sold pre-cut in five-count soft packs. It is made at My Father in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Same blend as Animal Cracker in a small size. Halfwheel's reviews put strength around medium with full flavor and body; Famous lists it as full. It was shown in 2014 and shipped in January 2015.

cigars.about: A 5 x 55 robusto gordo with a San Andrés wrapper and a double Nicaraguan binder, named for Surrogates co-founder Dan Welsh's late dog Kenji. Welsh set out to make it the fullest cigar in the Surrogates range.
cigars.researchNote: AKC stands for 'A Kenji Cigar'. It launched in 2019 as a limited production sold through select Surrogates accounts, but retailers such as Famous still stock it.

cigars.about: Made for the tenth anniversary of the Surrogates brand, with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It began in 2022 as a limited perfecto and became a regular robusto in 2023.
cigars.researchNote: Tatuaje retired the 5 1/4 x 52 robusto in April 2026; retailers still have stock. Limited sizes were the 5 3/8 x 48 Britanicas Extra (2022) and 6 3/4 x 42 Lonsdale Extra (2024). Retailers disagree on strength: Neptune says medium, Famous says full.

cigars.about: A 6 x 50 toro in the Surrogates range, named because it became the last cigar of the night for co-founder Dan Welsh. It pairs a Nicaraguan corojo 99 wrapper with tobacco from Nicaragua, Mexico and the U.S.
cigars.researchNote: The blend also has U.S. leaf: Famous places Connecticut broadleaf in the binder, Neptune lists USA in the filler. Famous files it under Ecuadorian Sumatra, but halfwheel and Neptune say Nicaraguan corojo. Both retailers list full strength, though Famous's description says medium-bodied.

cigars.about: A limited Surrogates release from Tatuaje inspired by guitar amplifier tubes, with a stepped cap and brushed foot. Each 20-count box holds ten 4 x 54 and ten 5 x 54 cigars in the same Ecuadorian habano blend.
cigars.researchNote: Planned as an annual series with changing blends; the 2025 run was about 10,000 of each size. Neptune's spec and Cigar Coop say medium; Neptune's description says medium-full and halfwheel found medium-plus. Neptune says the EL554 wrapper is one priming higher.

cigars.about: The Connecticut shade entry in Altadis U.S.A.'s non-Cuban H. Upmann 1844 family, with an Ecuadorian wrapper over Honduran binder and filler. It is made in Honduras at Flor de Copan.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis lists the Churchill at 7 x 50; halfwheel's launch coverage had it at 7 x 54. Halfwheel's review found the nicotine strength milder than medium.

cigars.about: A finance-themed extension of H. Upmann The Banker from Altadis U.S.A., blended by the Grupo de Maestros at Tabacalera de García. It comes in ten-count boxes made to look like a laptop.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis only says the wrapper is Ecuadorian and rates strength 6; Neptune and Cigar Coop call it Sumatra and medium. Halfwheel's review found it stronger, medium-full to full with full body.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The second H. Upmann line made by AJ Fernandez in Estelí for Altadis U.S.A. It puts a triple-fermented Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper over binder and filler grown on Fernandez's Nicaraguan farms.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis calls it medium to full; Neptune lists medium. Altadis's spec table says the filler is Nicaraguan and Brazilian, but its own description and halfwheel say all Nicaraguan.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped H. Upmann made by AJ Fernandez in Estelí for Altadis U.S.A., with an Ecuadorian wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco. It arrived in 2026 as a regular production line.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel calls it H. Upmann Nicaragua by AJ Fernandez Sunrise; Neptune drops the word Nicaragua.

cigars.line: by AJ Fernandez Heritage Finca Providencia
cigars.about: A limited single-farm H. Upmann from AJ Fernandez and Altadis U.S.A., made entirely from 2021 and 2022 harvest tobacco grown on Fernandez's Finca Providencia in Nicaragua. It comes in one 6 x 55 size.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 8,250 boxes of 20 at $20 a cigar. The wrapper variety and the exact factory are not published. Altadis describes it as medium to full; Famous lists full.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro made by AJ Fernandez for Altadis U.S.A. to mark 180 years of the H. Upmann name. Its wrapper is medio tiempo, the small top leaves found above the ligero on some plants.
cigars.researchNote: 5,000 boxes of 10 Churchills; a 6 x 50 Toro was sold only in 180 humidors of 50. Neptune and Famous list full strength; halfwheel's review of the Toro found medium-full. The wrapper seed variety is not published.

cigars.about: A limited H. Upmann from Altadis U.S.A. sold in a box shaped like a gold bar, a nod to founder Hermann Upmann's banking career. The current version is the 7 x 56 Ingot Arbitrage released in late 2024.
cigars.researchNote: The blend shown is the third Ingot (2024, 5,000 boxes of 12); the 2016 and 2017 Ingots were different blends and sizes. Altadis's release lists Dominican and Nicaraguan filler; halfwheel and Neptune list Nicaraguan only.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade and Ecuadorian Sumatra (barber pole)
cigars.about: A barber pole cigar in the H. Upmann 1844 family from Altadis U.S.A., twisting a light Connecticut shade leaf and a darker Sumatra leaf together as the wrapper. Barbier is German for barber, a nod to the founder's roots.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrapper leaves, so no single wrapper type applies. Despite the Special Edition name, halfwheel lists it as regular production. Halfwheel's review found it mild to medium in strength.

cigars.about: An H. Upmann from Altadis U.S.A. built around Dominican tobacco from grower Jose Mendez & Co., including pilotico and andullo leaf, under an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. The name refers to the island the Dominican Republic shares with Haiti.
cigars.researchNote: No longer on Altadis's current H. Upmann lineup, but no discontinuation notice was found. Neptune lists it as full; halfwheel and Cigar Coop reviews put it around medium. Cigar Coop calls the wrapper Ecuadorian habano; halfwheel and Neptune say Sumatra.

cigars.about: A Honduran puro from Maya Selva Cigars built for the company's 20th anniversary. It grew out of a 2015 limited lancero and became a permanent collection.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in Europe in 2016 and in the U.S. in 2017; the Toro was added in 2022. The maker calls it medium-bodied, while Neptune's write-up says medium to full. The 2015 No. 20 Lancero that inspired it was a separate limited run with a different wrapper.

cigars.about: The Year of the Tiger entry in Maya Selva's annual Lunar New Year series, a Honduran puro made in one toro size and sold in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Shipped in December 2021 for the 2022 Lunar New Year. The wrapper's seed variety is not published.

cigars.about: The Year of the Rabbit entry in Maya Selva's Lunar New Year series, a Honduran puro in a single 5 1/2 x 48 size. It was limited to 2,023 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Released in fall 2022 for the 2023 Lunar New Year. The wrapper's seed variety is not published; Neptune lists it as a Colorado shade. The packaging honors the Mayan ruler 18 Rabbit of Copán.

cigars.about: The Year of the Dragon entry in Maya Selva's Lunar New Year series, a Honduran puro in a 7 1/2 x 52 double corona. It was limited to 2,024 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: The maker describes the profile as strong, but Neptune lists it as Medium. Released in late 2023 for the 2024 Lunar New Year. The wrapper's seed variety is not published.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Maya Selva Cigars
cigars.about: The Year of the Snake entry in Maya Selva's Lunar New Year series, a 6 1/8 x 52 pirámide with a double binder. It was limited to 2,025 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Strength comes from the maker calling the profile strong. Unlike the earlier zodiac releases it is not a Honduran puro: one binder leaf and part of the filler are Nicaraguan. Made at the company's own factory in Danlí.

cigars.about: The Year of the Horse entry in Maya Selva's Lunar New Year series, a 7 x 52 double corona with a Jamastrán wrapper and binder. Production was limited to 20,000 cigars.
cigars.researchNote: The maker mentions the cigar's strength but gives no rating, so strength is left blank. Debuted at InterTabac in September 2025 for the 2026 Lunar New Year.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Maya Selva Cigars
cigars.about: The Year of the Goat entry in Maya Selva's Lunar New Year series, a 6 x 56 Honduran puro with a strip of dark Jamastrán leaf wrapped around the foot. It is limited to 2,027 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: The maker describes it as medium to full bodied. Debuted at InterTabac in September 2026 with European shipping expected in November; a U.S. release had not been confirmed at announcement.

cigars.about: A 7 x 58 salomon marking Maya Selva's 30th anniversary. The cigars were rolled in 2019 for the 25th anniversary, held back by the pandemic, and aged about six years before release.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,500 numbered boxes of 10, each cigar in its own coffin. The maker does not fully disclose the filler and publishes no strength or tasting notes.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A perfecto in the Highclere Castle line that Foundation makes with the Earl of Carnarvon's family, created for the 100th anniversary of the discovery of King Tut's tomb. Its box copies a storage chest found in the tomb.
cigars.researchNote: The filler is undisclosed; the maker only says it is aged three years. Foundation rates it Medium, while Neptune lists it as Full. It began as a 2022 limited edition and now returns each November in a small run of about 700 boxes of 12.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A Connecticut Shade corona named for one of Nicholas Melillo's grandfathers and sold with its broadleaf sibling Pasquale as the Charter Oak Especiales. It is a richer blend than the core Charter Oak Shade.
cigars.researchNote: Sources split on where the shade wrapper is grown: Neptune says USA, halfwheel's review says Ecuador, and Foundation does not say. Foundation rates it Medium, but halfwheel found it closer to medium-full. Regular production, capped at about 500 boxes of 12 per quarter.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A Connecticut Broadleaf corona named for one of Nicholas Melillo's grandfathers and sold with its shade sibling Pegnataro as the Charter Oak Especiales. It is a fuller blend than the core Charter Oak Broadleaf.
cigars.researchNote: Foundation rates it Medium to Full, while Neptune lists it as Full. Regular production, capped at about 500 boxes of 12 per quarter.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut Broadleaf and Connecticut Havana Seed hybrid
cigars.about: A 7 x 58 salomon marking Foundation Cigar Company's tenth anniversary, wrapped in a Connecticut-grown broadleaf and Havana seed hybrid. It was sold in 10-count boxes and a rarer 20-count box.
cigars.researchNote: Planned at 35,000 cigars (2,000 boxes of 10 and 750 boxes of 20). Foundation rates it Medium to Full, while Neptune lists it as Full. A 2025 fire at the AJ Fernandez factory meant only about half the run shipped at first, with more boxes following in 2026.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A yearly perfecto in The Tabernacle line, named for the Ethiopian knighthood awarded to Foundation founder Nicholas Melillo. The cigars get extra cedar aging and the proceeds go to the Royal Ethiopian Trust.
cigars.researchNote: This is one annual size of The Tabernacle Broadleaf blend, about 700 to 750 boxes of 12 a year. Foundation rates it Full, but halfwheel's reviewer found it milder than that. Foundation lists an all-Nicaraguan filler, while halfwheel's review lists Honduras and Nicaragua.

cigars.about: An event-only Foundation cigar honoring the first known U.S. cigar factory, opened in Suffield, Connecticut in 1810. It is not sold and comes in three-count boxes given with select box purchases at Foundation events.
cigars.researchNote: The filler is undisclosed. The maker's blend table and halfwheel give a Brazilian Mata Fina binder, though the maker's own description says the binder is undisclosed too. Where it is rolled is not published.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The lighter-wrapper version of Foundation's soft box-pressed Sumatra line, named for the ancient Ethiopian kingdom said to hold the Ark of the Covenant. It launched in 2023 as Metapa and was renamed in 2024.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Metapa Claro until the 2024 rename; the blend did not change. Foundation rates the Aksum line Medium to Full, while Neptune lists the Claro as Medium and halfwheel's reviewer found it just over medium.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The dark-wrapper version of Foundation's soft box-pressed Sumatra line, named for the ancient Ethiopian kingdom said to hold the Ark of the Covenant. It launched in 2023 as Metapa and was renamed in 2024.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Metapa Maduro until the 2024 rename; the blend did not change. The wrapper is a maduro-processed Ecuadorian Sumatra, not broadleaf. Neptune's strength field says Medium, but its write-up and Foundation both say medium to full.

cigars.line: The Original San Andrés Valley Cigar
cigars.factory: Nueva Matacapan de Tabacos S.A. de C.V.
cigars.about: A reworked Te-Amo blend made by the Turrent family as a Mexican puro from San Andrés Valley tobacco with a habano-seed wrapper. Altadis U.S.A. launched it in the United States in 2024 in three sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Full name is Te Amo, the Original San Andrés Valley Cigar; the maker's site simply calls it Te-Amo. Maker's scale shows medium-full and its text says full bodied, while Neptune lists medium and halfwheel's review found the strength mild to medium.

cigars.about: One of five Te-Amo World Selection Series blends from the Turrent family, each built to echo a different cigar country's style. The Dominicana Blend is the mildest of the set, with a Criollo '98 wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's text calls it medium-bodied while its strength scale shows mild-medium. The maker does not say where the wrapper and binder are grown.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Corojo '98 (Cuban seed grown in the San Andrés Valley)
cigars.about: The Cuban-style entry in Te-Amo's World Selection Series, made by the Turrent family with Cuban-seed Corojo and Criollo tobaccos grown in Mexico's San Andrés Valley.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's strength scale shows medium, but its description calls the blend full-bodied. The band reads Cuba Blend.

cigars.about: The Honduran-style entry in Te-Amo's World Selection Series from the Turrent family. It pairs Honduran filler with a San Andrés Corojo wrapper and a Negro San Andrés binder.
The all-Mexican entry in Te-Amo's World Selection Series, a dark-wrapped puro of San Andrés Valley tobacco from the Turrent family. It is the strongest blend in the series on the maker's scale.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's spec lists an H. Criollo San Andrés wrapper, but its description says San Andrés Negro. Its strength scale shows full while the text says medium to full-bodied.

cigars.about: The Nicaraguan-style entry in Te-Amo's World Selection Series from the Turrent family. It uses Nicaraguan long filler under a Mexican-grown Criollo wrapper and a San Andrés maduro binder.
cigars.researchNote: Strength comes from the maker's dot scale; the description gives no strength word.

cigars.filler: Mexico (Negro San Andrés Oscuro, Negro San Andrés Claro, Habano Claro)
cigars.about: A Te-Amo line from the Turrent family that nods to the small hand-rolling shops once found across the San Andrés Valley. The maker describes it as made entirely of Mexican tobacco under a Connecticut wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it Atelier Te-Amo and publishes no sizes, tasting notes or release date, and does not say if it is regular or limited. Strength comes from the maker's dot scale.

cigars.about: The newest core Nub line from Oliva, putting a Mexican wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler in the brand's short, thick format. It debuted at InterTabac 2026 and reached U.S. stores in October 2026.
cigars.researchNote: The maker only says the wrapper is Mexican; Holt's names it as San Andrés. The 464T torpedo is exclusive to U.S. retailers.

cigars.about: A coffee-infused Nub from Oliva, originally launched in 2014 as Nub Café Cappuccino and later renamed. It is the lightest of the three Nuance roasts, with a Connecticut wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored cigar, formerly Nub Café Cappuccino. halfwheel and Neptune say it is made in the Dominican Republic by General Cigar for Oliva, while Holt's lists Nicaragua. Maker lists Nicaraguan filler; Neptune lists Dominican and Nicaraguan.

cigars.about: A coffee-infused Nub from Oliva, originally launched in 2014 as Nub Café Espresso and later renamed. It is the darkest of the three Nuance roasts, with a Sumatra wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored cigar, formerly Nub Café Espresso. halfwheel and Neptune say it is made in the Dominican Republic by General Cigar for Oliva, while Holt's lists Nicaragua. Maker lists Nicaraguan filler; Neptune lists Dominican and Nicaraguan.

cigars.about: A Corojo-wrapped Nub made at Oliva's factory in Estelí with Nicaraguan binder and filler. Holt's sells it in the usual 4 x 60 and 4 x 64 torpedo Nub shapes.
cigars.researchNote: Only Holt's lists this cigar; it is not on the maker's current site, so it may be a retailer exclusive or no longer made. Holt's does not say where the Corojo wrapper is grown.

cigars.about: The fourth core line from Mo Maali's Patina Cigars, introduced at PCA 2022 and made at NACSA in Estelí. It wraps a broadleaf binder and U.S. and Nicaraguan fillers in an Ecuadorian Sumatra oscuro leaf.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it a medium-full blend; halfwheel's review of the Copper size found it closer to medium.

cigars.about: A core Patina line released in 2024 and made at NACSA in Estelí. Owner Mo Maali revived the name from a dormant Chicago shop exclusive that helped spark his interest in boutique cigars.
cigars.researchNote: The earlier Oro de Nicaragua was made by My Father for Casa de Montecristo in Chicago; this is a different blend. Patina billed it as its fullest cigar at launch, and reviews put the strength between medium and medium-full.

cigars.about: A regular-production Patina line launched in October 2025 and made at NACSA in Estelí. It was the company's first box-pressed cigar, with a round toro added in April 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Patina bills it as the fullest profile in its lineup, but halfwheel and Developing Palates reviews rated the strength around medium with full flavor. BP means box-pressed. A Red Pill Sumatra version has been teased.

cigars.about: Patina's first limited edition, released in 2023 to mark the company's first five years. It was also the brand's first Connecticut broadleaf wrapped cigar and was named Developing Palates' top cigar of 2023.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 500 numbered boxes of 10 (5,000 cigars) in one 6 x 52 toro size.

cigars.about: Patina's 2024 limited edition, a 5 x 54 robusto made at NACSA in Estelí that began shipping in November 2024. It uses the same broadleaf over San Andrés leaf pairing as the earlier Patina Anniversary.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 500 boxes of 10 (5,000 cigars). Reviewers rated the strength from medium to medium-full.

cigars.about: A limited collaboration between Mo Maali of Patina Cigars and Tyler Jeffery of Viso Horny, blended together at NACSA in Estelí and released in July 2025. It came unbanded with a green foot ribbon in bundles of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Patina y Viso Verdigris, a joint release with Viso Horny. Limited to 300 bundles of 10 and shipped to only 10 stores. Strength and body are from halfwheel's review.

cigars.about: The second limited collaboration between Patina Cigars and Viso Horny, a green candela-wrapped robusto extra made at NACSA in Estelí. It shipped in March 2026 ahead of St. Patrick's Day.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Patina y Viso Horny Leprechaun Dust. Limited to 200 bundles of 10. The binder and filler are described only as grown by Oliva Tobacco Co., with no countries given.

cigars.about: An all-Nicaraguan cigar with a habano wrapper, made by Erik Espinosa at the La Zona factory in Esteli as a companion to the 601 Steel line.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers disagree on strength: Famous Smoke Shop lists it as medium, while Neptune describes it as full-bodied and full-strength. Both call the blend all-Nicaraguan; no binder is listed separately and no release year is published.

cigars.about: A full-bodied Nicaraguan puro with a dark habano oscuro wrapper, made by Espinosa at the La Zona factory in Esteli. It was created in 2014 as an exclusive for Famous Smoke Shop.
cigars.researchNote: Exclusive to Famous Smoke Shop. The Bolt size was added after the original four.

cigars.about: Espinosa's fuller take on a Connecticut-wrapped cigar, with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It returned in 2021 as an annual limited edition in a 6 x 50 toro.
cigars.researchNote: The original 601 Black came from EO Brands, was dropped in 2010 and had a small 2016 reissue; 2021 is the current limited version. It is stronger than the light wrapper suggests: halfwheel found the strength building to near full.

cigars.about: A limited 601 blend from Espinosa with a Brazilian wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, made at La Zona. The company describes it as medium to medium-plus.
cigars.researchNote: First shipped in 2016 in very small numbers (about 100 boxes), then reissued in April 2023 as a 6 x 52 toro limited to 500 boxes of 10. The 2016 wrapper was described as Brazilian habano.

cigars.about: A limited 601 blend from Espinosa with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, made at La Zona. The company describes it as medium-plus to full.
cigars.researchNote: First shipped in 2016 in very small numbers (about 100 boxes), then reissued in April 2023 as a 6 x 52 toro limited to 500 boxes of 10.

cigars.about: A limited edition marking 20 years of the 601 brand, using the same Connecticut broadleaf wrapper type as the regular 601 Blue over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It comes in one oval-pressed 6 3/4 x 56 size made at AJ Fernandez's San Lotano factory in Ocotal.
cigars.researchNote: Initial run is 4,000 boxes of 10, which Espinosa says could grow. halfwheel rated strength medium-plus to medium-full; Neptune lists it as full and sells it as 601 Maduro 20th Anniversary.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andrés Maduro (Maduro version) or Ecuadorian Habano (Habano version)
cigars.about: A stronger offshoot of Espinosa's 601 La Bomba, sold in two wrapper versions and named for the extra-long tobacco fuse that hangs from the cap. It debuted at the company's La Zona Palooza event in November 2020.
cigars.researchNote: Two cigars share the name: a San Andrés Maduro and an Ecuadorian Habano, both box-pressed 6 x 52 toros sold in bundles of 10. Very strong; the blend is closer to the La Bomba Sake Bomb than the regular La Bomba. Tasting notes are from the Maduro.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped member of Ventura Cigar Company's PSyKo SEVEN family, built from seven tobaccos from six countries. It is rolled in the Dominican Republic and is the mildest of the line.
cigars.researchNote: The filler is an undisclosed multi-country blend. halfwheel listed the launch Robusto as 4 3/4 x 50, while Ventura's site lists 5.5 x 50.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro in Ventura's PSyKo SEVEN family, blended by Indiana Ortez and made at the Ortez family factory in Condega. It uses a Nicaraguan-grown Connecticut wrapper from a 2007 crop.
cigars.researchNote: Ventura calls it medium to full; Neptune lists medium. Sizes are from Ventura's site; halfwheel listed the launch sizes as 5 x 50, 6 x 50 and 6 x 60.

cigars.about: A mild to medium blend from the original five Archetype cigars that Ventura Cigar Company launched in 2016, a line themed on the hero's journey. It was made for Ventura at Davidoff's Occidental factory in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Ventura and halfwheel call the wrapper Dominican Connecticut; Neptune lists Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade and medium strength. Ventura did not publish the binder or filler; the San Vicente binder is from Neptune. Neptune marks it discontinued.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican Habano (Natural) or Mexican San Andrés (Maduro)
cigars.about: A value-priced bundle cigar from Ventura Cigar Company, sold wrapped in brown butcher paper. It uses mixed filler with long filler at the head and comes in Natural and Maduro versions.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper fields describe the Natural; the Maduro uses Mexican San Andrés. The filler is an undisclosed multi-country blend. Shown in 2016, shipped from February 2017.

cigars.about: A value-priced line from Ventura Cigar Company named for Hugo Cassar, the head of its parent distributor Phillips & King. Ventura lists a single mild blend called The Master.
cigars.researchNote: Ventura does not publish the binder, the wrapper's origin or where it is rolled. A 50-ring Hugito is also listed, at 3.5 inches in one place and 3.75 in another. Not the same cigar as the Rocky Patel-made Hugo Chairman.

cigars.about: An unbanded, low-priced cigar that Ventura Cigar Company says has been sold since 1976. The Natural and Maduro are all Nicaraguan tobacco, and there is also an all-Dominican Connecticut version.
cigars.researchNote: Fields describe the Natural; Maduro (Nicaraguan) and Connecticut (all Dominican tobacco) versions are also sold. Ventura does not publish the factory or the country where it is rolled. Its page lists the Natural Torpedo two ways, 5 x 50 and 6 x 52.

cigars.about: A regular-production El Rey del Mundo from Forged Cigar Company with a Cameroon-seed wrapper grown by the Eiroa family in Honduras. It is rolled at STG Danlí and priced under 10 dollars.
cigars.researchNote: The maker now lists it as Appointment Cameroon. halfwheel's launch story gave Ecuadorian and Nicaraguan fillers and a 6 1/2 x 60 Gordo; the maker lists Nicaraguan and Honduran fillers and a 5 x 60 Gordo.

cigars.about: The second cigar in El Rey del Mundo's Appointment series, with an Arapiraca wrapper from Brazil's Alagoas region over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is rolled at STG Danlí in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium bodied; Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.about: A Honduran puro from El Rey del Mundo with a Connecticut-seed shade wrapper grown in Honduras' Talanga Valley. It is an affordable, mild to medium everyday cigar made at STG Danlí.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it mellow to medium; Neptune lists it as mild. A 6 1/2 x 44 Lonsdale was a limited run of 500 boxes, and the Churchill was added in 2025.

cigars.about: A limited-edition Honduran puro made for El Rey del Mundo by Justo Eiroa of JRE Tobacco at the Aladino factory. It was the first El Rey del Mundo to use habano and corojo tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,000 boxes of 16 in one 6 x 50 size. The maker's press release calls it medium strength, while its Cigar World page rates the body medium to full.

cigars.about: A limited follow-up to El Rey del Mundo King of the World, rolled in 2021 at STG Estelí and aged for more than four years before release. Unlike the Honduran original, it is made in Nicaragua with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,000 boxes of 16. The maker describes it as medium to full bodied; Neptune lists it as full. A different blend and factory from the 2024 King of the World.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A limited-edition El Rey del Mundo blended and made by AJ Fernandez in Estelí for Forged Cigar Company. It is a fuller, Nicaraguan-forward take on a brand better known for Honduran cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 3,800 boxes of 10 in a single 6 x 52 toro. The maker's press release names it El Rey del Mundo by AJ; retailers list it as by AJ Fernandez. Full strength is Neptune's rating; the maker only calls it fuller-bodied than the regular line.

cigars.about: The first Man O' War blend, made by AJ Fernandez in Esteli for Cigars International. It pairs an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Man O' War is a Cigars International house brand blended and rolled by AJ Fernandez.

cigars.about: A Man O' War blend from AJ Fernandez. The only format confirmed on sale is a 4 x 32 cigarillo sold in tins of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Blend not confirmed. Mike's Cigars describes a San Andres maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan and Brazilian filler with a Habano 2000 binder, medium to full, but its own spec table lists the wrapper as Nicaraguan. Only the cigarillo size was confirmed.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A San Andrés wrapped Man O' War made by AJ Fernandez for Cigars International, introduced in 2021. It is sold as the strongest blend in the Man O' War range.
cigars.researchNote: Billed as the strongest Man O' War, but the Blind Man's Puff panel rated it medium in strength with medium-full body, so strength is left blank.

cigars.about: The Connecticut wrapped entry in the Man O' War range, made by AJ Fernandez for Cigars International with Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Blend is from the Cigars International listing. Sizes and strength could not be confirmed.

cigars.about: A dark wrapped Man O' War from AJ Fernandez, sold in boxes of 20 in three sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Cigars Direct lists Damnation as its own Man O' War line, not under Side Projects. It gives a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper, Nicaraguan Habano binder and Nicaraguan filler at medium-full, but no second source confirmed the blend.

cigars.about: One of the small Man O' War Side Projects blends by AJ Fernandez, a single 6.5 x 56 toro gordo with a Pennsylvania Broadleaf maduro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Single size sold in boxes of 12 through Cigars International. It was on the market by 2012; current availability was not confirmed.

cigars.about: A mild to medium line from OZ Family Cigars, Tim Ozgener's company, made at Ernesto Perez-Carrillo's Casa Carrillo factory. Firsat is Turkish for opportunity.
cigars.researchNote: Box-pressed. The maker calls it mild to medium; Neptune lists it as mild. The company now goes by OZ Family Cigars and is part of Crowned Heads.

cigars.about: The fourth regular line from OZ Family Cigars and its first made at NACSA in Nicaragua. The name joins the Turkish word for dark with Lake Toba in Sumatra, a nod to the wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium to full; Neptune lists it as medium. Tim Ozgener describes the flavor as a hearty bolognese with a maple finish.

cigars.about: Tim Ozgener's modern take on CAO Brazilia, named for the Maracana stadium in Rio. It is made at My Father's Honduran factory with a Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Box-pressed. Neptune lists it as full strength and made in Nicaragua; halfwheel and Cigars Direct say Honduras, and Cigars Direct says medium-full. Said to be the first My Father made cigar to use Brazilian tobacco.

cigars.about: A one-time 6 x 50 toro from OZ Family Cigars for the 2026 World Cup, made by My Father in Esteli. The blend draws on tobacco from several countries that played in the tournament.
cigars.researchNote: 2,026 boxes of 10. halfwheel says the binder is undisclosed; Neptune lists it as Nicaraguan. Neptune rates it full and Cigars Direct medium-full, while halfwheel's reviewer found the strength mild to medium.

cigars.about: The second release in Ozgener's annual Pi Synesthesia limited series, named for a set of paintings by CAO founder Cano Ozgener. It was blended to be spicier than the first release.
cigars.researchNote: 2,500 boxes of 12. It follows the 2022 original (yellow ribbon), which was made in Nicaragua. Neptune's spec table says medium, but its description says medium to full and Cigars Direct says medium-full.

cigars.about: The third release in the annual Pi Synesthesia limited series from OZ Family Cigars, announced in October 2024. It is a 6 x 52 toro made at Casa Carrillo.
cigars.researchNote: Follows Yellow (2022) and Red (2023). The blend details come from Neptune's listing only.

cigars.about: A 2026 regular line from Davidoff's AVO brand and the first AVO made outside the Dominican Republic. It is rolled at the Honduran factory best known for Camacho.
cigars.researchNote: Davidoff does not name the wrapper variety. Neptune lists it as medium; Cigars Direct says medium-full.

cigars.about: The fourth blend in AVO's Syncro series, released in 2021. It uses a Dominican wrapper over an Ecuadorian binder with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper variety is not named. Neptune describes the wrapper color as maduro.

cigars.about: A 2025 limited edition marking ten years of AVO Syncro Nicaragua. It is a box-pressed diadema with a modified version of the Syncro Nicaragua blend.
cigars.researchNote: Single size, 6 5/8 x 50. 3,400 boxes of 20 were released for the U.S. The blend is not identical to the regular Syncro Nicaragua.

cigars.about: A 2024 AVO limited edition made with hip-hop DJ D-Nice. It is a 6 1/2 x 50 toro extra with an Ecuadorian wrapper, Mexican binder and Dominican and U.S. filler.
cigars.researchNote: 6,900 boxes of 15 worldwide. One of the filler tobaccos was aged in used bourbon barrels.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Varies by season: Ecuadorian Corojo (Spring, Summer), Mexican San Andrés Maduro (Fall), Ecuadorian Connecticut (Winter)
cigars.about: A 2023 AVO limited series of four different blends, one for each season, all in the same 6 5/8 x 50 diadema shape. Each uses some filler aged up to 14 years.
cigars.researchNote: Four separate cigars: Spring, Summer, Fall and Winter, each with its own wrapper, so ask which season is in the box. 4,000 boxes of 10 of each.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, plus Nicaragua (East), Honduras (West), Honduras and Peru (South)
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Varies by edition: Ecuadorian (East, West), Dominican (North), Ecuadorian Connecticut (South)
cigars.about: AVO's first regional series: four limited blends that were each sold only to stores in one part of the U.S. East and West came out in 2019, North and South in 2020.
cigars.researchNote: Four different cigars, not one blend. Davidoff called West the stronger of the first pair. Neptune lists East at 6 x 53; halfwheel says 6 x 55.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Condega ligero, Estelí viso, Jalapa viso, Ometepe viso)
cigars.about: A box-pressed Connecticut Broadleaf line from Rick Rodriguez's West Tampa Tobacco Co., introduced at the 2026 PCA trade show. It is made in Estelí at Garmendia, the factory behind most of the company's lines, and the sizes carry barbershop names.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is from one retailer listing (Neptune lists it as full); the maker has not published one. All three sizes are box-pressed.

cigars.about: A regular production line that Rick Rodriguez made with his mentor Ernesto Perez-Carrillo at Casa Carrillo in the Dominican Republic. It is the first West Tampa cigar made at that factory.
cigars.researchNote: Shown at PCA 2024 but did not reach stores until January 2025.

cigars.about: The third and last cigar in West Tampa's food-themed Cook Book Series, named for co-founder Rick Rodriguez. It is a single 6 x 52 toro limited to 1,000 boxes of 50.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper's country is not disclosed; Neptune lists it as Nicaraguan Habano and calls the cigar full strength, while halfwheel's review found it medium. Neptune also lists Garmendia as the factory, but halfwheel's review and the maker's quote say Tabacalera Pages.

cigars.about: The second cigar in West Tampa's Cook Book Series, named for the fried crab croquette tied to Tampa's Ybor City. It is a short 4 1/2 x 60 perfecto sold in boxes of 50 with a recipe card.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is undisclosed and production numbers were not released. Neptune lists it as medium; halfwheel's review found the nicotine strength milder than that. Halfwheel names Garmendia as the factory while Neptune lists NACSA.

cigars.about: A watch-themed limited edition from West Tampa, sold in 10-count boxes that include a cutter styled after a Rolex GMT. The company says the cigars were aged about three and a half years before release.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,500 boxes of 10. Cigar Aficionado describes the wrapper as Connecticut broadleaf from a 2019 crop and calls the cigar medium bodied; halfwheel's review found it stronger, medium-plus to medium-full.

cigars.about: The first cigar in West Tampa's Cook Book Series, named for the nickname of Columbus Drive in Tampa and its boliche restaurants. It was a single 6 x 60 gordo limited to 500 boxes of 50.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is undisclosed; the company says only that the tobacco came from Tampa's Oliva Tobacco Co.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto), Honduras (La Entrada, Jamastran), Nicaragua (Estelí)
cigars.about: A value-priced non-Cuban Cohiba from General Cigar, made in Honduras rather than the Dominican Republic. It launched in 2025 at under 10 dollars a cigar.
cigars.researchNote: This is the General Cigar (non-Cuban) Cohiba. The maker calls it medium bodied; halfwheel's review found the body closer to medium-full.

cigars.about: The first non-Cuban Cohiba rolled in the United States, made at El Titan de Bronze in Miami's Little Havana. A new limited size or blend has come out each spring since 2021.
cigars.researchNote: Each size was a one-year release: Toro in 2021, Corona Gorda in 2022, Prominente in 2023. The 2024 to 2026 releases (Reserva Roja, Azul, Plata) use different blends. Retailers disagree on strength: Neptune lists medium and Famous Smoke lists full.

cigars.about: The 2024 release in Cohiba's Miami-made Serie M line, a 6 1/2 x 54 toro extra with a Nicaraguan corojo wrapper and binder. It was limited to 2,500 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: General Cigar's press release called it medium-plus, while halfwheel's review found the nicotine strength a little under medium.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Jalapa viso and ligero, Estelí), Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano)
cigars.about: The 2025 release in Cohiba's Miami-made Serie M line, a 6 x 52 toro with a Dominican corojo wrapper. It was limited to 3,000 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: General Cigar did not publish a strength rating. Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Jalapa viso and ligero, Estelí), Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano)
cigars.about: The 2026 release in Cohiba's Miami-made Serie M line, a 6 x 52 toro and the first in the series with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper. It is limited to 3,000 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune and Famous Smoke both list it as full strength, while halfwheel's review found it medium to medium-plus. Famous Smoke's listing also shows a Dominican corojo wrapper, which was the 2025 Reserva Azul; the maker and halfwheel say Mexican San Andrés.

cigars.about: The rarest and most expensive non-Cuban Cohiba, built from vintage-dated tobaccos and sold in individual tubes. The 2025 release is a 7 x 50 Churchill priced around 250 dollars a cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Blend shown is the 2025 release. The original 2021 C8 was a different cigar: a 7 1/4 x 54 with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, sold in 10-count briefcase sets.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The second blend in Altadis U.S.A.'s Trinidad Espiritu series, themed on Brazil and built around a Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper. Rafael Nodal and AJ Fernandez blended it and it is made at Fernandez's factory in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: This is the non-Cuban Trinidad from Altadis U.S.A. The maker calls it medium to full bodied; retailers disagree, with Neptune listing medium and Famous Smoke listing full.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The third blend in the Trinidad Espiritu series, themed on Mexico with a San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos. It is soft-pressed and made by AJ Fernandez in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: This is the non-Cuban Trinidad from Altadis U.S.A. The company describes it as medium to full; Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A limited Trinidad Espiritu release themed on Miami, made entirely of Nicaraguan tobacco by AJ Fernandez. It comes in one belicoso size and was limited to 4,000 boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: Despite the name it is made in Nicaragua, not Miami. The wrapper leaf type is not published. Neptune lists strength as full and describes the body as medium to full.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A collaboration between Altadis U.S.A.'s Trinidad brand and the Tommy Bahama lifestyle label. It is a Nicaraguan puro made by AJ Fernandez with tobacco from his own farms.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Trinidad x Tommy Bahama Island Collection. The wrapper leaf type is not published.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan-made Trinidad blended by Rafael Nodal with tobaccos from Nestor Plasencia Jr.'s farms.
cigars.researchNote: Details are from the Famous Smoke listing only; the binder, filler, factory and release year are not published there. It says the tobaccos come from Plasencia's Nicaraguan farms.

cigars.about: A maduro version of Matilde's mild Serena line, swapping the Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper for Mexican San Andrés. Matilde was founded by the late Jose Seijas, longtime head of Tabacalera de Garcia, and his sons.
cigars.researchNote: Co-owner Enrique Seijas describes the strength as at or just shy of medium.

cigars.about: A small-batch 6 x 50 toro from Matilde and the company's first blend to use Peruvian tobacco, a leaf founder Jose Seijas was fond of. It began shipping in October 2024, weeks before his death.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium to full bodied, but halfwheel's review found the nicotine strength mild. Matilde describes it as a small-batch limited release while halfwheel lists it as regular production. One line on the maker's page says Habano wrapper; its spec list and halfwheel say Sumatra.

cigars.about: A tribute cigar to Matilde founder Jose Seijas, the longtime head of Tabacalera de Garcia who died in 2024. It is a 6 x 52 toro aged more than a year, with part of the proceeds going to a Parkinson's foundation in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: The 2025 run was 750 boxes of 20, and Matilde plans to release it once a year. The maker lists strength as medium to full; halfwheel's review found it medium to medium-plus.

cigars.about: The second blend in Matilde's small-batch Limited Exposure series, first released as a 6 x 50 toro in 2022 with a robusto and lonsdale added in 2023. It wears a purple band.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the blend: Matilde's site lists an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler, while halfwheel reported an Ecuadorian corojo wrapper over all-Dominican filler. The maker's site also lists the toro as 6 x 54; halfwheel has it at 6 x 50.

cigars.about: The third blend in Matilde's Limited Exposure series, released in 2026 four years after No. 2. It uses an even split of Dominican and Nicaraguan filler, a departure from the company's mostly Dominican blends.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 350 boxes each of Robusto and Toro and 250 of the Lonsdale. Sizes are from halfwheel's release report; Matilde's site instead lists the four core-line sizes (corona, robusto, toro bravo, grande).

cigars.filler: Dominican Habano Seco, Nicaraguan Habano Viso, Honduran Habano Seco
cigars.about: The broadleaf-wrapped version of Bolivar Cofradia, made by Scandinavian Tobacco Group in Honduras for the non-Cuban Bolivar brand. It swaps the regular Cofradia's wrapper and binder and is priced as a value cigar.
cigars.researchNote: This is the non-Cuban Bolivar from STG. The same published blend first appeared in 2022 as the limited Cofradia by Lost & Found Oscuro. The maker gives no strength; Famous Smoke lists it as full.

cigars.filler: Brazilian Mata Fina, Colombian, Nicaraguan Condega, Nicaraguan Esteli
cigars.about: A regular production line for the non-Cuban Bolivar brand, made by Scandinavian Tobacco Group in Honduras. The blend leans on South American tobaccos, a nod to the countries tied to Simon Bolivar.
cigars.researchNote: This is the non-Cuban Bolivar from STG. Famous Smoke lists it as medium-full while Neptune lists it as full; the maker only calls it bold.

cigars.about: A 2022 collaboration between Robert Caldwell of Lost & Found and STG, released under the Bolivar Cofradia name in five-packs. It used Ecuadorian Sumatra and Connecticut broadleaf leaf that had been aged five to eight years.
cigars.researchNote: Non-Cuban Bolivar from STG. This is the EMS (natural) version; the Oscuro flips the wrapper and binder. Strength is blank because sources disagree: Cigar Aficionado says it was blended to be mild to medium, while Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.about: The broadleaf-wrapped half of the 2022 Bolivar Cofradia collaboration between Robert Caldwell of Lost & Found and STG, sold in five-packs. It used Connecticut broadleaf and Ecuadorian Sumatra leaf aged five to eight years.
cigars.researchNote: Non-Cuban Bolivar from STG. The same published blend became the regular Cofradia Oscuro line in 2024. Cigar Aficionado calls it the stronger of the two Lost & Found blends and Neptune lists it as full, but no maker rating exists.

cigars.about: A limited edition toro from Scandinavian Tobacco Group marking what it counts as more than 130 years of the Bolivar name. The filler includes uncommon Argentine and Paraguayan tobacco, and it comes in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: This is the non-Cuban Bolivar from STG, one size only. Neptune lists it as full, with no second source for strength. STG dates the brand idea to 1895; Habanos cites 1902.

cigars.about: The first cigar from Tony Bellatto and Craig Rossi's La Barba brand. It was first made in Honduras and was reworked in 2016 around Dominican tobacco with a Dominican corojo wrapper, rolled at Tabacalera William Ventura.
cigars.researchNote: Discontinued in October 2022 after the fire at Tabacalera William Ventura, though the maker's site still shows it. The maker calls it medium plus; Neptune lists it as full. The blend given is the 2016 Dominican version; the original was made in Honduras.

cigars.filler: Dominican Corojo Ligero, Dominican Habano Vuelta Abajo (HVA) Seco
cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped Dominican cigar from Tony Bellatto of La Barba, built around a crop of tobacco he was shown at Tabacalera William Ventura. It was made in small batches as an everyday smoke.
cigars.researchNote: First released in 2015 as Siempre Tamboril, without the La Barba name. The maker describes the strength as light plus. It launched as regular production, but La Barba was wound down in 2022 and no source confirms it is still made.

cigars.about: La Barba's limited edition series built on small lots of well-aged tobacco under an Ecuadorian habano wrapper. Each edition came in one size and a different blend.
cigars.researchNote: Binder is undisclosed and the filler shown is the 2018 edition's; the 2016 blend was not published. 2016 was 500 boxes of 10 and 2018 was 2,000 boxes. The maker calls it full body, while Neptune calls it medium strength.

cigars.about: The second Ricochet blend from La Barba, created by Tony Bellatto, a trained sommelier, with Left Bank Bordeaux wine in mind. It pairs a Mexican sun grown wrapper with an Indonesian binder.
cigars.researchNote: Launched as regular production; whether it is still made is unclear, and Smokingpipes sells its remaining stock as Last Call. After the 2022 fire at Tabacalera William Ventura, halfwheel reported Ricochet production moving to the Ventura family's El Maestro factory. Cigar Coop describes the wrapper as natural San Andres leaf.

cigars.about: The Ricochet blend from La Barba dressed in an Ecuadorian Connecticut shade wrapper. halfwheel described it as the final La Barba release as founder Tony Bellatto moved to his Bellatto Premium Cigars company.
cigars.researchNote: Launched as regular production; Smokingpipes now sells remaining stock as Last Call, but no source states it is discontinued. Strength comes only from Smokingpipes, which rates it 2 out of 5. After the 2022 fire at Tabacalera William Ventura, halfwheel reported Ricochet production moving to the Ventura family's El Maestro factory.

cigars.about: A value-priced Saint Luis Rey line from Altadis U.S.A. that is made in the Dominican Republic instead of Honduras, where the brand has traditionally been made. It is rolled at Tabacalera de Garcia in La Romana.
cigars.researchNote: This is the non-Cuban Saint Luis Rey from Altadis U.S.A. The maker does not name the wrapper variety or give a strength; Neptune and Cigar Coop both put it at medium.

cigars.about: A follow-up to the Saint Luis Rey Carenas line from Altadis U.S.A., built around extra-aged tobacco and rolled at La Flor de Copan in Honduras. The name refers to Puerto Carenas, the old name for the Port of Havana.
cigars.researchNote: Non-Cuban Saint Luis Rey from Altadis U.S.A. Sources disagree under the wrapper: the maker says Nicaraguan binder and Honduran filler, halfwheel adds Nicaraguan filler, and Neptune and Cigar Coop list a Honduran binder. Neptune rates it medium; Cigar Coop found it building to medium-full.

cigars.about: The maduro version of the core Honduran-made Saint Luis Rey from Altadis U.S.A., wrapped in dark Mexican San Andres leaf. It is sold as a bold, budget-friendly cigar in two thick sizes.
cigars.researchNote: This is the non-Cuban Saint Luis Rey from Altadis U.S.A. The maker calls it bold without rating strength; Famous Smoke lists it as full while Holt's lists it as medium.

cigars.about: A big ring gauge maduro from the non-Cuban Saint Luis Rey brand, made in Honduras by Altadis U.S.A. It uses Connecticut broadleaf for both the wrapper and the binder.
cigars.researchNote: This is the non-Cuban Saint Luis Rey from Altadis U.S.A. The maker calls it fuller-bodied without rating strength; Famous Smoke lists it as full and Holt's lists the Serie G line as medium-full. Famous Smoke's description also mentions Honduran filler, which the maker does not list.

cigars.about: A 2026 release marking 30 years of the non-Cuban Saint Luis Rey, made for Altadis U.S.A. by Christian Eiroa, who blended the original 1996 Honduran version with his father. It aims to recall that first cigar's profile.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis describes it as medium to full; Cigar Dojo found medium-plus strength and Neptune lists it as medium. Sold only through brick-and-mortar shops. Pinareno is a seed variety that fits none of the wrapper categories; Neptune lists the wrapper color as Colorado.

cigars.about: The reblended replacement for the 2019 Eiroa Dark from Christian Eiroa's CLE Cigar Co., which he pulled after running short of the tobacco it needed. The 30th in the name marks his 30 years in the cigar business.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is undisclosed; Eiroa has only said it mixes Honduran tobacco with leaf from his Colombian farm, where the original Eiroa Dark was all Honduran corojo. halfwheel found it medium-plus to medium-full, while Neptune lists it as medium. The 11/18 is a 48/54/48 figurado.

cigars.about: A Honduran puro from Christian Eiroa's CLE Cigar Co., named after the Jamastran Valley, where the Eiroa family has grown tobacco for more than 50 years. It comes in triangular boxes that echo the old Camacho Diploma.
cigars.researchNote: CLE took it off its price list in March 2025 and now makes it only to order, so it is not discontinued but can be hard to find. Neptune rates it medium; halfwheel found the 2019 version medium-plus to medium-full, and CLE said a stronger version would follow in 2020. The 11/18 began as a TAA retailer exclusive.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Honduran puro from Christian Eiroa's CLE Cigar Co., following his First 20 Years anniversary cigar. Its corojo wrapper is aged more than five years to reach the reddish Colorado shade the line is named for.
cigars.researchNote: Colorado here is the wrapper color, not a place. Neptune's spec lists it as full while its description says medium to full; halfwheel found medium-plus strength. The 4 x 40 size appears at Neptune but not in the 2017 launch list.

cigars.about: A yearly Eiroa release from CLE Cigar Co. sold only to retailers who place orders at the PCA trade show. The blend, shapes and packaging change from one year to the next.
cigars.researchNote: Ask which year it is, because the wrapper changes: Honduran-grown Cameroon seed in 2021 and 2022, Honduran corojo in 2023, an undisclosed maduro in 2024, Mexican San Andres in 2025. Binder and filler are mostly undisclosed. The 2025 edition came only as a 6 x 52 toro.

cigars.about: A 10 inch by 50 ring gauge cigar from CLE Cigar Co. marking Christian Eiroa's 50th birthday and the company's 10th anniversary. Only 600 boxes of nine were made.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is officially undisclosed, though it was reported to be the same Honduran puro blend as Eiroa Classic. halfwheel found strength starting just under medium and ending just shy of full over a smoke of about five hours.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro from My Father Cigars with a Corojo 99 wrapper, made to mark 20 years of the Don Pepin Garcia brand. It wears a retro band modeled on one of the earliest Don Pepin bands.
cigars.researchNote: Debuted in May 2023 as a TAA retailer exclusive and opened to all stores in 2024. The Vintage name refers to the retro band, not aged tobacco. Holts lists it medium-full and Neptune full; halfwheel's reviewer found full flavor but only about medium strength.

cigars.about: A My Father Cigars line whose initials stand for El Rey de los Habanos, the Garcia family's first Miami factory and brand. The current version pairs a Sumatra rosado oscuro wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: This 2024 blend is new; earlier El Rey de los Habanos cigars used Nicaraguan and then Ecuadorian habano wrappers. The maker calls it medium bodied, Holts says medium-full and Neptune says full. Started as a TAA exclusive in late 2024 and went to all stores in 2025.

cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro from My Father Cigars released in 2023 for the 20th anniversary of the Don Pepin Garcia brand. It comes in one 6 1/2 x 52 size and includes some of the family's Pelo de Oro tobacco in the filler.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 5,000 boxes of 20, with 3,900 for the U.S. Holts calls it full and describes the wrapper as Cuban-seed oscuro; halfwheel's reviewer found medium to medium-full strength. Two humidor-only versions (Connecticut and Corojo, 6 1/2 x 54) are different blends.

cigars.about: A 2025 limited edition from My Father Cigars marking 20 years of the Series JJ line. It is a Nicaraguan puro with a shade-grown Corojo 99 wrapper from the Garcia family's Las Lometas farm.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,500 numbered boxes of 17: 16 toros with a lighter rosado wrapper and one salomon with a darker rosado oscuro wrapper. The maker describes the strength as 3/4 to full; Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.about: A 2026 limited edition from My Father Cigars marking 20 years of the Don Pepin Garcia Cuban Classic, the black label line. It is made entirely of Nicaraguan tobacco from the Garcia family's farms in one 6 1/2 x 52 size.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,500 boxes of 20, each with a My Father cutter. Neptune lists it as full; halfwheel's reviewer found medium-full strength that reached full in the final third.

cigars.about: The Connecticut shade version of Miami Cigar & Co.'s Nestor Miranda Special Selection, rolled by My Father Cigars in Esteli. It was built as Nestor Miranda's morning cigar to go with coffee.
cigars.researchNote: Debuted in 2012, was phased out in 2014 and returned in 2022 with a blend close to the original. The maker's site lists the same three countries but under binder, with Nicaraguan filler. Neptune rates it mild with medium body; halfwheel's reviewer found it closer to medium with a peppery start.

cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro made by My Father Cigars for Miami Cigar & Co. to mark co-founder Nestor Miranda's 80th birthday. It comes in three of his favorite shapes.
cigars.researchNote: Officially called NM80; some retailers list it as Nestor Miranda 80th Anniversary. Limited to 500 boxes of 10 per size; shown in 2023 and shipped January 2024. The maker only says all Nicaraguan tobacco; Neptune describes the wrapper as maduro.

cigars.about: A limited lancero from Miami Cigar & Co. with a blend and size chosen by Nestor Miranda himself. It is made at La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Released in 2021 as 500 boxes of 10, then repeated in August 2026 with the same blend, size and another 500 boxes. Neptune lists it as medium; halfwheel's reviewer found it building to medium-full.

cigars.about: A limited belicoso made for Miami Cigar & Co. by My Father Cigars in Nicaragua. It has been released three times, in 2011, 2012 and 2024.
cigars.researchNote: Blend shown is the 2024 release: a round all-Nicaraguan belicoso, 1,500 boxes of 10, for Miami Cigar's 35th anniversary. The 2012 release was box-pressed with a Connecticut broadleaf wrapper, and Neptune still lists that blend. Strength is from halfwheel's review; the 2024 wrapper variety is not published.

cigars.about: The fourth line from Mel Shah's Bombay Tobak, a Connecticut-wrapped cigar rolled in Costa Rica with a shaggy unfinished foot. Kesara is the Sanskrit word for saffron.
cigars.researchNote: No maker or retailer strength rating was found; halfwheel's reviewer said it leans mild with medium-plus flavor. The maker now says the filler is aged 16 years. Sizes are from the 2014 and 2015 launches and may not all still be offered.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Bombay Tobak's box-pressed Gaaja line, swapping in a Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper over the same four-country filler. It is rolled at Tabacos de Costa Rica.
cigars.researchNote: No published strength rating was found. Gaaja is pronounced GUY-yuh and refers to the elephant in Hindu tradition. The maker now says the filler is aged 16 years.

cigars.about: An extension of Bombay Tobak's MQBA line that keeps the Ecuadorian HVA wrapper from the company's own farm but adds filler from Paraguay, Peru and Nicaragua. Each cigar is packed in a glass tube.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2019 with a stated run of about 25,000 cigars, though the maker still lists it. The maker says the binder comes from its own farm; one halfwheel trade show report listed a Nicaraguan binder. No strength rating or tasting notes are published; Mayura means peacock in Sanskrit.

cigars.about: A value-priced, fuller-strength line from Bombay Tobak sold in bundles of 30. Despite the name it is rolled in Costa Rica, not Esteli, and Nicaraguan leaf is only part of the filler.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel's 2019 reports list the filler as Dominican piloto cubano and Nicaraguan; the maker's site now also lists Peru. Strength is from halfwheel, which called it fuller in strength and measured it at medium-plus.

cigars.about: The first shade-wrapped Casa Magna, made by Quesada at its own factory in the Dominican Republic rather than by Plasencia in Nicaragua. It is the lightest blend in the Casa Magna family.
cigars.researchNote: Strength and body are from halfwheel's review, which found it mild to just under medium. Neptune lists it as full, and Quesada describes it as robust for a Connecticut. Neptune's description also mentions Dominican filler; halfwheel lists Nicaraguan only.

cigars.about: A San Andrés-wrapped Casa Magna that Raquel Quesada blended with her father, made at Quesada's TABADEX factory in the Dominican Republic. It is a different blend from the all-Nicaraguan Casa Magna Colorado.
cigars.researchNote: Two more sizes were limited: a 6 x 54 box-pressed toro for TAA retailers (300 boxes) and a 7 x 40 lancero (100 boxes). Strength is from Neptune, which also says the U.S. filler is Pennsylvania leaf.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made by Plasencia for Quesada, the regular production follow-up to the limited 2011 Domus Magnus. Its sizes carry Roman names and come box or oval pressed.
cigars.researchNote: D. Magnus II is short for Domus Magnus II. halfwheel lists a 2007 sun grown Jalapa wrapper; Neptune calls the wrapper maduro and is the source for strength. Trajan, Hadrian and Marcus Aurelius were shaped sizes added in 2015.

cigars.about: A limited edition from Quesada marking 15 years of Casa Magna, the brand whose Colorado Robusto was Cigar Aficionado's top cigar of 2008. It comes in one 6 x 54 size and is made in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 3,500 boxes of 15. Neptune lists it as full and describes the wrapper as a Habano 2000 maduro; halfwheel lists only Ecuadorian habano and its reviewer found medium to medium-plus strength with fuller flavor.

cigars.about: A value-priced, Nicaraguan-forward Don Tomás blend from Scandinavian Tobacco Group, built around tobacco from a single Nicaraguan grower under a shade-grown Jalapa wrapper. It launched in Europe before coming to the U.S.
cigars.researchNote: Debuted in 2015 for international markets and was shown to the U.S. market in 2016. General Cigar rates it medium on its single body scale. The Nicaraguan leaf comes from grower Pedro Gurdian's farms in Jalapa, Condega, Pueblo Nuevo and Esteli.

cigars.about: The Cameroon-wrapped member of General Cigar's Honduran-made Don Tomás family, with Dominican, Mexican and Brazilian filler. It is known for its run of perfecto sizes.
cigars.researchNote: General Cigar describes it as medium to full in body; Neptune lists it as medium. The release year and Honduran origin are from Neptune, and the factory is not published.

cigars.about: A mild, Honduran-made Don Tomás with an Ecuadorian Connecticut shade wrapper over Dominican, Mexican and Nicaraguan filler. Its sizes are numbered from No. 100 to No. 700.
cigars.researchNote: Details come from Famous Smoke only; the binder, factory and release year were not found. Famous describes it as mild to medium bodied. General Cigar's own site does not currently list this line.

cigars.filler: Honduras (Jamastran ligero and seco, La Entrada viso)
cigars.about: A Honduran puro made at STG Danlí to mark the 50th anniversary of Don Tomás in 2021. Cincuenta means fifty in Spanish.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in Canada in August 2021 with a U.S. release through General Cigar planned for the following year; General Cigar's site does not list it now. No strength rating or tasting notes were found. The wrapper's seed variety is not published.

cigars.about: A value-priced Davidoff line launched as the follow-up to Zino Nicaragua, built on Honduran tobaccos under an Ecuadorian wrapper. It is rolled at the Camacho factory in Honduras and sold in boxes, fresh packs and tins, some of them pre-cut.
cigars.researchNote: Davidoff and halfwheel give an Ecuadorian wrapper; Neptune lists it as Honduran. The wrapper type is not published. Some fresh packs hold pre-cut cigars.

cigars.about: The larger-format tier of Davidoff's Zino Platinum brand, made in the Dominican Republic with Dominican and Peruvian filler under an Ecuadorian wrapper. It is known for big ring gauges, tubed sizes and a high price.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune rates it Medium, Holt's Medium-Full. Neptune's spec table gives a US Connecticut binder while its own description says Ecuadorian Connecticut.

cigars.about: The milder, smaller-format tier of Davidoff's Zino Platinum brand, made in the Dominican Republic with an Ecuadorian Connecticut shade wrapper over Dominican and Peruvian filler. It sells at a high price.
cigars.researchNote: Binder is unclear: Neptune's spec table says Connecticut, its description says Dominican. Neptune rates it Mild and describes it as mild to medium. The Grand Master also comes in a tube.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Honduran Cameroon-seed (THT-EKE 03/17 blend; PLdM wrapper undisclosed)
cigars.about: Christian Eiroa's flagship line for CLE. It started in 2014 with the PLdM (Primera Liga de Miami) blend rolled in Miami, and a second blend, THT-EKE 03/17, made in Honduras, was added in 2021.
cigars.researchNote: Two blends share this name. PLdM was rolled in Miami and its blend is undisclosed; THT-EKE 03/17 is made in Honduras with a Honduran-grown Cameroon-seed wrapper, the rest undisclosed. Taken off CLE's price list in March 2025 and now made to order, not discontinued.

cigars.about: A yearly limited cigar that CLE sells only to retailers who order at the PCA trade show, with a new blend each year. The 2025 edition is a 6 x 52 toro with a Cameroon-seed wrapper grown in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: The blend changes every year, so ask which year is on the shelf. Details here are the 2025 edition; the 2023 and 2024 editions used Connecticut wrappers.

cigars.about: A series of one-off CLE cigars made for the company's distributor in a single country. It began in 2024 with an Eiroa Classic 11/18 for Bulgaria, followed by France in 2025 and Austria in 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Each country gets a different blend and these are not sold in the US. Blend shown is Austria (500 boxes of 10). France used a Honduran-grown Cameroon-seed wrapper with the rest undisclosed (250 boxes of 10).

cigars.about: The Habano-wrapped follow-up to All Saints' Dedicación, with the same Nicaraguan binder and filler tobaccos in different proportions. It is made for Micky Pegg's company at Rocky Patel's TAVICUSA factory in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: All Saints calls it mild-medium; halfwheel's review put it at medium. Sizes were standardized in September 2025, so older boxes may carry the earlier names and sizes (Berkey 5 1/2 x 50, Commandant 6 1/2 x 52, Coach 7 x 48).

cigars.about: A lighter-wrapped version of All Saints' St. Francis that swaps the Ecuadorian oscuro leaf for an Ecuadorian Habano Colorado over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is made at Rocky Patel's TAVICUSA factory and smokes a step milder than the original.
cigars.researchNote: All Saints only says it is lower in strength than the medium-full original; halfwheel's review landed between medium and medium-full. Sizes were standardized in September 2025, so older boxes may be 5 1/2 x 50, 6 1/2 x 52 or 7 x 48.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Barber pole of Nicaraguan candela and Ecuadorian oscuro
cigars.about: A green and dark barber-pole short robusto with a long pigtail fuse, blended by All Saints for United Cigars' Firecracker series. It came out for St. Patrick's Day 2023 in a run of 300 boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: Blended by All Saints but sold by United Cigars as part of its Firecracker series. It has two wrappers twisted together, so it is not a pure candela.

cigars.about: A trio of figurados made by Arturo Fuente for Prometheus to mark ten years of the God of Fire brand. Prometheus describes them as the smoothest cigars in the God of Fire range.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper type is not published beyond Ecuadorian. Prometheus calls it medium bodied; Neptune says medium to full. The bands read 2012, but the cigars did not reach stores until 2015.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican Very Special Wrapper (VSW), lower priming, Chateau de la Fuente
cigars.about: A Dominican puro made by Arturo Fuente for Prometheus, wrapped in lower-priming leaf from the Chateau de la Fuente farm. It was announced for God of Fire's 15th anniversary, first shipped in late 2022, and is named for Prometheus founder Keith K. Park.
cigars.researchNote: An ongoing line, but Prometheus ships it to select retailers in very small quantities. The three Diadema sizes were added in 2026. Strength and body are from halfwheel's review; the maker gives none.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican Very Special Wrapper (VSW), top priming, Chateau de la Fuente
cigars.about: A Dominican puro made by Arturo Fuente for Prometheus to mark God of Fire's 20th anniversary in 2024. It uses the top priming of the same Chateau de la Fuente wrapper found on the KKP Special Reserve.
cigars.researchNote: Sister blend to the KKP Special Reserve, using higher-priming wrapper leaf. No strength rating or tasting notes are published by the maker. The Toro Extra 54 arrived in 2025 and the three Diademas in 2026.

cigars.about: A full-strength Cain blend made by Oliva in Estelí with Nicaraguan long filler under a Cuban-seed Nicaraguan wrapper. It is a value-priced line sold through Holt's.
cigars.researchNote: Appears to be sold only by Holt's. The binder and the exact wrapper variety are not published.

cigars.about: The mildest Cain, made by Oliva in Estelí with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over all-Nicaraguan binder and filler. It keeps some of the brand's pepper while staying around medium.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's sells it as Cain Connecticut CT; Neptune lists it as Cain Connecticut. Holt's rates it Medium, while Neptune describes it as medium to slightly full.

cigars.about: The classic core Henry Clay, an old Cuban brand name now made by Altadis U.S.A. in the Dominican Republic. It pairs a rustic Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper with Dominican binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis lists all-Dominican filler; Neptune also lists Brazilian filler. The brand dates to 1840s Cuba, and the box art shows the old Havana factory.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro in the Henry Clay War Hawk series, made by AJ Fernandez with Rafael Nodal for Altadis U.S.A. It comes in one 6 x 54 toro, first released in 2020 and brought back in late 2024.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis's launch press release called it medium bodied; Neptune rates it Full and calls the wrapper a Habano maduro. The 2020 run was 1,200 boxes of 20 and the 2024 return was 3,000 boxes.

cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped blend from Stephen Bailey's Cornelius & Anthony, rolled at Erik Espinosa's La Zona factory in Estelí. It uses the company's proprietary American binder over Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: Cornelius & Anthony went quiet after the owning family's cigarette company was sold in 2018, so what is on shelves is leftover stock. Neptune lists the American binder as US Connecticut.

cigars.about: A San Andrés maduro from Cornelius & Anthony named after owner Stephen Bailey's dachshund, who appears on the box. It was rolled at La Zona in Estelí with an American binder and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: The name is pronounced ee-shoog-urs. Cornelius & Anthony went quiet after the owning family's cigarette company was sold in 2018, so what is on shelves is leftover stock.

cigars.about: A mild Dominican house-selection toro sold under the Ashton name with a Connecticut shade wrapper. Neptune Cigar lists it as made by Fuente and sells it in single sticks and boxes of 100.
cigars.researchNote: Only found at Neptune Cigar; it does not appear on Ashton's own site, so treat the blend details as the retailer's listing. No tasting notes are published.

cigars.about: A medium Dominican house-selection toro sold under the Ashton name with an Ecuadorian sun grown Habano wrapper. Neptune Cigar lists it as made by Fuente.
cigars.researchNote: Only found at Neptune Cigar; it does not appear on Ashton's own site, so treat the blend details as the retailer's listing. No tasting notes are published.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (ligero, viso, seco), USA (Pennsylvania Broadleaf)
cigars.about: The Connecticut shade blend from Recluse, the house brand of Iconic Leaf Cigar Company, also known as the Amadeus White Label. It is rolled entubado in the Dominican Republic, and the robusto and toro are box-pressed.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as Recluse Amadeus White or simply Amadeus. The binder is a proprietary leaf the maker calls MBC, with no origin given. No specific tasting notes are published.

cigars.about: A San Andrés-wrapped Recluse blend from Iconic Leaf Cigar Company, rolled in the Dominican Republic. It was first shown in 2016 and given a national release in 2018.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it full bodied; Neptune calls it medium. Halfwheel and Neptune also list Nicaraguan Criollo 98 in the filler, which the maker's page omits. The country the Sumatra binder is grown in is not given.

cigars.about: A La Aroma de Cuba blend from Ashton, rolled by the Garcia family at My Father in Estelí with an Ecuadorian Habano Rosado wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos from their own farms. It is made in small yearly batches.
cigars.researchNote: First sold in a sampler in March 2025, then in boxes that September, with 2025 production capped at 3,000 boxes of 25. The 7 x 58 El Jefe was added in June 2026, first in a sampler with boxes planned for later in 2026.

cigars.about: A black-banded La Aroma de Cuba from Ashton, made at My Father with a high-priming Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over five-year-old Nicaraguan tobaccos from the Garcia family farms. Ashton calls it the rarest cigar in the brand.
