cigars.researchNote: One size only, a 6 x 52 toro in 24-count boxes. The first release in November 2025 was 2,000 boxes at about $25 a cigar. Ashton rates it full, but halfwheel's review found the strength closer to medium-plus.

cigars.about: A Toraño maduro made in Nicaragua with a dark Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper over Dominican and Nicaraguan ligero fillers. The retailer that lists it rates it full strength.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Carlos Toraño Signature. Specs come from one retailer, which does not name the factory, the release year or the origin of the broadleaf binder.

cigars.about: A Toraño cigar sold as a dessert-style smoke, with tobacco said to be aged in oak barrels that previously held sweet wine. It is listed by one retailer in a single robusto size.
cigars.researchNote: Only one retailer lists it, so the blend is left blank. That shop calls it a mild Dominican-made cigar with a Connecticut wrapper, and its own pages disagree on whether the barrels held port or a chocolate dessert wine.

cigars.about: A one-size limited release for the non-Cuban Sancho Panza brand, blended by Matt Booth and Justin Andrews with Oliva and rolled at Oliva's factory in Estelí. It shipped in 10-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Made for the brand by Oliva at its TABOLISA factory in Estelí. The number of cigars made was not disclosed. Launch price was $12.99.

cigars.about: A 5 x 50 robusto made in 2023 only for retailers in the Tobacconists' Association of America. It was the first Sancho Panza rolled in Nicaragua, credited to Justin Andrews and Matt Booth.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 750 boxes of 10 and sold only at TAA member shops. Launch price was $8.99. The maker did not publish a strength or the wrapper's seed type.

cigars.factory: Royal Agio Cigars factory (San Pedro de Macorís)
cigars.about: The fourth blend in Royal Agio's Balmoral Añejo XO family, a Dominican-made cigar with a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper and the brand's stalk-cut Brazilian Mata Norte in the filler. It reached US stores in 2019.
cigars.researchNote: Scandinavian Tobacco Group bought Royal Agio in 2020 and pulled Balmoral from the US, so what is on shelves is leftover stock. The brand name may still be used outside the US.

cigars.about: A collaboration between Boris Wintermans of Royal Agio and Litto Gomez of La Flor Dominicana, rolled at La Flor's factory with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Dominican binder and filler. It was the second and last cigar in the Serie Signaturas.
cigars.researchNote: Balmoral left the US in 2020 after Scandinavian Tobacco Group bought Royal Agio, which ended this series. The Brindis is a 7 x 55 double perfecto with a pigtail cap. Sold in boxes of 10.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: An Altadis U.S.A. line made by AJ Fernandez in Estelí with a dark Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos. Retailers rate it full strength.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis says the Nicaraguan tobaccos are aged more than four years. One retailer also lists Dominican leaf in the filler, but the maker and halfwheel say Nicaraguan only.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro from Altadis U.S.A., made by AJ Fernandez in Estelí and topped with a Habano-seed wrapper from the 2019 harvest. The same factory makes Onyx Bold Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is tied to the 2019 crop. One retailer says later runs will use wrapper from other harvests once that stock is gone.

cigars.about: The second Fonseca blend made by the Garcia family since My Father bought the US rights to the brand. It swaps the original's Nicaraguan Corojo wrapper for a Mexican San Andrés maduro over Garcia-grown Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: My Father calls it full bodied but gives no strength. Retailers range from medium to full, and halfwheel's review put strength at medium-plus. The maker's page also shows a Corojo 99 wrapper in its spec line, which conflicts with its own San Andrés description.

cigars.about: The newest San Cristobal from Ashton, rolled by the Garcia family at My Father in Estelí with a Cuban-seed Ecuadorian wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos from their farms. It began shipping in July 2026 as a regular line.
cigars.researchNote: Four sizes are box-pressed. The two thickest, Ocaso and Pacifico, are round. Dorado is a pyramid. Ashton rates the blend medium-full.

cigars.about: A fuller take on the mild, sweet-capped Baccarat, made in Honduras for Davidoff with a Habano wrapper and Nicaraguan filler. It keeps the brand's sweetened cap.
cigars.researchNote: The cap is sweetened, so tell guests before they light it. Retailers disagree on where the wrapper is grown: one lists Nicaragua and another the Dominican Republic. No maker spec sheet was found.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A box-pressed Nicaraguan cigar made for Padilla by AJ Fernandez, named for what would have been the 88th birthday of Heberto Padilla, the Cuban poet and father of brand owner Ernesto Padilla. The filler includes Pelo de Oro tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Maker lists an Ecuadorian Corojo wrapper; halfwheel and Cigar Aficionado call it Ecuadorian Habano. Maker calls it medium; Cigar Aficionado lists medium-full. The Robusto was Cigar Aficionado's No. 21 cigar of 2021 with 92 points.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A box-pressed Connecticut Broadleaf maduro with a pigtail cap, made for Padilla by AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua. It is named after the Hemingway novel.
cigars.researchNote: The band, Padilla's site and Cigar Aficionado's rating read For Whom the Bells Toll; Padilla called the band wording a printing error. Launched in 2021 as 400 five-packs in one 5 5/8 x 46 size. Medium is Cigar Aficionado's rating; the maker gives no strength.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped blend in Padilla's three-part Finest Hour series, named for Winston Churchill's 1940 speech. It is made for Padilla by AJ Fernandez in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2019 at an undisclosed Honduran factory, then moved to AJ Fernandez in late 2020. The maker gives no strength rating but says it is not a mild-mannered Connecticut; Neptune describes it as on the mild side.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: The red-banded sun grown blend in Padilla's Finest Hour series, named for Winston Churchill's 1940 speech. It is made for Padilla by AJ Fernandez in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2019 as Finest Hour Habano, a Nicaraguan puro made in Honduras, and moved to AJ Fernandez in late 2020. The maker now lists an Ecuadorian sun grown Habano wrapper, though one Padilla listing calls it Ecuadorian Corojo. Maker says medium-full; Neptune says medium.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: The black-banded maduro blend in Padilla's Finest Hour series, named for Winston Churchill's 1940 speech. It is made for Padilla by AJ Fernandez in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Padilla's main listing, halfwheel and Neptune give a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper, but Padilla's 2026 relaunch listing says San Andres maduro with Nicaraguan and Honduran filler. Maker calls it medium to full; Neptune says medium. Launched in 2019 in Honduras and moved to AJ Fernandez in late 2020.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A Corojo-wrapped addition to Padilla's Finest Hour series, an all-Nicaraguan blend rolled by AJ Fernandez in Esteli in a 6.5 x 50 short Churchill.
cigars.researchNote: New in 2026 and so far sold only as pre-production 5-packs in one size, some wearing plain white prototype bands. The maker says a boxed release will follow at a higher price. The maker describes it as medium-bodied.

cigars.about: A Padilla blend built on Aganorsa-grown Nicaraguan Corojo 99, sold direct through the Padilla website in four sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish the binder, factory, strength or tasting notes.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Padilla's Artefacto, pairing a Mexican San Andres wrapper with Nicaraguan fillers that include Aganorsa Corojo. It is sold direct through the Padilla website.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish the binder, factory or strength. Padilla says it is made in batches and was out of stock for nearly two years while one filler leaf was unavailable.

cigars.about: Padilla's best-known cigar, rolled in small batches at El Titan de Bronze in Miami's Little Havana. It is named for the corner of 8th Street and 11th Avenue, where the original 2005 version was made by Pepin Garcia.
cigars.researchNote: The blend and factory have changed several times since 2005; the current El Titan de Bronze version dates to 2020. The maker lists an Ecuadorian Corojo wrapper, while halfwheel and Neptune list a Nicaraguan wrapper. Neptune's description calls it medium to full.

cigars.about: The San Andres maduro counterpart to the Padilla Miami, with aged Nicaraguan fillers. It was introduced in 2012 as a small-batch cigar rolled at El Titan de Bronze in Miami.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2012 at El Titan de Bronze in Miami. Padilla's main listing still says it is rolled in Miami, but another Padilla listing says the blend was reworked in Nicaragua, so check where current stock is made before quoting it.

cigars.about: A lighter-wrapped edition of the Padilla Miami, keeping the same filler blend under a Habano Claro wrapper. It is rolled in very small batches at El Titan de Bronze in Miami's Little Havana.
cigars.researchNote: The maker describes it as slightly milder than the regular Miami and calls it an extremely limited release. The wrapper's country of origin and the binder are not published.

cigars.about: Factory seconds of the regular Padilla Miami, rolled at El Titan de Bronze in Miami and sold at a discount. The maker says they were set aside only because the wrapper color varied.
cigars.researchNote: Same cigar as the regular Padilla Miami with slight wrapper color variation, aged more than a year, per the maker. A one-time batch sold in 5-packs; the listing gives no size or blend details.

cigars.about: Padilla's flagship blend, introduced in 2006 and named for the birth year of Heberto Padilla, the Cuban poet and father of brand owner Ernesto Padilla. The original was made in Miami by Pepin Garcia.
cigars.researchNote: Made at several factories since 2006, including Pepin Garcia's in Miami, Raices Cubanas in Honduras and Oliva in Nicaragua (the version Holt's sells), so the blend varies by version. halfwheel says the 2014 Oliva release used an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. Padilla's recent 1932 small batches are rolled by AJ Fernandez.

cigars.about: A darker-wrapped take on the Padilla 1932 blend. This 6 x 46 Corona Gorda was rolled at El Titan de Bronze in Miami for the 10th anniversary of the retailer Napa Cigars.
cigars.researchNote: First sold in 2007 as 300 humidors of 45 cigars, a Nicaraguan puro from the Pepin Garcia years. Padilla's two listings for this Napa Cigars version disagree: one gives Ecuadorian Habano over Nicaraguan Corojo, the other an Ecuadorian Corojo oscuro wrapper over Nicaraguan Criollo.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A small-batch version of the Padilla 1932 blend finished in a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper and rolled by AJ Fernandez in Esteli. It was released in 2026 as a single lot of 6.5 x 55 Toros.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Small Batch, Lote 32-6; the 6 marks the sixth trial blend. One lot only with no second run promised, and each cigar has a red ribbon on the foot. The maker says it starts medium-full and builds to full.

cigars.about: A small-batch 2026 experiment on the Padilla 1932 blend that uses two Broadleaf maduro binders, which is where the 2X name comes from. It was sold direct from Padilla as a 5-pack of Torpedoes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not name the wrapper, filler, factory or strength. Released once as a website-only sampler.

cigars.about: A 2025 collaboration between Ernesto Padilla and Yaxel Ortiz, rolled at Ortiz's Best Cigars factory in Nicaragua with a dark Corojo wrapper. It is named after the memoir by Cuban writer Reinaldo Arenas.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel's first report left the wrapper's country undisclosed; its PCA 2025 coverage lists Ecuador. The binder is undisclosed. In October 2026 Padilla said regular production is suspended because the Corojo wrapper is hard to get, with only a few Toro 5-packs left.

cigars.about: A small-batch Padilla maduro first released in 2013 and brought back in 2025 as Vintage Reserve 3.0. The current version uses aged Nicaraguan fillers from Esteli and Jalapa under a dark maduro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The 2013 original was made by Oliva in Nicaragua with a Pennsylvania Broadleaf wrapper in Robusto, Torpedo and Churchill, as a numbered limited run. For the current 3.0 pre-release the maker does not name the wrapper leaf, binder, factory or size.

cigars.about: Padilla's first line, built around a golden hybrid-seed wrapper from the grower ASP that the maker likens to Connecticut smoothness with Habano bite. It was reintroduced in 2025 as a limited run of Toros sold direct.
cigars.researchNote: For the 2025 rerelease the maker does not publish the wrapper's country, binder, filler, factory, strength or exact Toro dimensions.

cigars.about: A small-batch Padilla blend built around tobacco from Ometepe, the volcanic island in Lake Nicaragua. It is sold direct from Padilla in 5-packs of Robustos.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish the wrapper, binder, factory, strength or exact Robusto dimensions. It comes and goes in batches because the Ometepe tobacco is hard to source.

cigars.binder: Dominican Republic (Monte Plata on the four original sizes)
cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, plus USA, Peru, Mexico or Nicaragua depending on the vitola
cigars.about: A Principle Cigars line made in small batches at Kelner Boutique Factory with Hendrik Kelner Jr., using tobaccos aged at least five years. Each vitola has its own blend, and the blends are adjusted with every production run.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it an ongoing limited production and reblends each run, so blends vary by vitola and batch. Patrie uses an Ecuadorian Habano hybrid wrapper. Brindille uses a Habano 2000 wrapper over an Ecuadorian Corojo binder.

cigars.about: A very long, slim 9 1/2 x 46 cigar added to the Aviator Series for its tenth anniversary. Founder Darren Cioffi designed the format so a fast smoker can keep the cigar cool.
cigars.researchNote: One size within the Aviator Series. Rolled in a single run in January 2023 and released in March 2024, limited to 200 boxes of 10.

cigars.about: A darker version of the Aviator Series made only when unusually dark, oily wrapper leaves turn up during sorting. The maker describes it as fuller and richer than the standard Aviator of the same vitola.
cigars.researchNote: Not a fixed blend or size. It uses the darkest wrapper leaves from a regular Aviator run with fillers shifted to higher primings, so the numbers made are unpredictable. The maker says it is never announced and is slipped into retailer shipments.

cigars.about: A charity project within the Aviator Series, named after the rescue aircraft once called Angels of Mercy. It is made in small quantities and aged for years before being offered.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish the blend or factory for this one. The current batch was made in 2019 and has been aging since.

cigars.about: The core blend of Principle's more approachable Accomplice line, an Ecuadorian Habano 2000 wrapper over a Dominican Cotui binder. The maker describes it as a balanced medium-bodied cigar with a classic Dominican profile.
cigars.researchNote: Accomplice dates to 2013, but this is a recent reblend the maker calls the new Accomplice. The maker does not name the factory for the Classic. A 7 x 39 Lancero is listed as arriving in fall 2026.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Principle's Accomplice line, with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over Nicaraguan and Dominican tobaccos. The current blend is made at Casa Carrillo.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's word for the strength is medium-plus. This is a recent reblend; an older Accomplice Maduro is still sold as Legacy Accomplice Maduro. A 7 x 58 Nightstick size has been announced.

cigars.about: The Connecticut version of Principle's Accomplice line, with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over a Dominican Monte Plata binder. The maker describes it as clean and creamy with a light touch of acidity.
cigars.researchNote: Part of the recently reblended Accomplice range. The maker does not name the factory or give a strength rating, only that it sits in a lighter register.

cigars.about: Principle's annual Christmas release, a 4 1/2 x 60 perfecto rounded at both ends to look like a tree ornament. The size stays the same each year but the blend is new every time.
cigars.researchNote: The blend shown is the 2025 edition, the first with a maduro wrapper. It changes every year: 2023 used an Ecuadorian HVA wrapper and the 2024 wrapper was not disclosed. Sold singly and in boxes of four.

cigars.about: A one-time 2023 release marking ten years of the Accomplice line, and the first collaboration between Principle and E.P. Carrillo. It comes in a single 6 1/2 x 54 size.
cigars.researchNote: Made at E.P. Carrillo's factory, which halfwheel lists as Tabacalera La Alianza. The maker says Cigar Journal named it one of its Top 25 cigars of 2023.

cigars.about: Principle's Connecticut line, built to bring Aviator-style complexity to a creamy Ecuadorian Connecticut cigar. It is one blend in a few sizes, made at Kelner Boutique Factory.
cigars.researchNote: The maker gives no strength; the rating here is from halfwheel's review of the Corona. The maker's store lists the filler as Dominican and Nicaraguan instead of Dominican and USA. The Corona arrived in June 2026, first as a Small Batch Cigar exclusive.

cigars.about: A long-filler Connecticut cigar from Principle with a lightly sweetened tip. The maker says the sweetness is felt on the lips and not in the smoke.
cigars.researchNote: This has a sweetened tip. The maker does not publish the blend, factory or a strength rating, and says only that it is not about weight or force. A 4 1/2 x 40 Demi is a Fuselage exclusive.

cigars.about: A very thin 6 x 26 handmade long-filler cigar, the first release in Principle's Petits Provocateurs line of small formats. In a cigar this slim the wrapper and binder supply most of the flavor.
cigars.researchNote: Flechette is the only size in the Petits Provocateurs line so far. The maker does not name the factory or give a strength rating.

cigars.about: A cigar made by Principle with the Frothy Monkey coffee shops of Nashville, blended to be smoked with coffee. The maker credits much of the flavor to a rare Dominican Cotui wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker names only the wrapper; binder, filler, factory and strength are not published.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera Palma, Tabacalera Diaz Cabrera, Kelner Boutique Factory, Casa Carrillo, TABADEX
cigars.about: A five-cigar box in which five Dominican cigar makers each blended a 6 x 50 toro inspired by Nina Simone's 1965 album I Put a Spell on You. The makers are Jochy Blanco, Eladio Diaz, Henke Kelner, Ernesto Perez-Carrillo and Manolo Quesada.
cigars.researchNote: Five different blends, so no single wrapper: Blanco used US Connecticut, Diaz Ecuador, Kelner Ecuador Habano hybrid, Carrillo Ecuador Habano, Quesada Ecuador Corojo. Each came from its blender's own factory, except Kelner's, made at his son's Kelner Boutique Factory. 5,000 boxes of five.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, Nicaragua, USA, Peru, Paraguay, Cameroon, Mexico, Honduras
cigars.about: A limited Principle cigar blended from tobaccos of ten countries, with a half leaf of each of eight filler tobaccos. All 3,000 were rolled by one roller in an empty Kelner Boutique Factory during the March 2020 shutdown.
cigars.researchNote: Only 3,000 were made, in March 2020. Each comes in a numbered coffin with a matching certificate. The maker gives no strength rating.

cigars.about: A limited Archive Collection release dressed in original 1920s chromolithographic bands and box labels. It is a 5 3/4 x 46 corona made at Casa Carrillo with mostly Nicaraguan tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium-bodied, while halfwheel's review found the strength mostly mild. The varietals are not disclosed. halfwheel reports 8,000 to 10,000 cigars, soft launched in late 2025 and shipped nationally in March 2026.

cigars.about: A limited 6 x 55 Archive Collection cigar sold in packs of five bundled in a vintage necktie, with bands styled after a 1960s shirt tag. It was released for Christmas 2025 and made at Kelner Boutique Factory.
cigars.researchNote: The maker describes it as light to medium in body. Sold only in five-packs, each wrapped in a different vintage tie. The first run was small, and the founder has said it may return.

cigars.about: An Archive Collection cigar on which every band is an original antique watch dial from a watchmaker's bench, so no two are alike. The original blend pairs an Ecuadorian Habano 2000 Rosado wrapper with Zimbabwean and Dominican tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not name the factory or give a strength for the original. The maker lists the binder as Burma (Zimbabwe). A Maduro version followed in March 2024.

cigars.line: Archive Collection Time to Burn Maduro
cigars.about: The maduro follow-up to Time to Burn, a 6 1/2 x 52 toro with a Mexican San Andres wrapper made at Casa Carrillo. Each of the 5,000 cigars wears a different antique watch dial as its band.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 5,000 cigars, released in March 2024. No strength rating is published.

cigars.about: The first release in Principle's Archive Collection, banded with original 1940s British bus tickets. It has a dark Ecuadorian Corojo wrapper over an Ecuadorian binder and Dominican filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's main site lists the size as 6 x 45 and its store lists 6 x 46. No strength rating is published. Sold as singles and five-packs.

cigars.about: A box-pressed San Andres maduro that Ernesto Padilla first blended for the Italian market, with Nicaraguan fillers from Condega and Jalapa. It is sold in the US in small lots through Padilla's own store.
cigars.researchNote: Padilla does not publish the binder or the factory. A box-pressed Robusto is also sold but its dimensions are not listed. The Italia name also covers Habano-wrapped cigars, so confirm which wrapper a guest means.

cigars.about: A value bundle line sold direct by Padilla in bundles of 25, with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over all long-filler Nicaraguan tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: Padilla describes it as medium to medium plus. Also sold as Robusto, Toro and Torpedo, but the maker lists no dimensions for those. Binder, factory and country of manufacture are not published.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped member of Padilla's direct-sold bundle line, made with all long-filler Nicaraguan tobaccos from Jalapa and Condega and sold in bundles of 25.
cigars.researchNote: Padilla calls the body "milder medium" and does not say where the Connecticut wrapper is grown. Also sold as Robusto, Toro and Torpedo, with no dimensions listed. Binder, factory and country of manufacture are not published.

cigars.about: The maduro member of Padilla's direct-sold bundle line: a San Andres maduro wrapper over long-filler Nicaraguan Criollo, sold unbanded in bundles of 25 as overrun stock.
cigars.researchNote: Padilla describes it as medium to medium plus. Also sold as Robusto, Toro and Torpedo, with no dimensions listed. Binder, factory and country of manufacture are not published.

cigars.about: A box-pressed 6 x 52 from Padilla with a San Andres maduro wrapper and a Connecticut Broadleaf binder over all-Corojo Nicaraguan filler. It is sold in five-packs through Padilla's own store.
cigars.researchNote: Padilla's product page calls it full-bodied, but its sampler pages describe the same cigar as medium in body. The factory and country of manufacture are not published. The store lists it as limited availability.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Sun-grown Corojo from Jalapa, Nicaragua (Cuban seed, medium priming)
cigars.about: A 6 x 52 torpedo from Padilla wrapped in sun-grown Jalapa Corojo, sold in five-packs through the company's own store. Padilla pitches it as richer than a Connecticut and smoother than a maduro.
cigars.researchNote: Padilla does not publish the filler, factory or a strength rating. A Padilla sampler page says it uses two maduro binders but gives no origin. Only the torpedo size is listed.

cigars.about: Padilla's take on the Cuban Behike shape: a 6 x 54 with a pigtail cap, rolled in Nicaragua with a San Andres maduro wrapper over Corojo filler. Sold in five-packs through Padilla's own store.
cigars.researchNote: This is a Padilla cigar in the Behike format, not a Cohiba Behike. Padilla's sampler pages list a BHK Maduro at 6 x 56 rather than 6 x 54. Binder and factory are not published.

cigars.about: A short 4 x 44 Habano-wrapped cigar with Nicaraguan long filler, built as a quick smoke and sold by Padilla in bundles of 25.
cigars.researchNote: Padilla does not say where the Habano wrapper is grown, and the binder, factory and country of manufacture are not published.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made with AGANORSA tobaccos under a Corojo rosado wrapper, launched in 2022 for international markets. It is named for the home city of Daniel Guerrero, who owns the Cósigna factory where it is rolled.
cigars.researchNote: Made for international markets, starting with Germany and Latvia, so a US guest is unlikely to have seen it. Ernesto Padilla described it as medium body. Sold in boxes of 20.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua, Honduras (mixed long and short filler)
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Honduran Habano (also Habano Maduro and Ecuadorian Connecticut versions)
cigars.about: Padilla's budget bundle cigar, a Cuban-sandwich smoke made from long and short filler left over from the brand's premium blends. It comes in Habano, Maduro and Connecticut wrappers.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed filler, not all long filler. Three wrappers are sold: Honduran Habano, a Honduran Habano Maduro, and Ecuadorian Connecticut. Blend details come from the retailer Famous Smoke Shop, not from Padilla.

cigars.about: An Ecuadorian Habano-wrapped line that Ernesto Padilla introduced in 2012 and had made by Oliva in Esteli. The Toro scored 93 points and ranked No. 12 on Cigar Aficionado's Top 25 of 2014.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the binder: Cigar Aficionado and Holt's list Nicaragua, while halfwheel lists Ecuadorian Habano. A separate Reserva Maduro also existed. It is no longer in Padilla's own store, and Holt's closeout stock is sold out.

cigars.about: A 7.5 x 40 lancero from Principle's Archive Collection that pays tribute to New York City in 1842, the year fresh water reached Manhattan. Each box includes an original New York and Harlem Railroad certificate issued that year.
cigars.researchNote: Principle does not name the factory or give a strength for this cigar. Most Principle cigars are rolled at Kelner Boutique Factory in the Dominican Republic. Principle says it marks 180 years since 1842, which puts the release in 2022.

cigars.about: A near Zimbabwe puro from Principle's Archive Collection, with Zimbabwean wrapper, binder and most of the filler plus a little Dominican piloto. It comes in boxes of five with a real Zimbabwe 20 billion dollar banknote.
cigars.researchNote: Zimbabwean wrapper is rare and fits none of the usual wrapper categories. Principle does not name the factory, the release year or a strength rating for this cigar. Principle's shop writes the name as Five-Twenty.

cigars.about: The Sazerac companion in Principle's Cocktail Collection, a series of cigars each built around a classic drink. It takes its name and New Orleans theme from the French Quarter pastry.
cigars.researchNote: Principle does not publish the blend, size, factory or strength for the Beignet. It is sold in boxes of 20.

cigars.about: The Negroni companion in Principle's Cocktail Collection, a series of cigars each built around a classic drink. Principle describes it as earthy and woody, meant to ground the drink's bitter orange.
cigars.researchNote: Principle does not publish the blend, size, factory or strength for The Count. It is sold in boxes of 20.

cigars.about: The Mai Tai companion in Principle's Cocktail Collection, a 5 x 50 robusto rolled at Kelner Boutique Factory in the Dominican Republic. It uses an Ecuadorian Habano 2000 wrapper over Dominican and US tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: Principle's shop page carries a tasting note that calls it full bodied with medium strength.

cigars.about: The Espresso Martini companion in Principle's Cocktail Collection, a series of cigars each built around a classic drink.
cigars.researchNote: Principle lists the Naomi on its Cocktail Collection page and in its shop but publishes no blend, size, factory, strength or tasting notes for it. It is sold in boxes of 20.

cigars.about: A full-bodied Dominican-made line from Platinum Nova, introduced at the 2026 PCA trade show. It is the first Platinum Nova blend offered in more than one size.
cigars.researchNote: Maker lists the wrapper as H2000 Oscuro; halfwheel describes it as a dark Ecuadorian habano. Sold in boxes of 10.

cigars.about: The 6 x 54 toro in Platinum Nova's Batch collection, with a dark San Andres wrapper over Dominican binder and filler. It joined the regular lineup in 2019.
cigars.researchNote: One size of the Batch collection; each Batch size is a different blend. Maker says Medium to Full, Neptune lists Medium.

cigars.about: The 6 x 54 torpedo in Platinum Nova's Batch collection, a Dominican blend under an Ecuadorian Habano 2000 wrapper. It joined the regular lineup in 2019.
cigars.researchNote: One size of the Batch collection; each Batch size is a different blend.

cigars.about: A mild 5 x 54 robusto in Platinum Nova's Batch collection with a Connecticut shade wrapper and a lightly sweetened tip. It is made in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: The cap is lightly sweetened. The maker only says Connecticut shade; the USA origin comes from Neptune. halfwheel's 2019 listing of the Batch Robusto showed an Ecuadorian Habano 2000 wrapper instead.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro robusto in Platinum Nova's Batch collection, introduced at the 2022 PCA trade show. It was the first Nicaraguan-made cigar in the Batch series.
cigars.researchNote: Made in Nicaragua, not at the Dominican factory. Neptune lists El Puente Cigars as the factory, but halfwheel says the Toro in this blend is made at Barrera Cigars in Esteli, so the factory is left blank. Neptune calls the wrapper a maduro and lists strength as Full.

cigars.about: The 6 x 54 toro version of Platinum Nova's Batch Nicaragua blend, a Nicaraguan puro added at the 2024 PCA trade show. It is made in Esteli, Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Same blend as the Batch Robusto Nicaragua in a larger size. halfwheel names Barrera Cigars in Esteli as the factory and Jalapa as the wrapper region; the maker's page only says Nicaragua.

cigars.about: The Dominican version of Platinum Nova's 484, a short 4 x 48 cigar sold in soft packs of four. The name comes from the 48 x 4 size.
cigars.researchNote: Maker calls it Medium Plus; Neptune's spec table says Medium. The 484 comes in two blends, this Dominican one and a Nicaraguan one.

cigars.about: The Nicaraguan version of Platinum Nova's 484, a short 4 x 48 cigar sold in soft packs of four. It was among the company's first cigars made in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Made in Nicaragua; the factory name comes from Neptune only. The Esteli binder and Jalapa filler regions come from Cigar Coop; the maker just says Nicaragua. There is also a Dominican 484.

cigars.about: A 7 x 50 Churchill from Platinum Nova named for the five boroughs of New York City. It was the company's first cigar to use a double binder.
cigars.researchNote: Double binder: halfwheel lists Colombian Cubita plus a Corojo of undisclosed origin. Sold in boxes of five, each cigar named for a New York borough, all the same blend.

cigars.about: A 5 x 70 perfecto from Platinum Nova shaped and decorated to look like a football. It has a Habano 2000 wrapper over Dominican binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel and Neptune call it a limited release of 250 boxes of 11, though the maker still sells it. halfwheel listed it as Champion Series Football with an Ecuadorian Habano 2000 CT wrapper.

cigars.about: A 5 1/2 x 50 robusto from Platinum Nova's core lineup with an Ecuadorian Habano 2000 wrapper over Dominican binder and filler. It debuted with the regular production range in 2019.
cigars.researchNote: Maker rates it Mild to Medium and also calls it medium bodied; Neptune's spec table says Medium.

cigars.about: A 6 x 50 toro from Platinum Nova with a dark, double-fermented Ecuadorian oscuro wrapper over Dominican tobaccos. It debuted with the regular production range in 2019.
cigars.researchNote: Maker says Medium to Full; Neptune lists Full.

cigars.about: A 7 x 43 pigtail lancero from Platinum Nova with a light chestnut Ecuadorian wrapper over Dominican binder and filler. The maker pitches it as a creamy morning cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Maker bills it as light and creamy but also calls it medium bodied; Neptune lists Medium. Maker gives the wrapper as H2000 CT Ecuador; Neptune's spec table says Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade.

cigars.about: A full-bodied 6 x 54 toro released in 2021 as the follow-up to Leo X, the cigar that marked CEO Leonor "Leo" Abzaradel's tenth year in the business. It was the company's first cigar made in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel announced it as a limited edition in boxes of 11, but its show report listed regular production and the maker still sells it. The factory name comes from Neptune only; halfwheel said the Nicaraguan factory was undisclosed.

cigars.about: A medium-bodied 6 1/4 x 56 cigar launched at the 2022 PCA trade show to mark CEO Leonor "Leo" Abzaradel's 12th year in the business. Unlike the Leo 11, it is made in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel listed it as regular production in boxes of 12 and the maker still sells it; Neptune and Cigar Coop call it a limited edition. The factory name comes from Neptune.

cigars.about: A 6 x 60 big ring gauge cigar from Platinum Nova with a dark Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Dominican binder and filler. It debuted with the regular production range in 2019.
cigars.researchNote: Maker says Medium to Full; Neptune's spec table says Medium.

cigars.about: A box-pressed 6 1/4 x 55 torpedo from Platinum Nova with a dark Mexican San Andres wrapper over Dominican binder and filler. It debuted with the regular production range in 2019.
cigars.researchNote: Maker says Medium to Full; Neptune lists Full. Flavor words come from Neptune, since the maker publishes none.

cigars.about: A 7 1/4 x 54 torpedo from Platinum Nova introduced at the 2023 PCA trade show. It is named after the exoplanet Trappist-1g, whose color resembles the brand's signature shade.
cigars.researchNote: Maker lists a broadleaf binder and Dominican filler; halfwheel reported the reverse, a Dominican binder and Pennsylvania broadleaf filler. Maker says Medium to Full; Neptune lists Medium.

cigars.about: A 5 x 43 pigtail corona from Platinum Nova's Limited Edition series, the company's first releases, which shipped in early 2019. It pairs an Ecuadorian wrapper with Dominican binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: One of six Limited Edition sizes, each its own blend; halfwheel reported 3,000 cigars per size in boxes of 12. Maker writes the wrapper as Ecuador 2000, its shorthand for Habano 2000 on other lines. Maker rates it Medium to Full and also calls it medium bodied; Neptune lists Medium.

cigars.about: A box-pressed 5 1/2 x 52 cigar from Platinum Nova's Limited Edition series, which first shipped in early 2019. It uses a Habano 2000 wrapper, a Nicaraguan Esteli binder and Dominican filler.
cigars.researchNote: One of six Limited Edition sizes, each its own blend; halfwheel reported 3,000 cigars per size in boxes of 12. Maker calls it Medium Plus; Neptune lists Medium. The wrapper's country of origin is not published.

cigars.about: A 6 1/4 x 54 cigar from Platinum Nova's Limited Edition series, which first shipped in early 2019. It has an Ecuadorian wrapper over a Nicaraguan Esteli binder and Dominican filler.
cigars.researchNote: One of six Limited Edition sizes, each its own blend; halfwheel reported 3,000 cigars per size in boxes of 12. Maker writes the wrapper as Ecuador 2000, its shorthand for Habano 2000 on other lines. Maker says Medium to Full; Neptune lists Medium.

cigars.about: A short 4 1/2 x 56 perfecto from Platinum Nova's Limited Edition series, which first shipped in early 2019. It uses a Nicaraguan Rojiza 2000 wrapper and binder over Dominican filler.
cigars.researchNote: One of six Limited Edition sizes, each its own blend; halfwheel reported 3,000 cigars per size in boxes of 12. Maker says Medium to Full; Neptune lists Medium. The maker calls the wrapper Rojiza 2000 and does not name the seed.

cigars.about: A 6 x 50 toro from Platinum Nova's Limited Edition series, which first shipped in early 2019. It has a dark San Andres wrapper over a Dominican Piloto binder and Dominican filler.
cigars.researchNote: One of six Limited Edition sizes, each its own blend; halfwheel reported 3,000 cigars per size in boxes of 12. Maker says Medium to Full; Neptune lists Medium.

cigars.about: A 5 1/2 x 55 torpedo from Platinum Nova's Limited Edition series, which first shipped in early 2019. It has a Habano 2000 wrapper over Dominican binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: One of six Limited Edition sizes, each its own blend; halfwheel reported 3,000 cigars per size in boxes of 12. The wrapper's country of origin is not published.

cigars.about: A box-pressed toro sold in a square tube, named after founder Nick Fusco's grandfather Gonzalo "Pepe" Torre. It is made for El Mago at Miguel Pinto's MGE Cigars Factory in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium-strong; Cigar Coop rated it medium strength with medium to full body, and Neptune lists medium. Cigar Dojo and Cigar Coop listed Pepe among the 2022 debut cigars, but halfwheel dates the box-pressed tubo to May 2023.

cigars.about: El Mago's first robusto, a box-pressed cigar with a Cameroon wrapper. The name is Spanish for mystical and refers to the bond between the founder's grandparents.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune says the Cameroon wrapper is capped at the head and foot with a lighter shade leaf. Cigar Dojo's 2022 launch list showed a Místico with a two-tone San Andrés wrapper; the Cameroon robusto shipped in 2023.

cigars.about: El Mago's mild Connecticut toro, one of the brand's 2022 debut cigars and sold in tubes. The name is Spanish for triumphant.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers sell it as Triunfante Connecticut. The country the Corojo binder is grown in is not published.

cigars.about: The Habano-wrapped toro from El Mago's 2022 debut lineup, sold in tubes. Its packaging is modeled on The James Hotel, the Miami Beach Art Deco hotel the founder's grandfather owned.
cigars.researchNote: The maker and Neptune call it medium; Cigar Dojo listed it as mild-medium at launch.

cigars.about: The maduro toro from El Mago's 2022 debut lineup, sold in tubes. It has a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over a Sumatra binder and filler from Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium to full; Neptune lists it as medium. The country the Sumatra binder is grown in is not published.

cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped toro in a tube, released in 2023 as a nod to Miami-Cuban culture. The founder's grandfather was born in Cuba.
cigars.researchNote: The maker and halfwheel call the wrapper Connecticut destapado without naming a country; Neptune lists it as U.S. Connecticut Shade. The medium strength comes from Neptune only.

cigars.about: El Mago's lancero, with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over a Criollo binder. Neptune says the name comes from a lotus flower painting by the founder's grandmother, Maria Torre.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune describes the wrapper as Ecuadorian Habano maduro. The medium strength comes from Neptune only.

cigars.about: A thick 5 1/2 x 56 maduro that the maker bills as a bold, full-bodied smoke. Neptune describes it as the strongest cigar in the El Mago range.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it full-bodied and Neptune's write-up calls it the strongest El Mago, though Neptune's spec table lists medium.

cigars.about: A 6 x 48 "thin toro" in a round tube with a Nicaraguan-grown Sumatra wrapper. It shipped in April 2024 in boxes of 14.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel and Cigar Coop reported a limited edition of 1,000 boxes of 14, and Cigar Coop said in 2025 that the run had ended and Jaguar replaced it. The maker still shows it and Neptune still stocks it.

cigars.about: El Mago's first 6 x 60, sold in round tubes in boxes of 10. It is named for the disco era that shaped Miami nightlife when the founder's grandparents moved there.
cigars.researchNote: The maker and halfwheel say the binder is Criollo; Neptune's spec table says Corojo. The full strength comes from Neptune; the maker only calls it bold, spicy and smooth.

cigars.about: A small-batch 3 1/2 x 50 short robusto sold as a three-pack in a box made to look like a deck of cards. The box art shows a wizard lighting a cigar with a dragon's flame.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it a rare batch and only says it is Nicaraguan and medium; the wrapper and binder come from Neptune, which says just 500 boxes were made. Neptune also sells an Alakazam 2.0 Churchill at 7 x 50.

cigars.about: A box-pressed toro in a square tube that began shipping in summer 2025 as a regular production cigar. It is named after the old Jaguar the founder's grandmother drove him around in as a child.
cigars.researchNote: The full strength comes from Neptune only; the maker has not published a strength.

cigars.about: A value-priced box-pressed robusto sold in 25-count bundles. The name recalls the founder smoking cigars on the beach with his grandfather.
cigars.researchNote: Cigar Dojo reports it was made in limited quantities before joining the regular lineup in February 2026. The company describes it as medium to full bodied.

cigars.about: One of four James Avenue blends, all 6 x 54 box-pressed toros sold in boxes of 20. The line is named for the Miami Beach street where the founder's grandfather owned The James Hotel.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel says the countries of the wrapper and Habano binder are undisclosed; Cigar Dojo reports the binder is Nicaraguan. No strength is published. Each James Avenue blend has its own binder and filler recipe.

cigars.about: One of four James Avenue blends, all 6 x 54 box-pressed toros sold in boxes of 20. The line is named for the Miami Beach street where the founder's grandfather owned The James Hotel.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel says the countries of the wrapper and Criollo binder are undisclosed; Cigar Dojo reports the binder is Nicaraguan. No strength is published. Each James Avenue blend has its own binder and filler recipe.

cigars.about: One of four James Avenue blends, all 6 x 54 box-pressed toros sold in boxes of 20. The line is named for the Miami Beach street where the founder's grandfather owned The James Hotel.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel says the country of the Sumatra-seed binder is undisclosed; Cigar Dojo reports the binder is Ecuadorian. No strength is published. Each James Avenue blend has its own binder and filler recipe.

cigars.about: One of four James Avenue blends, all 6 x 54 box-pressed toros sold in boxes of 20. The line is named for the Miami Beach street where the founder's grandfather owned The James Hotel.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel says the countries of the wrapper and Corojo binder are undisclosed; Cigar Dojo reports the binder is Ecuadorian. No strength is published. Each James Avenue blend has its own binder and filler recipe.

cigars.about: The "sword" half of a two-cigar limited release from July 2026, banded in gold and built around a Sumatra wrapper as the bolder of the pair. It was blended to go with The Defender.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 250 boxes of 20 and offered to retailers only together with The Defender. The company says it will not be made again. Medium strength comes from Neptune only; the maker calls it the bolder of the two.

cigars.about: The "shield" half of a two-cigar limited release from July 2026, banded in purple with a Cameroon wrapper as the smoother of the pair. It was blended to go with The Offender.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 250 boxes of 20 and offered to retailers only together with The Offender. The company says it will not be made again. Medium strength comes from Neptune only.

cigars.about: The first release in El Mago's Collectible Tin Series, a 5 x 50 box-pressed robusto that shipped in March 2026. The series was inspired by a vintage tobacco tin the founder found while thrifting.
cigars.researchNote: Tin #1 of a planned seven. Sold in five-count collectible tins, limited to 1,000 tins (5,000 cigars), and offered first to El Mago's invite-only S-Tier retailers. The company calls it mild to medium; Neptune lists medium.

cigars.about: The second release in El Mago's Collectible Tin Series, a 5 x 50 box-pressed robusto that shipped in March 2026. It uses the same San Andrés maduro wrapper as Oyama Omen over a broadleaf binder.
cigars.researchNote: Tin #2 of a planned seven. Sold in five-count collectible tins, limited to 1,000 tins (5,000 cigars), and offered first to El Mago's invite-only S-Tier retailers. Strength is unsettled: the company says slightly stronger than the mild-to-medium Oyama Omen, while Neptune lists full.

cigars.about: The third release in El Mago's Collectible Tin Series, a 5 x 50 box-pressed robusto that shipped in May 2026. The company describes it as full-bodied.
cigars.researchNote: Tin #3 of a planned seven. Sold in five-count collectible tins, limited to 1,000 tins (5,000 cigars), and offered first to El Mago's invite-only S-Tier retailers.

cigars.about: The fourth release in El Mago's Collectible Tin Series, a 5 x 50 box-pressed robusto with a Corojo wrapper that shipped in May 2026. halfwheel scored it 86.
cigars.researchNote: Tin #4 of a planned seven. Sold in five-count collectible tins, limited to 1,000 tins (5,000 cigars), and offered first to El Mago's invite-only S-Tier retailers. The company calls it medium-bodied; halfwheel's review found medium-full body with strength just under medium.

cigars.about: The Connecticut shade version of United Cigars' house line, built on the same Dominican broadleaf blend as the other United cigars. It is made at Tabacalera Magia Cubana in the Dominican Republic and debuted at the 2024 PCA show.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as United Connecticut. No clear strength rating: the maker's text calls it a milder smoke, but the meter graphic on its page sits past medium. It launched in three sizes; the 6 x 28 Pencil appears only on the maker's page.

cigars.about: The San Andrés maduro version of United Cigars' house line, made at Tabacalera Magia Cubana in the Dominican Republic. The line dates to 2010 and was reblended in 2023 when it changed from box-pressed to round.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as United Maduro. The maker calls it medium-plus. Its page text mentions Brazilian Mata Fina filler and a Cuban-seed Habano binder, but its own blend table and halfwheel list an all-Dominican binder and filler. Box-pressed until 2023, round since.

cigars.about: The Ecuadorian Habano version of United Cigars' house line, made at Tabacalera Magia Cubana in the Dominican Republic. It took over the spot long held by United Natural in the lineup.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as United Sungrown, formerly United Natural; guests may know the old name. Launched in 2010 box-pressed and reblended as a round cigar in 2023. The maker's text only says bold; its meter sits a little past medium and Two Guys calls it medium strength.

cigars.about: A value bundle cigar from United Cigars with a Cameroon wrapper over a Dominican binder and filler. It is one of four Classic bundles that share the same blend and differ only in wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in bundles of 20. Mild to medium on both the maker's meter and Two Guys' meter, though Two Guys' text says medium bodied. The maker does not name the factory or the country.

cigars.about: A value bundle cigar from United Cigars with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over a Dominican binder and filler. The maker describes it as the milder morning cigar of the four Classic bundles, which share one blend and differ only in wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in bundles of 20. The maker calls it a milder cigar and its page meter sits between mild and medium. The maker does not name the factory or the country.

cigars.about: A value bundle cigar from United Cigars with a Cuban-seed Habano wrapper grown in Ecuador over a Dominican binder and filler. It is one of four Classic bundles that share the same blend and differ only in wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Contains no Cuban tobacco; the name refers to the Cuban-seed wrapper grown in Ecuador. Sold in bundles of 20. Mild to medium on both the maker's meter and Two Guys' meter; the factory is not named.

cigars.about: A value bundle cigar from United Cigars with a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper over a Dominican binder and filler. It is one of four Classic bundles that share the same blend and differ only in wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in bundles of 20. The maker's meter shows mild to medium, the same as the other Classic bundles, though its text calls the Maduro more robust and Two Guys' meter shows medium. The maker does not name the factory or the country.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan cigar made by Perdomo for United Cigars and named for the Garofalo family, which owns United and Two Guys Smoke Shop. This version wears an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over aged Nicaraguan tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: United's meter sits a little past medium and Two Guys' meter shows medium, though Two Guys' text calls it mild to medium. halfwheel lists the Torpedo at 6 1/2 x 54, while United and Two Guys list 6 x 54.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made by Perdomo for United Cigars and named for the Garofalo family, which owns United and Two Guys Smoke Shop. This version uses a Nicaraguan maduro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: United's text calls it full-bodied, but the meter on the same page sits between medium and full and Two Guys rates it 5 of 10. halfwheel lists the Torpedo at 6 1/2 x 54, while United and Two Guys list 6 x 54.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made by Perdomo for United Cigars and named for the Garofalo family, which owns United and Two Guys Smoke Shop. This version uses a Nicaraguan sun grown wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: United calls it medium to full. halfwheel lists the Torpedo at 6 1/2 x 54, while United and Two Guys list 6 x 54.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Ligero, Criollo '98, Corojo '98), USA (Connecticut Broadleaf)
cigars.about: A Dominican-made cigar from United Cigars, rolled by the Ventura family, with an Ecuadorian Habano 2000 wrapper and some Connecticut broadleaf in the filler. It began as a limited edition honoring Navy SEAL families and became a regular line in 2025.
cigars.researchNote: First released in 2024 as a 6 x 54 limited edition; regular production since March 2025. United's meter reads medium to full, but halfwheel's review found the strength a little under medium. United lists the Gordo at 6.5 x 60; halfwheel says 6 x 60.

cigars.about: A full-bodied cigar created by United Cigars with Arnold André for the 250th anniversary of the United States, made in the Dominican Republic. It comes in 12-count metal tins that double as an ashtray.
cigars.researchNote: The blend debuted earlier in 2026 as the limited Independence Firecracker; the Robusto and Toro followed on September 1, 2026 as regular production. United's page still describes the line as a limited celebration.

cigars.about: A Honduran puro made for United Cigars by the Eiroa family at the Aladino factory in Las Lomas, Jamastran, using only tobacco from Julio Eiroa's farm. The name means grandfather and the sizes are named for family members.
cigars.researchNote: United calls it medium to full; halfwheel's review of the Nieto found strength and body both at medium. halfwheel lists the Nieta at 5 1/4 x 44, while United lists a 46 ring.

cigars.about: A short, value-priced Connecticut shade cigar from United Cigars, made at Tabacalera Magia Cubana in the Dominican Republic and sold in boxes of 50. It was relaunched in 2022 around an aged Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The brand dates to 2006 under Victor Vitale; United bought it in 2013 and relaunched it with a new blend in 2022. Strength is read from the meter on United's page; halfwheel found plenty of flavor but very little nicotine.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Connecticut, Habano or Maduro (three versions)
cigars.about: A budget Dominican cigar from United Cigars, sold 50 to a box in one 6 x 45 size with a choice of Connecticut, Habano or Maduro wrapper. The maker openly pitches it as an inexpensive everyday smoke rather than a first-quality cigar.
cigars.researchNote: One name covers three wrapper versions, so check which one is in the box. The maker says outright that these are not first quality cigars. Strength is read from the single meter graphic on the maker's page.

cigars.about: A Connecticut shade cigar from the German company Arnold André, rolled at its own factory in Santiago, Dominican Republic, and distributed in the U.S. by United Cigars. It is the lighter of the two Montosa blends.
cigars.researchNote: An Arnold André brand distributed in the U.S. by United since 2022; sold in Europe as Montosa Claro. Arnold André calls it mild to medium per halfwheel, though United's text says medium bodied. The binder is Mexican San Andrés per halfwheel, Mexican Sumatra per Arnold André.

cigars.about: The darker, fuller Montosa blend from the German company Arnold André, with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper. It is rolled at Arnold André's factory in Santiago, Dominican Republic, and distributed in the U.S. by United Cigars.
cigars.researchNote: An Arnold André brand distributed in the U.S. by United since 2022. United calls it fuller bodied than the Natural and its meter sits a little past medium, while Two Guys rates it 3 of 10. halfwheel also lists dark fired Kentucky in the filler, which United does not.

cigars.about: A Dominican-made cigar from the German company Arnold André whose filler includes Brazilian Araperique, a tobacco aged under pressure in oak whiskey barrels in the perique style. United Cigars distributes it in the U.S.
cigars.researchNote: An Arnold André brand; United is the U.S. distributor (since 2022). United's blend table leaves out the Nicaraguan filler that Arnold André lists. The Belicoso is 6.2 x 50 per Arnold André, but United's page lists 6.5 x 60.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, Brazil, Nicaragua, USA (Dark Fired Kentucky)
cigars.about: A Dominican-made cigar from the German company Arnold André that blends fire-cured Kentucky tobacco, dried over smoldering oak and hickory, into the filler for a smoky note. United Cigars distributes it in the U.S.
cigars.researchNote: An Arnold André brand; United is the U.S. distributor (since 2022). Binder is Bahia Sumatra per Arnold André, but United's page says Bahia Ecuadorian. The Belicoso is 6.2 x 50 per Arnold André, but United's page lists 6.5 x 60.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped blend in the signature line of Dominican cigar maker Jose Dominguez, made at the Magia Cubana factory in Santiago and distributed by United Cigars since 2018. Part of the tobacco is grown by the Dominguez family.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is read from the meter graphic on United's page, where it sits at the low end of medium. United lists Nicaraguan filler for this blend; halfwheel and Two Guys list only Dominican and Pennsylvania broadleaf. halfwheel calls the line Signature Series.

cigars.about: The San Andrés maduro blend in the signature line of Dominican cigar maker Jose Dominguez, made at the Magia Cubana factory in Santiago and distributed by United Cigars since 2018. It is the bolder of the two Signature blends.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is read from the meter graphic on United's page. United lists Pennsylvania broadleaf in the filler; halfwheel and Two Guys list only Nicaraguan and Dominican filler for the Maduro. halfwheel calls the line Signature Series.

cigars.about: A Dominican cigar created by Carlos Guillermo and made at the Magia Cubana factory, with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Dominican tobaccos. United Cigars brought it to the U.S. in 2022 and sells it in boxes of 15.
cigars.researchNote: Carlos Guillermo's brand, launched in the Dominican Republic in 2019 and distributed in the U.S. by United since 2022. halfwheel and retailers call the line simply Yaya. United calls it medium to full, while Two Guys' meter shows medium.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Condega, Ometepe, Pueblo Nuevo, Masatepe Chincagre)
cigars.about: A collaboration between Definition founder Jamond Hackley and Luciano Meirelles, rolled at the Luciano Cigars factory in Esteli. It debuted at the 2023 PCA show in one size and gained a toro and a lancero in 2024.
cigars.researchNote: First announced as Genesis, then renamed GEN413. The wrapper is an Ecuadorian broadleaf hybrid that the maker writes as Habano-Ecuador Broadleaf. The maker describes it as medium bodied.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Condega, Ometepe, Pueblo Nuevo, Masatepe Chincagre)
cigars.about: A follow-up to the GEN 413 made with Luciano Meirelles that swaps the original's wrapper and binder, putting San Andrés on the outside. It was introduced at the 2025 PCA show.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's page reuses the original GEN 413 text, so its summary line shows the old wrapper and binder and the medium-bodied rating is carried over. Its blend section and halfwheel both give San Andrés over the Ecuadorian hybrid binder. The 6 x 54 size is from halfwheel.

cigars.about: One of Definition's earliest blends, a box-pressed Ecuadorian Habano over Nicaraguan tobacco released in fall 2019. It was the company's first cigar that was not a maduro.
cigars.researchNote: Sold on the maker's site as Prolific BP (box pressed). The factory is not published.

cigars.about: A San Andrés maduro version of Definition's Prolific, planned for the company's seven-year anniversary in January 2026 and pushed back by production timing. The maker says it is a step up in strength from the Habano original.
cigars.researchNote: The maker has not published the binder, filler, size or a strength rating for this one.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro that Definition positions at the top of its lineup, released in spring 2022. The maker rates it medium-plus to full.
cigars.researchNote: The maker gives the wrapper only as Nicaragua, with no leaf type. The 6.5 x 54 is sold as The Chairman Toro.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro built around aged ligero leaf, which is where the name comes from (Definition plus ligero). Definition calls it the strongest cigar it makes and says it burns slowly.
cigars.researchNote: Pronounced Deaf-A-Hairo. The maker calls it its strongest offering but files it under both Medium and Full Bodied in its shop.

cigars.about: A blend first rolled for a private celebration on September 19, 2020, with no plan to sell it. Feedback from the guests led Definition to release it to the market that winter.
cigars.researchNote: Part of the 919 Series. The maker dates the release to winter 2020/2021 and does not publish a strength rating.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Definition's 919, using an Ecuadorian maduro wrapper in place of the Habano. The 919 name marks the September 19, 2020 celebration the blend was first made for.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's page lists the filler as Nicaragua in one place and Nicaragua and Honduras in another. No strength rating or release year is published for the Maduro.

cigars.about: A box-pressed salomon from Definition, named because the shape looks like a baseball bat. It was released in summer 2021 and comes in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish a strength rating or the factory.

cigars.about: The maduro version of The Goods, a box-pressed salomon shaped like a baseball bat. Definition released it in summer 2024 and sells it in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Strength comes from the maker's shop, which files it under Full Bodied.

cigars.about: A full-bodied Ecuadorian maduro launched in summer 2020 as a tribute to The Nobility, Definition's first cigar. The name comes from the maker's line that we are all equal in the end.
cigars.researchNote: The maker describes it as full-bodied. The factory is not published.

cigars.about: A full-strength San Andrés cigar made for Definition's first anniversary in January 2020 and built around tobacco from the Concepcion area of Ometepe, Nicaragua. It left regular production in 2022 and now returns each September.
cigars.researchNote: No longer regular production: the maker pulled it in 2022 and now releases it every September at the start of the NFL season, with a burgundy band for the Washington Commanders. Sold as Conception Box Pressed Toro.

cigars.about: A medium-bodied Cameroon-wrapped cigar over Nicaraguan tobacco, released in summer 2020. Founder Jamond Hackley named it after the neo-noir films he was watching during the pandemic.
cigars.researchNote: Also called Noir Cameroon, to tell it apart from Noir Connecticut. The maker lists the wrapper only as Cameroon.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped member of Definition's Noir pair, which the maker rates mild to medium. It uses an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it mild to medium. No separate release year is published for the Connecticut version.

cigars.about: A short, fat maduro perfecto from Definition. The blend was first made as a 6 x 60 and then moved to the pig shape to give it a different look from the Equalizer.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's blend table says 4.5 x 60, while its story text mentions a 4.25 inch length. No strength rating or release year is published. Boxes hold 24.

cigars.about: Definition's dedicated lancero, an Ecuadorian maduro over Nicaraguan tobacco released in January 2021. The maker says it took seven attempts to get the blend right.
cigars.researchNote: Only made as a lancero, in boxes of 30. The maker describes it as bold but smooth and gives no formal strength rating.

cigars.about: A dark, box-pressed cigar released in 2025 and the first Definition blend to use Pennsylvania broadleaf. Anillo is Spanish for ring, a nod to the fabric bands the brand is known for.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's site lists it at 6 x 54 and calls it medium-bodied. halfwheel lists 6 1/4 x 54 and found medium strength building to medium-full, with medium-full body. The factory is undisclosed.

cigars.about: A San Andrés toro introduced at the 2026 PCA show and named for the pivot foot in basketball. The 5 honors Jalen Rose's jersey number and the kelly green band honors Slippery Rock University.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists it as 6 x 54, while halfwheel's trade show report listed 6 x 52. Also written DC Pi5ot. No strength rating is published.

cigars.about: A San Andrés toro introduced at the 2026 PCA show and named for the house number of founder Jamond Hackley's grandparents' home. halfwheel scored it 87.
cigars.researchNote: Strength and body are from halfwheel's review, which found mild to medium nicotine strength with medium body and fuller flavor. The maker gives no rating. The factory is undisclosed.

cigars.about: A box-pressed maduro made to mark the fifth anniversary of Definition Cigars, which launched in 2019. The maker describes it as full flavored and full bodied.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is secret: the maker lists wrapper, binder and filler as unavailable. The maker also writes the name as 5 Años and does not say how limited it is.

cigars.about: A limited edition that Definition blended with input from a select group of its customers, built around the idea of community and family. The maker rates it medium-plus to full.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is secret: the maker lists the wrapper, binder and filler as Passion, Loyalty and Gratitude. Also called DC Kinsman LE.

cigars.about: A San Andrés cigar made with Preston Gray, owner of Tailored Smoke Cigar Lounge, to mark the lounge's 10th anniversary. Unlike most lounge exclusives, it is also sold through Definition's own store.
cigars.researchNote: Created as an anniversary cigar for Tailored Smoke Cigar Lounge. The maker does not publish the size, strength, release year or how limited it is.

cigars.about: An amaretto flavored cigar in the Tatiana line from Miami Cigar & Co., rolled at La Aurora. The Classic corona and Mini tin sizes were added in 2026 alongside the older Dolce.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers vary on strength: Neptune lists it Mild, and Famous Smoke lists some Tatiana cigars Mild and others Mild-Medium.

cigars.about: A cappuccino flavored cigar in the Tatiana line from Miami Cigar & Co., rolled at La Aurora. The Classic corona and Mini tin sizes were added in 2026 alongside the older Dolce.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers vary on strength: Neptune lists it Mild, and Famous Smoke lists some Tatiana cigars Mild and others Mild-Medium.

cigars.about: A flavored Tatiana corona from Miami Cigar & Co. with mint, rum and citrus flavoring. It was introduced at the 2018 IPCPR trade show and comes in one size.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke lists it Mild-Medium on the item page but Mild on its Tatiana Classic page; Neptune lists the same blend in other flavors as Mild. Halfwheel's 2018 launch report called it a Dominican puro, but later halfwheel reports and retailers give an Indonesian wrapper.

cigars.about: The cherry flavored cigar in the Tatiana line from Miami Cigar & Co., one of the core flavors of the brand. Made for Miami Cigar & Co. by La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers vary on strength: Neptune lists it Mild, and Famous Smoke lists some Tatiana cigars Mild and others Mild-Medium.

cigars.about: The chocolate flavored cigar in the Tatiana line from Miami Cigar & Co., one of the core flavors of the brand. Made for Miami Cigar & Co. by La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers vary on strength: Neptune lists it Mild, and Famous Smoke lists some Tatiana cigars Mild and others Mild-Medium.

cigars.about: A cinnamon flavored cigar in the Tatiana line from Miami Cigar & Co. Made for Miami Cigar & Co. by La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers vary on strength: Neptune lists it Mild, and Famous Smoke lists some Tatiana cigars Mild and others Mild-Medium.

cigars.about: A cognac flavored cigar in the Tatiana line from Miami Cigar & Co., added to the brand in 2010. Made for Miami Cigar & Co. by La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers vary on strength: Neptune lists it Mild, and Famous Smoke lists some Tatiana cigars Mild and others Mild-Medium.

cigars.about: A Tatiana line from Miami Cigar & Co. that is not infused. It is a traditional Connecticut blend in full sizes with only a sweetened cap, made by La Aurora.
cigars.researchNote: Not a flavored cigar like the rest of Tatiana: only the cap is sweetened.

cigars.about: A multi-flavor Tatiana cigar from Miami Cigar & Co. flavored with passion fruit, vanilla and cognac. It joined the brand in 2011 as part of the Trio series.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers vary on strength: Neptune lists it Mild, and Famous Smoke lists some Tatiana cigars Mild and others Mild-Medium. Some retailers sell it as Tatiana Trio Fusion Frenzy.

cigars.about: A berry flavored Tatiana cigar from Miami Cigar & Co. with vanilla, honey and cognac flavoring. It is one of the best sellers in the brand and is made by La Aurora.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers vary on strength: Neptune lists it Mild, and Famous Smoke lists some Tatiana cigars Mild and others Mild-Medium. Some retailers sell it as Tatiana Trio Groovy Blue. A 6.25 x 52 Belicoso has been a limited TAA exclusive.

cigars.about: A fall themed Tatiana corona from Miami Cigar & Co. flavored with pumpkin, cinnamon and brown sugar. It was introduced at the 2018 IPCPR trade show and comes in one size.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists it Mild; Famous Smoke lists it Mild-Medium. Halfwheel's 2018 launch report called it a Dominican puro, but later halfwheel reports and retailers give an Indonesian wrapper.

cigars.about: The honey flavored cigar in the Tatiana line from Miami Cigar & Co., one of the core flavors of the brand. Made for Miami Cigar & Co. by La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers vary on strength: Neptune lists it Mild, and Famous Smoke lists some Tatiana cigars Mild and others Mild-Medium.

cigars.about: A mandarin orange flavored Tatiana from Miami Cigar & Co., offered only in the small Dolce and Minis sizes. Made for Miami Cigar & Co. by La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers vary on strength: Neptune lists it Mild, and Famous Smoke lists some Tatiana cigars Mild and others Mild-Medium. Retailers spell it Mandarin.

cigars.about: A coffee and chocolate flavored Tatiana from Miami Cigar & Co., sold in three sizes with their own names. It is made in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers disagree on the blend: Neptune lists a Nicaraguan binder with Mexican and Honduran filler, Famous Smoke lists Dominican filler. Both give a Sumatra wrapper. Neptune says Mild, Famous Mild-Medium.

cigars.about: A multi-flavor Tatiana cigar from Miami Cigar & Co. flavored with vanilla, almond, coffee and cocoa. Made for Miami Cigar & Co. by La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers vary on strength: Neptune lists it Mild, and Famous Smoke lists some Tatiana cigars Mild and others Mild-Medium. Some retailers sell it as Tatiana Trio Night Cap.

cigars.about: The rum flavored cigar in the Tatiana line from Miami Cigar & Co., one of the core flavors of the brand. Made for Miami Cigar & Co. by La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers vary on strength: Neptune lists it Mild, and Famous Smoke lists some Tatiana cigars Mild and others Mild-Medium.

cigars.about: A multi-flavor Tatiana cigar from Miami Cigar & Co. with a sweet dried fruit and candy profile. It joined the brand in 2011 as part of the Trio series.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers vary on strength: Neptune lists it Mild, and Famous Smoke lists some Tatiana cigars Mild and others Mild-Medium. Some retailers sell it as Tatiana Trio Sweet Euphoria.

cigars.about: A tropical flavored Tatiana from Miami Cigar & Co., offered only as the 5 x 30 Dolce cigarillo. Made for Miami Cigar & Co. by La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke lists it Mild-Medium; Neptune lists other Tatiana Dolce flavors as Mild. Sources do not say which fruits the flavor is based on.

cigars.about: The vanilla flavored cigar in the Tatiana line from Miami Cigar & Co., one of the core flavors of the brand. Made for Miami Cigar & Co. by La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers vary on strength: Neptune lists it Mild, and Famous Smoke lists some Tatiana cigars Mild and others Mild-Medium.

cigars.about: A multi-flavor Tatiana cigar from Miami Cigar & Co. flavored with vanilla cream, hazelnut and whiskey. Made for Miami Cigar & Co. by La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers vary on strength: Neptune lists it Mild, and Famous Smoke lists some Tatiana cigars Mild and others Mild-Medium. Some retailers sell it as Tatiana Trio Waking Dream.

cigars.about: A limited flavored toro released in October 2023 for the 25th anniversary of the Tatiana brand. Miami Cigar & Co. made 2,500 boxes of 10 at La Aurora.
cigars.researchNote: The blend and the flavoring are undisclosed. One size only, 25,000 cigars total. Halfwheel rated strength mild-medium; Neptune lists it Mild.

cigars.about: The core line from Philip Wynne's Felipe Gregorio brand, founded in 1990. It is a medium to full Habano blend sold in seven sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not say where the leaf is grown or where it is rolled now. Cigar Aficionado reported in 2014 that the core line had been reblended as a Costa Rican puro made at Wynne's own factory there. A San Andres maduro version is also sold.

cigars.about: A limited line that Felipe Gregorio brings back only every seven years, built around Pelo de Oro, an old Cuban-seed tobacco grown in Costa Rica. The first edition came out in 2007 and the second in 2014.
cigars.researchNote: Blend and sizes are the maker's. Country and factory are for the 2014 edition, a Costa Rican puro per halfwheel; Cigar Aficionado names the factory Fabrica de Tabacos Santa Marta. The 2007 original was made in the Dominican Republic.

cigars.about: An offshoot of the Felipe Gregorio Power line that was reblended and relaunched in 2015 in regular parejo sizes. The Lord Byron size placed 15th on Cigar Coop's 2015 cigar of the year list.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists a San Andres Negro wrapper, Pennsylvania binder and full strength. Cigar Coop's 2015 review listed an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper with Piloto Cubano binder and called it medium to medium-full. Country is from that 2015 review; the maker does not state it.

cigars.about: A medium line Philip Wynne created to mark his fiftieth birthday, named for his birth year. The filler is aged seven years, and two sizes scored 90 in Cigar Aficionado.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel's 2017 trade show report called the wrapper Cuban-seed Costa Rican leaf and listed other sizes (FG 56, 54, 52, 46); the maker lists Ecuadorian Cameroon. Country and the box press are from the retailer the maker links to.

cigars.about: The mild, creamy cigar in the Felipe Gregorio range, with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Dominican tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish where this line is rolled.

cigars.about: A medium to full Felipe Gregorio blend with a Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper, sold in two short, thick sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish where this line is rolled. The Magnum 54 is actually a 55 ring gauge.

cigars.about: A medium to full Felipe Gregorio line whose tobaccos were aged together for more than five years in cedar trunks, which the maker says fuses the blend.
cigars.researchNote: Country is from a 2014 Cigar Aficionado report that Refusion is made in the Dominican Republic; the maker's site does not state it.

cigars.about: A Felipe Gregorio line built around Pelo de Oro, an old Cuban-seed tobacco that Philip Wynne grows in Costa Rica. It first appeared in 2006 and was relaunched in 2014.
cigars.researchNote: The blend has changed over time. The 2014 version was a Costa Rican puro rolled at the Tres Tierras factory in Costa Rica in five sizes (halfwheel); the maker's site now lists a Peruvian filler and two sizes and does not say where it is rolled.

cigars.about: A box-pressed, medium to full Felipe Gregorio line sold as Don Cirilo Reserva Familiar. It starts nutty and floral and builds toward cocoa and espresso.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish where this line is rolled. The No. 2 is a torpedo. A 2014 blog review covered a Maduro version with an Ecuadorian Cameroon maduro wrapper and said the line debuted in 2012.

cigars.about: A medium Felipe Gregorio line best known for its large Salomon figurado. It has an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish where this line is rolled. Older reviews list a different blend under the same wrapper: Nicaraguan Habano 92 binder with Dominican Corojo, Mata Fina and Nicaraguan filler, and more figurado sizes.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Cameroon and Mexican San Andres
cigars.about: A medium to full Felipe Gregorio line that uses two wrapper leaves, Ecuadorian Cameroon and Mexican San Andres. Capas is Spanish for wrappers.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrappers are used, so no single wrapper category fits. The maker does not publish where this line is rolled.

cigars.about: A big ring gauge Felipe Gregorio line with a closed foot and an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. The maker rates it full.
cigars.researchNote: Country is from a 2014 Cigar Aficionado report that Minotaur is made in the Dominican Republic. The maker calls it full; the retailer the maker links to calls it medium-plus and sells it as No. 1 to No. 4 (6.8 x 68, 5 x 60, 4 x 60, 3 x 56).

cigars.about: A medium Felipe Gregorio cigar named for Emperor Haile Selassie, who was known as Ras Tafari before his coronation. A share of the proceeds goes to the Ethiopian Crown Council.
cigars.researchNote: The maker writes the name both as Ras Tafari and Rastafari. The maker does not publish where this line is rolled. The filler is listed as Jamaican Cow Tongue tobacco.

cigars.about: The maduro cigar in Felipe Gregorio's Petrus family, with a Mexican San Andres wrapper. The maker rates it full.
cigars.researchNote: Country is from a 2014 Cigar Aficionado report that the Petrus brand is made in the Dominican Republic; the maker's site does not state it for this line.

cigars.about: A creamy, medium cigar in Felipe Gregorio's Petrus family, with an Ecuadorian HVA wrapper over Corojo binder and Piloto Cubano filler.
cigars.researchNote: Country is from a 2014 Cigar Aficionado report that the Petrus brand is made in the Dominican Republic; the maker's site does not state it for this line.

cigars.binder: Costa Rica (Pelo de Oro, aged 10 years)
cigars.about: A single-size limited edition marking 30 years of Felipe Gregorio, sold in jars of 25. Its filler is a 1998 Honduran crop harvested before Hurricane Mitch stripped the topsoil in Copan.
cigars.researchNote: The factory is undisclosed. halfwheel reported 300 jars of 25 (7,500 cigars) at $40 each, while the maker's site says 500 jars. A later batch has been sold without jars.

cigars.about: A limited Felipe Gregorio release made with tobacco aged 15 years, with the finished cigars rested five more years in cedar trunks. It comes in signed, dated and numbered cabinet boxes of 25.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish where this line is rolled, tasting notes or a release year.

cigars.about: A limited torpedo named after the Bond character from Goldfinger, made with ten-year-old tobaccos. Only 5,000 cigars were made, and it was the first cigar in the series that later produced Octopussy.
cigars.researchNote: Release year is disputed, so it is left blank: Cigar Aficionado and Cigar Journal both say 2012, while the maker's site says 2023. The maker does not publish where this line is rolled.
