cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Habano 2000 Rosado (Coral Red) or Mexican San Andres Negrito (Sepia Maduro)
cigars.about: A limited Bond-themed collector's set from Felipe Gregorio: a carbon fiber humidor of 26 cigars with a matching cutter and lighter. It comes in two blends, Coral Red and Sepia Maduro, with fillers aged seven years.
cigars.researchNote: Two versions, so no single wrapper or strength: Coral Red is medium, Sepia Maduro is fuller. Cigar Aficionado lists Brazilian, Nicaraguan and Dominican filler; the maker says Costa Rica, Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic. 500 boxes of each at $728, billed as Octopussy 2024 but shipped in 2025.

cigars.about: A limited Felipe Gregorio cigar whose tobaccos spend three years in cedar trunks with Bois Bande bark, cocoa beans, vanilla and spices. The one size, Venus, comes in boxes of 24 decorated with Botticelli's Birth of Venus.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's site gives no blend or strength; those come only from the retailer the maker links to, so treat them as unconfirmed. First announced for 2022 and held back for more aging. The maker does not publish where this line is rolled.

cigars.about: A collaboration cigar Felipe Gregorio makes for the Marine Reconnaissance Foundation, which supports the Marine Recon community. It comes in one toro size.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish a strength or where it is rolled.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, Nicaragua, USA (Pennsylvania Broadleaf), Peru
cigars.about: The founding Casdagli line, blended by Hendrik Kelner Jr. at the Kelner Boutique Factory to echo the Cuban cigars the brand began with in the 1990s. It is known for classic and unusual shapes such as the Cotton Tail figurado.
cigars.researchNote: Core sizes use Dominican Cotui. Grand Café wears Brazilian Cubra, Grand Café Maduro Ecuadorian Corojo and 25 Aniversario an Ecuadorian wrapper. 25 Aniversario is a limited yearly release.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Brazilian Cubra (C #1, C #2); Ecuadorian Corojo (C #3, C #1 Maduro); Dominican Cotui (A)
cigars.about: A Casdagli line honoring family patriarch Emmanuel Casdagli, made at the Kelner Boutique Factory in the Dominican Republic. The cigars have a flared, unfinished foot and were blended to pair with teas and citrus flavors.
cigars.researchNote: Each size is its own blend, so there is no single wrapper. C #2 and C #3 are rated medium strength, the others medium to full. Basilica A also has Pennsylvania Broadleaf in the filler.

cigars.about: A set of small Casdagli cigars with coffee names, first made for Swedish coffee shops and meant to be smoked with coffee. They are made at the Kelner Boutique Factory with a Cotui wrapper grown by the Kelner family.
cigars.researchNote: Rosetta Maduro swaps the Cotui wrapper for Ecuadorian Corojo maduro. Ristretto is the strongest, rated medium strength and full body. The maker dates the line to 2016; halfwheel says the Rosetta debuted in 2015.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, Nicaragua; some sizes add USA or Peru
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Brazilian Cubra (Gran Mareva, Mareva Especial); Ecuadorian Corojo (Gran Mareva Gold, Mareva Spalato No. 2); Ecuador (Jure)
cigars.about: Made in partnership with Cigar Club Mareva in Split, Croatia, home of the Cigar Smoking World Championship. Club founder Marko Bilić selects each blend, and most are made by Hendrik Kelner Jr.
cigars.researchNote: Each size is its own blend. Jure is the exception: made at IGM Cigars in Costa Rica with an undisclosed binder and filler. Halfwheel lists Mareva Spalato No. 2 at 5 1/2 x 50; the maker says 6 x 49.

cigars.filler: Peru, Dominican Republic, third leaf undisclosed
cigars.about: A Casdagli line made at IGM Cigars in Costa Rica and named for the POW number of Jeremy Casdagli's grandfather, who stitched coded messages into his embroidery during World War II. Part of each sale goes to the Red Cross.
cigars.researchNote: Partly secret blend: Enigma and Lorenz disclose only the Ecuadorian wrapper, and the other sizes keep a third filler undisclosed. Capped at 4,000 cigars per size a year. The maker's text calls it mild but its spec table says medium. Halfwheel lists Needle at 7 1/2 inches; the maker says 7.

cigars.about: Created for the D'Boiss Club Bespoke lounge in Tallinn, Estonia, and made at IGM Cigars in Costa Rica. It was blended to stand in for scarce Cuban cigars, with a sweet honey and almond character.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are undisclosed; the maker only says they are rare tobaccos from Costa Rica. Halfwheel describes it as a limited production line. The wrapper variety is not published, only its Claro Colorado shade.

cigars.about: A small-production Casdagli line rolled in Costa Rica, named after a 6th century Arabian poem in a nod to the family's history breeding Arabian race horses. It is known for its figurado shapes and Peruvian and Dominican filler.
cigars.researchNote: Pony Express adds a second, Nicaraguan binder. The maker names IGM Cigars as the factory; halfwheel lists Tabacos de la Cordillera and gives the Cremello a Costa Rican wrapper. The maker dates the line to 2018, but halfwheel reported four-year-aged cigars from it that year.

cigars.about: A 2026 offshoot of Casdagli's Daughters of the Wind, made at IGM Cigars in Costa Rica. It uses a sun-grown Habano Rosado wrapper from one of the first harvests on the factory's own farm in Puriscal.
cigars.researchNote: The Lonsdale swaps the Nicaraguan filler for Peruvian. The wrapper is Habano seed with a rosado color.

cigars.about: Named for the Casdagli family's villa in Cairo and made at Tabacos de Costa Rica. The blends use 'mejorado' tobaccos that get a second fermentation of two to four months, and the maker counts them among its strongest cigars.
cigars.researchNote: The filler mix changes by size. The maker lists only Ecuador for the wrapper and binder; halfwheel lists both as Habano. The Salomone Edición Limitada is a separate limited size. Halfwheel lists the Corona Gorda at 5 1/2 inches; the maker says 5.6.

cigars.about: A limited salomon in the Villa Casdagli line, released in October 2025 to mark the line's two Cigar Journal Cigar Trophy awards. It is based on the Toro blend with extra Nicaraguan Esteli ligero and is made at Tabacos de Costa Rica.
cigars.researchNote: This is one limited size of the Villa Casdagli line: 600 boxes of 10 a year. The maker lists it as Salomone Ed. Limitada. Halfwheel's review found the strength closer to mild to medium.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Nicarita: Esteli Ligero), Peru (Peruvita: Habano Seco)
cigars.about: Two small 4 x 35 cigars from Casdagli that each showcase a single filler tobacco from the Villa Casdagli blend. They are mixed-filler smokes of about 25 minutes, made at Tabacos de Costa Rica.
cigars.researchNote: Strength differs by cigar: Nicarita (Nicaraguan Esteli ligero) is rated medium to full, Peruvita (Peruvian Habano seco) mild to medium. Both use sandwich filler, a mix of long and short leaf.

cigars.about: The first release in Casdagli's Dominita line, a small 4 x 35 Dominican puro made entirely from Corojo Original leaf grown by the Reyes family in Navarrete. It is a 25 to 30 minute smoke sold in 10-count cartons.
cigars.researchNote: One of two blends in the Dominita line, each a single 4 x 35 size. Halfwheel calls the factory De Los Reyes.

cigars.about: The second release in Casdagli's Dominita line, a small 4 x 35 Dominican puro made entirely from Corojo 2012 leaf grown by the Reyes family in Navarrete. It debuted at InterTabac 2026.
cigars.researchNote: One of two blends in the Dominita line, each a single 4 x 35 size. Halfwheel calls the factory De Los Reyes.

cigars.about: One of the first two blends in Casdagli's Brothers of the Sabre series on Napoleonic-era generals, named for French Marshal Michel Ney. It is the milder, creamy and nutty blend, made by Hendrik Kelner Jr. at the Kelner Boutique Factory.
cigars.researchNote: The series was first announced as The Napoleonic Collection. The wrapper variety is not published, only its Claro Colorado shade.

cigars.about: One of the first two blends in Casdagli's Brothers of the Sabre series, named for Prussian Field Marshal von Blücher, known as Marshal Forward. It is the stronger blend and uses Zimbabwean filler, which is uncommon in cigars, and is made at the Kelner Boutique Factory.
cigars.researchNote: The series was first announced as The Napoleonic Collection. The wrapper variety is not published.

cigars.about: A 2024 addition to Casdagli's Brothers of the Sabre series, named for French cavalry general Antoine Charles Louis de Lasalle. It is a mild to medium, creamy and nutty blend made at the Kelner Boutique Factory.
cigars.researchNote: The series was formerly called The Napoleonic Collection. The wrapper variety is not published, only its Claro Colorado shade.

cigars.about: A 2024 addition to Casdagli's Brothers of the Sabre series, named for Austrian Field Marshal Radetzky, called Vater (Father) by his troops. It is a medium to full blend with Zimbabwean filler, which is uncommon in cigars, made at the Kelner Boutique Factory.
cigars.researchNote: The series was formerly called The Napoleonic Collection. Blender Hendrik Kelner Jr. says the Petit Robusto may be the strongest blend the factory has made. The wrapper variety is not published.

cigars.about: A 2026 addition to Casdagli's Brothers of the Sabre series, named for Sir Hudson Lowe, the British governor of St Helena who guarded the exiled Napoleon. It uses Zimbabwean filler, which is uncommon in cigars, and is made at the Kelner Boutique Factory.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates the Piramide full bodied and the Toro medium to full. Halfwheel lists the release type as undisclosed. The wrapper variety is not published.

cigars.about: A 2026 addition to Casdagli's Brothers of the Sabre series, named for Joachim Murat, Napoleon's cavalry commander and King of Naples. It is a mild to medium, creamy all-Dominican filler blend made at the Kelner Boutique Factory.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates the Toro medium bodied and the Piramide medium to full. Halfwheel lists the release type as undisclosed. The wrapper variety is not published, only its Claro Colorado shade.

cigars.about: The mildest of the three Original blends from Adrian Magnus, made with non-aged tobacco at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic. It launched at InterTabac 2025 alongside Original Medium and Original Strong.
cigars.researchNote: Maker's spec table says Ecuador Habano wrapper, but its own description calls the wrapper Ecuadorian Shade and adds Honduras to the filler. Trade press calls the line Originals. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

cigars.about: The middle blend of the three Original cigars from Adrian Magnus, made with non-aged tobacco at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic. It launched at InterTabac 2025.
cigars.researchNote: Maker's description says the blend is entirely Nicaraguan, but its spec table and Cigar Coop list Nicaraguan and Dominican filler. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

cigars.about: The strongest of the three Original blends from Adrian Magnus, with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over non-aged tobacco. It is made at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic and launched at InterTabac 2025.
cigars.researchNote: Maker's strength scale shows medium-strong; Cigar Coop described it as full strength. Maker's description mentions only Nicaraguan filler, while its spec table adds Dominican. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

cigars.about: One of three XSO blends from Adrian Magnus, made with non-aged tobacco at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic. The line launched at InterTabac 2025.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's site lists a San Andres Mexico wrapper, but the launch coverage (Cigar Coop) gave a shade-grown Ecuadorian Habano wrapper and no Pennsylvania filler. Cigar Coop called it medium to full. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

cigars.about: The medium blend of the three XSO cigars from Adrian Magnus, wrapped in a broadleaf leaf over non-aged tobacco. It is made at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic and launched at InterTabac 2025.
cigars.researchNote: The origin of the broadleaf wrapper is not disclosed. Maker's description says 100% Nicaraguan tobacco from Jalapa, but its spec table and Cigar Coop list Nicaraguan and Dominican filler. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

cigars.about: The strongest of the three XSO blends from Adrian Magnus, made with non-aged tobacco at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic. The line launched at InterTabac 2025.
cigars.researchNote: Maker's spec table and Cigar Coop say San Andres Mexico wrapper, but the maker's own description says dark Broadleaf. Maker's strength scale shows medium-strong; Cigar Coop called it full. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

cigars.about: The mildest of the three blends in Montego, a value-priced line from Adrian Magnus. It is made at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic and launched at InterTabac 2025.
cigars.researchNote: The maker labels the line Montego MNTG. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

cigars.about: The middle blend of the three in Montego, a value-priced line from Adrian Magnus. It is made at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic and launched at InterTabac 2025.
cigars.researchNote: Maker's spec table and Cigar Coop say Ecuadorian Habano wrapper; the maker's description calls it Ecuadorian Shade. Maker's strength scale shows medium while its text and Cigar Coop say medium to full. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

cigars.about: The top blend of the three in Montego, a value-priced line from Adrian Magnus, with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over Nicaraguan filler. It is made at the company's own factory in the Dominican Republic and launched at InterTabac 2025.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's Robusto page lists a Nicaraguan binder, while its Toro and Belicoso pages and Cigar Coop say Indonesian. The maker rates it 3 out of 5 (medium); Cigar Coop described it as the boldest Montego. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

cigars.about: The youngest of the aged lines from Adrian Magnus, made with long-filler tobacco the maker says is aged five years. It is rolled in the Dominican Republic and was shown to US retailers at the 2025 PCA trade show.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper is agreed as Ecuadorian Connecticut. The maker lists an Ecuadorian binder with Honduran, Dominican and Nicaraguan filler; Stogie Press and a retailer list Dominican binder with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. Strength is disputed: the maker's scale shows light, Stogie Press says medium, and one retailer sells it as full.

cigars.about: A line from Adrian Magnus built on tobacco the maker says is aged seven years. It is rolled in the Dominican Republic and sits between Millennium and Imperials in the range.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists an Ecuadorian wrapper and binder with Ecuadorian, Nicaraguan and Honduran filler; one retailer instead lists Dominican binder and Dominican, Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler, and calls it medium to full. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

cigars.about: A line from Adrian Magnus built on long-filler tobacco the maker says is aged ten years. It is rolled in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's scale shows medium, but one retailer sells it as full bodied and lists Dominican and Nicaraguan binder with Dominican, Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

cigars.about: A cigar from the top tier of the Adrian Magnus range, made with long-filler tobacco the maker says is aged twelve years. It is the only cigar the maker rates at full strength and is rolled in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is taken from the maker's own site only; no independent spec sheet was found. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

cigars.about: An infused cigar from Adrian Magnus: long-filler tobacco the maker says is aged twelve years and infused with Hennessy XO cognac. It is rolled in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: This is an infused cigar, so store it apart from others. A 2023 review said the maker labeled it full while it smoked medium; the maker's site now shows medium. One article says only 5,000 boxes are made a year. Sizes converted from millimeters.

cigars.about: The flagship cigar from Adrian Magnus, made with tobacco the maker says is aged fifteen years. It is rolled in the Dominican Republic and sold as a limited edition.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it a limited edition but publishes no production count. Its Toro page shows medium-strong on the strength scale while the Petit Corona page shows medium. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

cigars.about: A limited edition toro from Adrian Magnus made with tobacco the maker says is aged twelve years. It is rolled in the Dominican Republic and comes in a dedicated limited-edition box.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is taken from the maker's own site only; no independent source was found. The maker publishes no production count. Size converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

cigars.about: A limited edition toro from Adrian Magnus made with tobacco the maker says is aged eleven years. The maker says it is limited to 5,000 hand-numbered boxes.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is taken from the maker's own site only; no independent source was found. The maker's text speaks of Dominican origins, but its spec table lists no Dominican leaf. Size converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

cigars.about: A sweet-leaning cigar from Adrian Magnus that the maker groups with its infused cigars and describes as organically sweet. It is rolled in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists 1808 under Infused and titles the Toro 'Organically Sweet Premium Cigars', but does not say how it is sweetened. The blend is taken from the maker's own site only. Sizes converted from the maker's millimeter figures.

cigars.about: A core Lampert line rolled at Tabacos de Costa Rica and inspired by the local Pura Vida lifestyle. It is known for a smooth, slightly mineral profile and tobaccos aged four to five years.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's current page lists the wrapper as "Ecuador H. Criollo" with binder and filler undisclosed; its press releases and halfwheel give Habano 2000. Halfwheel dates the Robusto Grande to 2022, but the line was already on sale in 2021. Gordito and Toro Grande were added in 2025.

cigars.about: Lampert's original Costa Rican line, which grew out of founder Stefan Lampert's My Cigar Lab custom blending project. Each size is sold under its own name, such as El Gringo and Don Patron.
cigars.researchNote: Guests may ask for the sizes by name. The maker describes it as mild to medium-strong and says the blend is adjusted by size. Halfwheel also lists Gatsby (6 x 52, Ecuadorian habano criollo hybrid wrapper) and Kingpin (4 x 62, criollo wrapper) under Oro.

cigars.line: Oro Line Short Perfecto Small Batch Production
cigars.about: A short, fat double perfecto with a pigtail cap in Lampert's Oro family, made in small yearly batches in Costa Rica. It is sold in the U.S. as the Oro Kingpin.
cigars.researchNote: This is one size of the Oro Line, known in the U.S. as Kingpin. The maker's page lists an Ecuador Connecticut wrapper, Dominican and Peruvian filler and 4 1/2 x 62; halfwheel and a retailer list a dark Ecuadorian criollo wrapper, added Nicaraguan filler and 4 x 62. The maker says quantities are very limited each year.

cigars.about: A limited Lampert release rolled in 2023 at Tabacos de Costa Rica and launched at the 2024 PCA trade show. It carries an extra band marked 2023.
cigars.researchNote: Rolled in 2023 but released in early 2024; 450 boxes of 10 for the U.S. The maker's product page lists Brazil for both binder and filler, while its press release and halfwheel give a Habano 2000 binder and four-country filler.

cigars.about: Lampert's 2025 limited edition and the company's first box-pressed cigar, made at Tabacos de Costa Rica. It was limited to 500 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: 500 boxes of 10 were made, 200 of them for the U.S. Halfwheel reports the blend returning in late 2026 as a 7 1/4 x 50 double corona sold in jars. Tasting notes come from a retailer, not the maker.

cigars.about: Lampert's 2026 limited edition, a box-pressed toro with a Connecticut-seed wrapper made at Tabacos de Costa Rica. It began shipping in August 2026.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates strength 3.5 out of 5; a retailer calls it medium. The maker lists the binder as Ecuador, while halfwheel lists Habano 2000 with origin undisclosed. Tasting notes come from a retailer, not the maker.

cigars.about: A 2026 Lampert release named for the witch of Slavic folklore, made at Tabacos de Costa Rica in a single toro size. Only the Ecuadorian Habano wrapper is disclosed.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are undisclosed. The maker rates strength 4 out of 5, while one retailer calls it full. Halfwheel calls it a limited edition; production numbers were not announced.

cigars.about: A Costa Rican Lampert cigar offered in one 6 x 56 toro size. The maker describes it as medium in strength and keeps the whole blend private.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper, binder and filler are all undisclosed. The maker rates it 3 out of 5 for strength. The maker's page says it will be available but gives no release date or factory name.

cigars.about: A limited Lampert release made in Costa Rica, described by the maker as an evolution of the Limitada 2023 blend with one added undisclosed tobacco. It is currently sold only to Lampert Black Card members.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are undisclosed. The maker rates strength 4.5 out of 5 (between medium-full and full) but gives no word for it. Currently a Black Card member exclusive. No factory or release year is published.

cigars.about: A short Connecticut-wrapped Lampert cigar made at Tabacos de Costa Rica. It is currently sold only to Lampert Black Card members.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are undisclosed. The maker gives the length as 119 mm (about 4 11/16 inches) and rates strength 2.5 out of 5 (between mild-medium and medium). Currently a Black Card exclusive ahead of a wider release.

cigars.about: The first blend in Lampert's Nicaraguan 1675 series and the cigar that introduced the brand to the U.S. in 2021. It was blended by Indiana Ortez and is made at the Ortez family factory in Condega.
cigars.researchNote: Since mid 2025 only the Toro is shipped to U.S. stores; the Robusto and Short Robusto continue abroad. The maker's page text gives the Short Robusto as 3 1/2 x 52, while halfwheel and retailers list 3 3/4 x 52.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped blend in Lampert's Nicaraguan 1675 series, built to founder Stefan Lampert's own taste. It uses four-year-old Ortez family tobacco from Jalapa and Condega.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates strength 2 out of 5 and calls the cigar medium-bodied; one retailer lists it as medium. Since mid 2025 only the Toro is shipped to U.S. stores.

cigars.about: The maduro blend in Lampert's Nicaraguan 1675 series, with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco. Morado is Spanish for purple.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates strength 4 out of 5 and calls it medium to full-bodied; at launch Lampert described it as full-bodied. Since mid 2025 only the Toro is shipped to U.S. stores.

cigars.about: A 2026 addition to Lampert's Nicaraguan 1675 series and the brand's first oval-pressed cigar. All of its tobacco is aged at least five years.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are undisclosed. It shipped in March 2026, and after the launch U.S. stores get only the Toro Grande. The maker rates strength 4 out of 5 and calls it full-bodied; halfwheel's reviewer found it closer to medium-plus.

cigars.about: Lampert's full-bodied Dominican cigar. It launched in 2023 and has since been reblended by Hendrik Kelner Jr. at his Kelner Boutique Factory.
cigars.researchNote: The maker keeps the current Kelner blend undisclosed and rates it 3.5 out of 5; one retailer calls it full and lists an Ecuadorian Habano HVA wrapper. The original 2023 version was made at El Maestro with a Mexican San Andres wrapper, so older boxes are a different cigar.

cigars.about: A Dominican Lampert cigar made by Julian Sued in Tamboril and soft-launched through Small Batch Cigar in 2022. The Toro was for the U.S. and the Short Robusto for Europe.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's release names an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper; halfwheel lists Ecuadorian Connecticut, though its reviewer said the leaf did not look like one. It is no longer in the maker's current lineup. One retailer lists a later Swiss-only Short Robusto made at KBF with a different blend.

cigars.about: The third yearly Family Reserve from Lampert, made at the Kelner Boutique Factory in the Dominican Republic. It was limited to 800 boxes of 10 and is essentially the same cigar as the 2022 release.
cigars.researchNote: 800 boxes of 10 were made and it shipped in December 2023. No strength rating or tasting notes are published for this release.

cigars.about: The mildest blend in the Kafie 1901 core line, with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Dominican tobaccos aged at least four years. It was first made in Honduras and has been rolled at La Aurora in the Dominican Republic since 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Maker rates strength 6/10 and body 7/10. Maker lists all-Dominican filler; halfwheel and Neptune add Nicaraguan filler. Maker says it has been in the portfolio since 2014, while halfwheel reported it shipping in April 2015.

cigars.about: The first Kafie 1901 blend, named for founder Dr. Gaby Kafie's father, Don Fernando. It launched in 2013 as a Honduran-made cigar and was reblended at La Aurora in 2022 with a Cameroon binder and Dominican andullo in the filler.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as DF Maduro or Kafie 1901 Maduro. Maker rates strength and body 8/10; Neptune lists it as Medium. The 2013 original was made at Tabacalera Puros Aliados in Honduras with a different binder and filler.

cigars.about: A Kafie 1901 core line blend that the maker calls its boldest, pairing a double-fermented Mexican San Andrés wrapper with an all-Nicaraguan binder and filler. It debuted in 2016 as a Honduran-made cigar and was reworked when production moved to La Aurora in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Maker rates strength 7/10 and body 8/10; Neptune lists it as Full. The 2016 original was box pressed, made in Honduras, and had a Honduran binder with Brazilian and Dominican filler. It was first announced under the name La Union.

cigars.about: A core Kafie 1901 blend with a sun-grown Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper that the maker calls its bestseller. It started as a Honduran-made cigar and has been rolled at La Aurora in the Dominican Republic since 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Maker rates strength and body 7/10; Neptune lists it as Medium. Maker lists Brazilian filler, while halfwheel and Neptune list Peruvian pelo de oro instead. Maker says 'since 2014' but halfwheel reported a November 2015 release.

cigars.about: A Dominican puro made to mark founder Dr. Gaby Kafie's 50th birthday; the L is the Roman numeral for 50. He blended it with La Aurora master blender Manuel Inoa, and it was the first blend to come out of Kafie's partnership with that factory.
cigars.researchNote: Maker rates strength 7/10 and body 6/10; Neptune lists it as Medium. Halfwheel listed the Belicoso at 54 ring, while the maker and Neptune list 52.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped version of Kafie 1901's value-priced house blend, made with long filler at La Aurora. The version now sold has a sweetened tip.
cigars.researchNote: Current version is sweet tipped (added 2024) and boxed; the unsweetened 2022 bundle came in four sizes. Maker calls it mild to medium (5/10); Neptune lists Medium. The Liga de la Casa name dates to 2018, but halfwheel first reports a Connecticut version in the 2022 La Aurora relaunch.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Kafie 1901's value-priced house blend, made with long filler at La Aurora. The version now sold has a sweetened tip.
cigars.researchNote: Maker lists an Ecuadorian habano maduro wrapper; halfwheel and Neptune call it Honduran. Sold since 2018 as a Honduran-made bundle with a San Andrés maduro wrapper, then remade with long filler at La Aurora in 2022 and given a sweet tip in 2024. Maker calls it mild to medium; Neptune lists Medium.

cigars.about: The natural habano version of Kafie 1901's value-priced house blend, made with long filler at La Aurora. The version now sold has a sweetened tip.
cigars.researchNote: Maker lists an Ecuadorian habano wrapper; halfwheel and Neptune call it Honduran. Sold since 2018 as a Honduran-made bundle, then remade with long filler at La Aurora in 2022 and given a sweet tip in 2024. Maker calls it mild to medium; Neptune lists Mild.

cigars.line: Liga de la Casa Sweet Tip
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Connecticut, Ecuadorian Habano Natural or Ecuadorian Habano Maduro
cigars.about: Kafie 1901's first sweet-tipped cigars, shown at the 2024 PCA trade show. The line comes in three wrapper versions, Connecticut, Habano Natural and Habano Maduro, all made at La Aurora.
cigars.researchNote: Three blends under one name, so the wrapper depends on the version; these are the same cigars as the current Liga de la Casa Connecticut, Natural and Maduro. Kafie did not disclose the blends at launch; the binder and filler come from its own store listing. Neptune calls the two habano wrappers Honduran.

cigars.about: The Connecticut version of Kafie 1901's unbanded bundle line, made at La Aurora. It uses mixed (medium) filler from tobacco left over from rolling the company's other blends.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed filler, not long filler, and sold without bands. Maker lists an Indonesian binder; Neptune lists Honduran. Halfwheel dates this La Aurora version to 2023 but mentioned an earlier Naked bundle in 2022.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Kafie 1901's unbanded bundle line, made at La Aurora. It uses mixed (medium) filler from tobacco left over from rolling the company's other blends.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed filler, not long filler, and sold without bands. Maker lists an Indonesian binder; Neptune lists Honduran. Halfwheel dates this La Aurora version to 2023 but mentioned an earlier Naked bundle in 2022.

cigars.about: The natural habano version of Kafie 1901's unbanded bundle line, made at La Aurora. It uses mixed (medium) filler from tobacco left over from rolling the company's other blends.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed filler, not long filler, and sold without bands. Maker lists an Indonesian binder; Neptune lists Honduran. Halfwheel dates this La Aurora version to 2023 but mentioned an earlier Naked bundle in 2022.

cigars.about: A limited Kafie 1901 release named for the stilt houses in Miami's Biscayne Bay, blended by Dr. Gaby Kafie with La Aurora's Manuel Inoa. Its binder and filler were aged for about a year in barrels that once held Dominican rum.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are not disclosed. It was shown at PCA 2025 with 500 boxes of each size planned, but halfwheel reported in April 2026 that the release was pushed to fall 2026, so check whether it has shipped.

cigars.about: A one-size lancero made by Kafie for the Limited Cigar Association, released on December 27, 2021. The name means 'old year' and it was meant to be smoked on New Year's Eve.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Año Viejo by Kafie through Limited Cigar Association retailers, not as part of the regular Kafie 1901 line. Production numbers were not disclosed.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Habano Natural, Ecuadorian Connecticut, Mexican San Andrés or Mexican San Andrés Maduro, depending on the blend
cigars.about: A 2021 set of six small-run blends from Kafie's own Honduran factory, built from tobacco lots too small for a regular line. They were sold in 10-count bundles through Kafie's BoutiqueSmoke.com store.
cigars.researchNote: Six releases with four different wrappers, so there is no single wrapper. Each release was limited to 2,000 cigars. Kafie left the Honduran factory in late 2021.

cigars.about: The Ecuadorian Connecticut blend in Serino's original Royale series, made for the Serino family at Omar González-Alemán's La Corona factory in Estelí. It is the mildest of the Royale blends.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2016 as Serino Royale 20th Anniversary in a different set of sizes. The current four sizes came with Serino's 2021 version of the line.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Jalapa Criollo '98 medio tiempo and Corojo '99, Estelí Criollo '98)
cigars.about: The middle blend of the Serino Royale series, a medium-bodied Nicaraguan cigar under a lighter Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. It is made at La Corona in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: Early coverage calls the wrapper Ecuadorian Habano claro (Habano 2000 seed). Launched in 2016 as Serino Royale 20th Anniversary; the current three sizes came with Serino's 2021 version of the line.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Jalapa Criollo '98 medio tiempo, Estelí Corojo '99 and Criollo '98)
cigars.about: The strongest blend of the Serino Royale series. It pairs a dark Ecuadorian Habano 2000 wrapper with aged Nicaraguan tobacco from Estelí and Jalapa.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is a Habano 2000 seed oscuro, not broadleaf. Serino says full-bodied on one page and medium-full on another; Atlantic Cigar lists Full, while halfwheel and Cigar Coop found medium to medium-full. Current sizes came with the 2021 version.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Jalapa Criollo '98 and Corojo '99, Estelí Criollo '98)
cigars.about: Carson Serino's personal blend, inspired by the Cuban cigars he smoked on a backpacking trip to Iceland. It is a Nicaraguan cigar aimed at a Cuban-style profile, rolled at La Corona in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: The Dalia and Corona launched as limited sizes of 300 boxes each. A 6 1/2 x 54 Sublime from the 2017 launch is not on Serino's current list. Cigar Aficionado names a Jalapa Criollo '98 binder; Serino's site says Jalapa Corojo '99.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Ometepe Criollo '98, Estelí Corojo '99 and Criollo '98, Jalapa Corojo '99)
cigars.about: A medium-bodied Nicaraguan line from Serino named for the Taíno people of the Caribbean, who are credited with introducing tobacco to Europeans. It is made at La Corona in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as Taíno White Label. A 5 1/2 x 44 size called The 44 began as a CigarClub.com exclusive and went nationwide in 2021, but Serino's line page does not list it. halfwheel found strength a little above medium.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano, Olor, Criollo '98), Nicaragua (Criollo '98)
cigars.about: A Dominican-made extension of Serino's Taíno line, blended with Jochy Blanco and rolled at his Tabacalera Palma factory. The three sizes carry Taíno words as names.
cigars.researchNote: Announced in 2019 with an Ecuadorian Habano 2000 wrapper, which Serino's line page and some retailers still list. It shipped in June 2021 with Ecuadorian Sumatra. Serino gives no strength; halfwheel found it just under medium, Atlantic Cigar lists medium-full.

cigars.about: The first release from Studio Serino, the company's small artisan division. It is a rosado-wrapped Nicaraguan cigar with Peruvian and Pennsylvania tobacco in the filler, named partly as a nod to the Beatles song Eleanor Rigby.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Studio Serino Elenor Rose. The Eagle is a perfecto. Serino calls it a medium to full blend, while Atlantic Cigar lists Medium. A 4 1/2 x 45 RPM 45 size was added in 2026 as a 3,000-cigar limited run.

cigars.about: A single-size, Cuban-style blend made by the Serino family with David Imber, using five-year-old tobaccos and traditional methods such as slow fermentation, wooden molds and hand bunching. It is rolled at La Corona in Estelí and sold in 10-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Styled BYGONE. Comes in one size only. halfwheel's review put strength at medium-full; Atlantic Cigar lists it as Medium. Serino does not name the Peruvian filler leaf.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Estelí Criollo '98, Jalapa Corojo '99), USA (Pennsylvania broadleaf)
cigars.about: Serino's value-priced line, first rolled for a family friend's destination wedding and later turned into a regular release. It is made at La Corona in Estelí and sold in paper-wrapped bundles of 10 with a pigtail cap and brushed foot.
cigars.researchNote: First sold in spring 2021 as a CigarClub.com exclusive, then went national in December 2021 with Pennsylvania broadleaf added to the filler. Serino also sells a newer box-pressed version in Gordo 6 x 58, Sublime 6 x 54 and Robusto Grande 5 x 54.

cigars.about: A limited 9 1/4 inch A-size cigar from Serino built around tobaccos from the 2012 crop, rolled at La Corona in 2016 and then aged before release. It was sold in single coffins.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,000 single coffins. halfwheel found it mild to mild-medium; Developing Palates called it medium. Ring gauge is 47 in the spec tables, though halfwheel's text also says 49.

cigars.filler: Nicaraguan Corojo '99, Criollo '98, two undisclosed Caribbean tobaccos
cigars.about: A small-batch cigar sold only through Serino's own shop, made with seven-year-aged tobaccos, rolled entubado style and then aged 15 months. It is sold without cellophane in ribbon-tied five-packs.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only through Serino's own shop in small batches. Most of the blend is undisclosed, and Serino does not publish the binder, factory, country or strength. Sizes are given in metric: 49 x 194 mm and 52 x 124 mm.

cigars.about: A small-batch limited edition robusto sold by Serino, created as a passion project by two friends named Griff and Dave. It is rolled at La Corona in Nicaragua and uses medio tiempo leaf in the blend.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Vanguard Limited Edition in boxes of 10, and only Serino's own shop describes it. No release year is given. Serino's wording is medium-full bodied.

cigars.about: One of three Zingotita blends, a small brand of Costa Rican cigars that Serino took over when its founder retired. The three are meant to follow the smoker through the day, and this is the morning one.
cigars.researchNote: Zingotita is a separate brand name owned and sold by Serino. The maker only says the blends mix Costa Rican and Nicaraguan tobaccos; the factory, binder, filler and release year are not published. Serino describes it as light, with no formal strength given.

cigars.about: One of three Zingotita blends, a small brand of Costa Rican cigars that Serino took over when its founder retired. The three are meant to follow the smoker through the day, and this is the midday one.
cigars.researchNote: Zingotita is a separate brand name owned and sold by Serino. The maker only says the blends mix Costa Rican and Nicaraguan tobaccos; the factory, binder, filler and release year are not published. Serino describes it as bold, with no formal strength given.

cigars.about: One of three Zingotita blends, a small brand of Costa Rican cigars that Serino took over when its founder retired. The three are meant to follow the smoker through the day, and this is the evening one.
cigars.researchNote: Zingotita is a separate brand name owned and sold by Serino. The maker only says the blends mix Costa Rican and Nicaraguan tobaccos; the factory, binder, filler and release year are not published. Serino describes the strength as medium-heavy.

cigars.about: The robusto of the Cuban Ramon Allones brand and its best known cigar, often shortened to RASS. It is sold in boxes of 25 and cabinet bundles of 50.
cigars.researchNote: Cuban puro. Habanos also writes the name as Allones Specially Selected. halfwheel dates its debut to 1980, but no second source confirms the year, so it is left blank.

cigars.about: The double corona of the Cuban Ramon Allones brand and one of only a few regular production sizes. Habanos names it alongside the Specially Selected as the brand's most renowned vitola.
cigars.researchNote: Cuban puro. The UK distributor lists it in the singular, as Gigante.

cigars.about: The smallest regular production Ramon Allones, a short Cuban petit corona in the Minuto format.
cigars.researchNote: Cuban puro. The UK distributor lists it in the singular, as Small Club Corona.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Cuban (Vuelta Abajo), aged at least two years
cigars.about: The Ramon Allones Edicion Limitada for 2019, a Cuban belicoso sold worldwide in green boxes of 10. It brings back the size of the 2005 Ramon Allones Belicoso made for the UK.
cigars.researchNote: Edicion Limitada 2019, announced in 2019 but first sold in the UK in August 2020. Habanos rates the brand full strength; halfwheel's review found this cigar medium-plus. Factory undisclosed.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Cuban (Vuelta Abajo), aged at least two years
cigars.about: The Ramon Allones Edicion Limitada for 2024, a Cuban cigar in the Nuevos size, which was new to the Cuban range. It comes in boxes of 20 and went on sale first in Switzerland in April 2025.
cigars.researchNote: Edicion Limitada 2024, first sold April 2025. Habanos and the UK distributor give 156 mm x 49 (Nuevos), used here; halfwheel's reports list 6 3/8 x 47. Full is Habanos's rating for the brand as a whole, not this release.

cigars.about: A Cuban Edicion Regional made for Andorra and named for Charlemagne. It is a robusto extra limited to 10,000 numbered boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Andorra exclusive from the 2025 Edicion Regional program, on sale August 2026. Third Ramon Allones regional in the Genios size, after Sur and Hermitage. Full is Habanos's rating for the brand as a whole, not this release.

cigars.about: A Cuban Edicion Regional for Bulgaria that marks the 30th anniversary of distributor Kaliman Caribe. It is a double robusto limited to 6,000 numbered boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Bulgaria exclusive from the 2025 Edicion Regional program, on shelves June 2026. Full is Habanos's rating for the brand as a whole, not this release.

cigars.about: The first Cuban Edicion Regional made for Monaco, named for the principality's casino. It shares its size with the Romeo y Julieta Wide Churchills and is limited to 6,000 numbered boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Monaco exclusive from the 2025 Edicion Regional program. Announced January 2026 as coming within weeks; no on-sale date was found, so the release year is left blank. Full is Habanos's rating for the brand as a whole, not this release.

cigars.about: A Cuban Edicion Regional for the United Kingdom marking 230 years of distributor Hunters & Frankau. Its white band and yellow ribbon recall the original Ramon Allones Private Stock of the early 1900s.
cigars.researchNote: UK exclusive from the 2020 Edicion Regional program: 3,600 numbered boxes of 25. The size is 170 mm, given as 6 3/4 or 6 7/10 inches. Full is Habanos's rating for the brand as a whole, not this release.

cigars.about: A Cuban Edicion Regional for Italy marking 20 years of distributor Diadema. It is a corona sold in decorative glass jars of 25, limited to 4,500 numbered jars.
cigars.researchNote: Italy exclusive from the 2020 Edicion Regional program, released September 2022. It is 3 mm shorter than the H. Upmann Noellas. Full is Habanos's rating for the brand as a whole, not this release.

cigars.about: A Cuban Edicion Regional for the Netherlands in the 109 shape, a long parejo with a rounded, tapered head. It is limited to 2,020 boxes of 40 cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Netherlands exclusive from the 2020 Edicion Regional program, released March 2022. Full is Habanos's rating for the brand as a whole, not this release.

cigars.about: A Cuban Edicion Regional toro made for the Nordic and Baltic countries through Habanos Nordic. It is limited to 6,000 numbered boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Nordic and Baltic exclusive from the 2020 Edicion Regional program, released October 2021. Habanos rates the brand full strength, but halfwheel's review found it medium in strength with a lighter body. Factory undisclosed.

cigars.about: A Cuban Edicion Regional for Germany made to honor the 90th birthday of Heinrich Villiger, co-founder of the German distributor 5th Avenue. It is limited to 18,000 numbered boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Germany exclusive from the 2020 Edicion Regional program, launched September 2021 and also sold in Austria and Poland. Full is Habanos's rating for the brand as a whole, not this release.

cigars.about: A Cuban Edicion Regional perfecto made for Mexico in the same shape as the Partagas Presidentes. It is limited to 6,000 numbered boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Mexico exclusive, released May 2021. Not the same cigar as the 2014 Ramon Allones Perfectos for Switzerland, which was 5 2/5 x 48. Full is Habanos's rating for the brand as a whole, not this release.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Habano from Ometepe and Condega), Colombia
cigars.about: The Connecticut Shade blend in Warfighter Tobacco's Field series, one of the six original core lines from the veteran-owned company. It is rolled in Estelí and starts with some spice before finishing smooth.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish a strength rating. Production moved from a Dominican factory to Plasencia in Estelí in 2017, then to Tabacalera Carreras in March 2020. The company said the blends stayed the same after the 2017 move.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Habano from Estelí and Condega), Dominican Republic
cigars.about: The Sumatra-wrapped blend in Warfighter Tobacco's Field series, which the company pitches as its everyday cigar. It is one of the six original core lines and is rolled in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish a strength rating. Production moved from a Dominican factory to Plasencia in Estelí in 2017, then to Tabacalera Carreras in March 2020. The company said the blends stayed the same after the 2017 move.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Habano from Ometepe and Jalapa), Colombia
cigars.about: The maduro in Warfighter Tobacco's Field series, described by the company as the boldest of the three Field blends. It is one of the six original core lines and is rolled in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish a strength rating, only that it is the boldest of the Field line. Production moved from a Dominican factory to Plasencia in 2017, then to Tabacalera Carreras in March 2020.

cigars.filler: Honduras (Habano from Jamastran), Nicaragua (Habano from Jalapa, Habano ligero from Estelí)
cigars.about: The Corojo-wrapped blend in Warfighter Tobacco's Garrison series, one of the company's six original core lines. It opens creamy, turns spicy, and is rolled in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: Formerly sold as the 5.56 MM Garrison Corojo. The maker does not publish a strength rating. Made at Tabacalera Carreras since March 2020, before that at Plasencia.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Habano from Jalapa, Ometepe and Estelí)
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro with a Habano Rosado wrapper in Warfighter Tobacco's Garrison series, one of the company's six original core lines. The maker says it smokes stronger than the Field line without being overpowering.
cigars.researchNote: Formerly sold as the 7.62 MM Garrison Rosado. The maker does not publish a strength rating, only that it is stronger than the Field line. Made at Tabacalera Carreras since March 2020, before that at Plasencia.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Habano from Ometepe and Estelí, Habano ligero from Condega)
cigars.about: The dark maduro in Warfighter Tobacco's Garrison series, one of the company's six original core lines. It uses a Honduran Habano Oscuro Maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan filler and is rolled in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: Formerly sold as the .50 Cal Garrison Oscuro Maduro. The maker calls it dark and bold but does not publish a strength rating. Made at Tabacalera Carreras since March 2020, before that at Plasencia.

cigars.about: A single-size toro from Warfighter Tobacco made as a tribute to people who work nights. A thin strip of Honduran candela circles the cap as a nod to night vision green.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium bodied. halfwheel's review found the body medium but the nicotine strength mild, and one retailer lists it medium-full. Scored 91 at halfwheel and ranked #18 on its 2024 Top 25.

cigars.about: Warfighter Tobacco's mixed filler cigar, made from the cuttings of its core lines with an added long leaf for construction and a Habano wrapper. It was developed in 2020, named for that year, and sold in bundles.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed filler, not long filler: the maker uses cuttings from its core lines plus a long leaf. The maker calls it mild to medium bodied, while one retailer lists it medium. Countries of origin for the wrapper, binder and filler are not published.

cigars.about: A single-size toro marking Warfighter Tobacco's first ten years, with a dark Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. Unlike most anniversary cigars it is a regular production line.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium bodied, while one retailer lists it medium-full. It is regular production despite the anniversary name.

cigars.about: A single-size toro from Warfighter Tobacco with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is the company's former Heroes Sports charity cigar, renamed and made a core line in 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Same blend and size as the Warfighter Heroes Sports released in 2022; only the name and band changed in 2026. The maker describes it as medium to medium-bold, and one retailer lists it medium-full.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Habano from Jalapa and Estelí, Habano ligero from Estelí)
cigars.about: The fifth release in Warfighter Tobacco's small batch Victory series, a shaggy foot 6 x 54 with a Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos. It comes in signed and numbered boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 350 boxes of 10, each signed and numbered by company president Jon Simons. halfwheel reports the blend is the same as earlier Victory editions. No strength rating or tasting notes are published.

cigars.about: The fourth release in Warfighter Tobacco's Victory series, a 6 x 54 toro with a Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It was the first Victory sold through retail shops as well as online.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,000 boxes of 10 (20,000 cigars). halfwheel first described it as a 6 x 54 torpedo with a shaggy foot, then as a toro when it shipped. No strength rating or tasting notes are published.

cigars.about: A collaboration between Warfighter Tobacco and Caleb Francis, who went to Estelí to blend it alongside the company. It is a 6 x 52 with a Habano Oscuro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish where the wrapper is grown, the factory, a strength rating or whether it is limited. It went on sale on the maker's store in September 2026.

cigars.about: An event-only cigar from Warfighter Tobacco introduced on April 1, 2025. It is a 6 x 52 toro that is given away at Warfighter events and is not sold.
cigars.researchNote: The blend and the factory are deliberately undisclosed, in keeping with the name. It is never sold, only handed out at Warfighter events.

cigars.about: The Black line is a Dominican puro from Bob de Goede's Xhaxhi Bobi brand, rolled at Kelner Boutique Factory. Each size has its own name, such as El Ingeniero for the robusto.
cigars.researchNote: El Ingeniero is the robusto. Baba Jan (petit corona) is listed with the same blend and photo but is not labeled Black. A Black Toro was added in 2026 with no size or blend published, and the distributor rates the line medium plus where Developing Palates reviewers called it medium.

cigars.about: The Red line from Bob de Goede's Xhaxhi Bobi brand, whose cigars are made at several Dominican factories. The US distributor sells a Red Toro in bundles of 10.
cigars.researchNote: No blend or dimensions are published for the Red Toro. El Licenciado (robusto) and Mi Hermano (petit corona) are pictured with the same red band, so they look like the named sizes of this line, but no source says so outright.

cigars.about: A 4 x 43 petit corona from the Dominican brand Xhaxhi Bobi. The distributor lists it as an all-Dominican blend and pictures it with the red band.
cigars.researchNote: Appears to be the petit corona of the Red line, with El Licenciado as the robusto: the distributor uses the same photo for both. Mi Hermano is listed only as all Dominican, while El Licenciado has a detailed blend with Peruvian filler. Strength is listed as medium plus and the text calls it medium bodied.

cigars.filler: Dominican San Vicente, Dominican Corojo, Dominican Piloto Cubano, Peruvian Pelo de Oro
cigars.about: A 5 x 50 robusto from Bob de Goede's Xhaxhi Bobi brand, named in honor of Hendrik Kelner Jr. It uses a Dominican Yamasa wrapper over mostly Dominican tobaccos with some Peruvian Pelo de Oro.
cigars.researchNote: Named after Hendrik Kelner Jr., who made Bob de Goede's first cigars. The listing does not name the factory outright. It wears the red band, so it looks like the robusto of the Red line, with Mi Hermano as the petit corona.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped cigar in the Xhaxhi Bobi range, made in the Dominican Republic. Sunrise is the petit corona and Sunset is the robusto, and the distributor rates the blend mild to medium.
cigars.researchNote: Same blend in two sizes: Sunrise is the 4 x 43 petit corona and Sunset is the 5 x 50 robusto. The factory is not published.

cigars.about: The Grey line from the Dominican brand Xhaxhi Bobi, listed by the distributor as blended and rolled at Torres Garcia.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is not published. The Sexy Cuchi lancero was previously listed by the distributor as Grey Lancero.

cigars.about: A 7 x 38 lancero from Xhaxhi Bobi, listed as an all-Dominican blend and sold in bundles of 10.
cigars.researchNote: The distributor's page was originally titled Grey Lancero, so this may be the lancero of the Grey line under a new name. The factory is not published.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Ecuadorian Habano cigar made for Xhaxhi Bobi at Tabacalera El Artista in the Dominican Republic. SQ refers to the square press and the number to the ring gauge.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as SQ44 Habano (4 x 44) and SQ50 Habano (5 x 50), both box pressed. Luxury Cigar Club lists the Dominican filler as Corojo 98 instead of Criollo 98 and rates it medium plus.

cigars.about: A box-pressed San Andres wrapped cigar from Xhaxhi Bobi with Dominican binder and filler. It comes in the same two SQ sizes as the SQ Habano.
cigars.researchNote: Also written Seven Vikings. The distributor rates it medium strength but describes it as full flavored. The factory is not published.

cigars.about: A 6 x 50 toro from Xhaxhi Bobi with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Dominican binder and filler. The distributor sells it in five packs.
cigars.researchNote: No strength or factory is published. The only listing found is a five pack that is currently sold out, so it is unclear whether it is still made.

cigars.about: The 2024 limited edition from Bob de Goede's Xhaxhi Bobi brand, a 5.5 x 54 robusto grande with a Corojo wrapper sold in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: The listing gives seed varieties only (Corojo, H2000, HVA, Criollo 98, Havana 92) and not where the leaves were grown. The factory is not published.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andres (the 2025 edition is a San Andres and Habano barber pole)
cigars.about: A holiday limited edition from Xhaxhi Bobi that has come out in a different form each time. The 2024 release was a San Andres toro and the 2025 release a San Andres and Habano barber pole.
cigars.researchNote: The distributor lists binder and filler as undisclosed. Privada sells an aged earlier batch as Grinchy (6 x 50) and lists a Pennsylvania binder with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. Size and wrapper change by year, so check the band year.

cigars.about: A Halloween limited edition from Xhaxhi Bobi with a Mexican San Andres wrapper. It first appeared in October 2021 as a Privada Limited Cigar Association release, and the US distributor now sells a dated LE 2026 edition.
cigars.researchNote: The distributor lists the LE 2026 binder and filler as undisclosed and gives its size only as "5x5x50", which is unclear. Privada's 2021 release was a 6 x 50 toro with a Pennsylvania binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. Medium-full is the 2026 rating.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Connecticut, sweet tipped, with a maduro heart applied
cigars.about: A small sweet-tipped perfecto from Xhaxhi Bobi with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper and a maduro leaf heart on each cigar. It is sold in boxes of five through Sir Louis Cigars, the brand's US distributor.
cigars.researchNote: The cap is sweetened. The size is given only as Petite Perfecto with no measurements, and no strength or factory is published. The distributor calls it ultra limited.

cigars.about: The first line from ADV & McKay, the company founded by Henderson Ventura and Swiss sommelier Marcel Knobel. It is a medium Dominican-made cigar with a Mexican wrapper and it opens the brand's ongoing explorer story.
cigars.researchNote: The maker only says Mexican wrapper; halfwheel says Mexican habano seed, and Neptune's write-up says Ecuadorian Habano. halfwheel lists the Gran Toro as 6 x 54, retailers as 6 x 56. Sold in Europe from 2017 and widely in the US from 2019; made at Mina del Rey since 2023.

cigars.about: The second ADVentura core line, a medium Dominican-made cigar with a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper over tobaccos from four other countries. The maker calls it the most complex blend in its portfolio.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in Europe before its US arrival in June 2019; no source gives the original release year. halfwheel lists Pinzón as 5 x 50, while Neptune and Cigars Direct list 5.5 x 50. Made at Mina del Rey since 2023; Tabacalera William Ventura before.

cigars.about: The third ADVentura line and the one the company used for its US trade show debut in 2019. It has an Ecuadorian Habano 2000 wrapper and is known for boxes shaped like boats.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium plus; Neptune lists medium. The 7 x 40 Emperor's Edition lancero is a limited release. Made at Mina del Rey since 2023; Tabacalera William Ventura before.

cigars.about: ADVentura's Connecticut shade blend, released in 2020 alongside King's Gold as part of The Royal Return. The Corona placed third on halfwheel's Top 25 cigars of 2020.
cigars.researchNote: The maker describes it as a mild cigar with full flavor; Neptune lists medium and halfwheel's reviewer found medium strength. The 3.5 x 44 Tear five-pack was added in 2026. Now made at Mina del Rey; Tabacalera William Ventura before 2023.

cigars.about: ADVentura's Connecticut broadleaf blend, released in 2020 as the fuller counterpart to Queen's Pearls. It is made in batches because the broadleaf wrapper is hard to get, so it goes out of stock at times.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it full-bodied and full-strength; Neptune lists medium and halfwheel's reviewer found it under medium in strength. A 3.5 x 44 Golden Tooth five-pack was added in 2026. Now made at Mina del Rey; Tabacalera William Ventura before 2023.

cigars.about: A one-size limited extension of The Royal Return, launched at PCA 2024 as the first cigar from ADVentura's Elite Broker program. It was created with sales broker Adrian Acosta, whose father supplied some of the tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: One-time run of 2,000 boxes of 10, and the wrapper's origin is not disclosed. The maker and halfwheel give a Dominican binder with Sumatra-seed filler; Neptune lists a Sumatra binder and Dominican filler. Strength is Neptune's listing only.

cigars.about: A 2022 ADVentura line with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Dominican tobaccos that include medio tiempo leaf. It is known for its talking box, which plays a pirate recording when the lid is opened.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium plus to full-bodied; Neptune lists medium. First made at Tabacalera William Ventura; halfwheel reports all production moved to the company's Mina del Rey factory in 2023.

cigars.about: The 2024 follow-up to Barbarroja's Invasion, with a lighter Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Dominican binder and filler. The company says it is its fastest-selling blend, and its box also plays a recording when opened.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not state a strength; medium is Neptune's listing, and halfwheel's reviewer found little nicotine strength. A maduro version called High Tide is a separate limited release.

cigars.line: Blue Eyed Jack's Revenge Maduro High Tide
cigars.about: The maduro version of Blue Eyed Jack's Revenge, swapping in a darker Mexican San Andrés wrapper on the same Dominican binder and filler. It comes in a single diadema size and returned for a second limited run in 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Known as High Tide; the maker gives no strength, Neptune lists full and halfwheel's reviewer found medium-plus. Neptune lists 6 x 50, but the maker confirmed 6.5 x 50 to halfwheel. The 2026 run was 1,000 boxes of 10 for retailers who attended PCA.

cigars.about: The newest ADVentura core line, cast in the brand's story as the truce between the pirates of Barbarroja's Invasion and Blue Eyed Jack's Revenge. It is the company's first cigar to use binder and filler from its own Dominican farm.
cigars.researchNote: First appeared in 2025 as a 5 x 52 belicoso in the Captain's Collection sampler with an undisclosed blend; the three regular sizes shipped in July 2026 with a refined blend. The maker's page does not name the wrapper; Ecuadorian Sumatra-seed is from halfwheel and Neptune.

cigars.about: A line ADVentura makes only for its Elite Accounts, about 20 retailers, named for the crying woman of Mexican folklore. It launched in 2022 as a robusto, with a corona and a metal-banded toro added later as limited runs.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium plus; Neptune lists medium. halfwheel lists Dominican and Nicaraguan filler for the robusto and corona, and Dominican plus Indonesian binders for the toro. The corona (1,000 boxes of 10, 2023) and toro (800 boxes of 10, 2025) were limited runs.

cigars.about: ADVentura's charity cigar, a Connecticut shade short belicoso sold in sealed humidified packs. Part of each pack's price goes to El Aposento, a project in Tamboril that provides eyeglasses and school supplies for children of cigar workers.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in Switzerland in 2019 and reached US retailers in May 2022. The maker's page says mild-medium; halfwheel reports the company calling it mild. The maker and halfwheel give the size as 5 x 52; Neptune lists 4 x 52 and sells a 4-cigar pack.

cigars.about: A toro sold in boxes of 10 that marks ten years of the ADVentura brand, which was founded in 2016. It is made in the Dominican Republic with Dominican binder and filler under a wrapper the company has not disclosed.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune's listing is the only source found; the maker's site and halfwheel do not cover it. Neptune says the wrapper is undisclosed. Release year and production run are not stated, and Neptune's factory entry (Tabacalera William Ventura) could not be confirmed.

cigars.about: A single-size Cameroon-wrapped cigar from Luis Falto of Puerto Rico, rolled at La Aurora in small numbers. Hato Viejo is the Dominican farm that grew most of the tobacco and ELH are the grower's initials.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 100 boxes of 20. First announced in 2020 as a 25th anniversary cigar called Edición ELH Hato Viejo 2018 with a Corojo wrapper in a different size; the cigar that shipped in 2021 is the 6 x 47 Cameroon blend. Cigar Aficionado calls the size a toro.

cigars.about: A slim lonsdale from Falto, the Puerto Rico based boutique brand whose cigars are all rolled at La Aurora in the Dominican Republic. The maker describes it as medium bodied and not overly complex.
cigars.researchNote: Falto makes each blend in one size only. The maker lists the same tobaccos for the Lonsdale and the Robusto, and calls this one medium bodied.

cigars.about: A 5 x 50 robusto from Falto, the Puerto Rico based boutique brand whose cigars are all rolled at La Aurora in the Dominican Republic. The maker describes it as medium to full bodied with a touch of pepper.
cigars.researchNote: Falto makes each blend in one size only. The maker lists the same tobaccos for the Robusto and the Lonsdale, and calls this one medium to full bodied.

cigars.about: A petit belicoso with a Cameroon wrapper from Falto, the Puerto Rico based boutique brand made at La Aurora. The maker describes it as smooth and rich with a woody note.
cigars.researchNote: Made in one size only. The maker does not publish a strength for it.

cigars.about: A short perfecto from Falto with a Cameroon wrapper over Dominican tobaccos, rolled at La Aurora. The maker says it is made from a single mold dating to 1923, with a closed head and foot.
cigars.researchNote: The ring gauge tapers: 42 at the head and 47 at the foot. The maker calls it medium to full flavored but gives no strength.

cigars.about: A 4 x 40 petit corona from Falto with a Brazilian wrapper, rolled at La Aurora. Luis Falto made it as a short smoke with a lot of flavor for when time is limited.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the wrapper only as Brazil, with no leaf type. It calls the cigar full flavored but gives no strength.

cigars.about: A 5 3/4 x 48 corona gorda sold under the Tabacalera Falto, Inc. name, with a Dominican wrapper over an Indonesian Sumatra binder. The maker describes it as medium bodied and built on well-aged tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: The maker labels it Tabacalera Falto, Inc. "Selección Especial" and gives the wrapper only as Dominican Republic, with no leaf type.

cigars.about: A 5 1/2 x 47 corona gorda that Luis Falto blended for the tenth anniversary of Tabacalera Falto, with a Nicaraguan wrapper. It is rolled at La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Blended for the company's tenth anniversary; the company dates itself to 1995, but no source gives the release year. The maker lists the wrapper only as Nicaraguan and gives no strength.

cigars.about: A La Obra cigar listed on Falto's own site, shown with a purple band and a cedar sleeve. Falto cigars are rolled at La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists it, but the text and specs under it are a copy of the Legado entry, so no blend or size is confirmed. Halfwheel covered a 2023 limited La Obra Babalú Ayé (5 1/2 x 52, Ecuadorian HVA wrapper, 100 boxes of 15); no source says whether Azojuano is that cigar.

cigars.about: The cigar Luis Falto made to mark 30 years of Falto Cigars, with a Dominican Criollo 98 wrapper over a double binder. It is rolled at La Aurora and comes in one size.
cigars.researchNote: Regular production but only 160 boxes of 20 a year. Falto says the name means duties, or to him the opportunity to work. The maker's site entry currently shows the Legado text and specs by mistake.

cigars.about: A lancero blended for the 25th anniversary of Tabacalera Falto and rolled at La Aurora. It is made in this one size only.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the wrapper: the maker says Dominican Corojo, halfwheel's 2020 news and Cigar Coop said Ecuadorian HVA over a Dominican Criollo 98 binder, and halfwheel's review table says Ecuadorian Corojo. Regular production, about 100 boxes per run.

cigars.about: A lancero that Luis Falto dedicated to tobacco growers, rolled at La Aurora. The name refers to the growers and to the furrow cut before planting.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only in Puerto Rico before its 2021 US release. Ongoing but about 100 boxes of 25 per run. Halfwheel's spec list adds Nicaragua to the filler; Cigar Aficionado and Cigar Coop say Dominican only. The maker's site entry shows the Hato Viejo text by mistake.

cigars.about: Falto's first box-pressed cigar, made for the company's 23rd anniversary and rolled at La Aurora. LJF stands for Luis Juan Falto and the name means Founder's Reserve.
cigars.researchNote: Regular production, but each run is limited to 100 boxes of 20. The maker says it starts medium flavored and builds to full flavored, without giving a strength.

cigars.about: Lure's first line, a Nicaraguan puro with a dark corojo oscuro wrapper that soft launched in September 2023. The sizes are named for family and friends and sold in paper-wrapped bundles of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Maker rates it medium-plus. Two launch sizes, The BLT (6 x 54 torpedo) and The Sir Gar (7 x 48 churchill), are no longer on the maker's list. Halfwheel named Tabacalera Pages as the factory in 2024; the maker now says its cigars are made at La Tabacaria in Estelí.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Estelí, Jalapa, plus Ometepe in the robusto and Condega in the toro)
cigars.about: Lure's second core line, a Nicaraguan puro with a habano wrapper introduced in early 2024. Each size uses a slightly different filler recipe.
cigars.researchNote: The Mean Jean, added in July 2024, is a stronger blend rated full, with a Habano 2000 wrapper, Ometepe binder and Ometepe ligero. Halfwheel named Tabacalera Pages as Lure's factory in 2024; the maker now says its cigars are made at La Tabacaria in Estelí.

cigars.about: Lure's third core line, a Nicaraguan puro with a dark double maduro wrapper released in February 2025. The maker rates it full strength, and the Joe names nod to a cup of coffee.
cigars.researchNote: Maker rates it full; Halfwheel's review of The Big Joe found it topped out at medium-full. Halfwheel listed Tabacalera Pages as the factory in 2025; the maker now says its cigars are made at La Tabacaria in Estelí.

cigars.about: Lure's fourth core line, a pair of box-pressed Nicaraguan puros with a maduro wrapper launched in October 2025. It brought back The Brown-E-Trout as a regular cigar and added the slightly bolder Lil' Trout.
cigars.researchNote: The launch release rates The Brown-E-Trout medium and The Lil' Trout medium-plus; the maker's site lists each a step higher. The Brown-E-Trout first appeared in 2024 as a limited Catch & Release cigar with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper.

cigars.about: A small box-pressed rothschild from Lure, sold in resealable 5-packs that look like a bag of frozen fish sticks. It grew out of blend testing for the Habano line.
cigars.researchNote: Annual limited release: a round version came out in small numbers in 2024 and the box-pressed one followed in May 2025. Luxury Cigar Club lists an Ecuadorian Habano 2000 wrapper and medium strength. Halfwheel named Tabacalera Pages as the factory in 2025; the maker now says its cigars are made at La Tabacaria.

cigars.about: Lure's limited holiday blend, first released in November 2024 and brought back in March 2026 in one robusto extra size. Each run has been 3,000 cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Specs are for the 2026 release. The 2024 original used a Habano 2000 wrapper, was rated medium-plus and was made at Tabacalera Pages. The maker's site still describes the Habano 2000 version and calls it full.

cigars.about: A limited double-banded broadleaf toro that Lure releases each June in memory of the founder's father, Lou Cross Jr. The second band carries the years 1933 and 2023.
cigars.researchNote: The 2024 debut was a 6 x 52 toro rolled at Tabacalera Pages, limited to 1,200 cigars. The 2025 edition grew to 6 x 54 and 4,500 cigars, and the maker did not disclose that year's factory.

cigars.about: A limited San Andrés-wrapped blend in two torpedo sizes that Lure sold only to retailers who ordered at the 2026 PCA trade show. It reached shelves in June 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,700 of The Ono and 2,500 of The Kingfish. Halfwheel's trade show post listed an Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed wrapper, but its news stories, its review and the founder's own quote all say Mexican San Andrés. Halfwheel's review found the strength medium to medium-plus.

cigars.about: A limited robusto grande from Lure that shipped in August 2026, named for the future father-in-law of the founder's son and banded with a peacock bass. It uses Honduran as well as Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: About 4,000 cigars, sold at roughly 20 retailers. Strength and flavor notes come from a single retailer listing, which calls it medium-plus; no maker rating was found.

cigars.about: A limited Year of the Horse cigar made jointly by Lure and its distributor Valacari, named for a mythical seahorse. It is a box-pressed Nicaraguan puro with five-year-old filler, released in February 2026.
cigars.researchNote: A Lure and Valacari collaboration limited to 2,500 cigars at 18 retailers. Strength is from one retailer listing; Halfwheel's review found it medium-plus in body with little nicotine strength. Flavor notes are from that review.

cigars.about: A limited box-pressed toro from September 2025 made jointly by Lure and its distributor Valacari. It pairs the wrapper from Lure's Corojo Oscuro line with the binder and filler of Valacari's Lumineer.
cigars.researchNote: A Lure and Valacari collaboration limited to 2,500 cigars at ten retailers. Maker describes the strength as medium to full.

cigars.about: A slim broadleaf lonsdale released in January 2026 as part of Lure's limited Catch & Release series. It was made as a thinner companion to The Last Cast.
cigars.researchNote: Part of the Catch & Release series: 1,800 cigars, sold in 5-packs.

cigars.about: The first cigar in Lure's limited Catch & Release series, a box-pressed toro released in early 2024.
cigars.researchNote: The maker spells it The Speckl'd Perch. It was a one-time Catch & Release drop from early 2024, and no published blend, factory or strength was found.

cigars.about: The first Casa 1910 cigar and its flagship, a Mexican puro with a Sumatra-seed wrapper over San Andrés Negro binder and filler. It is named for the Chihuahua town where the Mexican Revolution began.
cigars.researchNote: The factory, in the San Andrés Valley of Veracruz, is not disclosed. It launched as a 5 x 50 robusto only; the Corona and Toro were added in April 2026.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andrés Negro maduro, aged 5 years
cigars.about: A Mexican puro made entirely of San Andrés Negro tobacco under a five-year-aged maduro wrapper. It is the stronger sibling of Cuchillo Parado, named for a Pancho Villa victory in the Mexican Revolution.
cigars.researchNote: The maker now lists it as Full; at its 2022 launch it was described as medium to full. It debuted as a 6 x 54 toro extra, which became a 6 x 52 Toro in the 2026 lineup. The factory is not disclosed.

cigars.about: A third core line from Casa 1910, a Mexican puro with a San Andrés Colorado Maduro wrapper over a San Andrés Claro binder. It is named for the city of Ébano, site of a 1915 battle.
cigars.researchNote: Announced in 2024 and delayed more than once; it was last scheduled for Q3 2026 and the maker's site still showed it as Coming Soon in October 2026, so it may not be on shelves yet. No tasting notes are published. The factory is not disclosed.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andrés Negro Colorado Maduro
cigars.about: One of two blends in Casa 1910's lower-priced Mexigars bundle line, made entirely of Mexican tobacco. The band is applied upside down so it looks like a volcano erupting as the cigar burns.
cigars.researchNote: Shown in 2024 as Mexigars MX-1 and renamed Colorado before shipping in April 2025. The Gordo was added in April 2026. The factory is not disclosed.

cigars.filler: Mexico (Habano Mexico Especial, San Andrés Negro)
cigars.about: One of two blends in Casa 1910's lower-priced Mexigars bundle line, a Mexican puro with a Mexican-grown habano wrapper. It is sold in bundles of 25 alongside the Mexigars Colorado.
cigars.researchNote: Shown in 2024 as Mexigars MX-2; some retailers list it as HBA. halfwheel's trade show listings give the wrapper as San Andrés Negro, while its news stories and the retailers say Mexican Habano. The factory is not disclosed.

cigars.about: A 6 x 54 torpedo from Casa 1910's Nicaraguan-made Cavalry Edition, with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper over a Mexican San Andrés binder. It is named for the white-starred mare ridden by Pancho Villa.
cigars.researchNote: One of three Cavalry Edition cigars, each sold in a single size; it is a close relative of the As de Oro toro. Neptune lists it as Medium while the company called the line medium to full bodied. Discontinued in 2026 and the factory was never disclosed.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Estelí ligero, Jalapa seco and viso, Ometepe viso)
cigars.about: A 6 x 54 toro extra from Casa 1910's Nicaraguan-made Cavalry Edition, with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper, Mexican San Andrés binder and Nicaraguan filler. It is named for Emiliano Zapata's horse.
cigars.researchNote: One of three Cavalry Edition cigars, each sold in a single size; it is a close relative of the Lucero torpedo. The halfwheel review found medium strength with medium-full to full body. Discontinued in 2026 and the factory was never disclosed.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Jalapa seco and viso, Estelí ligero)
cigars.about: A 6 x 60 gordo from Casa 1910's Nicaraguan-made Cavalry Edition, with a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is named for one of Pancho Villa's horses, a dark stallion.
cigars.researchNote: One of three Cavalry Edition cigars, each sold in a single size, and the only one with a San Andrés wrapper. Neptune lists it as Medium while describing it as medium to full bodied. Discontinued in 2026 and the factory was never disclosed.

cigars.about: A thick 5 1/2 x 58 cigar from Casa 1910's Dominican-made Soldadera Edition, with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper and Brazilian Arapiraca binder. It honors Amelia Robles, who fought in Zapata's army disguised as a man.
cigars.researchNote: Strength varies by source: Neptune describes it as medium to full but tags it Full, and another retailer says Medium. It is one of three Soldadera cigars, each its own blend in a single size. Discontinued in 2026.

cigars.about: A 5 x 50 robusto from Casa 1910's Dominican-made Soldadera Edition, with a Connecticut shade wrapper over Dominican binder. It honors Petra Herrera, who fought with Pancho Villa's forces and later led a brigade of women.
cigars.researchNote: The company calls it medium strength; Neptune's description says medium to full. halfwheel names the wrapper only as Connecticut, and retailers specify Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade. One of three Soldadera cigars, each its own blend in one size; discontinued in 2026.

cigars.about: A 6 x 52 toro from Casa 1910's Dominican-made Soldadera Edition, with a habano wrapper over a double binder of Mexican and Dominican leaf. It is named for a woman soldier from Oaxaca who fought with both Villa and Zapata.
cigars.researchNote: The company did not disclose where the habano wrapper is grown; Neptune lists it as Ecuadorian Habano maduro. The company calls it medium to full, and Neptune tags it Full. One of three Soldadera cigars, each its own blend in one size; discontinued in 2026.
