cigars.about: A limited aged version of the Cuchillo Parado robusto, using cigars rolled in 2020 from 2015 tobacco and rested three more years in cedar. Only 50 boxes of 50 were released, 2,500 cigars in all.
cigars.researchNote: Same blend as the regular Cuchillo Parado, which the maker rates Medium; no separate strength or tasting notes are published for the Reserva. It came only as a 5 x 50 robusto at $18. The factory is not disclosed.

cigars.about: The Connecticut Shade version of Nat Cicco's flagship HHB, sold by distributor Zander-Greg in 10-count boxes. It has a pigtail cap and a closed foot and was pitched as an affordable alternative to the Cohiba Behike.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2012 simply as HHB; it became HHB Classic once the Habano-wrapped Gold was added. The maker's site lists the Corona Extra as 6.25 x 50, but halfwheel and retailers list it as 5.25 x 60. The maker and Cigar Aficionado call it medium, while some retailers list it as full.

cigars.about: The Habano-wrapped version of Nat Cicco's flagship HHB, released to mark the brand's 50th anniversary. Like the Classic it has a pigtail cap and a closed foot and comes in 10-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers describe the wrapper as a reddish Habano maduro. The maker's site lists the Corona Extra as 6.25 x 50, but halfwheel and retailers list it as 5.25 x 60. The maker rates it medium, while Neptune and Cigars Direct list it as full.

cigars.about: A semi box-pressed, long-filler cigar with a pigtail cap and closed foot, named for the year Nat Cicco was founded. It is made in Nicaragua at Omar Ortez's Agrotabacos factory, and Cigar Aficionado ranked the Churchill No. 18 on its Top 25 of 2018.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium to full; Neptune lists it as full and describes the wrapper as a Habano maduro. The 2012 launch release described a Nicaraguan Habano-seed wrapper, but the maker now lists Ecuadorian Habano.

cigars.about: A box-pressed figurado made to mark 55 years of the Nat Cicco brand, blended by the late Rolando Villamil at the Dominican factory that also makes Epic Cigars. It came in 10-count boxes and was among the most expensive cigars the brand has sold.
cigars.researchNote: Also called the Nat Cicco Fifty Five. It was shown at the 2021 trade show but did not reach stores until February 2022. The maker's site now marks it discontinued, and production numbers were never disclosed.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro in oversized formats with a flared, shaggy open foot that gives the cigar its name. It wears a reddish maduro wrapper and comes in boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: The maker and Cigars Direct call it full, while Neptune's description says medium-bodied. The maker lists the Juniors at 7.5 x 60, but Neptune and Cigars Direct list it at 6.5 x 60. The maker does not name the factory.

cigars.about: A value-priced Nicaraguan cigar from Zander-Greg's Nat Cicco brand with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, sold in boxes of 24. Cigar Aficionado has rated it 92 points.
cigars.researchNote: Not shown on the maker's own site. halfwheel says it was introduced in 2016 with a wide release in July 2017. A 7.5 x 40 Lancero was announced for fall 2022.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut Broadleaf (Natural); Maduro and Candela versions also made
cigars.about: The original Nat Cicco Rejects, the budget cigar from 1965 that started the factory seconds category. It is a mild medium-filler cigar made in the Dominican Republic in Natural, Maduro and Candela wrappers.
cigars.researchNote: Usually listed simply as Nat Cicco Rejects. The maker lists the Natural wrapper as Connecticut and the Maduro as Jamaican, and rates the Maduro medium; a 2013 company release says Connecticut Broadleaf. Company releases describe machine bunching with a homogenized binder and mixed remnant filler.

cigars.about: A handmade Cuban sandwich style budget cigar added to the Nat Cicco Rejects family in 2016. It pairs Nicaraguan filler with an Indonesian binder and comes in Natural or Maduro Habano wrappers.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel lists it as Rejects Nicaragua. The Natural is rated medium and the Maduro medium to full. The wrapper's country is undisclosed, and the maker does not say where the cigar is rolled.

cigars.about: A plain-looking bundle cigar from Nat Cicco made entirely of Nicaraguan long-filler tobacco. It was introduced in 2017 as a low-priced, medium to full strength everyday smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Also written Nicaraguan Long Fillers. The maker's text says medium to full, but the strength scale on the same page shows full. All three components are Nicaraguan, but the maker does not name the wrapper type or say where the cigar is rolled.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Cuban-seed Rosado (Natural and Maduro); Habano on the Habano version
cigars.about: Nat Cicco's first handmade, all-tobacco value cigar, a Nicaraguan Cuban sandwich blend sold in bundles of 20. It comes in Natural, Maduro and Habano versions.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the Natural and Maduro wrappers as Cuban Rosado with no country; Cigars Direct calls the Natural Ecuadorian Sumatra. The maker rates the Natural mild to medium and the Maduro and Habano medium. The Habano version was added in 2013.

cigars.about: A mild budget cigar from Nat Cicco made in the Dominican Republic with picadura (tobacco remnant) filler under a Connecticut broadleaf wrapper. It comes in Natural and Maduro.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates the Natural mild and the Maduro mild to medium. It lists both binder and filler only as picadura, with no countries, and does not name the factory.

cigars.about: A long-running mild budget cigar from Nat Cicco that was first made in Jamaica and is now made in the Dominican Republic. It uses picadura (tobacco remnant) filler and comes in Natural and Maduro in slim, traditional shapes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's page conflicts with itself: the text says Connecticut broadleaf wrapper, while the spec list calls the wrapper, binder and filler Jamaican. A 2013 company release gave larger sizes (Presidents 7.5 x 46, Regales 7.5 x 34). The Natural is mild and the Maduro mild to medium.

cigars.about: One of the first two Saga blends from the Reyes family's De Los Reyes factory in Santiago, introduced in 2014. The original pairs a reddish Brazilian Cubra wrapper with a Dominican Habano binder.
cigars.researchNote: Blend shown is the original. Cigar Coop reported a 2024 revamp with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Dominican tobaccos in the same three sizes, so newer boxes may differ. The maker called it medium-bodied; retailers list medium to full strength.

cigars.about: A light Ecuadorian Connecticut cigar from De Los Reyes, launched in 2019 as the company's first mild to medium blend. The binder and filler come from the Reyes family farms in the Dominican Republic, and the name refers to leisure time after work.
cigars.researchNote: The maker bills it as mild to medium; Neptune and Corona Cigar list it as medium. The 6 x 44 Corona was added in 2023 and comes in 8-count boxes.

cigars.line: Short Tales Tomo I: Tales of High Priming
cigars.about: The first volume of Saga's Short Tales series from De Los Reyes, released in 2016 in a box built to look like an old book. It is a short, thick cigar made with high-priming leaf and is known as the strongest of the series.
cigars.researchNote: Each Short Tales tomo is its own blend in a single size, sold in book-style boxes of 10. The series was planned for ten volumes and seven have been released.

cigars.line: Short Tales Tomo II: Tales of the Land Cotuí
cigars.about: The second Short Tales volume, released in late 2016. It is a short torpedo built around a Dominican wrapper grown in Cotuí on a farm owned by Monika Kelner, and was blended to be lighter in nicotine than Tomo I.
cigars.researchNote: Sources differ on strength: Neptune lists Full, Cigar Coop medium to full, and halfwheel's later review found it closer to medium. Halfwheel gives the size as 4 7/8 x 52; Neptune and Cigar Coop list 5 x 54.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano Mejorado viso), Brazil (Habano viso)
cigars.about: The third Short Tales volume, shown at the 2017 trade show alongside Tomos IV and V. L.I.V. stands for Labor Ipse Voluptas, Latin for the pleasure is in the work itself, and it is a small medium-bodied corona.
cigars.researchNote: One blend in one size, sold in book-style boxes of 10. Halfwheel and retailers list 4 1/4 x 42; Cigar Coop lists 4 1/2 x 42.

cigars.about: The fourth Short Tales volume, a small perfecto introduced in 2017. L.O.V. stands for Labor Omnia Vincit, Latin for work conquers all.
cigars.researchNote: One blend in one size, sold in book-style boxes of 10. Neptune lists it as medium; Cigar Coop's review rated both strength and body medium to full.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano Mejorado viso), USA (Connecticut Broadleaf viso)
cigars.about: The fifth Short Tales volume, a thin 5 x 34 panatela with a light Ecuadorian wrapper, introduced in 2017. L.A.V. stands for Laudamus Abundantia Veteres, Latin for we honor the richness of time past.
cigars.researchNote: One blend in one size. Neptune lists it as medium; halfwheel found it starting just above mild and reaching medium at the end, and Cigar Coop rated it mild to medium.

cigars.line: Short Tales Tomo VI: The Sixth Element: El Tabaco
cigars.about: The sixth Short Tales volume, a 5 1/2 x 58 gordo with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper, released in 2018. It was Cigar Coop's 2019 Cigar of the Year.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune and Cigar Coop rate it medium, though halfwheel's first review found medium-full strength and full body. Halfwheel lists a Sumatra binder of undisclosed origin, while Cigar Coop lists a Dominican San Vicente binder.

cigars.line: Short Tales Tomo VII: Tales of the Land: Navarrete
cigars.about: The seventh and most recent Short Tales volume, a box-pressed robusto released in 2021. It is named for Navarrete, the Dominican town where the Reyes family harvested its first crop of Piloto Cubano tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: One blend in one size, sold in book-style boxes of 10. Neptune lists it as medium; halfwheel and Cigar Coop both found it medium to full.

cigars.about: A Dominican puro with a Corojo 2006 wrapper, introduced in 2014 as one of the first two Saga blends from the Reyes family. The maker describes it as full in both strength and body.
cigars.researchNote: Current availability is unclear: Neptune shows no stock and Corona Cigar no longer lists it. The maker calls it full strength; Cigar Coop's review found it medium rising to medium-full. The factory was called Corporación Cigar Export when it launched.

cigars.about: An offshoot of Saga Golden Age that debuted in 2023, built around a Dominican wrapper grown in Yamasá by Monika Kelner. The wrapper is always from a crop four years old, so the 2023 release used 2019 leaf.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not disclose the binder or filler; Corona Cigar and Cigar Coop describe it as a Dominican puro. One size in boxes of 10, with 5,000 boxes for the 2023 release. Retailers rate it medium, while halfwheel found the strength mild to just under medium.

cigars.about: The first release in Saga's gemstone-themed Gem Series from De Los Reyes, named for Dominican amber. It debuted at InterTabac 2025 and launched in the U.S. at the 2026 PCA show, with ten band designs that form a picture of amber across the box.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel reports some North American filler, while Cigar Coop calls it a Dominican puro. Halfwheel lists the Corona at 5 5/8 x 48 and Cigar Coop at 5 3/4 x 48. The maker describes it as medium-bodied, and it comes in boxes of 20.

cigars.about: The original house blend of United Cigars' Firecracker, a 3 1/2 x 50 short robusto with a long pigtail cap shaped like a fuse. It is the regular production cigar behind the many limited Firecracker collaborations.
cigars.researchNote: United calls it full-bodied; Corona lists medium to full and Neptune medium. halfwheel and Neptune call the wrapper Ecuadorian Habano and add Nicaraguan filler. The Firecracker idea dates to 2006-2007 at Two Guys Smoke Shop; the house blend's own launch year is not published.

cigars.about: The dark-wrapper version of United Cigars' regular production Firecracker, a 3 1/2 x 50 short robusto with a fuse-style pigtail. It was previously sold as the Black Bomb Firecracker.
cigars.researchNote: Formerly the Black Bomb Firecracker, whose 2023 blend halfwheel listed with a Sumatra binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. United calls it full-bodied; Neptune lists medium and an Ecuadorian maduro wrapper.

cigars.about: The third regular production Firecracker blend from United Cigars, shown at TPE 2024 and shipped that April. It is a 3 1/2 x 50 short robusto with the line's fuse-style pigtail and a Connecticut shade wrapper.
A darker United Cigars house blend in the 3 1/2 x 50 Firecracker format with the fuse-style pigtail. It was reblended and repackaged in 2023 and is now sold as the Firecracker Maduro.
cigars.researchNote: The name was retired: halfwheel reports it became the Firecracker Maduro. The blend shown is the 2023 version; United never disclosed the earlier blend or its launch year. No strength rating is published.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Barber pole of Dominican Candela and Mexican San Andres
cigars.about: A St. Patrick's Day Firecracker from United Cigars with a green and dark barber pole wrapper and a candela fuse. It shipped in early 2021 in five-packs, with about 14,500 cigars made.
cigars.researchNote: Two-leaf barber pole wrapper, so no single wrapper type applies. halfwheel lists it at 3 x 50, but the Developing Palates review lists 3 1/2 x 50. Strength is from that review.

cigars.about: The 2026 Firecracker, made with Arnold André for the 250th anniversary of the United States and sold in 12-count tins that double as ashtrays. The blend proved popular enough that United turned it into the regular Independence line in Robusto and Toro.
cigars.researchNote: United's page calls the blend full-bodied, but its announcement said medium-plus strength and Corona Cigar lists medium to full. Leaf details and flavors come from United's page for the regular Independence line, which is the same blend. Over 30,000 cigars were made.

cigars.about: J.C. Newman's 2025 entry in the Firecracker Series, marking 60 years since Stanford Newman brought Cameroon wrapper to premium cigars. It wears the El Baton band but is a different blend, limited to 500 boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: Also called the El Baton Cameroon Firecracker. It is not the regular El Baton blend. Strength is from Corona Cigar's listing.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Corojo 99 and Criollo 98, Jalapa and Esteli)
cigars.about: Aganorsa Leaf's 2024 Firecracker, putting the JFR Lunatic Loco blend into the 3 1/2 x 50 fuse-capped format. It is an all-Nicaraguan cigar sold in boxes of 20 as a limited release.
cigars.researchNote: Aganorsa bills Lunatic Loco as its strongest cigar. Production numbers were not disclosed.

cigars.about: The 2023 Firecracker from E.P. Carrillo, using the Pledge blend in the 3 1/2 x 50 fuse-capped format. It was limited to 1,000 boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates the Pledge line full, but the Developing Palates review of this short size found it closer to medium. It is one limited size of the Pledge line.

cigars.about: A Firecracker made by El Artista with baseball Hall of Famer David Ortiz, using a modified version of the Big Papi Slugger blend. It came out in March 2022 with 1,000 boxes of 20 and returned in 2023 with 200 more boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Strength and body come from halfwheel and Developing Palates reviews, which ranged from medium-plus to medium-full.

cigars.about: Foundation Cigar Co.'s Firecracker, putting The Wise Man Maduro blend into the 3 1/2 x 50 fuse-capped size. It debuted in June 2021 with 500 boxes of 20 and came back in 2022 and 2023.
cigars.researchNote: One limited size of The Wise Man Maduro line. Foundation rates the line medium; halfwheel's review found medium-plus strength with medium-full body. United said the 2023 batch would be the last.

cigars.about: HVC's entry in the Firecracker Series, a 3 1/2 x 50 fuse-capped take on its annual Black Friday release. It shipped in November 2020 and was limited to 500 boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: No maker strength rating is published. The Developing Palates panel put it between medium-full and full, with most calling it full.

cigars.filler: Italy (upper Tiber valley, Verona, Pontecorvo), United States (Kentucky, Tennessee)
cigars.wrapperLeaf: North American fire-cured Kentucky (grown in Kentucky and Tennessee)
cigars.about: A hand-rolled Italian cigar from the Lucca factory with a U.S. fire-cured Kentucky wrapper and a rougher-cut filler. It has the classic double-tapered Toscano shape and can be smoked whole or cut in half.
cigars.researchNote: No binder. Maker rates strength 6 of 7 and body 5 of 7. Famous Smoke lists the wrapper as Italian and the size as 6 x 38, but the maker says the wrapper is U.S.-grown and halfwheel measures 6 2/3 inches by 41 ring at the middle.

cigars.about: The standard Toscano, sold since 1930 and made in Lucca from fire-cured Kentucky tobacco with an Italian wrapper. It gets a shorter fermentation than the Antico, which makes for a sharper, livelier smoke.
cigars.researchNote: No binder; Smokingpipes lists it as machine-made. Maker rates strength and body 5 of 7, while Famous Smoke calls it Full. The maker does not publish a size, so 6 x 38 is the retailer listing.

cigars.about: The strong, traditional Toscano, introduced in 1973 and made in Lucca. Its U.S. Kentucky wrapper is fire-cured for over 30 days on hickory and oak, and the cigar is fermented and aged more than ten months.
cigars.researchNote: No binder; Smokingpipes lists it as machine-made. Maker rates strength and body 6 of 7. Smokingpipes lists the wrapper as Italian, but the maker and Famous Smoke say U.S.-grown; 6 x 38 is the retailer size, since the maker does not publish one.

cigars.about: A lighter, sweeter Toscano introduced in 1982 for the centenary of Giuseppe Garibaldi's death, built on Kentucky tobacco from the Benevento area. The maker describes it as medium in strength with a mellow, aromatic character.
cigars.researchNote: No binder; Smokingpipes lists it as machine-made. Maker rates strength and body 4 of 7 and calls it medium, while Famous Smoke lists it Full and 6 x 38. Halfwheel says the imported filler is U.S. Kentucky.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Italian dark fire-cured Kentucky from Tuscany
cigars.about: A wide-bellied Toscano made entirely from Italian Kentucky tobacco grown in Tuscany, Lazio and Campania. It was sold only in Italy before coming to the U.S. in April 2026.
cigars.researchNote: No binder. Maker rates strength 7 of 7 and body 6 of 7, its top strength rating. The maker's 2026 date is the U.S. launch; it was already on sale in Italy by May 2025, so the original release year is not confirmed.

cigars.factory: Manifatture Sigaro Toscano (Campese, near Bassano del Grappa)
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nostrano del Brenta (Havana-seed, dark air-cured) from Veneto
cigars.about: Toscano's first air-cured cigar, made from Nostrano del Brenta, a Havana-seed tobacco grown in the Veneto region. It is short and thick, has a binder, and needs humidor storage, unlike the fire-cured Toscanos.
cigars.researchNote: Maker calls the strength light to medium; Famous Smoke lists Medium. It debuted in 2024 as a limited release and returned in 2025 as regular production. Keep it in a humidor at 65 to 70 percent.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Italian fire-cured Kentucky from Valtiberina, Tuscany
cigars.about: A 2024 Toscano made entirely from Kentucky-seed fire-cured tobacco grown in Italy, with most of the filler from Benevento. The first U.S. release was 500 boxes of 30.
cigars.researchNote: No binder. Strength and body are from the halfwheel review, and the ring gauge is not published. Halfwheel's review table says regular production, but the first U.S. release was 500 boxes and it is not on the maker's current U.S. list.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Italian fire-cured Kentucky from Valtiberina, Tuscany
cigars.about: The first blend in Toscano's Master Aged line, with an Italian wrapper over a half Italian, half American Kentucky filler. Like the whole series it is aged 360 days in climate-controlled rooms after rolling.
cigars.researchNote: No binder; the maker spells it Serie 1. Maker rates strength 5 of 7 and body 6 of 7, while Famous Smoke lists Full and 6 3/4 x 40. Unlike most Toscanos, the Master Aged cigars should be kept in a humidor.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: North American fire-cured Kentucky from Tennessee
cigars.about: The second Master Aged blend, with a Tennessee-grown Kentucky wrapper fire-cured for 30 days over a mix of Italian and American filler. It is aged 360 days after rolling.
cigars.researchNote: No binder; the maker spells it Serie 2. Maker rates strength and body 6 of 7. Halfwheel gives 6 1/3 x 40 while Famous Smoke lists 6 3/4 x 40; keep it in a humidor.

cigars.about: The all-American blend in the Master Aged line, made in Lucca from stalk-cut, long fire-cured U.S. Kentucky tobacco for both wrapper and filler. It is aged 360 days after rolling.
cigars.researchNote: No binder; the maker spells it Serie 3. Maker rates strength and body 6 of 7 and Famous Smoke lists Full, but halfwheel's reviewer found it peaked just under medium in strength. Keep it in a humidor.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Italian micro-fermented fire-cured Kentucky from Valtiberina, Tuscany
cigars.about: A thicker Master Aged release from 2023 whose Italian wrapper spends about ten days in a hot, humid room to start a micro-fermentation. It is aged 360 days after rolling.
cigars.researchNote: No binder. Maker rates strength and body 6 of 7. Maker says the filler is half Tuscan and half Kentucky and Tennessee, while halfwheel reported all Italian; halfwheel gives 6 1/3 x 46 and Famous Smoke lists 6 3/4 x 44.

cigars.about: The shortest and thickest Master Aged cigar, released in 2025 with a micro-fermented Italian wrapper over Italian and American Kentucky filler. It measures 50 ring at the middle and tapers to 38 at the ends.
cigars.researchNote: No binder; the maker spells it Serie 5. Maker rates strength and body 6 of 7. Maker and halfwheel give 5 x 50, while Famous Smoke lists 5 1/2 x 46.

cigars.about: A tribute to Louis J. Zucca, founder of the family company that owns Emilio. It is blended by James Brown of Black Label Trading Co. and rolled at his Fabrica Oveja Negra in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Maker's line page lists an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, but its 2020 and 2021 releases were limited editions with dual Nicaraguan Habano and Sun Grown wrappers in a barber pole. The 2017 original had an Ecuadorian Habano binder and Nicaraguan filler. A 6 1/2 x 42 Lonsdale was added in 2021.

cigars.about: Emilio's Connecticut-wrapped core line and the milder entry in the portfolio. It was reblended and redesigned in 2019 by James Brown and is made at Fabrica Oveja Negra in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: First released in 2012 as Emilio AF Suave; the current blend and look date from 2019. The maker calls the wrapper Connecticut without saying where it is grown, and does not publish a strength.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Emilio's Suave, added to the core line in 2022. James Brown blended it and describes it as medium in both body and strength.
cigars.researchNote: Maker's line page lists Nicaraguan filler only, while its 2022 press release says Nicaragua and Dominican. Halfwheel's 2022 news called the wrapper Ecuadorian habano; the maker says Ecuador Maduro.

cigars.about: A core Emilio line with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, made at Fabrica Oveja Negra in Esteli. Its artwork shows a vinyl record labeled Side 1.
cigars.researchNote: Maker lists sizes by dimensions only; the size names are borrowed from the Emilio AF1, which has the same wrapper and sizes. The maker does not say Side 1 is a renamed AF1 and publishes no strength for it.

cigars.about: A core Emilio line with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, made at Fabrica Oveja Negra in Esteli. Its artwork shows a vinyl record labeled Side 2.
cigars.researchNote: Maker lists sizes by dimensions only; the size names are borrowed from the Emilio AF2, which has the same wrapper and sizes. The maker does not say Side 2 is a renamed AF2 and publishes no strength for it.

cigars.about: Launched at the 2016 IPCPR show as one of Emilio's first new blends after Gary Griffith left, made at James Brown's Fabrica Oveja Negra. The name is a musical term for a simple song or melody.
cigars.researchNote: Maker's page shows the small size as 4.55 x 48; reviews list it as a 4 1/2 x 48 Rothschild. Blind Man's Puff (2018) listed the wrapper as Ecuadorian Habano Maduro with an Ecuadorian binder; the maker now lists a Nicaraguan Habano binder.

cigars.about: A limited Sumatra-wrapped version of Emilio's Suave, shown at the 2026 PCA show and shipped in August 2026. It is blended by James Brown and made at Fabrica Oveja Negra.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 5,000 cigars per size (250 boxes of 20). The maker only says Sumatra; halfwheel reports the leaf is grown in Indonesia. The maker does not publish a strength.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Corojo and Ecuadorian Maduro (dual wrapper)
cigars.about: A 2025 limited edition from Emilio with two wrappers rolled in a barber pole pattern. James Brown blended it at Fabrica Oveja Negra and calls it bold and spice forward.
cigars.researchNote: Barber pole of Ecuadorian Corojo and Ecuadorian Maduro wrappers, so it is not a single-wrapper cigar. Limited to 250 boxes of 20 per size. No strength rating is published.

cigars.about: First released by Emilio in 2011 and named after an old word for a cat. James Brown remade it at Fabrica Oveja Negra in 2018, and it now comes back as a limited Halloween release.
cigars.researchNote: Maker's page shows the 2018 Nicaraguan puro in two sizes. The 2023 and 2025 Seasonal Editions are a 5 x 50 robusto with an Ecuador Maduro and Corojo barber pole wrapper; the maker calls the 2025 medium strength. The original 2011 blend was renamed Mousa in the La Musa series in 2012.

cigars.about: A limited Nicaraguan puro from Emilio, remade by James Brown at Fabrica Oveja Negra. The name dates to 2012, when the original Grimalkin was renamed La Musa.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's 2019 release calls the wrapper Nicaraguan Sun Grown; halfwheel lists it as Nicaraguan habano. The Oveja Negra version was shown in 2019 and shipped in March 2020, 250 boxes of 25 per size. A 2021 store-exclusive lancero used an Ecuadorian maduro wrapper.

cigars.about: A small-production Emilio blend made at Fabrica Oveja Negra, with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan and Dominican tobaccos. It is made in very small quantities and is one of the lesser known Emilio lines.
cigars.researchNote: Maker lists it under limited releases in a single 5 x 50 size; halfwheel in 2021 called it regular production in very small quantities. A 4 1/2 x 46 Corona Extra was announced in 2021. No launch year or strength is published; it was already being made by early 2019.

cigars.about: A limited edition from Emilio that debuted in 2022 as a single robusto and returned in 2023 in three sizes. James Brown blended it at Fabrica Oveja Negra as a stronger, earthier cigar than the rest of the Emilio range.
cigars.researchNote: Strength ratings vary: halfwheel called the 2022 release medium-full building to full, while Cigar Coop and Developing Palates put the 2023 release at medium or just under. The maker only says it is a step up in strength from the rest of Emilio. The 2023 run was 200 boxes of 20 per size.

cigars.about: The mildest of the five Gourmet Collection blends Jake Wyatt launched with in 2020, wrapped in Ecuadorian Connecticut. It is built to be smooth and creamy.
cigars.researchNote: Reblended in 2026 when production moved from the Dominican Republic to Honduras. The original version was made at Tabacalera JVM with Dominican binder and filler and San Andres maduro accent leaf. A 7 x 49/64 figurado is sold as a limited edition.

cigars.about: One of the five Gourmet Collection blends Jake Wyatt launched with in 2020, now wrapped in a Habano Oscuro leaf. The name refers to being in the zone in sports.
cigars.researchNote: Maker's catalog rates strength Medium but calls it medium-full bodied. Wrapper origin is not stated. Reblended in 2026 with the move to Honduras; the original Dominican-made version used a Dominican habano rosado wrapper with candela accents over Dominican binder and filler.

cigars.about: A San Andrés maduro blend from Jake Wyatt's Gourmet Collection, part of the company's 2020 launch. It is named for the English philosopher Herbert Spencer.
cigars.researchNote: Reblended in 2026 when production moved to Honduras. The original version was made at Tabacalera JVM in the Dominican Republic with Dominican binder and filler and Ecuadorian Connecticut accent leaf.

cigars.about: The candela-wrapped blend in Jake Wyatt's Gourmet Collection, part of the company's 2020 launch. The maker describes it as creamy and buttery.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper origin is not stated for the current blend. Reblended in 2026 with the move to Honduras; the original Dominican-made version used a Dominican candela wrapper with San Andres maduro accents over Dominican binder and filler.

cigars.about: A Corojo-wrapped blend from Jake Wyatt's Gourmet Collection, part of the company's 2020 launch. The name stands for unsuspected inner resource.
cigars.researchNote: Maker's catalog rates strength Medium but calls it medium-full bodied. Reblended in 2026 with the move to Honduras; the original Dominican-made version used a Dominican habano rosado wrapper with San Andres maduro accents over Dominican binder and filler.

cigars.about: Jake Wyatt's seventh line, soft-launched in late 2020 and given a full release in 2021. The name reflects the hope that it has a calming effect on the smoker.
cigars.researchNote: The maker now lists a Sumatra wrapper, origin not stated. halfwheel listed Ecuadorian habano over Dominican binder and filler for the original 2020-21 version made at Tabacalera JVM. The line was reblended in 2026 with the move to Honduras.

cigars.about: A full-bodied San Andrés maduro blend in Jake Wyatt's Connoisseur Collection, named for co-founder Gerard Abajian's son. It debuted in 2023 as the company's boldest cigar to that point.
cigars.researchNote: Reblended in 2026 when production moved to Honduras. The original 2023 version was made at Casamorabo Tabacalera in the Dominican Republic with a corojo binder and filler that included Pennsylvania broadleaf.

cigars.about: A dark, smoky blend in Jake Wyatt's Connoisseur Collection that debuted in 2024 and is known for its Tennessee fire-cured tobacco. It is named for the figure in Greek myth who flew too close to the sun.
cigars.researchNote: Maker rates it Medium-Full to Full and now lists only an Oscuro wrapper, origin not stated. The original Dominican-made blend used Mexican San Andres maduro, Dominican olor binder and Tennessee fire-cured and Pennsylvania broadleaf filler. A 7 x 49/64 salomon is a limited edition.

cigars.about: The lightest of the three blends in Jake Wyatt's value-priced Titan Series, released in 2026 with a claro wrapper. It is the most approachable of the trio.
cigars.researchNote: One of three blends in the Titan Series (Goliad, Colossus, Omega) that share a binder and filler and differ only in wrapper. The wrapper's origin is not disclosed.

cigars.about: The darkest and strongest of the three blends in Jake Wyatt's value-priced Titan Series, released in 2026 with an oscuro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: One of three Titan Series blends (Goliad, Colossus, Omega) that share a binder and filler and differ only in wrapper. Maker's catalog rates it Medium-Full to Full and its site calls it full-bodied. The wrapper's origin is not disclosed.

cigars.about: The rosado-wrapped blend in Jake Wyatt's value-priced Titan Series, released in 2026. It sits between Goliad and Colossus and leans on sweetness and spice.
cigars.researchNote: One of three blends in the Titan Series (Goliad, Colossus, Omega) that share a binder and filler and differ only in wrapper. The wrapper's origin is not disclosed.

cigars.about: An everyday, lower-priced line Jake Wyatt released in September 2026 in a single toro size. It uses a wrapper from Nicaragua's Jalapa region.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists Nicaraguan and Honduran filler; halfwheel also lists United States tobacco in the filler. No strength rating or wrapper leaf type is published; the maker only calls it approachable.

cigars.about: The original PG blend, launched in 1990 by Dr. Paul Garmirian alongside his book The Gourmet Guide to Cigars. It is a medium Dominican cigar made by Davidoff's Dominican operation and known for long aging, including vintage boxes rolled in the 1990s.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it 5 out of 10 in strength. The line has about 20 sizes; ten are listed here. It was long rolled at Davidoff's Occidental Cigar Factory in Santiago, and halfwheel reports that production has since moved to Davidoff's O.K. Cigars.

cigars.about: A 1999 follow-up to the original PG Gourmet Series with a little more spice. It is aged in cedar boxes and sits just above the original in strength.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it 5.5 out of 10 in strength and does not say where the Connecticut Shade wrapper is grown. It launched with the Torpedo and Robusto; the Connoisseur and Belicoso Fino followed in 2001.

cigars.about: A two-size regular production line released in October 2025 to mark 35 years of the PG Gourmet Series. It pairs an Ecuadorian habano wrapper with Dominican binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel's news story names the Occidental Cigar Factory, but its later review says that factory closed and the cigars are made at Davidoff's O.K. Cigars. The maker says 135 smokers tested the blend before release.

cigars.about: Released in July 2020 as the third Gourmet Series blend and a marker of the brand's 30th year. It is the richest of the three Gourmet Series blends, with a darker Ecuadorian habano wrapper over Dominican tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: Also called Gourmet Series III. The maker rates it 6.5 out of 10 in strength. halfwheel's review names both the Occidental Cigar Factory and Davidoff's O.K. Cigars as the factory; PG production has since moved to O.K. Cigars.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Habano (the maker calls it a dark, oily Oscuro Maduro)
cigars.about: A limited edition that began shipping in November 2015 for the brand's 25th year, first as 25,000 Connoisseur toros. A Short Robusto followed in 2016 and a Belicoso in 2024.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls the wrapper an Oscuro Maduro and does not name its origin; halfwheel identifies it as Ecuadorian habano. The maker rates it 7.5 out of 10, medium to full in strength but full in flavor. Each size was a limited run: 25,000 Connoisseurs, 150 boxes of Short Robusto and 200 boxes of Belicoso.

cigars.about: A full bodied limited edition that marked the brand's 20th year in 2010, blended with Henke Kelner and Eladio Diaz. It started as a single Connoisseur toro and grew to seven sizes, each boxed by production year.
cigars.researchNote: Also sold as PG Symphony 20. The blend is mostly undisclosed: the maker only cites a dark, oily wrapper, a Havana seed binder and four fillers. The maker rates it 8.5 out of 10 and dates the release to 2010; halfwheel says the first size appeared in 2009.

cigars.about: A full bodied line introduced in 2005 for the brand's 15th year, starting with the Belicoso Extra. It puts a dark Nicaraguan wrapper over aged Dominican binder and filler and now runs to ten sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it 8 out of 10 in strength and says the filler comes from the same farms used for the first PG cigars in 1990.

cigars.about: A full bodied member of the PG Gourmet Series with a Nicaraguan colorado wrapper over aged Dominican binder and filler. The maker describes it as aromatic and smoother than its strength suggests.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it 8 out of 10 in strength and does not give a release year.

cigars.about: A Gourmet Series blend introduced in 2001 and built around tobaccos aged about ten years. It uses an Ecuadorian wrapper, an aged Dominican binder and Dominican and Ecuadorian fillers.
cigars.researchNote: Often shortened to R.E. The maker lists only an Ecuadorian wrapper and rates it 7 out of 10, medium to full; halfwheel identifies the wrapper as Ecuadorian Connecticut. halfwheel found the Gran Panatela full in flavor but mild in strength.

cigars.about: The maduro member of the PG Gourmet Series, with a Connecticut broadleaf wrapper, an Indonesian binder and Dominican and Brazilian fillers. The maker describes it as deep in flavor but smooth.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it 7 out of 10 in strength and gives no release year, though it sells Toritos rolled in 2003. It does not say where the broadleaf wrapper is grown.

cigars.about: PG's lower priced, light to medium line, sold since 1997 in nine numbered sizes. It is known as a consistent everyday smoke and is popular with golfers.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it 4 out of 10 in strength and credits the rollers at Tabacos Dominicanos, the Kelner and Davidoff operation that makes all PG cigars. No tasting notes are published beyond smoothness.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian-grown Connecticut (since 2019); originally a Dominican wrapper
cigars.about: A full bodied, lower priced sister to the Artisan's Selection, introduced at the 2011 IPCPR trade show in three sizes. It began as a Dominican puro and has used an Ecuadorian-grown Connecticut wrapper since 2019.
cigars.researchNote: Two versions exist: the original 2011 Dominican puro, which the maker rates 8.5 out of 10, and the Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapped version made since 2019, rated 7.5. The 2011 launch release claimed 9.25 out of 10. No tasting notes are published.

cigars.about: A one-time limited toro from Jeremy McDonald's Wildfire Cigar Co., named after a fly fishing term. It was the first of the company's monthly made-to-order releases and shipped in March 2026.
cigars.researchNote: The factory is undisclosed; Wildfire says only that it is made in the Dominican Republic. Production numbers were not announced. The maker says it starts medium and finishes full, while halfwheel's reviewer found the strength below medium.

cigars.about: A limited robusto extra from Wildfire Cigar Co. with a San Andrés wrapper and an unusual Sumatra-seed binder grown in India. It was the second of the company's monthly made-to-order releases, shipping in April 2026.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the filler as Criollo 98, Ecuadorian and Corojo; halfwheel lists Ecuadorian habano and Nicaraguan Criollo 98. Halfwheel says the Sumatra-seed binder was grown in India, while one retailer lists it as Indonesian. Production numbers were not announced.

cigars.about: A limited corona gorda from Wildfire Cigar Co. built around a five-year-old Ecuadorian corojo wrapper and meant to show the lighter side of the company's blending. It shipped in July 2026 as part of the monthly made-to-order series.
cigars.researchNote: The maker writes the name with a hyphen; halfwheel and Cigar Dojo write Radio Octave. A one-and-done run made to the number of retailer orders, with the total not disclosed.

cigars.about: The October 2026 release in Wildfire Cigar Co.'s monthly made-to-order limited series, a single robusto extra themed around unplugging from phones and screens. Its band shows a towable camper like the one in the company's trade show booths.
cigars.researchNote: Fifth release in the series Wildfire informally calls the Camp Counselor Enrollment Program. The maker has not published a strength rating. One retailer calls it medium-bodied and lists it as 5 1/2 x 54, while halfwheel and Cigar Dojo give 5 1/4 x 54.

cigars.about: Wildfire Cigar Co.'s first regular production line from 2021, since discontinued and brought back in August 2026 as a reworked limited edition. The new version is a box-pressed toro made in the Dominican Republic with a different filler blend.
cigars.researchNote: Details shown are the 2026 limited version. The original 2021 line was made at Joya de Nicaragua in Corona Gorda (5 5/8 x 46), Robusto (5 1/4 x 50) and Toro (6 1/4 x 52), also with a Mexican claro wrapper, and is discontinued. Wildfire calls the new one medium-bodied.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The debut limited edition from Jeremy McDonald's Wildfire Cigar Co., a single Churchill made at Joya de Nicaragua. It shipped in September 2021 and was limited to 750 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 7,500 cigars. Strength, body and flavors come from halfwheel's review, which found it below medium strength until the final third. It scored 89 there.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A limited Churchill from Wildfire Cigar Co. shown at PCA 2024 and made at Joya de Nicaragua. Wildfire says it uses the same tobaccos as The Single in different positions and proportions to show how much that changes a cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 500 boxes of 10. Wildfire says the components match The Single, though The Single's binder was originally listed as Nicaraguan. No strength rating or tasting notes were published.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto), Mexico (San Andrés), USA (Pennsylvania Broadleaf)
cigars.about: A limited corona gorda from Wildfire Cigar Co. released at PCA 2024 and made in Danlí, Honduras. It is the second part of a three-part series modeled on the parts of a rock song, following The Intro.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 500 boxes of 10. The wrapper is listed only as Dominican, with no seed type given. No strength rating or tasting notes were published.

cigars.about: A limited corona gorda from Wildfire Cigar Co. introduced at TPE 2023 and made in Danlí, Honduras. It is the first part of a three-part series modeled on the parts of a rock song: intro, hook and breakdown.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 700 boxes of 10. It was Wildfire's first cigar from the Honduran factory best known for Cavalier Genève. No strength rating or tasting notes were published.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto), USA (Pennsylvania Broadleaf), Nicaragua (Jalapa), Paraguay
cigars.about: A three-size line from Wildfire Cigar Co. introduced in 2023 and made in Danlí, Honduras, notable for including Paraguayan tobacco in the filler. It launched as regular production but Wildfire has since stopped offering regular lines.
cigars.researchNote: Strength and body come from halfwheel's review of the Robusto, which found it mild to just under medium. Cigars Lover rated the Corona Gorda medium. Halfwheel reports Wildfire no longer has regular production offerings.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A three-size line from Wildfire Cigar Co. launched at PCA 2023 and made at Joya de Nicaragua. The name is a Celtic word tied to a bear god, a nod to the bear in the company's trade show booth.
cigars.researchNote: Launched as regular production in 2023; halfwheel reports Wildfire no longer has regular production offerings. No strength rating or tasting notes were found.

cigars.about: A limited toro made as a collaboration between Wildfire Cigar Co. and Caldwell Cigar Co., created to pair with Ammunition Whiskey. It was a PCA 2023 exclusive that reached stores in November 2023.
cigars.researchNote: A Wildfire and Caldwell collaboration, limited to 300 boxes of 10 at about 15 stores. The binder and fillers are from the Dominican Republic and Nicaragua, but which is which was not published. No strength rating or tasting notes were published.

cigars.about: The mildest of the three core Casa Cuevas blends, rolled at the Cuevas family's own factory in Santiago. It pairs an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: Maker's website calls it mild; the maker's catalog and Neptune's description say mild to medium. A 6 x 60 Gordo is in the maker's catalog but not on its website size list.

cigars.about: The red-banded core Casa Cuevas blend, made at the family's Tabacalera Las Lavas factory in Santiago. An Ecuadorian Habano wrapper sits over a Nicaraguan binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: The Prensado is box pressed. Maker's website lists Dominican and Nicaraguan filler; its catalog adds Colombian and Pennsylvania leaf and calls the cigar medium plus. A 6 x 60 Gordo is in the catalog but not on the website.

cigars.about: The black-banded core Casa Cuevas blend with a naturally fermented Mexican San Andres wrapper. It is made at the family's Tabacalera Las Lavas factory and is known for mixing sweetness with spice.
cigars.researchNote: Maker's website says medium-plus; its catalog and Neptune say medium. The catalog and halfwheel also list Pennsylvania filler, which the website leaves out. The Prensado is box pressed; a 6 x 60 Gordo is in the catalog only.

cigars.about: A family blend first made by Luis Cuevas Sr. in the early 2000s and brought back in 2019. It uses an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over a Habano binder and three-country filler.
cigars.researchNote: Maker says the blend dates to 2005 and came back in 2019. Maker calls it smooth and mellow; the medium rating is Neptune's. The maker does not say where the Habano binder is grown; Neptune calls it Dominican.

cigars.about: The maduro version of the Cuevas Reserva, an older family blend that returned in 2019. It has a Mexican San Andres wrapper over a Dominican Piloto Cubano binder and is said to be a favorite of Luis Cuevas Sr.
cigars.researchNote: Company describes it as full flavored with medium to full body. Neptune's spec says medium strength while its description says full; halfwheel's review found medium-plus. The maker's catalog lists an Olor binder instead of Piloto Cubano.

cigars.about: A 2021 line blended by Luis Cuevas Jr. and his son Alec as a tribute to Luis Cuevas Sr. and the family's tobacco lineage. It uses a Honduran Corojo wrapper and filler that includes Peruvian leaf.
cigars.researchNote: The maker and Neptune call it full bodied. Halfwheel's review found the strength closer to medium to medium-full.

cigars.about: Named for the Spanish word for sledgehammer, after burglars used sledgehammers to break into the company's Miami warehouse in 2019. It is a single 6 x 52 toro with a shaggy foot and pigtail cap, billed as the company's first full strength cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Began as a 500-box limited edition in 2019 and became regular production in 2020. Blend is from the maker's catalog and halfwheel; the maker's website instead lists a Dominican Olor binder and no Colombian filler.

cigars.about: The darker follow-up to La Mandarria, released in 2024 in the same 6 x 52 toro with an uncovered foot and pigtail cap. It swaps in a Mexican San Andres wrapper over an Ecuadorian Habano binder.
cigars.researchNote: Blend is from halfwheel, Cigar Coop and Neptune. The maker's catalog instead lists a Habano Oscuro wrapper, Honduran Corojo binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. Strength varies: halfwheel says medium, Cigar Coop medium to full, Neptune full.

cigars.about: Spanish for new blood, this 2022 line was blended by Alec Cuevas, the fifth generation of the family. It was the first Casa Cuevas cigar to use a Cameroon-seed wrapper, grown in Ecuador.
cigars.researchNote: The maker and Neptune list the Robusto at 4 3/4 x 54; halfwheel lists 4 3/4 x 52. Alec Cuevas told halfwheel the filler also has about two percent Kentucky fire-cured tobacco. Maker says medium to full; Neptune lists full.

cigars.about: A limited 7 x 43 pigtail-capped size of the Casa Cuevas Habano blend that the company calls a lancero. Flaco is Spanish for skinny, and the company says the cigars are named for Alec Cuevas.
cigars.researchNote: One limited size of the Habano line. First released in 2018 at 500 boxes of 10, then brought back in 2022 as Limited Edition Flaco Habano 2021 at 750 boxes of 10. The 2018 release was listed with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler only.

cigars.about: A limited 7 x 43 pigtail-capped size of the Casa Cuevas Maduro blend that the company calls a lancero. Flaco is Spanish for skinny, and the company says the cigars are named for Alec Cuevas.
cigars.researchNote: One limited size of the Maduro line. First released in 2018 at 500 boxes of 10, then brought back in 2022 as Limited Edition Flaco Maduro 2021 at 750 boxes of 10.

cigars.about: The first and longest-running line from Jonathan Fiant's J. London Cigars, introduced in 2014. It uses an Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed leaf for both wrapper and binder and is made at Tabacalera William Ventura.
cigars.researchNote: Maker rates it mild to medium in strength with medium to full body. The Nicaraguan filler was first disclosed in 2025; older listings say Dominican only. Made in small annual runs; sizes such as the Fat Robusto, The A, Piramide and 10th Anniversary were small batches or store exclusives.

cigars.about: A regular production line that Jonathan Fiant of J. London created with Jesus Martinez of Martinez Cigars, released in 2023. One cigar in each box of 10 robustos carries a dagger and blood drops cut from darker tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the country of origin as the United States, rolled by Martinez Cigars in New York City. The maker does not publish a strength. Halfwheel gives the wrapper and binder as Ecuadorian; the maker's page just says Corojo and Habano.

cigars.filler: Criollo 98, Habano 92, Habano 2000, HVA, Piloto Cubano (origins undisclosed)
cigars.about: A 2024 limited edition blended by Jonathan Fiant with Eladio Diaz and rolled at Diaz's factory in the Dominican Republic. It is the first cigar built around the Mr. London character, planned as a once-a-year release.
cigars.researchNote: The first release, called The Introduction, was limited to 400 boxes of 10 and aged a year after rolling. The company has not disclosed where the wrapper or filler tobaccos were grown and does not publish a strength.

cigars.about: The first release in J. London's Telephone Booth Series of small batch limited editions, shipped in December 2022. It is an unbanded robusto sold in paper-wrapped packs of five with a blue phone booth sticker.
cigars.researchNote: Made at an undisclosed factory in the Dominican Republic. Limited to 600 numbered packs of five, 3,000 cigars. The countries the tobaccos come from are not disclosed. No published strength was found.

cigars.about: The second release in J. London's Telephone Booth Series, shipped in April 2023. It is a 6 x 56 with a Mexican San Andres wrapper, sold unbanded in five-count paper-wrapped packs.
cigars.researchNote: Made at an undisclosed factory in the Dominican Republic. Limited to 600 packs of five, 3,000 cigars. Halfwheel also refers to it as the Green Telephone Booth. No published strength was found.

cigars.about: The third release in J. London's Telephone Booth Series, shipped in July 2023. It is a short 4 1/2 x 54 robusto with a pigtail cap and a habano maduro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Made at an undisclosed factory in the Dominican Republic. Limited to 800 packs of five, 4,000 cigars. In 2025 the blend returned as a 6 3/4 x 42 store exclusive for LA Aficionados Cigar Collective, 190 packs of 10. No published strength was found.

cigars.about: A September 2023 release in J. London's Telephone Booth Series, a 5 1/2 x 46 corona gorda with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. It was the first cigar in the series to wear a band.
cigars.researchNote: Made at an undisclosed factory in the Dominican Republic. Limited to 800 packs of five, 4,000 cigars. The tobacco is said to be aged four to six years. No published strength was found.

cigars.about: A November 2023 release in J. London's Telephone Booth Series, a 5 x 50 robusto. Its Dominican broadleaf maduro wrapper was grown on virgin soil, according to owner Jonathan Fiant.
cigars.researchNote: Made at an undisclosed factory in the Dominican Republic. Limited to 800 packs of five, 4,000 cigars. It was previewed at PCA 2023 as the Purple Telephone Booth. No published strength was found.

cigars.about: A May 2024 release in J. London's Telephone Booth Series, a 5 1/2 x 46 that the company calls a lonsdale. It uses a Mexican San Andres wrapper over olor and criollo 98 tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: Made at an undisclosed factory in the Dominican Republic. Limited to 800 packs of five, 4,000 cigars. No published strength was found.

cigars.filler: Criollo 98 Medio Tiempo (origin undisclosed), Dominican Republic (Olor San Victor Medio Tiempo), USA (Pennsylvania)
cigars.about: An August 2024 release in J. London's Telephone Booth Series, a 5 1/2 x 52 robusto. It uses a Mexican San Andres wrapper with medio tiempo leaves and Pennsylvania tobacco in the filler.
cigars.researchNote: Made at an undisclosed factory in the Dominican Republic. Limited to 800 packs of five, 4,000 cigars. Not the same cigar as the J. London Gold Series. No published strength was found.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (San Victor Olor), Criollo 98 Viso and Medio Tiempo (origin undisclosed)
cigars.about: A December 2024 release in J. London's Telephone Booth Series, a 5 1/2 x 50 robusto. It is unusual for using a Dominican olor leaf as the wrapper, over a Mexican San Andres binder.
cigars.researchNote: Made at an undisclosed factory in the Dominican Republic. Limited to 800 packs of five, 4,000 cigars. Not the same cigar as the 2023 Orange Telephone Booth. No published strength was found.

cigars.about: The original Valacari blend, a Nicaraguan puro with a Habano wrapper from the small company Nimmer Ahmad founded in 2016. It is the medium-bodied core of the Neoclassic family.
cigars.researchNote: Valacari moved all production from Tabacalera Pages de Nicaragua to La Tabacaria Cigars in Esteli in fall 2025. Since 2026 every core line comes only as a 5 x 54 robusto and a 6 x 52 toro, in boxes of 20.

cigars.about: Valacari's Connecticut shade cigar, with an Ecuadorian wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It was sold as The Messenger until the 2026 rebrand put it alongside the Neoclassic Habano.
cigars.researchNote: This is The Messenger renamed in 2026; The Messenger first came out in October 2019. Older Messenger specs listed fillers from Jalapa, Condega and Ometepe.

cigars.about: Valacari's maduro core line, a medium to full blend of Nicaraguan binder and filler under a dark wrapper. It is aimed at smokers who want something bolder than the Neoclassic.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the wrapper. Valacari's site lists Mexican San Andres maduro, but halfwheel and Cigar Coop reported in April 2026 that Nobility was reblended with an Ecuadorian maduro wrapper. Check the box.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro with a Habano 2000 wrapper, introduced by Valacari at the 2025 PCA show after about four years of development.
cigars.researchNote: Valacari calls it medium plus. It launched in 2025 as a 5 x 50 robusto, 6 x 52 toro and 6 x 60 gordo; the 2026 lineup is a 5 x 54 robusto and a 6 x 52 toro.

cigars.about: Valacari's broadleaf cigar, with an American-grown Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper over an Ometepe binder and Nicaraguan filler. It joined the core line in late November 2024 and is the fullest of the regular blends.
cigars.researchNote: Sizes above are from Valacari's page. halfwheel reported that from 2026 Astronomia is sold only as a 5 x 54 robusto and a 6 x 52 toro, so the 5 x 50 and corona gorda may be older stock.

cigars.about: Valacari's tenth anniversary cigar, named with the Latin word for tenth. It pairs a Mexican San Andres maduro wrapper with all Nicaraguan binder and filler, and Valacari calls it its boldest blend.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 500 boxes of 20 (10,000 cigars) a year. Sold as a single 6 x 52 toro, though Cigar Coop's announcement also listed a 5 x 54 robusto. Strength and flavors are from halfwheel's review.

cigars.about: A limited edition in Valacari's numbered MK series. Valacari lists it among its limited editions but has not published the blend.
cigars.researchNote: Confirmed by name only. Valacari has not published the wrapper, blend, size or year.

cigars.about: A limited edition in Valacari's numbered MK series. Valacari lists it among its limited editions but has not published the blend.
cigars.researchNote: Confirmed by name only. Valacari has not published the wrapper, blend, size or year.

cigars.about: A limited edition in Valacari's numbered MK series. Valacari lists it among its limited editions but has not published the blend.
cigars.researchNote: Confirmed by name only. Valacari has not published the wrapper, blend, size or year.

cigars.about: A dated limited edition offshoot of Valacari's Neoclassic line. Valacari's site shows 2023 and 2025 editions in its archive and a 2026 edition as coming soon.
cigars.researchNote: Valacari lists editions dated 2023 and 2025, with 2026 coming soon. It has not published the wrapper, blend or size.

cigars.about: A 2026 collaboration between Valacari and Lure Cigars, released for the Year of the Horse with a seahorse theme. It is a box-pressed Nicaraguan puro with five-year-old fillers, limited to 2,500 cigars.
cigars.researchNote: A joint Lure and Valacari release, so it may be shelved under either brand. 250 bundles of 10. No official strength: halfwheel's review found two of three cigars mild in nicotine with medium to medium plus body, and the third noticeably stronger.

cigars.about: The first Connecticut shade line from Crux, a Minnesota-founded brand, made for it by Plasencia in Esteli. It reached stores in late 2017 and is the red-banded original of the three Epicure blends.
cigars.researchNote: Some retailers list it as Epicure Shade. halfwheel's review found mild to medium strength with fuller body; Neptune's spec table says medium. The Short Salomone finished 15th in halfwheel's 2019 Consensus.

cigars.about: The third Epicure blend from Crux, a Nicaraguan puro that keeps the Epicure binder and filler and adds a Nicaraguan habano seco wrapper. It shipped in June 2023 and the Toro made halfwheel's Top 25 of 2024 at number 17.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The maduro version of Crux Epicure and the brand's first San Andres cigar, with a Mexican maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It was previewed in 2018 as Epicure Galant and shipped under the Maduro name in May 2019.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel and Cigar Coop say it is made at AJ Fernandez, the one Crux line not from Plasencia at the time; Neptune's spec table lists Plasencia. It was first announced as Epicure Galant, renamed over a trademark concern.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro with a Jalapa habano wrapper and one of the first lines Crux launched in 2014. It leans toward larger ring gauges and was repackaged in 2019.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune describes the wrapper as a Habano maduro. Robusto Extra and Gordo dimensions are from the 2014 launch specs; the Toro was added in 2019 and the Double Corona in 2021. The Gordo has Crux's Marblehead cap, a 109-style head.

cigars.about: A Crux line with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, made at Plasencia in Esteli. It was shown in 2015 and began shipping in May 2016.
cigars.researchNote: Strength reads differently by reviewer: Blind Man's Puff called it medium-strong and Cigar Coop a stronger cigar, while halfwheel found it medium. A 5 1/4 x 54 Robusto Extra was in the original lineup but is not on Crux's current list.

cigars.about: Crux's small ring gauge line, a nod to the Cuban Partagas Serie du Connaisseur, with a Jalapa habano wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and Honduran filler. It first shipped in January 2016 and came back in new packaging in 2021 after a hiatus.
cigars.researchNote: Announced at the 2015 trade show, so some sources date it 2015. Off the market from late 2019 until June 2021; the blend did not change. Strength and body are from Blind Man's Puff's review.

cigars.about: One of the first Crux blends from 2014, dropped before the 2019 rebrand and brought back in January 2026 with a new blend. The current version uses an Ecuadorian habano wrapper over Nicaraguan and Honduran tobaccos in three sizes of 48 ring gauge or less.
cigars.researchNote: Specs are for the 2026 reblend. The 2014 original had a Jalapa wrapper and binder with Esteli and Jamastran fillers. Reviewers vary on strength: Cigar Coop found medium rising to medium-full, Developing Palates ranged from medium to full.

cigars.about: Crux's once-a-year limited line, built around a Nicaraguan Enganoso wrapper the company says is grown only for it, over a Connecticut broadleaf binder. It started with the box-pressed PB5 and has grown to several sizes that share the blend.
cigars.researchNote: Crux says about 1,000 boxes are made a year. The PB5 was announced in 2015 and first shipped in 2016, so sources give either year. Neptune calls it full-bodied; Cigar Coop found medium strength with medium to full body.

cigars.about: Crux's value-priced line, named for the company's Marblehead cap, a 109-style head between a belicoso and a rounded cap. It was shown at PCA 2025, shipped in January 2026, and is the first Crux cigar made at Tabacalera Pages.
cigars.researchNote: Crux calls it medium-full bodied, but Cigar Coop and Developing Palates both found it medium. Crux lists the binder and filler together as Nicaraguan and Indonesian; halfwheel gives an Indonesian binder and Nicaraguan filler. Also sold as Marblehead Habano.

cigars.about: The maduro follow-up to Crux's value-priced Marblehead line, with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It was announced at PCA 2026 and began shipping in June 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Both sizes have the Marblehead cap, Crux's 109-style head. halfwheel's review found full flavor with body and strength building from just under medium to medium plus.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, Nicaragua, Honduras, Costa Rica
cigars.about: A group of ten El Septimo cigars, most of them short and thick, each with a color in its name. El Septimo is a high-priced brand made in Costa Rica, founded in 2005 and owned by Zaya Younan since 2019.
cigars.researchNote: This is a collection of ten different cigars, not one blend. The maker keeps the wrapper undisclosed. Strength varies by cigar: the maker rates Excepcion White 2 of 5, Rebelde Blue and Bullet Blue 4 of 5, and Small Sabor Blue 5 of 5.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, Nicaragua, Honduras, Costa Rica
cigars.about: El Septimo's highest-priced regular range, mostly large ring gauge cigars with five filler leaves each. It shares its name with owner Zaya Younan and is made in Costa Rica.
cigars.researchNote: A collection of eight different cigars; the maker keeps the wrapper undisclosed. Several are described as full-bodied, and Bullet Black is rated 4 of 5 in strength. The limited Doble Gran Reserva and Mi Familia are also sold under this collection.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut or maduro depending on the cigar (origin undisclosed)
cigars.about: A series of El Septimo cigars named for historical rulers, launched in 2022 as the company's first use of Connecticut wrapper alongside maduro versions. It includes some of the brand's lower-priced cigars and is made in Costa Rica.
cigars.researchNote: A collection of separate cigars in Connecticut and maduro wrappers of undisclosed origin. The maker rates the core cigars 2 of 5 in strength and calls Empress Sheba (added 2023) medium to full-bodied. King Sargon sizes began as humidor-only cigars and Vartan the Dragon is a limited edition.

cigars.about: Seven El Septimo cigars, each named for a famous painter and tied to one of the seven days of creation. Released in 2021 and made in Costa Rica, each size is presented as its own blend.
cigars.researchNote: The maker keeps the wrapper undisclosed, and at launch said each of the seven sizes is a different blend. It rates them 3 of 5 in strength, or medium. The Van Gogh is 9 x 55 per the maker and 9 x 56 per halfwheel.

cigars.about: A two-cigar El Septimo line introduced in 2019 and marketed toward women who smoke cigars. It was announced a few months after Zaya Younan bought the brand and is made in Costa Rica.
cigars.researchNote: The maker keeps the wrapper undisclosed. It rates Coco 2 of 5 in strength and Marilyn 3 of 5 (medium-bodied). At the 2019 launch halfwheel reported the line was made entirely of Costa Rican tobacco, which differs from the binder and filler the maker lists now.

cigars.about: El Septimo's line of toro-sized cigars named from the Epic of Gilgamesh, launched in 2020 as the brand's first 50 ring gauge cigars at a lower price. King Sargon was added in 2021.
cigars.researchNote: Three different blends: the maker rates Aqua Anu 2 of 5 in strength, Sable Shamash 3 of 5 and King Sargon 4 of 5. The maker keeps the wrapper undisclosed. In 2020 halfwheel listed Aqua Anu and Sable Shamash as Costa Rican puros, which differs from what the maker lists now.

cigars.about: One of El Septimo's lowest-priced lines, released in 2024 in four sizes named for wine regions and a style of sake. It uses an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper and tobaccos aged at least five years, and is made in Costa Rica.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the binder as Ecuadorian Habano 2004; halfwheel reported Habano 2000. halfwheel calls it one blend in four sizes. The maker says some of the Bordeaux size's filler is aged in wine barrels, and it describes the Rioja as full-bodied.

cigars.line: Queen Sheba Conquest Edition Series II
cigars.about: A 2026 follow-up to El Septimo's Empress of Sheba from the Emperor Collection, with a new blend in a slimmer 6 x 54 toro. It is a regular production cigar.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is undisclosed; the maker's description speaks of maduro. The maker's site sells this cigar as Empress Sheba Toro within the Emperor Collection. The original Empress Sheba is a 6 x 60 gordo from 2023.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, Nicaragua, Honduras, Costa Rica
cigars.about: A single-size limited edition marking El Septimo's 20th anniversary in 2025, priced at $125 a cigar. The maker says the tobaccos are aged seven to ten years and that more than 60 people took part in the blending.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,000 boxes of 14, sold through the top 50 accounts. The maker's site lists the wrapper as undisclosed and Costa Rica in the filler; halfwheel reports an Ecuadorian wrapper and Ecuador in the filler instead of Costa Rica. Strength and body are from halfwheel's review; the maker gives none.

cigars.about: A 2026 limited edition set from El Septimo owner Zaya Younan, with sizes named for his wife and children. Each of the five sizes comes in both a Connecticut-seed and a maduro wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only as a complete 20-cigar set, two of each size and wrapper, priced at $2,000 and limited to 1,000 boxes. The origin of both wrappers is undisclosed. The maker lists it under the Zaya Collection.

cigars.about: One of Dissident's two original core lines, first shipped in 2013 and relaunched in 2019 with a new blend made at Fabrica Oveja Negra in Esteli. Dissident is a small punk-themed brand now owned by Cynn and Joshua Coburn.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper has changed: the 2019 relaunch used a Brazilian wrapper, and in 2022 it switched to Sumatra because of tobacco availability. Some retailers still describe the Brazilian wrapper. Full strength is Neptune's rating; the 2013 original was a Nicaraguan puro.

cigars.about: A box-pressed maduro and one of Dissident's two core lines, reworked in 2019 at Fabrica Oveja Negra with a punk rock theme in place of the older video game branding.
cigars.researchNote: First shown in 2013 with a video game theme and a different blend; the current blend dates from 2019. Famous Smoke's brand overview calls it medium to full with a San Andres wrapper, but its line page, Neptune and halfwheel list Ecuadorian maduro, and both retailers rate it full.

cigars.about: A single-size petite corona with a Pennsylvania broadleaf wrapper, released by Dissident in 2020 alongside Rave and Tirade and made at Fabrica Oveja Negra.
cigars.researchNote: Comes in one size only. It started as a small batch release and moved into the core line when the brand changed owners at the end of 2021.

cigars.about: Dissident's Connecticut-wrapped cigar, released in 2020 as a box-pressed robusto and joined in 2023 by a smaller round robusto. It is made at Fabrica Oveja Negra in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Stronger than a typical Connecticut: halfwheel's review found medium-plus strength with full flavor and body. Neptune lists it as full strength. Both sizes use the same blend.

cigars.about: A single-size corona gorda with a Mexican San Andres wrapper, released by Dissident in 2020 alongside Rant and Rave and made at Fabrica Oveja Negra.
cigars.researchNote: Comes in one size only. Famous Smoke's brand overview describes an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, but its line page and halfwheel both list Mexican San Andres. It moved from small batch to the core line at the end of 2021.

cigars.about: Dissident's recurring limited edition, a barber pole cigar with two Ecuadorian wrappers made at Fabrica Oveja Negra. It first appeared in 2015 and has returned in 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2023.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrappers, so no single wrapper type applies. The 2015 original was a 6 x 54 Honduran puro, and the blend was changed completely in 2019. The 2019 release was 6 x 54; 2021 and 2023 were 6 x 52 box-pressed, with production numbers undisclosed.

cigars.about: A limited edition robusto that was the first new Dissident cigar after Cynn and Joshua Coburn bought the brand. It debuted in 2022 and came back for a second batch in 2024.
cigars.researchNote: Rojiso is a reddish wrapper shade, filed here under Rosado as the closest type. The 2022 release was limited to 500 boxes of 20; the 2024 quantity was not disclosed. The company calls the profile mild to medium.

cigars.about: A 2023 limited edition robusto from Dissident, described as a toned-down round version of the HOME blend with the same two Ecuadorian wrappers. It is made at Fabrica Oveja Negra.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrappers, so no single wrapper type applies. The company calls the profile "medium bold"; halfwheel's review found medium-plus strength, medium-full body and full flavor. Production numbers are not disclosed.

cigars.about: A 2024 limited edition from Dissident with two Ecuadorian wrappers, sold as a regular item only by retailers in the Midwest and at events elsewhere. Owner Cynn Coburn made it as a nod to her Midwestern roots.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrappers, so no single wrapper type applies. Regular retail sales were limited to stores in ten Midwestern states, with event-only availability elsewhere. Production numbers are not disclosed.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Sumatra-seed and Connecticut-seed (barber pole, origin undisclosed)
cigars.about: A 2024 limited edition barber pole robusto from Dissident, made as a tribute to punk singer Wendy O. Williams of the Plasmatics. It is produced at Fabrica Oveja Negra in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrappers of undisclosed origin, so no single wrapper type applies. Strength and body are from halfwheel's review, which found it mild at the start and just under medium later. Production numbers are not disclosed.

cigars.factory: Aganorsa Leaf (Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A.)
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro with a shade-grown Connecticut-seed wrapper, made for Black Star Line by Aganorsa Leaf. It is milder than the Dark War Witch that followed and is named after a 2012 film.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the Lancero at 7.5 x 40, while halfwheel and Blind Man's Puff list it at 7 x 38. Strength and body are from the Blind Man's Puff review, as the maker does not state them.

cigars.about: A stronger follow-up to War Witch that swaps the Connecticut shade wrapper for Corojo 99. It is a Nicaraguan puro made by Aganorsa Leaf.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it full strength and full body, but a Blind Man's Puff panel rated it medium. The 4.75 x 60 Perfecto was a 2024 run of 200 boxes of 10.

cigars.about: The Corojo-wrapped version of El Milagro, Black Star Line's first brand name. It is rolled by Aganorsa Leaf in Nicaragua with a double binder and triple cap.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it full-bodied with robust strength and does not say where the wrapper is grown. El Milagro launched in 2019 at El Titan de Bronze in Miami with Habano and San Andres wrappers; the year the Aganorsa-made Corojo joined is not published.

cigars.about: The Habano-wrapped version of El Milagro, the name Black Star Line launched with in 2019. The current cigar is rolled by Aganorsa Leaf in Nicaragua with a double binder and triple cap.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not state a strength or where the wrapper is grown. The 2019 original was a different cigar: a 6 x 54 toro made at El Titan de Bronze in Miami with a Nicaraguan wrapper, Ecuadorian binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler, which Stogie Press found medium.

cigars.about: A San Andres-wrapped cigar over Nicaraguan tobaccos made by Aganorsa Leaf, billed as full strength and full body. It is named for the Ethiopian town known for its rock-cut churches.
cigars.researchNote: The Toro and Gordo are the core sizes. The Robusto and Lancero arrived in 2024 in small runs of 2,000 and 3,000 cigars.

cigars.about: A shaggy-foot Connecticut Broadleaf cigar made at Tabacalera La Isla in the Dominican Republic. Owner Aric Bey is a retired Chicago firefighter, and part of the proceeds go to the firefighter charity Ignite the Spirit.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls the 6 x 46 a Corona. A 5 x 50 Robusto came first in 2023 as a 1,000-cigar event release. The name is from the Queen song Don't Stop Me Now.

cigars.about: A San Andres-wrapped cigar made at Fabrica Oveja Negra, the Nicaraguan factory behind Black Label Trading Company. It honors the victims of the 1923 Rosewood massacre in Florida and filmmaker John Singleton.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not state a strength. halfwheel found it medium to medium-plus, with a noticeable nicotine kick late in two of three cigars.

cigars.about: Black Star Line's fifth anniversary cigar, named for the Yoruba word for five. It was the brand's first cigar made at Espinosa's La Zona factory in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Strength and body are from the halfwheel review, as the maker does not state them. A 6.5 x 48 box-pressed Corona Extra was a 70-bundle exclusive for Oak Glen Tobacconist in California.

cigars.filler: United States, Brazil, Dominican Republic, Peru
cigars.about: A Dominican-made robusto that marks the time Martin Luther King Jr. spent working on a tobacco farm before college. The black and old gold band uses the colors of his fraternity, Alpha Phi Alpha.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 250 boxes of 20. Cigar Coop and Stogie Press also list Nicaraguan tobacco in the filler, which halfwheel leaves out. The company calls it medium-bodied; reviewers found the strength medium to medium-plus.

cigars.about: A San Andres-wrapped corona gorda made at La Zona in Esteli. It is named for Eugene Bullard, an American who flew for France in World War I and is recognized as the first Black combat fighter pilot.
cigars.researchNote: The first run was 200 bundles of 10 cigars, shipping from May 2026. No strength or tasting notes have been published yet.

cigars.about: The first line from Meerapfel Cigar, the family famous for growing Cameroon wrapper. It is named for the late Richard Meerapfel and comes in a chest with a tray that doubles as an ashtray.
cigars.researchNote: Binder, filler, factory and country are not disclosed. Each size is capped at 613 boxes a year, and only the Double Robusto is confirmed as released out of seven planned sizes. Strength and body are from the halfwheel review.

cigars.about: The second Meerapfel Cigar line, named for Meir Meerapfel, who set up the family's cigar factory in Untergrombach, Germany in 1876. It wears the family's own Cameroon wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Binder, filler, factory and country are not disclosed. The company says a vintage Cameroon wrapper dresses all its Master Blends, though halfwheel's review lists the wrapper as undisclosed. Each size is capped at 613 boxes a year; it reached U.S. stores in February 2023.

cigars.about: The third Meerapfel Cigar line, named for Ernest Meerapfel, who left Germany in the late 1800s to source tobacco abroad. It uses the family's Cameroon wrapper, and the Double Robusto comes in a casket with an ornate ashtray.
cigars.researchNote: Binder, filler, factory and country are not disclosed. Each size is capped at 613 boxes a year. halfwheel found medium strength with full body, while Cigar Coop found mild to medium strength with medium body.

cigars.about: A yearly limited Meerapfel toro sold in two-cigar wooden coffins with a numbered lithograph. Proceeds go to cigar rights groups: several organizations including Cigar Rights of America in 2024, and the Premium Cigar Association in 2025.
cigars.researchNote: Each year's release is 613 two-count coffins, or 1,226 cigars. Binder, filler, factory and country are not disclosed. Strength and body are from halfwheel's review of the 2024 release.

cigars.about: A 2026 Meerapfel limited edition in one 6 x 50 size, sold in paulownia wood chests of 99 cigars. The plan is one blend a year, made once.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 180 chests of 99 cigars, due to ship in the fourth quarter of 2026. Binder, filler, factory and country are not disclosed. The flavor word is the company's own description, as no reviews exist yet.

cigars.about: The Meerapfel family's personal blend, an extension of their 2014 La Estancia brand and now part of the Family Reserve Blends. It reached U.S. stores in April 2026.
cigars.researchNote: The blend, factory and country are not disclosed. The original 2014 La Estancia was made in Honduras and included Cuban filler, but the family has not said the same of this one. Strength is from halfwheel's 2019 review, which found it mild at first and past medium by the end.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Connecticut-wrapped line in the Meerapfel Family Reserve Blends, sold in boxes of 25. It is one of the family's more affordable cigars and came to U.S. stores in April 2026.
cigars.researchNote: The binder, factory and country are not disclosed. Size III is 6 x 50 on the maker's page but 6 x 60 in halfwheel's list. No strength is published.

cigars.about: The lowest-priced line in the Meerapfel Family Reserve Blends, made in Nicaragua and sold unbanded in bundles of 10. It came to U.S. stores in April 2026.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper, binder, filler and factory are not disclosed, and no strength is published. halfwheel calls the 3.75 x 52 a Short Torpedo.

cigars.about: A banded, boxed sibling of Machetero in the Meerapfel Family Reserve Blends. It is a separate blend with a darker oscuro wrapper, sold in boxes of 10.
