cigars.researchNote: The binder, filler and factory are not disclosed, and no strength is published. The plain Machetero is made in Nicaragua, but no source says so for the Exclusiva. Its Double Corona is 7 x 52, half an inch shorter than Machetero's.

cigars.about: A line in the Meerapfel Family Reserve Blends, formerly The Selection, which the maker describes as bold and structured. It comes in sets of 10 with sizes named after Spanish noble titles.
cigars.researchNote: The blend, factory and country are not disclosed, and no strength is published. It is the one Family Reserve line not offered in the U.S.

cigars.factory: Las Villas Cigars (formerly Tabacalera La Perla)
cigars.about: One of six blends in Stallone's Cowboy Series, each named for a horse coat color. This one pairs a reddish Brazilian Corojo wrapper with an Ecuadorian binder and Nicaraguan filler, and all three sizes are box-pressed.
cigars.researchNote: Part of the Cowboy Series. 2020 is the U.S. launch; the brand was founded in 2014 and sold abroad first.

cigars.factory: Las Villas Cigars (formerly Tabacalera La Perla)
cigars.about: A Cowboy Series blend from Tony Barrios's Stallone Cigars with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over a Brazilian binder and Nicaraguan filler. Both sizes are box-pressed.
cigars.researchNote: Part of the Cowboy Series. The maker rates it Medium plus. 2020 is the U.S. launch; the brand sold abroad before that.

cigars.factory: Las Villas Cigars (formerly Tabacalera La Perla)
cigars.about: A Cowboy Series blend with a dark Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It comes in three box-pressed sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Part of the Cowboy Series. The maker calls it medium-full; Cigar Coop's review found medium strength with medium-full body. 2020 is the U.S. launch.

cigars.factory: Las Villas Cigars (formerly Tabacalera La Perla)
cigars.about: The Nicaraguan puro of Stallone's Cowboy Series, wrapped in a near-black maduro leaf. It comes in three box-pressed sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Part of the Cowboy Series. Cigar Coop reported in 2022 that it was renamed Azabache Maduro, though the maker's site still shows Negro Maduro. 2020 is the U.S. launch.

cigars.factory: Las Villas Cigars (formerly Tabacalera La Perla)
cigars.about: The lightest-wrapped blend in Stallone's Cowboy Series, using a U.S.-grown Connecticut Shade wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is sold in two round sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Part of the Cowboy Series. The maker rates it Medium plus, stronger than most Connecticut Shade cigars. 2020 is the U.S. launch.

cigars.factory: Las Villas Cigars (formerly Tabacalera La Perla)
cigars.about: A Cowboy Series blend with a dark U.S.-grown Broadleaf wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is sold in two round sizes and is the only Cowboy Series blend the maker rates full strength.
cigars.researchNote: Part of the Cowboy Series. The maker calls it full; Cigar Coop and Developing Palates both found it closer to medium in strength. 2020 is the U.S. launch.

cigars.about: A short, thick, budget-priced cigar from Stallone that launched at the 2021 Tobacco Plus Expo. It uses an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper with Connecticut Broadleaf in the filler and comes in one size.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel and Cigar Coop list the size as 4 x 58; the maker's spec graphic reads 4.5 x 50. The maker calls it medium, but halfwheel's review found it medium-full to full.

cigars.about: A big 6 1/2 x 60 Nicaraguan puro from Stallone with a Broadleaf-seed wrapper grown in Nicaragua. The unfinished shaggy foot is a nod to the feathered feet of a Clydesdale horse.
cigars.researchNote: Released as a limited edition in November 2021. Cigar Aficionado reported 1,000 boxes of 20 with more possible later, while Cigar Coop cited 2,000 boxes. The maker's site still lists it alongside its regular lines.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Sumatra (Oscuro on the Rothschild, Natural on the Short Toro)
cigars.about: Stallone's value-priced line, introduced at the 2023 PCA show and sold in bundles of 25. Each of the two sizes gets its own shade of Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over a double binder and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: The two sizes use different wrappers: the Rothschild has the darker Oscuro leaf, which the blender says adds cocoa and light pepper.

cigars.about: A 2022 limited edition named after the first horse Tony Barrios knew, which belonged to his grandfather. The filler tobaccos were aged in barrels that once held Flor de Caña rum.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 250 boxes of 20 (5,000 cigars). The wrapper is a habano-Sumatra hybrid seed developed by Tony Barrios. No strength, country or factory was published for this release; Stallone's other cigars are made at Las Villas Cigars in Nicaragua.

cigars.about: The original Patoro line, launched in 2001 by the Swiss company and made at De Los Reyes in the Dominican Republic. It uses aged Dominican binder and filler under an Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The 2015 U.S. edition was announced with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper and Neptune still lists habano; the maker and recent halfwheel coverage say Ecuadorian Connecticut. The maker rates strength 3 of 5 but elsewhere calls the line mild.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano, Corojo, San Vicente)
cigars.about: Patoro's black-banded Dominican puro, first released in 2003 and built mostly on piloto cubano tobacco aged five to eight years. It reached the U.S. in 2018.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it 5 of 5 for strength, its strongest line, but halfwheel's review of the Perfecto found it only a little past medium. The 2018 U.S. debut was a small allotment for top accounts.

cigars.about: The first Patoro line sold in the U.S., arriving in 2014 with a blend adjusted for the American market. The U.S. version wears a Brazilian wrapper over Dominican binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Two versions share this name: the U.S. Serie P has a Brazilian wrapper, while the European one on the maker's site has a Cameroon wrapper and is sold in the U.S. as Serie P Cameroon. 2014 is the U.S. launch, and the strength is Neptune's listing.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano, Corojo, San Vicente)
cigars.about: The original European version of Patoro's Serie P, with a Cameroon wrapper over Dominican tobaccos aged three to four years. It came to the U.S. in two sizes in 2022 alongside the Brazilian-wrapped American Serie P.
cigars.researchNote: In Europe this blend is simply called Serie P; 2022 is its U.S. release. Strength is from the maker's own rating of 2 out of 5, as no retailer rating was found.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Brazilian Cubra (Cuban-seed hybrid grown in Bahia)
cigars.about: A Patoro line named for its Cubra wrapper, a Cuban and Brazilian seed hybrid grown in Bahia, over Dominican binder and filler. It was introduced in Europe in 2014 and came to the U.S. unchanged in 2016.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's text calls it medium to strong, but its strength graphic shows 3 of 5 and Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.about: Patoro's 20th anniversary cigar, named for the pale, calcium-rich soil of the Cibao Valley where its binder and filler are grown by Leo Reyes. Those tobaccos are aged four to eight years and finished with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The mildest Patoro line. It launched in November 2021 as an exclusive for one Texas shop and went national in July 2022, when the Robusto was added.

cigars.about: A Dominican puro from Patoro built around a wrapper leaf aged for ten years, using the same filler as the Gran Añejo Reserva. It was sold in Switzerland first and reached the U.S. in 2017.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's text calls it medium strength, though its strength graphic shows 4 of 5. The Perfecto's ring gauge is listed as 48 by halfwheel and about 53 to 54 by the maker and Cigar Coop. The original release year is not published; it reached the U.S. in 2017.

cigars.about: A Dominican puro from Patoro whose tobaccos are aged nine to twelve years before rolling. VA stands for Very Aged, and the line began with a robusto in Switzerland in 2010.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in the U.S. as VA XO and made each year in small amounts. halfwheel and Neptune call it medium in strength while the maker's graphic shows 4 of 5. The Extra Robusto is listed with a 55 or 58 ring depending on the source.

cigars.about: Patoro's 25th anniversary cigar from 2026, a Dominican puro of aged tobaccos made in a single salomon shape at De Los Reyes. Patoro's Pablo Richard told halfwheel the blend is close to the VA XO line.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 600 boxes of 20 (12,000 cigars), with 300 boxes for the U.S. in June 2026 and 300 for Europe that September. U.S. price was $35 a cigar.

cigars.about: David Blanco's personal blend in the Blanco family's Liga Exclusiva de Familia pair, rolled by Plasencia in Nicaragua. It puts a Pennsylvania Broadleaf maduro wrapper over all-Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: The Maduro is David Blanco's personal blend; the Connecticut is Cesar Blanco's.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: U.S. Connecticut Shade seed grown in the Talanga Valley, Honduras
cigars.about: Cesar Blanco's personal blend in the Blanco family's Liga Exclusiva de Familia pair, rolled by Plasencia in Nicaragua. It uses a Honduran-grown Connecticut Shade wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers disagree on strength: Cigar Place rates it Mild-Medium, Neptune rates it Medium. The 6 1/2 x 54 Torpedo was in the 2012 launch lineup but Cigar Place no longer lists it.

cigars.about: Blanco's full-strength Nicaraguan puro, made by Plasencia in Esteli with a Corojo Oscuro wrapper and three ligero leaves in the filler. Retailers say the name comes from the nine tries it took to settle the blend.
cigars.researchNote: Launch year is not published; it was already on sale before 2012. The Minuto was announced in 2016 as 4 1/2 x 38 but is sold as 4 x 38, in five-packs.

cigars.about: A Blanco line honoring Prince Hall, the abolitionist regarded as the founder of Black Freemasonry, made at Plasencia in Esteli. The Maduro uses a Nicaraguan habano maduro wrapper over a Sumatran binder and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Prince Hall by Blanco; the launch release called it Habano Maduro. The 7 x 70 is Boaz in Maduro and Jachin in Rosado. Halfwheel names the factory as Plasencia, while Cigar Coop lists La Catedral de Tabaco. Strength is not published.

cigars.about: A Blanco line honoring Prince Hall, the abolitionist regarded as the founder of Black Freemasonry, made in Esteli, Nicaragua. The Rosado is a Nicaraguan puro with a habano rosado wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Prince Hall by Blanco; the launch release called it Habano Rosado. The 7 x 70 is Jachin in Rosado and Boaz in Maduro. Halfwheel names the factory as Plasencia, while Cigar Coop lists La Catedral de Tabaco. Strength is not published.

cigars.about: The fourth blend in Blanco's collaboration with Bryan Glynn of the Cigar Obsession YouTube channel, named for Glynn himself. All four sizes are box-pressed with pigtail caps and made at Plasencia in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: The Toro is a barber pole that adds a Honduran-grown Connecticut Shade wrapper alongside the San Andres. The Figurado tapers from 60 to 54 ring. Strength is not published.

cigars.about: The first blend from Blanco's collaboration with Bryan Glynn of the Cigar Obsession YouTube channel, made by Plasencia in Nicaragua. It is box-pressed with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel lists all-Nicaraguan binder and filler; Neptune lists the filler as Nicaragua and Honduras. Strength is Neptune's rating.

cigars.about: The second blend from Blanco's collaboration with Bryan Glynn of the Cigar Obsession YouTube channel, made by Plasencia in Nicaragua. It was Blanco's first cigar with a Cameroon wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the blend: halfwheel lists Nicaraguan binder and filler, while Neptune lists a Mexican San Andres binder with Brazilian and Nicaraguan filler. Neptune rates strength Medium and calls it full-bodied.

cigars.about: The third blend from Blanco's collaboration with Bryan Glynn of the Cigar Obsession YouTube channel, made by Plasencia in Nicaragua. It is a Nicaraguan puro with a habano wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel calls the wrapper habano only; Neptune says Nicaraguan habano. Halfwheel lists the Robusto as 5 x 52, Neptune as 5 x 54. Strength is Neptune's rating.

cigars.about: The dark, full-strength cigar that founder Desiree Sylver first commissioned and that launched Drunk Chicken Cigars in 2019. It is rolled in the United States with a Mexican San Andres wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Usually called DCO. Made at an undisclosed factory in Florida. The maker lists the Toro as both 6 x 52 and 6 x 54.

cigars.about: One of the five blends Drunk Chicken Cigars launched with in 2019, a medium-strength habano rolled in the United States. It has also been offered as a box-pressed robusto.
cigars.researchNote: Made at an undisclosed factory in Florida. The maker hints at one more undisclosed tobacco in the blend and calls it both medium-bodied and medium to full. Its site lists the Toro as both 6 x 52 and 5.5 x 52.

cigars.about: A stronger San Andres maduro version of Drunk Chicken's Mother Clucker, introduced at the 2026 PCA show. Unlike the original, it is rolled in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel reports a limited edition of 300 boxes of 20, made at an undisclosed Nicaraguan factory. Size is unsettled: halfwheel reported 5 1/2 x 50, while the maker's site lists a Toro as both 6 x 52 and 6 x 54.

cigars.about: One of the five blends Drunk Chicken Cigars launched with in 2019, a thick-ring habano rolled in the United States. It began as a Gordo and a short 4 x 60 torpedo.
cigars.researchNote: Made at an undisclosed factory in Florida. The maker lists the Toro as both 6 x 52 and 5 x 54. A 5 1/2 x 50 Robusto exists only in the FreshPak sampler.

cigars.about: One of the five blends Drunk Chicken Cigars launched with in 2019, a medium habano with Dominican filler. It is rolled in the United States.
cigars.researchNote: Made at an undisclosed factory in Florida. The maker lists the Toro as both 6 x 52 and 6 x 54.

cigars.about: A milder, creamier Connecticut-wrapped version of Drunk Chicken's Living The Dream, introduced at the 2026 PCA show. Unlike the original, it is rolled in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel reports a limited edition of 300 boxes of 20, made at an undisclosed Nicaraguan factory. Size is unsettled: halfwheel reported 5 1/2 x 50, while the maker's site lists a 6 x 52 Toro.

cigars.about: The mild cigar among the five blends Drunk Chicken Cigars launched with in 2019, finished with a lightly sweetened tip. It is rolled in the United States with a Connecticut wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Also written Sweet Dreams. It has a sweetened tip. Made at an undisclosed factory in Florida. The maker lists Nicaraguan filler but its description also mentions Dominican, and its site tags the wrapper as US Connecticut.

cigars.about: Drunk Chicken's strongest blend, a Pennsylvania Broadleaf cigar released once a year in limited numbers since 2020. It is rolled in the United States.
cigars.researchNote: Annual limited release, made at an undisclosed Florida factory. It was 5 1/2 x 50 from 2020 to 2023 and 5 x 54 in 2024. The maker now lists a Toro as 6 x 52, 6 x 54 and 5.5 x 52 in different places.

cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped toro with Nicaraguan ligero filler, and the first Drunk Chicken cigar made outside the United States. It debuted at the 2025 PCA show.
cigars.researchNote: The maker writes both The Henchmen and The Henchman; halfwheel uses The Henchman. Halfwheel lists a Nicaraguan binder and a 6 x 54 size in a 250-box run; the maker says Ecuador binder and 6 x 52. Factory is undisclosed.

cigars.about: Apostate No. 1, one of the three blends the Salt Lake City brand launched with in 2021. It is made under Jochy Blanco at Tabacalera Palma and is meant as the introduction to the lineup.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish a strength; retailers list it as medium. The 4.5 x 44 Petite Corona is part of The Eight Witnesses, the same small size made in all eight core blends.

cigars.about: Apostate No. 2, named for a Mormon scriptural word for honeybee and blended with tobaccos chosen for sweetness. It is made at Tabacalera Palma and was one of the brand's three launch blends.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish a strength. halfwheel describes the wrapper as San Andrés maduro, with Ecuadorian Connecticut stripes and a stinger-style cap. The 4.5 x 44 size is part of The Eight Witnesses set.

cigars.about: Apostate No. 3, a slim torpedo shaped to suggest a compass needle and named for the compass in Mormon scripture. The maker pitches it as its most versatile blend, made at Tabacalera Palma.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the torpedo at 6 x 45; halfwheel's launch story gave 6 1/4 x 45. No strength or tasting notes are published by the maker.

cigars.about: Apostate No. 4, a candela-wrapped cigar named after Quetzalcoatl. Its green wrapper is Dominican-grown corojo seed, which is unusual for a candela, and it is made at Tabacalera Palma.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish a strength. halfwheel calls the 6.5 x 46 size a corona extra; the maker calls it a corona gorda.

cigars.about: Apostate No. 5, a long Churchill with an Ecuadorian corojo wrapper that the maker describes as the softer side of corojo. It is made at Tabacalera Palma and debuted at the 2023 PCA show.
cigars.researchNote: No strength or specific tasting notes are published by the maker.

cigars.about: Apostate No. 6, the brand's first box-pressed cigar, pairing a Pennsylvania broadleaf wrapper with an African Cameroon binder. It is made at Tabacalera Palma and debuted at the 2023 PCA show.
cigars.researchNote: No strength or specific tasting notes are published by the maker.

cigars.about: Apostate No. 7, the darkest cigar in the core range, with a San Andrés oscuro wrapper on a thick torpedo. It is made at Tabacalera Palma and shipped in September 2024 as one of the final two core blends.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish a strength. The maker lists the US filler only as USA; halfwheel identifies it as Connecticut broadleaf.

cigars.about: Apostate No. 8, the last of the eight core blends, which the maker calls its most complex. It wraps an Ecuadorian Connecticut Desflorado leaf over a broadleaf binder and is made at Tabacalera Palma.
cigars.researchNote: Strength, body and tasting notes come from halfwheel's review of the 4.5 x 44 Petite Corona (scored 91), not from the maker. The maker itself describes a rich body and long finish.

cigars.about: Apostate's first limited edition and its first cigar made outside Tabacalera Palma, rolled at Oveja Negra in Estelí. It is a single 5.5 x 48 robusto limited to 250 boxes of 20, or 5,000 cigars.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it The Death Mask 2026 Special Edition and publishes no strength. The maker and Cigar Dojo list Nicaraguan and US filler; halfwheel lists Nicaraguan only. It shipped October 1, 2026 at $20 each.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98 ligero, Olor viso, seco), USA (Pennsylvania Broadleaf)
cigars.about: The mild house line of Saarbrücken retailer Salih Dalay, a round long-filler with a light Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper. It is rolled in the Dominican Republic and sold as an affordable everyday cigar.
cigars.researchNote: "Hell" is German for light, as in the pale wrapper. The maker rates the sizes very mild to mild. There is also a small 4 x 25 Minutos; sizes are converted from millimetres.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98 ligero, Olor viso, seco), USA (Pennsylvania Broadleaf)
cigars.about: The maduro counterpart to Dalay Hell, the house brand of Saarbrücken retailer Salih Dalay. It is a sweet, chocolatey medium cigar with a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper, made at the company's Zauberberg factory in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: "Dunkel" is German for dark. The maker says the line is moving from box-pressed to round during the year. Retailer Noblego lists a different blend (Ecuador maduro wrapper, Dominican binder, Dominican and Brazilian filler).

cigars.about: A Dalay house line blended by Michael Grossklos around Honduran corojo-seed tobacco from the Jamastran valley, under an Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper. Every size uses the same blend, so the small formats smoke noticeably stronger than the large ones.
cigars.researchNote: Despite the name it is rolled in the Dominican Republic at Zauberberg in Santiago; Honduras refers to the Jamastran filler leaf. The maker rates it medium, Noblego calls it mild to medium, with the Half Corona the strongest and the Presidente the mildest.

cigars.about: A Dalay house line blended by Michael Grossklos to recall the sweet, chocolatey maduros of the 1990s cigar boom. It uses a US broadleaf wrapper over a Dominican binder and filler from three countries.
cigars.researchNote: Despite the name it is made in the Dominican Republic, not Honduras. The maker rates it medium; Noblego calls it mild to medium. The maker says the Half Corona scored 93 points in Zigarren Magazin.

cigars.about: Salih Dalay's tribute to his birth city, blended by Michael Grossklos with Turkish pipe tobacco aged over twelve months in the filler. The band and box carry artwork by Istanbul micro-painter Hasan Kale.
cigars.researchNote: The maker only describes the wrapper as a rustic leaf from Ecuador, with no leaf type. The maker says the Toro scored 90 points in Cigar Journal. Retailer Noblego lists the Toro at 152 mm and the Principe at 120 mm, against the maker's 139 mm and 114 mm.

cigars.about: The first Dalay cigar made in Nicaragua, developed by Salih Dalay and Michael Grossklos with Luciano Meirelles and rolled at his factory in Estelí. It has a double binder and an all-Nicaraguan filler from four regions.
cigars.researchNote: Planned as a limited edition but turned into a regular series once enough tobacco was available. The filler includes Masatepe leaf fermented underground. The maker says the Toro scored 90 points in Cigar Journal.

cigars.about: A Dalay line whose Dominican filler tobaccos are fermented in used casks from the company's own Andalusian brandy. The dark Ecuadorian wrapper gets an extra fermentation that leaves it visibly marbled.
cigars.researchNote: There is also a limited Robusto Especial (5 5/8 x 54) sold in a ceramic jar of 20, limited to 360 jars. The Super Churchill ring gauge of 54 comes from retailer Noblego, as the maker's page omits it. Sizes are converted from millimetres.

cigars.about: A short Dalay cigar for a half-hour break, blended by Michael Grossklos and made at the company's Zauberberg factory. It is themed on the Turkish folk figure Nasreddin Hodja and sold in paper-wrapped bundles of five with one of his stories inside.
cigars.researchNote: Single size, 95 mm x 48, sold as the Petite Robusto. The maker's spec sheet says medium, while its text calls the line mild to medium and mild in character. It premiered in Saarbrücken on May 15, 2026, and the maker does not name the wrapper leaf type.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (including Flor de Carbonell, 20/20 seed and Criollo 98)
cigars.about: A limited Dominican puro in Dalay's occasional Limitada series, blended by Michael Grossklos from tobaccos aged up to 15 years. It comes in one Gran Belicoso size and uses a wrapper given an extra fermentation.
cigars.researchNote: One size only, 154 mm x 57. Noblego reports 350 boxes of 20, or 7,000 cigars, and the tasting notes come from Noblego. The maker does not name the wrapper leaf type and says the blend uses the last of its 2008 crop Criollo 98.

cigars.about: The Connecticut Shade blend in the three core LH lines from Nicholas Syris, rolled in Costa Rica. The names Claro, Colorado and Maduro refer to wrapper shade.
cigars.researchNote: Two versions exist. The current Claro was reblended to be a milder, traditional Connecticut. The stronger original, with the black and gold band, came back in 2018 in Robusto, Toro and Gordo. No reviewer or maker strength rating was found.

cigars.about: The Ecuadorian Habano blend in the three core LH lines from Nicholas Syris, rolled at Tabacos de Costa Rica. It was the third LH blend to reach the U.S., debuting at the 2015 trade show.
cigars.researchNote: Strength and body are from Cigar Coop's review; halfwheel found it below medium for most of the smoke. Cigar Coop lists the filler as Brazil, Nicaragua and Peru instead of Ecuador, Peru and Nicaragua.

cigars.about: The maduro blend in the three core LH lines from Nicholas Syris, using an Ecuadorian Criollo maduro wrapper and rolled in Costa Rica. It came to the U.S. with the Claro in 2014.
cigars.researchNote: Strength, body and flavors are from Cigar Coop's reviews. Cigar Coop lists the filler as Nicaragua, Peru and Brazil, and in 2019 called the wrapper Ecuadorian Habano Maduro.

cigars.about: A 6 x 52 toro from LH Cigars that was first made for private clients outside the U.S. and came to the American market in 2020. It wears the original black and gold LH band.
cigars.researchNote: Also called Lavida Habana LE. Binder and filler are undisclosed. 2020 is the U.S. launch; it was sold abroad for years before. Strength and body are from Cigar Coop's review.

cigars.about: A line named for LH Cigars founder Nicholas Syris that grew out of the Nick & Jim P.B.E. collaboration. It began as a lonsdale made for 2nd Street Cigars and went national in 2020 with the Panzon figurado.
cigars.researchNote: Strength, body and flavors are from Cigar Coop's Panzon review, which found it building to medium-full in the last third. The Nick Sofos salomon carries the Nick name but is a different blend.

cigars.about: A blend from LH Cigars named with the Greek form of Nick, after founder Nicholas Syris' Greek roots. The company made it as a stronger, bolder option than its other cigars.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it stronger and fuller bodied than its other blends, but no rating was found. Cigar Coop treats it as part of the Nick line. Launched in one size with more promised.

cigars.about: A 6 x 58 short salomon from LH Cigars, named with the Greek word for wise as a nod to founder Nicholas Syris' heritage. It is sold under the Nick name but uses its own blend.
cigars.researchNote: An extension of the Nick line in one size, with a different blend from the other Nick cigars. Strength, body and flavors are from Cigar Coop's review.

cigars.about: The first LH Cigars blend with a Mexican San Andres wrapper, released in 2024 as part of the Nick family. It is made at Tabacos de Costa Rica in two sizes.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel reports 10,000 robustos and 25,000 toros made; Cigar Coop calls it a limited production line. Strength, body and flavors are from Cigar Coop's review.

cigars.about: A limited cigar marking ten years of LH Cigars in the U.S. market, made at Tabacos de Costa Rica. Its 5 7/8 x 52 size is a tribute to the Cohiba Siglo VI.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are undisclosed, and the production number was not released. halfwheel rated strength mild with medium body; Cigar Coop rated both medium.

cigars.about: The Connecticut Broadleaf version of R&R's full strength Gran Corona line. Made by Raul Reyner at Mi Havana Cigars in Esteli, Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Sizes are from the maker's site. halfwheel's launch story lists different dimensions: 5 x 60, 6 1/2 x 54 and 6 x 60.

cigars.about: The Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro version of R&R's full strength Gran Corona line. Made by Raul Reyner at Mi Havana Cigars in Esteli, Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's product titles spell it Habana Oscuro. halfwheel lists the perfecto as 6 1/2 x 54; the maker says 6 1/2 x 52.

cigars.about: The Mexican San Andres version of R&R's full strength Gran Corona line. Made by Raul Reyner at Mi Havana Cigars in Esteli, Nicaragua.
The mild Connecticut shade version of R&R's Pax Romana line, with a San Andres binder over Nicaraguan filler. Made by Raul Reyner at Mi Havana Cigars in Esteli, Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Neither the maker nor halfwheel says where the Connecticut seed wrapper is grown. The maker rates it mild; halfwheel reports the Pax Romana line as mild-medium and lists Dominican and Nicaraguan filler.

cigars.about: The Habano Claro version of R&R's Pax Romana line, the milder end of the range. Made by Raul Reyner at Mi Havana Cigars in Esteli, Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The Ecuador wrapper origin is from halfwheel, which also lists Dominican and Nicaraguan filler and a 6 1/2 x 54 perfecto and 6 x 57 salomon. The maker lists only Nicaraguan filler.

cigars.about: The Mexican San Andres version of R&R's Pax Romana line, blended to stay on the mild side. Made by Raul Reyner at Mi Havana Cigars in Esteli, Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel lists Dominican and Nicaraguan filler; the maker lists only Nicaraguan.

cigars.about: The Connecticut Broadleaf version of R&R's medium strength Soldier King line. Made by Raul Reyner at Mi Havana Cigars in Esteli, Nicaragua.
The box pressed Habano Claro version of R&R's medium strength Soldier King line. Made by Raul Reyner at Mi Havana Cigars in Esteli, Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The Ecuador wrapper origin is from halfwheel; the maker's site does not state it.

cigars.line: The Soldier King Mexico San Andres
cigars.about: The box pressed Mexican San Andres version of R&R's medium strength Soldier King line. Made by Raul Reyner at Mi Havana Cigars in Esteli, Nicaragua.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Ligero, San Vicente Olor, Oro Seco aged 18 years)
cigars.about: A mild Dominican cigar that uses Connecticut Shade leaf for both wrapper and binder over filler that includes tobacco aged 18 years. It is made for Cusano, now a Davidoff brand, by Hendrik Kelner.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as Cusano 18 Double Connecticut. Neptune lists it as mild, Mike's Cigars as mild to medium. halfwheel reported in 2016 that Davidoff's new Dominican lines would replace the 18 Series, but retailers still stock it.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Olor, Piloto, Oro aged 18 years)
cigars.about: The maduro counterpart to Cusano 18, pairing a dark Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper with Brazilian Mata Fina and Dominican filler that includes tobacco aged 18 years. It is made in the Dominican Republic for Cusano, a Davidoff brand.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the Mata Fina: Neptune's description puts a Brazilian Mata Fina leaf under the Broadleaf wrapper, while the spec tables at Neptune and Mike's Cigars list a Dominican binder with Brazilian leaf in the filler. Neptune lists it as medium, Mike's as medium to full.

cigars.about: A bundled cigar from Cusano's Celebrity Series, blended as a Cuban-style smoke with an Ecuadorian wrapper over Dominican binder and filler. CC stands for Cusano Cubans.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune's guide and Mike's spec table say medium to full, Neptune's product listing says medium, and Mike's description calls it mellow. It uses mixed short and long filler. Part of the value-priced Celebrity Series with M1, MC and P1.

cigars.about: The first cigar in Cusano's Celebrity Series, a mild bundled Dominican with a Connecticut Shade wrapper. It was made as a low-cost alternative for fans of mild Connecticut cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper origin disagrees: Mike's Cigars and halfwheel say Ecuadorian Connecticut, Neptune lists US Connecticut Shade. Neptune calls it mild, Mike's medium. It uses mixed short and long filler. The 2016 M1 Connecticut bundles came in Robusto, Churchill 7 x 48 and Gordo 6 x 60.

cigars.about: A bundled Dominican cigar from Cusano's Celebrity Series with a Connecticut Shade wrapper over Dominican binder and filler. It is sold as a creamy everyday smoke at a low price.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune describes it as a medium Connecticut; Mike's Cigars lists medium to full. Mike's says it is made at Hendrik Kelner's Tabadom factory. The wrapper's country of origin is not stated.

cigars.about: The maduro member of Cusano's Celebrity Series, a bundled Dominican cigar with a dark wrapper over Dominican binder and filler. It is made for Cusano by Hendrik Kelner of Davidoff.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune calls it medium; Mike's Cigars lists medium to full. The wrapper origin is not given for the original. The 2016 P1 Maduro bundle line uses a Mexican wrapper, Ecuadorian Connecticut binder and Dominican filler.

cigars.about: A value-priced Dominican cigar with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper, launched in 2016 as the first new Cusano since Davidoff bought the brand in 2009.
cigars.researchNote: Launched as Cusano Dominican Connecticut. halfwheel reports an Ecuadorian Connecticut binder; Cigar World lists the binder as Dominican.

cigars.about: A value-priced Dominican maduro with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper, released in 2016 alongside the Dominican Connecticut as part of Davidoff's Cusano relaunch.
cigars.researchNote: Launched as Cusano Dominican Maduro.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98 viso, Corojo ligero, Piloto seco), Nicaragua (Jalapa seco)
cigars.about: The debut line from Freud Cigar Co., named for Sigmund Freud's concept of the superego. It was blended with Wiber Ventura and is made at Tabacalera William Ventura in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's spec list shows a Dominican corojo-seed wrapper, but the blender's quote on the same page and halfwheel both say Ecuadorian. The blender calls strength medium to medium-strong; halfwheel's review found mild strength with medium body. The Magnum went on hiatus in late 2023 when the Belicoso was added.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Pelo de Oro, Corojo, Havana 92, Piloto Cubano)
cigars.about: Freud's second regular line and its first core cigar from Eladio Diaz's Tabacalera Diaz Cabrera. The blend is known for including Pelo de Oro, a rarely used tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: The maker describes it as between medium and full bodied. halfwheel's review put strength at medium and body at medium-full.

cigars.about: Freud's first limited edition, a Dominican puro blended by Eladio Diaz and rolled at his Tabacalera Diaz Cabrera factory. The name is Greek for the highest form of love.
cigars.researchNote: The full blend is not disclosed beyond being all Dominican with seven tobaccos. Limited to 3,500 boxes of 10. The follow-up in 2025 was respelled Agapi and is a different blend.

cigars.about: The second release in Freud's Eladio Diaz limited edition series, a single torpedo with a Mexican wrapper over a Dominican binder. It follows the 2022 Agape under a new spelling.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 300 boxes of 10. Renamed from Agape because people mispronounced it. halfwheel gave two different filler lists for it, so only the countries are recorded here.

cigars.line: Limited Edition Sigmund: Chapter One - The Disruptor
cigars.about: A limited edition released in 2023 for Sigmund Freud's birthday, blended by Eladio Diaz and made at his Tabacalera Diaz Cabrera factory in a single 7 1/2 x 50 size.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is undisclosed. The company says only that it uses seven tobaccos, five of them in the filler. Limited to 3,500 boxes of 10.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Broadleaf, Criollo 98 viso, Piloto), Ecuador (Corojo viso)
cigars.about: A licensed Elvis Presley cigar from Freud Cigar Co., made at Tabacalera William Ventura in a slender 7 x 38 size. The first edition launched in early 2026.
cigars.researchNote: First edition was 1,000 boxes of 10. The company has said it plans to make Elvis a regular release. halfwheel calls the size a lancero.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (seco), Ecuador (Habano viso), Dominican Republic (San Vicente ligero), Criollo 98 viso of undisclosed origin
cigars.about: The first line in Freud Cigar Co.'s Carlos & Maria brand, which carries no Freud branding. It was blended by Wiber Ventura and is rolled at El Maestro, a small factory run by Tabacalera William Ventura.
cigars.researchNote: No strength rating is published by the maker. halfwheel's review found strength on the milder side of medium with fuller flavor.

cigars.about: The second Carlos & Maria release from Freud Cigar Co., a limited 6 x 60 blended by Wiber Ventura and made at Tabacalera William Ventura.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 500 boxes of 10. The maker calls the size a Magnum. It is a different blend from the regular Amorío.

cigars.about: The flagship line from El Titan de Bronze, a small family-run factory on Calle Ocho in Miami's Little Havana. This version was reblended in 2024 with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper over all-Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: This is the 2024 Redemption first sold through General Cigar; the factory took distribution back in August 2026. The maker calls the wrapper Sun Grown Habano without an origin; halfwheel gives Ecuador. The older Redemption Sun Grown and Maduro are separate blends.

cigars.about: The maduro version of El Titan de Bronze's Redemption, rolled at the family's factory in Miami's Little Havana. It pairs a Mexican San Andrés wrapper with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: A different blend from the 2024 Redemption, which has all-Nicaraguan binder and filler.

cigars.about: A sun grown Ecuadorian habano blend in El Titan de Bronze's Redemption family, rolled in Miami's Little Havana. It uses Dominican and Nicaraguan filler and smokes at medium.
cigars.researchNote: Not the same cigar as the 2024 Redemption, which has all-Nicaraguan binder and filler and comes in three sizes.

cigars.about: The first El Titan de Bronze cigar made outside the United States, rolled at NACSA in Nicaragua rather than at the Miami factory. It has a broadleaf wrapper over a Mexican binder and Nicaraguan filler and is priced well below the Miami-made lines.
cigars.researchNote: Not made in Miami: it is rolled at NACSA in Nicaragua. The maker's page also calls it Redemption Nicaragua. No source states where the broadleaf wrapper is grown.

cigars.about: The mild Connecticut-wrapped cigar from El Titan de Bronze, rolled at the family's factory in Miami's Little Havana. The maker pitches it as a morning or first cigar.
A full bodied maduro from El Titan de Bronze, rolled in Miami's Little Havana with a dark Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper. The maker says it is not meant for beginners.
A dark habano-wrapped cigar from El Titan de Bronze in Miami's Little Havana, sold in bundles rather than boxes. The maker says it is bunched entubado style and finished with a triple cap.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish the binder, filler or where the wrapper is grown. It calls the cigar medium bodied but also says it is not a beginner's cigar.

cigars.about: A limited cigar marking 30 years of El Titan de Bronze, which the maker dates to 1995. It comes in one 6.5 x 52 size in boxes of 10, with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan and Dominican tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: Limited release in one size, sold in boxes of 10. The maker gives no release date or production number.

cigars.about: One of the original blends from Fermin Perez Cigars, a Miami brand founded in 2021 by Cuban-born Fermin Perez Jr. and made in Estelí, Nicaragua. It is the balanced habano in the core lineup.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not say where the Habano wrapper is grown and publishes no size list; the 6 x 54 Toro is the only size confirmed. Production moved in September 2026 from Perez's own Estelí factory to Tabacalera Familia Disla; he says the blends did not change.

cigars.about: One of the original blends from Fermin Perez Cigars, made in Estelí, Nicaragua. It is a Connecticut shade cigar built to be smooth without being flavorless.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's page calls it medium bodied; the Cigar Press review it cites rated it mild in strength and medium in body, and names the wrapper as Ecuadorian. Only the 6 x 54 Toro is confirmed. Production moved in September 2026 from Perez's own Estelí factory to Tabacalera Familia Disla; he says the blends did not change.

cigars.about: The maduro in the Fermin Perez core lineup, made in Estelí, Nicaragua with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over an Indonesian binder and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it full flavored; reviewers put it at medium to full. The Toro also comes in a tube. Production moved in September 2026 from Perez's own Estelí factory to Tabacalera Familia Disla; he says the blends did not change.

cigars.about: A box pressed habano from Fermin Perez Cigars, made in Estelí, Nicaragua. It uses an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper and a Habano binder over Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: The brand also calls this line simply Royal. The maker publishes no sizes or strength rating and does not say where the Habano binder is grown. Production moved in September 2026 from Perez's own Estelí factory to Tabacalera Familia Disla; he says the blends did not change.

cigars.about: A sweet-tipped habano from Fermin Perez Cigars, made in Estelí, Nicaragua as a nod to Miami's Little Havana. The filler includes tobacco from Jalapa and the island of Ometepe.
cigars.researchNote: The cap is sweetened, which is worth telling a guest. The maker publishes no sizes or binder and does not say where the wrapper is grown. Production moved in September 2026 from Perez's own Estelí factory to Tabacalera Familia Disla; he says the blends did not change.

cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped cigar from Fermin Perez Cigars, made in Estelí, Nicaragua with a Jalapa binder and Nicaraguan and Dominican filler. The maker describes it as medium bodied.
cigars.researchNote: The maker also calls it Esmeralda Connecticut and does not say where the wrapper is grown or list sizes. Production moved in September 2026 from Perez's own Estelí factory to Tabacalera Familia Disla; he says the blends did not change.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro from Fermin Perez Cigars in which the wrapper, binder and filler are all grown in Estelí, where it is also rolled. It comes in a single corona size in boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: New in fall 2026 and made in one size only. The maker calls it bold but gives no strength rating. Binder and filler varietals are not disclosed.

cigars.about: A habano-wrapped line from Fermin Perez Cigars, made in Estelí, Nicaragua with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. The maker describes it as medium to full bodied.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish the binder, filler or sizes. Production moved in September 2026 from Perez's own Estelí factory to Tabacalera Familia Disla; he says the blends did not change.

cigars.about: A four-size regular line from Paul Stulac Cigars with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is rolled at Las Villas Cigars in Nicaragua under Guillermo Pena.
cigars.researchNote: Soft-launched in July 2025 as a 6 x 52 toro called the Katman Edition; the full four-size line shipped in early 2026. Privada Cigar Club lists the blend as undisclosed and gives slightly different sizes.

cigars.about: A long-running Paul Stulac blend with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over a Sumatra binder and Nicaraguan filler. It was first rolled in Miami by Guillermo Pena and is now made in Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Privada lists a Habano Rosado wrapper, but halfwheel, Cigar Coop and Blind Man's Puff all say Connecticut Broadleaf. First rolled in Miami, it moved to Tabacalera La Perla in Nicaragua by 2019. The toro was 6 x 56 in 2014 lists; halfwheel's 2026 size list for the brand gives 6 x 52.

cigars.about: A long-running Paul Stulac blend sold in the same four sizes as Red Screaming Sun. Reviews describe a dark Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over a Sumatra binder and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree. Blind Man's Puff gives a dark Ecuadorian Habano wrapper and medium to strong strength; Privada lists Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade, mild to medium, and a 6 x 56 toro. First rolled in Miami; Privada now lists Las Villas in Esteli, Nicaragua.

cigars.about: Paul Stulac's 2020 return to the market, with a name that means The New Beginning. The regular production version is a Connecticut Broadleaf robusto extra sold through the Limited Cigar Association.
cigars.researchNote: Two different blends carry this name. The regular production one is the Paul Stulac Exclusiva (5 1/2 x 54, broadleaf). The Privada Limitada (5 x 54) uses a Mexican San Andres wrapper over a Habano 2000 binder and was a Privada exclusive.

cigars.about: A limited series Paul Stulac started in late 2013 to ship cigars fresh off the rolling table, wrapped in newspaper. Each release is a tweaked or one-off blend in its own size.
cigars.researchNote: The blend changes by release. The 2013 debut was a 6 x 56 torpedo rolled in Miami, a tweaked White Blinding Light (Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, Sumatra binder, Nicaraguan filler). Privada lists a Sumatra Rosado toro and torpedo made at Las Villas in Esteli; that is not confirmed elsewhere.

cigars.about: A Paul Stulac cigar sold only to Privada Cigar Club members, named for his years in Miami. Privada is the only place it is listed.
cigars.researchNote: Privada is the only source. It lists a 6 x 52 toro with a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, made at Las Villas in Esteli. Treat the blend as unconfirmed: Privada's listings for other Paul Stulac lines conflict with halfwheel.

cigars.about: A Paul Stulac cigar sold through Privada Cigar Club in singles and boxes of 20. Privada is the only place it is listed.
cigars.researchNote: Privada is the only source. It lists a 6 x 60 gordo with a Mexican San Andres maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, full strength, made at Las Villas in Esteli. Treat the blend as unconfirmed: Privada's listings for other Paul Stulac lines conflict with halfwheel.

cigars.about: A Paul Stulac cigar sold through Privada Cigar Club in singles and boxes of 20. Privada is the only place it is listed.
cigars.researchNote: Privada is the only source. It lists a 6 x 56 toro grande with a Mexican San Andres maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, full strength, made at Las Villas in Esteli. Treat the blend as unconfirmed: Privada's listings for other Paul Stulac lines conflict with halfwheel.

cigars.about: The mildest of the three original 1502 blends from Enrique Sanchez's Global Premium Cigars, box pressed and made at Plasencia in Esteli. The maker calls its style fina fuerte, or fine strong.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it mild plus (about 4 to 4.6 out of 10); Neptune lists it as Mild. All sizes are box pressed.

cigars.about: The middle-strength blend of the three original 1502 lines from Global Premium Cigars. It pairs a dark Ecuadorian wrapper with Nicaraguan tobaccos from Jalapa and Esteli and is made at Plasencia.
cigars.researchNote: The maker only says the wrapper is a dark leaf from Ecuador and does not name the seed. It rates the cigar medium plus (6 to 7 out of 10); Neptune lists Medium. Neptune lists the lancero as 7 x 38, the maker and halfwheel as 7 x 40.

cigars.about: The strongest of the three original 1502 blends from Global Premium Cigars. It uses a dark San Andres maduro wrapper over a double Nicaraguan binder and Nicaraguan filler, and is made at Plasencia.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's site only calls the wrapper a maduro sun-grown leaf; halfwheel and Neptune identify it as Mexican San Andres. All sizes are box pressed.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Nicaraguan puro from Global Premium Cigars using tobacco from the country's four main growing regions. The maker places it between the Emerald and the Ruby in strength.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's site also spells it 1502 Nicaraguan. It is sometimes called 1502 White for its white band. The maker describes it as medium plus; Neptune lists Medium.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro with a dark maduro wrapper, introduced by Global Premium Cigars at the 2016 trade show. It is made at Plasencia in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Strength varies by source: the maker called it medium-full to full at launch, Neptune's spec says Medium while its description says full strength. halfwheel gives the robusto as 5 x 50; the maker and Neptune list 5 x 52.

cigars.about: A limited 1502 release from Global Premium Cigars, made at Plasencia with some tobacco aged 18 years. XO stands for extra old, as in cognac, and boxes are individually numbered.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is not disclosed; the wrapper is dark. The maker calls it mild plus (5 to 6.4 out of 10), while Neptune lists Medium strength and calls it full bodied. The first release was a 6 x 50 toro in 1,502 numbered boxes of 10; other sizes followed.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A single-size toro released in 2022 to mark ten years of Global Premium Cigars and the 1502 brand. Unlike the other 1502 lines, it is made by AJ Fernandez rather than Plasencia.
cigars.researchNote: An anniversary cigar that is ongoing regular production, not a limited edition.

cigars.about: The core line from El Viejo Continente, a Nicaraguan brand founded by Spanish tobacconist Daniel Guerrero. It uses an Ecuadorian wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos from Jalapa and Condega.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls the wrapper Ecuador Rosado; halfwheel and Neptune call it Ecuadorian Habano. The maker says medium strength, halfwheel reported medium-full and Neptune lists Full. It came to the US at the 2016 IPCPR show through Tabacos Costa Nicaragua (Tabacosta).

cigars.about: The maduro line from El Viejo Continente, with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos from Jalapa and Condega. It comes in five sizes from a small Piccolo to a long Lancero.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists a Jalapa binder and medium strength; Neptune lists an Ecuadorian Habano binder and Full strength.

cigars.about: El Viejo Continente's Connecticut blend, a single toro with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos from Jalapa and Condega. The maker pitches it as an any-time-of-day smoke.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it mild to medium-mild, while Neptune lists it as Full. The maker gives the toro as 6 1/4 x 60; Neptune sells it as 6 x 56.

cigars.about: The fuller line from El Viejo Continente, named after the Roman term for the Mediterranean Sea. It has a dark Ecuadorian wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos and comes in several short, thick sizes plus a culebras and a lancero.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists an Ecuador Oscuro wrapper with all-Nicaraguan binder and filler, medium to full. Neptune describes a Habano maduro wrapper, Nicaraguan Habano binder and Brazilian plus Nicaraguan filler, Full strength, and a 5 3/4 x 30 culebras.

cigars.about: A special edition salomon made to mark the fifth anniversary of El Viejo Continente, using tobaccos aged for five years. It comes in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish the blend, only that the tobaccos are aged five years and the cigar is full bodied. It is listed under Special Edition with no production numbers.

cigars.about: A special edition from El Viejo Continente built entirely from Esteli-area tobacco as a tribute to the region. The maker says it was the first box-pressed cigar made at its factory.
cigars.researchNote: The maker says only that it is 100% Esteli tobacco, from Esteli and Pueblo Nuevo, and does not name the wrapper leaf or say which leaf is binder or filler. It is a box-pressed special edition in boxes of 10, with no production numbers.

cigars.about: A special edition from El Viejo Continente with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos from four regions. It is sold in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Listed by the maker under Special Edition, with no production numbers published.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped cigar in Cayman Cigar Company's core range, described by the maker as smooth, creamy and approachable. The company gives all of its net profits to charity.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel calls it Sovereign II. Reblended in 2025; before that it was made in the Cayman Islands. U.S. stock is now made at Tabacalera La Isla in the Dominican Republic, and the maker publishes no strength rating.

cigars.about: A core line from Cayman Cigar Company with a Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and Dominican filler. The company gives all of its net profits to charity.
cigars.researchNote: Reblended and resized in 2025. U.S. stock is made at Tabacalera La Isla in the Dominican Republic, while Cayman and U.K. stock is rolled in the Cayman Islands. The maker calls it bold but balanced and gives no formal strength rating.

cigars.about: A corojo-wrapped core line from Cayman Cigar Company, pitched as the medium to full step up from the Sovereign No. 2. The company gives all of its net profits to charity.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the blend: the maker lists Nicaraguan Corojo over a Nicaraguan Sumatra binder, while halfwheel's 2025 relaunch report gave Ecuadorian corojo over a Dominican binder. U.S. stock is made in the Dominican Republic. The maker's U.S. cigars page does not list it.

cigars.about: A San Andrés-wrapped Nicaraguan cigar blended by Esteban Disla and made at his factory in Estelí for Cayman Cigar Company. It was the company's first line from that factory.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel and the box call it The Doubloon. The maker describes it as full-bodied, spicy and rich.

cigars.about: A box-pressed Connecticut Broadleaf cigar with a pigtail cap, made for Cayman Cigar Company at Esteban Disla's factory in Estelí. It joined the core range at the 2026 PCA show.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it full-bodied. Halfwheel's review found full flavor but strength finishing at medium-full and body around medium-plus. All three sizes are box-pressed.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andrés with Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed accents
cigars.about: A limited 6 x 58 perfecto from Cayman Cigar Company with two contrasting wrappers and a shaggy decorative head, made by Esteban Disla in Estelí. The name nods to Las Tortugas, the name Columbus gave the Cayman Islands.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 250 boxes of 10, sold through brick-and-mortar shops only. It uses two wrappers, a dark San Andrés and a lighter Connecticut-seed. The maker pitches it as bold and spicy, but halfwheel's review found strength mild to just under medium.

cigars.about: A limited 5 x 50 robusto with a habano-seed wrapper, the first cigar Cayman Cigar Company sold that was made in Nicaragua. Only 2,500 cigars were produced.
cigars.researchNote: The company did not disclose the blend or the factory and calls it medium to medium-plus. Limited to 250 bundles of 10. Halfwheel reported it going on sale in March 2025, though the maker refers to it as a 2024 release.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Habano 2000, Piloto Cubano, Habano 92, Broadleaf)
cigars.about: The first regular production line from Eladio Díaz, the former Davidoff production chief who now runs his family's Tabacalera Díaz Cabrera. The name refers to his career before and after leaving to work with his children.
cigars.researchNote: The company describes it as medium to full-bodied. Halfwheel's review of the Pasion found full flavor with strength closer to medium to medium-plus. Distributed in the U.S. by Arango Cigar Co.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Corojo, Criollo 98, Negrito), Peru (Pelo de Oro)
cigars.about: The second core line from Eladio Díaz, named for the small Dominican factory where he started working with tobacco at age seven. Two sizes are named for his first mentor, Francisco Biloria Vencosme.
cigars.researchNote: Cigar Aficionado reports it is meant to be full-bodied, and Díaz calls it the strongest and most complex blend he has made. It starts creamy and sweet before building. Distributed in the U.S. by Arango Cigar Co.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Habano 2000, Piloto Cubano, Criollo 98), Peru (Pelo de Oro)
cigars.about: A Connecticut-seed wrapped line Eladio Díaz made in honor of his mother, whose family nickname gives the cigar its name. It uses tobacco from the southern Dominican Republic along with Peruvian pelo de oro.
cigars.researchNote: Announced in August 2026 with a debut at InterTabac in September and U.S. shipping expected in early November 2026, so it may not be on shelves yet. Díaz describes it as a pleasant medium body. Pricing had not been set at announcement.

cigars.about: A limited 7 x 52 cigar marking Eladio Díaz's 70th birthday and the first of his long-running private birthday cigars to be sold. It was first meant only for Europe before Arango brought part of the run to the U.S.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,400 boxes of 14, with 300 boxes for the U.S. The blend uses seven tobaccos but the leaf varieties were not published. Strength and flavors here come from halfwheel's review, which found it just under medium.

cigars.about: The limited cigar for Eladio Díaz's 71st birthday, a 6 x 54 toro built to show off tobacco from San Juan de la Maguana and Las Matas de Farfán in the southern Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,000 numbered boxes of 10. Díaz calls it medium to full in strength. Distributed in the U.S. by Arango Cigar Co.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98, HVA, Corojo 99, Piloto Cubano, Negrito)
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican sun-grown Corojo-seed, aged four years
cigars.about: The limited cigar for Eladio Díaz's 72nd birthday, an all-Dominican blend that combines tobacco from the country's established northern fields and its revived southern growing region.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,500 boxes of 12. Díaz rates its strength 7 out of 10; no other strength rating was found. The binder is Mexican San Andrés Negro seed grown in the Dominican Republic, and the wrapper comes from the south of the country.

cigars.binder: Dominican Republic (Sumatra seed and San Andrés Negro seed)
cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (barrel-aged Habano 2000, Corojo 99, Criollo 98, Corojo 06, Piloto Cubano)
cigars.about: The limited cigar for Eladio Díaz's 73rd birthday, an all-Dominican blend of eight tobaccos with a double binder and a wrapper from the southern part of the country.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 2,000 boxes of 11, each holding ten toro extras and a single robusto. Strength and flavors here come from halfwheel's review, which found strength running from mild up to medium-plus by the end.

cigars.about: The first boxed cigar from Griff Howie and Dave Imber, a closed-foot robusto blended with Tony and Carson Serino and Omar González Alemán at the La Corona factory in Estelí. It is named for the university newspaper where the two founders met.
cigars.researchNote: The blend includes a quarter leaf of medio tiempo. No strength rating is published. The maker says it is released once a year; a 4.5 x 50 Founders Select version was a one-off run of 200 cigars.

cigars.about: Griff & Dave's first Miami-made cigar, a closed-foot Connecticut robusto rolled at the Cremo factory in the Overtown neighborhood. It was sold in small-batch 10-packs.
cigars.researchNote: Sold out on the maker's site. No strength rating is published.

cigars.about: A small-batch 5 x 50 from Griff & Dave named for the founders' birth months, December and February. The cigars rested in the factory aging room for 24 months before release.
cigars.researchNote: Sold out on the maker's site. The factory, country and wrapper origin are not published. The maker says it worked with Barrel King on the release, without spelling out the process.

cigars.about: A holiday blend from Griff & Dave with a San Andrés maduro wrapper over aged Nicaraguan and Dominican fillers, built around Christmas spice flavors.
cigars.researchNote: Sold out on the maker's site. The binder, factory, country and strength are not published.

cigars.about: The first blend Griff & Dave sold, a 5.25 x 46 made from Dominican and Nicaraguan tobaccos and meant as an everyday smoke.
cigars.researchNote: The maker says only that it blends Dominican and Nicaraguan tobaccos and is full of flavor but low on strength. The wrapper, factory and country are not published. Sold out on the maker's site.

cigars.about: The first release in Griff & Dave's unbanded test blend series, a 4.5 x 44 made in the Dominican Republic and sold in very small quantities.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is deliberately undisclosed: the maker says only that it is handmade in the Dominican Republic. Sold in unbanded 10-count bundles and listed as sold out.

cigars.about: The second release in Griff & Dave's unbanded test blend series, a 6 x 52 toro with a habano wrapper made at the La Corona factory in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper's country of origin is not published. Sold in unbanded 10-count bundles and listed as sold out.

cigars.about: A low-priced bundle cigar from Altadis U.S.A., made in the Dominican Republic with a Connecticut Shade wrapper over aged Dominican and Honduran long filler. It is the mild, mellow blend in the Casa de Garcia range.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis describes it as smooth and mellow without a strength rating; Neptune lists it as mild.

cigars.about: The dark-wrapped version of Altadis U.S.A.'s Casa de Garcia bundle line, made in the Dominican Republic with aged Dominican and Honduran long filler. It is a smooth, inexpensive everyday maduro.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis's spec table lists a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper, but its own description calls it a Connecticut Shade leaf sun-ripened until nearly black. Altadis gives no strength rating and calls the flavors mellow; medium is Neptune's listing.

cigars.about: A Sumatra-wrapped blend in Altadis U.S.A.'s Casa de Garcia bundle line, made in the Dominican Republic with a Connecticut Broadleaf binder and Dominican and Honduran long filler. Altadis describes it as mellow in strength with a slow burn.
cigars.researchNote: Altadis does not say where the Sumatra wrapper is grown. Strength is from Altadis's own wording, a mellow strength.

cigars.about: The fuller-bodied blend in Altadis U.S.A.'s Casa de Garcia bundle line, with a dark Nicaraguan Habano 2000 wrapper. Despite the name it is rolled in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the binder and filler. Altadis's spec table and Neptune list a Connecticut Broadleaf binder with Nicaraguan, Broadleaf and Colombian filler, but Altadis's own description says Nicaraguan binder. halfwheel's 2013 report said Nicaraguan binder over Dominican filler.

cigars.about: The stronger of the two Casa de Garcia Centenario blends, a value-priced bundle cigar that Altadis U.S.A. has made in Nicaragua with the Plasencia family. It pairs an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is unsettled. Altadis rates it 4 on a numeric scale that reaches at least 9 on its other pages, while Neptune lists it as full. Altadis says it is made with the Plasencia family but has not named the factory.

cigars.about: The milder of the two Casa de Garcia Centenario blends, a value-priced bundle cigar that Altadis U.S.A. has made in Nicaragua with the Plasencia family. It uses an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel's 2022 launch report called this blend the White Label; Altadis and retailers list it as Gold Label. Neptune lists medium, while Altadis rates it 3 on a numeric scale that reaches at least 9, so it may smoke milder. The specific Plasencia factory has not been named.

cigars.about: The first cigar from Gellis Family Cigars, the brand Warped founder Kyle Gellis put his family name on. It is a single 5 1/8 x 43 size with a closed foot, aged a year in Spanish cedar before boxing.
cigars.researchNote: Blend details vary by source. The maker's brand page says Ecuador Habano 2000 wrapper and Ecuador binder, but its shop page lists an Ecuador Corojo '99 wrapper and Dominican San Vicente binder. halfwheel reported a habano 2000 rosada wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder.

cigars.about: The second release from Kyle Gellis's Gellis Family Cigars, a single 5 1/4 x 48 robusto with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. It is named for the way the family's Cane Corso sauntered around the office and is aged a year in cedar before boxing.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's brand page rates it medium to full while its shop page says medium. halfwheel's reviewer found the strength mild to medium. The maker says Cigar Aficionado named it No. 16 Cigar of the Year with 95 points.

cigars.about: The annual limited edition from Gellis Family Cigars, a 6 x 52 toro capped at 500 boxes of 15 each year. The name is a watchmaking term, and each year's blend is made once and not repeated.
cigars.researchNote: The blend changes every year; the one shown is the maker's listed blend, matching the 2024 debut. Per halfwheel, the 2025 release went only to non-U.S. retailers with a Brazilian Arapiraca binder, and the 2026 uses a Mexican San Andres binder. All keep an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper.

cigars.about: The first Nicaraguan-made line from Gellis Family Cigars, a soft box-pressed Nicaraguan puro rolled at NACSA in Esteli. It uses all sun grown tobacco from Esteli, Ometepe, Condega and Jalapa.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium plus, a step above medium. It launched in Corona Gorda and Toro; the Petit Robusto appears on the maker's shop, and a 6 1/2 x 42 Lonsdale was a limited store exclusive.

cigars.about: A 5 x 50 robusto from Gellis Family Cigars with a Mexican San Andres maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, rolled at NACSA in Esteli. It is made in small batches rather than continuously.
cigars.researchNote: Released in batches; halfwheel reports the first batch arrived in July 2026 and was 6,000 cigars, and describes it as sitting between a limited edition and a core line.

cigars.about: A small 4 1/2 x 32 cigar from Gellis Family Cigars, made as a short smoke for travel and sold in cabinets of 50. It has an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper and is rolled at Tabacalera La Isla in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's only rating is labeled body: medium. The maker calls the size a panetela; halfwheel calls it a petite corona.

cigars.about: A budget bundle cigar from General Cigar, handmade in Nicaragua with a Connecticut Shade wrapper and a lightly sweetened cap. It was one of the two original Odyssey blends.
cigars.researchNote: The cap is lightly sweetened. halfwheel lists the wrapper as Honduran Connecticut; Neptune's description just says Connecticut Shade.

cigars.about: A budget bundle cigar from General Cigar, handmade in Nicaragua with a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper over a Honduran binder and Nicaraguan filler. It was one of the two original Odyssey blends.
The maduro addition to General Cigar's budget Odyssey bundle line, made for the company in Nicaragua at Plasencia. It has a dark Nicaraguan wrapper over a Honduran binder and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: It launched in five sizes; some retailers now stock only the Toro and Gigante.

cigars.about: A mild, sweet-capped member of General Cigar's budget Odyssey bundle line, handmade in Nicaragua. It has a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper over a Honduran binder and a Honduran and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: The cap is sweetened. Neptune lists it as mild, while Mike's Cigars lists medium. Neptune stocks only the 6 x 54 Toro; the other four sizes come from Mike's Cigars listings.

cigars.about: A coffee-infused cigar in General Cigar's budget Odyssey bundle line, handmade in Nicaragua and sold in bundles of 12. It has a dark Indonesian wrapper and binder over Nicaraguan Habano and Indonesian filler.
cigars.researchNote: This is a flavored, coffee-infused cigar. Neptune lists it as medium, while Mike's Cigars lists mild to medium.

cigars.about: The strongest blend in General Cigar's budget Odyssey bundle line, made at STG Esteli in Nicaragua. It uses a Nicaraguan Jalapa wrapper, a Nicaraguan Habano binder and Nicaraguan and Colombian ligero filler.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper's seed type is not published, only that it is a dark Jalapa leaf. It launched in five sizes; some retailers now stock only the Toro.

cigars.about: The first line from Texas-based Emperors Cut, launched in 2018 as a single Toro and expanded to four sizes in 2020. It is rolled at Omar Ortez's factory in Condega, Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium-to-full bodied. halfwheel calls the wrapper Nicaraguan Colorado; Cigar Coop calls it Colorado Maduro. halfwheel lists the original Toro as 5 1/2 x 52, while the maker and Cigar Coop list 6 1/2 x 52.

cigars.about: The second Emperors Cut line, made at La Aurora in the Dominican Republic and launched in October 2020. Its three sizes are named for jazz musicians: Trane, Miles and Dizzy.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the Gordito length: the maker lists 4 x 58, halfwheel 5 x 58 and Cigar Coop 6 x 58. No strength is published.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Jalapa ligero, viso and seco), Colombia (cubita)
cigars.about: The maduro blend in the Emperors Cut Red Tail Series, a tribute to the Tuskegee Airmen named for the 332nd Fighter Group. It is made at La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: One of the blends in the Red Tail Series, alongside Warhawk (Natural) and Hellfighter. No strength is published.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Jalapa seco and viso, Condega viso), Dominican Republic (Habano 2020)
cigars.about: The natural-wrapper blend in the Emperors Cut Red Tail Series, named for the Curtiss P-40 Warhawk flown by the Tuskegee Airmen. It is made at La Aurora in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: One of the blends in the Red Tail Series, alongside 332nd (Maduro) and Hellfighter. No strength is published.

cigars.about: A newer addition to the Emperors Cut Red Tail Series, a box-pressed torpedo honoring the Harlem Hellfighters of World War I. It has a dark San Andrés wrapper over a Pennsylvania binder.
cigars.researchNote: Only the maker's shop page describes it, as a new arrival sold in 5-count packs. The factory, country, strength, release year and whether it is regular production are not published.

cigars.about: A limited Emperors Cut release made at La Aurora in the Dominican Republic with a Cameroon wrapper. Production was capped at 1,000 cigars, with shipping set for August 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Size is disputed: the maker's shop sells it as Prophecy (Divine), a Toro 6.5 x 52, while halfwheel and Cigar Coop report a 7 x 52 Churchill. The maker calls it medium-to-full bodied. Limited to 1,000 cigars.

cigars.about: A medium-bodied line from AG Cigars, the brand of former Cuban custom roller Alejandro "Alex" González Arias. It pairs an Ecuadorian wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker gives only "Ecuadorian" for the wrapper and calls it medium-bodied. The factory and release year are not published for this line; halfwheel says AG Cigars are made in Nicaragua. The Lancero is sold separately as AG Lancero Natural.

cigars.about: The bolder line from AG Cigars by Alex González, also called GAOTU Black Label. It uses a Habano 2000 wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, with sizes named for Masonic degrees.
cigars.researchNote: The maker also calls it GAOTU Black Label and G.A.O.T.U., and describes it as medium to full-bodied. Where the Habano 2000 wrapper is grown, the factory and the release year are not published; halfwheel says AG Cigars are made in Nicaragua.

cigars.about: A 7 x 52 cigar in the 109 shape from AG Cigars by Alex González, sold in boxes of 10. It placed fifth on halfwheel's Consensus list for 2025.
cigars.researchNote: Often called the Ambassador 109. The maker gives only "Ecuadorian" for the wrapper and publishes no strength or tasting notes.

cigars.about: A large 6 x 59 pyramid from AG Cigars by Alex González, sold in boxes of 5. It has an Ecuadorian wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists it as Piramides Gloriosos and gives only "Ecuador" for the wrapper. Strength, factory, release year and whether it is regular production are not published; halfwheel says AG Cigars are made in Nicaragua.

cigars.about: A limited celebrity cigar from AG Cigars made for actor Jamie Foxx. Its 5.9 x 58 size refers to his 5'9" height and his age of 58.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,500 boxes of 10. One filler country is undisclosed and the wrapper type is given only as Ecuadorian. halfwheel's review found medium to medium-full strength with medium-plus body.

cigars.about: A limited celebrity cigar from AG Cigars made for retired Baltimore Ravens linebacker Ray Lewis. Its 6.2 x 52 size refers to his 6'2" height and his jersey number 52.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,500 boxes of 10. One filler country is undisclosed. No strength or tasting notes are published. Lewis earlier had a separate cigar line made by Rocky Patel.

cigars.about: The mildest line from California-based Casa de Sueños, introduced in May 2022. It is made at De Los Reyes in the Dominican Republic with a light Ecuadorian wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel and Blind Man's Puff call the wrapper Ecuadorian Claro, while Cigar Coop calls it Connecticut Shade. The maker bills it as its mildest cigar; Blind Man's Puff rated it mild-medium and halfwheel's review found medium strength.

cigars.about: The first line from Casa de Sueños, launched in November 2019. The name means The Dreamer and it is made at De Los Reyes in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it its medium blend; Blind Man's Puff rated the Toro medium-strong. The box-pressed Prensa (6 x 58) was added in April 2026.

cigars.about: The second line from Casa de Sueños and the fullest in its core lineup. It is made at De Los Reyes in the Dominican Republic with Nicaraguan filler under an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it the fullest-bodied cigar in its lineup, but Blind Man's Puff rated the Toro Gordo medium in strength. The maker's product page and Cigar Coop list the Perfecto as 6 1/4 x 54; the maker's lineup page says 6.5 x 54. Blind Man's Puff gives a 2019 release, not confirmed elsewhere.

cigars.about: The first blend in Inception, the fourth regular line from Casa de Sueños. It is made at De Los Reyes in the Dominican Republic and was released in September 2026.
cigars.researchNote: The maker describes it as medium-bodied. The wrapper is given only as Ecuador, with no leaf type.

cigars.about: The fifth anniversary cigar from Casa de Sueños, a box-pressed robusto gordo with a pigtail cap released in 2024. It was made at De Los Reyes and limited to 300 boxes of 12.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 300 boxes of 12. Part of the filler is undisclosed. halfwheel's 2024 review lists it as 5 1/2 x 58, though a 2026 halfwheel article calls the vitola 6 x 58. halfwheel found strength building from medium to full; the maker gives no strength.

cigars.about: An aged release of the El Soñador Salomon from Casa de Sueños, using cigars rolled in 2019 and held in reserve until April 2026. It is limited to 100 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: This is one size of El Soñador, the 7 x 56 Salomon, in the same blend but rolled in 2019 and aged. halfwheel calls it Reserva Salomon 2019. Limited to 100 boxes of 10.

cigars.factory: Chateau Diadem factory (Santiago de los Caballeros)
cigars.about: A Dominican-made line from Chateau Diadem named after the Caribbean trade winds, using an Ecuadorian corojo wrapper in place of the habano 2000 on Conviction. It was introduced as a creamier, more affordable option in three sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's strength scale shows medium for the Robusto 52 and Gran Toro and medium to full for the Corona Gorda, and its text calls the Gran Toro full bodied. The co-founder described the line to Cigar Journal as mild to medium. Launched at InterTabac 2026.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Esteli Criollo), Dominican Republic (Criollo 98, Piloto Cubano)
cigars.factory: Chateau Diadem factory (Santiago de los Caballeros)
cigars.about: The debut blend from Chateau Diadem, the Dominican brand founded by cousins Emily Sahakian and Thierry Farah. It pairs an Ecuadorian habano 2000 wrapper with Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers and is rested six months before release.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in the US as Certitude because of a trademark issue; the cigars are the same. Strength is read from the maker's scale graphic, which sits between medium and full.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Esteli Criollo), Dominican Republic (Criollo 98, Piloto Cubano)
cigars.factory: Chateau Diadem factory (Santiago de los Caballeros)
cigars.about: The US-market name for Chateau Diadem's Conviction blend, renamed over a trademark issue. Apart from the name and packaging it is the same Dominican-made cigar with an Ecuadorian habano 2000 wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Same cigar as Conviction, which keeps that name outside the US. Launched at PCA 2025 in six sizes.

cigars.factory: Chateau Diadem factory (Santiago de los Caballeros)
cigars.about: A single-size Chateau Diadem blend built around Connecticut Broadleaf in the filler under an Ecuadorian corojo wrapper. The company says it took nearly three years to develop and treats it as its showpiece cigar.
cigars.researchNote: The Connecticut Broadleaf is in the filler, not the wrapper. The maker describes it as full bodied. Launched at InterTabac 2026.

cigars.about: A collaboration between Chateau Diadem and blender Eladio Diaz, made at his Tabacalera Diaz Cabrera next door to the Chateau Diadem factory in Santiago. It comes in one robusto extra size and is aged a year before release.
cigars.researchNote: On sale in Europe since 2024 and in the US from PCA 2026. Cigar Journal's 2024 story called it a limited edition with a Dominican corojo wrapper and five fillers; the maker and halfwheel say Ecuadorian corojo and four Dominican fillers.

cigars.about: Chateau Diadem's value line: handmade medium-filler cigars sold in bundles of 10 in three sizes. The maker describes it as an everyday smoke at a lower price than its long-filler lines.
cigars.researchNote: Medium filler, not long filler. The maker does not publish the blend, strength or the three sizes.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Esteli viso, Jalapa seco), USA (Pennsylvania viso)
cigars.about: The first line from Despot Cigars, built around four classic formats with one blend. Despot Cigars is the private label of Serbian brothers Jovan and Ugljesa Despot, rolled in Esteli, Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium to full, while Blind Man's Puff and US retailer Luxury Cigar Club call it medium. The factory is not disclosed. Blind Man's Puff lists its release date as April 2022.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Jalapa volado, Esteli viso, Jalapa viso)
cigars.about: Despot's second line, blended for aroma over strength, with two short formats and two large traditional ones. Despot Cigars is the private label of Serbian brothers Jovan and Ugljesa Despot, rolled in Esteli, Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists an all-Nicaraguan filler. US retailer Luxury Cigar Club shows the Serie J blend with Pennsylvania filler on its Serie U pages. The factory is not disclosed.
