cigars.about: Despot's third line, using an Ecuadorian rosado wrapper over Jalapa and Ometepe fillers in two 54-ring formats and two large classic shapes. Despot Cigars is the private label of Serbian brothers Jovan and Ugljesa Despot, rolled in Esteli, Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The factory is not disclosed and the maker publishes no specific tasting notes.

cigars.about: Despot's fourth and fullest line, adding Pennsylvania Broadleaf to the filler and filling in formats the earlier series lacked. Despot Cigars is the private label of Serbian brothers Jovan and Ugljesa Despot, rolled in Esteli, Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: The maker says the wrapper and binder are the same Habano 2000 from Ecuador. Its blend list names Jalapa and Condega fillers, while its longer description says Ometepe and Jalapa. The factory is not disclosed.

cigars.about: A limited edition from Despot Cigars made in honor of Cigar Lounge Libertador in Belgrade, Serbia. It uses an Ecuadorian habano claro wrapper and binder over Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is close to Serie U. The maker does not publish the size, strength or release year.

cigars.about: The first limited edition from Despot Cigars, made as a tribute to its Serie J line. It is one large 7.5 by 52 cigar made with tobacco aged at least seven years.
cigars.researchNote: One size only, 7.5 x 52. The maker says every leaf is aged at least seven years but does not publish the blend, strength or release year.

cigars.about: The core range from EGM Cigars, a Swiss-based house led by Ettore Gabriele Moraschinelli. They are Dominican puros made with Cibao Valley tobacco in Cuban-style formats such as the Laguito sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates each size: Encantos light to medium; Petit Encantos, Robustos, Blecos and Diademas medium; Bravos, Escudos, Poderosos, Tiburones and Media Coronas medium to full. It names no leaf varieties or factory. Sizes are published in millimetres.

cigars.about: EGM's first blend that is not a Dominican puro, putting an American-grown Broadleaf maduro wrapper over Cibao Valley binder and filler. It comes in three sizes and is rolled by hand in Santo Domingo.
cigars.researchNote: The maker says only American-grown Broadleaf; halfwheel identifies it as Pennsylvania Broadleaf and the factory as ABAM Cigars in Santo Domingo. The maker rates it medium to full, and halfwheel's reviewer put it closer to medium-plus. Sizes are published in millimetres.

cigars.about: The top line from EGM Cigars, a Dominican puro of aged Cibao Valley tobacco in three sizes with foot bands naming each vitola. It was unveiled in London in autumn 2025.
cigars.researchNote: An ongoing line, but the maker says it is made in very limited quantities. Sizes are published in millimetres (130 x 55, 145 x 57, 170 x 52). Praxedes is a pyramid and Paraisos has a pigtail cap.

cigars.about: A single long, thin 178 mm by 34 ring cigar from EGM that revives the old Ninfa format. It is a Dominican puro rolled by hand with Cibao Valley tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: One size only, sold in boxes of 10 and 25. The blend is seco-dominant Dominican tobacco; Cigar Journal reports two years of age and halfwheel three. It debuted in Kuwait on February 9, 2026. halfwheel names the factory; the maker does not.

cigars.about: A collaboration between EGM Cigars and entrepreneur Alexander Kraft: three pigtail-capped formats made in the Dominican Republic. The box lid carries a logo honoring Kraft's late dog.
cigars.researchNote: The maker describes Connecticut wrappers while also calling the cigars Dominican puros, and Cigar Journal lists the wrapper origin as Dominican Republic. The Robusto came first in 2023 and the two larger sizes followed in 2024.

cigars.about: A co-branded version of EGM's Bravos, made with the Tuxedo Society. It is a Dominican puro in the Laguito No. 4 format, 119 mm by 52 ring, sold in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: This is the Bravos size from EGM's Classic Collection with co-branded bands and box. The maker does not say whether it is a limited run, and does not name leaf varieties or the factory.

cigars.about: One of the first two blends from Somm, the brand of sommelier and distributor Vlada Stojanov, named as shorthand for Bordeaux. It has a San Andrés wrapper and Honduran broadleaf in the filler, and is rolled at the Cavalier Genève factory in Danlí.
cigars.researchNote: Made in small batches, and halfwheel classed the first 400-box Robusto run as a limited edition. The maker calls it medium-bodied, while halfwheel found the strength mild to medium. A 5 5/8 x 46 Corona Gorda was a limited 2024 run.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Estelí seco and viso), Honduras (Jamastran seco), Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano)
cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped companion to Somm BDX, named for the white wines of Bordeaux. All of the tobacco was aged at least three years before rolling at the same Honduran factory that makes BDX.
cigars.researchNote: The maker describes it as light to medium in body. Halfwheel also lists Jalapa tobacco in the Nicaraguan filler, where the maker lists only Estelí.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98, Criollo 99 and other Dominican leaf)
cigars.about: Somm's third blend, named for the Spanish wine region and made at Eladio Diaz's Tabacalera Díaz Cabrera. It uses a Dominican Corojo wrapper over a Sumatra binder and Dominican fillers aged three to four years.
cigars.researchNote: Soft launched in December 2023 through Luxury Cigar Club before wider release in early 2024. A 7 x 39 Lancero was a limited run of 1,000 cigars in December 2024.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (San Vicente), Peru (Pelo de Oro), BVS African hybrid (origin undisclosed)
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican, Bonao (1997 harvest, Kelner family reserve)
cigars.about: A limited edition pyramid made for Somm at Hendrik Kelner Jr.'s Kelner Boutique Factory from very old Kelner family tobaccos, including a 1997 wrapper. It came in numbered boxes of five signed by Kelner.
cigars.researchNote: Production figures differ: the maker says 3,000 cigars, halfwheel reported 300 boxes of five (1,500 cigars). The maker calls the body medium-full, while halfwheel found the strength about medium. The wrapper variety is not published.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Condega viso, Estelí seco, Jalapa seco, Jalapa viso)
cigars.about: A one-off limited edition from Somm and its first all-Nicaraguan blend, built around a 14-year-old Estelí wrapper. It was rolled in November 2024 at the Cavalier Genève factory in Honduras and named after founder Vlada Stojanov's daughter.
cigars.researchNote: About 220 bundles of five (roughly 1,100 cigars). Halfwheel rated strength just under medium and body just over medium. Unlike the original Premier Cru, it is made in Honduras, not at Kelner Boutique Factory.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Condega viso, Estelí seco, Jalapa seco, Jalapa viso)
cigars.about: The follow-up to Somm Premier Cru Petra, using the same Nicaraguan tobaccos with the wrapper and binder swapped. It was rolled in January 2025 at the Cavalier Genève factory in Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,027 cigars and sold only through Small Batch Cigar. The original Petra's 14-year-old Estelí wrapper is the binder here and its Jalapa binder is the wrapper. No strength rating or tasting notes are published.

cigars.about: The lightest of the Bandolero series from Nelson Alfonso's Selected Tobacco, also called Serie A. The maker's catalogue lists it as an all-Peruvian blend rated light to medium.
cigars.researchNote: Also called Serie A. The maker's catalogue lists Peruvian wrapper, binder and filler and rates it light to medium. Halfwheel and Neptune both describe the wrapper as Ecuadorian, and Neptune lists it as full.

cigars.about: The middle-strength Bandolero series from Selected Tobacco, also called Serie C. It pairs an Ecuadorian wrapper with a Peruvian binder and is rolled at Tabacos de Costa Rica.
cigars.researchNote: Also called Serie C. The maker rates it medium to full (the Traviesos torpedo is listed as light), while Neptune lists it as full. Halfwheel describes the filler as Dominican, Nicaraguan and undisclosed.

cigars.about: The strongest Bandolero series from Selected Tobacco, also called Serie T. It uses an Ecuadorian wrapper over a Peruvian binder with Nicaraguan ligero and seco in the filler.
cigars.researchNote: Also called Serie T. Vanidosos is a 6 x 54 pyramid. The wrapper variety is not published.

cigars.about: A medium-strength Bandolero series from Selected Tobacco with an Ecuadorian wrapper, Nicaraguan binder and Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler. The maker lists the finished cigars as aged four years.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's catalogue lists Dominican leaf in place of Nicaraguan for part of the Irónicos and Magníficos blends, and rates the small Intrépidos as light. Bandolero Premium, sold in the U.S., uses the same vitola names and tobacco origins.

cigars.about: An extra-aged Bandolero from Selected Tobacco. The cigars are rolled in Costa Rica, then aged three years in Madrid in humidors lined with five kinds of cedar.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel's launch story called it limited production, while its PCA 2025 report listed it as regular production. It shares vitola names and tobacco origins with the maker's Selección Especial series. No strength rating is published.

cigars.about: One of the core Byron lines from Nelson Alfonso's Selected Tobacco, also written Serie Siglo XIX. The cigars are rolled at Tabacos de Costa Rica and aged for years after rolling before release.
cigars.researchNote: Also written Serie Siglo XIX. The maker rates it medium to full, while Neptune describes it as medium-bodied. Aged vintage and humidor editions of the Grand Poemas and Épique Poemas are limited.

cigars.about: One of the core Byron lines from Selected Tobacco, also written Serie Siglo XX. It is rolled at Tabacos de Costa Rica and given several years of aging after rolling.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is only partly disclosed and sources differ: the maker's catalogue lists a Peruvian binder with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler, while halfwheel reported an undisclosed binder and Dominican and Peruvian filler. The maker rates it medium to full; Neptune says medium-bodied.

cigars.about: The mildest of the three Byron century lines from Selected Tobacco, also written Serie Siglo XXI. It is rolled at Tabacos de Costa Rica and the regular release is aged about four years after rolling.
cigars.researchNote: Sources differ on the wrapper: halfwheel called it Ecuadorian habano in 2018 and Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed in 2025, and earlier reports gave a Dominican binder. The maker lists the Distinguidos with a different blend (Nicaraguan wrapper) and rates it medium to full.

cigars.about: A Byron line launched in November 2022 ahead of the brand's 175th anniversary. The cigars are aged in both cedar and French oak rooms at Tabacos de Costa Rica.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's catalogue calls it Selección 1850 and rates the No. 1 and No. 2 medium and the No. 3 and No. 4 medium to full; halfwheel found the No. 2 mild in strength. The Grand Bouquet (6 x 58) and Líricos (9 1/4 x 55) figurados are sold only at events. The wrapper variety is not published.

cigars.about: A limited release of the Byron 21st Century Aristócratas given ten years of aging, more than twice the four years the regular version gets. It comes in 25-count black lacquer boxes.
cigars.researchNote: One size of the Byron 21st Century line with extra aging, not a separate blend. Halfwheel calls the wrapper Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed here but called the same line's wrapper Ecuadorian habano in 2018. Strength is the maker's rating for the regular Aristócratas.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, Mexico, Nicaragua, United States (broadleaf)
cigars.about: A value-priced line launched in 2014 under General Cigar's Foundry brand and now sold by Forged Cigar Co. It uses a Connecticut-grown Habano wrapper over an Ecuadorian Sumatra binder and a four-country filler.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers sometimes call it Chillin' Moose Habano and list the Robusto as 5 x 50; the maker's site lists 5 1/2 x 50. The Toro is sold by retailers but is not on the maker's site, and the Corona was discontinued in 2025. The factory is not published.

cigars.about: The maduro follow-up to Chillin' Moose, released in 2016 with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is a budget cigar made at STG Estelí and sold by Forged Cigar Co.
cigars.researchNote: The Toro was added in February 2025 and the Corona was discontinued in 2025. Some retailers list the Robusto as 5 x 50, and Neptune lists the country as Dominican Republic, but halfwheel reports it is made at STG Estelí in Nicaragua.

cigars.about: A large ring gauge extension of Chillin' Moose from Forged Cigar Co., launched in 2022. It is a budget Nicaraguan puro made in Estelí, with nothing smaller than a 60 ring gauge.
cigars.researchNote: Strength ratings differ: the maker's Cigar World site rates it medium, Famous Smoke says medium-full and Neptune lists full.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Bull Moose, a budget Nicaraguan puro made in Estelí in the same four large ring gauge sizes. It is sold by Forged Cigar Co. under the Chillin' Moose brand.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's Cigar World site rates it medium-full, while Famous Smoke and Neptune both call it full. It was shown at the 2023 PCA trade show and shipped that August.

cigars.filler: Colombia, Dominican Republic, Nicaragua, United States (broadleaf)
cigars.about: The Connecticut shade member of the Chillin' Moose family, launched in March 2023 and made at STG Danlí in Honduras. It is a budget six-country blend and was the first Moose cigar offered in a toro.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's Cigar World site rates it mellow, while Neptune lists it as medium. Halfwheel's review found mild strength with medium or fuller body and noticeable pepper.

cigars.about: The first League of Fat Bastards blend, made at Joya de Nicaragua and developed remotely during the pandemic by founder Adam Levine. The brand gives 40 percent of its net profits to men's mental health causes.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel describes the wrapper as Ecuadorian-grown Havana seed; Neptune lists it as an Ecuadorian maduro. Strength is Neptune's listing. It launched in three sizes; the Corona and Giggly Piggly came later.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Condega seco and ligero, Jalapa viso)
cigars.about: The second League of Fat Bastards line, a bolder San Andres-wrapped blend made at Joya de Nicaragua. Profits from the Giggly Piggly size go to mental health causes for first responders.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it full-bodied and Neptune lists it as full; Neptune's write-up also calls it full to medium.

cigars.about: A slim corona blended by Raquel and Patricia Quesada of Quesada Cigars as a tribute to women in the cigar world. It is sold in five-packs.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is secret; the Quesada sisters did not even tell the brand owner. Cigar Aficionado lists a Dominican wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler and rates it medium-full (90 points); Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.about: The first limited edition from League of Fat Bastards, a single 6 x 52 toro named for the friend who has your back. Production was limited to 5,000 cigars.
cigars.researchNote: The company did not name the factory; Neptune lists Joya de Nicaragua as the maker. The company calls it medium to full bodied, while Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Habano (milder blend) and Mexican San Andres (stronger blend)
cigars.about: A four-pack of coronas honoring first responders and the US armed forces, with two cigars each of a milder and a stronger blend. It was sold only to retailers at the 2026 PCA trade show.
cigars.researchNote: Two blends in one pack: the lighter one has a habano wrapper, the heavier one Mexican San Andres. The rest of the blend, the exact corona size and the factory were not disclosed. First run was 400 packs.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Habano 20/20 ligero, HVA ligero, Piloto Mejorado ligero)
cigars.about: A Dominican puro from the Reyes family's De Los Reyes factory, named for third-generation grower Julio Samuel Reyes Fermin. It was the last new regular Don Julio line until Sang Bleu in 2024.
cigars.researchNote: Don Julio is a brand of De Los Reyes (formerly Corporacion Cigar Export), not the tequila. The maker called it medium bodied but full in flavor; Neptune lists medium and Corona Cigar lists medium to full. The Paca is box pressed.

cigars.about: A Dominican puro with a habano-seed wrapper, made by De Los Reyes. Released in 2024, it was the first new regular Don Julio line since Punta Espada in 2014.
cigars.researchNote: Strength and flavors come from halfwheel's review of the P2 size, which started medium and built to medium-full. halfwheel reports a habano-seed wrapper; Corona Cigar lists Dominican corojo and medium strength. The P2 and Salomon are shaped, pricier sizes.

cigars.line: Year of the Dragon Limited Edition
cigars.about: A 2024 Chinese zodiac limited edition from De Los Reyes under its Don Julio brand, sold as a single 6 x 52 toro. It was limited to 800 boxes of 24 worldwide.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls the blend under the wrapper a secret and says only that it includes aged Dominican tobaccos. The maker gave no strength rating; Corona Cigar lists it as medium to full.

cigars.line: Year of the Snake Limited Edition
cigars.about: The second Chinese zodiac limited edition for De Los Reyes' Don Julio brand, a 6 x 54 toro released in April 2025. Production was 500 boxes of 24.
cigars.researchNote: No strength rating or tasting notes were published.

cigars.line: Year of the Horse Limited Edition
cigars.about: The 2026 Chinese zodiac limited edition from De Los Reyes' Don Julio brand, a 6 x 54 toro that shipped in February 2026. It is limited to 500 boxes of 24.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel describes it only as an Ecuadorian habano wrapper over Dominican tobaccos. No strength rating or tasting notes were published.

cigars.about: A San Andres maduro from Atlanta-based ATL Cigar Co., made in Esteli. The maker bills it as full bodied but smooth, strong without being harsh.
cigars.researchNote: It was reblended in 2022 when production moved to Tabacalera Pichardo, now Luciano Cigars. A 6 3/4 x 50 Elegance toro extra was added in 2023 but is not on the maker's current size list.

cigars.about: ATL Cigar Co.'s fourth release, a San Andres-wrapped Nicaraguan blend that debuted in 2021 as a single 6 x 54 toro. The name nods to Atlanta's quiet influence on music, film and culture.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium-plus in strength. A 6 1/2 x 50 Double Robusto was added in 2023 but is not on the maker's current size list.

cigars.about: ATL Cigar Co.'s tribute to the late Congressman John Lewis, taking its name from his call to get into good trouble. The maker describes it as medium in strength but full bodied, with a natural sweetness.
cigars.researchNote: The blend has changed more than once. The maker now lists a Sumatra wrapper (origin not stated); halfwheel reported a 2023 reblend with an Ecuadorian habano 2000 wrapper. It was first made at Tabacalera Hernandez, then Luciano Cigars; the maker does not name the current factory.

cigars.about: The first mild-to-medium cigar from ATL Cigar Co., named after Flannery O'Connor's first novel. It debuted in 2023 and is made in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: The fillers come from three Nicaraguan regions the maker does not name.

cigars.about: A full-strength cigar from ATL Cigar Co., released in 2026 and named for the integrated jazz club inside Paschal's Motor Hotel in Atlanta. The company rates it 4.8 out of 5 in strength.
cigars.researchNote: Also written La Carrousel-1960. Unlike the older ATL lines, it is made at Casa Y Hernandez in Esteli.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano, Criollo 98, Corojo 99, San Vicente)
cigars.about: The first blend from Avowed Cigar Co., a brand started by people behind Small Batch Cigar and made at Klaas Kelner's factory. Each size is its own blend, named for the date that blend was approved.
cigars.researchNote: Each size is blended separately: the 6.29 adds Cotui tobacco and is the gentler one, the 7.05 is more intense, and the 11.25 adds a leaf of Brazilian Cubra. The maker gives no strength rating.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano, Criollo 98, San Vicente)
cigars.about: Avowed's all-day cigar, blended by Klaas Kelner with a darker-than-usual Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. It launched in 2025 alongside The Vow.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper looks darker than a typical Connecticut but the cigar is mild-medium. The Corona Gorda, added in 2026, uses a slightly modified blend with a different priming of piloto cubano.

cigars.filler: Corojo 99, San Vicente, Piloto Cubano, Criollo 98, Pennsylvania Broadleaf
cigars.about: Avowed's third regular line, released in February 2026 for the company's first anniversary. It is the brand's first cigar with an Ecuadorian corojo wrapper and includes its first box-pressed size.
cigars.researchNote: The box-pressed robusto gets extra Pennsylvania broadleaf in the filler. Boxes hold 15 cigars, each with a different band.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano, San Vicente, Criollo 98), USA (Pennsylvania)
cigars.about: Avowed's first limited edition, built around a small supply of an Ecuadorian hybrid wrapper that has not been grown in more than a decade. It comes in one size and was limited to 2,000 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium-plus; halfwheel's reviewer found medium strength with full flavor. The wrapper is a hybrid the company calls Capa Marron, so it does not fit a standard wrapper type.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Cotui, Corojo 99, Criollo 98, Piloto Cubano, San Vicente)
cigars.about: A limited version of Avowed's The Vow 6.29 toro, released for Father's Day 2025 with higher-priming fillers and two years of age. Production was 450 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: This is a limited edition of one size of The Vow, not a separate line. On paper the blend matches the regular 6.29; the maker says the extra age makes it creamier. No strength rating was published.

cigars.about: One of the two debut lines from Domain Cigars, the company started by Esteban Disla and Daniel Lance. It is the milder of the pair, a San Andrés wrapped Nicaraguan blend made at Domain's own factory in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: Maker calls it medium intensity. Sold in nine sizes, three of them box pressed.

cigars.about: One of the two debut lines from Domain Cigars, made at the company's own factory in Estelí. It pairs an Ecuadorian habano wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler and is pitched as the bolder of the two.
cigars.researchNote: The maker gives no strength rating, only "impactful intensity". halfwheel's review found the nicotine strength a little under medium with medium-plus body, so do not promise a powerhouse.

cigars.about: Domain's third line, a Connecticut broadleaf wrapped cigar over Nicaraguan binder and ligero-heavy filler. The company says about 90 percent of the blend comes from Negentropy, and it grew out of the No7B prototype.
cigars.researchNote: Maker gives no strength rating. Cigar Coop's review put strength and body at medium rising to medium-full. A 5 x 42 Corona Heritage Cabinet size was added in 2026 for select retailers.

cigars.about: Domain's first Connecticut-seed wrapped line, released in 2026 and made at the company's factory in Estelí. The filler includes Vanguard Aegis, a corojo and criollo 98 cross that Domain says it developed.
cigars.researchNote: Maker calls it medium-bodied and gives no strength rating; halfwheel's review landed around medium. His Eminence is a belicoso with a shaggy foot.

cigars.about: A prototype blend from Domain Cigars that first went to retailers in a 2024 launch sampler and became the basis for the Entropy line. The prototype batch was about 2,000 cigars, and what was left was sold through 18 retailers in plain white Limited Factory Sample bands.
cigars.researchNote: Also written N7B. Entropy is the finished version: it uses a different broadleaf crop and one changed filler leaf. No strength rating or tasting notes were published.

cigars.about: The first line from German Engineered Cigars, a Hamburg company led by co-founders Oliver Nickels and Jan Klaas Mahler. It launched in 2016 and is made in the Dominican Republic, with sizes also labeled by their volume in cubic centimeters.
cigars.researchNote: The size lineup was reworked in 2025; older sizes such as #18, #36 and #64 differ from the current four. The maker's single rating is given as body: medium.

cigars.about: A bolder take on the RVGN line that German Engineered Cigars released in 2026 for its 10th anniversary. It is made in the Dominican Republic and was the company's first cigar with an NFC chip in the band.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not name the wrapper seed, so it is not confirmed as San Andrés. The 4 x 50 size is sold in the AKUT blister pack.

cigars.about: The second line from German Engineered Cigars, introduced in 2022. It is the mildest in the range, with a Connecticut-seed wrapper grown in Nicaragua, and is made in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: Sizes are the maker's current list; the 2022 launch sizes were different.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan-made line from German Engineered Cigars with an Ecuadorian habano oscuro wrapper, first released in late 2022. Apart from the wrapper it is all Nicaraguan tobacco.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's single rating is given as body: medium. The 2022 announcement listed the perfecto as 5 1/2 x 54; the maker now lists 5 x 54.

cigars.about: The fullest blend from German Engineered Cigars, released in 2025. It uses Mexican San Andrés for both wrapper and binder over Dominican filler and was blended by Hostos Fernández.
cigars.researchNote: At launch halfwheel also listed a Toro (6 1/4 x 52) and Gordo (6 x 60); the maker's site now shows only the two robusto sizes.

cigars.about: One of three core lines from Hermanos de Armas (HDA Cigars), a veteran-owned brand founded by Andray McCuien and Zack Van Ginkel. It has an Ecuadorian habano wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Made at Fabrica Oveja Negra until mid 2026, then moved to Rojas Cigars; the company says the blend was matched. No strength rating is published.

cigars.about: One of three core lines from Hermanos de Armas (HDA Cigars), a veteran-owned brand. It has an Ecuadorian sun grown wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, and the maker says flavor and strength build as it burns.
cigars.researchNote: Made at Fabrica Oveja Negra until mid 2026, then moved to Rojas Cigars; the company says the blend was matched. No strength rating is published.

cigars.about: The maduro in the three-line core range from Hermanos de Armas (HDA Cigars), a veteran-owned brand. It has an Ecuadorian maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, and the maker points to a touch of sweetness.
cigars.researchNote: Made at Fabrica Oveja Negra until mid 2026, then moved to Rojas Cigars; the company says the blend was matched. No strength rating is published.

cigars.about: The first limited edition from Hermanos de Armas (HDA Cigars), released in 2025 in a single robusto size. It used an Indonesian Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: A one-time 2025 release that the maker says is gone. No strength rating or tasting notes are published.

cigars.about: The 2026 limited edition from Hermanos de Armas (HDA Cigars), a 6 x 50 toro blended with Lee Marsh of Stolen Throne and made at the Rojas factory in Estelí. The name nods to U.S. surveillance aircrews.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 600 boxes of 20. The maker's page calls the 6 x 50 a robusto; halfwheel lists it as a toro. No strength rating is published.

cigars.about: The original Regius of London line from the British brand owned by Akhil Kapacee, a Nicaraguan puro made by Plasencia. It was sold in the U.K. first and reached U.S. stores in late 2011.
cigars.researchNote: Often just called Regius or Regius of London; Black Label is the band color. halfwheel found the robusto a solid medium and the corona milder; Cigar Coop had the corona at medium, rising late. The U.K. launch year is not confirmed.

cigars.about: A maduro-wrapped Regius line that the company says builds on the Black Label with an updated blend. It went into wide release in March 2018 in five sizes, sold in 25-count boxes.
cigars.researchNote: Regius did not disclose the wrapper origin, binder, filler or factory. No official strength; halfwheel's review of the corona found it just under medium.

cigars.about: The first Regius Exclusivo U.S.A., known as the red label, a Nicaraguan puro made by Plasencia. It debuted at Casa de Montecristo in Illinois in May 2014 and began shipping nationally at the end of that August.
cigars.researchNote: Described as medium bodied. Sizes disagree: halfwheel lists Pressed Perfecto 6 1/2 x 54 and Toro Extra 6 1/2 x 46, Cigar Coop lists both as 6 1/2 x 56. The Fat Perfecto tapers from 60 to 54 ring.

cigars.about: The second Regius Exclusivo U.S.A. release, a Nicaraguan puro with a white and silver band that launched in September 2014. It shares the six sizes of the red label version.
cigars.researchNote: White Label is the band; the formal name is Claro Especial Exclusivo U.S.A. It is not the Dominican-made Regius White Label from 2012. Strength and body are from Cigar Coop's review. Cigar Coop lists two sizes as 6 1/2 x 56 where halfwheel has 54 and 46 ring.

cigars.about: The third and last Regius Exclusivo U.S.A. blend, with a blue band and a dark San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco. It was released in early 2016 and is made by Plasencia.
cigars.researchNote: Billed as the strongest Regius at the time, but both halfwheel and Cigar Coop found it about medium. Cigar Coop lists the Pressed Perfecto and Toro Extra as 6 1/2 x 56; halfwheel has 6 1/2 x 54 and 6 1/2 x 46.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: The original Ave Maria blend, a Knights Templar themed cigar made by AJ Fernandez in Esteli, Nicaragua and sold mainly through large catalog retailers. It pairs an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper with Nicaraguan and Honduran tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: Holts and Cigars Direct list it as medium to full, while Neptune says medium. Each size carries a Crusades themed name rather than a standard shape name.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: The Connecticut shade version of Ave Maria, made by AJ Fernandez in Esteli with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is the mildest cigar in the Ave Maria family.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune's spec table says mild while its description and Cigars Direct both say mild to medium.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: An Ave Maria line from AJ Fernandez with a sun grown wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and fillers from Brazil, Mexico and Nicaragua. It comes in three sizes sold in boxes of 24.
cigars.researchNote: Cigars Direct and Neptune both call it full strength, but the Blind Man's Puff panel found it mild to medium. The wrapper's country is not published. An older 5.5 x 55 size of the original Ave Maria blend is also called The Lionheart, so check the band.

cigars.about: An Ave Maria line sold as a single 6 x 54 toro, individually packaged and sold ten to a box. It uses a sun grown Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Cigars Direct sells it as a Toro Tubo while Neptune describes individual coffins. The wrapper's country and the factory are not published for this line, though Ave Maria as a brand is made by AJ Fernandez.

cigars.about: The flagship of the relaunched Los Statos Deluxe brand from Forged Cigar Co., reblended in 2022 by Matt Booth and Justin Andrews. It is made in Honduras with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The brand's full name is Los Statos Deluxe, so Deluxe is not a separate line. It is an old General Cigar brand, named after a discontinued Cuban marca, that was fully revamped in 2022. The maker calls it medium-plus.

cigars.filler: Honduras (Jamastran, La Entrada), Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano)
cigars.about: The Connecticut Broadleaf wrapped version of Los Statos Deluxe, added a year after the 2022 relaunch and also made at STG's factory in Danli, Honduras. The maker describes it as a full-bodied blend.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is the maker's word, full-bodied. The maker does not give a separate strength rating.

cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua
cigars.about: The mildest Los Statos Deluxe blend, created by Matt Booth and Justin Andrews and rolled at Joya de Nicaragua. It puts an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over a Nicaraguan habano binder with Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania broadleaf fillers.
cigars.researchNote: Made in Nicaragua, unlike the Honduran-made core and Maduro lines. The maker lists the Churchill as 7 x 49 while halfwheel lists 7 x 48. Strength and body are from halfwheel's review.

cigars.about: A one-size limited release made with William Ventura in the Dominican Republic for the Los Statos Deluxe brand. It shipped in March 2024 in a run of 3,000 boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 3,000 boxes of 10, and the press release said the blend would be retired after this run. Matt Booth described it as medium to medium-plus. Halfwheel calls the shape a robusto extra while Neptune lists it as a figurado.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, Nicaragua, plus Peru and USA in some sizes
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican (Cotui) on the Favoritos and Short Robusto; Cuban-seed Brazilian on the Robusto Imperial and Toro Magno
cigars.about: The red-banded core line from Hendrik Kelner Jr., made at his Kelner Boutique Factory in the Dominican Republic. It debuted in 2013, and each of the four sizes is its own blend.
cigars.researchNote: The sizes are not the same blend: two use a Dominican wrapper and two a Brazilian one, and the fillers change from size to size. Halfwheel also calls the line Clasico and has listed the Robusto Imperial as both 5 x 51 and 5 x 52. Casdagli has distributed the brand in the U.S. since 2023.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (HVA, San Vicente, Kelner Family Reserve Habano), Nicaragua (Condega Ligero)
cigars.about: A single toro that Hendrik Kelner Jr. blended in 2017 to honor his father, longtime Davidoff blender Hendrik "Henke" Kelner. It leans on tobaccos from the Kelner family's Dominican farms.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel's 2017 and 2024 pieces give a Dominican Cotui wrapper, but its 2023 article says Ecuadorian corojo. The ring gauge is listed as both 51 and 52. Neptune sells it as La Familia Henkie.

cigars.about: A 4 x 46 follow-up to the Henkie released in 2024, with its own blend built around the smaller cigars Hendrik "Henke" Kelner smokes today. It is made at the Kelner Boutique Factory.
cigars.researchNote: It is a different blend from the Henkie toro, not just a smaller size. Halfwheel's review found the strength mild with medium body, while Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98, Habano), Peru (Pelo de Oro)
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Corojo (Dominican per halfwheel in 2016 and 2018, Ecuadorian per halfwheel in 2023)
cigars.about: A single-size toro from Hendrik Kelner Jr. that began in 2016 as a 300 box limited edition and became a regular production cigar in 2018. It keeps the Limited Edition name even though it is now ongoing.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel's own reports differ: the wrapper is Dominican corojo in 2016 and 2018 but Ecuadorian corojo in 2023, the size is 6 x 54 or 6 x 55, and older reports add Nicaraguan filler. Its 2016 review found the strength mild, building to about medium.

cigars.about: The debut cigar from Supreme Tobacco, a Haitian grower that rolls its own brand in Haiti. It uses Haitian binder and filler under a sun grown habano wrapper and launched at the 2021 PCA show.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's site says the wrapper is Ecuadorian Habano, while halfwheel reported a Dominican-grown sun grown habano at the 2021 launch. It launched simply as Bohekio. The name is pronounced bo-hay-kee-oh.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Bohekio from Haiti's Supreme Tobacco, with an Ecuadorian Habano maduro wrapper over Haitian binder and filler. The maker describes it as medium to full bodied.
cigars.researchNote: The 6 x 60 Double Toro is sold in bundles only.

cigars.about: A line from Haiti's Supreme Tobacco that the maker positions as an everyday smoke. It uses a sun grown Ecuadorian habano wrapper over Haitian binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not publish a strength or a release year for this line.

cigars.about: A second, value-priced blend from Supreme Tobacco sold in bundles of 20. It pairs a habano wrapper with a Connecticut Broadleaf binder and Dominican and Brazilian fillers.
cigars.researchNote: Details come from Neptune only, and the line is not shown on the maker's site. Neptune lists it as made in the Dominican Republic, which differs from the Haitian-made Bohekio lines, and the blend has no Haitian tobacco.

cigars.about: The original cigar from the partnership between Scandinavian Tobacco Group and the Buffalo Trace Distillery, launched in 2021 through Cigars International and Meier & Dutch. It is made at General Cigar Dominicana and sold in glass tubes.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel reported at launch that it is neither infused nor aged in bourbon barrels, though some retailers describe barrel aging. Retailers disagree on strength: Cigars Direct says medium, Corona Cigar says medium to full, and Neptune says full.

cigars.binder: Brazil (Arapiraca, aged six months in bourbon barrels)
cigars.about: A Buffalo Trace line whose binder spends six months in used Buffalo Trace bourbon barrels. It started with the Special F figurado in 2022 and grew into a three-shape series in 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Same blend components as the original Buffalo Trace, but with the barrel-aged binder. The Special Selection name arrived in July 2026 when the Special L and Special S joined the 2022 Special F. Retailers list it as medium to full, while halfwheel's Special F review found it about medium.

cigars.binder: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98, aged in Buffalo Trace barrels)
cigars.about: A single 6 x 50 toro from Scandinavian Tobacco Group and Buffalo Trace Distillery, with a Dominican binder aged in Buffalo Trace barrels. It shipped in November 2025 in barrel-styled boxes of 10 that include a branded coin.
cigars.researchNote: The number made has not been disclosed, and the factory is not named. It is a new blend, not the original Buffalo Trace recipe. Halfwheel's review put the strength at medium-plus and did not find barrel flavors.

cigars.binder: Honduras or Nicaragua, depending on the blend
cigars.filler: Nicaragua, Honduras, Dominican Republic, Panama, depending on the blend
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Varies by blend: Ecuadorian Habano, Ecuadorian Sumatra, Honduran Corojo, Ecuadorian Sun Grown, and a Honduran Corojo and Maduro barber pole
cigars.about: A 25-cigar set from Scandinavian Tobacco Group and Sazerac with five different blends, each made to pair with one whiskey in Buffalo Trace's Prohibition Collection Series #2. It was limited to 750 numbered boxes priced at $500.
cigars.researchNote: This is a sampler of five blends, five cigars each: Old Fashioned Mountain Corn, Anderson's Belle, Silver Wedding, V.O.P. and Mirror Brook. STG says they range from medium to medium-full. They are made in Honduras at a factory STG has not named.

cigars.about: The original Cibao line from Jose "Jochy" Blanco of Tabacalera Palma, named for the Dominican valley where its binder and filler are grown. It is a mellow, budget-priced Dominican cigar with a Connecticut shade wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Mike's does not say where the Connecticut shade wrapper is grown; Neptune lists Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade for the brand. halfwheel dates the brand to 1985, Neptune to 1986. Neptune also sells a Cibao Cibaitos cigarillo (4 1/4 x 32).

cigars.about: The Connecticut shade version of the Cibao Seleccion Especial, the 2019 relaunch of Jochy Blanco's Cibao brand in the US through Smoke Miami. It uses Dominican binder and filler grown by Blanco and is made at his Tabacalera Palma.
cigars.researchNote: The company called it medium-bodied at launch. halfwheel does not give the wrapper's country; Neptune's Cibao page lists Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade. Launched in 2019, and current availability is unclear.

cigars.about: The Ecuadorian habano version of the Cibao Seleccion Especial, the 2019 relaunch of Jochy Blanco's Cibao brand in the US through Smoke Miami. It uses Dominican binder and filler grown by Blanco and is made at his Tabacalera Palma.
cigars.researchNote: The company called it medium-bodied at launch. Launched in 2019, and current availability is unclear.

cigars.about: The Mexican San Andres maduro version of the Cibao Seleccion Especial, the 2019 relaunch of Jochy Blanco's Cibao brand in the US through Smoke Miami. It uses Dominican binder and filler grown by Blanco and is made at his Tabacalera Palma.
cigars.researchNote: The company called it medium-to-full bodied at launch, the fullest of the three. Launched in 2019, and current availability is unclear.

cigars.about: One of the original blends from the late Henry "Don Kiki" Berger, now made by Karen Berger's company in Esteli. Today it is sold as a short 4 1/2 x 54 figurado with binder and filler from the family's Nicaraguan farm.
cigars.researchNote: The maker only says the wrapper is Ecuadorian; Neptune calls it Ecuadorian Criollo over a Corojo binder. Neptune rates the strength Full and describes the body as medium to full. A barber pole version (maduro and Connecticut wrappers, same size) was added in 2023.

cigars.about: A full-bodied Nicaraguan puro with a maduro wrapper, blended by the late Kiki Berger and made in Esteli by Karen Berger's company.
cigars.researchNote: The El Gordo (7 x 70) also comes in a barber pole version.

cigars.about: A maduro-wrapped blend from Karen Berger's Esteli Cigar Factory, sold under the Don Kiki name in three large ring gauge sizes. The maker describes it as medium-full and smooth.
cigars.researchNote: The maker does not say where the maduro wrapper is grown or name the binder. It describes the filler as all from Esteli.

cigars.about: A full-bodied Nicaraguan puro with a maduro wrapper and a pigtail cap, sold under the Don Kiki name.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune is the only source and gives no sizes. The maker's site no longer lists a Black Label and Neptune has no cigars for sale under it, so treat it as discontinued.

cigars.about: The original La Gianna Havana, first made in 1994 for David Garofalo of Two Guys Smoke Shop to mark the birth of his daughter Gianna. It is a mild Honduran cigar with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper, sold by his United Cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists a US Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper and Nicaraguan origin. The maker says Ecuadorian Connecticut, made in Danli, Honduras, and halfwheel agrees on a Connecticut shade wrapper and the Honduran factory.

cigars.about: The maduro version of United Cigars' La Gianna Havana, with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over Honduran binder and filler. It is a medium-bodied cigar made in Danli, Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists it as made in Nicaragua. The maker and halfwheel say Danli, Honduras.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Connecticut with a sweetened cap
cigars.about: The sweet-tipped version of La Gianna Havana from United Cigars, with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper and a sweetened cap. It first appeared in 2001, left the market, and came back in 2021.
cigars.researchNote: The cap is sweetened and carries a thin strip of darker San Andres leaf. The maker calls it medium-bodied; Cigar Coop calls it mild to medium. The maker's page lists the filler simply as Honduran, while halfwheel and Cigar Coop include Dominican Criollo 98.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Connecticut and Mexican San Andrés (barber pole)
cigars.about: A limited barber pole cigar released in 2024 for the 30th anniversary of La Gianna Havana, twisting the Connecticut wrapper of the Natural with the San Andres wrapper of the Maduro. It comes in one 6 x 54 toro in gold boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrappers in a barber pole, so no single wrapper category fits. The blend table on the maker's page lists only an Ecuador Connecticut wrapper with Honduran binder and filler, which conflicts with its own text and with halfwheel. United did not say how many boxes were made.

cigars.about: A chocolate-flavored cigar from Miami Beach Sweets, a flavored brand distributed by Nick Fusco's El Mago Cigars. It is made in Esteli, Nicaragua, in a single tubed 6 x 44 corona.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored (infused) cigar. Chocolate is one of four flavors that share the same blend and size. The sources do not say where the Habano wrapper or Corojo binder are grown.

cigars.about: A cognac-flavored cigar from Miami Beach Sweets, a flavored brand distributed by Nick Fusco's El Mago Cigars. It is made in Esteli, Nicaragua, in a single tubed 6 x 44 corona.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored (infused) cigar. Cognac is one of four flavors that share the same blend and size. The sources do not say where the Habano wrapper or Corojo binder are grown.

cigars.about: A grape-flavored cigar from Miami Beach Sweets, a flavored brand distributed by Nick Fusco's El Mago Cigars. It is made in Esteli, Nicaragua, in a single tubed 6 x 44 corona.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored (infused) cigar. Grape is one of four flavors that share the same blend and size. The sources do not say where the Habano wrapper or Corojo binder are grown.

cigars.about: A vanilla-flavored cigar from Miami Beach Sweets, a flavored brand distributed by Nick Fusco's El Mago Cigars. It is made in Esteli, Nicaragua, in a single tubed 6 x 44 corona.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored (infused) cigar. Vanilla is one of four flavors that share the same blend and size. The sources do not say where the Habano wrapper or Corojo binder are grown.

cigars.about: The cigar Broncano Cigar Co. came to market with: a 6 x 52 toro rolled at La Aurora in March 2004 and aged about 20 years before release. Broncano was founded in 2022 by Marine Corps veteran Martin Smith.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as The Vintage Toro, one size only. The maker says it was produced at La Aurora in March 2004 and aged 20 years. Whiskey Network named it its 2024 Cigar of the Year.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98 seco, Corojo), USA (Broadleaf ligero), Africa (seco)
cigars.about: Part of Broncano's Classic line, a 6 x 52 toro made at Hendrik Kelner Jr.'s Kelner Boutique Factory in the Dominican Republic. It pairs an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper with a Dominican binder and a four-part filler blend.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as The Royal Blue Toro, one size only. It went nationwide in February 2025 after a soft launch at select retailers. The maker does not publish a strength for this blend.

cigars.about: Part of Broncano's Classic line, a 6 x 50 toro with a Mexican San Andres wrapper over an Ecuadorian Habano binder and Dominican filler. The maker rates it medium to full.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as The Silver Toro, one size only. Broncano has not disclosed the factory or country where it is made. It went nationwide in February 2025 after a soft launch at select retailers.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98, Piloto Cubano), Mexico (San Andrés Morron), USA (Broadleaf)
cigars.about: The third cigar in Broncano's Classic line, a 6 x 52 toro made at Kelner Boutique Factory in the Dominican Republic. It uses an HVA Ecuador wrapper over a Dominican San Vicente binder and a multi-country filler.
cigars.researchNote: Sold as The Rubí Toro, one size only. The maker lists the wrapper as HVA Ecuador without explaining the term; HVA is a Habano-seed variety, so it is filed under Habano. The maker does not publish a strength for this blend.

cigars.about: The first cigar from ChiMolly, a young brand built around Chinese art and culture. It is a habano-wrapped blend rolled at Mi Havana in Esteli and wears a red band.
cigars.researchNote: The 7 x 52 Double Corona was added in April 2026 as a PCA show exclusive in boxes of 10. Flavor words come from halfwheel's review of that size.

cigars.about: ChiMolly's second line, a step up in strength from Pangu. It pairs an Ecuadorian corojo wrapper with a San Andres binder and wears a blue band.
ChiMolly's third blend and its broadleaf-wrapped option, shown at the 2025 PCA show. It comes in the same two sizes as Pangu and Dynasty.
cigars.researchNote: ChiMolly does not publish a strength for this line.

cigars.about: A single-size collaboration between ChiMolly and Fox Cigar, a Phoenix retailer. It is a 6 x 52 toro that ChiMolly calls a Robusto E.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 500 boxes of 20, released December 2025. Sold as a Fox Cigar exclusive, though Fox also wholesales it to other shops. Fox Cigar lists it as medium strength.

cigars.about: The original Pier 28 blend from Tim Wong, a longtime West Coast cigar sales rep, made at Espinosa's La Zona factory in Esteli. It started as a regional release for shops in his West Coast territory.
cigars.researchNote: The four launch sizes were published by dimension only, without vitola names. The Lancero was announced in 2016 but did not ship widely until 2019.

cigars.about: The second Pier 28 line from Tim Wong, a San Andrés maduro over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is made at Espinosa's La Zona factory in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: A small batch reached a few stores in August 2016 ahead of FDA rules, in different sizes. The sizes listed are from the 2017 wide release.

cigars.about: A dark Brazilian-wrapped Pier 28 line from Tim Wong, made at La Zona in Esteli. Its black and orange band is a nod to the San Francisco Giants.
cigars.researchNote: Flavor words come from halfwheel's review of the Perfecto, which found the strength climbing to full by the end.

cigars.about: Tim Wong's Connecticut-wrapped Pier 28, blended with viso and seco leaf and no ligero to sit between old-style and newer, fuller Connecticuts. Its teal band nods to the San Jose Sharks.
cigars.researchNote: A small batch reached stores in 2016 ahead of FDA rules; that version was announced with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. The national release came in fall 2019.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98 Ligero), Ecuador (Habano 2000 Viso), USA (Pennsylvania Broadleaf Viso, Pennsylvania Ligero)
cigars.about: The flagship maduro from Tradecraft Cigars, the brand started by Gary and Robert Blumenthal of Tinder Box International. It is blended with Wiber Ventura in the Dominican Republic and named for the Roman short sword.
cigars.researchNote: Maker calls the profile full. The 5 1/2 x 52 Belicoso is a limited size (150 boxes of 12, 2026). The Box Press has a 109-style belicoso head and joined in August 2026.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98 Seco, Corojo Ligero), Ecuador (Habano 2000 Ligero), USA (Pennsylvania Ligero)
cigars.about: Tradecraft's medium-bodied habano, made at Tabacalera William Ventura in Tamboril. The name refers to Project Azorian, the CIA's 1974 recovery of a sunken Soviet submarine.
cigars.researchNote: The 5 1/2 x 46 Corona Gorda is a limited size (150 boxes of 12, 2026). The maker lists Pennsylvania ligero in the filler; halfwheel describes that leaf as Pennsylvania broadleaf.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98 Seco, Corojo Seco), Ecuador (Habano 2000 Viso), Nicaragua (Jalapa)
cigars.about: Tradecraft's Connecticut-wrapped line, a mild to medium toro blended with Wiber Ventura in the Dominican Republic. It comes in one size.
cigars.researchNote: Announced with the brand in October 2025 but did not ship until late January 2026. One size only so far. The maker's filler list also names Connecticut leaf alongside the Habano 2000.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Olor Viso), Nicaragua (Condega Viso, Jalapa Viso), USA (Connecticut Broadleaf Viso)
cigars.about: Tradecraft's fourth core line, a full-bodied Sumatra-wrapped cigar with an all-viso filler. It is made by Hostos Fernandez Quesada at Tabacalera La Isla in Santiago and named for the Japanese word for ninja.
cigars.researchNote: Announced October 2026. It launched first through Luxury Cigar Club, with other retailers to follow in December 2026. Unlike the other Tradecraft lines, it is not made at William Ventura.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Drew Estate's budget Chateau Real. The original was discontinued along with the rest of the line, and a San Andrés-wrapped Toro now appears at Famous Smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Status is unclear: halfwheel said in August 2024 the Maduro was still discontinued, but Famous Smoke now lists a new San Andrés maduro Toro. Specs here are from that Famous listing; binder and filler are not published.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A Miami Cigar & Co. line inspired by Nestor Miranda's safari trips, with sizes named in Swahili after African animals. The current version is blended and made by AJ Fernandez in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: The original Africa line dates to the mid-2000s; the current AJ Fernandez blend shipped in November 2019. Neptune lists it as full, but halfwheel's review found it closer to medium-plus with little nicotine kick. A fifth size, Kudu (4 x 44), is no longer on the maker's site.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98, Olor), Nicaragua, USA (Pennsylvania Broadleaf)
cigars.about: A value-priced Dominican-made Connecticut shade cigar from Miami Cigar & Co., introduced alongside the Don Lino Maduro in 2021.
cigars.researchNote: Factory is undisclosed: Neptune lists La Aurora, but halfwheel was told it is not made there. halfwheel's review rated the strength mild-medium. It is no longer on Miami Cigar's site and Neptune marks most sizes discontinued, so it may be phased out.

cigars.about: A value-priced Dominican-made cigar from Miami Cigar & Co. with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper, introduced alongside the Don Lino Connecticut in 2021.
cigars.researchNote: Factory is undisclosed: Neptune lists La Aurora, but halfwheel was told the 2021 Don Linos are not made there. It is no longer on Miami Cigar's site and Neptune marks sizes discontinued, so it may be phased out.

cigars.about: A mild, honey-flavored Dominican cigar with an Indonesian wrapper. Havana Honeys is a Scandinavian Tobacco Group brand.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored cigar. Blend details come from one retailer, Neptune. STG moved the brand from General Cigar to Forged Cigar Co. in February 2026.

cigars.about: A mild, rum-flavored Dominican cigar with an Indonesian wrapper. Havana Honeys is a Scandinavian Tobacco Group brand.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored cigar. Blend details come from one retailer, Neptune. STG moved the brand from General Cigar to Forged Cigar Co. in February 2026.

cigars.about: A mild, vanilla-flavored Dominican cigar with an Indonesian wrapper. Havana Honeys is a Scandinavian Tobacco Group brand.
cigars.researchNote: Flavored cigar. Blend details come from one retailer, Neptune. STG moved the brand from General Cigar to Forged Cigar Co. in February 2026.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: The original Nicaraguan puro from Artesano del Tobacco, the company of former Cigar Inn owners Billy and Gus Fakih. It is made by AJ Fernandez in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: Cigar Dojo rates it medium-full in strength and full in body; Neptune lists it as full. The Club 500 is box-pressed.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped version of Viva La Vida from Artesano del Tobacco, made by AJ Fernandez. It pairs an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper with the Nicaraguan core of the original and is more peppery than most Connecticuts.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's page lists the Churchill as 6 x 54, but halfwheel and Neptune both give 7 x 54. A 7 x 38 Lancero has been announced. Neptune lists it as medium; halfwheel's reviews found the strength mild to mild-medium.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A release marking five years of Viva La Vida from Artesano del Tobacco. It keeps the original Nicaraguan binder and filler under a Habano-seed maduro wrapper grown in Connecticut, in two box-pressed shapes.
cigars.researchNote: Regular production despite the anniversary name. The maker lists the Club 500 Sabroso as 5.25 x 58; halfwheel and Neptune list it as 5 1/4 x 56. Neptune labels it full, but halfwheel's review found the strength medium to medium-full. The maker gives no word for it.

cigars.about: A budget Dominican cigar from Jochy Blanco's Indian Head brand family, made at Tabacalera Palma. The Connecticut is the mildest of the three Cuban Aristocrat blends.
cigars.researchNote: No maker page found; the blend is from Neptune. Mike's Cigars lists all-Dominican tobacco and medium to full strength in its spec box while describing it as mellow to medium. Neptune says the brand dates to 2007.

cigars.about: A budget Dominican cigar from Jochy Blanco's Indian Head brand family, made at Tabacalera Palma. The Habano is the medium-bodied blend of the three Cuban Aristocrat versions.
cigars.researchNote: No maker page found; the blend is from Neptune. Mike's Cigars lists all-Dominican tobacco and medium to full strength. Neptune says the brand dates to 2007.

cigars.about: A budget Dominican cigar from Jochy Blanco's Indian Head brand family, made at Tabacalera Palma. The Maduro is the strongest of the three Cuban Aristocrat blends.
cigars.researchNote: No maker page found. Neptune's brand page names a Mexican San Andrés wrapper, while its spec box says only Maduro and Mike's Cigars lists a Dominican wrapper. Neptune rates it full; Mike's says medium to full.

cigars.about: The first cigar from Fortis Cigar Company, on the market since 2023 and made with AJ Fernandez in Estelí. It uses a San Andrés maduro wrapper the maker says is aged five years over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates the Toro medium and the Robusto medium-full. Neptune calls the 6 x 56 a Toro Gordo and says the filler is Corojo 99, Criollo 98 and ligero from AJ Fernandez's farms.

cigars.about: The Ecuadorian Habano-wrapped version of the Fortis Gran Reserva, made with AJ Fernandez in Estelí over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in one size. Neptune calls the 6 x 56 a Toro Gordo.

cigars.about: The Connecticut shade version of the Fortis Gran Reserva, made with AJ Fernandez in Estelí. It is the mildest of the three Gran Reserva blends.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it mild-medium and lists a Dominican Piloto and Nicaraguan binder; Neptune rates it mild and lists a Nicaraguan binder only. Sold in one size, which Neptune calls a Toro Gordo.

cigars.about: A collaboration between Jochy Blanco of Tabacalera Palma and retailer Aaron Saide of Sans Pareil. It is built around an Ecuadorian Habano rosado wrapper over Dominican tobaccos grown mostly by Blanco.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune spells the line Perfection. The filler includes seco leaves aged five and six years. It was quietly on sale from about 2016 and formally shown at the 2017 trade show.

cigars.about: A box-pressed line from Jochy Blanco of Tabacalera Palma and Aaron Saide of Sans Pareil. It uses a dark Brazilian Cubra wrapper over Dominican Piloto and Criollo 98 grown by Blanco.
cigars.researchNote: Sizes are numbered rather than named. halfwheel gives the No. 5 as 5 1/2 x 55; Neptune lists it as 5 5/8 x 55. It was quietly on sale from about 2016 and formally shown at the 2017 trade show.

cigars.about: The first Connecticut-wrapped La Instructora, made at Tabacalera Palma with a US-grown Connecticut shade wrapper over aged Dominican binder and filler from Jochy Blanco. The blend has no ligero.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists it as medium; brand owner Aaron Saide describes it as smooth and on the milder side. Production is ongoing but limited in quantity.

cigars.about: A value-priced, sweet-tipped long-filler cigar from Jochy Blanco's La Galera and Indianhead company, made at Tabacalera Palma. The cap is sweetened but the tobacco is not infused.
cigars.researchNote: The Rough Rider Sweets name dates to about 2001; this version launched in May 2016. halfwheel and Mike's Cigars call it mild, while Neptune's spec lists medium. Sources name the Dominican binder variously as Olor or Piloto Cubano.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Rough Rider Sweets, with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper and binder over Dominican filler and a sweetened cap. It is made at Tabacalera Palma for Jochy Blanco's La Galera and Indianhead company.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers disagree on strength: Mike's Cigars lists mild to medium, Neptune lists medium. The Gordo is listed by Mike's only.

cigars.about: A green candela-wrapped addition to La Galera's value-priced Rough Rider brand, introduced at PCA 2025. It uses a Dominican candela wrapper over a Mexican binder with Cameroon and Dominican fillers.
cigars.researchNote: halfwheel calls it Rough Rider Candela; retailers list it as Rough Rider Sweets Candela. Strength is from Neptune only.

cigars.about: The original value-priced Villa Zamorano from Maya Selva Cigars, handmade in Honduras and sold mostly in bundles. It is known as an inexpensive everyday smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel calls the wrapper Sumatra without saying where it is grown; Neptune's spec table lists a Honduran wrapper. A 2014 halfwheel report gave a different blend with a Brazilian Mata Fina binder, so the recipe has changed over time.

cigars.about: A step up from the original Villa Zamorano, made by Maya Selva Cigars in Danli with a habano wrapper from the company's own Santa Eulalia farm. It comes in boxes rather than bundles.
cigars.researchNote: Now also sold as VZ Reserva. Halfwheel describes it as a Honduran puro, while Neptune lists Nicaraguan and Honduran filler. It reached Europe in late 2016 and the U.S. in 2018.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Maya Selva Cigars
cigars.about: An all-Honduran blend from Maya Selva Cigars named for Danli, the cigar-making capital of Honduras. It is the third Villa Zamorano line, after the Clasica and Reserva.
cigars.researchNote: The Carmelita wrapper is a variety grown for Maya Selva and fits no standard wrapper category. Neptune lists medium strength; halfwheel's reviewer found it mild to just under medium. The Corto 46 perfecto was added in Europe in July 2026 with no U.S. date yet.

cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped toro made in Nicaragua by Gurkha in partnership with the Volition America apparel brand. It is one of three blends in a line that raises money for Folds of Honor scholarships.
cigars.researchNote: Made by Gurkha, which has not said where the wrapper is grown or which factory makes it. Neptune lists an Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper and names Tabacalera Las Villas as the manufacturer. Sold in boxes of 13, with 13 percent of revenue going to Folds of Honor.

cigars.about: A habano-wrapped toro made in Nicaragua by Gurkha in partnership with the Volition America apparel brand. It is one of three blends in a line that raises money for Folds of Honor scholarships.
cigars.researchNote: Made by Gurkha, which has not said where the wrapper is grown or which factory makes it. Neptune names Tabacalera Las Villas as the manufacturer. Sold in boxes of 13, with 13 percent of revenue going to Folds of Honor.

cigars.about: A maduro-wrapped toro made in Nicaragua by Gurkha in partnership with the Volition America apparel brand. It is one of three blends in a line that raises money for Folds of Honor scholarships.
cigars.researchNote: Made by Gurkha; wrapper origin and factory are undisclosed, though Neptune names Tabacalera Las Villas as the manufacturer. Medium strength is Neptune's rating; the maker only calls it bold and rich. Boxes of 13, with 13 percent of revenue going to Folds of Honor.

cigars.about: A Connecticut shade cigar from Tony Bellatto's company that began as a private blend of Dominican cigar maker William Ventura. The Edition name marks Gene Bellatto's 50 years in the cigar business.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are undisclosed; William Ventura has not told even Bellatto. Strength is Smokingpipes' rating of 3 out of 5; there is no maker rating. It was shown in 2022 but did not ship until September 2023 because of the Tabacalera William Ventura fire.

cigars.about: A dark Brazilian-wrapped cigar from Bellatto Premium Cigars that started as William Ventura's private blend for friends and family. It is meant to recall old-school Dominican cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are undisclosed. Shown in 2022 but not shipped until September 2023 after the Tabacalera William Ventura fire moved production to the family's El Maestro factory. Strength and flavors are from halfwheel's review; there is no maker rating.

cigars.about: The first line released under the Bellatto Premium Cigars name, built by Tony Bellatto as an affordable everyday cigar. Every size launched at under $10.
cigars.researchNote: No maker strength rating is published. Halfwheel's reviewer found it mild to medium in strength with medium body. Tabacalera William Ventura burned in September 2022 and many Bellatto lines moved to the family's El Maestro factory.

cigars.about: A house cigar made for the BLEND Bar with Davidoff Cigars lounges by Klaas Kelner's Kelner Cigars factory in Santiago, Dominican Republic. It launched in August 2024 in four sizes, in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Full name is BLEND Dominicano La Familia 2023 Edition. Limited to 20,000 cigars (2,000 boxes of 10). The lounge's announcement calls it medium-bodied and says the tobaccos were aged at least three years.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (San Vicente Mejorado seco, San Vicente visus, Piloto visus, Piloto seco, Yamasá visus)
cigars.about: A very large salomones made by Davidoff exclusively for the BLEND Bar lounges. It was developed over five years and comes in red lacquered boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,000 boxes of 10 and sold only at BLEND Bar locations. Launched at $95 a cigar; the lounge's site now lists it at $124.99. The 702 wrapper comes from a growing region Davidoff keeps to itself.

cigars.line: 10 Year Anniversary Davidoff BLEND Exclusive Edition
cigars.about: A Davidoff toro made to mark ten years of BLEND's Indianapolis lounge. It is sold in boxes of 10 through the lounge.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 1,000 boxes of 10 at $599 a box. Cigar Dojo reports a Dominican wrapper, Ecuadorian binder and five Dominican fillers aged at least five years; the lounge's own page does not break the blend out. No strength rating is published.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98, HVA, Piloto Cubano), Nicaragua (Jalapa)
cigars.about: The debut blend from Ceniza Fina, the brand started by Sam and Rosie Lopez of Fine Ash Cigars in Glendale, Arizona. It is blended by Hostos Fernandez Quesada and made in Santiago, Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Ceniza Fina means fine ash in Spanish. Only the Robusto Gordo is box-pressed in this blend.

cigars.about: The second Ceniza Fina blend, a mellow box-pressed Connecticut made at Tabacalera La Isla for the owners of Fine Ash Cigars in Arizona. It launched at the 2025 PCA trade show.
cigars.researchNote: All four sizes are box-pressed. Early Corona cellophane and boxes were mislabeled 5 x 42; the cigar is 5 1/2 x 48.

cigars.about: The third Ceniza Fina blend and the strongest of the three, a box-pressed Connecticut broadleaf made at Tabacalera La Isla in Santiago. It began shipping in July 2026.
cigars.researchNote: Sold only in box-pressed sizes. The maker calls it the brand's richest and darkest cigar so far.

cigars.about: The first cigar from Civil Pleasures, a New York City brand started by four friends. It is a box-pressed robusto made by Joya de Nicaragua with five-year-old filler.
cigars.researchNote: Launched at $30 a cigar; the brand's site now lists singles at $25.

cigars.about: A boxed cigar from New York brand Civil Pleasures, sold on its site alongside the CP1.
cigars.researchNote: Civil Pleasures has not published the blend, size or factory. The product page text is the CP1 description reused, so do not quote those details for Sport!. Listed at $149.99 a box.

cigars.line: Zaidi's NYC x Civil Pleasures Classic Cigar
cigars.about: A collaboration cigar between Civil Pleasures and Zaidi's NYC, sold in packs of three on the Civil Pleasures site.
cigars.researchNote: The blend, size and factory are not published. The product page text is the CP1 description reused, so do not quote those details for this cigar. Listed at $30 for a pack of three.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro from photographer Edgar Hoill, released in 2013 through Christian Eiroa's Fabricas Unidas and CLE. It came in perfecto and shaggy-foot shapes wrapped in Hoill's artwork.
cigars.researchNote: Not the same cigar as the 2012 Room101 OSOK. The maduro shade, full strength and size measurements come from Neptune's listing; halfwheel only calls it a Nicaraguan puro from an undisclosed factory and gave different pre-release dimensions. A 4 x 44 Cabroncito was added in 2014.

cigars.about: A Mexican puro from Edgar Hoill made entirely of San Andrés tobacco at the Turrent family's Casa Turrent factory. It is one of very few cigars using the leaf for wrapper, binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Strength and flavors are from halfwheel's review, which called it an earth bomb. A small 4 x 44 Cabronsito was added in 2019 as a limited release sold to only 50 retailers.

cigars.line: Los Tejanos by OSOK x Rojas
cigars.about: A joint line from Edgar Hoill of OSOK and Noel Rojas of Rojas Cigars, named for Texans of Mexican descent. It pairs a Mexican wrapper with Nicaraguan tobacco from the Somoto Valley.
cigars.researchNote: Noel Rojas calls it medium-bodied; halfwheel's review found it slightly stronger than medium. At launch the Lancero was rolled at Rojas's shop in Richardson, Texas, and the other sizes at Tabacalera Flor de San Luis. Rojas opened his own Esteli factory in 2021, so current production may differ.

cigars.about: The first house blend from LA Cigar Collective, a cigar shop in Metairie, Louisiana, near New Orleans, made for it by Quesada in the Dominican Republic. The name means Chosen Father and it is a tribute to the blender's late mentor.
cigars.researchNote: A shop exclusive sold in singles and bundles of 10. The shop describes it as light to medium bodied with a Cuban-style profile. Part of each sale goes to Bridge House/Grace House in New Orleans.

cigars.about: The second house blend from LA Cigar Collective, made at Tabacalera La Isla in the Dominican Republic. It is pronounced Gree Gree and is named for a New Orleans Voodoo charm.
cigars.researchNote: A shop exclusive. The shop does not publish a strength or tasting notes. Its page gives the Lonsdale as 6.5 x 43 in the size picker and 6 x 43 in the description.

cigars.about: The third house blend from LA Cigar Collective, blended by Klaas Kelner in the Dominican Republic as a fuller cigar than Kelner blends are usually known for. It is named for the torch carriers of New Orleans Mardi Gras night parades.
cigars.researchNote: A shop exclusive sold in singles and boxes of 15. The shop says the filler is 60 percent ligero.

cigars.about: The first cigar from Peter James Cigar Co., a joint venture between the Peter James leather case company and Luciano Cigars. It uses tobacco aged three to ten years and is made by a single buncher and roller in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: Regular production but capped at about 100 cigars a day. Luxury Cigar Club lists the profile as medium-plus, and halfwheel's reviewer found medium-plus strength with medium-full body. Tasting notes are from the halfwheel review.

cigars.about: One of two Los Estoico 54 blends launched in 2022 by Peter James Leather Co., the maker of leather cigar cases. It is made in Estelí and comes in one size.
cigars.researchNote: The 54 is not the ring gauge: it honors the first cigar the founder took from his father. It launched under Peter James Leather Co., before Peter James Cigar Co. was formed in 2024. One filler leaf is undisclosed, and Luxury Cigar Club calls the size a toro.

cigars.about: The darker of the two Los Estoico 54 blends launched in 2022 by Peter James Leather Co., with a San Andrés wrapper. It is made in Estelí and comes in one size.
cigars.researchNote: The 54 is not the ring gauge: it honors the first cigar the founder took from his father. Luxury Cigar Club lists the profile as medium-plus and calls the size a toro. One filler leaf is undisclosed.

cigars.about: The debut cigar from Surpassion, a veteran-founded brand with military-themed lines. It is made at Tabacalera La Isla in Santiago, Dominican Republic, with tobaccos aged five years.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it medium-plus, with body running medium to full. Luxury Cigar Club lists it as medium and Creekside as full. Creekside's page says it is handmade in Nicaragua, but the maker says Tabacalera La Isla in the Dominican Republic.

cigars.about: Surpassion's second line, a milder Connecticut-wrapped cigar honoring the U.S. Army Infantry. It was released on June 14, 2025, the Army's 250th birthday, and is made at Tabacalera La Isla.
cigars.researchNote: Luxury Cigar Club lists the profile as medium, while the maker and Creekside say mild to medium. All tobaccos are aged five years.

cigars.about: Surpassion's full-bodied Broadleaf line, a tribute to 250 years of U.S. Army Artillery. It is made at Tabacalera La Isla in the Dominican Republic and began shipping in January 2026.
cigars.researchNote: All tobaccos are aged at least five years.

cigars.about: A line from Nelson Alfonso's Selected Tobacco, the company behind Atabey and Byron, aged at least five years in rooms lined with cedar and French oak. It is rolled at Tabacos de Costa Rica.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel and the box call it Alfonso Extra Añejo, while the distributor United Cigars and Neptune call it Alfonso Añejo. It is regular production but made in small yearly batches. Halfwheel's reviewer found it on the lighter side of medium.

cigars.about: The darker follow-up to the Alfonso Añejo from Nelson Alfonso's Selected Tobacco, aged five years in rooms lined with Spanish cedar and French oak. It is rolled at Tabacos de Costa Rica.
cigars.researchNote: The distributor United Cigars calls it medium to full, while Neptune lists it as medium. United lists the filler as Dominican and Peruvian, but halfwheel and Neptune say Dominican and Nicaraguan. The Exclusivos is a torpedo, and Neptune lists the Preciosos as 7 x 40.

cigars.about: The flagship brand of Nelson Alfonso's Selected Tobacco, rolled at Tabacos de Costa Rica and aged at least five years after rolling. Alfonso is known for his packaging design work for Habanos, including the Cohiba Behike.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel reports the maker does not disclose the blend, so the wrapper, binder and Peruvian ligero here are what the U.S. distributor United Cigars lists. Neptune rates it medium, and halfwheel's reviewer found medium-plus. Two more sizes exist: Spiritus (7.5 x 40) and Benditos (7.25 x 58).

cigars.about: A darker, limited version of Atabey that was first announced in 2021 as an NFT and reached stores as a real cigar in 2023. It is rolled in Costa Rica and aged at least five years in rooms lined with cedar and French oak.
cigars.researchNote: Released in a limited batch each year to select stores. The Delirios, added in 2025, is sold in a 10-count travel humidor. The Habano Maduro wrapper is from the distributor United Cigars, halfwheel says only Ecuadorian, and the medium strength and tasting notes are from Neptune's Delirios listing.

cigars.about: A value-priced, big ring gauge line from Davidoff of Geneva USA, launched in 2018 with box art by the New York art duo UR New York. Halfwheel reports it is the former Room101 Big Payback blend brought back under a new name.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune sells it as Back2Back URNY Connecticut. The sizes have no vitola names, just dimensions. Halfwheel says only Connecticut wrapper, and Neptune specifies Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade.

cigars.about: The Nicaraguan puro in Davidoff of Geneva USA's value-priced Back2Back line, launched in 2018 with box art by UR New York. Halfwheel reports it is the former Room101 Big Payback blend under a new name.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune sells it as Back2Back URNY Nicaragua and lists it as rolled in Honduras from all Nicaraguan tobacco. The wrapper type is not published beyond Nicaraguan. The sizes have no vitola names, just dimensions.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: The regular-production line in Oliva's 2022 relaunch of Cuba Aliados, the old Rolando Reyes Sr. brand. It is a Honduran puro made by Julio Eiroa's JRE Tobacco Co.
cigars.researchNote: Despite the name it is not the original Reyes blend. Neptune sells it as Cuba Aliados Natural and gives the Habano and Corojo leaf types, while halfwheel lists all three components simply as Honduran. Neptune rates it medium, and halfwheel's reviewer found little nicotine strength.

cigars.about: The limited line in Oliva's 2022 relaunch of the Cuba Aliados brand, blended and made by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo at his Dominican factory. The wrapper is an Ecuadorian Sumatra leaf aged five years.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 15,000 boxes of 20, with 10,000 for the U.S. The brand is owned by Oliva's parent company. Tasting notes are from the halfwheel review.

cigars.about: Maya Selva's Nicaraguan puro, launched in 1999. The name is the Tawahka word for a rolled tobacco leaf.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on where it is rolled: Neptune says Maya Selva's factory in Danlí, Honduras, while halfwheel's 2022 review lists Plasencia Cigars in Nicaragua. Neptune rates it mild to mild-medium, and halfwheel's reviewer found it medium.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Maya Selva's Cumpay, an all-Nicaraguan blend offered in two sizes. The Robusto joined the earlier Volcán in 2021.
cigars.researchNote: The maker describes it as medium to full, and Neptune lists it as full. Sources disagree on where Cumpay is rolled: Neptune says Maya Selva's factory in Danlí, Honduras, while halfwheel lists the core line at Plasencia in Nicaragua.

cigars.about: The first line from Don Emmanuel Cigars, blended with Eladio Díaz, the former Davidoff master blender, and made at his factory in the Dominican Republic. It is named for the creator gods of Sumerian mythology.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is published only as Dominican, and 2024 is the U.S. debut year reported by halfwheel. The Corona Fina comes in tins of five, and the Enki is a figurado added in 2026. Strength and tasting notes are from Neptune.
