cigars.about: A limited two-blend release from Don Emmanuel Cigars and Eladio Díaz, sold in boxes of 14 with seven Sun and seven Moon toros. Both blends use tobacco aged in rum barrels.
cigars.researchNote: This is two cigars in one box, so there is no single wrapper: Sun is the lighter Connecticut-seed blend and Moon is the fuller Habano blend. Limited to 777 numbered boxes. Neptune lists the strength as medium and gives the tasting notes: cedar, cream and nuts for Sun, earth, coffee and cocoa for Moon.

cigars.about: The house line of IGM Cigars, the family-run Costa Rican factory that also makes Casdagli. It is a medium blend built around Costa Rican tobacco under an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Luxury Cigar Club lists the whole line with a Habano maduro wrapper and Costa Rican, Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler. Neptune gives that blend only for the limited Rockets size. The size called Toro is a 5 x 52 robusto.

cigars.about: A short, thick torpedo in the IGM 537 line with a darker Habano maduro wrapper and a fuller blend than the regular sizes. It is made at the IGM Cigars factory in Costa Rica.
cigars.researchNote: This is one limited size (4 x 60 torpedo) of the IGM 537 line, with a different, fuller blend than the regular sizes.

cigars.about: A value-priced cigar from General Cigar (Scandinavian Tobacco Group), introduced at the 2016 trade show. It pairs a Honduran-grown Connecticut wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune rates it Medium, Mike's Cigars Medium to Full. Retailers say it is rolled in Nicaragua, but the maker did not disclose the factory at launch.

cigars.about: The Habano-wrapped version of General Cigar's value-priced La Estrella Cubana, introduced in 2016. It uses a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper over a Honduran binder and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune rates it Medium, Mike's Cigars Medium to Full. Retailers say it is rolled in Nicaragua, but the maker did not disclose the factory at launch.

cigars.about: A long-running Honduran bundle cigar made with tobacco from the Jamastran Valley and sold in bundles of 25. It is known as an inexpensive everyday smoke with a sweetened cap.
cigars.researchNote: The cap is sweetened, which is worth telling a guest. Retailers describe it as mild to medium. Famous Smoke says it comes from the same Honduran factory as Camacho and Baccarat, and Neptune lists Davidoff as the maker.

cigars.about: The maduro version of the National Brand Honduran bundle cigar, sold in bundles of 25. It uses the same Honduran filler under a dark maduro wrapper and has a lightly sweetened tip.
cigars.researchNote: The cap is sweetened. Famous Smoke calls the wrapper Honduran Broadleaf maduro, while Neptune just lists a Honduran maduro wrapper. Neptune lists Davidoff as the maker.

cigars.about: The core line from Fable Cigars, a small brand started by Sean Kremenetski and Mitul Shah in 2016. The line is themed on the number seven, the fourth prime, and uses a Pennsylvania broadleaf wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Originally made at RoMa Craft's Nica Sueno factory in Esteli. Production moved to Cordoba & Morales when the brand returned in 2025, with the same blend on paper. Earlier sizes such as Mi (5 3/4 x 46) and Doc (4 1/4 x 52) were not part of the relaunch.

cigars.about: A limited barber pole toro and the first release in Fable's Scions series, which is themed on fathers and their children. It was Fable's first Honduran cigar, rolled at the factory behind Cavalier Geneve.
cigars.researchNote: Two wrappers are twisted together, a Honduran Habano and a Connecticut leaf whose origin is not stated. Limited to 250 bundles of 20 cigars.

cigars.about: A mild, budget-priced Dominican cigar blended and made by the Fuente family at Tabacalera A. Fuente. The natural version wears a Connecticut Shade wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists the wrapper as Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade with a Nicaraguan binder, while Famous Smoke gives the wrapper origin as Connecticut. Neptune and Holt's call it mild, Famous Smoke medium.

cigars.about: The Connecticut Broadleaf maduro version of Montesino, a budget-priced Dominican cigar made by the Fuente family at Tabacalera A. Fuente using aged Dominican tobaccos.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's calls the brand mild, while Famous Smoke lists the Maduro as medium and the brand as mellow to medium. Holt's carries only the Robusto and Toro in Maduro.

cigars.about: A short, unbanded value cigar from Enrique Sanchez's Global Premium Cigars, the company behind 1502. It is sold in five-packs and the name means little pieces in Spanish.
cigars.researchNote: It launched in 2018 as a 4 1/2 x 50 made at Plasencia, moved to the Diamond factory in 2019, and is now sold as a 4 x 50. Neptune lists Barreda Cigars as the current maker.

cigars.about: The second Cachitos blend from Global Premium Cigars, a short unbanded 4 x 50 with a U.S. Connecticut Shade wrapper over Nicaraguan tobaccos. It is sold in five-packs.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists the strength as Medium but describes the profile as mild to medium bodied. Unlike the original Cachitos, this blend has no Honduran tobacco.

cigars.about: A cigar line from accessory company Quality Importers, made for it by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo at Casa Carrillo in Santiago. Each cigar is sold with a branded cutter as part of its packaging concept.
cigars.researchNote: The binder and filler are not disclosed, beyond coming from the Carrillo inventory.

cigars.about: The San Andres maduro blend of Conspiracy, the cigar line from accessory company Quality Importers. It is made by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo at Casa Carrillo in Santiago.
cigars.researchNote: The binder and filler are not disclosed, beyond coming from the Carrillo inventory.

cigars.about: The Connecticut blend of Ilegal, a line from La Familia Robaina (formerly White Hat), the company behind Hirochi Robaina's HR cigars. It is made at Omar Gonzalez-Aleman's La Corona factory in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are not disclosed. Neptune's listing says Medium but its description calls it mild, and it describes the wrapper as USA Connecticut where halfwheel says Ecuadorian. The name is the Spanish spelling of illegal.

cigars.about: The San Andres blend of Ilegal from La Familia Robaina (formerly White Hat), blended with help from Esteban Disla of Nica Sueno. It is made at the La Corona factory in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are not disclosed. halfwheel's review put the strength between medium and full; Neptune's listing says Medium but its description says full. Neptune now marks it discontinued.

cigars.about: A Scandinavian Tobacco Group brand built around Ecuadorian wrapper, with the name pointing to the equator. The original blend has an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Only the Gordo could be confirmed; other sizes may exist. Neptune's specs name the NACSA factory, though its description says Oliva Cigar Co.

cigars.about: The second Latitude Zero blend from Scandinavian Tobacco Group, created by Raul Disla at the NACSA factory with tobaccos from Oliva Tobacco Co. It has an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper and is billed as full-bodied.
cigars.researchNote: The maker describes it as full-bodied and does not give a separate strength.

cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A big-ring-gauge line from Drew Estate and Joya de Nicaragua, blended by Jonathan Drew and rolled at the Joya de Nicaragua factory. It is named after a Public Enemy song and was discontinued in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Made at Joya de Nicaragua, not Drew Estate's own factory. The binder is Connecticut shade leaf, which Neptune lists as Ecuadorian. MUWAT Kentucky Fire Cured is a different blend that stayed in production.

cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A 4 x 44 petit corona in Drew Estate's MUWAT line, made at Joya de Nicaragua with a stronger Extra Fuerte version of the blend. It began in late 2011 as a New Havana Cigars exclusive and went national in 2012.
cigars.researchNote: This is one size of the MUWAT line, formally MUWAT EF (Extra Fuerte) Bait Fish, with a slightly stronger blend than the 60 ring sizes. Neptune's listing says Medium but describes it as fuller than the rest of the line. The line was discontinued in 2022.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: A San Andres wrapped Nicaraguan cigar made by AJ Fernandez for Jeff Nasser, who owns Nasser's Lounge in Petion-Ville, Haiti. It began in 2023 as a shop exclusive and AJ Fernandez started selling it to U.S. stores in September 2024.
cigars.researchNote: The maker also calls it The Goat Maduro. The maker says medium to full; Neptune and Mike's Cigars list Medium. The maker and halfwheel's 2025 review give the Toro as 6 x 54, while Neptune and earlier halfwheel news say 6 x 52.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua
cigars.about: The second Nasser blend, made by AJ Fernandez in Esteli with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper and a double binder. It went on sale in March 2026.
cigars.researchNote: The maker and Mike's Cigars list the wrapper as Ecuadorian Connecticut; halfwheel calls it an Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed habano. The maker says mild to medium, while Mike's lists Medium.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan cigar with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper from Veritas Cigar Co., the company chaired by Chris Weber. Neptune describes it as a mellow, mild to medium smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Blend details come from one retailer, Neptune, whose description says mild to medium while its spec field says Medium. Only the Toro could be confirmed. The line was on sale by early 2017.

cigars.about: The San Andres maduro version of the Veritas Torch, made in Nicaragua over Nicaraguan binder and filler. Neptune describes it as a medium bodied cigar that is bold but smooth.
cigars.researchNote: Blend details come from one retailer, Neptune. Only the Toro could be confirmed.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, USA, undisclosed South American country
cigars.about: The debut line from Vance Taylor's Stoic Cigars, made at Klaas Kelner's factory in the Dominican Republic. The four sizes are named for the Stoic virtues.
cigars.researchNote: One of the filler countries is not disclosed. The maker describes it as full flavored without heavy strength but gives no strength rating.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, Ecuador, USA, undisclosed South American country
cigars.about: The second line from Stoic Cigars, made at Kelner Cigars in the Dominican Republic with an Ecuadorian corojo wrapper. It shipped to stores in September 2025 in the same four sizes as the original Stoic.
cigars.researchNote: One of the filler countries is not disclosed. Strength, body and flavors are from halfwheel's review of the Moderation size, not from the maker.

cigars.factory: Fabrica de Tabacos Nica Sueno S.A.
cigars.about: The second cigar from Tyler Jeffery's Viso Horny brand, made at the Nica Sueno factory that produces RoMa Craft. Every leaf in it comes from the viso priming, the middle of the tobacco plant.
cigars.researchNote: Limited to 500 bundles of 10 (5,000 cigars). The name refers to the 5 x 55 size. Strength, body and flavors are from halfwheel's review, which put strength between medium and medium-plus.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Corojo-seed and Candela barber pole (origin undisclosed)
cigars.about: A barber pole robusto from Tyler Jeffery's Viso Horny brand, made at Fabrica Oveja Negra in Esteli. It pairs a corojo-seed leaf with green candela on the wrapper and uses only viso priming fillers.
cigars.researchNote: Two-leaf barber pole wrapper, so no single wrapper category applies. Wrapper and binder origins are undisclosed. Limited to 500 bundles of 10.

cigars.about: The debut line from Rafael Cifuentes III, whose family once owned the Partagas factory in Havana. It is rolled at El Titan de Bronze in Miami with entubado bunching and a triple cap, and was modeled on 1990s Partagas Serie D No. 4.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel reported each size limited to 1,000 boxes of 10 at launch, but it was still on sale in 2025, so the production status is unclear. Boxes are date stamped. Strength is from one retailer, Neptune.

cigars.about: A small, rough-looking cheroot from General Cigar's El Credito factory, home of La Gloria Cubana. Two factory supervisors came up with it in 2011; it is shaped by hand without a mold and uses two filler leaves.
cigars.researchNote: Launched as El Perrito War of Flavors. The name means little dog. It is sold unbanded in boxes of 50, and halfwheel notes both ends are open so it needs no cutting.

cigars.about: A mild Honduran cigar with a Connecticut-seed shade wrapper and a lightly sweetened cap. The brand dates to 1993 and now belongs to the Davidoff group.
cigars.researchNote: The cap is sweetened. Retailers disagree on the binder: Mike's Cigars says Mexican, Neptune says Honduran.

cigars.about: A value-priced Altadis U.S.A. cigar handmade in Honduras, with a Connecticut shade wrapper over Mexican San Andres binder and filler. The sizes are named for Spanish explorers.
cigars.researchNote: Strength varies by seller: Cigar World says mellow to medium, Neptune says Mild, Famous says Medium. Neptune marks its sizes as discontinued, though Altadis still lists the line.

cigars.about: A Miami Cigar & Co. brand that debuted at the 2025 PCA show and shipped that June. It pairs a Brazilian Cuban-seed wrapper with an Ecuadorian Sumatra-seed binder and Dominican filler.
cigars.researchNote: Has a sweetened cap and some Black Cavendish pipe tobacco in the filler, per halfwheel. Halfwheel lists the factory as undisclosed, while Neptune says La Aurora. The maker says mild-medium; retailers list Medium.

cigars.about: A budget bundle cigar handmade in Esteli, Nicaragua, with an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. It is a Cuban sandwich, meaning it uses mixed short and long filler.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed-filler Cuban sandwich. Mike's Cigars lists Nicaraguan, Dominican and Honduran filler, while Holt's describes the blend as Nicaraguan. Mike's lists the Herencia at 50 ring; Neptune and Holt's say 52.

cigars.about: The second line from Artesano del Tobacco, made by AJ Fernandez with a San Andres maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco from his farms. The name means the octopus, and it launched in the U.S. in January 2023.
cigars.researchNote: The maker names the factory as San Lotano; halfwheel lists Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua in Esteli and Neptune says Ocotal. Strength and body are from Neptune, since the maker gives no written rating. The Octo Ocho is a three-cigar culebra.

cigars.about: A value-priced cigar from J.C. Newman, made in Tampa and named for the company's El Reloj factory in Ybor City and its four-sided clock tower. It uses an Ecuadorian Havana-seed sun grown wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Not on J.C. Newman's list of current brands, but Neptune and Mike's Cigars still sell the 8 x 53 El Ocho, so its status is unclear. The binder is listed by one retailer only.

cigars.about: A cinnamon-flavored cigar licensed from Fireball Cinnamon Whisky and made for Scandinavian Tobacco Group in the Dominican Republic. It launched in 2022 through Thompson Cigar before going to other stores.
cigars.researchNote: Cinnamon-flavored cigar; the factory is not disclosed. Neptune lists the Corona at 6 3/8 inches rather than 6 1/4. Strength is from one retailer.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made by Aganorsa Leaf for the value-priced Nica Libre brand. It has a Nicaraguan Corojo wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Also written Nica Libre x Aganorsa. Made by Aganorsa Leaf at its TABSA factory. Four sizes launched in 2020, but one retailer now lists only the 6 x 60 Titan.

cigars.about: A 2020 release from Rafael Nodal's Oliveros brand, part of the Aging Room family, made at Plasencia. The tobacco was aged two years, the cigars rested six months, then sat boxed for nearly three more years before shipping.
cigars.researchNote: One of three Gran Retorno blends, with Habano and Maduro. An older Gran Retorno made by El Galan was a different cigar. The 2020 run was 400,000 cigars across all three blends.

cigars.about: United Cigars' revival of a Dutch cigar brand that dates to the 1770s and went out of business in 1937. The new version is made by Hendrik Kelner Jr.'s factory with tobacco from the Kelner family farms.
cigars.researchNote: The 2022 debut size, The Admiral, was limited to 250 boxes before the line grew in 2023. A 4 1/2 x 43 Cooper is sold at events only. United's launch release called it medium in strength and medium-plus in body; its site now says medium to full bodied.

cigars.about: A low-priced mixed filler handmade from the ABAM factory in the Dominican Republic, run by blender Jose Matias Maragoto. It is sold only by Neptune Cigar as an everyday value cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed filler, not long filler. Despite the name it contains no Cuban tobacco. It is a Neptune Cigar exclusive, so that retailer is the only source for the blend.

cigars.about: A budget mixed filler handmade from Honduras, tied to the Baccarat family in the Davidoff group and finished with a sweetened cap. It is sold as an inexpensive everyday cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Mixed filler with a sweet cap. The one retailer that lists it rates it mild in its specs but calls it spicy and medium to full in its text, so strength is left blank. It marks the 200 and Havana Twist as discontinued.

cigars.about: The first cigar from 1966 Cigars, a Honduran company started by Roberto Argueta and named for the year his father was born. It is a single toro made in Danli that debuted at the 2024 PCA trade show.
cigars.researchNote: No published strength rating was found. Flavor words come from the brand owner's own description.

cigars.about: A Dominican puro that marked the return of Victor Nicolas' Chogui brand in 2022. It replaced the original Dos77 with a sun grown corojo wrapper over tobacco from grower Leo Reyes.
cigars.researchNote: The brand is properly spelled Chogüí. Strength is from halfwheel: medium-plus, touching medium-full, in 2022 and mild-medium to medium on a 2024 revisit. The single size is called Rogusto, a blend of robusto and gusto.

cigars.about: A cigar made in honor of Esteban Disla, co-owner of the NicaSueño factory best known for RoMa Craft Tobac. The name is a nickname his mentor Sergio Cuevas gave him, and the line is distributed by Pospiech Inc.
cigars.researchNote: Made at the RoMa Craft factory but not sold through RoMa Craft. Strength is from halfwheel's review; no maker rating was found.

cigars.about: A limited edition made for the 80th birthday of Hendrik "Henke" Kelner, the longtime Davidoff cigar maker, blended by him and his son Klaas. It is a single 7 x 50 double-tapered perfecto.
cigars.researchNote: Binder and filler are undisclosed beyond some Dominican tobacco from Yamasa. Limited to 2,000 boxes of 10, with 1,500 for the U.S. Strength and body are from halfwheel's review.

cigars.about: A limited line from Nelson Alfonso's Selected Tobacco, the company behind Byron and Atabey, blended with his sons. The cigars are rolled in Costa Rica and then aged four years in cedar-lined rooms in Spain.
cigars.researchNote: Debuted only in a gift set of five tubed cigars with an ashtray. Production numbers were not disclosed. Strength and body are from halfwheel's review.

cigars.about: The first release in Queen of the West, the house brand of Cincinnati retailer Creekside Cigar Co. It is a single toro made at Hostos Fernandez Quesada's La Isla factory in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Queen of the West is a nickname for Cincinnati. Creekside lists the strength as medium and describes it as a medium-plus cigar. It says this is the first of three core lines.

cigars.about: The house cigar of Venture 1492, the sister company Kyle Gellis of Warped Cigars set up to help new brands with distribution and branding. It is a single 5 1/2 x 48 size made in Santiago, Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Gran Corona is the only size of the Venture 1492 line. Strength and body are from halfwheel's review, which found it building to medium-full by the end.
